entries.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally given Opening of an Office and granted the title Marquis of Yongkang County.

entries.zh: 及上受禪，拜大將軍，進爵郡公。
entries.en: When Yang Jian ascended the throne, Hong was made Grand General and promoted to Duke of a Commandery.
entries.literal: When the emperor accepted the abdication, he was appointed Grand General and advanced in rank to Duke of a Commandery.

entries.zh: 尋贈其父為柱國、尚書令、河間郡公。
entries.en: Shortly thereafter his late father was posthumously honored as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Hejian Commandery.
entries.literal: Soon afterward his father was posthumously ennobled as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Hejian Commandery.

entries.zh: 其年立弘為河間王，拜右衛大將軍。
entries.en: That year Hong was created Prince of Hejian and appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: That same year Hong was installed as Prince of Hejian and appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 歲餘，進授柱國。
entries.en: A little over a year later he was promoted to Pillar of State.
entries.literal: After more than a year, he was advanced to Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 時突厥屢為邊患，以行軍元帥率眾數萬，出靈州道，與虜相遇，戰，大破之，斬數千級。
entries.en: When the Turks were repeatedly raiding the frontier, he served as commander of the field army at the head of tens of thousands of men. Marching out along the Lingzhou route, he met the enemy in battle and routed them, beheading several thousand.
entries.literal: At the time the Turks were a repeated menace on the frontier; as commander of the field army he led a force of tens of thousands by the Lingzhou route, encountered the barbarians, fought, and utterly defeated them, taking several thousand heads.

entries.zh: 賜物二千段，出拜甯州總管，進位上柱國。
entries.en: Rewarded with two thousand bales of textiles, he was appointed Director-General of Ning Province and promoted to First Rank Pillar of State.
entries.literal: He was granted two thousand bales of goods, was sent out as Director-General of Ning Province, and advanced to First Rank Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 弘在州，治尚清靜，甚有恩惠。
entries.en: As provincial governor he favored a light, unobtrusive administration and was widely regarded as a benevolent ruler.
entries.literal: In his province, Hong's governance valued quiet simplicity, and he showed much kindness and grace.

entries.zh: 後數載，征還京師。
entries.en: After several years he was summoned back to the capital.
entries.literal: Several years later he was recalled to the capital.

entries.zh: 未幾，拜蒲州刺史，得以便宜從事。
entries.en: Not long afterward he was made governor of Pu Prefecture with authority to act at his own discretion.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed governor of Pu Prefecture and granted discretion to act as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 時河東多盜賊，民不得安。
entries.en: Banditry was rampant in Hedong at the time, and the people lived in constant fear.
entries.literal: At the time there were many bandits in Hedong, and the people could not live in peace.

entries.zh: 弘奏為盜者百餘人，投之邊裔，州境帖然，號為良吏。
entries.en: Hong identified more than a hundred robbers and had them sent to the frontier. With the territory at peace, he won renown as an outstanding official.
entries.literal: Hong petitioned regarding more than a hundred robbers, exiling them to the frontier regions; the territory of the prefecture became calm, and he was acclaimed as a good official.

entries.zh: 每晉王廣入朝，弘輒領揚州總管，及晉王歸籓，弘複還蒲州。
entries.en: Whenever Prince Guang of Jin visited the capital, Hong would temporarily serve as Director-General of Yang Province; when the prince returned to his fief, Hong would go back to Pu.
entries.literal: Whenever Prince Jin Guang came to court for an audience, Hong would take charge as Director-General of Yang Province; when the Prince of Jin returned to his fief, Hong would resume his post at Pu.

entries.zh: 在官十餘年，風教大洽。
entries.en: Over more than a decade in office, he brought local customs and moral instruction into excellent order.
entries.literal: In office for more than ten years, customs and education were thoroughly harmonized.

entries.zh: 煬帝嗣位，征還，拜太子太保。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Hong was recalled and made Grand Mentor to the crown prince.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Hong was recalled and appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 歲餘，薨。
entries.en: A little over a year later he died.
entries.literal: After more than a year, he died.

entries.zh: 大業六年，追封郇王。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Daye (610), he was posthumously created Prince of Xun.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Daye, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.

entries.zh: 子慶嗣。
entries.en: His son Qing inherited his title.
entries.literal: His son Qing succeeded him.

entries.zh: 雄寬容下士，朝野傾矚。
entries.en: Xiong was gracious toward men of talent, and all eyes in court and country turned toward him.
entries.literal: Xiong was tolerant and deferential toward gentlemen; court and countryside alike looked to him with admiration.

entries.zh: 高祖惡其得眾，陰忌之，不欲其典兵馬。
entries.en: Emperor Wen resented his popularity and secretly distrusted him; he did not want Xiong in command of military forces.
entries.literal: Gaozu disliked his winning the loyalty of the masses and secretly envied him, not wishing him to command troops and horses.

entries.zh: 乃下冊書，拜雄為司空，曰：「維開皇九年八月朔壬戌，皇帝若曰：於戲！
entries.en: He therefore issued an investiture edict creating Xiong Minister of Works: "On the first day, renxu, of the eighth month, ninth year of Kaihuang, the emperor speaks: Alas!
entries.literal: Thereupon he issued an investiture document appointing Xiong as Minister of Works, saying: "It is the first day renxu of the eighth month of the ninth year of Kaihuang; the emperor says: Alas!

entries.zh: 惟爾上柱國、左衛大將軍、宗正卿、廣平王，風度寬弘，位望隆顯，爰司禁旅，綿曆十載。
entries.en: You, First Rank Pillar of State, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Prince of Guangping—of generous bearing and illustrious standing, you have commanded the palace guard these ten years past.
entries.literal: You, First Rank Pillar of State, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Prince of Guangping—your bearing is broad and magnanimous, your rank and repute lofty and illustrious; you have long managed the forbidden troops, continuously for ten years.

entries.zh: 入當心腹，外任爪牙，驅馳軒陛，勤勞著績。
entries.en: Within you have been the emperor's trusted confidant; without you have wielded the dynasty's authority, serving tirelessly at court with conspicuous merit.
entries.literal: Within you served as intimate confidant; without you wielded imperial power; you hurried about the palace halls, and your diligent toil has shown merit.

entries.zh: 念舊庸勳，禮秩加等。
entries.en: In recognition of your long and faithful service, your ceremonial rank is hereby raised.
entries.literal: Recalling your old ordinary merit, ceremonial rank is advanced a grade.

entries.zh: 公輔之寄，民具爾瞻，宜竭乃誠，副茲名實，是用命爾為司空。
entries.en: The burden of a chief minister rests on you, and the people look to you accordingly. Devote yourself fully to the charge. I therefore appoint you Minister of Works.
entries.literal: The trust of a state minister—the people all look up to you; you should exhaust your sincerity to match this name and reality; therefore I appoint you Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 往欽哉！
entries.en: Go forth and fulfill this trust!
entries.literal: Go—revere this!

entries.zh: 光應寵命，得不慎歟！」
entries.en: You have received an honor of the highest kind—act with all due care!"
entries.literal: To reflect glory upon this favored appointment—can you not be cautious!"

entries.zh: 外示優崇，實奪其權也。
entries.en: Outwardly it was a mark of highest honor; in fact it removed him from command.
entries.literal: Outwardly it showed high esteem; in reality it stripped him of authority.

entries.zh: 雄無職務，乃閉門不通賓客。
entries.en: With no official duties left to him, Xiong shut his gates and refused visitors.
entries.literal: Xiong had no official duties and thereupon shut his gate, refusing to receive guests.

entries.zh: 尋改封清漳王。
entries.en: He was soon re-created Prince of Qingzhang.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qingzhang.

entries.zh: 仁壽初，高祖曰：「清漳之名，未允聲望。」
entries.en: Early in the Renshou era Emperor Wen said, "The title Prince of Qingzhang does not match his standing."
entries.literal: At the start of Renshou, Gaozu said: "The name Qingzhang does not accord with his reputation."

entries.zh: 命職方進地圖，上指安德郡以示群臣曰：「此號足為名德相稱。」
entries.en: He ordered the map brought and, pointing to Ande Commandery, showed it to the officials: "This title is worthy of his reputation."
entries.literal: He ordered the Bureau of Garrisons to present a map; pointing to Ande Commandery he showed the officials and said: "This title is fully worthy to match his name and virtue."

entries.zh: 於是改封安德王。
entries.en: Xiong was thereupon re-created Prince of Ande.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Ande.

entries.zh: 楊處綱，高祖族父也。
entries.en: Yang Chugang was an elder kinsman of Emperor Wen on the Yang clan side.
entries.literal: Yang Chugang was a senior clansman of Gaozu on the father's side.

entries.zh: 生長北邊，少習騎射。
entries.en: Raised on the northern frontier, he trained in riding and archery from boyhood.
entries.literal: He grew up on the northern frontier and from youth practiced horsemanship and archery.

entries.zh: 在周嘗以軍功拜上儀同。
entries.en: Under the Northern Zhou he was promoted to Senior Acting Associate on the strength of his military service.
entries.literal: Under the Zhou he was once appointed Senior Acting Associate in Chief of an Office for military merit.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，贈其父鐘葵為柱國、尚書令、義城縣公，以處綱襲焉。
entries.en: When Yang Jian took the throne, he posthumously honored Chugang's father Zhongkui as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Yicheng County, and Chugang inherited the title.
entries.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he posthumously ennobled Chugang's father Zhongkui as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Yicheng County; Chugang inherited the title.

entries.zh: 授開府，督武候事。
entries.en: He was granted the privilege of opening his own office and put in charge of the Martial Guard.
entries.literal: He was granted Opening of an Office and supervised the affairs of the Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 尋為太子宗衛率，轉左監門郎將。
entries.en: He soon became Colonel Director of the crown prince's clan guard, then transferred to Left Commandant of the Monitoring Gate.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he became Colonel Director of the Heir Apparent's Clan Guard and then transferred to Left Commandant of the Monitoring Gate.

entries.zh: 後數載，起授右領軍將軍。
entries.en: Several years later he was recalled and appointed Right Corps Commander General.
entries.literal: Several years later he was appointed Right Corps Commander General.

entries.zh: 處綱雖無才藝，而性質直，在官強濟，亦為當時所稱。
entries.en: Chugang had no special gifts, but he was upright by nature and forceful in office, and won respect in his day.
entries.literal: Although Chugang had no special talent or accomplishment, his nature was straightforward; in office he was forceful and effective, and was likewise praised at the time.

entries.zh: 尋拜蒲州刺史，吏民悅之。
entries.en: He was soon made governor of Pu Prefecture, where officials and commoners alike welcomed him.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Pu Prefecture, and officials and people were pleased with him.

entries.zh: 進位大將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to Grand General.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Grand General.

entries.zh: 後遷秦州總管，卒官。
entries.en: He was later transferred to Director-General of Qin Province, where he died in office.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred as Director-General of Qin Province and died in office.

entries.zh: 諡曰恭。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous name Respectful (Gong).
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Gong ("Respectful").

entries.zh: 楊子崇，高祖族弟也。
entries.en: Yang Zichong was a younger clansman-cousin of Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Yang Zichong was a clansman and younger cousin of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 父盆生，贈荊州刺史。
entries.en: His father Pensheng was posthumously honored as governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: His father Pensheng was posthumously made governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 子崇少好學，涉獵書記，有風儀，愛賢好士。
entries.en: Zichong loved study from childhood, read widely, carried himself with dignity, and delighted in talented men.
entries.literal: Zichong from youth loved learning, ranged widely through books and records, had dignified bearing, and loved worthies and honored gentlemen.

entries.zh: 開皇初，拜儀同，以車騎將軍恆典宿衛。
entries.en: Early in the Kaihuang era he was made Acting Associate and regularly performed palace guard duty as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: In the early Kaihuang period he was appointed Acting Associate and regularly served as Palace Guard with the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 後為司門侍郎。
entries.en: He later served as Vice Director of the Department of Gatekeepers.
entries.literal: Later he became Vice Director of the Department of Gatekeepers.

entries.zh: 煬帝嗣位，累遷候衛將軍，坐事免。
entries.en: After Emperor Yang came to the throne, he rose to General of the Guarding Retinue but was dismissed when implicated in an offense.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, through repeated promotion he became General of the Guarding Retinue, but was dismissed on account of an offense.

entries.zh: 未幾，複令檢校將軍事。
entries.en: Not long afterward he was again entrusted with provisional command of military affairs.
entries.literal: Before long he was again ordered to serve provisionally as a general on military matters.

entries.zh: 從帝幸汾陽宮，子崇知突厥必為寇患，屢請早還京師，帝不納。
entries.en: When he accompanied the emperor to the Fenyang Palace, Zichong was convinced the Turks would soon raid the frontier and repeatedly urged an early return to the capital, but the emperor refused to listen.
entries.literal: Accompanying the emperor to the Fenyang Palace, Zichong knew the Turks would surely become a raiding menace and repeatedly petitioned for an early return to the capital; the emperor did not accept.

entries.zh: 尋有雁門之圍。
entries.en: Soon afterward came the siege at Yanmen.
entries.literal: Before long there was the siege at Yanmen.

entries.zh: 及賊退，帝怒之曰：「子崇怯軟，妄有陳請，驚動我眾心，不可居爪牙之寄。」
entries.en: When the enemy withdrew, the emperor raged at him: "Zichong is cowardly and weak. His ill-timed warnings have unsettled the army. He is unfit to hold a commander's post."
entries.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the emperor angrily said: "Zichong is cowardly and soft, recklessly making petitions and disturbing the hearts of my troops—he cannot hold the trust of a close military post."

entries.zh: 出為離石郡太守，治有能名。
entries.en: He was demoted to Administrator of Lishi Commandery, where he nevertheless earned a reputation for effective administration.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Lishi Commandery and gained a reputation for capable governance.

entries.zh: 自是突厥屢寇邊塞，胡賊劉六兒複擁眾劫掠郡境，子崇上表請兵鎮遏。
entries.en: From then on the Turks raided the frontier repeatedly, and the rebel Liu Liu'er gathered forces to pillage the commandery. Zichong petitioned for troops to restore order.
entries.literal: From this time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier passes, and Hu bandit Liu Liu'er again gathered followers to plunder the commandery territory; Zichong submitted a memorial requesting troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 帝複大怒，下書令子崇巡行長城。
entries.en: The emperor erupted in anger again and ordered Zichong to make a patrol inspection of the Great Wall.
entries.literal: The emperor again flew into a rage and issued an edict ordering Zichong to inspect the Great Wall.

entries.zh: 子崇出百餘裡，四面路絕，不得進而歸。
entries.en: Zichong marched out more than a hundred li, but every route was blocked and he was forced to turn back.
entries.literal: Zichong went out more than a hundred li; roads were cut off on all sides, and he could not advance and returned.

entries.zh: 時百姓饑饉，相聚為盜，子崇前後捕斬數千人。
entries.en: With famine driving people to banditry, Zichong captured and executed several thousand in the course of his duties.
entries.literal: At the time the common people were famine-stricken and gathered to become bandits; Zichong in succession captured and beheaded several thousand.

entries.zh: 歲餘，朔方梁師都、馬邑劉武周等各稱兵作亂，郡中諸胡複相嘯聚。
entries.en: A little over a year later, Liang Shidu in Shuofang and Liu Wuzhou in Mayi each rose in arms, and the non-Han peoples of the commandery likewise began gathering in rebellion.
entries.literal: After more than a year, Liang Shidu of Shuofang, Liu Wuzhou of Mayi, and others each raised troops in rebellion; the various Hu in the commandery again rallied one another in assembly.

entries.zh: 子崇患之，言欲朝集，遂與心腹數百人自孟門關將還京師。
entries.en: Alarmed by the growing chaos, Zichong announced that he would go to court and, with several hundred trusted men, set out from Mengmen Pass toward the capital.
entries.literal: Distressed by this, Zichong said he wished to attend a court assembly and thereupon, with several hundred trusted followers, set out from Mengmen Pass intending to return to the capital.

entries.zh: 輜重半濟，遇河西諸縣各殺長吏，叛歸師都，道路隔絕，子崇退歸離石。
entries.en: Their baggage train was still half across the river when word came that the counties west of the Yellow River had killed their magistrates and joined Liang Shidu. With the roads cut off, Zichong retreated to Lishi.
entries.literal: When the baggage train was half across, they encountered the various counties west of the river each killing their chief officials and defecting to Shidu; the roads were cut off, and Zichong withdrew back to Lishi.

entries.zh: 所將左右，既聞太原有兵起，不復入城，遂各叛去。
entries.en: His men, hearing that an army had risen at Taiyuan, refused to re-enter the city and deserted one by one.
entries.literal: The followers he had brought, having heard that troops had risen at Taiyuan, would no longer enter the city and thereupon each deserted and left.

entries.zh: 子崇悉收叛者父兄斬之。
entries.en: Zichong rounded up the fathers and elder brothers of the deserters and had them all executed.
entries.literal: Zichong entirely apprehended the fathers and elder brothers of the deserters and beheaded them.

entries.zh: 後數日，義兵夜至城下，城中豪傑複出應之。
entries.en: A few days later rebel troops appeared outside the walls by night, and prominent locals inside the city opened the gates to join them.
entries.literal: Several days later, righteous-army troops arrived at the city by night, and bold heroes within the city again came out to answer them.

entries.zh: 城陷，子崇為仇家所殺。
entries.en: The city fell, and Zichong was killed by men who bore a grudge against him.
entries.literal: The city fell; Zichong was killed by an enemy family.

entries.zh: 觀德王雄，初名惠，高祖族子也。
entries.en: Guande Prince Xiong, originally named Hui, was a clansman-son of Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Guande Wang Xiong, originally named Hui, was a clansman's son of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 父紹，仕周，曆八州刺史、儻城縣公，賜姓叱呂引氏。
entries.en: His father Shao had served the Northern Zhou as governor of eight provinces in succession, held the title Duke of Tangcheng County, and been granted the surname Chilüyin.
entries.literal: His father Shao served under Zhou, successively governing eight provinces as governor, and was Duke of Tangcheng County, granted the surname Chilüyin.

entries.zh: 雄美姿儀，有器度，雍容閒雅，進止可觀。
entries.en: Xiong was handsome and dignified, with a calm, elegant bearing and a presence that commanded respect.
entries.literal: Xiong had handsome bearing, possessed capacity and magnanimity, was composed and refined in leisure, and his advances and halts were admirable to behold.

entries.zh: 周武帝時，為太子司旅下大夫。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he held the post of Junior Grand Master of the crown prince's retinue protocol.
entries.literal: During Emperor Wu of Zhou's reign, he served as Junior Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Retinue Protocol.

entries.zh: 帝幸雲陽宮，衛王直作亂，以其徒襲肅章門，雄逆拒破之。
entries.en: When the emperor visited the Yunyang Palace, Prince Zhi of Wei rebelled and led his followers in an assault on the Suzhang Gate; Xiong met the attack and routed them.
entries.literal: When the emperor visited the Yunyang Palace, Prince Wei Zhi raised a rebellion and with his followers attacked the Su Zang Gate; Xiong met them in resistance and defeated them.

entries.zh: 進位上儀同，封武陽縣公，邑千戶。
entries.en: He was promoted to Senior Acting Associate and created Duke of Wuyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Senior Acting Associate, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyang County with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 累遷右司衛上大夫。
entries.en: He rose through the ranks to Senior Grand Master of the Right Guard Bureau.
entries.literal: Through repeated promotion he became Senior Grand Master of the Right Guard Bureau.

entries.zh: 大象中，進爵邗國公，邑五千戶。
entries.en: In the Daxiang era he was promoted to Duke of Han with a fief of five thousand households.
entries.literal: In the Daxiang period he was advanced to Duke of Han State with a fief of five thousand households.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，雍州牧畢王賢謀作難，雄時為別駕，知其謀，以告高祖。
entries.en: While Yang Jian served as chancellor, Bi Wang Xian, Governor of Yong Province, plotted rebellion. Xiong, then serving as assistant administrator, discovered the plot and reported it to Yang Jian.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was chancellor, Bi Wang Xian the Governor of Yong Province plotted rebellion; Xiong was then an assistant administrator, learned of the plot, and reported it to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 賢伏誅，以功授柱國、雍州牧，仍領相府虞候。
entries.en: Xian was executed. For this service Xiong was made Pillar of State and Governor of Yong Province while continuing to command the chancellor's guard patrol.
entries.literal: Xian was executed after confessing guilt; for this merit Xiong was appointed Pillar of State and Governor of Yong Province, and still headed the chancellor's guard patrol.

entries.zh: 周宣帝葬，備諸王有變，令雄率六千騎送至陵所。
entries.en: At Emperor Xuan of Zhou's funeral, fearing the princes might cause trouble, the court ordered Xiong to escort the procession to the tomb with six thousand cavalry.
entries.literal: At the burial of Emperor Xuan of Zhou, fearing that the various princes might create trouble, he ordered Xiong to lead six thousand cavalry to escort the procession to the tomb site.

entries.zh: 進位上柱國。
entries.en: He was promoted to First Rank Pillar of State.
entries.literal: He was advanced to First Rank Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，除左衛將軍，兼宗正卿。
entries.en: When Yang Jian took the throne, Xiong was appointed Left Guard General and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
entries.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was made Left Guard General and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

entries.zh: 俄遷右衛大將軍，參預朝政。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and given a voice in state affairs.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and participated in court governance.

entries.zh: 進封廣平王，食邑五千戶，以邗公別封一子。
entries.en: He was created Prince of Guangping with a fief of five thousand households, and one son was separately given the title Duke of Han.
entries.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping with a fief of five thousand households; one of his sons was separately enfeoffed with the title of Duke of Han.

entries.zh: 雄請封弟士貴，朝廷許之。
entries.en: Xiong petitioned to have his younger brother Shigui enfeoffed, and the court agreed.
entries.literal: Xiong requested that his younger brother Shigui be enfeoffed; the court granted it.

entries.zh: 或奏高熲朋黨者，上詰雄於朝。
entries.en: When someone accused Gao Jiong of forming a faction, the emperor questioned Xiong about it at court.
entries.literal: When someone memorialized that Gao Jiong had formed a clique, the emperor interrogated Xiong in court.

entries.zh: 雄對曰：「臣忝衛宮闈，朝夕左右，若有朋附，豈容不知！
entries.en: Xiong replied, "I serve at the emperor's side day and night. If Gao Jiong had gathered a clique, I would surely know of it!
entries.literal: Xiong replied: "I am honored to guard the inner palace, at the emperor's side morning and night—if there were clique attachment, how could I not know it!

entries.zh: 至尊欽明睿哲，萬機親覽，熲用心平允，奉法而行。
entries.en: Your Majesty is wise and personally oversees every matter of state. Gao Jiong is fair-minded and acts strictly according to law.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is discerning, clear, and sagacious, personally reviewing all affairs of state; Jiong's mind is even and fair, and he acts in accordance with law.

entries.zh: 此乃愛憎之理，惟陛下察之。」
entries.en: This accusation springs from personal likes and dislikes. I ask Your Majesty to see through it."
entries.literal: This is simply the logic of favor and hatred—I ask Your Majesty to discern it."

entries.zh: 高祖深然其言。
entries.en: Emperor Wen found his answer entirely convincing.
entries.literal: Gaozu deeply approved of his words.

entries.zh: 雄時貴寵，冠絕一時，與高熲、虞慶則、蘇威稱為「四貴」。
entries.en: At the height of his career Xiong's favor eclipsed all rivals; together with Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and Su Wei he was known as one of the "Four Exalted Ones."
entries.literal: At the time Xiong's honor and favor surpassed all others of the age; together with Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and Su Wei he was called the "Four Nobles."

entries.zh: 雄弟達，字士達。
entries.en: Xiong's younger brother Da, courtesy name Shida.
entries.literal: Xiong's younger brother Da, styled Shida.

entries.zh: 少聰敏，有學行。
entries.en: Clever from youth, he was a man of learning and integrity.
entries.literal: From youth he was clever and keen, with learning and conduct.

entries.zh: 仕周，官至儀同、內史下大夫，遂甯縣男。
entries.en: Under the Northern Zhou he rose to Acting Associate and Junior Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and held the title Baron of Suining County.
entries.literal: Serving under Zhou, he reached the offices of Acting Associate and Junior Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and was Baron of Suining County.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，拜給事黃門侍郎，進爵為子。
entries.en: When Yang Jian took the throne, Da was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and promoted to viscount.
entries.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and advanced in rank to Viscount.

entries.zh: 時吐谷渾寇邊，詔上柱國元諧為元帥，達為司馬。
entries.en: When the Tuyuhun raided the frontier, Yuan Xie was appointed commander with Da as his chief of staff.
entries.literal: At the time the Tuyuhun raided the frontier; an edict appointed First Rank Pillar of State Yuan Xie as commander and Da as chief of staff.

entries.zh: 軍還、兼吏部侍郎，加開府。
entries.en: On the army's return he was additionally made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and granted the privilege of opening his own office.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was additionally made Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Personnel and granted Opening of an Office.

entries.zh: 歲餘，轉內史侍郎，出為鄯、鄭、趙三州刺史，俱有能名。
entries.en: A little over a year later he became Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, then served as governor of Shan, Zheng, and Zhao in succession, earning a reputation for competent administration in each.
entries.literal: After more than a year he transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and was sent out as governor of the three provinces of Shan, Zheng, and Zhao, all with reputations for capable administration.

entries.zh: 平陳之後，四海大同，上差品天下牧宰，達為第一，賜雜彩五百段，加以金帶，擢拜工部尚書，加位上開府。
entries.en: After the conquest of Chen and the unification of the realm, the emperor ranked every provincial governor in the land. Da placed first. He was rewarded with five hundred bales of colored silks and a gold belt, promoted to Director of the Ministry of Public Works, and granted the rank of Senior Opening of an Office.
entries.literal: After the pacification of Chen, when the realm under heaven was united, the emperor graded all the prefectural governors of the land; Da ranked first and was granted five hundred bales of mixed colored silks, additionally given a gold belt, promoted to Director of the Department of Public Works, and given the rank of Senior Opening of an Office.

entries.zh: 達為人弘厚，有局度。
entries.en: Da was openhearted and magnanimous, a man of broad vision and steady judgment.
entries.literal: Da as a man was magnanimous and generous, with capacity and breadth of vision.

entries.zh: 楊素每言曰：「有君子之貌，兼君子之心者，唯楊達耳。」
entries.en: Yang Su often said, "Among those who look the gentleman and are one in spirit, Yang Da is the only example I know."
entries.literal: Yang Su often said: "Among those who have both the appearance of a gentleman and the heart of a gentleman, there is only Yang Da."

entries.zh: 獻皇后及高祖山陵制度，達並參豫焉。
entries.en: Da played a part in planning the tomb arrangements for Empress Xian and Emperor Wen alike.
entries.literal: In the regulations for the tombs of Empress Xian and Gaozu, Da participated in all of them.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：高祖始遷周鼎，眾心未附，利建同姓，維城宗社，是以河間、觀德，咸啟山河。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: When Emperor Wen first seized the Mandate, loyalties were still unsettled. He enfeoffed men of the Yang clan to buttress the throne—thus the princes of Hejian and Guande were both granted domains spanning mountains and rivers.
entries.literal: The historiographers say: When Gaozu first moved the tripod of Zhou, hearts were not yet attached; enfeoffing those of the same surname to protect the altars of state was advantageous—therefore Hejian and Guande both opened territories across mountains and rivers.

entries.zh: 屬乃葭莩，地非寵逼，故高位厚秩，與時終始。
entries.en: Being only distant kin and holding no positions that threatened the throne, they enjoyed high rank and generous stipends from start to finish.
entries.literal: Their kinship was but as reed and rush roots; their domains were not positions of favor and pressure—therefore high rank and thick stipends lasted with the times from beginning to end.

entries.zh: 楊慶二三其德，志在苟生，變本宗如反掌，棄慈母如遺跡，及身而絕，宜其然矣。
entries.en: Yang Qing was inconstant in his loyalties and cared only to save his own skin—changing his clan as easily as turning his hand, abandoning his stepmother as if she were nothing. That his line ended with him was only to be expected.
entries.literal: Yang Qing wavered in his virtue twofold and threefold, his aim set on saving his own life—changing his original clan as easily as turning over the palm, abandoning his loving mother as if leaving no trace; that his line ended in his own person was fitting indeed.

entries.zh: 觀王位登臺袞，慶流後嗣，保茲寵祿，實仁厚之所致乎！
entries.en: Guande Prince Xiong rose to the highest honors, and his descendants inherited his rank and favor—is that not the reward of a generous and forbearing nature?
entries.literal: Guande's position reached the highest court rank; blessing flowed to his descendants who preserved these favors and stipends—was this not truly the effect of benevolence and generosity!

entries.zh: 自昏狂嗣位，多曆歲年，剝削生民，塗炭天下。
entries.en: Ever since that benighted tyrant took the throne, year after year he has stripped the people bare and plunged the land into misery.
entries.literal: Since the benighted and mad ruler succeeded to the throne, many years have passed, plundering the living people and scorching the realm.

entries.zh: 璿室瑤台之麗，未極驕奢；
entries.en: The marvels of his jade halls and azure towers scarcely exhaust his arrogance and excess;
entries.literal: The splendor of jade chambers and azure terraces has not yet reached the limit of arrogant extravagance;

entries.zh: 糟丘酒池之荒，非為淫亂。
entries.en: Nor are his meat hills and wine pools simply wanton indulgence—they mark something far worse.
entries.literal: The wastefulness of wine pools and meat hills is not merely for the sake of debauchery.

entries.zh: 今者共舉義旗，勘剪凶虐，八方同德，萬里俱來，莫不期入關以亡秦，爭渡河而滅紂。
entries.en: Today we have raised the banner of righteous rebellion to strike down a brutal regime. From every quarter men have rallied, arriving from a thousand miles away, each longing to sweep into Guanzhong as the armies did when they brought down Qin, or to cross the river and topple a tyrant as when Zhou fell to the Zhou founders.
entries.literal: Now we jointly raise the banner of righteousness to punish and cut down the cruel and tyrannical; the eight directions share one purpose, and men come from ten thousand li; none fail to aspire to enter the passes as Qin was destroyed, or to cross the river to annihilate Zhou as Shang was overthrown.

entries.zh: 東窮海、岱，南洎江、淮，凡厥遺人，承風慕義，唯滎陽一郡，王獨守迷。
entries.en: From the eastern seas and Mount Tai to the Yangtze and the Huai, every survivor who still breathes has taken up our cause—yet in all this, only Xingyang Commandery, and Your Highness alone, still clings to the doomed order.
entries.literal: East to the sea and Mount Tai, south to the Yangtze and Huai, all the surviving people catch the wind and admire the cause—only in Xingyang Commandery does Your Highness alone stubbornly hold to delusion.

entries.zh: 夫微子紂之元兄，族實為重，項伯籍之季父，戚乃非疏，然猶去朝歌而入周，背西楚而歸漢。
entries.en: Wei Zi was King Zhou of Shang's own elder brother—the tie of blood could scarcely have been closer; Xiang Bo was Xiang Ji of Western Chu's uncle—hardly a distant kinsman—yet both men left Chaoge to join King Wu of Zhou, and turned from Western Chu to serve the Han.
entries.literal: Wei Zi was King Zhou of Shang's elder brother by blood—the kinship was truly weighty; Xiang Bo was Xiang Ji the Overlord of Western Chu's uncle—the affinity was by no means distant—yet they still left Chaoge to enter Zhou and turned their backs on Western Chu to return to Han.

entries.zh: 豈不眷戀宗祊，留連骨肉，但識寶鼎之將移，知神器之先改。
entries.en: Did they not love their ancestral altars and feel the pull of kinship? They simply understood that the Mandate was already shifting, and that the throne would soon pass to another house.
entries.literal: Was it not that they cherished the ancestral altars and were bound to their flesh and blood? They simply recognized that the precious tripod was about to be transferred and knew that the divine vessel would change hands first.

entries.zh: 而王之先代，家住山東，本姓郭氏，乃非楊族。
entries.en: Your own ancestors came from the east, bore the surname Guo, and were never truly of the Yang line.
entries.literal: Moreover, Your Highness's forebears dwelt in Shandong; their original surname was Guo—they are not of the Yang clan at all.

entries.zh: 止為宿與隋朝先有勳舊，遂得預沾磐石，名在葭莩。
entries.en: Only because of old ties of service to the Sui did you come to be treated as one of the dynasty's closest and most trusted kin.
entries.literal: Merely because of longstanding meritorious ties with the Sui dynasty in former days, you were privileged to share in the solidity of bedrock and counted among the closest kin.

entries.zh: 婁敬之與漢高，殊非血胤，呂布之于董卓，良異天親，芝焚蕙歎，事不同此。
entries.en: Lou Jing stood with Emperor Gaozu of Han though they shared no blood; Lü Bu served Dong Zhuo though heaven had made them no kin. When one orchid withers the others may grieve, but your case is not like that.
entries.literal: Lou Jing and Emperor Gaozu of Han were utterly without blood relation; Lü Bu and Dong Zhuo were truly unlike natural kin—the orchid burns while the sweet flag sighs; this matter is not the same as those.

entries.zh: 又王之昏主，心若豺狼，仇忿同胞，有逾沉、閼，惟勇及諒，咸磬甸師，況及族類為非，何能自保！
entries.en: And consider your sovereign: benighted and wolf-hearted, more savage toward his own brothers than the worst villains of old. Princes Yong and Liang were wiped out to the last man—why would your branch of the family fare any better?
entries.literal: Moreover, Your Highness's sovereign is a benighted ruler whose heart is like a wolf or jackal; he treats his own brothers with enmity exceeding the parricides Chen and Que; only Yong and Liang met annihilation at the frontier—what fate awaits even your clan when guilt is imputed? How can you preserve yourself!

entries.zh: 為王計者，莫若舉城從義，開門送款，安若太山，高枕而臥，長守富貴，足為美談，乃至子孫，必有餘慶。
entries.en: If I may advise Your Highness, your best course is to surrender the city and join our cause—to open the gates and submit. You would be as secure as Mount Tai itself, sleeping at ease while your wealth and rank endure. That would be a tale worth telling, and your descendants would reap the reward.
entries.literal: For Your Highness's counsel, nothing is better than surrendering the city to join the righteous cause, opening the gates to offer allegiance—you would be secure as Mount Tai, sleeping with head on high pillow, long preserving wealth and honor, ample material for fine story, and even to your descendants there would surely be leftover blessing.

entries.zh: 今王世充屢被摧蹙，自救無聊，偷存晷漏，詎能支久？
entries.en: Wang Shichong is already battered on every side, barely able to save himself; he lives on borrowed time. How long can he last?
entries.literal: Now Wang Shichong has repeatedly been driven and pressed; he cannot save himself and lives on stolen moments—how can he hold out long?

entries.zh: 段達、韋津，東都自固，何暇圖人？
entries.en: Duan Da and Wei Jin are busy holding the Eastern Capital together—they have no time to think of anyone else.
entries.literal: Duan Da and Wei Jin in the Eastern Capital fortify themselves—what leisure have they to think of others?

entries.zh: 世充朝亡，達便夕滅。
entries.en: When Shichong falls in the morning, Duan Da will be gone by nightfall.
entries.literal: If Shichong dies in the morning, Da will perish by evening.

entries.zh: 又江都荒湎，流宕忘歸，內外崩離，人神怨憤。
entries.en: Meanwhile the emperor at Jiangdu gives himself over to dissipation and shows no sign of returning. Court and country are coming apart, and both men and gods are filled with fury.
entries.literal: Furthermore, at Jiangdu the emperor indulges in wild debauchery, drifting away and forgetting to return; within and without there is collapse and separation, and men and spirits alike seethe with resentment.

entries.zh: 上江米船，皆被抄截，士卒饑餒，半菽不充，事切析骸，義均煮弩。
entries.en: Grain ships heading upriver are seized before they arrive; the soldiers starve, unable even to fill half their bellies with beans. Men are already reduced to splitting the dead for meat—in spirit no different from boiling a bowstring for soup.
entries.literal: Rice ships coming upriver are all intercepted and seized; soldiers hunger and starve, with not even half a portion of beans to fill them—the situation presses toward splitting bones for food; righteousness demands boiling bowstrings for broth.

entries.zh: 舉烽火于驪山，諸侯莫至；
entries.en: Beacon fires blaze on Mount Li, yet no allies come to the rescue—
entries.literal: Beacon fires were raised on Mount Li, yet no feudal lords came;

entries.zh: 浮膠船于漢水，還日未期。
entries.en: while the emperor amuses himself with his glued boats on the Han, with no return in sight.
entries.literal: while glue boats float on the Han River—the day of return is not yet set.

entries.zh: 王獨守孤城，絕援千里，餱糧之計，僅有月餘，敝卒之多，才盈數百，有何恃賴，欲相拒抗！
entries.en: Your Highness holds a lone city a thousand li from any help. Your dry rations will last barely a month; your weary troops number only a few hundred at best. What do you have to resist us with?
entries.literal: Your Highness alone holds a solitary city, with aid cut off a thousand li away; stores of dry provisions will last barely a month or more; worn-out soldiers barely exceed a few hundred—upon what do you rely, that you wish to resist us!

entries.zh: 求枯魚於市肆，即事非虛；
entries.en: To go to the market for dried fish is no mere figure of speech—
entries.literal: To seek dried fish in the marketplace—the matter is no empty figure;

entries.zh: 因歸雁以運糧，竟知何日。
entries.en: and to hope wild geese might bring your grain, who can say when that would be?
entries.literal: to rely on returning wild geese to transport grain—who knows what day that might be?

entries.zh: 然城中豪傑，王之腹心，思殺長吏，將為內啟。
entries.en: And within your walls are men of spirit among your closest followers, already plotting to slay their superiors and open the gates from inside.
entries.literal: Yet within the city are bold heroes, Your Highness's trusted confidants, who think of killing the chief official and will open from within.

entries.zh: 正恐禍生匕首，釁發蕭牆，空以七尺之軀，懸賞千金之購，可為寒心，可為酸鼻者也。
entries.en: I fear disaster may come from a dagger at close hand, or rebellion erupt behind your own walls—you would offer up your life while a price of a thousand in gold is put on your head. The thought makes one shudder; it turns the stomach.
entries.literal: One truly fears disaster arising from a dagger, trouble bursting from within the palace walls—you would in vain offer your seven-foot frame with a thousand in gold placed on your head; it is enough to chill the heart and sour the nose.

entries.zh: 幸能三思，自求多福。
entries.en: I urge you to weigh this carefully and choose what will bring you fortune.
entries.literal: I hope you will think thrice and seek your own greater blessing.

entries.zh: 煬帝嗣位，轉納言，仍領營東都副監，帝甚信重之。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Da became Palace Reporter and served concurrently as deputy supervisor of the Eastern Capital project. The emperor trusted and relied on him deeply.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Palace Reporter, still concurrently serving as Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Eastern Capital; the emperor greatly trusted and valued him.

entries.zh: 遼東之役，領右武衛將軍，進位左光祿大夫，卒于師，時年六十二。
entries.en: During the Liaodong campaign he served as General of the Right Martial Guard and was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. He died in camp at the age of sixty-two.
entries.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he commanded as General of the Right Martial Guard, was advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died in the army; at the time he was sixty-two.

entries.zh: 帝嘆惜者久之，贈吏部尚書、始安侯。
entries.en: The emperor mourned him at length and posthumously honored him as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Marquis of Shi'an.
entries.literal: The emperor sighed in regret for a long time and posthumously granted him Director of the Department of State Affairs Personnel and Marquis of Shi'an.

entries.zh: 諡曰恭。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous name Respectful (Gong).
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Gong ("Respectful").

entries.zh: 贈物三百五十段。
entries.en: Three hundred fifty bales of goods were granted in his honor.
entries.literal: Three hundred fifty bales of goods were granted in tribute.

entries.zh: 隋書卷四十三列傳第八
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume 43, Biographies 8
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 43, Biographies, Number Eight

entries.zh: 滕穆王瓚，字恆生，一名慧，高祖母弟也。
entries.en: Prince Teng the Mu, Zan, styled Hengsheng and also known as Hui, was a younger brother of Emperor Gaozu by the same mother.
entries.literal: Teng the Mu Prince Zan, styled Hengsheng, also named Hui, was Gaozu's younger brother by the same mother.

entries.zh: 周世以太祖軍功封竟陵郡公，尚武帝妹順陽公主，自右中侍上士遷禦伯中大夫。
entries.en: During the Northern Zhou, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling for the Grand Duke's military service, married Emperor Wu's younger sister Princess Shunyang, and advanced from Right Palace Attendant to Imperial Chamberlain.
entries.literal: In the Zhou era, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling Commandery, married Emperor Wu's younger sister Princess Shunyang, and rose from Right Palace Attendant Superior Gentleman to Imperial Chamberlain Grand Master.

entries.zh: 保定四年，改為納言，授儀同。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Baoding (564), he was appointed Director of Discourse and granted the rank of Palace Attendant Companion.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was changed to Director of Discourse and granted Palace Attendant Companion.

entries.zh: 瓚貴公子，又尚公主，美姿儀，好書愛士，甚有令名於當世，時人號曰楊三郎。
entries.en: As a prince of the blood who had married an imperial princess, Zan was striking in appearance, devoted to books, and generous to men of talent. He enjoyed great renown in his day, and contemporaries called him Yang the Third.
entries.literal: Zan was a nobleman's son and had also married a princess; handsome in bearing, fond of books and cherishing scholars, he had a very fine reputation in his age, and people of the time called him Yang the Third Lord.

entries.zh: 武帝甚親愛之。
entries.en: Emperor Wu held him in exceptional affection.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu was very intimate with and fond of him.

entries.zh: 平齊之役，諸王鹹從，留瓚居守，帝謂之曰：「六府事殷，一以相付。
entries.en: When the campaign to conquer Qi began, all the princes went with the army, but Zan was left behind to hold the capital. The emperor told him, "The Six Offices are overwhelmed with business; I leave everything in your hands.
entries.literal: In the campaign to pacify Qi, all the princes followed along; Zan was left to remain and guard, and the Emperor said to him: 'The Six Offices' affairs are pressing—I entrust them all to you.

entries.zh: 朕將遂事東方，無西顧之憂矣。」
entries.en: I am going east to finish the campaign, and I shall have no need to glance back over my shoulder toward the west."
entries.literal: I shall complete the affair in the east and have no worry of looking back to the west.'

entries.zh: 其見親信如此。
entries.en: Such was the depth of trust placed in him.
entries.literal: Thus was he seen to be trusted and favored.

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，遷吏部中大夫，加上儀同。
entries.en: After Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Zan was promoted to Grand Master in the Ministry of Personnel and granted the rank of Senior Palace Attendant Companion.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was transferred to Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel and given Senior Palace Attendant Companion.

entries.zh: 未幾，帝崩，高祖入禁中，將總朝政，令廢太子勇召之，欲有計議。
entries.en: Before long the emperor died. Gaozu entered the inner palace to assume control of the government, summoned the deposed Crown Prince Yong, and intended to consult with him on strategy.
entries.literal: Before long the Emperor died; Gaozu entered the inner palace, was about to take overall control of court affairs, ordered the deposed Crown Prince Yong summoned, and wished to have plans discussed.

entries.zh: 瓚素與高祖不協，聞召不從，曰：「作隋國公恐不能保，何乃更為族滅事邪？」
entries.en: Zan had long been on bad terms with Gaozu. When he heard the summons, he refused to come and said, "Even as Duke of Sui you may not be able to keep your position—why press on toward something that will destroy the whole clan?"
entries.literal: Zan had long been at odds with Gaozu; hearing the summons he did not obey and said: 'Being made Duke of Sui probably cannot be preserved—why then go further and do a thing that exterminates the clan?'

entries.zh: 高祖作相，遷大將軍。
entries.en: After Gaozu became chancellor, Zan was appointed Grand General.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, he was transferred to Grand General.

entries.zh: 尋拜大宗伯，典修禮律。
entries.en: He was soon made Grand Director of Ritual and put in charge of revising the ritual and penal codes.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Director of Ritual and supervised the compilation of ritual and penal codes.

entries.zh: 進位上柱國、邵國公。
entries.en: He was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Shao.
entries.literal: He advanced in rank to Senior Pillar of State and Duke of Shao.

entries.zh: 瓚見高祖執政，群情未一，恐為家禍，陰有圖高祖之計，高祖每優容之。
entries.en: Seeing Gaozu in power while opinion in the realm remained divided, Zan feared disaster for his own house and secretly plotted against him, yet Gaozu repeatedly showed him leniency.
entries.literal: Zan saw Gaozu holding power while popular sentiment was not united, feared a family disaster, and secretly had plans to plot against Gaozu; Gaozu each time treated him with forbearance.

entries.zh: 及受禪，立為滕王。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Zan was created Prince of Teng.
entries.literal: When he received the abdication, he was established as Prince of Teng.

entries.zh: 後拜雍州牧。
entries.en: He was later appointed Governor of Yong Province.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 上數與同坐，呼為阿三。
entries.en: The emperor often sat with him as an equal and called him "Little Third."
entries.literal: The Emperor several times sat with him together and called him Little Third.

entries.zh: 後坐事去牧，以王就第。
entries.en: Later he was removed from office for an offense and returned to his princely residence.
entries.literal: Later, because of an affair, he was removed from the governorship and, as a prince, retired to his mansion.

entries.zh: 綸字斌籀，性弘厚，美姿容，頗解鐘律。
entries.en: Lun, styled Binzhou, was openhearted and handsome and had considerable knowledge of music theory.
entries.literal: Lun, styled Binzhou, was by nature magnanimous and generous, handsome in appearance, and rather understood bells and pitch pipes.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，封邵國公，邑八千戶。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Lun was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao with a fief of eight thousand households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao with a fief of eight thousand households.

entries.zh: 明年，拜邵州刺史。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed Governor of Shao Prefecture.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed Governor of Shao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 晉王廣納妃于梁，詔綸致禮焉，甚為梁人所敬。
entries.en: When Prince Jin Guang took a bride from Liang, Lun was ordered to convey the betrothal gifts on his behalf and won great respect among the Liang court.
entries.literal: Prince of Jin Guang took a consort in Liang; an edict ordered Lun to convey the ceremonial gifts, and he was greatly respected by the people of Liang.

entries.zh: 綸以穆王之故，當高祖之世，每不自安。
entries.en: Because of his father's disgrace as Prince Teng the Mu, Lun never felt secure throughout Gaozu's reign.
entries.literal: Because of the Mu Prince, during Gaozu's reign Lun was each time ill at ease.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，尤被猜忌。
entries.en: After Emperor Yang came to the throne, suspicion against him deepened still further.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he was especially subjected to suspicion.

entries.zh: 綸憂懼不知所為，呼術者王琛而問之。
entries.en: Tormented by fear and uncertainty, Lun summoned the diviner Wang Chen to consult him.
entries.literal: Lun, anxious and fearful, did not know what to do; he summoned the diviner Wang Chen and questioned him.

entries.zh: 琛答曰：「王相祿不凡。」
entries.en: Chen replied, "Your Highness's countenance and fortune are no ordinary matter."
entries.literal: Chen answered: 'Your princely physiognomy and emolument are not ordinary.'

entries.zh: 乃因曰：「滕即騰也，此字足為善應。」
entries.en: He went on, "The character for Teng also means to soar—surely an auspicious sign for you."
entries.literal: He then took occasion to say: 'Teng is the same as soaring; this character is sufficient as a good omen.'

entries.zh: 有沙門惠恩、崛多等，頗解占候，綸每與交通，常令此三人為度星法。
entries.en: There were also the monks Hui'en and Jueduo, who were skilled in divination. Lun associated with them regularly and often had the three of them practice astrological prognostication.
entries.literal: There were monks Hui'en, Jueduo, and others who were rather skilled in observing omens; Lun frequently associated with them and often had these three men perform star-measuring methods.

entries.zh: 有人告綸怨望咒詛，帝命黃門侍郎王弘窮治之。
entries.en: Someone reported that Lun was nursing resentment and practicing curses. The emperor ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong to investigate the case thoroughly.
entries.literal: Someone reported that Lun harbored resentment and cursed; the Emperor ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong to investigate it to the end.

entries.zh: 弘見帝方怒，遂希旨奏綸厭蠱惡逆，坐當死。
entries.en: Seeing the emperor's anger, Hong shaped his findings to please him and reported that Lun had practiced malign sorcery and treason, crimes punishable by death.
entries.literal: Hong saw that the Emperor was just then angry and accordingly, to please the intent, memorialized that Lun had practiced malign sorcery and wicked rebellion and, by the statute, deserved death.

entries.zh: 帝令公卿議其事，司徒楊素等曰：「綸希冀國災，以為身幸。
entries.en: The emperor ordered the high ministers to deliberate. Minister of Education Yang Su and others said, "Lun has been praying for calamity to befall the state, treating national disaster as his personal opportunity.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered the nobles and ministers to discuss the matter; Minister of Education Yang Su and others said: 'Lun hoped for national disaster as his own personal good fortune.

entries.zh: 原其懷惡之由，積自家世。
entries.en: The roots of his malice lie deep in his family's history.
entries.literal: Tracing the origin of his harboring of evil, it accumulated from his own family for generations.

entries.zh: 惟皇運之始，四海同心，在於孔懷，彌須協力。
entries.en: At the dawn of a new dynasty, when the realm should stand united, those bound by the closest ties of kinship ought all the more to lend their strength together.
entries.literal: Only at the beginning of the imperial fortune, when the four seas were of one heart, among those of closest kin all the more must there be joined effort.

entries.zh: 其先乃離阻大謀，棄同即異，父悖于前，子逆於後，非直覬覦朝廷，便是圖危社稷。
entries.en: His forebears obstructed great state designs, forsaking unity for division; the father rebelled in one generation and the son in the next. This is not mere ambition for the throne—it is a plot to bring down the dynasty itself.
entries.literal: His forebears then obstructed great plans, abandoned unity and took to difference; the father was disloyal before, the son rebellious after—not merely coveting the court, but indeed plotting to endanger the altars of state.

entries.zh: 為惡有狀，其罪莫大，刑茲無赦，抑有舊章，請依前律。」
entries.en: The evidence of his crimes is clear, and no offense could be graver. The law allows no mercy here. We ask that he be sentenced under the established statutes."
entries.literal: Doing evil has clear evidence; his crime is the greatest; punishment here admits no pardon—yet there are also old statutes; we request execution according to the prior code.'

entries.zh: 帝以公族不忍，除名為民，徙始安。
entries.en: Unable to bring himself to execute a kinsman, the emperor struck Lun from the rolls of nobility, reduced him to commoner status, and exiled him to Shi'an.
entries.literal: The Emperor, unable to bear this against a member of the imperial clan, struck his name from the rolls and made him a commoner, banishing him to Shi'an.

entries.zh: 諸弟散徙邊郡。
entries.en: His younger brothers were likewise dispersed to remote border commanderies.
entries.literal: His younger brothers were scattered and banished to frontier commanderies.

entries.zh: 大業七年，親征遼東，綸欲上表，請從軍自效，為郡司所遏。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Daye (611), when the emperor campaigned in person against Liaodong, Lun tried to submit a memorial offering to join the army and prove his loyalty, but the local officials prevented it.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Daye, when the Emperor personally campaigned in Liaodong, Lun wished to submit a memorial requesting to follow the army and offer his service, but was blocked by the prefectural officials.

entries.zh: 未幾，複徙硃崖。
entries.en: Before long he was transferred again, this time to Zhuya.
entries.literal: Before long he was again banished to Zhuya.

entries.zh: 及天下大亂，為賊林仕弘所逼，攜妻子竄于儋耳。
entries.en: When the empire collapsed into chaos, he was harried by the rebel Lin Shihong and fled with his wife and children to Dan'er.
entries.literal: When the empire fell into great disorder, he was pressed by the bandit Lin Shihong, took wife and children, and fled to Dan'er.

entries.zh: 後歸大唐，為懷化縣公。
entries.en: He later submitted to the Tang and was enfeoffed as Duke of Huaihua County.
entries.literal: Later he returned to Great Tang and was made Duke of Huaihua County.

entries.zh: 瓚妃宇文氏，先時與獨孤皇后不平，及此鬱鬱不得志，陰有咒詛。
entries.en: Zan's consort, Lady Yuwen, had long been at odds with Empress Dugu. Now bitter and thwarted, she secretly practiced curses against the empress.
entries.literal: Zan's consort, of the Yuwen clan, had earlier been on bad terms with Empress Dugu; at this time, depressed and without achieving her aims, she secretly had curses and imprecations.

entries.zh: 上命瓚出之，瓚不忍離絕，固請。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Zan to divorce her, but Zan could not bear to cast her off and pleaded repeatedly to keep her.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Zan to send her out; Zan could not bear to part from her and firmly pleaded.

entries.zh: 上不得已，從之，宇文氏竟除屬籍。
entries.en: The emperor reluctantly agreed, but Lady Yuwen was ultimately struck from the imperial clan rolls.
entries.literal: The Emperor, having no alternative, followed this; the Yuwen clan was in the end removed from the register of kin.

entries.zh: 瓚由是忤旨，恩禮更薄。
entries.en: From that point Zan fell out of favor, and the emperor's kindness toward him grew still colder.
entries.literal: Zan thereby went against the imperial will, and favor and ceremony grew still thinner.

entries.zh: 開皇十一年，從幸栗園，暴薨，時年四十二。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang (591), while accompanying the emperor to Chestnut Garden, he died suddenly at the age of forty-two.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang, accompanying the emperor on a visit to Chestnut Garden, he died suddenly; he was forty-two.

entries.zh: 人皆言其遇鴆以斃。
entries.en: Everyone said he had been killed by poisoned wine.
entries.literal: Everyone said that he encountered poisoned wine and died thereby.

entries.zh: 子綸嗣。
entries.en: His son Lun succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Lun succeeded.

entries.zh: 衛昭王爽，字師仁，小字明達，高祖異母弟也。
entries.en: Prince of Wei the Illustrious, Shuang, styled Shiren and known in youth as Mingda, was Gaozu's younger half-brother.
entries.literal: Wei the Illustrious Prince Shuang, styled Shiren, childhood name Mingda, was Gaozu's younger brother by a different mother.

entries.zh: 周世，在繈褓中，以太祖軍功，封同安郡公。
entries.en: During the Zhou, while still an infant, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tong'an for the Grand Duke's military service.
entries.literal: In the Zhou era, while still in swaddling clothes, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tong'an Commandery.

entries.zh: 六歲而太祖崩，為獻皇后之所鞠養，由是高祖于諸弟中特寵愛之。
entries.en: When he was six the Grand Duke died, and Empress Xian raised him herself. For this reason Gaozu cherished him above all his other brothers.
entries.literal: At six years the Grand Duke died; he was reared and nourished by Empress Xian, and thereby Gaozu among all his younger brothers especially favored and loved him.

entries.zh: 十七為內史上士。
entries.en: At seventeen he was appointed Superior Gentleman in the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: At seventeen he became Palace Secretariat Superior Gentleman.

entries.zh: 高祖執政，拜大將軍、秦州總管。
entries.en: When Gaozu assumed control of the government, Shuang was appointed Grand General and Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province.
entries.literal: When Gaozu held power, he was appointed Grand General and Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province.

entries.zh: 未之官，轉授蒲州刺史，進位柱國。
entries.en: He never took up the Qin post and was instead appointed Governor of Pu Prefecture and promoted to Pillar of State.
entries.literal: He did not take up the post; he was transferred and appointed Governor of Pu Prefecture and advanced to Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 及受禪，立為衛王。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Shuang was created Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: When the abdication was received, he was established as Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 尋遷雍州牧，領左右將軍。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Governor of Yong Province and placed in command of the Left and Right Guards.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province and concurrently led the Left and Right Generals.

entries.zh: 俄遷右領軍大將軍，權領并州總管。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was made Grand General of the Right Army Guard and given provisional authority as Commander-in-Chief of Bing Province.
entries.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Army Guard and provisionally commanded Bing Province as Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 歲餘，進位上柱國，轉涼州總管。
entries.en: A year later he was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Liang Province.
entries.literal: After more than a year he advanced to Senior Pillar of State and was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Liang Province.

entries.zh: 爽美風儀，有器局，治甚有聲。
entries.en: Shuang was distinguished in bearing, possessed breadth of vision, and governed with great renown.
entries.literal: Shuang was handsome in bearing and had capacity and vision; his governance had a very fine reputation.

entries.zh: 蔡王智積，高祖弟整之子也。
entries.en: Prince of Cai Zhiji was the son of Gaozu's younger brother Zheng.
entries.literal: Prince of Cai Zhiji was the son of Gaozu's younger brother Zheng.

entries.zh: 整周明帝時，以太祖軍功，賜爵陳留郡公。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Ming of Zhou, Zheng was enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu for the Grand Duke's military service.
entries.literal: Zheng, in Emperor Ming's time of Zhou, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements, was granted the title Duke of Chenliu Commandery.

entries.zh: 尋授開府、車騎大將軍。
entries.en: He was soon appointed to the Grand Preceptorate and made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Preceptorate and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 從武帝平齊，至并州，力戰而死。
entries.en: He followed Emperor Wu in the conquest of Qi and died fighting fiercely at Bingzhou.
entries.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he reached Bing Province and died fighting with all his strength.

entries.zh: 及高祖作相，贈柱國、大司徒、冀定瀛相懷衛趙貝八州刺史。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chancellor, Zheng was posthumously honored as Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Education and as Governor of Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Huai, Wei, Zhao, and Bei.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, he was posthumously given Pillar of State, Grand Minister of Education, and Governor of the eight provinces Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Huai, Wei, Zhao, and Bei.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，追封蔡王，諡曰景。
entries.en: After Gaozu took the throne, Zheng was posthumously created Prince of Cai with the posthumous name Jing.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai with posthumous name Jing.

entries.zh: 以智積襲焉。
entries.en: Zhiji succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: Zhiji succeeded to this.

entries.zh: 又封其弟智明為高陽郡公，智才為開封縣公。
entries.en: His younger brothers Zhiming and Zhicai were also enfeoffed, as Duke of Gaoyang and Duke of Kaifeng respectively.
entries.literal: His younger brothers Zhiming and Zhicai were also enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang Commandery and Duke of Kaifeng County respectively.

entries.zh: 尋拜智積為開府儀同三司，授同州刺史，儀衛資送甚盛。
entries.en: Zhiji was soon appointed Grand Preceptorate with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and made Governor of Tong Prefecture, with a splendid escort and lavish provisions for his journey.
entries.literal: Soon Zhiji was appointed Grand Preceptorate with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and given the post of Governor of Tong Prefecture; ceremonial guards and supplies sent forth were very lavish.

entries.zh: 頃之，以修謹聞，高祖善之。
entries.en: Before long his prudent and dutiful conduct won notice, and Gaozu was pleased with him.
entries.literal: Before long, because of his cultivated carefulness he became known, and Gaozu approved of him.

entries.zh: 在州未嘗嬉戲遊獵，聽政之暇，端坐讀書，門無私謁。
entries.en: As governor he never indulged in games or hunting. In the intervals between hearing cases he sat upright with a book, and no private visitors came to his gate.
entries.literal: In the prefecture he never played games or went hunting; in the leisure between hearing cases he sat upright reading books, and at his gate there were no private callers.

entries.zh: 有侍讀公孫尚儀，山東儒士，府佐楊君英、蕭德言，並有文學，時延於座，所設唯餅果，酒才三酌。
entries.en: His Reader-in-Waiting Gongsun Shangyi was a scholar from Shandong, and his aides Yang Junying and Xiao Deyan were men of letters. He would invite them to join him from time to time, but served only cakes and fruit, with no more than three rounds of wine.
entries.literal: There were Reader-in-Waiting Gongsun Shangyi, a Shandong scholar, and prefectural aides Yang Junying and Xiao Deyan, all possessed of literary learning; he would from time to time invite them to his seat, and what was set out was only cakes and fruit, with wine no more than three rounds.

entries.zh: 家有女妓，唯年節嘉慶，奏於太妃之前，其簡靜如此。
entries.en: He kept female musicians in his household, but they performed only at festivals and celebrations, and then only before the Princess Dowager. Such was the austerity of his ways.
entries.literal: His household had female performers, but only at New Year festivals and joyous celebrations would they perform before the Princess Dowager—such was his simplicity and quietness.

entries.zh: 昔高祖龍潛時，景王與高祖不睦，其太妃尉氏又與獨孤皇后不相諧，以是智積常懷危懼，每自貶損。
entries.en: In earlier days, when Gaozu was still rising to power, Prince Jing had been on bad terms with him, and Prince Jing's consort of the Yu clan had clashed with Empress Dugu. For this reason Zhiji lived in constant fear and continually humbled himself.
entries.literal: In former times, when Gaozu was still in obscurity, Prince Jing was on bad terms with Gaozu, and his Princess Dowager of the Yu clan was also not in harmony with Empress Dugu; for this reason Zhiji constantly harbored fear and danger and each time humbled himself.

entries.zh: 高祖知其若是，亦哀憐之。
entries.en: Gaozu understood his situation and pitied him.
entries.literal: Gaozu knew that he was thus and also pitied him.

entries.zh: 人或勸智積治產業者，智積曰：「昔平原露朽財帛，苦其多也。
entries.en: When someone urged Zhiji to build up his estates, he said, "Long ago the Prince of Pingyuan displayed his rotting stores of silk and gold, lamenting that he had too much.
entries.literal: Some urged Zhiji to manage estates and property; Zhiji said: 'In former times Pingyuan exposed rotting wealth and silk, vexed that there was so much.

entries.zh: 吾幸無可露，何更營乎？」
entries.en: I am fortunate to have nothing worth displaying—why should I accumulate more?"
entries.literal: I am fortunate to have nothing to expose—why then go further and manage?'

entries.zh: 有五男，止教讀《論語》、《孝經》而已，亦不令交通賓客。
entries.en: He had five sons and taught them only the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety, and would not let them cultivate connections with guests.
entries.literal: He had five sons and taught them only to read the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety, and also did not allow them to associate with guests.

entries.zh: 或問其故，智積答曰：「卿非知我者。」
entries.en: When someone asked why, Zhiji replied, "You do not understand me at all."
entries.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zhiji answered: 'You are not one who knows me.'

entries.zh: 其意恐兒子有才能，以致禍也。
entries.en: His fear was that talented sons would bring disaster upon the family.
entries.literal: His meaning was that he feared his sons might have talent and thereby bring disaster.

entries.zh: 開皇二十年，征還京第，無他職任，闔門自守，非朝覲不出。
entries.en: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang he was recalled to the capital and given no further office. He kept his household closed and did not leave home except for required court audiences.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang he was summoned back to his capital mansion, held no other office, kept his household closed and guarded, and did not go out except for court audiences.

entries.zh: 十二年，從駕江都，寢疾。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu and fell ill.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the imperial carriage to Jiangdu and took to his bed with illness.

entries.zh: 帝時疏薄骨肉，智積每不自安，及遇患，不呼醫。
entries.en: The emperor had grown cold toward his kinsmen, and Zhiji had long lived in anxiety. When he fell ill, he did not call for a physician.
entries.literal: The Emperor at that time was distant and thin toward his kin; Zhiji was each time ill at ease, and when he encountered illness he did not summon physicians.

entries.zh: 臨終，謂所親曰：「吾今日始知得保首領沒于地矣。」
entries.en: On his deathbed he told those close to him, "Only today do I know that I may keep my head and be laid in the earth in peace."
entries.literal: At the end, he said to those close to him: 'Today I finally know that I can preserve my head and be buried in the earth.'

entries.zh: 時人哀之。
entries.en: Those who heard it were moved to pity.
entries.literal: People of the time pitied him.

entries.zh: 有子道玄。
entries.en: He left a son named Daoxuan.
entries.literal: He had a son Daoxuan.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：周建懿親，漢開磐石，內以敦睦九族，外以輯寧億兆，深根固本，崇獎王室。
entries.en: The historiographer says: Zhou enfeoffed worthy kinsmen and Han created bedrock princes—inwardly to bind the nine clans in harmony, outwardly to secure the realm's countless people, planting deep roots and strengthening the foundation while honoring the royal house.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Zhou established worthy kinsmen, Han enfeoffed bedrock princes; inwardly to foster harmony among the nine clans, outwardly to bring peace to the hundred million subjects, planting deep roots and strengthening the foundation, honoring and encouraging the royal house.

entries.zh: 安則有以同其樂，衰則有以恤其危，所由來久矣。
entries.en: In prosperity they could share in its joys; in decline they could be sheltered from its perils. This has been so from ancient times.
entries.literal: In security there was means to share their joy; in decline there was means to relieve their peril—the origin of this is long.

entries.zh: 魏、晉以下，多失厥中，不遵王度，各徇所私。
entries.en: From Wei and Jin onward, many lost the proper balance, ignored royal standards, and each pursued private ends.
entries.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, many lost the proper mean, did not follow royal standards, and each pursued private ends.

entries.zh: 抑之則勢齊於匹夫，抗之則權侔于萬乘，矯枉過正，非一時也。
entries.en: When suppressed their power equaled that of commoners; when they resisted their authority rivaled that of the sovereign—overcorrecting the past has not been a problem of one age alone.
entries.literal: When repressed their power equaled that of commoners; when they resisted their authority matched that of ten thousand chariots—overcorrecting past wrongs has not been a matter of one time.

entries.zh: 得失詳乎前史，不復究而論焉。
entries.en: The gains and losses are set out in earlier histories; I shall not pursue the matter further here.
entries.literal: Gains and losses are detailed in former histories; I shall not pursue and discuss them further.

entries.zh: 高祖昆弟之恩，素非篤睦，閨房之隙，又不相容。
entries.en: Gaozu's ties with his brothers were never warm, and private household quarrels likewise could not be tolerated.
entries.literal: Gaozu's bond with his brothers was never deeply affectionate; private household quarrels likewise could not be endured.

entries.zh: 至於二世承基，其弊愈甚。
entries.en: When the second generation inherited the throne, the maladies grew still worse.
entries.literal: As for the second generation inheriting the foundation, its maladies grew still worse.

entries.zh: 是以滕穆暴薨，人皆竊議；
entries.en: Thus when Prince Teng the Mu died suddenly, everyone whispered in private;
entries.literal: Thus when Teng the Mu died suddenly, everyone whispered in private speculation;

entries.zh: 蔡王將沒，自以為幸。
entries.en: when Prince of Cai was about to die, he considered himself fortunate.
entries.literal: when Prince of Cai was about to die, he thought himself fortunate.

entries.zh: 唯衛王養於獻後，故任遇特隆，而諸子遷流，莫知死所，悲夫！
entries.en: Only Prince of Wei, raised by Empress Xian, therefore received exceptional favor—yet the princes were exiled and scattered, and no one knew where they perished. How tragic!
entries.literal: Only Wei the Prince, reared by Empress Xian, therefore received exceptional appointment and favor—yet the sons were banished and dispersed, and no one knew where they died. Alas!

entries.zh: 其錫以茅土，稱為磐石，行無甲兵之衛，居與氓隸為伍。
entries.en: Though granted feudal domains and called bedrock princes, they went without armed escort and lived among common bondsmen.
entries.literal: Though bestowed feudal domains and called bedrock princes, they traveled without armed guards and lived among common bondsmen.

entries.zh: 外內無虞，顛危不暇，時逢多難，將何望焉！
entries.en: With no security within or without, they had no respite before ruin; in an age of many calamities, what could they hope for!
entries.literal: With no security within or without, they had no leisure before collapse; meeting many hardships in their age—what could they hope for!

entries.zh: 道悼王靜，字賢籀，滕穆王瓚之子也。
entries.en: Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing, styled Xianzhou, was a son of Prince Teng the Mu, Zan.
entries.literal: Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing, styled Xianzhou, was the son of Teng the Mu Prince Zan.

entries.zh: 出繼叔父嵩。
entries.en: He was given in adoption to succeed his uncle Song.
entries.literal: He went out to succeed his paternal uncle Song.

entries.zh: 嵩在周代，以太祖軍功，賜爵興城公，早卒。
entries.en: During the Zhou, Song had been granted the title Duke of Xingcheng for the Grand Duke's military service and died young.
entries.literal: Song, in the Zhou era, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements, was granted the title Duke of Xingcheng and died early.

entries.zh: 高祖踐位，追封道王，諡曰宣。
entries.en: After Gaozu took the throne, Song was posthumously created Prince of Dao with the posthumous name Xuan.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dao with posthumous name Xuan.

entries.zh: 以靜襲焉。
entries.en: Jing succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: Jing succeeded to this.

entries.zh: 卒，無子，國除。
entries.en: He died without heirs, and the princedom was abolished.
entries.literal: He died without sons, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 其年，以爽為行軍元帥，步騎七萬以備胡。
entries.en: That year Shuang was made campaign commander-in-chief with seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to guard against the northern peoples.
entries.literal: That year, with Shuang as campaign commander-in-chief, seventy thousand foot and horse were sent to guard against the Hu.

entries.zh: 出平涼，無虜而還。
entries.en: He marched out from Pingliang, found no enemy, and returned.
entries.literal: He went out from Pingliang; there were no barbarians and he returned.

entries.zh: 明年，大舉北伐，又為元帥。
entries.en: The following year, on a major northern campaign, he again served as commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: The next year, on a great northern expedition, he again served as commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 河間王弘、豆盧勣、竇榮定、高熲、虞慶則等分道而進，俱受爽節度。
entries.en: Prince of Hejian Hong, Doulu Ji, Dou Rongding, Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and others advanced on separate routes, all under Shuang's command.
entries.literal: Prince of Hejian Hong, Doulu Ji, Dou Rongding, Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and others advanced by separate routes, all receiving Shuang's command and control.

entries.zh: 爽親率李充節等四將出朔州，遇沙缽略可汗于白道，接戰，大破之，虜獲千餘人，驅馬牛羊巨萬。
entries.en: Shuang personally led Li Chongjie and three other generals out of Shuozhou, met Qaghan Shabolüe at White Road, and routed him decisively. They took more than a thousand prisoners and drove off tens of thousands of horses, cattle, and sheep.
entries.literal: Shuang personally led Li Chongjie and four other generals out from Shuozhou, encountered Shabolüe Qaghan on White Road, joined battle, and routed him greatly; captives numbered more than a thousand, and horses, cattle, and sheep driven off were in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 沙缽略可汗中重創而遁。
entries.en: Qaghan Shabolüe himself was gravely wounded and fled.
entries.literal: Shabolüe Qaghan was struck with a grave wound and fled.

entries.zh: 高祖大悅，賜爽真食梁安縣千戶。
entries.en: Gaozu was delighted and granted Shuang a permanent fief of one thousand households in Liang'an County.
entries.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and granted Shuang a true fief of one thousand households in Liang'an County.

entries.zh: 六年，複為元帥，步騎十五萬，出合川。
entries.en: In the sixth year he again served as commander-in-chief at the head of one hundred fifty thousand troops, marching out from Hechuan.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he again served as commander-in-chief with one hundred fifty thousand foot and horse, going out from Hechuan.

entries.zh: 突厥遁逃而返。
entries.en: The Turks fled before him, and he returned without a major engagement.
entries.literal: The Turks fled in escape and he returned.

entries.zh: 明年，征為納言。
entries.en: The following year he was recalled to court as Director of Discourse.
entries.literal: The next year he was summoned to serve as Director of Discourse.

entries.zh: 高祖甚重之。
entries.en: Gaozu held him in the highest regard.
entries.literal: Gaozu greatly valued him.

entries.zh: 集字文會，初封遂安王，尋襲封衛王。
entries.en: Ji, styled Wenhui, was first created Prince of Suian and soon succeeded as Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: Ji, styled Wenhui, was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Suian; soon he succeeded to the enfeoffment as Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 煬帝時，諸侯王恩禮漸薄，猜防日甚。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yang, princes of the blood received ever less honor and favor, while suspicion and surveillance grew daily sharper.
entries.literal: In Emperor Yang's time, for the feudal princes favor and ceremony gradually grew thin, and suspicion and guard daily deepened.

entries.zh: 集憂懼不知所為，乃呼術者俞普明章醮以祈福助。
entries.en: Consumed by anxiety and fear, Ji summoned the ritual specialist Yu Puming to perform Daoist rites of supplication for divine aid.
entries.literal: Ji, anxious and fearful, did not know what to do; he then summoned the technician Yu Puming to perform zhang jiao rites to seek blessing and aid.

entries.zh: 有人告集咒詛，憲司希旨，鍛成其獄，奏集惡逆，坐當死。
entries.en: Someone reported that Ji was practicing curses. The judicial authorities shaped the case to please the throne, convicted him of treason, and recommended the death penalty.
entries.literal: Someone reported that Ji cursed; the judicial office, to please the intent, forged the case to completion and memorialized that Ji had committed wicked rebellion and, by the statute, deserved death.

entries.zh: 天子下公卿議其事，楊素等曰：「集密懷左道，厭蠱君親，公然咒詛，無慚幽顯。
entries.en: The emperor referred the case to the high ministers for deliberation. Yang Su and others said, "Ji has secretly embraced heterodox arts, practiced malign sorcery against his sovereign and kin, and openly uttered curses without shame before Heaven or earth.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the matter down to the nobles and ministers for discussion; Yang Su and others said: 'Ji secretly harbored the left path, practiced malign sorcery against ruler and kin, openly cursed and imprecated, without shame before the hidden and the manifest.

entries.zh: 情滅人理，事悖先朝，是君父之罪人，非臣子之所赦，請論如律。」
entries.en: He has abandoned all human decency and violated the principles of the founding reign. He is a criminal against his sovereign and father, and no subject may excuse such conduct. We ask that he be sentenced under the law."
entries.literal: His sentiment extinguishes human reason, his affairs rebel against the former court—he is a criminal against ruler and father, not one whom subjects and sons may pardon; we request judgment according to the statutes.'

entries.zh: 時滕王綸坐與相連，帝不忍加誅，乃下詔曰：「綸、集以附萼之華，猶子之重，縻之好爵，匪由德進。
entries.en: At the time Prince of Teng Lun was implicated in the same affair. Unable to bring himself to execute them, the emperor issued an edict: "Lun and Ji are like blossoms on the imperial stem, bearing the weight of princes of the blood. They were granted noble rank, yet not for any merit of their own.
entries.literal: At that time Prince of Teng Lun was implicated and connected in the case; the Emperor could not bear to execute them and issued an edict saying: 'Lun and Ji, as the blossom attached to the calyx, bear the weight due a son of the imperial line—they were bound to fine ranks, not advanced by virtue.

entries.zh: 正應與國升降，休戚是同，乃包藏妖禍，誕縱邪僻。
