entries.en: They ought to rise and fall with the dynasty and share its fortunes. Instead they harbored malign designs and gave free rein to wickedness.
entries.literal: They ought properly to rise and fall with the state and share its joys and sorrows alike; yet they harbored demonic calamity and wantonly indulged wicked perversity.

entries.zh: 在三之義，愛敬俱淪；
entries.en: The bonds of the three relationships—love and respect alike—have been utterly abandoned;
entries.literal: The obligations among the three—love and respect were both lost;

entries.zh: 急難之情，孔懷頓滅。
entries.en: and the ties of kinship in times of crisis have been cast aside entirely.
entries.literal: the feeling in urgent hardship—close kinship suddenly extinguished.

entries.zh: 公卿議既如此，覽以潸然。
entries.en: When I read the ministers' recommendation, tears came to my eyes.
entries.literal: The nobles' discussion being thus, on reading it tears flowed.

entries.zh: 雖複王法無私，恩從義斷，但法隱公族，禮有親親。
entries.en: Though the law knows no favoritism and affection must yield to justice, the statutes make allowance for the imperial clan, and ritual teaches us to cherish our kin.
entries.literal: Although the king's law knows no partiality and favor must yield to righteousness, yet the law makes allowance for the imperial clan and ritual has its cherishing of kin.

entries.zh: 致之極辟，情所未忍。」
entries.en: To put them to death is more than my heart can endure."
entries.literal: To bring them to extreme punishment—emotion could not bear it.'

entries.zh: 於是除名為民，遠徙邊郡。
entries.en: He therefore struck their names from the rolls, reduced them to commoner status, and exiled them to remote border commanderies.
entries.literal: Thereupon their names were struck and they were made commoners, banished far to frontier commanderies.

entries.zh: 遇天下大亂，不知所終。
entries.en: When the empire collapsed into chaos, no one knew what became of him.
entries.literal: When the empire fell into great disorder, no one knew their end.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，滕王綸、衛王集並以讒構得罪，高陽公智明亦以交遊奪爵，智積逾懼。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Prince of Teng Lun and Prince of Wei Ji were both convicted on charges of slanderous plotting; Duke of Gaoyang Zhiming likewise lost his title for improper associations, and Zhiji grew ever more fearful.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Prince of Teng Lun and Prince of Wei Ji were both convicted through slanderous plotting; Duke of Gaoyang Zhiming likewise lost his rank for improper associations, and Zhiji grew ever more fearful.

entries.zh: 大業七年，授弘農太守，委政僚佐，清靜自居。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Daye (611) he was appointed Governor of Hongnong, entrusted administration to his aides, and lived in quiet seclusion.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Daye he was appointed Governor of Hongnong; he entrusted government to his aides and maintained quiet seclusion.

entries.zh: 及楊玄感作亂，自東都引軍而西，智積謂官屬曰：「玄感聞大軍將至，欲西圖關中。
entries.en: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and led his army west from the Eastern Capital, Zhiji told his officials, "Xuangan has heard that the main army is approaching and intends to march west and seize Guanzhong.
entries.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and led his army west from the Eastern Capital, Zhiji told his officials: 'Xuangan has heard that the main army is coming and wishes to march west and seize Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 若成其計，則根本固矣。
entries.en: If he succeeds in this plan, his foundation will be secure.
entries.literal: If he succeeds in this plan, his foundation will be secure.

entries.zh: 當以計縻之，使不得進。
entries.en: We must use stratagem to hold him in place and keep him from advancing.
entries.literal: We must use stratagem to tether him and keep him from advancing.

entries.zh: 不出一旬，自可擒耳。」
entries.en: Within ten days he can be captured."
entries.literal: Within ten days he can be captured.'

entries.zh: 及玄感軍至城下，智積登陴詈辱之，玄感怒甚，留攻之。
entries.en: When Xuangan's army reached the walls, Zhiji mounted the battlements and hurled insults at him. Xuangan was furious and remained to besiege the city.
entries.literal: When Xuangan's army reached the walls, Zhiji mounted the battlements and reviled him with insults; Xuangan was greatly enraged and stayed to besiege the city.

entries.zh: 城門為賊所燒，智積乃更益火，賊不得入。
entries.en: The rebels set the city gate ablaze, so Zhiji added more fuel to the fire and the rebels could not enter.
entries.literal: The city gate was set afire by the rebels; Zhiji then added more fuel to the flames, and the rebels could not enter.

entries.zh: 數日，宇文述等援軍至，合擊破之。
entries.en: Within days the relief armies under Yuwen Shu and others arrived, and in a combined attack they defeated him.
entries.literal: Within several days the relief armies under Yuwen Shu and others arrived, and in combined attack they defeated him.

entries.zh: ○道悼王靜
entries.en: ○ Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing
entries.literal: ○ Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing

entries.zh: 未幾，爽寢疾，上使巫者薛榮宗視之，雲眾鬼為厲。
entries.en: Before long Shuang fell gravely ill. The emperor sent the shaman Xue Rongzong to examine him, and Rongzong reported that a host of ghosts were tormenting him.
entries.literal: Before long Shuang took to his bed with illness; the Emperor sent the shaman Xue Rongzong to observe him, who said that many ghosts were causing his affliction.

entries.zh: 爽令左右驅逐之。
entries.en: Shuang ordered his attendants to drive the spirits away.
entries.literal: Shuang ordered his attendants to drive them off.

entries.zh: 居數日，有鬼物來擊榮宗，榮宗走下階而斃。
entries.en: A few days later ghostly beings attacked Rongzong; he stumbled down the steps and died on the spot.
entries.literal: After several days, ghostly things came and struck Rongzong; Rongzong went down the steps and died.

entries.zh: 其夜爽薨，時年二十五。
entries.en: That same night Shuang died at the age of twenty-five.
entries.literal: That night Shuang died; he was twenty-five.

entries.zh: 贈太尉、冀州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Governor of Ji Province.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Commandant and Governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 子集嗣。
entries.en: His son Ji succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Ji succeeded.

entries.zh: ○衛昭王爽嗣王集
entries.en: ○ Prince of Wei the Illustrious, Shuang; His Heir Wang Ji
entries.literal: ○ Wei the Illustrious Prince Shuang; heir Wang Ji

entries.zh: 隋書卷四十四列傳第九
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Four, Biographies Nine
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Four, Biographies Nine

entries.zh: 協字欽仁，好學，有雅量。
entries.en: Xie, styled Qinren, loved learning and possessed refined composure.
entries.literal: Xie styled Qinren, loved learning, and had refined breadth.

entries.zh: 起家著作佐郎，後轉秘書郎。
entries.en: He began as assistant in the bureau of composition and later became secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: He began his career as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and later transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 開皇中，其父在廣州有功，上令協齎詔書勞問，未至而父卒。
entries.en: During Kaihuang his father had distinguished himself at Guangzhou; the emperor sent Xie with a commendatory edict, but he arrived too late.
entries.literal: In Kaihuang his father had merit at Guangzhou; the emperor ordered Xie to carry an edict of commendation, but before he arrived his father died.

entries.zh: 上以其父身死王事，拜協柱國。
entries.en: Because his father had died in imperial service, the emperor made Xie pillar of state.
entries.literal: Because his father died in the king's service, the emperor appointed Xie Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 後曆定、息、秦三州刺史，皆有能名，卒官。
entries.en: He later governed Ding, Xi, and Qin in turn, earning a name for competence, and died in office.
entries.literal: Later he served in succession as Prefect of Ding, Xi, and Qin—all had reputation for ability—and died in office.

entries.zh: 洸弟藝藝字世文，少受業國子。
entries.en: Guang's younger brother Yi, styled Shiwen, studied in his youth at the imperial academy.
entries.literal: Guang's younger brother Yi—Yi styled Shiwen—in youth received instruction at the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 周武帝時，數以軍功致位上儀同，賜爵修武縣侯，邑八百戶。
entries.en: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he rose repeatedly through military merit to upper pillar of state and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with eight hundred households.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he repeatedly through military merit reached Upper Pillar of State, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with a fief of eight hundred households.

entries.zh: 授左旅下大夫。
entries.en: He was appointed lower grand master of the left brigade.
entries.literal: He was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Left Brigade.

entries.zh: 出為魏郡太守。
entries.en: He was sent out as prefect of Wei.
entries.literal: He went out as Prefect of Wei.

entries.zh: 及高祖為丞相，尉迥險圖不軌，朝廷微知之，遣藝季父孝寬馳往代迥。
entries.en: When Gaozu was chancellor, Yuwen Jiong plotted treason; the court had wind of it and sent Yi's uncle Xiaokuan posthaste to replace him.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yuwen Jiong secretly plotted rebellion; the court slightly knew it and sent Yi's younger uncle Xiaokuan to gallop and replace Jiong.

entries.zh: 孝寬將至鄴，因詐病，止傳舍，從迥求藥，以察其變。
entries.en: As Xiaokuan neared Ye he feigned illness at a relay station and asked Jiong for medicine to probe his intentions.
entries.literal: When Xiaokuan was about to reach Ye he feigned illness, stopped at the relay station, and asked Jiong for medicine to observe his changes.

entries.zh: 迥遣藝迎孝寬。
entries.en: Jiong sent Yi to welcome Xiaokuan.
entries.literal: Jiong sent Yi to welcome Xiaokuan.

entries.zh: 孝寬問迥所為，藝党於迥，不以實答。
entries.en: Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was up to; Yi, loyal to Jiong, lied.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was doing; Yi sided with Jiong and did not answer truthfully.

entries.zh: 孝寬怒，將斬之，藝懼，乃言迥反狀。
entries.en: Xiaokuan grew angry and was about to execute him; terrified, Yi revealed Jiong's rebellion.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan was angry and was about to behead him; Yi feared and then spoke of Jiong's rebellious condition.

entries.zh: 孝寬於是將藝西遁，每至亭驛，輒盡驅傳馬而去。
entries.en: Xiaokuan then fled west with Yi, at every post driving off all relay horses.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan thereupon took Yi and fled west; at every post station he would drive off all relay horses and leave.

entries.zh: 複謂驛司曰：「蜀公將至，宜速具酒食。」
entries.en: He also told each station master, "The Duke of Shu is coming—prepare food and drink at once."
entries.literal: He again told the post official: "The Duke of Shu is about to arrive—you should quickly prepare food and drink."

entries.zh: 迥尋遣騎追孝寬，追人至驛，輒逢盛饌，又無馬，遂遲留不進，孝寬與藝由是得免。
entries.en: Jiong sent pursuers; at every station they found feasts but no horses and fell behind, so Xiaokuan and Yi escaped.
entries.literal: Jiong soon sent horsemen to pursue Xiaokuan; when the pursuers reached the post they always met lavish feasts and again had no horses, so they delayed and did not advance—Xiaokuan and Yi thereby escaped.

entries.zh: 高祖以孝寬故，弗問藝之罪，加授上開府，即從孝寬擊迥。
entries.en: Out of regard for Xiaokuan, Gaozu did not punish Yi, promoted him to upper pillar of state, and sent him with Xiaokuan against Jiong.
entries.literal: Gaozu because of Xiaokuan did not inquire into Yi's crime, added appointment as Upper Pillar of State, and immediately followed Xiaokuan in attacking Jiong.

entries.zh: 及破尉惇，平相州，皆有力焉。
entries.en: He played a major part in defeating Yuwen Dun and pacifying Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: When they broke Yuwen Dun and pacified Xiangzhou, he had strength in both.

entries.zh: 以功進位上大將軍，改封武威縣公，邑千戶。
entries.en: For his achievements he was promoted to upper grand general and made Duke of Wuwei with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: For merit he advanced to Upper Grand General, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Wuwei with a fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 以修武縣侯別封一子。
entries.en: One son was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu.
entries.literal: As Marquis of Xiuwu he enfeoffed one son separately.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，進封魏興郡公。
entries.en: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was raised to Duke of Weixing.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he was advanced to Duke of Weixing.

entries.zh: 歲餘，拜齊州刺史。
entries.en: A year later he was appointed prefect of Qi.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Prefect of Qi.

entries.zh: 為政清簡，士庶懷惠。
entries.en: His administration was clear and simple, and officials and people alike were grateful.
entries.literal: His government was clear and simple; gentry and commoners cherished his kindness.

entries.zh: 在職數年，遷營州總管。
entries.en: After several years he was transferred to commissioner-general of Ying.
entries.literal: After several years in office he was transferred to Commissioner-General of Ying.

entries.zh: 藝容貌瑰偉，每夷狄參謁，必整儀衛，盛服以見之，獨坐滿一榻。
entries.en: Yi was striking in appearance; whenever frontier peoples came to audience he arrayed full guard of honor and splendid dress, sitting alone across an entire couch.
entries.literal: Yi's appearance was grand and imposing; whenever barbarians of the Yi came to audience he would always array guards of honor and wear splendid dress to receive them, sitting alone and filling a whole couch.

entries.zh: 番人畏懼，莫敢仰視。
entries.en: The tribesmen were awed and dared not meet his gaze.
entries.literal: The barbarians feared and did not dare look up.

entries.zh: 而大治產業，與北夷貿易，家資巨萬，頗為清論所譏。
entries.en: Yet he amassed great estates and traded with northern tribes until his household wealth reached millions, drawing criticism from moralists.
entries.literal: Yet he greatly developed estates and traded with the northern Yi; family wealth reached tens of millions, and he was rather ridiculed in pure discussion.

entries.zh: 開皇十五年卒官，時年五十八。
entries.en: In Kaihuang year fifteen he died in office at fifty-eight.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang he died in office, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 諡曰懷。
entries.en: His posthumous name was Huai.
entries.literal: Posthumous title Huai.

entries.zh: 藝弟沖沖字世沖，少以名家子，在周釋褐衛公府禮曹參軍。
entries.en: Yi's younger brother Chong, styled Shichong, entered office under the Zhou as ritual officer in the household of the Duke of Wei.
entries.literal: Yi's younger brother Chong—Chong styled Shichong—in youth as a son of a famous house, upon leaving the sackcloth under Zhou became Army Ritual Officer of the Duke of Wei's household.

entries.zh: 後從大將軍元定渡江伐陳，為陳人所虜，周武帝以幣贖而還之。
entries.en: He later followed Yuan Ding across the Yangzi against Chen, was captured, and was ransomed back by Zhou Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: Later he followed Grand General Yuan Ding in crossing the river to attack Chen and was captured by the Chen; Emperor Wu of Zhou redeemed him with treasure and returned him.

entries.zh: 帝複令沖以馬千匹使于陳，以贖開府賀拔華等五十人及元定之柩而還。
entries.en: The emperor sent him to Chen with a thousand horses to ransom fifty captives including Heba Hua and recover Yuan Ding's coffin.
entries.literal: The emperor again ordered Chong to go to Chen with a thousand horses as envoy, to redeem fifty men including Pillar of State Heba Hua and Yuan Ding's coffin and return.

entries.zh: 沖有辭辯，奉使稱旨，累遷少禦伯下大夫，加上儀同。
entries.en: Eloquent as an envoy, he rose to lower imperial bearer grand master with the added rank of upper pillar of state.
entries.literal: Chong had eloquence in debate; as envoy he answered the purpose and was repeatedly promoted to Lower Imperial Bearer Grand Master, with Upper Pillar of State added.

entries.zh: 于時稽胡屢為寇亂，沖自請安集之，因拜汾州刺史。
entries.en: When the Jiéhu raided repeatedly he volunteered to pacify them and was made prefect of Fen.
entries.literal: At that time the Jiéhu repeatedly made raids and disturbances; Chong himself requested to pacify them and was appointed Prefect of Fen.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，征為兼散騎常侍，進位開府，賜爵安固縣侯。
entries.en: At Gaozu's accession he was summoned as concurrent regular attendant, made pillar of state, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Angu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned as Concurrent Regular Attendant, advanced to Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Angu.

entries.zh: 歲餘，發南汾州胡千餘人北築長城，在途皆亡。
entries.en: A year later more than a thousand southern Fenzhou Hu sent north to build the Great Wall deserted on the march.
entries.literal: After more than a year, over a thousand men of the southern Fenzhou Hu were sent north to build the Long Wall, and on the road all fled.

entries.zh: 上呼沖問計，沖曰：「夷狄之性，易為反覆，皆由牧宰不稱之所致也。
entries.en: The emperor asked his counsel; Chong said, "Barbarians are quick to turn treacherous when their overseers are unfit.
entries.literal: The emperor called Chong to ask his plan; Chong said: "The nature of the Yi and Di is easy to turn back and forth—all is caused by pastoral officials not fitting their posts.

entries.zh: 臣請以理綏靜，可不勞兵而定。」
entries.en: I can pacify them by just governance without troops."
entries.literal: Your servant requests to soothe them with reason; without troubling the army it can be settled."

entries.zh: 上然之，因命沖綏懷叛者。
entries.en: The emperor agreed and sent Chong to win over the deserters.
entries.literal: The emperor approved and ordered Chong to soothe and cherish the rebels.

entries.zh: 月餘皆至，並赴長城，上下書勞勉之。
entries.en: Within a month all returned and went to the wall; the court praised them in edicts.
entries.literal: Within a month all arrived and all went to the Long Wall; edicts from above and below praised and encouraged them.

entries.zh: 尋拜石州刺史，甚得諸胡歡心。
entries.en: He was soon made prefect of Shi and won the frontier peoples' loyalty.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Shi and greatly won the hearts of the various Hu.

entries.zh: 以母憂去職。
entries.en: He resigned to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 俄而起為南寧州總管，持節撫慰。
entries.en: He was soon recalled as commissioner-general of Nanning with credentials to pacify the south.
entries.literal: Shortly he was recalled as Commissioner-General of Nanning, holding credentials to comfort and soothe.

entries.zh: 複遣柱國王長述以兵繼進。
entries.en: Pillar of State Wang Changshu was sent with troops in support.
entries.literal: Again Pillar of State Wang Changshu was sent with troops to follow in support.

entries.zh: 沖上表固讓。
entries.en: Chong petitioned firmly to decline.
entries.literal: Chong memorialized firmly declining.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「西南夷裔，屢有生梗，每相殘賊，朕甚湣之，已命戎徒，清撫邊服。
entries.en: An edict read: "Southwestern tribes repeatedly rebel and slaughter one another; We pity them and have sent troops to pacify the frontier.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The Yi tribes of the southwest repeatedly show obstinacy; they constantly slaughter one another, and We greatly pity them. We have already ordered warriors to clear and soothe the border regions.

entries.zh: 以開府器幹堪濟，識略英遠，軍旅事重，故以相任。
entries.en: Your capacity and insight suit military command, and We therefore entrust this mission to you.
entries.literal: Because as Pillar of State your capacity and ability can cross difficulties, your insight and strategy are heroic and far-reaching, and military affairs are weighty, We therefore entrust you.

entries.zh: 知在艱疚，日月未多，金革奪情，蓋有通式。
entries.en: Though your mourning is recent, custom allows service to resume in wartime.
entries.literal: Knowing you are in the hardship of mourning and the days and months are not many, the metal and leather seizing feeling—there is a general rule.

entries.zh: 宜自抑割，即膺往旨。」
entries.en: Restrain your grief and obey this order at once."
entries.literal: You should yourself restrain and cut short, and immediately receive the former decree."

entries.zh: 沖既至南寧，渠帥爨震及西爨首領皆詣府參謁。
entries.en: At Nanning the chieftains Cuan Zhen and the western Cuan leaders all came to his headquarters.
entries.literal: When Chong reached Nanning, chieftain Cuan Zhen and the western Cuan leaders all came to the headquarters to pay respects.

entries.zh: 上大悅，下詔褒揚之。
entries.en: The emperor was delighted and issued a commendatory edict.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict praising him.

entries.zh: 其兄子伯仁，隨沖在府，掠人之妻，士卒縱暴，邊人失望。
entries.en: His nephew Boren, serving on his staff, seized women and soldiers plundered until the frontier lost faith.
entries.literal: His elder brother's son Boren followed Chong at the headquarters, seized people's wives, and soldiers indulged in violence—the border people lost hope.

entries.zh: 上聞而大怒，令蜀王秀治其事。
entries.en: The emperor was furious and ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to investigate.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly angry and ordered Prince of Shu Xiu to investigate the matter.

entries.zh: 益州長史元岩，性方正，案沖無所寬貸，沖竟坐免。
entries.en: Yi region chief administrator Yuan Yan investigated without favor and Chong was dismissed.
entries.literal: Chief Administrator of Yi Region Yuan Yan by nature was upright and square; investigating Chong he showed no indulgence, and Chong in the end was dismissed for the offense.

entries.zh: 其弟太子洗馬世約，譖岩于皇太子。
entries.en: His brother Shiyue, crown prince libationer, slandered Yan to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: His younger brother the Crown Prince's Libationer Shiyue slandered Yan to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 上謂太子曰：「古人有沽酒酸而不售者，為噬犬耳。
entries.en: The emperor told the crown prince, "The ancients had a wine seller whose stock turned sour because of a biting dog.
entries.literal: The emperor told the Crown Prince: "The ancients had one whose wine turned sour and would not sell—because of a biting dog.

entries.zh: 今何用世約乎？
entries.en: What use is Shiyue to you now?
entries.literal: Now what use is Shiyue?

entries.zh: 適累汝也。」
entries.en: He will only burden you."
entries.literal: He will only burden you."

entries.zh: 世約遂除名。
entries.en: Shiyue was struck from the registers.
entries.literal: Shiyue was thereupon removed from the rolls.

entries.zh: 後數載，令沖檢校括州事。
entries.en: Years later Chong was ordered to inspect Kuozhou.
entries.literal: Several years later Chong was ordered to inspect and manage Kuozhou affairs.

entries.zh: 時東陽賊帥陶子定、吳州賊帥羅慧方並聚眾為亂，攻圍婺州永康、烏程諸縣，沖率兵擊破之。
entries.en: Rebel leaders Tao Ziding and Luo Huifang besieged Wuzhou counties; Chong routed them.
entries.literal: At that time the bandit chieftain Tao Ziding of Dongyang and the bandit chieftain Luo Huifang of Wu Region both gathered crowds in rebellion, attacking and besieging Yongkang of Wuzhou and Wucheng and other counties; Chong led troops and defeated them.

entries.zh: 改封義豐縣候，檢校泉州事。
entries.en: He was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yifeng and made inspector of Quanzhou.
entries.literal: He changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Yifeng and was made inspector of Quanzhou affairs.

entries.zh: 尋拜營州總管。
entries.en: He was soon made commissioner-general of Ying again.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Commissioner-General of Ying.

entries.zh: 沖容貌都雅，寬厚得眾心。
entries.en: Refined in bearing and generous in manner, he won popular loyalty.
entries.literal: Chong's appearance was refined and elegant; generous and thick, he won the people's hearts.

entries.zh: 懷撫靺鞨、契丹，皆能致其死力。
entries.en: He soothed the Mohe and Khitan until they would fight to the death for him.
entries.literal: Comforting and soothing the Mohe and Khitan, he could all bring them to devote their utmost strength.

entries.zh: 奚、霫畏懼，朝貢相續。
entries.en: The Xi and Xie tribes submitted and sent tribute in succession.
entries.literal: The Xi and Xie feared and were in awe; tribute and missions followed in succession.

entries.zh: 高麗嘗入寇，沖率兵擊走之。
entries.en: When Goguryeo raided he drove them back by force.
entries.literal: Goguryeo once entered in raid; Chong led troops and struck and drove them off.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，高祖為豫章王暕納沖女為妃，征拜民部尚書。
entries.en: In Renshou, Gaozu betrothed Chong's daughter to Prince Yang Guang and made him minister of the people.
entries.literal: In Renshou, Gaozu for Prince of Yuzhang Yang Guang took Chong's daughter as consort and summoned him as Minister of the People.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒，時年六十六。
entries.en: He died soon afterward at sixty-six.
entries.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-six.

entries.zh: 少子挺，最知名。
entries.en: His youngest son Ting was the most famous.
entries.literal: His youngest son Ting was most renowned.

entries.zh: 從父弟壽壽字世齡。
entries.en: His paternal cousin Shou, styled Shiling.
entries.literal: Paternal cousin Shou—Shou styled Shiling.

entries.zh: 父孝寬，周上柱國、鄖國公。
entries.en: His father Xiaokuan was Zhou upper pillar of state and Duke of Yun.
entries.literal: Father Xiaokuan was Zhou Upper Pillar of State and Duke of Yun.

entries.zh: 壽在周，以貴公子，早有令譽，為右侍上士，遷千牛備身。
entries.en: Under the Zhou the young noble Shou won early renown as right attendant upper gentleman and thousand-ox guard.
entries.literal: Shou in Zhou, as a son of an honored house, early had fine reputation, was Right Attendant Upper Gentleman, and transferred to Thousand-Ox Guard.

entries.zh: 趙王為雍州牧，引為主簿。
entries.en: When Prince Zhao became prefect of Yong he made Shou his chief clerk.
entries.literal: When Prince Zhao was Prefect of Yong Region he drew him as Chief Clerk.

entries.zh: 尋遷少禦伯。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to lower imperial bearer.
entries.literal: Soon he transferred to Lower Imperial Bearer.

entries.zh: 武帝親征高氏，拜京兆尹，委以後事。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu campaigned against the Gao he made Shou metropolitan governor of Jingzhao with charge of the rear.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu personally campaigned against the Gao clan he appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and entrusted him with rear affairs.

entries.zh: 以父軍功，賜爵永安縣侯，邑八百戶。
entries.en: For his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with eight hundred households.
entries.literal: Because of his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with a fief of eight hundred households.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，以其父平尉迥，拜夀儀同三司，進封滑國公，邑五千戶。
entries.en: When Gaozu was chancellor he made Shou pillar of state, third rank, then Duke of Hua with five thousand households for pacifying Jiong.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, because his father pacified Yuwen Jiong he appointed Shou Pillar of State, Third Rank, advanced to Duke of Hua with a fief of five thousand households.

entries.zh: 俄以父喪去職。
entries.en: He soon resigned to mourn his father.
entries.literal: Shortly he left office on mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 高祖愛禪，起令視事，尋遷恆、毛二州刺史，頗有治名。
entries.en: At the founding of Sui he was recalled to duty, then governed Heng and Mao with distinction.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the love of abdication he recalled him and ordered him to resume duties; soon he transferred to Prefect of Heng and Mao—in both he had reputation for good governance.

entries.zh: 開皇十年，以疾征還，卒于家，時年四十二。
entries.en: In Kaihuang year ten he was recalled ill and died at home at forty-two.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang, because of illness he was summoned back and died at home, aged forty-two.

entries.zh: 諡曰定。
entries.en: His posthumous name was Ding.
entries.literal: Posthumous title Ding.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，高祖為晉王昭納其女為妃。
entries.en: In Renshou Gaozu betrothed his daughter to Prince Yang Zhao of Jin.
entries.literal: In Renshou, Gaozu for Prince of Jin Yang Zhao took his daughter as consort.

entries.zh: 以其子保巒嗣。
entries.en: His son Baoluan succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Baoluan succeeded.

entries.zh: 世康從父弟操，字元節，剛簡有風概。
entries.en: Shikang's paternal cousin Cao, styled Yuanjie, was stern, principled, and imposing.
entries.literal: Shikang's paternal cousin Cao, styled Yuanjie, was firm and simple with spirit and bearing.

entries.zh: 仕周，致位上開府、光州刺史。
entries.en: Under the Zhou he rose to upper pillar of state and prefect of Guang.
entries.literal: Serving Zhou, he reached Upper Pillar of State and Prefect of Guang.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，以平尉迥功，進位柱國，封平桑郡公，曆青、荊二州總管，卒官。
entries.en: When Gaozu was chancellor he was made pillar of state and Duke of Pingsang for pacifying Jiong, then commissioner-general of Qing and Jing until he died in office.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, for merit in pacifying Yuwen Jiong he advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingsang, and served in succession as Commissioner-General of Qing and Jing—he died in office.

entries.zh: 諡曰靜。
entries.en: His posthumous name was Jing.
entries.literal: Posthumous title Jing.

entries.zh: 柳機，字匡時，河東解人也。
entries.en: Liu Ji, styled Kuangshi, was a native of Jie in Hedong.
entries.literal: Liu Ji—Ji styled Kuangshi—was a native of Jie in Hedong.

entries.zh: 父慶，魏尚書左僕射。
entries.en: His father Qing was left vice director of the secretariat under the Wei.
entries.literal: Father Qing was Wei Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 機偉儀容，有器局，頗涉經史。
entries.en: Ji had imposing presence and breadth of vision and was well read in the classics and histories.
entries.literal: Ji had grand bearing and capacity, and was quite versed in the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 年十九，周武帝時為魯公，引為記室。
entries.en: At nineteen, when Zhou Emperor Wu was still Duke of Lu, Ji became his recorder.
entries.literal: At age nineteen, in the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou when he was Duke of Lu, he was drawn as Recorder.

entries.zh: 及帝嗣位，自宣納上士累遷少納言、太子宮尹，封平齊縣公。
entries.en: When the emperor succeeded he rose from secretariat gentleman to lower chamberlain and palace chamberlain of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingqi.
entries.literal: When the emperor succeeded to the throne, from Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat he was promoted in succession to Lower Chamberlain and Palace Chamberlain of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingqi.

entries.zh: 從帝平齊，拜開府，轉司宗中大夫。
entries.en: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was made pillar of state, then grand master of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi he was appointed Pillar of State and transferred to Grand Master of the Department of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 宣帝時，遷禦正上大夫。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuan he became upper grand master of imperial rectification.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he transferred to Upper Grand Master of the Imperial Rectification.

entries.zh: 機見帝失德，屢諫不聽，恐禍及己，托于鄭譯，陰求出外，於是拜華州刺史。
entries.en: Seeing the emperor's debauchery and failing to reform him, Ji feared for his life, relied on Zheng Yi, and secured appointment as prefect of Hua.
entries.literal: Ji saw the emperor's loss of virtue and repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded; fearing disaster would reach himself, he entrusted himself to Zheng Yi and secretly sought to go outside, and was thereupon appointed Prefect of Hua.

entries.zh: 及高祖作相，征還京師。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he was recalled to the capital.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was summoned back to the capital.

entries.zh: 時周代舊臣皆勸禪讓，機獨義形於色，無所陳請。
entries.en: When Zhou ministers urged abdication Ji alone showed open disapproval and made no petition.
entries.literal: At that time the old ministers of the Zhou all urged abdication; Ji alone showed righteousness in his countenance and made no memorial request.

entries.zh: 俄拜衛州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon made prefect of Wei.
entries.literal: Shortly he was appointed Prefect of Wei.

entries.zh: 及踐阼，進爵建安郡公，邑二千四百戶，征為納言。
entries.en: At the founding of Sui he was raised to Duke of Jian'an with twenty-four hundred households and made chamberlain.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne he advanced in noble rank to Duke of Jian'an with a fief of twenty-four hundred households and was summoned as Chamberlain.

entries.zh: 機性寬簡，有雅望，然當近侍，無所損益，又好飲酒，不親細務，在職數年，複出為華州刺史。
entries.en: Though refined and respected, he drank heavily, neglected detail, and after years at court returned to Hua as prefect.
entries.literal: Ji by nature was generous and simple, with refined standing, yet while serving in close attendance he made no additions or subtractions; he also loved drinking wine and did not attend to fine affairs—in office several years he again went out as Prefect of Hua.

entries.zh: 奉詔每月朝見。
entries.en: He was ordered to attend court monthly.
entries.literal: He received an edict to attend court monthly.

entries.zh: 尋轉冀州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to prefect of Ji.
entries.literal: Soon he transferred to Prefect of Ji.

entries.zh: 後征入朝，以其子述尚蘭陵公主，禮遇益隆。
entries.en: Recalled to court, he gained favor when his son Shu married Princess Lanling.
entries.literal: Later he was summoned to court; because his son Shu married Princess Lanling, favor and treatment grew richer.

entries.zh: 初，機在周，與族人文城公昂俱曆顯要。
entries.en: In Zhou days he and his kinsman Duke Ang of Wencheng had both held high office.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Ji was in Zhou, he together with his clansman the Duke of Wencheng Ang both held prominent posts.

entries.zh: 及此，機、昂並為外職，楊素時為納言，方用事，因上賜宴，素戲機曰：「二柳俱摧，孤楊獨聳。」
entries.en: Now Ji and Ang served in the provinces while Yang Su, chamberlain and favorite, jested at court: "Both willows are broken; the lone poplar stands tall."
entries.literal: By this time Ji and Ang were both in outer posts; Yang Su at the time was Chamberlain and just then wielded power—therefore at an imperial feast Su jested to Ji: "Both willows are broken down; the lone poplar stands tall alone."

entries.zh: 坐者歡笑，機竟無言。
entries.en: The company laughed; Ji said nothing.
entries.literal: Those seated laughed; Ji in the end had no words.

entries.zh: 未幾，還州。
entries.en: He soon returned to his province.
entries.literal: Before long he returned to his province.

entries.zh: 前後作牧，俱稱寬惠。
entries.en: As regional governor he was always praised for lenient rule.
entries.literal: Before and after as governor he was all called generous and kind.

entries.zh: 後數年，以疾征還京師，卒于家，時年五十六。
entries.en: Years later, recalled ill, he died at home at fifty-six.
entries.literal: Several years later, because of illness he was summoned back to the capital and died at home, aged fifty-six.

entries.zh: 贈大將軍、青州刺史，諡曰簡。
entries.en: He was posthumously made grand general and prefect of Qing with the temple name Jian.
entries.literal: Posthumously made Grand General and Prefect of Qing, with posthumous title Jian.

entries.zh: 子述嗣。
entries.en: His son Shu succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Shu succeeded.

entries.zh: 子述柳述，字業隆，性明敏，有幹略，頗涉文藝。
entries.en: Shu, styled Yelong, was clever, capable, and accomplished in letters.
entries.literal: Shu—Liu Shu styled Yelong—was by nature bright and keen, had capacity and strategy, and was quite versed in literary arts.

entries.zh: 少以父廕，為太子親衛。
entries.en: Through his father's privilege he became a close guard of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In youth through his father's shade he became Close Guard of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 後以尚主之故，拜開府儀同三司、內史侍郎。
entries.en: Marriage to an imperial princess brought him pillar of state with insignia of office and vice director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Later because of marrying the princess he was appointed Pillar of State with the insignia of office, Third Rank, and Secretariat Vice Director.

entries.zh: 上于諸婿中，特所寵敬。
entries.en: Among the imperial sons-in-law the emperor favored and respected him above the rest.
entries.literal: Among all the sons-in-law the emperor especially favored and respected him.

entries.zh: 歲餘，判兵部尚書事。
entries.en: A year later he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of war.
entries.literal: After more than a year he concurrently judged Ministry of War affairs.

entries.zh: 丁父艱去職。
entries.en: He resigned to observe mourning for his father.
entries.literal: He left office on mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 未幾，起攝給事黃門侍郎事，襲爵建安郡公。
entries.en: He was soon recalled as acting vice director of the yellow gate and inherited the dukedom of Jian'an.
entries.literal: Before long he was recalled to act as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Vice Director, inheriting the noble rank Duke of Jian'an.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，判吏部尚書事。
entries.en: During Renshou he was given concurrent charge of the civil service ministry.
entries.literal: In Renshou he concurrently judged Ministry of the Civil Service affairs.

entries.zh: 述雖職務修理，為當時所稱，然不達大體，暴於馭下，又怙寵驕豪，無所降屈。
entries.en: Though efficient and praised at court, he lacked breadth of vision, bullied subordinates, and grew arrogant on imperial favor.
entries.literal: Though Shu's duties were well ordered and praised in the age, he did not comprehend the larger pattern, was harsh in controlling subordinates, and also relied on favor and was arrogant and overbearing, bowing to no one.

entries.zh: 楊素時稱貴幸，朝臣莫不讋憚，述每陵侮之，數於上前面折素短。
entries.en: Yang Su then dominated the court, yet Shu repeatedly humiliated him and exposed his faults before the emperor.
entries.literal: Yang Su at the time was called honored and favored; court ministers all feared him—Shu each time insulted him and several times before the emperor exposed Su's faults.

entries.zh: 判事有不合素意，素或令述改之，輒謂將命者曰：「語僕射，道尚書不肯。」
entries.en: When Su ordered him to alter a decision Shu refused, telling the messenger, "Tell the Vice Director the Minister will not."
entries.literal: When judging affairs did not accord with Su's intent, Su sometimes ordered Shu to change them; he would tell the bearer of orders: "Tell the Vice Director—the Minister says he will not."

entries.zh: 素由是銜之。
entries.en: Su therefore nursed a grievance against him.
entries.literal: Su thereby bore a grudge.

entries.zh: 俄而楊素亦被疏忌，不知省務。
entries.en: Soon Yang Su too fell from favor and neglected his duties.
entries.literal: Shortly Yang Su was also distanced and suspected, not knowing provincial affairs.

entries.zh: 述任寄逾重，拜兵部尚書，參掌機密。
entries.en: Shu's responsibilities grew; he became minister of war and shared state secrets.
entries.literal: Shu's commission grew heavier; he was appointed Minister of War and shared in confidential matters.

entries.zh: 述自以無功可紀，過叨匪服，抗表陳讓。
entries.en: Believing he had no merit for such rank, he petitioned to resign.
entries.literal: Shu himself thought he had no merit to record and had excessively received unfitting rank; he submitted a memorial firmly declining.

entries.zh: 上許之，令攝兵部尚書事。
entries.en: The emperor agreed and had him act as minister of war.
entries.literal: The emperor permitted it and ordered him to act as Minister of War.

entries.zh: 上于仁壽宮寢疾，述與楊素、黃門侍郎元岩等侍疾宮中。
entries.en: When the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Shu attended him with Yang Su and Yuan Yan.
entries.literal: When the emperor lay ill at Renshou Palace, Shu together with Yang Su, Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Yan, and others attended the illness in the palace.

entries.zh: 時皇太子無禮于陳貴人，上知而大怒，因令述召房陵王。
entries.en: Learning the crown prince had insulted Lady Chen, the emperor angrily ordered Shu to summon Prince Yong of Fangling.
entries.literal: At that time the Crown Prince was disrespectful to Lady Chen; when the emperor knew he was greatly angry and ordered Shu to summon the Prince of Fangling.

entries.zh: 述與元岩出外作敕書，楊素聞之，與皇太子協謀，便矯詔執述、岩二人，持以屬吏。
entries.en: Shu and Yuan Yan went out to draft the edict; Yang Su conspired with the crown prince, forged orders, and had them arrested.
entries.literal: Shu and Yuan Yan went outside to draft the edict; Yang Su heard and conspired with the Crown Prince, then forged an edict to arrest Shu and Yan and hand them to the officials.

entries.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，述竟坐除名，與公主離絕。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Shu was dismissed and separated from the princess.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Shu was dismissed for the offense and separated from the princess.

entries.zh: 徙述于龍川郡。
entries.en: He was exiled to Longchuan.
entries.literal: Shu was banished to Longchuan commandery.

entries.zh: 公主請與述同徙，帝不聽，事見《列女傳》。
entries.en: The princess asked to share his exile; the emperor refused—the account appears in the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》.
entries.literal: The princess requested to be banished with Shu; the emperor did not listen—the matter is recorded in the "Biographies of Exemplary Women" (Lie nü zhuan).

entries.zh: 述在龍川數年，複徙寧越，遇瘴癘而死，時年三十九。
entries.en: After years in Longchuan he was moved to Ningyue, where miasma killed him at thirty-nine.
entries.literal: After several years in Longchuan he was again banished to Ningyue; encountering miasma he died, aged thirty-nine.

entries.zh: 弟旦旦字匡德，工騎射，頗涉書籍。
entries.en: His younger brother Dan, styled Kuangde, excelled at horsemanship and archery and was well read.
entries.literal: Younger brother Dan—Dan styled Kuangde—was skilled at mounted archery and quite versed in books.

entries.zh: 起家周左侍上士，累遷兵部下大夫。
entries.en: He entered service under the Zhou as left attendant upper gentleman and rose to lower grand master of war.
entries.literal: He began his career as Zhou Left Attendant Upper Gentleman and was repeatedly promoted to Lower Grand Master of War.

entries.zh: 頃之，益州總管王謙起逆，拜為行軍長史，從梁睿討平之，以功授儀同三司。
entries.en: When Wang Qian of Yi rebelled he served as campaign chief administrator under Liang Rui and was made pillar of state, third rank.
entries.literal: Shortly Commissioner-General Wang Qian of Yi rose in rebellion; he was appointed Campaign Chief Administrator and followed Liang Rui in suppressing and pacifying him; for merit he was appointed Pillar of State, Third Rank.

entries.zh: 開皇元年，加授開府，封新城縣男，遷授掌設驃騎。
entries.en: In Kaihuang year one he was made pillar of state, enfeoffed Baron of Xincheng, and given command of the setting pillar of cavalry.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was additionally appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Baron of Xincheng, and transferred to command the Setting Pillar of Cavalry.

entries.zh: 曆羅、淅、魯三州刺史，並有能名。
entries.en: He governed Luo, Xi, and Lu in turn, all with a reputation for competence.
entries.literal: He served in succession as Prefect of Luo, Xi, and Lu—all had reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 大業初，拜龍川太守。
entries.en: At the start of Daye he was made prefect of Longchuan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Prefect of Longchuan.

entries.zh: 民居山洞，好相攻擊，旦為開設學校，大變其風。
entries.en: The people lived in mountain caves and raided one another until Dan founded schools and transformed their ways.
entries.literal: The people lived in mountain caves and loved to attack one another; Dan established schools and greatly changed their customs.

entries.zh: 帝聞而善之，下詔褒美。
entries.en: The emperor praised him in an edict.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard he approved and issued an edict praising him.

entries.zh: 四年，征為太常少卿，攝判黃門侍郎事。
entries.en: In year four he was recalled as vice minister of imperial sacrifices and acting vice director of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and acted as Concurrent Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 卒官，年六十一。
entries.en: He died in office at sixty-one.
entries.literal: He died in office, aged sixty-one.

entries.zh: 子燮，官至河內掾。
entries.en: His son Xie rose to administrator of Henei.
entries.literal: His son Xie reached the office of Administrator of Henei.

entries.zh: 旦弟肅肅字匡仁，少聰敏，閑於占對。
entries.en: Dan's younger brother Su, styled Kuangren, was clever and quick in debate from youth.
entries.literal: Dan's younger brother Su—Su styled Kuangren—in youth was clever and keen, skilled in repartee.

entries.zh: 起家周齊王文學。
entries.en: He began under the Zhou as literary scholar to Prince Wen of Qi.
entries.literal: He began his career as Literary Scholar to Prince Wen of Qi under the Zhou.

entries.zh: 武帝見而異之，召拜宣納上士。
entries.en: Zhou Emperor Wu was impressed and appointed him upper gentleman of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu saw him and was struck by him; he was summoned and appointed Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 高祖作相，引為賓曹參軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he was made guest army officer.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was drawn as Guest Army Officer.

entries.zh: 開皇初，授太子洗馬。
entries.en: In early Kaihuang he became crown prince libationer.
entries.literal: In early Kaihuang he was appointed Crown Prince Libationer.

entries.zh: 陳使謝泉來聘，以才學見稱，詔肅宴接，時論稱其華辯。
entries.en: When the Chen envoy Xie Quan came, Su was ordered to entertain him and was praised for eloquence.
entries.literal: When Chen envoy Xie Quan came on a mission, because of literary talent he was praised; an edict ordered Su to entertain him—opinion of the time called his brilliance and eloquence.

entries.zh: 轉太子內舍人，遷太子僕。
entries.en: He became crown prince inner attendant, then crown prince steward.
entries.literal: He transferred to Crown Prince Inner Attendant and was promoted Crown Prince Steward.

entries.zh: 太子廢，坐除名為民。
entries.en: When the crown prince was deposed he was reduced to commoner status.
entries.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed he sat for dismissal and was made a commoner.

entries.zh: 大業中，帝與段達語及庶人罪惡之狀，達雲：「柳肅在宮，大見疏斥。」
entries.en: In Daye the emperor discussed the deposed heir with Duan Da, who said, "Liu Su had been greatly slighted in the palace."
entries.literal: In Daye the emperor spoke with Duan Da about the deposed heir's wicked conduct; Da said: "Liu Su in the palace was greatly slighted and rejected."

entries.zh: 帝問其故，答曰：「學士劉臻，嘗進章仇太翼于宮中，為巫蠱事。
entries.en: The emperor asked why. Duan Da answered, "The scholar Liu Zhen once brought Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for sorcery.
entries.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he answered: "Scholar Liu Zhen once introduced Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for witchcraft affairs.

entries.zh: 肅知而諫曰：'殿下帝之塚子，位當儲貳，誡在不孝，無患見疑。
entries.en: Su warned, "You are the emperor's heir—beware unfilial conduct, not suspicion."
entries.literal: Su knew and remonstrated: "Your Highness is the emperor's heir by tomb and shrine; your station should be heir apparent—caution lies in unfilial conduct, not in being suspected.

entries.zh: 劉臻書生，鼓搖脣舌，適足以相誑誤，願殿下勿納之。
entries.en: Liu Zhen is a scholar who wags his tongue—do not heed him.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen is a bookish man who wags his lips and tongue—he is fit only to deceive and mislead; I beg Your Highness not to accept him."

entries.zh: '庶人不懌，他日謂臻曰：'汝何故漏泄，使柳肅知之，令面折我？
entries.en: The deposed heir was displeased and later demanded of Zhen, "Why did you leak this so Liu Su could rebuke me to my face?"
entries.literal: The deposed heir was displeased and another day said to Zhen: "Why did you leak it and let Liu Su know, making him rebuke me to my face?

entries.zh: '自是後言皆不用。」
entries.en: After that his counsel went unheeded."
entries.literal: From then on his words were not heeded."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「肅橫除名，非其罪也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Su was wrongly dismissed—it was not his fault."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Su was rashly removed from the rolls—not his crime."

entries.zh: 召守禮部侍郎，轉工部侍郎，大見親任。
entries.en: He was recalled as vice minister of rites, then works, and greatly trusted.
entries.literal: He was summoned to act as Vice Minister of Rites, transferred to Vice Minister of Works, and greatly trusted.

entries.zh: 每行幸遼東，常委之于涿郡留守。
entries.en: On each Liaodong campaign he left Su as guardian at Zhuo.
entries.literal: Whenever the emperor campaigned in Liaodong he repeatedly entrusted him to remain and guard at Zhuo.

entries.zh: 十一年卒，時年六十二。
entries.en: In year eleven he died at sixty-two.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-two.

entries.zh: 從弟雄亮雄亮字信誠。
entries.en: His paternal cousin Xiongliang, styled Xincheng.
entries.literal: Paternal cousin Xiongliang—Xiongliang styled Xincheng.

entries.zh: 父檜，仕周華陽太守。
entries.en: His father Hui was prefect of Huayang under the Zhou.
entries.literal: Father Hui served as Zhou Prefect of Huayang.

entries.zh: 遇黃眾寶作亂，攻陷華陽，檜為賊所害。
entries.en: When Huang Zhongbao rebelled and took Huayang, Hui was killed.
entries.literal: Encountering Huang Zhongbao's rebellion, Huayang was attacked and taken; Hui was killed by the bandits.

entries.zh: 雄亮時年十四，哀毀過禮，陰有復仇之志。
entries.en: Xiongliang was fourteen; his mourning exceeded propriety and he secretly vowed revenge.
entries.literal: Xiongliang was then fourteen; his grief and destruction exceeded the rites, and secretly he had the will to take revenge.

entries.zh: 武帝時，眾寶率其所部歸於長安，帝待之甚厚。
entries.en: Later Zhongbao submitted to Chang'an and was generously treated by Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wu's time Zhongbao led his followers in submission to Chang'an; the emperor treated him very generously.

entries.zh: 雄亮手斬眾寶於城中，請罪闕下，帝特原之。
entries.en: Xiongliang slew Zhongbao in the city and surrendered for punishment; the emperor pardoned him.
entries.literal: Xiongliang with his own hand beheaded Zhongbao in the city and requested punishment below the gate; the emperor specially pardoned him.

entries.zh: 尋治梁州總管記室，遷湖城令，累遷內史中大夫，賜爵汝陽縣子。
entries.en: He served as recorder on the Liang commissioner-general's staff, then magistrate of Hucheng, then secretariat grand master and Viscount of Ruyang.
entries.literal: Soon he managed the records office of the Liang Region Commissioner-General, transferred to Magistrate of Hucheng, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Viscount of Ruyang.

entries.zh: 司馬消難作亂江北，高祖令雄亮聘于陳，以結鄰好。
entries.en: When Sima Xiaonan rebelled, Gaozu sent him to Chen to secure an alliance.
entries.literal: When Sima Xiaonan rebelled north of the river, Gaozu ordered Xiongliang to go on mission to Chen to secure neighborly good relations.

entries.zh: 及還，會高祖受禪，拜尚書考功侍郎，尋遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: On his return Gaozu had taken the throne; he became vice director for merit evaluation, then yellow gate attendant.
entries.literal: When he returned, Gaozu had received the abdication; he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat for Merit Evaluation and soon transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 尚書省凡有奏事，雄亮多所駁正，深為公卿所憚。
entries.en: He often rejected Secretariat memorials and was feared by the ministers.
entries.literal: Whenever the Secretariat had memorials to present, Xiongliang many times rejected and corrected them, and the public ministers deeply feared him.

entries.zh: 俄以本官檢校太子左庶子，進爵為伯。
entries.en: He was soon made acting left heir apparent of the crown prince and raised to earl.
entries.literal: Shortly with his original office he inspected and acted as Left Heir Apparent of the Crown Prince, advanced in noble rank to Earl.

entries.zh: 秦王俊之鎮隴右也，出為秦州總管府司馬，領山南道行台左丞，卒官，時年五十一。
entries.en: When Prince Jun of Qin went to Longyou he served as his chief administrator and south mountain route assistant until he died at fifty-one.
entries.literal: When Prince of Qin Jun went to secure Longyou he went out as Chief Administrator of the Qin Region Commissioner-General's office, concurrently Left Assistant of the South Mountain Route Campaign Headquarters—he died in office, aged fifty-one.

entries.zh: 有子贊。
entries.en: He had a son Zan.
entries.literal: He had a son Zan.

entries.zh: 從子謇之謇之字公正。
entries.en: His nephew Jianzhi, styled Gongzheng.
entries.literal: Nephew Jianzhi—Jianzhi styled Gongzheng.

entries.zh: 父蔡年，周順州刺史。
entries.en: His father Cai'nian was prefect of Shun under the Zhou.
entries.literal: Father Cai'nian was Zhou Prefect of Shun.

entries.zh: 謇之身長七尺五寸，儀容甚偉，風神爽亮，進止可觀。
entries.en: Jianzhi stood seven feet five inches, imposing in bearing and graceful in movement.
entries.literal: Jianzhi's body was seven feet five inches; his bearing was very imposing, his spirit bright and clear, his advance and stop worth viewing.

entries.zh: 為童兒時，周齊王憲嘗遇謇之於途，異而與語，大奇之。
entries.en: As a boy he met Prince Xian of Qi, who was astonished and recommended him.
entries.literal: As a child, Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou once met Jianzhi on the road, was struck by him and conversed—he greatly marveled.

entries.zh: 因奏入國子，以明經擢第，拜宗師中士，尋轉守廟下士。
entries.en: He entered the imperial academy, passed the classics examination, and became master of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: He therefore memorialized entry into the Imperial Academy; through the classics examination he was selected, appointed Master of the Imperial Clan, and soon transferred to Lower Gentleman Guarding the Temple.

entries.zh: 武帝嘗有事太廟，謇之讀祝文，音韻清雅，觀者屬目。
entries.en: Reading prayers at the Grand Temple with clear, elegant delivery, he drew every eye.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu once had business at the Grand Temple, Jianzhi read the prayer text with clear and elegant tone and pitch—observers fixed their eyes on him.

entries.zh: 帝善之，擢為宣納上士。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and made him upper gentleman of the secretariat.
entries.literal: The emperor approved and promoted him to Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 及高祖作相，引為田曹參軍，仍諮典簽事。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he became field army officer and registry adviser.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was drawn as Field Army Officer and still consulted on registry affairs.

entries.zh: 開皇初，拜通事舍人，尋遷內史舍人，曆兵部、司勳二曹侍郎。
entries.en: In early Kaihuang he was communications attendant, then secretariat attendant, then vice director of war and merit.
entries.literal: In early Kaihuang he was appointed Communications Attendant and soon transferred to Secretariat Attendant, serving in succession as Vice Director of War and Vice Director of Merit.

entries.zh: 朝廷以謇之有雅望，善談謔，又飲酒至石不亂，由是每梁、陳使至，輒令謇之接對。
entries.en: The court valued his wit and his capacity to drink a stone of wine without disorder, and always sent him to receive Liang and Chen envoys.
entries.literal: The court because Jianzhi had refined standing, was skilled in wit, and also could drink to a stone measure without disorder—therefore whenever Liang or Chen envoys arrived they always ordered Jianzhi to receive them.

entries.zh: 後遷光祿少卿。
entries.en: He was later made vice minister of the imperial household.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 出入十餘年，每參掌敷奏。
entries.en: For more than ten years he helped draft and present memorials.
entries.literal: Entering and leaving over more than ten years, each time he shared in drafting and presenting memorials.

entries.zh: 會吐谷渾來降，朝廷以宗女光化公主妻之，以謇之兼散騎常侍，送公主于西域。
entries.en: When Tuyuhun submitted, he escorted Princess Guanghua west as concurrent regular attendant.
entries.literal: When Tuyuhun came to submit, the court married the imperial clan daughter Princess Guanghua to them and made Jianzhi Concurrent Regular Attendant to escort the princess to the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 俄而突厥啟民可汗求結和親，複令謇之送義成公主于突厥。
entries.en: When the Türk Qimin Qaghan sought alliance he escorted Princess Yicheng to the Türks.
entries.literal: Shortly the Tujue Qimin Qaghan sought marriage alliance; again Jianzhi was ordered to escort Princess Yicheng to the Tujue.

entries.zh: 謇之前後奉使，得二國所贈馬千餘匹，雜物稱是，皆散之宗族，家無餘財。
entries.en: On both missions he received over a thousand horses and gave everything to his kin, leaving nothing at home.
entries.literal: Jianzhi on former and latter missions received over a thousand horses from the two states and miscellaneous goods in proportion—all he distributed to his clan; the family had no surplus wealth.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，出為肅州刺史，尋轉息州刺史，俱有惠政。
entries.en: In Renshou he governed Su, then Xi, both with benevolent rule.
entries.literal: In Renshou he went out as Prefect of Su and soon transferred to Prefect of Xi—in both he had benevolent government.

entries.zh: 後二歲，以母憂去職。
entries.en: Two years later he resigned to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: Two years later he left office on mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 煬帝踐阼，複拜光祿少卿。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was again made vice minister of the imperial household.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 大業初，啟民可汗自以內附，遂畜牧於定襄、馬邑間，帝使謇之諭令出塞。
entries.en: In early Daye Qimin pastured near the border; the emperor sent Jianzhi to order him beyond the frontier.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Daye, Qimin Qaghan because he had submitted inward pastured between Dingxiang and Mayi; the emperor sent Jianzhi to instruct him to go beyond the passes.

entries.zh: 及還，奏事稱旨，拜黃門侍郎。
entries.en: His report pleased the emperor and he was made yellow gate vice director.
entries.literal: When he returned his memorial answered the purpose and he was appointed Yellow Gate Vice Director.

entries.zh: 時元德太子初薨，朝野注望，皆以齊王當立。
entries.en: When Crown Prince Yuande died, all expected Prince Qi to succeed.
entries.literal: At that time the Yuande Crown Prince had just died; court and countryside fixed their hopes—all thought the Prince of Qi would be established.

entries.zh: 帝方重王府之選，大業三年，車駕還京師，拜為齊王長史。
entries.en: In Daye year three the emperor made him chief administrator to Prince Qi.
entries.literal: The emperor was then weighting selections for the princely household; in the third year of Daye when the imperial carriage returned to the capital he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 帝法服臨軒，備儀衛，命齊王立於西朝堂之前，北面。
entries.en: In full ritual the emperor had Prince Qi stand before the western court hall facing north.
entries.literal: The emperor in ritual robes faced the hall, fully arrayed guards of honor, and ordered the Prince of Qi to stand before the western court hall, facing north.

entries.zh: 遣吏部尚書牛弘、內史令楊約、左衛大將軍宇文述等，從殿廷引謇之詣齊王所，西面立。
entries.en: Niu Hong, Yang Yue, and Yuwen Shu led Jianzhi to stand before the prince facing west.
entries.literal: He sent Minister of the Civil Service Niu Hong, Secretariat Director Yang Yue, Left Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu, and others from the hall to lead Jianzhi to the Prince of Qi's place, standing facing west.

entries.zh: 牛弘宣敕謂齊王曰：「我昔階緣恩寵，啟封晉陽，出籓之初，時年十二。
entries.en: Niu Hong proclaimed to Prince Qi, "Through imperial favor I was once enfeoffed at Jinyang; when I first went to my fief I was only twelve years old.
entries.literal: Niu Hong proclaimed the edict to the Prince of Qi: "I formerly through favor of fate was enfeoffed at Jinyang; when I first went out to the frontier I was twelve years old.

entries.zh: 先帝立我於西朝堂，乃令高熲、虞慶則、元旻等，從內送王子相于我。
entries.en: The former emperor had Gao Feng and others present Prince Xiang to me as companion.
entries.literal: The former emperor established me at the western court hall and ordered Gao Feng, Yu Qingze, Yuan Min, and others from within to send Prince Xiang to me.

entries.zh: 于時誡我曰：'以汝幼沖，未更世事，今令子相作輔於汝，事無大小，皆可委之。
entries.en: He warned me, "You are young—in all matters great or small entrust them to Xiang."
entries.literal: At that time he admonished me: "Because you are young and have not yet experienced worldly affairs, I now make Xiang your companion—in affairs great or small you may all entrust them to him.

entries.zh: 無得昵近小人，疏遠子相。
entries.en: Do not favor petty men or distance yourself from Xiang.
entries.literal: Do not draw near petty men or distance yourself from Xiang.

entries.zh: 若從我言者，有益於社稷，成立汝名行。
entries.en: If you heed this it will benefit the realm and your reputation.
entries.literal: If you follow my words it will benefit the altars of soil and grain and establish your name and conduct.

entries.zh: 如不用此言，唯國及身，敗無日矣。
entries.en: If you ignore it, ruin will come swiftly to you and the state.
entries.literal: If you do not use these words, only the state and your person—ruin will be without delay.

entries.zh: '吾受敕之後，奉以周旋，不敢失墜。
entries.en: I have kept this counsel ever since.
entries.literal: After I received the edict I held to it in all dealings and did not dare lose it.

entries.zh: 微子相之力，吾無今日矣。
entries.en: Without Xiang I would not be emperor today.
entries.literal: Without the strength of Xiang I would have no today.

entries.zh: 若與謇之從事，一如子相也。」
entries.en: Treat Jianzhi as you would Xiang."
entries.literal: If you work with Jianzhi, it is just like Xiang."

entries.zh: 又敕謇之曰：「今以卿作輔于齊，善思匡救之理，副朕所望。
entries.en: He charged Jianzhi, "Serve Qi as Xiang served me—fulfill my hope.
entries.literal: Again he charged Jianzhi: "Now I make you companion to Qi—think well on the principle of aiding and saving; match what I hope.

entries.zh: 若齊王德業修備，富貴自當鐘卿一門。
entries.en: If Qi cultivates virtue, your whole house will prosper.
entries.literal: If the Prince of Qi's virtue and enterprise are cultivated and complete, wealth and honor will naturally be heaped on your whole house.

entries.zh: 若有不善，罪亦相及。」
entries.en: If he errs, you will share the guilt."
entries.literal: If there is what is not good, guilt will also reach you."

entries.zh: 時齊王正擅寵，左右放縱，喬令則之徒，深見昵狎。
entries.en: Prince Qi then held favor and his intimates, including Qiao Lingze, ran wild.
entries.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi was just then monopolizing favor; his close attendants were unrestrained—men like Qiao Lingze were deeply drawn near and pampered.

entries.zh: 謇之雖知其罪失，不能匡正。
entries.en: Jianzhi knew their faults but could not correct them.
entries.literal: Jianzhi though he knew their faults and errors could not correct and straighten them.

entries.zh: 及王得罪，謇之竟坐除名。
entries.en: When Prince Qi fell from favor, Jianzhi was struck from the registers.
entries.literal: When the prince was guilty, Jianzhi in the end sat for dismissal from the rolls.

entries.zh: 帝幸遼東，召謇之檢校燕郡事。
entries.en: On the Liaodong campaign the emperor summoned him to oversee Yan commandery.
entries.literal: The emperor campaigned in Liaodong and summoned Jianzhi to inspect and manage Yan commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 及帝班師，至燕郡，坐供頓不給，配戍嶺南。
entries.en: On the return march he was convicted of failing to supply the army and was banished to Lingnan.
entries.literal: When the emperor returned the army and reached Yan commandery, he sat because provisions were not supplied and was assigned to garrison in Lingnan.

entries.zh: 卒于洭口，時年六十。
entries.en: He died at Kuangkou at the age of sixty.
entries.literal: He died at Kuangkou, aged sixty.

entries.zh: 子威明。
entries.en: His son was Weiming.
entries.literal: His son Weiming.

entries.zh: 族弟昂昂字千里。
entries.en: His clansman Ang, styled Qianli.
entries.literal: Clansman Ang—Ang styled Qianli.

entries.zh: 父敏，有高名，好禮篤學，治家如官。
entries.en: His father Min was renowned for propriety, learning, and running his household with official discipline.
entries.literal: Father Min had a lofty reputation, loved rites and pursued learning deeply, and managed the household like an office.

entries.zh: 仕周，曆職清顯。
entries.en: Under the Zhou he held prominent offices.
entries.literal: Serving Zhou, he held offices of clear prominence.

entries.zh: 開皇初，為太子太保。
entries.en: In early Kaihuang he became crown prince grand tutor.
entries.literal: In early Kaihuang he was Crown Prince Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 昂有器識，幹局過人。
entries.en: Ang had vision and administrative talent beyond ordinary men.
entries.literal: Ang had capacity and insight; his organizing ability surpassed others.

entries.zh: 周武帝時，為大內史，賜爵文城郡公，致位開府，當途用事，百僚皆出其下。
entries.en: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he was grand secretariat director, Duke of Wencheng, pillar of state, and dominated the court.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wu of Zhou's time he was Grand Secretariat Director, enfeoffed as Duke of Wencheng, reached Pillar of State, held power on the road, and all hundred officials were below him.

entries.zh: 宣帝嗣位，稍被疏遠，然不離本職。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuan he was gradually sidelined but kept his post.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he was gradually distanced, yet did not leave his original post.

entries.zh: 及高祖為丞相，深自結納。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he allied himself closely with him.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he deeply bound himself in alliance.

entries.zh: 高祖大悅之，以為大宗伯。
entries.en: Gaozu was delighted and appointed him grand director of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased with him and made him Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 昂受拜之日，遂得偏風，不能視事。
entries.en: On the day of his appointment he suffered a stroke and could not take up his duties.
entries.literal: On the day Ang received the appointment he immediately suffered partial wind-stroke and could not handle affairs.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，昂疾愈，加上開府，拜潞州刺史。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne Ang recovered, was made upper pillar of state, and appointed prefect of Lu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication Ang's illness healed; he was added Upper Pillar of State and appointed Prefect of Lu.

entries.zh: 昂見天下無事，可以勸學行禮，因上表曰：
entries.en: Seeing the realm at peace, Ang memorialized that learning and ritual should be promoted:
entries.literal: Ang saw that under heaven all was peaceful and one could encourage learning and practice rites; he therefore submitted a memorial saying:

entries.zh: 韋世康，京兆杜陵人也，世為關右著姓。
entries.en: Wei Shikang, of Duling in Jingzhao, came from a family that for generations had ranked among the notable surnames of the Guanzhong region.
entries.literal: Wei Shikang—Wei Shikang was a native of Duling in Jingzhao; for generations his family had been a prominent clan of the Guanzhong west.

entries.zh: 祖旭，魏南幽州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Xu had served as inspector of Southern Youzhou under the Wei.
entries.literal: His grandfather Xu was Southern Youzhou Inspector under the Wei.

entries.zh: 父夐，隱居不仕，魏、週二代，十征不出，號為逍遙公。
entries.en: His father Jiong had retired from public life; summoned ten times under both Wei and Zhou, he never accepted appointment and was known as the Duke of Leisure.
entries.literal: His father Jiong lived in seclusion and did not take office; through the Wei and Zhou dynasties he was summoned ten times and did not emerge, and was styled the Carefree Duke.

entries.zh: 世康幼而沉敏，有器度。
entries.en: From childhood Shikang was thoughtful and quick-witted, with natural capacity and bearing.
entries.literal: Shikang in youth was deep and keen, and had breadth of character.

entries.zh: 年十歲，州辟主簿。
entries.en: At the age of ten he was recruited by his province as chief clerk.
entries.literal: At age ten he was summoned by the province as Registrar.

entries.zh: 在魏，弱冠為直寢，封漢安縣公，尚周文帝女襄樂公主，授儀同三司。
entries.en: While still young under the Northern Wei he entered the inner guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Zhou Emperor Wen, and received the rank of Pillar of State, Third Rank.
entries.literal: Under Wei, at weak cap he became Direct Attendant, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was appointed Pillar of State, Third Rank.

entries.zh: 後仕周，自典祠下大夫曆沔、硤二州刺史。
entries.en: He later served the Zhou, advancing from lower grand master of sacrifices to governor in turn of Mian and Qia.
entries.literal: Later he served Zhou, rising from Lower Grand Master of Sacrifices through the prefectures of Mian and Qia.

entries.zh: 從武帝平齊，授司州總管長史。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, he was made chief administrator on the staff of the Si Province commissioner-general.
entries.literal: Following Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Commissioner-General of Si Province.

entries.zh: 于時東夏初定，百姓未安，世康綏撫之，士民胥悅。
entries.en: The east had only just been pacified and the populace was still unsettled; Shikang reassured them until officials and people alike were content.
entries.literal: At that time the eastern regions had just been settled and the people were not yet at peace; Shikang soothed them, and gentry and commoners alike rejoiced.

entries.zh: 歲餘，入為民部中大夫，進位上開府，轉司會中大夫。
entries.en: A year later he was recalled to court as grand master of the ministry of the people, promoted to upper pillar of state, and then transferred to grand master of the department of accounts.
entries.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as Grand Master of the Ministry of the People, advanced to Upper Pillar of State, and transferred to Grand Master of the Department of Accounts.

entries.zh: 建安之後，海內大亂，京邑焚燒，憲章泯絕。
entries.en: After the Jian'an era, the realm fell into great disorder, the capital was burned, and statutes and regulations were lost.
entries.literal: After the Jian'an era, the realm fell into great disorder, the capital was burned, and statutes and regulations were extinguished.

entries.zh: 魏氏三方未平，無聞興造。
entries.en: The Wei house had not yet pacified the three regions, and nothing was heard of new construction.
entries.literal: The Wei house had not yet pacified the three regions, and nothing was heard of construction.

entries.zh: 晉則侍中裴頠議曰：「尊祖配天，其義明著，而廟宇之制，理據未分。
entries.en: Under Jin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Wei memorialized, saying, "Honoring the ancestors and matching Heaven—the meaning is clear; but the institution of temple buildings, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.
entries.literal: Under Jin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Wei memorialized, saying: "Honoring the ancestors and matching Heaven—the meaning is clear; but the institution of temple buildings, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.

entries.zh: 宜可直為一殿，以崇嚴父之祀，其餘雜碎，一皆除之。」
entries.en: It would be fitting to make simply one hall to exalt the sacrifice to the honored father; all the rest, miscellaneous and fragmentary, should be entirely removed."
entries.literal: It would be fitting to make simply one hall, to exalt the sacrifice to the honored father; all the rest, miscellaneous and fragmentary, should be entirely removed.

entries.zh: 宋、齊已還，鹹率茲禮。
entries.en: From Song and Qi onward, all followed this rite.
entries.literal: From Song and Qi onward, all followed this rite.

entries.zh: 此乃世之通儒，時無思術，前王盛事，於是不行。
entries.en: These were the universal Confucians of the age. The times lacked thoughtful methods, and the great affairs of former kings were thereby not carried out.
entries.literal: These were the universal Confucians of the age; the times lacked thoughtful methods, and the great affairs of former kings were thereby not carried out.

entries.zh: 後魏代都所造，出自李沖，三三相重，合為九室。
entries.en: What was built at the capital of Later Wei came from Li Chong: three by three layered together, making nine chambers in all.
entries.literal: What was built at the capital of Later Wei came from Li Chong: three by three layered together, making nine chambers in all.

entries.zh: 簷不覆基，房間通街，穿鑿處多，迄無可取。
entries.en: The eaves did not cover the foundation; rooms opened onto streets; there were many drilled and carved places—nothing in it was acceptable.
entries.literal: The eaves did not cover the foundation; rooms opened onto streets; there were many drilled and carved places—nothing in it was acceptable.

entries.zh: 及遷宅洛陽，更加營構，五九紛競，遂至不成，宗配之事，於焉靡托。
entries.en: When they moved the capital to Luoyang, they further undertook construction. Disputes over five chambers and nine chambers arose, and in the end it was not completed; the affairs of ancestral sacrifice and matching had nowhere to rest.
entries.literal: When they moved the seat to Luoyang, they further undertook construction; disputes over five chambers and nine chambers arose, and in the end it was not completed; the affairs of ancestral sacrifice and matching had nowhere to rest.

entries.zh: 隋書卷四十九列傳第十四
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume 49, Biographies 14
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Nine, Biographies Fourteen

entries.zh: 長孫覽，字休因，河南洛陽人也。
entries.en: Zhangsun Lan, whose courtesy name was Xiuyin, came from Luoyang in Henan.
entries.literal: Zhangsun Lan—Zhangsun Lan, courtesy name Xiuyin, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

entries.zh: 祖稚，魏太師、假黃鉞、上党文宣王。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhi had served as the Northern Wei's Grand Preceptor, held the provisional yellow battle-axe, and bore the title Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhi had been Grand Preceptor of Wei, holder of the provisional yellow battle-axe, and Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 父紹遠，周小宗伯、上党郡公。
entries.en: His father Shaoyuan had been the Northern Zhou's Junior Director of the Imperial Clan and Duke of Shangdang commandery.
entries.literal: His father Shaoyuan had been Junior Director of the Imperial Clan of Zhou and Duke of Shangdang commandery.

entries.zh: 覽性弘雅，有器量，略涉書記，尤曉鐘律。
entries.en: Lan was open and elegant in temperament, had breadth of mind, knew something of clerical work, and was particularly skilled in pitch pipes and musical theory.
entries.literal: Lan was magnanimous and refined in character, possessed capacity and measure, had a slight acquaintance with written records, and was especially versed in pitch pipes and musical scales.

entries.zh: 魏大統中，起家東宮親信。
entries.en: During the Northern Wei's Datong era he began his career as an intimate attendant in the crown prince's household.
entries.literal: In the Datong era of Northern Wei he first entered service as an intimate attendant in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 周明帝時，為大都督。
entries.en: Under Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou he held the post of Grand Commander-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou he served as Grand Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 武帝在籓，與覽親善，及即位，彌加禮焉，超拜車騎大將軍。
entries.en: While Yuwen Yong was still heir apparent he was close to Lan; once he became emperor he treated him with even greater honor and promoted him at a stroke to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu was still in his fief, he was on friendly terms with Lan; after he took the throne his courtesy toward him increased, and Lan was promoted in one step to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 每公卿上奏，必令省讀。
entries.en: Whenever ministers of state presented memorials, the emperor invariably had Lan review them first.
entries.literal: Whenever the high ministers submitted memorials, the emperor always had Lan read them over.

entries.zh: 覽有口辯，聲氣雄壯，凡所宣傳，百僚屬目，帝每嘉歎之。
entries.en: Lan was a gifted speaker with a powerful voice; whenever he delivered an imperial message the entire court watched him, and the emperor repeatedly expressed his admiration.
entries.literal: Lan had eloquence; his voice and bearing were imposing; whatever he announced, the hundred officials fixed their eyes upon him, and the emperor often praised and sighed over him.

entries.zh: 覽初名善，帝謂之曰：「朕以萬機，委卿先覽。」
entries.en: Lan had originally been named Shan. The emperor told him, "I am placing the weight of government upon you to review matters first."
entries.literal: Lan's original name had been Shan. The emperor said to him, "I entrust the myriad affairs of state to you for prior review."

entries.zh: 遂賜名焉。
entries.en: With that he gave him his present name.
entries.literal: Thereupon he bestowed the new name upon him.

entries.zh: 及誅宇文護，以功進封薛國公。
entries.en: After Yuwen Hu was killed, Lan was raised to Duke of Xue for his part in the plot.
entries.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, for his merit he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xue.

entries.zh: 其後曆小司空。
entries.en: He later served in turn as Junior Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Thereafter he successively held the post of Junior Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 從平齊，進位柱國，封第二子寬管國公。
entries.en: He took part in the conquest of Northern Qi, was promoted to Pillar of State, and his second son Kuan was enfeoffed as Duke of Guan.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign to pacify Qi, was promoted to Pillar of State, and his second son Kuan was enfeoffed as Duke of Guan state.

entries.zh: 宣帝時，進位上柱國、大司徒，俄曆同、涇二州刺史。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuan he rose to Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Education, and before long served in succession as governor of Tong and Jing prefectures.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Education, and soon afterward successively governed the two prefectures of Tong and Jing.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，轉宜州刺史。
entries.en: While Yang Jian was still Chancellor, Lan was reassigned as governor of Yi Prefecture.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor was Chancellor, Lan was transferred to Governor of Yi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 開皇二年，將有事於江南，征為東南道行軍元帥，統八總管出壽陽，水陸俱進。
entries.en: In the second year of Kaihuang (582), with war planned against the south, he was appointed campaigning commander-in-chief of the Southeast Circuit, leading eight area commanders from Shouyang in a combined land-and-water advance.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, as preparations were being made for operations in the Jiangnan region, he was summoned as campaigning commander-in-chief of the Southeast Circuit, commanding eight area commanders out of Shouyang, advancing by land and water together.

entries.zh: 師臨江，陳人大駭。
entries.en: As his forces approached the Yangtze, the Chen court was thrown into panic.
entries.literal: When the army reached the Yangtze, the people of Chen were greatly alarmed.

entries.zh: 會陳宣帝卒，覽欲乘釁遂滅之，監軍高熲以禮不伐喪而還。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan of Chen died, Lan wanted to exploit the moment and destroy Chen outright, but the supervising commander Gao Hui held that one must not campaign during a period of mourning and pulled the army back.
entries.literal: It happened that Emperor Xuan of Chen died; Lan wished to seize the opportunity and destroy Chen, but the supervising general Gao Hui, citing the rule that one does not attack during mourning, withdrew.

entries.zh: 上常命覽與安德王雄、上柱國元諧、李充、左僕射高熲、右衛大將軍虞慶則、吳州總管賀若弼等同宴，上曰：「朕昔在周朝，備展誠節，但苦猜忌，每致寒心。
entries.en: The emperor frequently had Lan dine with Prince Ande Xiong, Supreme Pillar of State Yuan Xie, Li Chong, Left Vice Director Gao Hui, General of the Right Guard Yu Qingze, and Wu Prefecture area commander He Ruo Bi, and said, "When I was still in the Zhou court I served with complete loyalty, yet I lived under endless suspicion and was repeatedly left heartsick.
entries.literal: The emperor often ordered Lan to feast together with Prince Ande Xiong, Supreme Pillar of State Yuan Xie, Li Chong, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Gao Hui, General of the Right Guard Yu Qingze, and Area Commander of Wu Prefecture He Ruo Bi, and said, "In former days in the Zhou court I showed every mark of loyalty, yet I suffered constant suspicion and was chilled at heart time and again.

entries.zh: 為臣若此，竟何情賴？
entries.en: What bond of trust can a minister have in such circumstances?
entries.literal: If a subject is treated thus, upon what affection may he rely?

entries.zh: 朕之於公，義則君臣，恩猶父子。
entries.en: In my dealings with you, duty makes us sovereign and subject, yet in feeling we are as father and son.
entries.literal: Between Us and you, the relation in duty is that of ruler and minister, but in affection it is like father and son.

entries.zh: 朕當與公共用終吉，罪非謀逆，一無所問。
entries.en: I intend to share lasting prosperity with you; short of plotting rebellion, you need fear no inquiry from me.
entries.literal: I shall share lasting good fortune with you; unless the crime is treason, I shall question you about nothing.

entries.zh: 朕亦知公至誠，特付太子，宜數參見之，庶得漸相親愛。
entries.en: I know your loyalty as well, and I am placing you especially in the service of the crown prince; visit him often so that affection may grow between you.
entries.literal: I also know your utmost sincerity and specially entrust you to the Crown Prince; you should visit him often, so that you may gradually grow close and fond of one another.

entries.zh: 柱臣素望，實屬於公，宜識朕意。」
entries.en: The chief support of the realm and its enduring hope truly lie with you—bear my meaning in mind."
entries.literal: The pillar of the state and its long-standing hope truly rest upon you; you should understand My intent."

entries.zh: 其恩禮如此。
entries.en: Such was the depth of favor and courtesy shown him.
entries.literal: His favor and courtesy were such as this.

entries.zh: 又為蜀王秀納覽女為妃。
entries.en: He also had Lan's daughter marry Prince Xiu of Shu.
entries.literal: He also had Lan's daughter taken in marriage for Prince Xiu of Shu.

entries.zh: 其後以母憂去職。
entries.en: He later resigned to observe mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: Later, on account of mourning for his mother, he left office.

entries.zh: 歲餘，起令復位。
entries.en: A little over a year later he was recalled to office.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was ordered to resume his post.

entries.zh: 俄轉涇州刺史，所在並有政績。
