entries.literal: Again he followed the Emperor in defeating Qi forces north of the Fen River, pressed the victory to take Gaobi, captured Jinyang, and at Jizhou seized Gao Jie—all with notable contribution.

entries.zh: 録前後功，加開府，別封蔡陽縣公，邑千戸。
entries.en: For his cumulative achievements he was granted an opened government office and separately enfeoffed as duke of Caiyang county with one thousand households.
entries.literal: Recording his earlier and later merit, he was granted the Opening of a Government Office and separately enfeoffed as Duke of Caiyang County with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 宣帝卽位，從韋孝寬略定淮南，毎爲先鋒。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan and always served as vanguard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan and each time served as vanguard.

entries.zh: 及淮南平，卽授淮州刺史，安集初附，甚得其歡心。
entries.en: When Huainan was pacified he was immediately made governor of Huaizhou; he settled the newly submitted population and greatly won their hearts.
entries.literal: When Huainan was pacified he was immediately appointed Governor of Huaizhou and settled the newly submitted population, greatly winning their hearts.

entries.zh: 髙祖受禪，加上開府，轉雲州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was granted senior opened office and transferred to governor of Yunzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, he was granted Senior Opening and transferred to Governor of Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 歳餘，征爲左武衞將軍。
entries.en: A little over a year later he was summoned as general of the left martial guard.
entries.literal: After a little more than a year he was summoned as General of the Left Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 及晉王廣之鎭并州也，朝廷妙選正人有文武才幹者，爲之僚佐。
entries.en: When Prince of Jin Guang was stationed at Bingzhou, the court carefully selected upright men of civil and military talent for his staff.
entries.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang was stationed at Bingzhou, the court carefully selected upright men with both civil and military talent to serve as his staff.

entries.zh: 上以徹前代舊臣，數持軍旅，詔徹總晉王府軍事，進爵齊安郡公。
entries.en: Because Che was an old minister who had often held military command, the emperor ordered him to oversee all military affairs of Prince Jin's household and raised him to duke of Qi'an commandery.
entries.literal: The Emperor, because Che was an old minister of the previous dynasty who had often held military command, ordered him to oversee all military affairs of the Prince of Jin's household and advanced him to Duke of Qi'an Commandery.

entries.zh: 時蜀王秀亦鎮益州，上謂侍臣曰：「安得文同王子相，武如李廣達者乎？」
entries.en: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu was also stationed at Yizhou; the emperor said to his attendants, "Where can I find a civil adviser like Wang Zixiang and a military one like Li Guangda?"
entries.literal: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu was also stationed at Yizhou; the Emperor said to his attendants: "Where can I find a civil adviser like Wang Zixiang and a military one like Li Guangda?"

entries.zh: 其見重如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

entries.zh: 崔彭，字子彭，博陵安平人也。
entries.en: Cui Peng, styled Zipeng, came from Anping in Boling.
entries.literal: Cui Peng, courtesy name Zipeng, was a native of Anping in Boling.

entries.zh: 祖楷，魏殷州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Kai had been governor of Yinzhou under Wei.
entries.literal: His grandfather Kai was Governor of Yinzhou under Wei.

entries.zh: 父謙，周荊州總管。
entries.en: His father Qian had been area commander of Jingzhou under Zhou.
entries.literal: His father Qian was Area Commander of Jingzhou under Zhou.

entries.zh: 彭少孤，事母以孝聞。
entries.en: Orphaned young, Peng was known for filial devotion to his mother.
entries.literal: Peng was orphaned young and was known for filial service to his mother.

entries.zh: 性剛毅，有武略，工騎射。
entries.en: Resolute and firm by nature, he had military stratagem and was skilled in mounted archery.
entries.literal: He was resolute and firm by nature, had military stratagem, and was skilled in mounted archery.

entries.zh: 善《周官》、《尚書》，略通大義。
entries.en: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou and the Book of Documents and had a general grasp of their meaning.
entries.literal: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou and the Book of Documents and had a general grasp of their essential meaning.

entries.zh: 周武帝時，為侍伯上士，累轉門正上士。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was senior attendant of the palace guard and rose to senior attendant of the gate guard.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Senior Attendant of the Palace Guard and was transferred in succession to Senior Attendant of the Gate Guard.

entries.zh: 及高祖為丞相，周陳王純鎮齊州，高祖恐純為變，遣彭以兩騎征純入朝。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen was chancellor, Prince Chen Chun of Zhou was stationed at Qizhou; fearing rebellion, the emperor sent Peng with two mounted escorts to summon Chun to court.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, Prince Chen Chun of Zhou was stationed at Qizhou; the Emperor feared Chun might rebel and dispatched Peng with two mounted escorts to summon Chun to court.

entries.zh: 彭未至齊州三十裡，因詐病，止傳舍，遣人謂純曰：「天子有詔書至王所，彭苦疾，不能強步，願王降臨之。」
entries.en: Thirty li from Qizhou Peng feigned illness, stopped at a relay station, and sent word to Chun: "The Son of Heaven has an edict for Your Highness; Peng is too ill to walk—please come to me."
entries.literal: When Peng was still thirty li from Qizhou he feigned illness, stopped at a relay station, and sent a man to tell Chun: "The Son of Heaven has an edict arriving at Your Highness's place; Peng suffers severe illness and cannot force himself to walk—Your Highness, please come down to me."

entries.zh: 純疑有變，多將從騎至彭所。
entries.en: Chun suspected trouble and came with many mounted followers.
entries.literal: Chun suspected something amiss and brought many mounted followers to Peng's place.

entries.zh: 彭出傳舍迎之，察純有疑色，恐不就征，因詐純曰：「王可避人，將密有所道。」
entries.en: Peng came out to meet him, saw suspicion on Chun's face, and fearing refusal, deceived him: "Your Highness may dismiss your attendants—I have something confidential to say."
entries.literal: Peng came out of the relay station to meet him, saw suspicion on Chun's face, and fearing he would not obey the summons, therefore deceived Chun, saying: "Your Highness may dismiss your attendants; I have something confidential to convey."

entries.zh: 純麾從騎，彭又曰：「將宣詔，王可下馬。」
entries.en: Chun dismissed his followers; Peng said again, "I am about to proclaim the edict—Your Highness should dismount."
entries.literal: Chun waved his followers away; Peng again said: "I am about to proclaim the edict—Your Highness may dismount."

entries.zh: 純遽下，彭顧其騎士曰：「陳王不從詔征，可執也。」
entries.en: Chun hurriedly dismounted; Peng turned to his horsemen and said, "Prince Chen refuses the summons—seize him."
entries.literal: Chun hurriedly dismounted; Peng turned to his horsemen and said: "Prince Chen refuses the edict summoning him to court—seize him."

entries.zh: 騎士因執而鎖之。
entries.en: The horsemen seized and shackled him.
entries.literal: The horsemen thereupon seized and shackled him.

entries.zh: 彭乃大言曰：「陳王有罪，詔征入朝，左右不得輒動。」
entries.en: Peng then declared loudly, "Prince Chen is guilty; by edict he is summoned to court—attendants must not move."
entries.literal: Peng then declared loudly: "Prince Chen is guilty; by edict he is summoned to court—attendants may not move rashly."

entries.zh: 其從者愕然而去。
entries.en: His followers stood stunned and departed.
entries.literal: His followers stood stunned and departed.

entries.zh: 高祖見而大悅，拜上儀同。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and made Peng senior equal honor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen saw this he was greatly pleased and appointed Peng Senior Equal Honor.

entries.zh: 及踐阼，遷監門郎將，兼領右衛長史，賜爵安陽縣男。
entries.en: When he ascended the throne, Peng became commandant of the gate guard and chief administrator of the right guard, and was enfeoffed as viscount of Anyang county.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne, Peng was transferred to Commandant of the Gate Guard and concurrently Chief Administrator of the Right Guard, and was granted the title Viscount of Anyang County.

entries.zh: 數歲，轉車騎將軍，俄轉驃騎，恆典宿衛。
entries.en: After several years he became general of chariots and cavalry, then general of fast cavalry, and constantly held charge of the palace guard.
entries.literal: After several years he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry, soon to General of Fast Cavalry, and constantly held charge of the palace guard.

entries.zh: 性謹密，在省闥二十餘年，每當上在仗，危坐終日，未嘗有怠惰之容，上甚嘉之。
entries.en: Careful and discreet by nature, for more than twenty years in the inner precincts he sat upright all day whenever the emperor was on armed duty and never showed negligence; the emperor greatly praised him.
entries.literal: He was careful and discreet by nature; for more than twenty years in the inner precincts, whenever the Emperor was on duty with arms he sat upright all day and never showed a negligent bearing, and the Emperor greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 上每謂彭曰：「卿當上日，我寢處自安。」
entries.en: The emperor often told Peng, "On the days you are on duty I sleep at ease."
entries.literal: The Emperor often said to Peng: "On the days you are on duty I sleep at ease."

entries.zh: 又嘗曰：「卿弓馬固以絕人，頗知學不？」
entries.en: He also once asked, "Your bow and horse skills are truly unmatched—do you know anything of learning?"
entries.literal: He also once said: "Your bow and horse skills are truly unmatched—do you know anything of learning?"

entries.zh: 彭曰：「臣少愛《周禮》、《尚書》，每於休沐之暇，不敢廢也。」
entries.en: Peng replied, "Your subject has loved the Rites of Zhou and the Book of Documents from youth, and never neglects them even on rest days."
entries.literal: Peng replied: "Your subject from youth has loved the Rites of Zhou and the Book of Documents, and in the leisure of rest days I have never neglected them."

entries.zh: 上曰：「試為我言之。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Then tell me something of them."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Try telling me something of them."

entries.zh: 彭因說君臣戒慎之義，上稱善。
entries.en: Peng expounded the doctrine of vigilance between ruler and minister, and the emperor praised it.
entries.literal: Peng thereupon expounded the doctrine of vigilance between ruler and minister, and the Emperor praised it.

entries.zh: 觀者以為知言。
entries.en: Those who witnessed it considered his words well chosen.
entries.literal: Those who witnessed it considered his words well chosen.

entries.zh: 後加上開府，遷備身將軍。
entries.en: He was later granted senior opened office and made general of the personal guard.
entries.literal: Later he was granted Senior Opening and transferred to General of the Personal Guard.

entries.zh: 明年，突厥沙缽略可汗犯塞，上令衛王爽為元帥，率眾擊之，以徹為長史。
entries.en: The following year the Turkic qaghan Shaboluoe raided the frontier; the emperor made Prince Wei Shuang supreme commander and Che his chief of staff.
entries.literal: The next year the Turkic qaghan Shaboluoe raided the frontier; the Emperor appointed Prince Wei Shuang supreme commander to lead troops against him, with Che as chief of staff.

entries.zh: 遇虜于白道，行軍總管李充言於爽曰：「周、齊之世，有同戰國，中夏力分，其來久矣。
entries.en: They encountered the enemy at Baidao; campaign commander Li Chong said to Shuang, "In the Zhou and Qi eras the realm was divided like the Warring States period, and this has long been so.
entries.literal: They encountered the enemy at Baidao; Campaign Commander Li Chong said to Shuang: "In the eras of Zhou and Qi it was like the Warring States period—the Central Lands were divided in strength, and this has long been so.

entries.zh: 突厥每侵邊，諸將輒以全軍為計，莫能死戰。
entries.en: Whenever the Turks raided the frontier, generals always made preserving the whole army their plan and none would fight to the death.
entries.literal: Whenever the Turks raided the frontier, generals always made preserving the whole army their plan and none would fight to the death.

entries.zh: 由是突厥勝多敗少，所以每輕中國之師。
entries.en: Hence the Turks won more often than they lost and always looked down on Chinese armies.
entries.literal: Hence the Turks won more often than they lost, and so they always looked down on the armies of the Central Lands.

entries.zh: 今者沙缽略悉國內之眾，屯據要險，必輕我而無備，精兵襲之，可破也。」
entries.en: Now Shaboluoe has mobilized all his forces and holds the strategic passes; he is sure to underestimate us and be unprepared—a strike with elite troops can break him."
entries.literal: Now Shaboluoe has mobilized all the forces within his realm and holds strategic passes; he is sure to underestimate us and be unprepared—a strike with elite troops can break him."

entries.zh: 爽從之。
entries.en: Shuang followed his advice.
entries.literal: Shuang followed his advice.

entries.zh: 諸將多以為疑，唯徹獎成其計，請與同行。
entries.en: Most of the generals were doubtful, but Che alone encouraged the plan and asked to go with them.
entries.literal: Most of the generals were doubtful, but only Che encouraged the plan and asked to go with them.

entries.zh: 遂與充率精騎五千，出其不意，掩擊大破之。
entries.en: Che and Chong then led five thousand elite cavalry, caught the enemy unawares, and routed them completely in a surprise attack.
entries.literal: Thereupon he and Chong led five thousand elite cavalry, caught the enemy unawares, and struck them in a surprise attack, routing them completely.

entries.zh: 沙缽略棄所服金甲，潛草中而遁。
entries.en: Shaboluoe abandoned the golden armor he was wearing and fled hidden in the grass.
entries.literal: Shaboluoe abandoned the golden armor he was wearing and fled hidden in the grass.

entries.zh: 以功加上大將軍。
entries.en: For his merit he was promoted to grand general-in-chief.
entries.literal: For merit he was promoted to Grand General-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 沙缽略因此屈膝稱籓。
entries.en: Because of this Shaboluoe bowed in submission and declared himself a vassal.
entries.literal: Because of this Shaboluoe bowed in submission and declared himself a vassal.

entries.zh: 未幾，沙缽略為阿拔所侵，上疏請援。
entries.en: Before long Shaboluoe was invaded by Aba and submitted a memorial requesting aid.
entries.literal: Before long Shaboluoe was invaded by Aba and submitted a memorial requesting aid.

entries.zh: 以徹為行軍總管，率精騎一萬赴之。
entries.en: Che was made campaign commander and led ten thousand elite cavalry to his relief.
entries.literal: Che was appointed Campaign Commander and led ten thousand elite cavalry to go to his aid.

entries.zh: 阿拔聞而遁去。
entries.en: Hearing of Che's approach, Aba fled.
entries.literal: When Aba heard of it he fled.

entries.zh: 及軍還，複領行軍總管，屯平涼以備胡寇，封安道郡公。
entries.en: When the army returned, Che again served as campaign commander, encamped at Pingliang against barbarian raids, and was enfeoffed as duke of Andao commandery.
entries.literal: When the army returned, Che again held the post of Campaign Commander, encamped at Pingliang to guard against barbarian raiders, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Andao Commandery.

entries.zh: 開皇十年，進位柱國。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Kaihuang he was raised to pillar of the state.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang he was promoted to Pillar of the State.

entries.zh: 及晉王廣轉牧淮海，以徹為揚州總管司馬，改封德廣郡公。
entries.en: When Prince of Jin Guang was transferred to govern the Huaihai region, Che was made chief administrator to the Yangzhou area command and re-enfeoffed as duke of Deguang commandery.
entries.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang was transferred to govern the Huaihai region, Che was appointed Chief Administrator to the Area Commander of Yangzhou and his title was changed to Duke of Deguang Commandery.

entries.zh: 尋徙封城陽郡公。
entries.en: He was soon re-enfeoffed as duke of Chengyang commandery.
entries.literal: Soon his fief was moved to Duke of Chengyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 其後突厥犯塞，徹複領行軍總管擊破之。
entries.en: Later, when the Turks raided the frontier, Che again served as campaign commander and routed them.
entries.literal: Afterward, when the Turks raided the frontier, Che again served as Campaign Commander and defeated them.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，遷左領軍大將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Peng was transferred to grand general of the Left Leading Army.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Peng was transferred to Grand General of the Left Leading Army.

entries.zh: 從幸洛陽，彭督後軍。
entries.en: Accompanying the emperor to Luoyang, Peng commanded the rear guard.
entries.literal: Accompanying the Emperor on a visit to Luoyang, Peng commanded the rear guard.

entries.zh: 時漢王諒初平，餘黨往往屯聚，令彭率衆數萬鎭遏山東，復領慈州事。
entries.en: With Liang, the Prince of Han, just pacified and remnant factions gathering, the emperor ordered Peng to lead tens of thousands of men to suppress the east of the mountains and again to hold charge of Cizhou.
entries.literal: At the time Liang, the Prince of Han, had just been pacified and remnant factions were often gathering; the Emperor ordered Peng to lead several tens of thousands of men to suppress the east of the mountains and again to hold charge of Cizhou affairs.

entries.zh: 帝以其淸，賜絹五百匹。
entries.en: The emperor granted him five hundred bolts of silk for his integrity.
entries.literal: The Emperor, because of his integrity, granted five hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 未幾而卒，時年六十三。
entries.en: Before long he died at the age of sixty-three.
entries.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-three.

entries.zh: 帝遣使弔祭，贈大將軍，諡曰肅。
entries.en: The emperor sent envoys to mourn him and posthumously invested him as grand general with the posthumous name Su.
entries.literal: The Emperor dispatched an envoy to offer mourning sacrifices and posthumously granted him Grand General with the posthumous title Su.

entries.zh: 子寶德嗣。
entries.en: His son Baode succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Baode succeeded.

entries.zh: 隋書卷五十四列傳第十九
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume 54, Biography 19
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 54, Biography 19

entries.zh: 杜彥，雲中人也。
entries.en: Du Yan was from Yunzhong.
entries.literal: Du Yan—Du Yan was a native of Yunzhong.

entries.zh: 父遷，屬葛榮之亂，徙家於幽。
entries.en: During Ge Rong's rebellion, his father Qian relocated the household to Youzhou.
entries.literal: His father Qian, during Ge Rong's rebellion, moved the family to You.

entries.zh: 彥性勇果，善騎射。
entries.en: Yan was bold and decisive by nature and excelled at horseback archery.
entries.literal: Yan by nature was brave and resolute, skilled in mounted archery.

entries.zh: 仕周，釋褐左侍上士，後從柱國陸通擊陳將吳明徹於土州，破之。
entries.en: He entered Zhou service as Left Attendant Senior Clerk and later followed Pillar of State Lu Tong to attack the Chen general Wu Mingche at Tuzhou and rout him.
entries.literal: He served Zhou, upon first appointment becoming Left Attendant Senior Clerk; later he followed the pillar of state Lu Tong in attacking the Chen general Wu Mingche at Tuzhou and defeated him.

entries.zh: 又擊叛蠻，克倉塠、白楊二柵，並斬其渠帥。
entries.en: He also campaigned against rebel tribes, took the stockades at Cangdui and Baiyang, and executed their leaders.
entries.literal: He again attacked rebel barbarians, captured the two stockades of Cangdui and Baiyang, and beheaded their chieftains.

entries.zh: 進平郢州賊帥樊志，以戰功拜大都督。
entries.en: He advanced to suppress the Yingzhou rebel Fan Zhi and, for his victories, was appointed Grand Commander.
entries.literal: Advancing, he pacified the Yingzhou bandit leader Fan Zhi and, for battle merit, was appointed Grand Commander.

entries.zh: 尋遷儀同，治隆山郡事。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Yitong and put in charge of Longshan commandery.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Yitong and administered the affairs of Longshan commandery.

entries.zh: 明年，拜隴州刺史，賜爵永安縣伯。
entries.en: The following year he became prefect of Longzhou and was created Baron of Yong'an.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed prefect of Longzhou and ennobled as Baron of Yong'an county.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉迥於相州，每戰有功，賜物三千段，奴婢三十口。
entries.en: While Gaozu was still chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuchi Jiong at Xiangzhou, distinguishing himself in every engagement and receiving three thousand bolts of goods and thirty slaves.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuchi Jiong at Xiangzhou; in every battle he had merit, and was granted three thousand bolts of goods and thirty household slaves.

entries.zh: 進位上開府，改封襄武縣侯，拜魏郡太守。
entries.en: He was promoted to Senior Commander-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangwu, and appointed administrator of Wei commandery.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Senior Commander-in-Chief, his fief changed to Marquis of Xiangwu county, and he was appointed administrator of Wei commandery.

entries.zh: 開皇初，授丹州刺史，進爵為公。
entries.en: Early in the Kaihuang era he was made prefect of Danzhou and raised to ducal rank.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed prefect of Danzhou and advanced in rank to duke.

entries.zh: 後六歲，征為左武衛將軍。
entries.en: Six years later he was recalled to the capital as general of the Left Martial Guard.
entries.literal: Six years later he was summoned to serve as general of the Left Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管與新義公韓擒相繼而進。
entries.en: During the conquest of Chen he served as campaign commander, advancing in concert with Duke of Xinyi Han Qin.
entries.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, as campaign commander he advanced in succession with the Duke of Xinyi, Han Qin.

entries.zh: 軍至南陵，賊屯據江岸，彥遣儀同樊子蓋率精兵擊破其柵，獲船六百餘艘。
entries.en: At Nanling the enemy held the riverbank; Yan sent Yitong Fan Zigai with an elite force to break their stockade and capture more than six hundred vessels.
entries.literal: When the army reached Nanling, the enemy held the riverbank; Yan sent Yitong Fan Zigai at the head of picked troops to smash their palisade and seize more than six hundred boats.

entries.zh: 渡江，擊南陵城，拔之，擒其守將許翼。
entries.en: He crossed the Yangzi, stormed Nanling, took the city, and captured its commander Xu Yi.
entries.literal: Crossing the river, he attacked Nanling city, took it, and captured its defending general Xu Yi.

entries.zh: 進至新林，與擒合軍。
entries.en: He pushed on to Xinlin and joined forces with Han Qin.
entries.literal: Advancing to Xinlin, he united his forces with Qin's.

entries.zh: 及陳平，賜物五千段，粟六千石，進位柱國，賜子寶安爵昌陽縣公。
entries.en: After Chen fell he received five thousand bolts of goods and six thousand piculs of grain, was promoted to Pillar of State, and his son Bao'an was created Duke of Changyang.
entries.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was granted five thousand bolts of goods and six thousand piculs of grain, advanced to Pillar of State, and his son Bao'an was ennobled as Duke of Changyang county.

entries.zh: 高智慧等之作亂也，複以行軍總管從楊素討之，別解江州圍。
entries.en: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled, he again served as campaign commander under Yang Su and on his own broke the siege of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rose in rebellion, he again served as campaign commander following Yang Su to suppress them and separately lifted the siege of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 智慧餘黨往往屯聚，保投溪洞，彥水陸兼進，攻錦山、陽父、若、石壁四洞，悉平之，皆斬其渠帥。
entries.en: Zhihui's scattered followers held out in mountain ravines; Yan struck by land and water, reduced the strongholds at Jinshan, Yangfu, Ruo, and Shibi, and executed their leaders.
entries.literal: Zhihui's remaining partisans often gathered and took refuge in stream caves; Yan advanced by land and water, attacked the four lairs of Jinshan, Yangfu, Ruo, and Shibi, pacified them all, and beheaded their chieftains.

entries.zh: 賊李陀擁眾數千，據彭山，彥襲擊破之，斬陀，傳其首。
entries.en: The rebel Li Tuo gathered several thousand men on Pengshan; Yan surprised and routed him, killed Tuo, and forwarded his head.
entries.literal: The bandit Li Tuo mustered several thousand men and held Pengshan; Yan raided and defeated him, beheaded Tuo, and sent his head to the capital.

entries.zh: 又擊徐州、宜豐二洞，悉平之。
entries.en: He also subdued the rebel bases at Xuzhou and Yifeng.
entries.literal: He again attacked the two lairs of Xuzhou and Yifeng and pacified them completely.

entries.zh: 賜奴婢百餘口。
entries.en: He was rewarded with more than a hundred slaves.
entries.literal: He was granted more than a hundred household slaves.

entries.zh: 拜洪州總管，甚有治名。
entries.en: Appointed regional commander of Hongzhou, he earned a strong reputation for effective administration.
entries.literal: He was appointed regional commander of Hongzhou and gained a great reputation for good governance.

entries.zh: 歲餘，雲州總管賀婁子幹卒，上悼惜者久之，因謂侍臣曰：「榆林國之重鎮，安得子幹之輩乎？」
entries.en: A year later Yunzhou commander Helou Zigan died. The emperor grieved for him at length and told his courtiers, "Yulin is a strategic bulwark of the realm—where shall we find another man like Zigan?"
entries.literal: After more than a year, Yunzhou regional commander Helou Zigan died; the emperor mourned him for a long time and said to his attendants: "Yulin is a vital fortress of the state—where can we find men like Zigan?"

entries.zh: 後數日，上曰：「吾思可以鎮榆林者，莫過杜彥。」
entries.en: A few days later he said, "When I think who should hold Yulin, no one surpasses Du Yan."
entries.literal: Several days later the emperor said: "When I consider who could guard Yulin, none surpasses Du Yan."

entries.zh: 於是征拜雲州總管。
entries.en: He was then recalled and appointed regional commander of Yunzhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was summoned and appointed regional commander of Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 突厥來寇，彥輒擒斬之，北夷畏憚，胡馬不敢至塞。
entries.en: Whenever Turks raided, Yan captured and executed them; the northern peoples stood in awe of him, and their horsemen no longer dared approach the border.
entries.literal: When the Turks came to raid, Yan would capture and behead them; the northern barbarians feared him, and Turkic horses dared not approach the frontier.

entries.zh: 後數年，朝廷複追錄前功，賜子寶虔爵承縣公。
entries.en: Some years later the court again recorded his earlier merit and created his son Baoqian Duke of Cheng.
entries.literal: Several years later the court again recorded his earlier merit and ennobled his son Baoqian as Duke of Cheng county.

entries.zh: 十八年，遼東之役，以行軍總管從漢王至營州。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, during the Liaodong campaign, he served as campaign commander under the Prince of Han and marched to Yingzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, as campaign commander he followed the Prince of Han to Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 上以彥曉習軍旅，令總統五十營事。
entries.en: Knowing Yan's mastery of military affairs, the emperor put him in overall charge of fifty camps.
entries.literal: Because the emperor knew Yan was versed in military affairs, he ordered him to oversee the affairs of fifty camps.

entries.zh: 及還，拜朔州總管。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed regional commander of Shuozhou.
entries.literal: Upon his return he was appointed regional commander of Shuozhou.

entries.zh: 突厥複寇雲州，上令楊素擊走之，是後猶恐為邊患，以彥素為突厥所憚，複拜雲州總管。
entries.en: When the Turks raided Yunzhou again, the emperor sent Yang Su to repel them; still anxious about the frontier, and knowing the Turks feared Yan, he reappointed him commander of Yunzhou.
entries.literal: The Turks again raided Yunzhou; the emperor ordered Yang Su to drive them off. Still fearing border trouble afterward, and because Yan had long been feared by the Turks, he was again appointed regional commander of Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 未幾，以疾征還，卒，時年六十。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was recalled because of illness and died at sixty.
entries.literal: Before long, recalled on account of illness, he died at the age of sixty.

entries.zh: 子寶虔，大業末，文城郡丞。
entries.en: His son Baoqian served late in the Daye era as assistant administrator of Wencheng commandery.
entries.literal: His son Baoqian, at the end of the Daye era, was assistant administrator of Wencheng commandery.

entries.zh: 高勱高勱，字敬德，渤海蓚人也，齊太尉、清河王嶽之子也。
entries.en: Gao Mai, courtesy name Jingde, was from Tiao in Bohai, the son of Qi Grand Marshal and Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue.
entries.literal: Gao Mai—Gao Mai, courtesy name Jingde, was a native of Tiao in Bohai, son of Qi Grand Marshal and Prince of Qinghe, Gao Yue.

entries.zh: 幼聰敏，美風儀，以仁孝聞，為齊顯祖所愛。
entries.en: Even as a boy he was quick-witted and handsome, famed for kindness and filial devotion, and a favorite of Qi Emperor Xianzu.
entries.literal: As a child he was clever, of fine bearing, renowned for benevolence and filial piety, and beloved by Emperor Xianzu of Qi.

entries.zh: 年七歲，襲爵清河王。
entries.en: At seven he inherited the title Prince of Qinghe.
entries.literal: At age seven he inherited the title Prince of Qinghe.

entries.zh: 十四為青州刺史，曆右衛將軍、領軍大將軍、祠部尚書、開府儀同三司，改封樂安王。
entries.en: At fourteen he was made prefect of Qingzhou and later held posts as general of the Right Guard, commander of the Palace Guard, minister of sacrifices, and Kaifu Yitong Sansi, eventually being enfeoffed as Prince of Le'an.
entries.literal: At fourteen he became prefect of Qingzhou, and successively served as general of the Right Guard, commander of the Palace Guard, minister of the Directorate of Sacrifices, and Kaifu Yitong Sansi; his fief was changed to Prince of Le'an.

entries.zh: 性剛直，有才幹，甚為時人所重。
entries.en: Upright and capable by nature, he was widely esteemed in his day.
entries.literal: By nature he was upright and firm, talented and capable, and greatly respected by men of his time.

entries.zh: 斛律明月雅敬之，每有征伐，則引之為副。
entries.en: Hulü Mingyue admired him greatly and always took him as second-in-command on campaign.
entries.literal: Hulü Mingyue held him in high esteem; whenever there was a campaign, he would take Mai as his deputy.

entries.zh: 遷侍中、尚書右僕射。
entries.en: He rose to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 及後主為周師所敗，勱奉太后歸鄴。
entries.en: When the Later Ruler was routed by Zhou forces, Mai escorted the empress dowager back to Ye.
entries.literal: When the Later Ruler was defeated by Zhou troops, Mai escorted the empress dowager back to Ye.

entries.zh: 時宦官放縱，儀同苟子溢尤稱寵倖，勱將斬之以徇。
entries.en: Eunuchs were running wild at court; Yitong Gou Ziyi was a particular favorite, and Mai was on the point of executing him as an example.
entries.literal: At the time eunuchs ran rampant; Yitong Gou Ziyi was especially favored, and Mai was about to behead him as a warning.

entries.zh: 太后救之，乃釋。
entries.en: The empress dowager intervened and Mai let him go.
entries.literal: The empress dowager rescued him, and Mai released him.

entries.zh: 劉文殊竊謂勱曰：「子溢之徒，言成禍福，何得如此！」
entries.en: Liu Wenshu whispered to Mai, "Men like Ziyi can make or break you with a word—how can you go so far!"
entries.literal: Liu Wenshu privately said to Mai: "Men like Ziyi can make fortune or ruin with a word—how can you act like this!"

entries.zh: 勱攘袂曰：「今者西寇日侵，朝貴多叛，正由此輩弄權，致使衣冠解體。
entries.en: Mai flung up his sleeves and said, "The western foe advances daily and great families are defecting—because men like these abuse power and have torn the court apart.
entries.literal: Mai rolled up his sleeves and said: "Now the western enemy presses daily, and many court nobles have defected—precisely because this lot manipulate power and have brought the ruling class to ruin.

entries.zh: 若得今日殺之，明日受誅，無所恨也。」
entries.en: If I could kill him today and die tomorrow, I would not regret it."
entries.literal: If I could kill him today and be executed tomorrow, I would have no regret."

entries.zh: 文殊甚愧。
entries.en: Wenshu was deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: Wenshu was deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: 既至鄴，勱勸後主：「五品已上家累，悉置三台之上，因脅之曰：'若戰不捷，則燒之。
entries.en: Once in Ye, Mai urged the Later Ruler: "Gather the families of every official of the fifth rank and above on the Three Platforms and tell them, 'If we do not win, we burn them.
entries.literal: When they reached Ye, Mai advised the Later Ruler: "Place the families of all officials of the fifth rank and above on the Three Platforms, and threaten them, saying: 'If the battle is not won, they will be burned.

entries.zh: '此輩惜妻子，必當死戰，可敗也。」
entries.en: They love their wives and children and will fight to the death—we can defeat the enemy.'"
entries.literal: These men cherish wife and children and will surely fight to the death—the enemy can be defeated.'"

entries.zh: 後主不從，遂棄鄴東遁。
entries.en: The Later Ruler refused, abandoned Ye, and fled east.
entries.literal: The Later Ruler would not follow this advice and abandoned Ye, fleeing east.

entries.zh: 勱恆後殿，為周軍所得。
entries.en: Mai always commanded the rearguard and was captured by Zhou forces.
entries.literal: Mai always brought up the rear and was captured by Zhou troops.

entries.zh: 武帝見之，與語，大悅，因問齊亡所由。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou met him, spoke with him, and was delighted; he then asked why Qi had perished.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him, spoke with him, and was greatly pleased; he then asked the cause of Qi's fall.

entries.zh: 勱發言流涕，悲不自勝，帝亦為之改容。
entries.en: Mai spoke through tears, overcome with grief, and the emperor's expression softened in sympathy.
entries.literal: As Mai spoke he wept, overcome with grief; the emperor too changed countenance for his sake.

entries.zh: 授開府儀同三司。
entries.en: He was appointed Palatine Unequalled in Honor.
entries.literal: He was appointed Palatine Unequalled in Honor.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，謂勱曰：「齊所以亡者，由任邪佞。
entries.en: While Gaozu was still chief minister, he told Mai, "Qi fell because it trusted wicked flatterers.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, he said to Mai: "Qi perished because it employed wicked flatterers.

entries.zh: 公父子忠良，聞於鄰境，宜善自愛。」
entries.en: Your father and you are known beyond the borders for loyalty—take good care of yourselves."
entries.literal: Your father and you are loyal and good, renowned in neighboring states—you should take good care of yourselves."

entries.zh: 勱再拜謝曰：「勱亡齊末屬，世荷恩榮，不能扶危定傾，以致淪覆。
entries.en: Mai bowed deeply and said, "I am a remnant of fallen Qi; my family long enjoyed imperial favor, yet I could not save the state from collapse.
entries.literal: Mai bowed twice and replied: "Mai is a remnant subject of fallen Qi; my house has long received favor and glory, yet I could not shore up peril and steady the tipping state, and so ruin came.

entries.zh: 既蒙獲宥，恩幸已多，況複濫叨名位，致速官謗。」
entries.en: I have already been shown more mercy than I deserve; to accept office on top of that would only invite reproach."
entries.literal: Having been spared, I have already received excessive grace; how much more if I undeservedly accept rank and office and hasten official censure."

entries.zh: 高祖甚器之，以勱檢校揚州事。
entries.en: Gaozu esteemed him greatly and placed him in provisional charge of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Gaozu thought highly of him and put Mai in charge of Yangzhou affairs on probation.

entries.zh: 後拜楚州刺史，民安之。
entries.en: He was later appointed prefect of Chuzhou, where the people lived in peace under his rule.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed prefect of Chuzhou, and the people were at peace under him.

entries.zh: 先是，城北有伍子胥廟，其俗敬鬼。
entries.en: North of the city stood a temple to Wu Zixu, and the people were devoted to spirit worship.
entries.literal: Earlier, north of the city wall there was a temple to Wu Zixu; the local custom was to revere spirits.

entries.zh: 祈禱者必以牛酒，至破產業。
entries.en: Worshippers had to sacrifice cattle and wine, often until their families were ruined.
entries.literal: Those who prayed had to offer cattle and wine, even to the ruin of their households.

entries.zh: 勱歎曰：「子胥賢者，豈宜損百姓乎？」
entries.en: Mai sighed and said, "Zixu was a worthy man—would he want the people ruined?"
entries.literal: Mai sighed and said: "Zixu was a worthy man—how could he wish to harm the common people?"

entries.zh: 乃告諭所部，自此遂止，百姓賴之。
entries.en: He issued orders throughout his district, the practice stopped, and the people were grateful.
entries.literal: He then issued proclamations throughout his jurisdiction; from then on the practice ceased, and the people were indebted to him.

entries.zh: 七年，轉光州刺史，上取陳五策，又上表曰：「臣聞夷凶翦暴，王者之懋功；
entries.en: In the seventh year he became prefect of Guang Prefecture, submitted five plans against Chen, and memorialized: "I have heard that subduing barbarian violence is the supreme achievement of a true king;
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be prefect of Guang Prefecture; he submitted five stratagems against Chen and also memorialized: "Your servant has heard that cutting down barbarian foes and eliminating the violent is the king's great merit;

entries.zh: 取亂侮亡，往賢之雅誥。
entries.en: and that striking a tottering foe is the counsel of the ancient sages.
entries.literal: to take advantage of disorder and insult the perishing is the elegant admonition of former worthies.

entries.zh: 是以苗民逆命，爰興兩階之舞；
entries.en: When the Miao rebelled, the dance of the two courts was staged;
entries.literal: Therefore when the Miao people defied orders, the dance of the two staircases was performed;

entries.zh: 有扈不賓，終召六師之伐。
entries.en: when Youhu refused allegiance, the six hosts were finally sent against them.
entries.literal: when Youhu failed to submit, in the end the six armies were summoned to punish them.

entries.zh: 皆所以寧一宇內，匡濟群生者也。
entries.en: All to bring peace under heaven and deliver the people.
entries.literal: All these were means to pacify the realm under heaven and succor the multitude of living beings.

entries.zh: 自昔晉氏失馭，天網絕維，群凶於焉蝟起，三方因而鼎立。
entries.en: Ever since the Jin lost control and order collapsed, rebels sprang up everywhere and three kingdoms stood in rivalry.
entries.literal: Since olden days when the Jin house lost the reins, heaven's net was torn and the cords broken; many villains rose like hedgehogs, and the three regions accordingly stood like a tripod.

entries.zh: 陳氏乘其際運，拔起細微，茜頊縱其長蛇，竊據吳會；
entries.en: The house of Chen seized its moment, rising from obscurity; Chen Qian extended his power like a great serpent and seized Wu and Kuaiji;
entries.literal: The Chen house seized this opportune fortune, rising from humble origins; Chen Qian stretched out like a long serpent and stealthily held Wu and Kuaiji;

entries.zh: 叔寶肆其昏虐，毒被金陵。
entries.en: Chen Shubao gave free rein to folly and cruelty, and his poison spread through Jinling.
entries.literal: Chen Shubao indulged his benighted cruelty, and poison spread over Jinling.

entries.zh: 數年已來，荒悖滋甚。
entries.en: For years his excesses have grown worse.
entries.literal: For several years now, wild perversity has grown ever worse.

entries.zh: 牝雞司旦，昵近奸回，尚方役徒，積骸千數，疆埸防守，長戍三年。
entries.en: Women rule at court, villains are his intimates, imperial workshops pile up thousands of corpses, and frontier troops serve three-year tours.
entries.literal: A hen crows at dawn; he draws close to wicked schemers; convict laborers of the imperial workshops pile up by the thousands; frontier defense keeps men on long garrison for three years.

entries.zh: 或微行暴露，沉湎王侯之宅；
entries.en: He wanders abroad in disguise, debauching himself in the houses of nobles;
entries.literal: At times he goes abroad incognito in revealing dress, drowning himself in the mansions of princes and marquises;

entries.zh: 或賓士駿騎，顛墜康衢之首。
entries.en: or gallops with rowdy companions until he falls in the public streets.
entries.literal: or with guest knights and swift steeds he tumbles at the head of the broad highway.

entries.zh: 有功不賞，無辜獲戮，烽燧日警，未以為虞，耽淫靡嫚，不知紀極。
entries.en: The worthy go unrewarded and the innocent are killed; beacon fires blaze daily yet he feels no alarm; sunk in debauchery, he knows no bounds.
entries.literal: Merit goes unrewarded, the innocent are put to death; beacon fires warn daily, yet he is not alarmed; sunk in lust and dissipation, he knows no limit.

entries.zh: 天厭亂德，妖實人興，或空裡時有大聲，或行路共傳鬼怪，或刳人肝以祠天狗，或自捨身以厭妖訛。
entries.en: Heaven rejects his misrule: omens multiply—strange cries in the sky, ghosts reported on every road, livers cut out to appease the celestial dog, men offering their own lives to ward off evil.
entries.literal: Heaven loathes chaotic virtue; portents arise and men stir—sometimes great sounds in the empty air, sometimes travelers all report ghosts and monsters, sometimes human livers are cut out to sacrifice to the celestial dog, sometimes men give up their own bodies to appease strange calamities.

entries.zh: 民神怨憤，災異薦發，天時人事，昭然可知。
entries.en: People and spirits alike are enraged; disasters follow one after another—the judgment of heaven is plain for all to see.
entries.literal: The people and the spirits are resentful and angry; disasters and anomalies arise in succession—the signs of heaven and the affairs of men are plainly evident.

entries.zh: 臣以庸才，猥蒙朝寄，頻曆籓任，與其鄰接，密邇仇讎，知其動靜，天討有罪，此即其時。
entries.en: I am but a mediocre man who has undeservedly held posts on Chen's border and know their movements well; heaven's punishment of the guilty has come—now is the time.
entries.literal: Your servant, with mediocre talent, has undeservedly received the court's trust, repeatedly holding frontier posts bordering Chen, close to this enemy, and knows their movements; heaven's punishment of the guilty—this is the moment.

entries.zh: 若戎車雷動，戈船電邁，臣難驚怯，請效鷹犬。」
entries.en: When the army marches and the fleet strikes, though I am no bold warrior, I beg to serve as your hunting dog."
entries.literal: If war chariots thunder forth and armed ships flash forward, though your servant is hardly bold, I beg to serve like hawk and hound."

entries.zh: 高祖覽表嘉之，答以優詔。
entries.en: Gaozu read the memorial with approval and answered with a gracious edict.
entries.literal: Gaozu read the memorial with approval and replied with an excellent edict.

entries.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以勱為行軍總管，從宜陽公王世積下陳江州。
entries.en: In the great campaign against Chen he served as campaign commander under Duke of Yiyang Wang Shiji and advanced on Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Mai served as campaign commander, following the Duke of Yiyang, Wang Shiji, in descending on Chen's Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 以功拜上開府，賜物三千段。
entries.en: For his service he was made Senior Commander-in-Chief and given three thousand bolts of goods.
entries.literal: For merit he was appointed Senior Commander-in-Chief and granted three thousand bolts of goods.

entries.zh: 隴右諸羌數為寇亂，朝廷以勱有威名，拜洮州刺史。
entries.en: The Qiang of Longyou raided repeatedly, and the court appointed Mai prefect of Taozhou for his renown.
entries.literal: The Qiang of Longyou often raided and rebelled; the court, because Mai had a formidable reputation, appointed him prefect of Taozhou.

entries.zh: 下車大崇威惠，民夷悅附，其山谷間生羌相率詣府稱謁，前後至者，數千餘戶。
entries.en: On taking office he combined firmness with kindness; Chinese and tribesmen alike submitted gladly, and Qiang from the valleys came in groups to pay homage—several thousand households in all.
entries.literal: Upon taking office he greatly promoted authority and kindness; Chinese and barbarians gladly submitted, and raw Qiang from the mountain valleys came in groups to the prefecture to pay homage—more than several thousand households in all.

entries.zh: 豪猾屏跡，路不拾遺，在職數年，稱為治理。
entries.en: Lawless elements disappeared, lost goods went untouched on the roads, and after several years he was praised as an excellent administrator.
entries.literal: The powerful and cunning vanished from sight; no one picked up lost goods on the road; during several years in office he was praised for good governance.

entries.zh: 後遇吐谷渾來寇，勱遇疾不能拒戰，賊遂大掠而去。
entries.en: Later, when Tuyuhun invaded, Mai was ill and unable to fight; the enemy looted extensively and withdrew.
entries.literal: Later when Tuyuhun came to raid, Mai fell ill and could not resist; the enemy plundered heavily and withdrew.

entries.zh: 憲司奏勱亡失戶口，又言受羌饋遺，竟坐免官。
entries.en: The inspectorate charged him with losing registered population and accepting Qiang bribes, and he was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: The inspectorate memorialized that Mai had lost registered households and also said he had accepted gifts from the Qiang; in the end he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 後卒于家，時年五十六。
entries.en: He later died at home at the age of fifty-six.
entries.literal: Later he died at home at the age of fifty-six.

entries.zh: 子士廉，最知名。
entries.en: His son Shilian was the most renowned.
entries.literal: His son Shilian was the most renowned.

entries.zh: 爾朱敞爾硃敞，字乾羅，秀容契胡人，爾硃榮之族子也。
entries.en: Erzhu Chang, courtesy name Qianluo, was a Qihu tribesman of Xiurong and a kinsman of Erzhu Rong.
entries.literal: Erzhu Chang, courtesy name Qianluo, was a man of the Qihu tribe of Xiurong, a clansman of Erzhu Rong.

entries.zh: 父彥伯，官至司徒、博陵王。
entries.en: His father Yanbo rose to Grand Minister of State and Prince of Boling.
entries.literal: His father Yanbo rose to Grand Minister of State and Prince of Boling.

entries.zh: 齊神武帝韓陵之捷，盡誅爾硃氏，敞小，隨母養于宮中。
entries.en: After Qi Emperor Shenwu's victory at Hanling the Erzhu clan was wiped out; Chang was still a child and was raised in the palace with his mother.
entries.literal: After Emperor Shenwu of Qi's victory at Hanling, the entire Erzhu clan was executed; Chang was young and was raised in the palace with his mother.

entries.zh: 及年十二，自竇而走，至於大街，見童兒群戲者，敞解所著綺羅金翠之服，易衣而遁。
entries.en: At twelve he slipped out through a hole in the wall onto the main street, saw children at play, stripped off his brocade and jeweled finery, traded clothes with one of them, and fled.
entries.literal: At age twelve he fled through a hole in the wall to the main street, saw children playing in a group, stripped off his brocade robes adorned with gold and kingfisher feathers, exchanged clothes, and escaped.

entries.zh: 追騎尋至，初不識敞，便執綺衣兒。
entries.en: Pursuers soon caught up; they did not recognize Chang at first and seized the child in brocade instead.
entries.literal: Pursuers soon arrived; at first they did not recognize Chang and seized the child in brocade.

entries.zh: 比究問知非，會日已暮，由是得免。
entries.en: Once questioning showed their mistake, night had fallen, and Chang got away.
entries.literal: When questioning revealed their mistake, night had already fallen, and so he escaped.

entries.zh: 遂入一村，見長孫氏媼踞胡床而坐。
entries.en: He came to a village where an old woman of the Zhangsun clan sat on a camp stool.
entries.literal: He then entered a village and saw an old woman of the Zhangsun clan seated on a camp chair.

entries.zh: 敞再拜求哀，長孫氏湣之，藏於複壁。
entries.en: Chang bowed and pleaded for mercy; she pitied him and hid him in a secret compartment of the wall.
entries.literal: Chang bowed twice and begged for pity; the Zhangsun woman took pity on him and hid him in a double wall.

entries.zh: 三年，購之愈急，跡且至，長孫氏曰：「事急矣，不可久留。」
entries.en: After three years the manhunt intensified and pursuers were closing in; the Zhangsun woman said, "This has become urgent—you cannot stay here any longer."
entries.literal: After three years the search grew ever more urgent and his trail was nearly found; the Zhangsun woman said: "The matter is urgent—you cannot stay long."

entries.zh: 資而遣之。
entries.en: She gave him supplies and sent him on his way.
entries.literal: She supplied him with funds and sent him away.

entries.zh: 遂詐為道士，變姓名，隱嵩山，略涉經史。
entries.en: He disguised himself as a Daoist priest, took a new name, and lived in seclusion on Mount Song, where he read a little in the classics and histories.
entries.literal: He then pretended to be a Daoist priest, changed his name, hid on Mount Song, and briefly studied the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 數年之間，人頗異之。
entries.en: Within a few years people began to regard him as remarkable.
entries.literal: Within a few years people found him rather unusual.

entries.zh: 嘗獨坐岩石之下，泫然而歎曰：「吾豈終於此乎？
entries.en: Once, sitting alone beneath a cliff, he wept and sighed, "Am I to end my days like this?
entries.literal: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed: "Am I to end my days like this?

entries.zh: 伍子胥獨何人也！」
entries.en: What was Wu Zixu, that he alone could rise so high!"
entries.literal: What sort of man was Wu Zixu alone!"

entries.zh: 於是間行微服，西歸於周。
entries.en: He then made his way west in disguise and returned to Zhou.
entries.literal: He then traveled by secret routes in humble dress and returned west to Zhou.

entries.zh: 太祖見而禮之，拜大都督、行台郎中，封靈壽縣伯，邑千五百戶。
entries.en: Grand Ancestor Yuwen Tai received him with honor, made him Grand Commander and Bureau Director of the Field Office, and created him Baron of Lingshou with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: Grand Ancestor [Yuwen Tai] received him with ceremony, appointed him Grand Commander and Bureau Director of the Field Office, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Lingshou county with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

entries.zh: 遷通直散騎常侍，轉車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵為侯。
entries.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, then made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and raised to marquis.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, then made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and advanced to marquis.

entries.zh: 保定中，遷使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: During the Baoding era he was made Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
entries.literal: During Baoding he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 天和中，增邑五百戶，曆信、臨、熊、潼四州刺史，進爵為公。
entries.en: During Tianhe his fief grew by five hundred households; he served as prefect of Xin, Lin, Xiong, and Tong in turn, and was raised to duke.
entries.literal: During Tianhe his fief was increased by five hundred households; he served successively as prefect of Xin, Lin, Xiong, and Tong [prefectures], and advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 武帝東征，上表求從，許之。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu marched east, Chang asked leave to accompany him and was permitted.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned eastward, Chang memorialized asking to follow, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 攻城陷陣，所當皆破，進位上開府。
entries.en: In assaults on cities and charges through enemy lines he was invariably victorious and was promoted to Senior Commander-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In storming cities and breaking battle lines, wherever he faced the enemy he prevailed, and he was advanced to Senior Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 除南光州刺史，入為護軍大將軍。
entries.en: He was made prefect of southern Guang Prefecture and later recalled to the capital as General of the Guard Army.
entries.literal: He was appointed prefect of southern Guang Prefecture and then entered the capital as General of the Guard Army.

entries.zh: 歲餘，轉膠州刺史。
entries.en: A year later he was transferred to Jiaozhou as prefect.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to be prefect of Jiaozhou.

entries.zh: 於是迎長孫氏及弟置於家，厚資給之。
entries.en: He then brought the Zhangsun woman and his younger brother into his home and supported them generously.
entries.literal: He then welcomed the Zhangsun woman and his younger brother into his household and provided for them generously.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，改封邊城郡公。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Chang was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Biancheng.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Chang's fief was changed to Duke of Biancheng commandery.

entries.zh: 黔安蠻叛，命敞討平之。
entries.en: When the Qian'an tribes rebelled, Chang was ordered to put them down.
entries.literal: The Qian'an barbarians rebelled, and Chang was ordered to suppress and pacify them.

entries.zh: 師旋，拜金州總管。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.

entries.zh: 尋轉徐州總管。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 在職數年，號為明肅，民吏懼之。
entries.en: After several years in office he was known for stern clarity, and both officials and commoners stood in awe of him.
entries.literal: During several years in office he was known for clarity and severity, and officials and commoners alike feared him.

entries.zh: 後以年老，上表乞骸骨，賜二馬軺車，歸於河內，卒于家，時年七十二。
entries.en: In old age he asked to retire; the court gave him a two-horse carriage, and he returned to Henei, where he died at seventy-two.
entries.literal: Later, on account of old age, he memorialized asking to retire; he was granted a two-horse light carriage, returned to Henei, and died at home at the age of seventy-two.

entries.zh: 子最嗣。
entries.en: His son Zui succeeded to his titles.
entries.literal: His son Zui succeeded him.

entries.zh: 周搖周搖，字世安，其先與後魏同源，初為普乃氏，及居洛陽，改為周氏。
entries.en: Zhou Yao, courtesy name Shi'an, shared origins with the Northern Wei; his clan was originally Punai, but after settling in Luoyang they took the surname Zhou.
entries.literal: Zhou Yao—Zhou Yao, courtesy name Shi'an, was of the same origin as Later Wei; originally of the clan Punai, when they settled in Luoyang they changed to the surname Zhou.

entries.zh: 曾祖拔拔，祖右六肱，俱為北平王。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Baba and grandfather Youliugong were both enfeoffed as Princes of Beiping.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Baba and grandfather Youliugong were both Princes of Beiping.

entries.zh: 父恕延，曆行台僕射、南荊州總管。
entries.en: His father Shuyan had served as Vice Director of the Field Office and regional commander of southern Jingzhou.
entries.literal: His father Shuyan successively served as Vice Director of the Field Office and regional commander of southern Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 搖少剛果，有武藝，性謹厚，動遵法度。
entries.en: As a youth Yao was resolute and skilled in arms, cautious and honest by nature, and scrupulous in observing the law.
entries.literal: Yao in youth was firm and resolute, skilled in martial arts, of a cautious and honest nature, and in conduct always observed the law.

entries.zh: 仕魏，官至開府儀同三司。
entries.en: He served the Wei and rose to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
entries.literal: He served Wei and rose to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 周閔帝受禪，賜姓車非氏，封金水郡公。
entries.en: When Zhou Emperor Min took the throne, Yao was granted the surname Chefei and created Duke of Jinshui.
entries.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication, he was granted the surname Chefei and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinshui commandery.

entries.zh: 曆夙、楚二州刺史，吏民安之。
entries.en: He served as prefect of Su and Chu in turn, and both officials and people lived in peace under his rule.
entries.literal: He served successively as prefect of Su and Chu [prefectures], and officials and people were at peace under him.

entries.zh: 從帝平齊，每戰有功，超授柱國，進封夔國公。
entries.en: He followed the emperor in the conquest of Qi, distinguished himself in every battle, was made Pillar of State, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Kui.
entries.literal: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, he had merit in every battle, was exceptionally appointed Pillar of State, and advanced to Duke of Kui.

entries.zh: 未幾，拜晉州總管。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.

entries.zh: 時高祖為定州總管，文獻皇后自京師詣高祖，路經搖所，主禮甚薄。
entries.en: Gaozu was then regional commander of Dingzhou; when Empress Wenxian traveled from the capital to visit him and passed through Yao's territory, Yao entertained her very sparingly.
entries.literal: At the time Gaozu was regional commander of Dingzhou; Empress Wenxian came from the capital to visit Gaozu and passed through Yao's jurisdiction, where the reception he provided was very meager.

entries.zh: 既而白後曰：「公廨甚富於財，限法不敢輒費。
entries.en: He then told the empress, "My offices are well supplied with funds, but the law forbids me to spend them freely.
entries.literal: He then told the empress: "The government offices are very rich in funds, but the law sets limits and I dare not spend freely.

entries.zh: 又王臣無得效私。」
entries.en: Besides, a prince's minister must not indulge private favor."
entries.literal: Moreover, as a king's minister one may not act out of private feeling."

entries.zh: 其質直如此。
entries.en: Such was his plain integrity.
entries.literal: Such was his plain uprightness.

entries.zh: 高祖以其奉法，每嘉之。
entries.en: Gaozu admired him for his strict adherence to the law.
entries.literal: Gaozu, because he upheld the law, always praised him.

entries.zh: 及為丞相，徙封濟北郡公，尋拜豫州總管。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chief minister, Yao was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jibei and soon appointed regional commander of Yuzhou.
entries.literal: When he became chief minister, Yao's fief was moved to Duke of Jibei commandery, and soon he was appointed regional commander of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，複姓周氏。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Yao resumed the surname Zhou.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Yao resumed the surname Zhou.

entries.zh: 開皇初，突厥寇邊，燕、薊多被其患，前總管李崇為虜所殺，上思所以鎮之，臨朝曰：「無以加周搖者。」
entries.en: Early in Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; Yan and Ji suffered greatly, and the former commander Li Chong was killed. The emperor sought someone to secure the region and declared at court, "No one surpasses Zhou Yao for this."
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; Yan and Ji suffered heavily; the former commander Li Chong was killed by the enemy. The emperor considered how to secure the region and said at court: "None surpasses Zhou Yao for this post."

entries.zh: 拜為幽州總管六州五十鎮諸軍事。
entries.en: He was appointed regional commander of Youzhou with authority over six prefectures and fifty garrisons.
entries.literal: He was appointed regional commander of Youzhou with military authority over six prefectures and fifty garrisons.

entries.zh: 搖修鄣塞，謹斥候，邊民以安。
entries.en: Yao repaired the border fortifications and kept watch posts alert, and the frontier people lived in peace.
entries.literal: Yao repaired border walls and stockades and kept watch posts strict; the frontier people were thereby secure.

entries.zh: 後六載，徙為壽州。
entries.en: Six years later he was transferred to Shouzhou.
entries.literal: Six years later he was transferred to Shouzhou.

entries.zh: 初，自以年老，乞骸骨，上召之。
entries.en: Having grown old, he had asked to retire; the emperor summoned him to court.
entries.literal: Earlier, considering himself old, he had asked to retire; the emperor summoned him.

entries.zh: 既引見，上勞之曰：「公積行累仁，曆仕三代，克終富貴，保茲遐壽，良足善也。」
entries.en: When he was received in audience, the emperor said to him, "You have lived a life of accumulated virtue, served three dynasties, kept your wealth and rank to the end, and enjoyed a long life—this is admirable indeed."
entries.literal: After he was received in audience, the emperor comforted him, saying: "Sir, you have accumulated conduct and heaped up benevolence, served through three dynasties, attained wealth and honor to the end, and preserved this long life—truly admirable."

entries.zh: 賜坐褥，歸於第。
entries.en: He was given a seat cushion and sent home to his estate.
entries.literal: He was granted a seat cushion and returned to his residence.

entries.zh: 歲餘，終於家，諡曰恭，時年八十四。
entries.en: A year later he died at home and was given the posthumous title Gong; he was eighty-four.
entries.literal: After more than a year he died at home; his posthumous title was Gong [Respectful], and he was eighty-four.

entries.zh: 獨孤楷，字修則，不知何許人也，本姓李氏。
entries.en: Dugu Kai, courtesy name Xiuzi, was of unknown origin and bore the surname Li by birth.
entries.literal: Dugu Kai, courtesy name Xiuzi, was of unknown origin; his original surname was Li.

entries.zh: 父屯，從齊神武帝與周師戰于沙苑，齊師敗績，因為柱國獨孤信所擒，配為士伍，給使信家，漸得親近，因賜姓獨孤氏。
entries.en: His father Tun fought for Qi Emperor Shenwu against Zhou forces at Shayuan; after Qi's defeat he was captured by Pillar of State Dugu Xin, assigned as a household servant, won Xin's trust over time, and was granted the surname Dugu.
entries.literal: His father Tun followed Emperor Shenwu of Qi in battle with Zhou troops at Shayuan; the Qi army was defeated, and he was captured by the pillar of state Dugu Xin, assigned as a common soldier to serve in Xin's household, gradually won closeness, and was granted the surname Dugu.

entries.zh: 楷少謹厚，便弄馬槊，為宇文護執刀，累轉車騎將軍。
entries.en: Kai was cautious and honest as a youth, skilled with horse and lance, served as Yuwen Hu's bodyguard, and rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: Kai in youth was cautious and honest, skilled with horse and lance, served as blade-bearer for Yuwen Hu, and was repeatedly transferred until he became General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 其後數從征伐，賜爵廣阿縣公，邑千戶，拜右侍下大夫。
entries.en: He took part in several campaigns, was created Duke of Guang'a with a fief of a thousand households, and appointed Right Attendant Grandee.
entries.literal: Afterward he followed several campaigns, was ennobled as Duke of Guang'a county with a fief of a thousand households, and appointed Right Attendant Grandee.

entries.zh: 週末，從韋孝寬平淮南，以功賜子景雲爵西河縣公。
entries.en: Late in the Zhou he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan, and his son Jingyun was created Duke of Xihe for his father's service.
entries.literal: At the end of Zhou he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan and, for merit, his son Jingyun was ennobled as Duke of Xihe county.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，進授開府，每督親信兵。
entries.en: While Gaozu was chief minister, Kai was made Commander-in-Chief and regularly led the trusted guard.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, Kai was advanced to Commander-in-Chief and regularly commanded trusted troops.

entries.zh: 及受禪，拜右監門將軍，進封汝陽郡公。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Kai was made General of the Right Gate Guards and enfeoffed as Duke of Ruyang.
entries.literal: When the abdication was received, he was appointed General of the Right Gate Guards and advanced to Duke of Ruyang commandery.

entries.zh: 數歲，遷右衛將軍。
entries.en: Several years later he was transferred to General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: Several years later he was transferred to General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 仁壽初，出為原州總管。
entries.en: Early in the Renshou era he was posted as regional commander of Yuanzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he went out as regional commander of Yuanzhou.

entries.zh: 時蜀王秀鎮益州，上征之，猶豫未發。
entries.en: Prince of Shu Xiu was then stationed in Yizhou; the emperor summoned him, but Xiu hesitated to set out.
entries.literal: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu held Yizhou; the emperor was summoning him but hesitated to set out.

entries.zh: 朝廷恐秀生變，拜楷益州總管，馳傳代之。
entries.en: Fearing Xiu might rebel, the court appointed Kai regional commander of Yizhou and sent him post-haste to replace him.
entries.literal: The court feared Xiu would rebel; Kai was appointed regional commander of Yizhou and hurried by post relay to replace him.

entries.zh: 秀果有異志，楷諷諭久之，乃就路。
entries.en: Xiu did harbor rebellious intent; Kai admonished him at length before he finally set out for the capital.
entries.literal: Xiu indeed harbored rebellious intent; Kai admonished and persuaded him for a long time before he set out on the road.

entries.zh: 楷察秀有悔色，因勒兵為備。
entries.en: Seeing regret on Xiu's face, Kai kept his troops under arms as a precaution.
entries.literal: Kai perceived that Xiu showed regret and therefore drew up his troops on guard.

entries.zh: 秀至興樂，去益州四十餘裡，將反襲楷，密令左右覘所為，知楷不可犯而止。
entries.en: At Xingle, still more than forty li from Yizhou, Xiu was about to turn and attack Kai; he sent men to spy on him, found Kai too formidable to challenge, and gave up the plan.
entries.literal: When Xiu reached Xingle, still more than forty li from Yizhou, he was about to turn back and surprise Kai; he secretly ordered his attendants to observe Kai's conduct, learned that Kai could not be taken lightly, and desisted.

entries.zh: 楷在益州，甚有惠政，蜀中父老於今稱之。
entries.en: Kai governed Yizhou with great kindness, and the elders of Shu still speak of him with praise.
entries.literal: Kai in Yizhou had very benevolent administration, and the elders of Shu still praise him to this day.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，轉并州總管。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Kai was transferred to regional commander of Bingzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Kai was transferred to regional commander of Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 遇疾喪明，上表乞骸骨。
entries.en: He fell ill and lost his sight, then memorialized asking to retire.
entries.literal: He fell ill and lost his sight, and memorialized asking to retire.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「公先朝舊臣，曆職二代，高風素望，臥以鎮之，無勞躬親簿領也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "You are a veteran of two reigns, renowned for your integrity; your presence alone will secure the region—you need not trouble yourself with daily paperwork."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Sir, you are an old minister of the former court, having served through two reigns; your lofty conduct and long-standing repute can secure the region even in repose—there is no need for you personally to handle ledgers and registers."

entries.zh: 遣其長子淩雲監省郡事。
entries.en: He sent Kai's eldest son Lingyun to supervise the commandery in his stead.
entries.literal: He sent Kai's eldest son Lingyun to oversee and administer the commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 其見重如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

entries.zh: 數載，轉長平太守，未視事而卒。
entries.en: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Changping but died before assuming office.
entries.literal: Several years later he was transferred to administrator of Changping but died before taking up the post.

entries.zh: 諡曰恭。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Gong.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Gong [Respectful].

entries.zh: 子淩雲、平雲，彥雲，皆知名。
entries.en: His sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun all achieved renown.
entries.literal: His sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun were all well known.

entries.zh: 楷弟盛，見《誠節傳》。
entries.en: Kai's younger brother Sheng is treated in the Biography of Loyal Martyrs.
entries.literal: Kai's younger brother Sheng is treated in the Biography of Loyal Martyrs.

entries.zh: 乞伏慧，字令和，馬邑鮮卑人也。
entries.en: Qi Fuhui, courtesy name Linghe, was a Xianbei from Mayi.
entries.literal: Qi Fuhui, courtesy name Linghe, was a Xianbei of Mayi.

entries.zh: 祖周，魏銀青光祿大夫，父纂，金紫光祿大夫，並為第一領民酋長。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhou was a Silver Radiance Grand Master of Wei; his father Zuan was a Golden Radiance Grand Master; both were first-rank tribal chieftains.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhou was Silver Radiance Grand Master of Wei; his father Zuan was Golden Radiance Grand Master; both were chieftains of the first rank among the settled peoples.

entries.zh: 慧少慷慨有大節，便弓馬，好鷹犬。
entries.en: As a youth Hui was openhanded and high-minded, skilled in archery and horsemanship, and devoted to falconry and hunting.
entries.literal: Hui in youth was generous and possessed of great integrity, skilled with bow and horse, and fond of hawks and hounds.

entries.zh: 齊文襄帝時，為行台左丞，加蕩寇將軍，累遷右衛將軍、太僕卿，自永甯縣公封宜民郡王。
entries.en: Under Qi Emperor Wenxiang he served as Left Assistant Director of the Field Office and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits, rose to General of the Right Guard and Minister of the Stud, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Yimin after holding the title Duke of Yongning.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wenxiang of Qi he was Left Assistant Director of the Field Office, additionally made General Who Sweeps Away Bandits, and successively promoted to General of the Right Guard and Minister of the Stud; from Duke of Yongning county he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yimin commandery.

entries.zh: 其兄貴和又以軍功為王，一門二王，稱為貴顯。
entries.en: His elder brother Guihe also became a prince through military merit; with two princes in one family they were accounted supremely eminent.
entries.literal: His elder brother Guihe also became a prince through military merit; one household with two princes was called eminent and illustrious.

entries.zh: 周武平齊，授使持節、開府儀同大將軍，拜佽飛右旅下大夫，轉熊渠中大夫。
entries.en: When Zhou Emperor Wu conquered Qi, Hui was made Bearer of the Staff and Grand Master Commander-in-Chief, appointed Junior Grandee of the Right Wing of the Rapid-as-Flying Guard, and later transferred to Grandee of the Xiongqu Regiment.
entries.literal: When Zhou Emperor Wu pacified Qi, Hui was granted Bearer of the Staff and Grand Master Commander-in-Chief, appointed Junior Grandee of the Right Wing of the Rapid-as-Flying Guard, and transferred to Grandee of the Xiongqu Regiment.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉惇于武陟，所當皆破，授大將軍，賜物八百段。
entries.en: While Gaozu was chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuchi Dun at Wuzhi, was victorious in every engagement, was made Grand General, and received eight hundred bolts of goods.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi; wherever he faced the enemy he prevailed, and he was appointed Grand General and granted eight hundred bolts of goods.

entries.zh: 及平尉迥，進位柱國，賜爵西河郡公，邑三千戶，賚物二千三百段。
entries.en: After Yuchi Jiong's rebellion was crushed, he was made Pillar of State, created Duke of Xihe with a fief of three thousand households, and given two thousand three hundred bolts of goods.
entries.literal: When Yuwen Yong was pacified, he was advanced to Pillar of State, ennobled as Duke of Xihe commandery with a fief of three thousand households, and granted two thousand three hundred bolts of goods.

entries.zh: 請以官爵讓兄，朝廷不許，論者義之。
entries.en: He asked to yield his rank and title to his elder brother; the court refused, but commentators praised his filial devotion.
entries.literal: He asked to yield his rank and title to his elder brother; the court did not permit it, but commentators praised his righteousness.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，拜曹州刺史。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Hui was appointed prefect of Caozhou.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Hui was appointed prefect of Caozhou.

entries.zh: 曹土舊俗，民多奸隱，戶口名簿帳，恆不以實。
entries.en: Cao had long been a place where people concealed households and falsified registers.
entries.literal: By old custom in Cao territory the people often concealed wrongdoing; household registers and name rolls were habitually not truthful.

entries.zh: 慧下車按察，得戶數萬。
entries.en: On taking office Hui conducted an investigation and registered tens of thousands of hidden households.
entries.literal: When Hui took office he investigated and uncovered tens of thousands of households.

entries.zh: 遷涼州總管。
entries.en: He was transferred to regional commander of Liangzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 先是，突厥屢為寇抄，慧於是嚴警烽燧，遠為斥候，虜亦素憚其名，竟不入境。
entries.en: The Turks had raided repeatedly; Hui tightened the beacon system and posted distant scouts, and because they had long feared his name, they never crossed the border.
entries.literal: Earlier the Turks had repeatedly raided; Hui now strictly alerted beacon towers, posted distant scouts, and the enemy had long feared his name—in the end they did not enter the border.

entries.zh: 歲餘，轉齊州刺史，得隱戶數千。
entries.en: A year later he was transferred to Qizhou as prefect and uncovered several thousand hidden households.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to prefect of Qizhou and uncovered several thousand concealed households.

entries.zh: 遷壽州總管。
entries.en: He was transferred to regional commander of Shouzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Shouzhou.

entries.zh: 其年，左轉杞州刺史，在職數年，遷徐州總管。
entries.en: That year he was demoted to prefect of Qizhou in Henan; after several years he was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: That same year he was transferred left to prefect of Qizhou [Qi prefecture]; after several years in office he was moved to regional commander of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 時年逾七十，上表求致仕，不許。
entries.en: By then he was over seventy and asked to retire, but the court refused.
entries.literal: By then he was over seventy and memorialized asking to retire; permission was not granted.

entries.zh: 俄轉荊州總管，又領潭、桂二州總管三十一州諸軍事。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to Jingzhou and given military authority over thirty-one prefectures as commander of Tan and Gui.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Jingzhou and additionally held military authority over thirty-one prefectures as commander of Tan and Gui [prefectures].

entries.zh: 其俗輕剽，慧躬行樸素以矯之，風化大洽。
entries.en: The region was lawless and volatile; Hui set an example of plain living and reformed the customs thoroughly.
entries.literal: The local custom was frivolous and violent; Hui personally practiced plain simplicity to correct it, and customs were greatly harmonized.

entries.zh: 曾見人以穀捕魚者，出絹買而放之，其仁心如此。
entries.en: Once he saw a man using grain as bait to catch fish; he paid silk to buy the catch and set the fish free—such was his kindness.
entries.literal: Once he saw someone using grain to catch fish; he paid out silk to buy the fish and released them—such was his benevolent heart.

entries.zh: 百姓美之，號其處曰西河公穀。
entries.en: The people praised him and named the place Duke of Xihe's Grain.
entries.literal: The people praised him and called that place Duke of Xihe's Grain.

entries.zh: 轉秦州總管。
entries.en: He was transferred to regional commander of Qinzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，為天水太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Hui became administrator of Tianshui.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Hui became administrator of Tianshui.

entries.zh: 大業五年，征吐谷渾，郡濱西境，民苦勞役，又遇帝西巡，坐為道不整，獻食疏薄，帝大怒，命左右斬之。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Daye, during the campaign against Tuyuhun, his commandery lay on the western frontier where the people were exhausted by labor levies; when the emperor passed westward, Hui was blamed because the road was not ready and the provisions were poor; the emperor was enraged and ordered him executed.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, during the campaign against Tuyuhun, the commandery bordered the western frontier; the people suffered under corvée labor, and when the emperor toured westward, Hui was charged because the road was not in order and the food offered was meager; the emperor was furious and ordered his attendants to behead him.

entries.zh: 見其無發，乃釋，除名為民。
entries.en: Seeing that he was bald, the emperor spared him but stripped him of rank and made him a commoner.
entries.literal: Seeing that he had no hair, the emperor released him, stripped his name and rank, and made him a commoner.

entries.zh: 卒於家。
entries.en: He died at home.
entries.literal: He died at home.

entries.zh: 張威，不知何許人也。
entries.en: Zhang Wei was of unknown origin.
entries.literal: Zhang Wei was of unknown origin.

entries.zh: 父琛，魏弘農太守。
entries.en: His father Chen had been administrator of Hongnong under the Wei.
entries.literal: His father Chen was administrator of Hongnong in Wei.

entries.zh: 威少倜儻有大志，善騎射，膂力過人。
entries.en: As a youth Wei was bold and ambitious, excelled at horseback archery, and possessed extraordinary strength.
entries.literal: Wei in youth was free-spirited and ambitious, skilled in mounted archery, and his physical strength surpassed other men.

entries.zh: 在周，數從征伐，位至柱國、京兆尹，封長壽縣公，邑千戶。
entries.en: Under the Zhou he campaigned repeatedly, rose to Pillar of State and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and was created Duke of Changshou with a fief of a thousand households.
entries.literal: Under Zhou he followed several campaigns, rose to Pillar of State and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshou county with a fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 王謙作亂，高祖以威為行軍總管，從元帥梁睿擊之。
entries.en: When Wang Qian rebelled, Gaozu appointed Wei campaign commander under Marshal Liang Rui to suppress him.
entries.literal: When Wang Qian rebelled, Gaozu made Wei campaign commander to follow the commander-in-chief Liang Rui in attacking him.

entries.zh: 軍次通穀，謙守將李三王擁勁兵拒守，睿以威為先鋒。
entries.en: The army halted at Tonggu, where Qian's defender Li Sanwang held the pass with elite troops; Rui made Wei his vanguard.
entries.literal: The army halted at Tonggu; Qian's defending general Li Sanwang held strong troops in defense, and Rui made Wei vanguard.

entries.zh: 三王初閉壘不戰，威令人詈侮以激怒之，三王果出陣。
entries.en: Sanwang at first refused battle behind his walls; Wei had men taunt and insult him until Sanwang came out to fight.
entries.literal: Sanwang at first closed the stockade and would not fight; Wei had men revile and insult him to provoke anger, and Sanwang indeed came out to battle.

entries.zh: 威令壯士奮擊，三王軍潰，大兵繼至，於是擒斬四千餘人。
entries.en: Wei sent his best fighters forward; Sanwang's army broke, the main force followed, and more than four thousand were killed or captured.
entries.literal: Wei ordered stalwarts to strike fiercely; Sanwang's army collapsed, the main force followed up, and more than four thousand were captured and beheaded.

entries.zh: 進至開遠，謙將趙儼眾十萬，連營三十裡。
entries.en: Advancing to Kaiyuan, they faced Qian's general Zhao Yan with a hundred thousand men in camps stretching thirty li.
entries.literal: Advancing to Kaiyuan, Qian's general Zhao Yan had a host of a hundred thousand with camps strung for thirty li.

entries.zh: 威鑿山通道，自西嶺攻其背，儼遂敗走。
entries.en: Wei cut a path through the mountains, struck from the western ridge against their rear, and Yan was routed.
entries.literal: Wei cut a passage through the mountain, attacked from the western ridge against their rear, and Yan was defeated and fled.

entries.zh: 追至成都，與謙大戰，威將中軍。
entries.en: They pursued to Chengdu and fought a great battle with Qian; Wei commanded the center.
entries.literal: Pursuing to Chengdu, they fought a great battle with Qian; Wei commanded the center army.

entries.zh: 及謙平，進位上柱國，拜瀘州總管。
entries.en: After Qian's defeat Wei was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and appointed regional commander of Luzhou.
entries.literal: When Qian was pacified, Wei was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and appointed regional commander of Luzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，曆幽、洛二州總管，改封晉熙郡公。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Wei served as regional commander of You and Luozhou in turn and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jinxi.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Wei successively served as regional commander of You and Luo [prefectures] and his fief was changed to Duke of Jinxi commandery.

entries.zh: 尋拜河北道行台僕射，後督晉王軍府事。
entries.en: He was soon made Vice Director of the Hebei Circuit Field Office and later supervised Prince Jin's military headquarters.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Hebei Circuit Field Office, and later supervised the military headquarters of Prince Jin.

entries.zh: 數年，拜青州總管，賜錢八十萬，米五百石，雜彩三百段。
entries.en: Several years later he was appointed regional commander of Qingzhou and given eight hundred thousand cash, five hundred piculs of grain, and three hundred bolts of silks.
entries.literal: Several years later he was appointed regional commander of Qingzhou and granted eight hundred thousand cash, five hundred piculs of grain, and three hundred bolts of mixed silks.

entries.zh: 威在青州，頗治產業，遣家奴于民間鬻蘆菔根，其奴緣此侵擾百姓。
entries.en: In Qingzhou Wei built up his estates and sent household slaves to sell radish roots among the people; the slaves used this as a pretext to harass the populace.
entries.literal: Wei in Qingzhou greatly built up estates and sent household slaves among the people to sell radish roots; the slaves on this account harassed the common people.

entries.zh: 上深加譴責，坐廢於家。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked him severely and dismissed him to his home.
entries.literal: The emperor sternly rebuked him, and he was dismissed and confined at home.

entries.zh: 後從上祠太山，至洛陽，上謂威曰：「自朕之有天下，每委公以重鎮，可謂推赤心矣。
