entries.en: Later, accompanying the emperor to sacrifice at Mount Tai and reaching Luoyang, the emperor said to Wei, "Since I gained the realm I have repeatedly entrusted you with vital posts—I have given you my full trust.
entries.literal: Later, following the emperor in sacrificing at Mount Tai and arriving at Luoyang, the emperor said to Wei: "Since I gained the realm, I have repeatedly entrusted you with vital posts—truly I have offered you my open heart.

entries.zh: 何乃不修名行，唯利是視？
entries.en: Why then have you neglected your reputation and looked only to profit?
entries.literal: Why then do you not cultivate reputation and conduct, but look only to profit?

entries.zh: 豈直孤負朕心，亦且累卿名德。」
entries.en: You have not only failed me but also stained your own good name."
entries.literal: This not only betrays my heart but also mars your own fame and virtue."

entries.zh: 因問威曰：「公所執笏今安在？」
entries.en: He then asked, "Where is the court tablet you once carried?"
entries.literal: He then asked Wei: "Where is the tablet you used to hold at court?"

entries.zh: 威頓首曰：「臣負罪虧憲，無顏複執，謹藏於家。」
entries.en: Wei bowed low and said, "I have offended and broken the law; I am ashamed to hold it again and have kept it at home."
entries.literal: Wei bowed his head and said: "Your servant has committed offense and fallen short of the statutes; I have no face to hold it again and have respectfully kept it at home."

entries.zh: 上曰：「可持來。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Bring it here."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Bring it here."

entries.zh: 威明日奉笏以見，上曰：「公雖不遵法度，功效實多，朕不忘之。
entries.en: The next day Wei brought the tablet to court; the emperor said, "Though you broke the law, your service has been great, and I have not forgotten it.
entries.literal: The next day Wei presented the tablet at audience; the emperor said: "Though you did not observe the law, your achievements were many, and I have not forgotten them.

entries.zh: 今還公笏。」
entries.en: I return your tablet to you now."
entries.literal: I now return your tablet."

entries.zh: 於是複拜洛州刺史，後封睆城郡公。
entries.en: He was then reappointed prefect of Luozhou and later enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was again appointed prefect of Luozhou and later enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng commandery.

entries.zh: 尋轉相州刺史，卒官。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to Xiangzhou as prefect and died in office.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to prefect of Xiangzhou and died in office.

entries.zh: 有子植，大業中，至武賁郎將。
entries.en: His son Zhi rose during the Daye era to Commandant of the Martial Guards.
entries.literal: He had a son Zhi who, in the Daye era, rose to Commandant of the Martial Guards.

entries.zh: 和洪，汝南人也。
entries.en: He Hong was from Runan.
entries.literal: He Hong was a native of Runan.

entries.zh: 少有武力，勇烈過人。
entries.en: As a youth he was physically powerful, and his courage exceeded that of ordinary men.
entries.literal: In youth he had martial prowess; his courage and fierceness surpassed other men.

entries.zh: 周武帝時，數從征伐，以戰功累遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he campaigned repeatedly and, for his victories, rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he followed several campaigns and, for battle merit, was repeatedly promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 時龍州蠻任公忻、李國立等聚眾為亂，刺史獨孤善不能禦。
entries.en: At that time the Longzhou tribesmen Ren Gongxin and Li Guoli gathered forces in rebellion, and Prefect Dugu Shan could not suppress them.
entries.literal: At the time the barbarians of Longzhou, Ren Gongxin, Li Guoli, and others gathered crowds in rebellion; the prefect Dugu Shan could not repel them.

entries.zh: 朝議以洪有武略，代善為刺史。
entries.en: The court decided that Hong had military talent and replaced Shan as prefect.
entries.literal: The court deliberated that Hong had military talent and replaced Shan as prefect.

entries.zh: 月餘，擒公忻、國立，皆斬首梟之，餘党悉平。
entries.en: Within a month he captured Gongxin and Guoli, executed them and displayed their heads, and pacified the remaining rebels.
entries.literal: After more than a month he captured Gongxin and Guoli, beheaded them both and displayed their heads, and the remaining partisans were all pacified.

entries.zh: 從帝攻河陰，洪力戰，陷其西門。
entries.en: He followed the emperor in the attack on Heyin, fought fiercely, and took the western gate.
entries.literal: Following the emperor in attacking Heyin, Hong fought fiercely and stormed the western gate.

entries.zh: 帝壯之，賞物千段。
entries.en: The emperor was impressed and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.
entries.literal: The emperor admired him and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.

entries.zh: 複從帝平齊，進位上儀同，賜爵北平侯，邑八百戶，拜左勳曹下大夫。
entries.en: He again followed the emperor in the conquest of Qi, was promoted to Senior Palace Attendant of the First Rank, created Marquis of Beiping with eight hundred households, and appointed Junior Grandee of the Left Merit Bureau.
entries.literal: He again followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was advanced to Senior Palace Attendant of the First Rank, ennobled as Marquis of Beiping with a fief of eight hundred households, and appointed Junior Grandee of the Left Merit Bureau.

entries.zh: 柱國王軌之擒吳明徹也，洪有功焉，加位開府，遷折衝中大夫。
entries.en: When Pillar of State Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche, Hong distinguished himself and was made Commander-in-Chief and transferred to Grandee of the Break-the-Ranks Regiment.
entries.literal: When the pillar of state Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche, Hong had merit therein; he was additionally made Commander-in-Chief and transferred to Grandee of the Break-the-Ranks Regiment.

entries.zh: 尉迥作亂相州，以洪為行軍總管，從韋孝寬擊之。
entries.en: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, Hong was appointed campaign commander under Wei Xiaokuan.
entries.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, Hong was made campaign commander to follow Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.

entries.zh: 軍至河陽，迥遣兵圍懷州，洪與總管宇文述等擊走。
entries.en: At Heyang, Jiong sent troops to besiege Huaizhou; Hong and Regional Commander Yuwen Shu drove them off.
entries.literal: When the army reached Heyang, Jiong sent troops to besiege Huaizhou; Hong with regional commander Yuwen Shu and others drove them off.

entries.zh: 又破尉惇于武陟。
entries.en: He also defeated Yuchi Dun at Wuzhi.
entries.literal: He again defeated Yuchi Dun at Wuzhi.

entries.zh: 及平相州，每戰有功，拜柱國，封廣武郡公，邑二千戶。
entries.en: When Xiangzhou fell he distinguished himself in every battle, was made Pillar of State, and was created Duke of Guangwu with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: When Xiangzhou was pacified, he had merit in every battle; he was appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Guangwu commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 前後賜物萬段，奴婢五十口，金銀各百挺，牛馬百匹。
entries.en: In all he received ten thousand bolts of goods, fifty slaves, a hundred ingots each of gold and silver, and a hundred head of cattle and horses.
entries.literal: Before and after he was granted ten thousand bolts of goods, fifty household slaves, a hundred ingots each of gold and silver, and a hundred head of cattle and horses.

entries.zh: 時東夏初平，物情尚梗，高祖以洪有威名，令領冀州事，甚得人和。
entries.en: Eastern China had only just been pacified and the region was still unsettled; Gaozu put Hong in charge of Jizhou for his renown, and he won the people's trust.
entries.literal: At the time eastern Xia had just been pacified and popular sentiment was still unsettled; Gaozu, because Hong had a formidable reputation, ordered him to take charge of Jizhou affairs, and he won great harmony among the people.

entries.zh: 數歲，征入朝，為漕渠總管監，轉拜泗州刺史。
entries.en: Several years later he was recalled to court, supervised the Grand Canal administration, and was transferred to Sizhou as prefect.
entries.literal: Several years later he was summoned to court, served as supervisor of the Grand Canal commandery, and was transferred to prefect of Sizhou.

entries.zh: 屬突厥寇邊，詔洪為北道行軍總管，擊走虜，至磧而還。
entries.en: When the Turks raided the frontier, Hong was made northern campaign commander, drove them off, and returned after reaching the desert.
entries.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Hong was ordered as campaign commander of the northern route; he drove off the enemy and returned upon reaching the desert.

entries.zh: 後遷徐州總管，卒，時年六十四。
entries.en: He was later transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou and died at sixty-four.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou and died at the age of sixty-four.

entries.zh: 侯莫陳穎，字遵道，代人也。
entries.en: Houmo Chenying, courtesy name Zundao, was from Dai.
entries.literal: Houmo Chenying, courtesy name Zundao, was a native of Dai.

entries.zh: 與魏南遷，世為列將。
entries.en: His family moved south with the Wei and for generations served as field commanders.
entries.literal: Moving south with Wei, his family for generations were ranking generals.

entries.zh: 父崇，魏、周之際，曆職顯要，官至大司空。
entries.en: His father Chong held high office during the transition from Wei to Zhou and rose to Grand Minister of Works.
entries.literal: His father Chong, between Wei and Zhou, held prominent posts in succession and rose to Grand Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 穎少有器量，風神警發，為時輩所推。
entries.en: As a youth Ying was broad-minded and keen of bearing, and his contemporaries held him in high regard.
entries.literal: Ying in youth had capacity and breadth of mind, a spirited and alert bearing, and was promoted by men of his generation.

entries.zh: 魏大統末，以父軍功賜爵廣平侯，累遷開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Late in the Wei Great Dominion era he was created Marquis of Guangping for his father's service and rose to Commander Unequaled in Honor (kaifu yitong sansi).
entries.literal: At the end of Great Dominion in Wei he was ennobled as Marquis of Guangping for his father's military merit and was repeatedly promoted to Commander Unequaled in Honor (kaifu yitong sansi).

entries.zh: 周武帝時，從滕王逌擊龍泉、文城叛胡，與柱國豆盧勣各帥兵分路而進。
entries.en: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he followed Prince of Teng Yu against the rebel Hu of Longquan and Wencheng, advancing by separate routes with Pillar of State Doulu Ji.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he followed Prince of Teng Yu in attacking the rebel Hu of Longquan and Wencheng; he and the pillar of state Doulu Ji each led troops by separate routes.

entries.zh: 穎懸軍五百餘裡，破其三柵。
entries.en: Ying marched more than five hundred li into enemy territory and captured three stockades.
entries.literal: Ying led his army deep for more than five hundred li and broke three of their stockades.

entries.zh: 先是，稽胡叛亂，輒略邊人為奴婢。
entries.en: Earlier, whenever the Ji Hu rebelled, they seized frontier people as slaves.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Ji Hu rebelled, they regularly seized frontier people as slaves.

entries.zh: 至是詔胡敢有壓匿良人者誅，籍沒其妻子。
entries.en: An edict now declared that any Hu who concealed commoners would be executed and his family confiscated.
entries.literal: At this time an edict declared that any Hu who dared conceal commoners should be executed and his wife and children registered and confiscated.

entries.zh: 有人言為胡村所隱匿者，勣將誅之，穎謂勣曰：「將在外，君命有所不行。
entries.en: When someone reported that commoners were hidden in a Hu village, Ji was about to execute the villagers; Ying told him, "A general in the field is not bound to obey every command from court.
entries.literal: Someone said concealed persons were hidden in a Hu village; Ji was about to execute them, and Ying said to Ji: "When the general is abroad, the ruler's command may in part go unheeded.

entries.zh: 諸胡固非悉反，但相迫脅為亂耳。
entries.en: Not all the Hu have rebelled; most were forced into it.
entries.literal: These Hu are certainly not all in rebellion; they have merely been compelled and coerced into disorder.

entries.zh: 大兵臨之，首亂者知懼，脅從者思降。
entries.en: When our armies advance, the ringleaders will fear for their lives and the followers will wish to surrender.
entries.literal: When great armies press upon them, the ringleaders will know fear and those coerced will think of surrender.

entries.zh: 今漸加撫慰，自可不戰而定。
entries.en: If we reassure them gradually, we can settle this without a battle.
entries.literal: If we now gradually add reassurance and comfort, we can secure the matter without fighting.

entries.zh: 如即誅之，轉相驚恐，為難不細。
entries.en: If we execute them now, we will only spread panic and make the trouble far worse.
entries.literal: If we execute them at once, they will in turn be alarmed and terrified, and the trouble will be no small matter.

entries.zh: 未若召其渠帥，以隱匿者付之，令自歸首，則群胡可安。」
entries.en: Better to summon their chieftains, hand the concealed persons over to them, and let them surrender voluntarily—the Hu will then be pacified."
entries.literal: Better to summon their chieftains, hand over the concealed persons to them, and order them to surrender of their own accord—then the Hu masses can be pacified."

entries.zh: 勣從之。
entries.en: Ji followed his advice.
entries.literal: Ji followed this advice.

entries.zh: 群胡感悅，爭來降附，北土以安。
entries.en: The Hu were grateful and submitted in great numbers, and the north was pacified.
entries.literal: The Hu masses were moved and pleased and vied to come and submit; the northern lands were thereby secure.

entries.zh: 遷司武，加振威中大夫。
entries.en: He was transferred to Director of Martial Affairs and made Grandee of the Shake-the-Foe Regiment.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Director of Martial Affairs and additionally made Grandee of the Shake-the-Foe Regiment.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，拜昌州刺史。
entries.en: While Gaozu was chief minister, Ying was appointed prefect of Changzhou.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, Ying was appointed prefect of Changzhou.

entries.zh: 會受禪，竟不行，加上開府，進爵升平郡公。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he never assumed that post; instead he was made Senior Commander-in-Chief and created Duke of Shengping.
entries.literal: Just as the abdication was received, he in the end did not take up the post; he was additionally made Senior Commander-in-Chief and advanced to Duke of Shengping commandery.

entries.zh: 俄拜延州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon appointed prefect of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 數年，轉陳州刺史。
entries.en: Several years later he was transferred to Chenzhou as prefect.
entries.literal: Several years later he was transferred to prefect of Chenzhou.

entries.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管從秦王俊出魯山道。
entries.en: In the conquest of Chen he served as campaign commander under Prince of Qin Yang Jun, advancing by the Lushan route.
entries.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, as campaign commander he followed Prince of Qin Jun out by the Lushan route.

entries.zh: 屬陳將荀法尚、陳紀降，穎與行軍總管段文振度江安集初附。
entries.en: When the Chen generals Xun Fashang and Chen Ji surrendered, Ying and Campaign Commander Duan Wenzhen crossed the Yangzi to settle the newly submitted territories.
entries.literal: When the Chen generals Xun Fashang and Chen Ji surrendered, Ying with campaign commander Duan Wenzhen crossed the river to settle and gather those who had just submitted.

entries.zh: 尋拜饒州刺史，未之官，遷瀛州刺史，甚有惠政。
entries.en: He was soon appointed to Raozhou but never took office; transferred to Yingzhou, he governed with notable kindness.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Raozhou but did not take office; he was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou, where he had very benevolent administration.

entries.zh: 在職數年，坐與秦王俊交通免官。
entries.en: After several years in office he was dismissed for associating with Prince of Qin Yang Jun.
entries.literal: During several years in office he was dismissed for communicating with Prince of Qin Jun.

entries.zh: 百姓將送者，莫不流涕，因相與立碑，頌穎清德。
entries.en: The people who came to see him off wept openly, and together they erected a stele praising his integrity.
entries.literal: Among the common people who came to see him off, none failed to weep; they together erected a stele praising Ying's pure virtue.

entries.zh: 未幾，檢校汾州事，俄拜邢州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was put in provisional charge of Fenzhou and shortly afterward appointed prefect of Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Before long he was put in provisional charge of Fenzhou affairs, and soon appointed prefect of Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，吏部尚書牛弘持節巡撫山東，以穎為第一。
entries.en: During Renshou, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong toured Shandong with imperial authority and ranked Ying first among the officials.
entries.literal: During Renshou, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Niu Hong, bearing the staff, toured and pacified Shandong and ranked Ying first.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉歎，優詔褒揚。
entries.en: Gaozu expressed his admiration and issued a gracious edict of praise.
entries.literal: Gaozu praised and sighed over this and issued an excellent edict commending him.

entries.zh: 時朝廷以嶺南刺史、縣令多貪鄙，蠻夷怨叛，妙簡清吏以鎮撫之，於是征穎入朝。
entries.en: The court believed that Lingnan officials were mostly corrupt and that the tribes were rebelling; it sought upright administrators to pacify the region and summoned Ying to court.
entries.literal: At the time the court considered that prefects and county magistrates in Lingnan were mostly greedy and base, and the barbarians resented and rebelled; they carefully selected upright officials to pacify them, and so Ying was summoned to court.

entries.zh: 及進見，上與穎言及平生，以為歡笑。
entries.en: At his audience the emperor spoke with him of old times and they shared a warm laugh.
entries.literal: When he was received in audience, the emperor spoke with Ying of their lives and took it as mirth.

entries.zh: 數日，進位大將軍，拜桂州總管十七州諸軍事，賜物而遣之。
entries.en: A few days later he was promoted to Grand General, appointed regional commander of Guizhou with authority over seventeen prefectures, given gifts, and sent south.
entries.literal: Several days later he was advanced to Grand General, appointed regional commander of Guizhou with military authority over seventeen prefectures, granted goods, and sent forth.

entries.zh: 及到官，大崇恩信，民夷悅服，溪洞生越，多來歸附。
entries.en: On taking office he won people with kindness and trust; Chinese and tribesmen alike submitted gladly, and many Yue from the hill country came to pledge allegiance.
entries.literal: When he reached his post he greatly promoted favor and trust; Chinese and barbarians submitted gladly, and many raw Yue from stream caves came to attach themselves.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，穎兄梁國公芮坐事徙邊，朝廷恐穎不自安，征歸京師。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Ying's elder brother Duke of Liang Rui was banished for an offense; fearing Ying might be unsettled, the court recalled him to the capital.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Ying's elder brother the Duke of Liang Rui was banished to the frontier for an offense; the court feared Ying would not feel secure and summoned him back to the capital.

entries.zh: 數年，拜恆山太守。
entries.en: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Hengshan.
entries.literal: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Hengshan.

entries.zh: 其年，嶺南、閩越多不附，帝以穎前在桂州有惠政，為南土所信伏，複拜南海太守。
entries.en: That year Lingnan and Min-Yue were largely in revolt; because Ying's earlier rule in Guizhou had won the south's trust, the emperor reappointed him administrator of Nanhai.
entries.literal: That same year Lingnan and the Min-Yue regions largely did not submit; the emperor, because Ying had earlier had benevolent administration in Guizhou and was trusted and revered in the southern lands, again appointed him administrator of Nanhai.

entries.zh: 後四歲，卒官。
entries.en: Four years later he died in office.
entries.literal: Four years later he died in office.

entries.zh: 諡曰定。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Ding.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Ding [Settled].

entries.zh: 子虔會，最知名。
entries.en: His son Qianhui became the most famous of his descendants.
entries.literal: His son Qianhui was the most renowned.

entries.zh: 【論】史臣曰：杜彥東夏、南服，屢有戰功，作鎮朔垂，胡塵不起。
entries.en: [Commentary] The historian writes: Du Yan won repeated victories in the east and south; on the northern frontier he kept the barbarians at bay.
entries.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Du Yan in eastern Xia and the southern domains repeatedly had battle merit; holding the northern frontier, Turkic dust did not rise.

entries.zh: 高勱死亡之際，志氣懍然，疾彼奸邪，致茲餘慶。
entries.en: Gao Mai faced Qi's fall with unbroken spirit, condemned its wicked ministers, and left his house a legacy of honor.
entries.literal: Gao Mai at the moment of Qi's fall had stern and unyielding spirit, hated those wicked and devious men, and thereby brought down this remaining blessing.

entries.zh: 爾硃敞幼有權奇，終能止足，崇基墜而複構，不亦仁且智乎！
entries.en: Erzhu Chang showed early resourcefulness and knew when to stop; his house fell and rose again—was this not wisdom joined to humanity!
entries.literal: Erzhu Chang in youth had resourceful strangeness and in the end knew when to stop; a lofty foundation fell and was built again—is this not both benevolent and wise!

entries.zh: 周搖以質實見知，獨孤以恤人流譽，乞伏慧能以國讓，侯莫陳所居治理，或知牧人之道，或踐仁義之路，皆有可稱焉。
entries.en: Zhou Yao was valued for integrity, Dugu Kai for compassion, Qi Fuhui for yielding honors to his brother, and Houmo Chenying for good governance—some knew how to rule the people, others walked the path of benevolence; each had qualities worth praise.
entries.literal: Zhou Yao was known for plain substance, Dugu for compassion toward the people, Qi Fuhui for ability to yield rank and state, and Houmo Chen for good governance wherever he served—some knew the way of shepherding the people, some walked the path of benevolence and righteousness; all had what may be praised.

entries.zh: 慧以供帳不厚，至於放黜，並結髮登朝，出入三代，終享祿位，不夭性齡，蓋其任心而行，不為矯飾之所致也。
entries.en: Hui was dismissed because his official hospitality was too plain; yet they all entered service young, served three dynasties, and died in honor at full span—because they acted from the heart and never put on airs.
entries.literal: Hui because his provisions and equipage were not lavish was even dismissed from office; yet all from youth entered court, passed through three dynasties, and in the end enjoyed salary and rank without shortened natural span—probably because they acted as their hearts directed and did not owe it to forced ornamentation.

entries.zh: 盧愷，字長仁，涿郡范陽人也。
entries.en: Lu Kai, courtesy name Changren, came from Fanyang in Zhuo Commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Kai, styled Changren, was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo Commandery.

entries.zh: 父柔，終於魏中書監。
entries.en: His father Rou had ended his career as director of the secretariat under Wei.
entries.literal: His father Rou ended his life as Director of the Secretariat of Wei.

entries.zh: 愷性孝友，神情爽悟，略涉書記，頗解屬文。
entries.en: Kai was by nature filial and devoted to his brothers, quick-witted and sharp of mind. He had some familiarity with letters and records and was fairly skilled at literary composition.
entries.literal: Kai's nature was filial and friendly; his spirit was clear and perceptive; he had slight involvement in writing and records, and was rather able at literary composition.

entries.zh: 周齊王憲引為記室。
entries.en: Prince Xian of Qi brought him in as master of records.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou summoned him as Master of Records.

entries.zh: 其後襲爵容城伯，邑千一百戶。
entries.en: He later inherited the title Baron of Rongcheng, with a fief of eleven hundred households.
entries.literal: Thereafter he inherited the rank of Baron of Rongcheng, with a fief of 1,100 households.

entries.zh: 從憲伐齊，愷說柏杜鎮下之。
entries.en: When he followed Xian in the campaign against Qi, Kai talked the garrison at Baidu into surrendering.
entries.literal: Following Xian in the campaign against Qi, Kai persuaded Baidu Garrison to submit.

entries.zh: 遷小吏部大夫，增邑七百戶。
entries.en: He was promoted to senior clerk in the ministry of personnel and received seven hundred additional households in his fief.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, with his fief increased by 700 households.

entries.zh: 染工上士王神歡者，嘗以賂自進，塚宰宇文護擢為計部下大夫。
entries.en: A dye-work artisan named Wang Shenhuan had once bought his way forward; Grand Minister Yuwen Hu raised him to senior clerk in the accounting bureau.
entries.literal: A dye-work artisan senior officer Wang Shenhuan had once used bribes to advance himself; Grand Minister Yuwen Hu promoted him to Senior Clerk in the Accounting Bureau.

entries.zh: 愷諫曰：「古者登高能賦，可為大夫，求賢審官，理須詳慎。
entries.en: Kai remonstrated: "In antiquity a man who climbed high and composed verse could qualify as a grandee. In seeking talent and assigning office, the principle demands careful deliberation.
entries.literal: Kai remonstrated, saying: "In antiquity, one who ascended high could compose poetry and qualify as a grandee; in seeking the worthy and examining officials, principle requires thorough care.

entries.zh: 今神歡出自染工，更無殊異，徒以家富自通，遂與搢紳並列，實恐惟鵜之刺，聞之外境。」
entries.en: Now Shenhuan rose from the dye pits without any distinction otherwise. He gained access solely through family wealth and now ranks beside the silk-gowned elite. I fear the sting of the proverb about a lone pelican among fine birds will be heard beyond our borders."
entries.literal: Now Shenhuan comes from dye work and has no other distinction; he has merely used family wealth to win access, and so stands alongside gentry officials—I truly fear the reproach of the lone pelican will be heard beyond our borders."

entries.zh: 護竟寢其事。
entries.en: Hu ultimately dropped the matter.
entries.literal: Hu ultimately set the matter aside.

entries.zh: 建德中，增邑二百戶。
entries.en: During the Jiande reign, he received two hundred more households in his fief.
entries.literal: In the Jiande era, his fief was increased by 200 households.

entries.zh: 歲餘，轉內史下大夫。
entries.en: A year or so later he was transferred to senior clerk in the imperial secretariat.
entries.literal: After a little over a year, he was transferred to Senior Clerk in the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 武帝在雲陽宮，敕諸屯簡老牛，欲以享士。
entries.en: While Emperor Wu was at Yunyang Palace, he ordered the garrisons to pick out old oxen, planning to use them to feed his soldiers.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu was at Yunyang Palace and ordered the garrisons to select old oxen, intending to use them to feast the troops.

entries.zh: 愷進諫曰：「昔田子方贖老馬，君子以為美談。
entries.en: Kai stepped forward to remonstrate: "Long ago Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse—a deed gentlemen still praise.
entries.literal: Kai advanced in remonstrance, saying: "In the past Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse, and gentlemen took it as a fine story.

entries.zh: 向奉明敕，欲以老牛享士，有虧仁政。」
entries.en: Yet the order just issued would slaughter old oxen to feed the troops. That falls short of humane rule."
entries.literal: Just now in obeying the clear edict, you wish to use old oxen to feast the troops—this falls short of humane governance."

entries.zh: 帝美其言而止。
entries.en: The emperor applauded his advice and halted the plan.
entries.literal: The Emperor praised his words and stopped.

entries.zh: 轉禮部大夫，為聘陳使副。
entries.en: He was made senior clerk in the ministry of rites and served as deputy on the embassy to Chen.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk in the Ministry of Rites and served as deputy envoy on the mission to Chen.

entries.zh: 先是，行人多從其國禮，及愷為使，一依本朝，陳人莫能屈。
entries.en: Before this, envoys had often followed Chen court etiquette. When Kai led the mission, he adhered entirely to his own court's protocol, and the Chen side could not make him yield.
entries.literal: Previously, envoys often followed Chen's ceremonial forms; when Kai became envoy, he followed his own court entirely, and the men of Chen could not bend him.

entries.zh: 四年秋，李穆攻拔軹關、柏崖二鎮，命愷作露布，帝讀之大悅，曰：「盧愷文章大進，荀景倩故是令君之子。」
entries.en: In the autumn of the fourth year, Li Mu took the garrisons at Zhiguan and Baiya. Kai was ordered to write the victory proclamation. The emperor read it with delight and said, "Lu Kai's writing has improved greatly. It is no wonder—Xun Jingqian was ever the son of a worthy father."
entries.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, Li Mu captured the two garrisons of Zhiguan and Baiya; Kai was ordered to compose a battle bulletin. The Emperor read it and was greatly pleased, saying: "Lu Kai's literary skill has greatly advanced—Xun Jingqian was indeed the son of a fine lord."

entries.zh: 尋授襄州總管司錄，轉治中。
entries.en: Soon after he was made registrar to the governor-general of Xiangzhou, then promoted to administering director.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Xiangzhou and then transferred to Administering Director.

entries.zh: 大象元年，征拜東京吏部大夫。
entries.en: In the first year of Daxiang he was summoned and appointed senior clerk of personnel in the eastern capital.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, he was summoned and appointed Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel in the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 開皇初，加上儀同三司，除尚書吏部侍郎，進爵為侯，仍攝尚書左丞。
entries.en: Early in the Kaihuang era he received the additional title of pillar of state, third rank, was appointed vice minister of personnel, was raised to marquis, and continued to act as left vice director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was given the additional title Pillar of State, Third Rank, appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced in rank to Marquis, and still acted as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 每有敷奏，侃然正色，雖逢喜怒，不改其常。
entries.en: Whenever he submitted memorials, he spoke plainly with a steady countenance. Neither favor nor wrath from the throne could shake his usual bearing.
entries.literal: Whenever he presented memorials, he was forthright and stern-faced; even when encountering joy or anger, he did not change his usual demeanor.

entries.zh: 帝嘉愷有吏幹，賜錢二十萬，並賚雜彩三百匹，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: The emperor praised Kai's administrative talent, gave him two hundred thousand coins and three hundred bolts of mixed silks, and added the title attendant cavalier at large.
entries.literal: The Emperor commended Kai for his administrative capacity, granted him 200,000 coins, and bestowed 300 bolts of assorted silks, adding Attendant Cavalier at Large.

entries.zh: 八年，上親考百僚，以愷為上。
entries.en: In the eighth year the emperor personally evaluated the bureaucracy and ranked Kai highest.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, the Emperor personally examined the hundred officials and ranked Kai as superior.

entries.zh: 愷固讓，不敢受，高祖曰：「吏部勤幹，舊所聞悉。
entries.en: Kai firmly declined, not daring to accept. Emperor Gaozu said, "Your diligence and competence in personnel matters are well known to me already.
entries.literal: Kai firmly declined and did not dare accept; Emperor Gaozu said: "Your diligence and capacity in the Ministry of Personnel are long known to me.

entries.zh: 今者上考，僉議攸同，當仁不讓，何愧之有！
entries.en: Today you receive the top grade with unanimous agreement. When the honor is rightly yours, why refuse it out of false modesty!
entries.literal: Now that the superior rating is unanimous in opinion, when duty calls one should not yield—what is there to be ashamed of!

entries.zh: 皆在朕心，無勞飾讓。」
entries.en: It is all clear in my mind—spare yourself the show of deference."
entries.literal: All of this is in my heart; there is no need for pretended modesty."

entries.zh: 歲餘，拜禮部尚書，攝吏部尚書事。
entries.en: A year or so later he was appointed minister of rites and also took charge of personnel affairs.
entries.literal: After a little over a year, he was appointed Minister of Rites and acted in the duties of Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 會國子博士何妥與右僕射蘇威不平，奏威陰事。
entries.en: At this time He Tuo, a doctor of the imperial university, bore a grudge against Vice Director Su Wei and reported secret misconduct on Wei's part.
entries.literal: It happened that Academician He Tuo of the Imperial University was at odds with Vice Director Su Wei and memorialized Wei's hidden affairs.

entries.zh: 愷坐與相連，上以愷屬吏。
entries.en: Kai was implicated in the case and the emperor turned him over to the judicial authorities.
entries.literal: Kai was implicated by association and the Emperor handed Kai over to the legal authorities.

entries.zh: 憲司奏愷曰：「房恭懿者，尉遲迥之党，不當仕進。
entries.en: The prosecutors reported: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yuchi Jiong and should never have been promoted.
entries.literal: The legal authorities memorialized against Kai: "Fang Gongyi was a follower of Yuwen Jiong and should not have been allowed to enter office.

entries.zh: 威、愷二人曲相薦達，累轉為海州刺史。
entries.en: Wei and Kai repeatedly shielded and promoted him until he rose to governor of Haizhou.
entries.literal: Wei and Kai both bent the rules to recommend and advance him, repeatedly transferring him until he became Governor of Haizhou.

entries.zh: 又吏部預選者甚多，愷不即授官，皆注色而遣。
entries.en: Moreover, many candidates passed preliminary selection in personnel, but Kai would not appoint them immediately—he marked them in red and dismissed them.
entries.literal: Moreover, many candidates were pre-selected in the Ministry of Personnel; Kai did not immediately grant office but marked them in red and sent them away.

entries.zh: 威之從父弟徹、肅二人，並以鄉正征詣吏部。
entries.en: Wei's paternal cousins Che and Su were both summoned to personnel as village magistrates.
entries.literal: Wei's cousins Che and Su were both summoned to the Ministry of Personnel as village magistrates.

entries.zh: 徹文狀後至而先任用，肅左足攣蹇，才用無算，愷以威故，授朝請郎。
entries.en: Che's paperwork arrived late yet he was appointed ahead of others. Su had a crippled left foot and no discernible talent, yet Kai made him a gentleman for court appearance out of regard for Wei.
entries.literal: Che's petition arrived late yet was appointed first; Su had a withered left foot and no talent to speak of, yet Kai, because of Wei, made him Gentleman for Court Appearance.

entries.zh: 愷之朋黨，事甚明白。」
entries.en: The evidence of Kai's clique-building was plain."
entries.literal: Kai's factional conduct was very clear."

entries.zh: 上大怒曰：「愷敢將天官以為私惠！」
entries.en: The emperor raged: "Kai dares to treat the court's offices as his personal patronage!"
entries.literal: The Emperor flew into a rage: "Kai dares to turn the offices of Heaven into private favors!"

entries.zh: 愷免冠頓首曰：「皇太子將以通事舍人蘇夔為舍人，夔即蘇威之子，臣以夔未當遷，固啟而止。
entries.en: Kai bared his head and prostrated himself: "The crown prince was about to appoint transmission officer Su Kui as palace attendant. Kui is Su Wei's son. I judged him unworthy of promotion and firmly petitioned to stop it.
entries.literal: Kai removed his cap and knocked his head, saying: "The Crown Prince was about to appoint Transmission Officer Su Kui as palace attendant; Kui is Su Wei's son. I thought Kui was unfit for transfer and firmly memorialized to stop it.

entries.zh: 臣若與威有私，豈當如此！」
entries.en: If I had private dealings with Wei, would I have done such a thing!"
entries.literal: If I had private relations with Wei, would I have acted thus!"

entries.zh: 上曰：「蘇威之子，朝廷共知，卿乃固執，以徼身幸。
entries.en: The emperor said, "Everyone at court knows Su Wei's son. You held fast anyway—clearly seeking personal advantage.
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Su Wei's son is known to the whole court; you nevertheless held fast, seeking personal fortune.

entries.zh: 至所不知者，便行朋附，奸臣之行也。」
entries.en: But for those you did not even know, you practiced favoritism. That is the conduct of a treacherous minister."
entries.literal: As for those you did not know, you practiced factional attachment—that is the conduct of a treacherous minister."

entries.zh: 於是除名為百姓。
entries.en: He was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒於家。
entries.en: Not long afterward he died at home.
entries.literal: Before long he died at home.

entries.zh: 自周氏以降，選無清濁，及愷攝吏部，與薛道衡、陸彥師等甄別士流，故涉黨固之譖，遂及於此。
entries.en: Since Zhou times official selection had made no distinction between worthy and unworthy. When Kai took charge of personnel, he worked with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi to sort the gentry by merit, and thus incurred the slander of forming a solid clique—which brought him to this end.
entries.literal: From the Zhou dynasty onward selection had no distinction of pure and impure; when Kai acted in the Ministry of Personnel, he with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others discriminated among the gentry streams, and so he fell under slanders of clique-forming.

entries.zh: 子義恭嗣。
entries.en: His son Yigong inherited his title.
entries.literal: His son Yigong succeeded.

entries.zh: 令狐熙，字長熙，燉煌人也，代為西州豪右。
entries.en: Linghu Xi, courtesy name Changxi, came from Dunhuang. His family had for generations been leading magnates of the western prefectures.
entries.literal: Linghu Xi, styled Changxi, was a man of Dunhuang; for generations his family had been powerful magnates of the Western Prefectures.

entries.zh: 父整，仕周，官至大將軍、始、豐二州刺史。
entries.en: His father Zheng served under Zhou, rising to grand general and governor of Shi and Feng prefectures.
entries.literal: His father Zheng served Zhou and reached the rank of Grand General and Governor of the two prefectures of Shi and Feng.

entries.zh: 熙性嚴重，有雅量，雖在私室，終日儼然。
entries.en: Xi was stern and dignified, with a refined breadth of mind. Even in his own home he maintained a grave bearing from morning to night.
entries.literal: Xi's nature was stern and weighty, with refined capacity; even in private quarters he remained dignified all day.

entries.zh: 不妄通賓客，凡所交給，必一時名士。
entries.en: He did not casually receive guests; every associate he made was a noted figure of the day.
entries.literal: He did not casually associate with guests; whoever he befriended was invariably a leading man of the age.

entries.zh: 博覽群書，尤明《三禮》，善騎射，頗知音律。
entries.en: He read widely among the classics and was especially learned in 《Three Rites》. He was skilled at mounted archery and had a fair knowledge of musical theory.
entries.literal: He broadly read the classics and was especially versed in 《Three Rites》; he was skilled at mounted archery and had considerable knowledge of music.

entries.zh: 起家以通經為吏部上士，尋授都督、輔國將軍，轉夏官府都上士，俱有能名。
entries.en: He entered service as a senior officer in personnel through classical learning, then became commander and general who supports the state, and later senior officer of the summer office—winning a name for competence at each post.
entries.literal: He began his career as a Senior Officer in the Ministry of Personnel through mastery of the classics, was soon appointed Commander and General Who Supports the State, and was transferred to Senior Officer of the Summer Office—all with reputations for competence.

entries.zh: 以母憂去職，殆不勝喪。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his mother and nearly did not survive his grief.
entries.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother and nearly could not survive the grief.

entries.zh: 其父戒之曰：「大孝在於安親，義不絕嗣。
entries.en: His father warned him: "The greatest filial piety is to bring your parents peace of mind. By duty you must not let the family line die out.
entries.literal: His father admonished him, saying: "The greatest filial piety lies in bringing peace to one's parents; by right one must not cut off the line of succession.

entries.zh: 吾今見存，汝又只立，何得過爾毀頓，貽吾憂也！」
entries.en: I am still alive, and you are my only son. How can you destroy yourself like this and leave me in anguish!"
entries.literal: I am still alive, and you are my only son—how can you go so far in ruining yourself and leaving me in worry!"

entries.zh: 熙自是稍加饘粥。
entries.en: From then on Xi gradually began to take thin gruel.
entries.literal: From then on Xi gradually took a little gruel.

entries.zh: 服闋，除小駕部，複丁父憂，非杖不起，人有聞其哭聲，莫不為之下泣。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was appointed junior master of the imperial carriage. He then mourned his father again, unable to rise without a staff. All who heard him weep wept in turn.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Junior Master of the Imperial Carriage; he again entered mourning for his father, and unless leaning on a staff he could not rise; whoever heard his weeping could not keep from weeping below him.

entries.zh: 河陰之役，詔令墨縗從事，還授職方下大夫，襲爵彭陽縣公，邑二千一百戶。
entries.en: At the battle of Heyin an edict ordered him to serve while still in mourning garb. On his return he was appointed junior grand master of the Bureau of Operations, inherited the title Duke of Pengyang, and received a fief of twenty-one hundred households.
entries.literal: In the campaign at Heyin, an edict ordered him to serve in ink-stained mourning garb; on return he was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Bureau of Operations, inherited the rank of Duke of Pengyang County, with a fief of 2,100 households.

entries.zh: 及武帝平齊，以留守功，增邑六百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, his fief was increased by six hundred households for his service as garrison commander.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Qi, for his merit as garrison commander his fief was increased by 600 households.

entries.zh: 進位儀同，曆司勳、吏部二曹中大夫，甚有當時之譽。
entries.en: He rose to pillar of state and served in turn as senior clerk in the bureaus of merits and personnel, earning great renown in his day.
entries.literal: He advanced to Pillar of State, served successively as Senior Clerk in the Bureaus of Merits and Personnel, and had great reputation in his time.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪之際，熙以本官行納言事。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Xi served in his existing post as acting Neiyan.
entries.literal: At the moment Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Xi acted in the duties of Neiyan in his original post.

entries.zh: 尋除司徒左長史，加上儀同，進爵河南郡公。
entries.en: Soon he was made left chief administrator of the ministry of education, given the additional title pillar of state, and raised to duke of Henan commandery.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Chief Administrator of the Ministry of Education, given the additional title Pillar of State, and advanced to Duke of Henan Commandery.

entries.zh: 時吐谷渾寇邊，以行軍長史從元帥元諧討之，以功進位上開府。
entries.en: When Tuyuhun raided the frontier, he served as chief administrator on campaign under Commander-in-Chief Yuan Xie. For his merit he was promoted to senior pillar of state.
entries.literal: When Tuyuhun raided the frontier, he went as Chief Administrator on campaign with Commander-in-Chief Yuan Xie to suppress them and, for merit, advanced to Senior Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 會蜀王秀出鎮於蜀，綱紀之選，鹹屬正人，以熙為益州總管長史。
entries.en: When Prince Xiu of Shu was sent to govern Shu, upright men were chosen to keep order, and Xi was appointed chief administrator to the governor-general of Yizhou.
entries.literal: When Prince of Shu Xiu went out to govern Shu, the choice of administrators all fell on upright men, and Xi was made Chief Administrator to the Governor-General of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 未之官，拜滄州刺史。
entries.en: Before he could take that post he was appointed governor of Cangzhou.
entries.literal: Before taking office he was appointed Governor of Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 時山東承齊之弊，戶口名簿籍類不以實。
entries.en: At that time Shandong still bore the abuses of Qi rule; household registers and name lists often did not reflect reality.
entries.literal: At that time Shandong still suffered the abuses of Qi; household registers and name lists often did not reflect reality.

entries.zh: 熙曉諭之，令自歸首，至者一萬戶。
entries.en: Xi explained the law to them and ordered voluntary surrender; ten thousand households came forward.
entries.literal: Xi enlightened them and ordered self-surrender; those who came numbered 10,000 households.

entries.zh: 在職數年，風教大洽，稱為良二千石。
entries.en: Within a few years in office customs and instruction were greatly improved, and he was hailed as an excellent governor.
entries.literal: In several years of office, customs and instruction were greatly harmonized, and he was called a fine governor of two thousand dan.

entries.zh: 開皇四年，上幸洛陽，熙來朝，吏民恐其遷易，悲泣於道。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Luoyang. When Xi came to court, officials and commoners, fearing he would be transferred, wept along the road.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang the Emperor visited Luoyang; Xi came to court, and officials and people, fearing he would be transferred, wept along the road.

entries.zh: 及熙複還，百姓出境迎謁，歡叫盈路。
entries.en: When Xi returned, the people went out beyond the border to welcome him, and cheers filled the roads.
entries.literal: When Xi returned again, the people went beyond the border to welcome and greet him, with shouts of joy filling the road.

entries.zh: 在州獲白烏、白麞、嘉麥，甘露降於庭前柳樹。
entries.en: While he governed, white crows, white musk deer, and fine wheat appeared in the prefecture, and sweet dew fell on the willow tree before his hall.
entries.literal: In the prefecture white crows, white musk deer, and fine wheat appeared, and sweet dew fell on the willow tree before the courtyard.

entries.zh: 八年，徙為河北道行台度支尚書，吏民追思，相與立碑頌德。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was transferred to director of revenue on the Hebei circuit executive. Officials and people, cherishing his memory, together erected a stele praising his virtue.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director of Revenue of the Hebei Circuit Executive and the officials and people, cherishing his memory, together erected a stele praising his virtue.

entries.zh: 及行台廢，授并州總管司馬。
entries.en: When the circuit executive was abolished, he was appointed administering director to the governor-general of Bingzhou.
entries.literal: When the executive was abolished, he was appointed Administering Director to the Governor-General of Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 後征為雍州別駕。
entries.en: He was later summoned as vice governor of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Later he was summoned as Vice Governor of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 尋為長史，遷鴻臚卿。
entries.en: Soon he became chief administrator, then was transferred to grand master for ceremonials.
entries.literal: Soon he became Chief Administrator, then was transferred to Grand Master for Ceremonials.

entries.zh: 後以本官兼吏部尚書，往判五曹尚書事，號為明幹，上甚任之。
entries.en: Later, while retaining his original post, he also served as minister of personnel and adjudicated the affairs of the five ministries. Known for clarity and competence, he enjoyed the emperor's great trust.
entries.literal: Later, in his original post he additionally served as Minister of Personnel and went to decide the affairs of the five ministries, being called clear and capable; the Emperor greatly relied on him.

entries.zh: 及上祠太山還，次汴州，惡其殷盛，多有奸俠，於是以熙為汴州刺史。
entries.en: When the emperor returned from the sacrifice at Mount Tai and stopped at Bianzhou, he disliked the city's prosperity and its many scoundrels, and so appointed Xi governor of Bianzhou.
entries.literal: When the Emperor returned from sacrificing at Mount Tai and stopped at Bianzhou, disliking its prosperity and the many scoundrels and ruffians, he therefore made Xi Governor of Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 下車禁遊食，抑工商，民有向街開門者杜之，船客停于郭外星居者，勒為聚落，僑人逐令歸本，其有滯獄，並決遣之，令行禁止，稱為良政。
entries.en: On taking office he banned itinerant food-sellers, restrained merchants and artisans, shut doors that opened directly onto the street, forced boat travelers lodging outside the city wall into settled communities, ordered migrants to return home, and cleared all delayed cases. Orders were enforced and prohibitions obeyed, and his rule was praised as excellent.
entries.literal: On taking office he forbade wandering food-vendors, suppressed merchants and artisans, blocked those who opened doors facing the street, compelled boat travelers who lodged outside the outer wall to settle in communities, ordered sojourners to return home, and decided and dispatched all delayed cases; orders were enforced and prohibitions observed, and it was called good governance.

entries.zh: 上聞而嘉之，顧謂侍臣曰：「鄴都天下難理處也。」
entries.en: The emperor heard of this and praised it, telling his attendants, "Ye was the hardest place in the realm to govern."
entries.literal: The Emperor heard and commended it, turning to his attendants and saying: "Ye City is the hardest place under Heaven to govern."

entries.zh: 敕相州刺史豆盧通，令習熙之法。
entries.en: He ordered Doulu Tong, governor of Xiangzhou, to adopt Xi's methods.
entries.literal: He ordered Governor of Xiangzhou Doulu Tong to study Xi's methods.

entries.zh: 其年來朝，考績為天下之最，賜帛三百匹，頒告天下。
entries.en: That year he came to court. His performance review ranked first in the realm; he received three hundred bolts of silk, and the announcement was issued throughout the empire.
entries.literal: That year he came to court; his performance review was the highest in the realm, and he was granted 300 bolts of silk and the announcement was issued throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 上以嶺南夷、越數為反亂，征拜桂州總管十七州諸軍事，許以便宜從事，刺史以下官得承制補授。
entries.en: Because the Yi and Yue peoples of Lingnan rebelled repeatedly, he was summoned as governor-general of Guizhou over seventeen prefectures with military authority, empowered to act as circumstances required. Officials below the rank of governor could be appointed on his authority.
entries.literal: Because the Yi and Yue of Lingnan repeatedly rebelled, he was summoned as Governor-General of Guizhou over seventeen prefectures with military authority, permitted to act as circumstances required; officials below governor could be appointed by imperial commission.

entries.zh: 給帳內五百人，賜帛五百匹，發傳送其家累，改封武康郡公。
entries.en: He was given five hundred tent guards, five hundred bolts of silk, relay transport for his household, and was re-enfeoffed as duke of Wukang commandery.
entries.literal: He was given 500 men within the tent guard, granted 500 bolts of silk, provided relay transport for his household, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang Commandery.

entries.zh: 熙至部，大弘恩信，其溪洞渠帥更相謂曰：「前時總管皆以兵威相脅，今者乃以手教相諭，我輩其可違乎？」
entries.en: When Xi reached his post he greatly extended grace and trust. The chieftains of the stream valleys said to one another, "Former governors all coerced us with military might. Now he instructs us with his own hand—how can we disobey?"
entries.literal: When Xi reached his post he greatly extended grace and trust; the chieftains of the stream valleys said to one another: "Former governors all coerced us with military might; now he instructs us with his own hand—how can we disobey?"

entries.zh: 於是相率歸附。
entries.en: They submitted in succession.
entries.literal: Thereupon they submitted in succession.

entries.zh: 先是，州縣生梗，長吏多不得之官，寄政于總管府。
entries.en: Previously the prefectures and counties had been stubborn and hard to govern; chief officials often could not take office, and administration was left to the governor-general's office.
entries.literal: Previously the prefectures and counties were stubborn and ungovernable; chief officials often could not take office, and governance was entrusted to the governor-general's office.

entries.zh: 熙悉遣之，為建城邑，開設學校，華夷感敬，稱為大化。
entries.en: Xi sent them all to their posts, built cities and towns, and established schools. Both Chinese and indigenous peoples were moved to respect him, calling his rule a great transformation.
entries.literal: Xi sent them all out, built cities and towns, established schools, and both Chinese and barbarians were moved to respect him, calling it great transformation.

entries.zh: 時有寧猛力者，與陳後主同日生，自言貌有貴相，在陳日，已據南海，平陳後，高祖因而撫之，即拜安州刺史。
entries.en: At that time there was Ning Mengli, born on the same day as Chen's last ruler. He claimed his features marked him for nobility. Under Chen he had already held the South Sea. After Chen fell, Emperor Gaozu comforted him and immediately appointed him governor of Anzhou.
entries.literal: At that time there was Ning Mengli, born on the same day as Chen's last ruler; he claimed his appearance had the signs of nobility. Under Chen he already held the South Sea; after Chen was pacified, Emperor Gaozu therefore comforted him and immediately appointed him Governor of Anzhou.

entries.zh: 然驕倨，恃其阻險，未嘗參謁。
entries.en: Yet he was arrogant and insolent, relying on his rugged terrain, and never came to pay his respects.
entries.literal: Yet he was arrogant and insolent, relying on his rugged terrain, and never came to pay respects.

entries.zh: 熙手書諭之 ，申以交友之分。
entries.en: Xi wrote him a personal letter, appealing to the bond of friendship.
entries.literal: Xi wrote him a personal letter, explaining the bond of friendship.

entries.zh: 其母有疢，熙複遺以藥物。
entries.en: When his mother fell ill, Xi once more sent her medicines.
entries.literal: His mother had an illness; Xi again sent her medicines.

entries.zh: 猛力感之，詣府請謁，不敢為非。
entries.en: Moved by this, Mengli came to the prefecture to pay his respects and no longer dared misbehave.
entries.literal: Mengli was moved, came to the prefecture to request audience, and did not dare do wrong.

entries.zh: 熙以州縣多有同名者，於是奏改安州為欽州，黃州為峰州，利州為智州，德州為歡州，東寧為融州，上皆從之。
entries.en: Because many prefectures and counties shared the same names, he memorialized to rename Anzhou as Qinzhou, Huangzhou as Fengzhou, Lizhou as Zhizhou, Dezhou as Huanzhou, and Dongning as Rongzhou. The emperor approved all the changes.
entries.literal: Because many prefectures and counties had the same names, he therefore memorialized to change Anzhou to Qinzhou, Huangzhou to Fengzhou, Lizhou to Zhizhou, Dezhou to Huanzhou, and Dongning to Rongzhou; the Emperor all approved.

entries.zh: 在職數年，上表曰：「臣忝寄嶺表，四載於茲，犬馬之年，六十有一。
entries.en: After several years in office he memorialized: "I am entrusted with the region beyond the ridges; four years have now passed. In the years allotted to a loyal servant I am sixty-one.
entries.literal: After several years in office he memorialized: "I am entrusted to the region beyond the ridges; four years have passed. In the years of a dog's service I am sixty-one.

entries.zh: 才輕任重，愧懼兼深，常願收拙避賢，稍免官謗。
entries.en: My talent is slight and my burden heavy; shame and fear weigh on me alike. I have long wished to withdraw my inadequacy and yield to the worthy, and so escape official blame.
entries.literal: My talent is slight and my burden heavy; shame and fear are both deep. I have long wished to withdraw my inadequacy and yield to the worthy, slightly escaping official slander.

entries.zh: 然所管遐曠，綏撫尤難，雖未能頓革夷風，頗亦漸識皇化。
entries.en: Yet the territory I govern is remote and vast, and pacification is especially difficult. Though I have not been able to reform barbarian customs at a stroke, I have gradually made them recognize imperial civilization.
entries.literal: Yet the territory I govern is remote and vast, and pacification is especially difficult; though I have not been able suddenly to reform barbarian customs, I have gradually made them know imperial transformation.

entries.zh: 但臣夙患消渴，比更增甚，筋力精神，轉就衰邁。
entries.en: But I have long suffered from wasting thirst, and lately it has grown worse. My sinews, strength, and spirit are failing by the day.
entries.literal: But I have long suffered from wasting thirst, and recently it has grown worse; sinew, strength, and spirit progressively decline.

entries.zh: 昔在壯齒，猶不如人，況今年疾俱侵，豈可猶當重寄！
entries.en: Even in my prime I was no match for others. Now that illness afflicts me as well, how can I still bear so heavy a charge!
entries.literal: Even in my prime I was still inferior to others; how much less now that illness attacks me together—how can I still bear a heavy trust!

entries.zh: 請解所任。」
entries.en: I beg to be released from my duties."
entries.literal: I request to be released from my post."

entries.zh: 優詔不許，賜以醫藥。
entries.en: A gracious edict refused his request and granted him medicines.
entries.literal: A gracious edict did not permit it and granted him medicines.

entries.zh: 熙奉詔，令交州渠帥李佛子入朝。
entries.en: Xi received the edict and ordered Li Fozi, a stream chieftain of Jiaozhou, to come to court.
entries.literal: Xi received the edict and ordered the stream chieftain Li Fozi of Jiaozhou to come to court.

entries.zh: 佛子欲為亂，請至仲冬上道，熙意在羈縻，遂從之。
entries.en: Fozi intended rebellion and asked to set out in mid-winter. Xi, intending to keep him on a loose rein, agreed.
entries.literal: Fozi wished to rebel and requested to set out in mid-winter; Xi, intending to keep him on a loose rein, agreed.

entries.zh: 有人詣闕訟熙受佛子賂而舍之，上聞而固疑之。
entries.en: Someone went to the palace to accuse Xi of accepting bribes from Fozi and releasing him. The emperor heard and firmly suspected him.
entries.literal: Someone went to the palace to accuse Xi of accepting bribes from Fozi and releasing him; the Emperor heard and firmly suspected.

entries.zh: 既而佛子反問至，上大怒，以為信然，遣使者鎖熙詣闕。
entries.en: Soon word came that Fozi had rebelled. The emperor was greatly enraged, believing the accusation true, and sent envoys to fetter Xi and bring him to court.
entries.literal: Soon word came that Fozi had rebelled; the Emperor was greatly enraged, believing it true, and sent envoys to fetter Xi and bring him to court.

entries.zh: 熙性素剛，鬱鬱不得志，行至永州，憂憤發病而卒，時年六十三。
entries.en: Xi had always been firm by nature. Depressed and unable to achieve his aims, he reached Yongzhou, fell ill from grief and anger, and died at sixty-three.
entries.literal: Xi's nature had always been firm; depressed and unable to achieve his aims, on reaching Yongzhou he fell ill from grief and anger and died, aged sixty-three.

entries.zh: 上怒不解，於是沒其家財。
entries.en: The emperor's anger did not subside, and his family property was confiscated.
entries.literal: The Emperor's anger did not subside, and so his family property was confiscated.

entries.zh: 及行軍總管劉方擒佛子送于京師，言熙實無贓貨，上乃悟，於是召其四子，聽預仕焉。
entries.en: When campaign commander Liu Fang captured Fozi and sent him to the capital, he reported that Xi had truly taken no bribes. The emperor then understood and summoned his four sons, permitting them to enter office.
entries.literal: When Campaign Commander Liu Fang captured Fozi and sent him to the capital, he said Xi truly had no bribe goods; the Emperor then understood, and summoned his four sons and permitted them to enter office.

entries.zh: 少子德棻，最知名。
entries.en: The youngest son, Defen, was the most renowned.
entries.literal: The youngest son Defen was the most renowned.

entries.zh: 薛胄，字紹玄，河東汾陰人也。
entries.en: Xue Zhou, courtesy name Shao'xuan, came from Fenyin in Hedong.
entries.literal: Xue Zhou, styled Shao'xuan, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.

entries.zh: 父端，周蔡州刺史。
entries.en: His father Duan had been governor of Cai prefecture under Zhou.
entries.literal: His father Duan was Governor of Cai Prefecture under Zhou.

entries.zh: 胄少聰明，每覽異書，便曉其義。
entries.en: Zhou was clever from youth. Whenever he read an unusual book he grasped its meaning at once.
entries.literal: Zhou from youth was clever; whenever he read unusual books he immediately understood their meaning.

entries.zh: 常歎訓注者不會聖人深旨，輒以意辯之，諸儒莫不稱善。
entries.en: He often lamented that commentators on the classics missed the sages' deeper intent and would argue from his own understanding. The scholars all praised his insight.
entries.literal: He often sighed that commentators on the classics did not grasp the sages' deep intent and would argue by his own understanding; all the scholars praised his correctness.

entries.zh: 性慷慨，志立功名。
entries.en: He was generous by nature and aspired to establish merit and fame.
entries.literal: His nature was generous; his ambition was to establish merit and fame.

entries.zh: 周明帝時，襲爵文城郡公。
entries.en: Under Emperor Ming of Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Wencheng commandery.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou he inherited the rank of Duke of Wencheng Commandery.

entries.zh: 累遷上儀同，尋拜司金大夫，後加開府。
entries.en: He rose repeatedly to Shang Yitong, was soon appointed daifu of the Bureau of Metals, and later received the additional rank of kaifu.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Pillar of State and soon appointed Senior Clerk in the Bureau of Metals, later added as Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，擢拜魯州刺史，未之官，檢校廬州總管事。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was promoted to governor of Lu prefecture. Before taking that post he was assigned to inspect the affairs of the governor-general of Luzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted and appointed Governor of Lu Prefecture; before taking office he inspected and managed the affairs of the Governor-General of Luzhou.

entries.zh: 尋除兗州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed governor of Yan prefecture.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 及到官，系囚數百，胄剖斷旬日便了，囹圄空虛。
entries.en: When he took office there were several hundred prisoners in custody. Zhou judged and cleared them within ten days, and the prisons stood empty.
entries.literal: When he reached office there were several hundred bound prisoners; Zhou judged and decided them within ten days and the prisons were empty.

entries.zh: 有陳州人向道力者，偽作高平郡守，將之官，胄遇諸途，察其有異，將留詰之。
entries.en: A man of Chen prefecture named Xiang Daoli had falsely posed as governor of Gaoping commandery and was on his way to take office. Zhou met him on the road, sensed something amiss, and was about to detain and question him.
entries.literal: There was a man of Chen Prefecture named Xiang Daoli who falsely posed as Governor of Gaoping Commandery and was going to take office; Zhou met him on the road, observed something strange about him, and was about to detain and question him.

entries.zh: 司馬王君馥固諫，乃聽詣郡。
entries.en: Assistant governor Wang Junfu firmly remonstrated, and Zhou allowed him to proceed to the commandery.
entries.literal: Assistant Governor Wang Junfu firmly remonstrated, and he therefore allowed him to proceed to the commandery.

entries.zh: 既而悔之，即遣主簿追禁道力。
entries.en: He soon regretted the decision and at once sent the chief clerk to pursue and detain Daoli.
entries.literal: He soon regretted it and immediately sent the chief clerk to pursue and detain Daoli.

entries.zh: 有部人徐俱羅者，嘗任海陵郡守，先是已為道力偽代之。
entries.en: A local man named Xu Juluo had once served as governor of Hailing commandery and had already been falsely replaced by Daoli.
entries.literal: There was a local man Xu Juluo who had once served as Governor of Hailing Commandery and had already been falsely replaced by Daoli.

entries.zh: 比至秩滿，公私不悟。
entries.en: By the time his term ended, neither officials nor the public had noticed the fraud.
entries.literal: By the time his term ended, neither public nor private parties had perceived it.

entries.zh: 俱羅遂語君馥曰：「向道力以經代俱羅為郡，使君豈容疑之？」
entries.en: Juluo then said to Junfu, "Daoli has long replaced me as governor by fraud. How can you, sir, still harbor suspicion?"
entries.literal: Juluo then said to Junfu: "Daoli has long replaced Juluo as governor by fraud—how can the governor tolerate suspicion?"

entries.zh: 君馥以俱羅所陳，又固請胄。
entries.en: Junfu, relying on Juluo's account, again pressed Zhou firmly.
entries.literal: Junfu, based on what Juluo stated, again firmly requested Zhou.

entries.zh: 胄呵君馥曰：「吾已察知此人詐也。
entries.en: Zhou rebuked Junfu: "I have already seen that this man is a fraud.
entries.literal: Zhou rebuked Junfu, saying: "I have already observed that this man is a fraud.

entries.zh: 司馬容奸，當連其坐！」
entries.en: The assistant governor harbors deceit. He should share the punishment!"
entries.literal: The assistant governor harbors deceit—he should be implicated in the punishment!"

entries.zh: 君馥乃止。
entries.en: Junfu then desisted.
entries.literal: Junfu then stopped.

entries.zh: 遂往收之，道力懼而引偽。
entries.en: He then went to arrest Daoli, who in fear confessed to the fraud.
entries.literal: He then went to arrest him; Daoli, in fear, confessed to the fraud.

entries.zh: 其發奸摘伏，皆此類也，時人謂為神明。
entries.en: His uncovering of fraud and exposure of hidden wrongdoing were all of this kind. People of the day called him uncannily perceptive.
entries.literal: His uncovering of fraud and exposure of hidden wrongdoing were all of this kind; people of the time called him divine.

entries.zh: 先是，兗州城東沂、泗二水合而南流，氾濫大澤中，胄遂積石堰之，使決令西注，陂澤盡為良田。
entries.en: Previously east of Yan prefecture city the Yi and Si rivers joined and flowed south, flooding a great marsh. Zhou piled stones to dam them and diverted the water westward, turning the marshes and pools into fertile fields.
entries.literal: Previously east of Yan Prefecture city the Yi and Si rivers joined and flowed south, flooding the great marsh; Zhou piled stones to dam them and made them break westward, and the marshes and pools all became good fields.

entries.zh: 又通轉運，利盡淮海，百姓賴之，號為薛公豐兗渠。
entries.en: He also opened transport routes, bringing profit to the Huai and Hai regions. The people relied on it and called it Duke Xue's Abundant Yan Canal.
entries.literal: He also opened transport routes, with profit reaching the Huai and Hai; the people relied on it and called it the Xue Duke's Abundant Yan Canal.

entries.zh: 胄以天下太平，登封告禪，帝王盛烈，遂遣博士登太山，觀古跡，撰《封禪圖》及儀上之。
entries.en: With the realm at peace, Zhou regarded the feng and shan rites as the supreme glory of emperors. He sent a doctor to ascend Mount Tai, observe ancient traces, and compose a 《Diagram of the Feng and Shan》, then presented the rites.
entries.literal: Zhou, because the realm was at peace, considered the feng and shan rites the supreme glory of emperors, and therefore sent a doctor to ascend Mount Tai, observe ancient traces, and compose 《Diagram of the Feng and Shan》 and present the rites.

entries.zh: 高祖謙讓不許。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu declined out of modesty and would not allow it.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu modestly declined and did not permit it.

entries.zh: 後轉郢州刺史，前後俱有惠政。
entries.en: Later he was transferred to governor of E prefecture, where his benevolent governance continued as before.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to Governor of E Prefecture; before and after he had benevolent governance.

entries.zh: 征拜衛尉卿，尋轉大理卿，持法寬平，名為稱職。
entries.en: He was summoned as Chamberlain of the Palace Guards, soon transferred to Chamberlain for Law Enforcement. He applied the law with breadth and fairness and was regarded as competent in office.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Grand Master for Imperial Entertainments, soon transferred to Grand Master for Law, held the law with breadth and fairness, and was called competent in office.

entries.zh: 後遷刑部尚書。
entries.en: He was later transferred to minister of punishments.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 時左僕射高熲稍被疏忌，及王世積之誅也，熲事與相連，上因此欲成熲罪。
entries.en: At that time Left Vice Director Gao Jiong was gradually estranged and suspected. When Wang Shiji was executed, Jiong's affairs were implicated, and the emperor therefore wished to complete Jiong's guilt.
entries.literal: At that time Left Vice Director Gao Jiong was gradually estranged and suspected; when Wang Shiji was executed, Jiong's affairs were connected, and the Emperor therefore wished to complete Jiong's guilt.

entries.zh: 胄明雪之，正議其獄。
entries.en: Zhou plainly exonerated him and judged the case on its merits.
entries.literal: Zhou clearly cleared him and rightly judged his case.

entries.zh: 由是忤旨，械系之，久而得免。
entries.en: Thus he offended the throne, was shackled and imprisoned, and only after a long while was set free.
entries.literal: Thereby he offended the imperial will, was shackled and imprisoned, and after a long time was released.

entries.zh: 檢校相州事，甚有能名。
entries.en: He inspected and managed the affairs of Xiang prefecture and won a great reputation for competence.
entries.literal: He inspected and managed the affairs of Xiang Prefecture and had a great reputation for competence.

entries.zh: 會漢王諒作亂并州，遣偽將綦良東略地，攻逼慈州。
entries.en: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled at Bingzhou, he sent the false general Qi Liang to advance east and attack, pressing Cizhou.
entries.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled at Bingzhou, he sent the false general Qi Liang to advance east and attack, pressing Cizhou.

entries.zh: 刺史上官政請援於胄，胄畏諒兵鋒，不敢拒，良又引兵攻胄，胄欲以計卻之，遣親人魯世范說良曰：「天下事未可知，胄為人臣，去就須得其所，何遽相攻也？」
entries.en: Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou. Zhou feared Prince Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse. Qi Liang then led troops to attack Zhou. Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to tell Qi Liang, "Affairs under Heaven are not yet settled. Zhou, as a minister, must choose his stand according to what is fitting. Why rush to attack one another?"
entries.literal: Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou; Zhou feared Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse. Liang again led troops to attack Zhou; Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to say to Liang: "Affairs under Heaven are not yet knowable. Zhou as a minister must choose his stand according to what is fitting—why rush to attack each other?"

entries.zh: 良於是釋去，進圖黎陽。
entries.en: Liang thereupon withdrew and advanced to plan against Liyang.
entries.literal: Liang thereupon released him and advanced to plan against Liyang.

entries.zh: 及良為史祥所攻，棄軍歸胄。
entries.en: When Shi Xiang attacked Liang, Liang abandoned his army and fled back to Zhou.
entries.literal: When Liang was attacked by Shi Xiang, he abandoned his army and returned to Zhou.

entries.zh: 朝廷以胄懷貳心，鎖詣大理。
entries.en: The court considered that Zhou harbored divided loyalty and fettered him to the court of law.
entries.literal: The court considered that Zhou harbored divided loyalty and fettered him to the Court of Law.

entries.zh: 相州吏人素懷其恩，詣闕理胄者百餘人，胄竟坐除名，配防嶺南，道病卒。
entries.en: The officials and people of Xiang prefecture had long cherished his kindness; more than a hundred went to the palace to plead for him. Zhou was ultimately stripped of rank and assigned to guard Lingnan, dying of illness on the road.
entries.literal: The officials and people of Xiang Prefecture had long cherished his grace; over a hundred went to the palace to plead for Zhou. Zhou ultimately was punished by removal from rank and assigned to guard Lingnan, dying of illness on the road.

entries.zh: 有子、獻，並知名。
entries.en: He had sons named Zi and Xian, both of whom became well known.
entries.literal: He had sons named He and Xian, both renowned.

entries.zh: 宇文弼，字公輔，河南洛陽人也，其先與周同出。
entries.en: Yu Wenbi, courtesy name Gongfu, came from Luoyang in Henan. His ancestors shared a common origin with the house of Zhou.
entries.literal: Yu Wenbi, styled Gongfu, was a man of Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors came from the same source as Zhou.

entries.zh: 祖直力覲，魏巨鹿太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhiliguan had been governor of Julu under Wei.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhiliguan was Governor of Julu under Wei.

entries.zh: 父珍，周宕州刺史。
entries.en: His father Zhen had been governor of Dang prefecture under Zhou.
entries.literal: His father Zhen was Governor of Dang Prefecture under Zhou.

entries.zh: 弼慷慨有大節，博學多通，仕周為禮部上士。
entries.en: Bi was generous and possessed of great integrity, broadly learned and widely versed. He served Zhou as senior officer in the ministry of rites.
entries.literal: Bi was generous and had great integrity, broadly learned and widely versed; he served Zhou as Senior Officer in the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 嘗奉使鄧至國及黑水、龍涸諸羌，前後降附三十餘部。
entries.en: He once served as envoy to the state of Dengzhi and to the Qiang of Heishui and Longge. In all, more than thirty tribes submitted to him.
entries.literal: He once served as envoy to the state of Dengzhi and to the Qiang of Heishui and Longge; before and after, over thirty tribes submitted.

entries.zh: 及還，奉詔修定《五禮》，書成奏之，賜公田十二頃，粟百石。
entries.en: On his return he received an edict to revise and fix the 《Five Rites》. When the work was completed he presented it and was granted twelve qing of public fields and a hundred shi of grain.
entries.literal: On return he received an edict to revise and fix 《Five Rites》; when the book was completed he presented it and was granted twelve qing of public fields and a hundred shi of grain.

entries.zh: 累遷少吏部，擢八人為縣令，皆有異績，時以為知人。
entries.en: He rose to junior clerk of personnel and promoted eight men to county magistrate, all of whom achieved unusual success. The age considered him a knower of men.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Junior Clerk of Personnel, promoted eight men as county magistrates, all with unusual achievements; the age considered him a knower of men.

entries.zh: 轉內史都上士。
entries.en: He was transferred to senior officer of the imperial secretariat.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Senior Officer of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 武帝將出兵河陽以伐齊，謀及臣下，弼進策曰：「齊氏建國，於今累葉，雖曰無道，籓屏之寄，尚有其人。
entries.en: Emperor Wu was about to send troops to Heyang to attack Qi and consulted his ministers. Bi advanced a plan: "The Qi state has stood for many generations. Though it is said to be without the Way, it still has men to hold its frontiers.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu was about to send troops to Heyang to attack Qi and consulted his ministers; Bi advanced a plan, saying: "The Qi state has established its realm through many generations; though it is said to be without the Way, in the charge of the frontier screen it still has its men.

entries.zh: 今之用兵，須擇其地。
entries.en: In deploying troops now one must choose the ground carefully.
entries.literal: In using troops now one must choose the place.

entries.zh: 河陽衝要，精兵所聚，盡力攻圍，恐難得志。
entries.en: Heyang is strategically vital and where elite troops gather. If one exhausts strength in siege, I fear it will be hard to achieve one's aim.
entries.literal: Heyang is strategically vital and where elite troops gather; if one exhausts strength in siege, I fear it will be hard to achieve one's aim.

entries.zh: 如臣所見，彼汾之曲，戍小山平，攻之易拔。
entries.en: As I see it, at the bend of the Fen the garrison sits on a small hill on level ground. It can be taken with ease.
entries.literal: As I see it, at the bend of the Fen the garrison is on a small hill and level ground; attacking it is easy to capture.

entries.zh: 用武之地，莫過於此，願陛下詳之。」
entries.en: Among places for employing troops there is none better than this. I beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully."
entries.literal: Among places for employing troops there is none better than this; I wish Your Majesty to examine it carefully."

entries.zh: 帝不納，師竟無功。
entries.en: The emperor did not accept it, and the campaign ultimately failed.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not accept it, and the army ultimately had no success.

entries.zh: 建德五年，大舉伐齊，卒用弼計。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Jiande he launched a great campaign against Qi and ultimately adopted Bi's plan.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande he launched a great campaign against Qi and ultimately used Bi's plan.

entries.zh: 弼於是募三輔豪俠少年數百人以為別隊，從帝攻拔晉州。
entries.en: Bi thereupon recruited several hundred bold young men of the three adjuncts as a separate detachment and followed the emperor in capturing Jin prefecture.
entries.literal: Bi thereupon recruited several hundred bold young men of the Three Adjuncts as a separate detachment and followed the Emperor in capturing Jin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 身被三創，苦戰不息，帝奇而壯之。
entries.en: His body received three wounds, yet he fought on without ceasing. The emperor marveled and considered him strong.
entries.literal: His body received three wounds; he fought bitterly without ceasing; the Emperor marveled and considered him strong.

entries.zh: 後從帝平齊，以功拜上儀同，封武威縣公，邑千五百戶，賜物千五百段，奴婢百五十口，馬牛羊千餘頭，拜司州總管司錄。
entries.en: Later he followed the emperor in pacifying Qi. For his merit he was appointed Senior Yitong, enfeoffed as duke of Wuwei county with a fief of fifteen hundred households, granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods, a hundred fifty slaves and maidservants, and more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and was made registrar to the governor-general of Si prefecture.
entries.literal: Later he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi; for merit he was appointed Senior Yitong, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei County with a fief of 1,500 households, granted 1,500 bolts of goods, 150 slaves and maidservants, and over a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Si Prefecture.

entries.zh: 宣帝嗣位，遷左守廟大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was transferred to left guardian of the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was transferred to Left Guardian of the Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 時突厥寇甘州，帝令侯莫陳昶率兵擊之，弼為監軍。
entries.en: At that time the Turks raided Gan prefecture. The emperor ordered Hou Mo Chen Chang to lead troops against them, with Bi as supervising general.
entries.literal: At that time the Turks raided Gan Prefecture; the Emperor ordered Hou Mo Chen Chang to lead troops to attack them, with Bi as supervising general.

entries.zh: 謂昶曰：「黠虜之勢，來如激矢，去若絕弦，若欲追躡，良為難及。
entries.en: He told Chang, "The force of cunning barbarians comes like a rushing arrow and departs like a broken bowstring. To pursue and overtake them is truly hard.
entries.literal: He said to Chang: "The force of cunning barbarians comes like a rushing arrow and departs like a broken bowstring; if one wishes to pursue and overtake them, it is truly hard to reach them.

entries.zh: 且宜選精騎，直趨祁連之西。
entries.en: For the moment one should choose elite cavalry and strike directly west of Qilian.
entries.literal: For the moment one should select elite cavalry and strike straight west of Qilian.

entries.zh: 賊若收軍，必自蓼泉之北，此地險隘，兼複下濕，度其人馬，三日方度，緩轡追討，何慮不及？
entries.en: If the bandits withdraw, they will necessarily come from north of Liaoyuan. That place is narrow and dangerous and also low and wet. Estimating their men and horses, three days are needed to cross. With loose reins pursue and attack—why worry about not catching up?
entries.literal: If the bandits withdraw their army, they will necessarily come from north of Liaoyuan; that place is narrow and dangerous and also low and wet; estimating their men and horses, three days are needed to cross. With loose reins pursue and attack—why worry about not catching up?

entries.zh: 彼勞我逸，破之必矣。
entries.en: They will be weary while we are rested. Breaking them is certain.
entries.literal: They will be weary while we are rested; breaking them is certain.

entries.zh: 若邀此路，真上策也。」
entries.en: If one blocks this route, it is truly the superior strategy."
entries.literal: If one intercepts this route, it is truly the best plan."

entries.zh: 昶不能用之，西取合黎，大軍行遲，虜已出塞。
entries.en: Chang could not adopt it and went west to take Heli. The main army moved slowly and the barbarians had already left the frontier.
entries.literal: Chang could not use it and went west to take Heli; the great army moved slowly and the barbarians had already left the frontier.

entries.zh: 其年，弼又率兵從梁士彥攻拔壽陽，尋改封安樂縣公，增邑六百戶，賜物六百段，加以口馬。
entries.en: That year Bi again led troops with Liang Shiyan to capture Shouyang. Soon he was re-enfeoffed as duke of Anle county, with his fief increased by six hundred households and six hundred bolts of goods granted, with dependents and horses added.
entries.literal: That year Bi again led troops with Liang Shiyan to capture Shouyang; soon he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anle County, with his fief increased by 600 households and 600 bolts of goods granted, with mouths and horses added.

entries.zh: 除澮州刺史，俄轉南司州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed governor of Kuai prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Si prefecture.
entries.literal: He was appointed Governor of Kuai Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Si Prefecture.

entries.zh: 後司馬消難之奔陳也，弼追之不及。
entries.en: Later, when Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Bi gave chase but failed to overtake him.
entries.literal: Later when Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Bi pursued but could not overtake him.

entries.zh: 遇陳將樊毅，戰於漳口，自旦及午，三戰三捷，虜獲三千人。
entries.en: He encountered Chen general Fan Yi and fought at the mouth of the Zhang River from dawn till noon. Three battles brought three victories, with three thousand captives and booty.
entries.literal: He encountered Chen General Fan Yi and fought at the mouth of the Zhang River from dawn till noon; three battles, three victories; captives and booty numbered 3,000 men.

entries.zh: 除黃州刺史，尋轉南定州刺史。
