entries.en: He was appointed governor of Huang prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Ding prefecture.
entries.literal: He was appointed Governor of Huang Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Ding Prefecture.

entries.zh: 開皇初，以前功封平昌縣公，加邑一千二百戶，入為尚書右丞。
entries.en: At the beginning of Kaihuang, for previous merit he was enfeoffed as duke of Pingchang county with his fief increased by twelve hundred households and entered office as right vice director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, for previous merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingchang County with his fief increased by 1,200 households and entered office as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 時西羌內附，詔弼持節安集之，置鹽澤、蒲昌二郡而還。
entries.en: At that time the western Qiang submitted internally. An edict ordered Bi to hold credentials and pacify them. He established the two commanderies of Yanzhe and Puchang, then returned.
entries.literal: At that time the Western Qiang submitted internally; an edict ordered Bi to hold credentials and pacify them, establishing the two commanderies of Yanzhe and Puchang, then returning.

entries.zh: 遷尚書左丞，當官正色，為百僚所憚，三年，突厥寇甘州，以行軍司馬從元帥竇榮定擊破之。
entries.en: He was transferred to left vice director of the secretariat. In office he was stern-faced, and the hundred officials feared him. In the third year the Turks raided Gan prefecture. As campaign administering director he followed commander-in-chief Dou Rongding and broke them.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; in office he was stern-faced, and the hundred officials feared him. In the third year the Turks raided Gan Prefecture; as Campaign Administering Director he followed Commander-in-Chief Dou Rongding and broke them.

entries.zh: 還除太僕少卿，轉吏部侍郎。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed vice minister of the imperial stud and transferred to vice minister of personnel.
entries.literal: On return he was appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 平陳之役，楊素出信州道，令弼持節為諸軍節度，仍領行軍總管。
entries.en: In the campaign to pacify Chen, Yang Su went by the Xin prefecture route. He ordered Bi to hold credentials as coordinator of the armies and still lead as campaign commander.
entries.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, Yang Su went by the Xin Prefecture route; he ordered Bi to hold credentials as coordinator of the armies and still lead as Campaign Commander.

entries.zh: 劉仁恩之破陳將呂仲肅也，弼有謀焉。
entries.en: When Liu Ren'en defeated Chen general Lü Zhongsu, Bi had a share in the planning.
entries.literal: When Liu Ren'en defeated Chen General Lü Zhongsu, Bi had a share in the planning.

entries.zh: 加開府，擢拜刑部尚書，領太子虞候率。
entries.en: He received the additional rank of Kaifu, was promoted to minister of punishments, and led the crown prince's guard of honored attendants.
entries.literal: He was given the additional rank of Kaifu, promoted and appointed Minister of Punishments, and led the Crown Prince's Guard of Honored Attendants.

entries.zh: 上嘗親臨釋奠，弼與博士論議，詞致清遠，觀者屬目。
entries.en: The emperor once personally attended the libation sacrifice. Bi debated with the doctors, his words clear and far-reaching, and observers fixed their eyes on him.
entries.literal: The Emperor once personally attended the libation sacrifice; Bi debated with the doctors, his words clear and far-reaching, and observers fixed their eyes on him.

entries.zh: 上大悅，顧謂侍臣曰：「朕今睹周公之制禮，見宣尼之論孝，實慰朕心。」
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and, turning to his attendants, said, "Today I behold the Duke of Zhou's establishment of rites and see Confucius's discussion of filial piety. It truly comforts my heart."
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and, turning to his attendants, said: "Today I behold the Duke of Zhou's establishment of rites and see Confucius's discussion of filial piety—it truly comforts my heart."

entries.zh: 於是頒賜各有差。
entries.en: Rewards were then distributed to each according to rank.
entries.literal: Thereupon rewards were distributed to each according to rank.

entries.zh: 時朝廷以晉陽為重鎮，并州總管必屬親王，其長史、司馬亦一時高選。
entries.en: At that time the court considered Jinyang a heavy garrison. The governor-general of Bingzhou necessarily belonged to an imperial prince, and the chief administrator and administering director were also chosen from the finest men of the age.
entries.literal: At that time the court considered Jinyang a heavy garrison; the Governor-General of Bingzhou necessarily belonged to an imperial prince, and the Chief Administrator and Administering Director were also chosen from the finest men of the age.

entries.zh: 前長史王韶卒，以弼有文武幹用，出為并州長史。
entries.en: The former chief administrator Wang Shao died. Because Bi had civil and military capacity he was sent out as chief administrator of Bingzhou.
entries.literal: The former Chief Administrator Wang Shao died; because Bi had civil and military capacity he was sent out as Chief Administrator of Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 俄以父艱去職，尋詔起之。
entries.en: Soon he left office to mourn his father. An edict soon recalled him to service.
entries.literal: Soon he left office on account of mourning for his father; soon an edict recalled him.

entries.zh: 十八年，遼東之役，授元帥漢王府司馬，仍尋領行軍總管。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, he was appointed administering director to the prince of Han's headquarters and soon also led as campaign commander.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, he was appointed Administering Director to the Prince of Han's headquarters and soon also led as Campaign Commander.

entries.zh: 軍還之後，曆朔、代、吳三州總管，皆有能 名。
entries.en: After the army returned he successively served as governor-general of Shuo, Dai, and Wu prefectures, winning a name for competence at each post.
entries.literal: After the army returned he successively served as Governor-General of the three prefectures of Shuo, Dai, and Wu, all with reputations for competence.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，征拜刑部尚書，仍持節巡省河北。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was summoned as minister of punishments and still held credentials to inspect Hebei.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was summoned as Minister of Punishments and still held credentials to inspect Hebei.

entries.zh: 還除泉州刺史。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed governor of Quan prefecture.
entries.literal: On return he was appointed Governor of Quan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 歲餘，複拜刑部尚書，尋轉禮部尚書。
entries.en: A year or so later he was again appointed minister of punishments and soon transferred to minister of rites.
entries.literal: After a little over a year he was again appointed Minister of Punishments and soon transferred to Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 弼既以才能著稱，曆職顯要，聲望甚重，物議時談，多見推許，帝頗忌之。
entries.en: Bi's talent and capacity were renowned, and he held successive prominent posts. His reputation was very weighty, and public discussion often praised him. The emperor grew jealous.
entries.literal: Bi, because his talent and capacity were renowned, held successive prominent posts, and his reputation was very weighty; public discussion at the time often praised him, and the Emperor was rather jealous.

entries.zh: 時帝漸好聲色，尤勤遠略，弼謂高熲曰：「昔周天元好聲色而國亡，以今方之，不亦甚乎？」
entries.en: At that time the emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns. Bi said to Gao Jiong, "In the past the Tianyuan Emperor of Zhou favored music and women and the state perished. Compared with today, is it not even worse?"
entries.literal: At that time the Emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns; Bi said to Gao Jiong: "In the past the Tianyuan Emperor of Zhou favored music and women and the state perished—compared with today, is it not even more so?"

entries.zh: 又言：「長城之役，幸非急務。」
entries.en: He also said, "The Great Wall labor service is fortunately not an urgent task."
entries.literal: He also said: "The Great Wall labor service is fortunately not an urgent task."

entries.zh: 有人奏之，竟坐誅死，時年六十二，天下冤之。
entries.en: Someone reported this. He was ultimately executed at sixty-two, and all under Heaven considered it unjust.
entries.literal: Someone memorialized this; he ultimately was punished by execution and died, aged sixty-two; all under Heaven considered it unjust.

entries.zh: 所著辭賦二十餘萬言，為《尚書》、《孝經注》行于時。
entries.en: His writings in prose and fu numbered over two hundred thousand words. He produced 《Notes on the Documents》 and 《Notes on the Classic of Filial Piety》 that circulated in his time.
entries.literal: His writings in prose and fu numbered over 200,000 words; he made 《Notes on the Documents》 and 《Notes on the Classic of Filial Piety》 that circulated in his time.

entries.zh: 有子儉、瑗。
entries.en: His sons were Jian and Yuan.
entries.literal: He had sons named Jian and Yuan.

entries.zh: 張衡，字建平，河內人也。
entries.en: Zhang Heng, courtesy name Jianping, came from Henei.
entries.literal: Zhang Heng, styled Jianping, was a man of Henei.

entries.zh: 祖嶷，魏河陽太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Ni had been governor of Heyang under Wei.
entries.literal: His grandfather Ni was Governor of Heyang under Wei.

entries.zh: 父光，周萬州刺史。
entries.en: His father Guang had been governor of Wan prefecture under Zhou.
entries.literal: His father Guang was Governor of Wan Prefecture under Zhou.

entries.zh: 衡幼懷志尚，有骨鯁之風。
entries.en: From youth Heng cherished ambition and integrity and had an unyielding spirit.
entries.literal: From youth Heng cherished ambition and integrity and had the air of unyielding bone.

entries.zh: 年十五，詣太學受業，研精覃思，為同輩所推。
entries.en: At fifteen he went to the imperial academy to study, refining his learning with deep thought, and was esteemed by his peers.
entries.literal: At fifteen he went to the Imperial Academy to receive instruction, refining his study with deep thought, and was pushed forward by his peers.

entries.zh: 周武帝居太后憂，與左右出獵，衡露發輿櫬，扣馬切諫。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for the empress dowager and went hunting with those at his side. Heng bared his head and wore mourning cloth, seized the horse, and remonstrated urgently.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for the Empress Dowager and went hunting with those at his side; Heng bared his head and coffin-cloth, seized the horse, and remonstrated urgently.

entries.zh: 帝嘉焉，賜衣一襲，馬一匹，擢拜漢王侍讀。
entries.en: The emperor commended him, granted one suit of clothes and one horse, and promoted him as reader to the prince of Han.
entries.literal: The Emperor commended him, granted one suit of clothes and one horse, and promoted him as Reader to the Prince of Han.

entries.zh: 衡又就沈重受《三禮》，略究大旨。
entries.en: Heng also studied the 《Three Rites》 under Shen Chong and came to grasp their larger meaning.
entries.literal: Heng again studied 《Three Rites》 under Shen Chong and broadly grasped their great intent.

entries.zh: 累遷掌朝大夫。
entries.en: He rose to grand master for the court.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Grand Master for the Court.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，拜司門侍郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was appointed vice minister of the gate office.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Gate Office.

entries.zh: 及晉王廣為河北行台，衡曆刑部、度支二曹郎。
entries.en: When Prince Guang of Jin became Hebei executive, Heng served successively as senior clerk in the bureaus of punishments and revenue.
entries.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang became Hebei Executive, Heng served successively as Senior Clerk in the Bureaus of Punishments and Revenue.

entries.zh: 後以台廢，拜并州總管掾。
entries.en: When the executive was abolished, he was appointed aide to the governor-general of Bingzhou.
entries.literal: Later, when the executive was abolished, he was appointed Aide to the Governor-General of Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 及王轉牧揚州，衡複為掾，王甚親任之。
entries.en: When the prince transferred to govern Yangzhou, Heng again became his aide. The prince greatly trusted and relied on him.
entries.literal: When the Prince transferred to govern Yangzhou, Heng again became his aide; the Prince greatly trusted and relied on him.

entries.zh: 衡亦竭慮盡誠事之，奪宗之計，多衡所建也。
entries.en: Heng also exhausted his mind and gave full loyalty in serving him. The plan to seize the succession was largely Heng's creation.
entries.literal: Heng also exhausted his mind and gave full loyalty in serving him; the plan to seize the succession was largely Heng's creation.

entries.zh: 以母憂去職，歲餘，起授揚州總管司馬，賜物三百段。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his mother. A year or so later he was recalled and appointed administering director to the governor-general of Yangzhou, granted three hundred bolts of goods.
entries.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother; after a little over a year he was recalled and appointed Administering Director to the Governor-General of Yangzhou, granted 300 bolts of goods.

entries.zh: 開皇中，熙州李英林聚眾反，署置百官，以衡為行軍總管，率步騎五萬人討平之。
entries.en: In Kaihuang, Li Yinglin of Xizhou gathered a crowd and rebelled, appointing officials. Heng was made campaign commander and led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress and pacify them.
entries.literal: In Kaihuang, Li Yinglin of Xizhou gathered a crowd and rebelled, appointing officials; Heng was made Campaign Commander and led 50,000 infantry and cavalry to suppress and pacify them.

entries.zh: 拜開府，賜奴婢一百三十口，物五百段，金銀雜畜稱是。
entries.en: He was appointed kaifu, granted a hundred thirty slaves and maidservants, five hundred bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
entries.literal: He was appointed Kaifu, granted 130 slaves and maidservants, 500 bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.

entries.zh: 及王為皇太子，拜衡右庶子，仍領給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: When the prince became crown prince, Heng was appointed right assistant to the heir apparent and still served as supervising attendant of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: When the Prince became Crown Prince, Heng was appointed Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and still led as Supervising Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 煬帝嗣位，除給事黃門侍郎，進位銀青光祿大夫，俄遷御史大夫，甚見親重。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed supervising attendant of the yellow gate, advanced to silver-gleaming grand master of the palace, and soon transferred to censor-in-chief. He was greatly trusted and honored.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed Supervising Attendant of the Yellow Gate, advanced to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace, and soon transferred to Censor-in-Chief; he was greatly trusted and honored.

entries.zh: 大業三年，帝幸榆林郡，還至太原，謂衡曰：「朕欲過公宅，可為朕作主人。」
entries.en: In the third year of Daye the emperor visited Yulin commandery. On returning to Taiyuan he said to Heng, "I wish to pass your residence. You can act as host for me."
entries.literal: In the third year of Daye the Emperor visited Yulin Commandery; on returning to Taiyuan he said to Heng: "I wish to pass your residence—you can act as host for me."

entries.zh: 衡於是馳至河內，與宗族具牛酒。
entries.en: Heng thereupon raced to Henei, where he and his clan prepared oxen and wine.
entries.literal: Heng thereupon galloped to Henei and with his clan prepared oxen and wine.

entries.zh: 帝上太行，開直道九十裡，以抵其宅。
entries.en: The emperor ascended the Taihang Mountains and opened a straight road ninety li to reach his residence.
entries.literal: The Emperor ascended the Taihang Mountains and opened a straight road ninety li to reach his residence.

entries.zh: 帝悅其山泉，留宴三日，因謂衡曰：「往從先皇拜太山之始，途經洛陽，瞻望於此，深恨不得相過，不謂今日得諧宿願。」
entries.en: The emperor was pleased with its mountain springs and remained feasting three days. He then said to Heng, "When I followed the late emperor in beginning the sacrifice at Mount Tai and passed by Luoyang, I looked toward this place and deeply regretted that I could not visit. I did not expect today to fulfill my long-held wish."
entries.literal: The Emperor was pleased with its mountain springs and remained feasting three days; he therefore said to Heng: "When I followed the late Emperor in beginning the sacrifice at Mount Tai and passed by Luoyang, I looked toward this place and deeply regretted that I could not visit— I did not expect today to fulfill my long-held wish."

entries.zh: 衡俯伏辭謝，奉斛上壽。
entries.en: Heng prostrated himself in thanks and offered a hu of wine to wish the emperor long life.
entries.literal: Heng prostrated himself in apology and presented a hu of wine to wish long life.

entries.zh: 帝益歡，賜其宅傍田三十頃，良馬一匹，金帶，縑彩六百段，衣一襲，禦食器一具。
entries.en: The emperor was even more pleased and granted thirty qing of good fields beside his residence, one fine horse, a gold belt, six hundred bolts of silk, one suit of clothes, and one set of imperial dining vessels.
entries.literal: The Emperor was even more pleased and granted thirty qing of good fields beside his residence, one fine horse, a gold belt, 600 bolts of silk, one suit of clothes, and one set of imperial dining vessels.

entries.zh: 衡固讓，帝曰：「天子所至稱幸者，蓋為此也，不足為辭。」
entries.en: Heng firmly declined. The emperor said, "Where the Son of Heaven arrives and calls it an imperial visit, it is for this. There is no need to decline."
entries.literal: Heng firmly declined; the Emperor said: "Where the Son of Heaven arrives and calls it an imperial visit, it is for this; it is not enough to decline."

entries.zh: 衡複獻食於帝，帝令頒賜公卿，下至衛士，無不沾洽。
entries.en: Heng again presented food to the emperor. The emperor ordered it distributed to the dukes and ministers down to the guards—none went without share.
entries.literal: Heng again presented food to the Emperor; the Emperor ordered it distributed to the dukes and ministers down to the guards—none went without share.

entries.zh: 衡以籓邸之舊，恩寵莫與為比，頗自驕貴。
entries.en: Because of his old ties in the princely residence, Heng enjoyed favor unmatched by any and became rather proud and self-important.
entries.literal: Heng, because of his old ties in the princely residence, enjoyed favor unmatched by any; he became rather proud and self-important.

entries.zh: 明年，帝幸汾陽宮，宴從官，特賜絹五百匹。
entries.en: The next year the emperor visited Fenyang Palace and feasted the accompanying officials, specially granting five hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: The next year the Emperor visited Fenyang Palace and feasted the accompanying officials, specially granting 500 bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 時帝欲大汾陽宮，令衡與紀弘整具圖奏之。
entries.en: At that time the emperor wished to enlarge Fenyang Palace and ordered Heng and Ji Hongzheng to prepare diagrams and present them.
entries.literal: At that time the Emperor wished to enlarge Fenyang Palace and ordered Heng and Ji Hongzheng to prepare diagrams and present them.

entries.zh: 衡承間進諫曰：「比年勞役繁多，百姓疲敝，伏願留神，稍加折損。」
entries.en: Heng seized an opportunity to remonstrate: "In recent years corvée labor has been numerous and the people weary and exhausted. I humbly beg Your Majesty to keep this in mind and slightly reduce the burden."
entries.literal: Heng seized an opportunity to advance in remonstrance, saying: "In recent years corvée labor has been numerous and the people weary and exhausted; I humbly wish Your Majesty to keep this in mind and slightly reduce and cut back."

entries.zh: 帝意甚不平。
entries.en: The emperor was deeply displeased.
entries.literal: The Emperor's mind was very displeased.

entries.zh: 後嘗目衡謂侍臣曰：「張衡自謂由其計畫，令我有天下也。」
entries.en: Later he once looked at Heng and said to his attendants, "Zhang Heng considers that through his planning he gave me the realm under Heaven."
entries.literal: Later he once looked at Heng and said to his attendants: "Zhang Heng considers that through his planning he gave me the realm under Heaven."

entries.zh: 時齊王暕失愛於上，帝密令人求暕罪失。
entries.en: At that time Prince Yan of Qi had lost the emperor's favor. The emperor secretly ordered men to seek Yan's faults.
entries.literal: At that time Prince of Qi Yan had lost the Emperor's favor; the Emperor secretly ordered men to seek Yan's faults.

entries.zh: 有人譖暕違制，將伊闕令皇甫詡從之汾陽宮。
entries.en: Someone slandered Yan for violating regulations, having Yique magistrate Huangfu Xu follow him to Fenyang Palace.
entries.literal: Someone slandered Yan for violating regulations, having Yique Magistrate Huangfu Xu follow him to Fenyang Palace.

entries.zh: 又錄前幸涿郡及祠恆岳時，父老謁見者衣冠多不整。
entries.en: He also recorded that when the emperor previously visited Zhuo commandery and sacrificed at Mount Heng, many of the elders who came to audience were not properly dressed.
entries.literal: He also recorded that when the Emperor previously visited Zhuo Commandery and sacrificed at Mount Heng, many of the elders who came to audience were not properly dressed.

entries.zh: 帝譴衡以憲司皆不能舉正，出為榆林太守。
entries.en: The emperor blamed Heng because the censorate could not investigate and correct this, and sent him out as governor of Yulin.
entries.literal: The Emperor blamed Heng because the censorate all could not investigate and correct this, and sent him out as Governor of Yulin.

entries.zh: 明年，帝複幸汾陽宮，衡督役築樓煩城，因而謁帝。
entries.en: The next year the emperor again visited Fenyang Palace. Heng supervised labor building Loufan city and thereby had audience with the emperor.
entries.literal: The next year the Emperor again visited Fenyang Palace; Heng supervised labor building Loufan city and thereby had audience with the Emperor.

entries.zh: 帝惡衡不損瘦，以為不念咎，因謂衡曰：「公甚肥澤，宜且還郡。」
entries.en: The emperor disliked that Heng had not grown thin and considered that he did not reflect on his fault. He therefore said to Heng, "You are very plump and sleek. You should for the moment return to your commandery."
entries.literal: The Emperor disliked that Heng had not grown thin and considered that he did not reflect on his fault; he therefore said to Heng: "You are very plump and sleek—you should for the moment return to your commandery."

entries.zh: 衡複之榆林。
entries.en: Heng was sent back to Yulin.
entries.literal: Heng again returned to Yulin.

entries.zh: 俄而敕衡督役江都宮。
entries.en: Before long an edict ordered Heng to oversee construction of the Jiangdu Palace.
entries.literal: Soon an edict ordered Heng to supervise labor on the Jiangdu Palace.

entries.zh: 有人詣衡訟宮監者，衡不為理，還以訟書付監，其人大為監所困。
entries.en: Someone went to Heng to sue the palace supervisor. Heng did not judge the case and instead returned the petition to the supervisor. That man was greatly harassed by the supervisor.
entries.literal: Someone went to Heng to sue the palace supervisor; Heng did not judge it and instead returned the petition to the supervisor; that man was greatly harassed by the supervisor.

entries.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感使至江都，其人詣玄感稱冤。
entries.en: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan arrived on a mission at Jiangdu. That man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan arrived on a mission at Jiangdu; that man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.

entries.zh: 玄感固以衡為不可。
entries.en: Xuangan was convinced that Heng was unfit for office.
entries.literal: Xuangan firmly considered Heng unacceptable.

entries.zh: 及與衡相見，未有所言，又先謂玄感曰：「薛道衡真為枉死。」
entries.en: When he met Heng, before anything was said Heng first told Xuangan, "Xue Daoheng was truly wrongly killed."
entries.literal: When he met Heng and before anything was said, Heng first said to Xuangan: "Xue Daoheng was truly wrongly killed."

entries.zh: 玄感具上其事，江都丞王世充又奏衡頻減頓具。
entries.en: Xuangan fully reported the matter. Jiangdu assistant governor Wang Shichong also memorialized that Heng repeatedly reduced provisions.
entries.literal: Xuangan fully reported the matter; Jiangdu Assistant Governor Wang Shichong also memorialized that Heng repeatedly reduced provisions.

entries.zh: 帝於是發怒，鎖衡詣江都市，將斬之，久而乃釋，除名為民，放還田裡。
entries.en: The emperor thereupon flew into rage, fettered Heng in Jiangdu city, and was about to execute him. After a long time he released him, stripped him of rank, made him a commoner, and sent him back to his fields.
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon flew into rage, fettered Heng to Jiangdu city, and was about to execute him; after a long time he released him, stripped him of rank and made him a commoner, and sent him back to his fields.

entries.zh: 帝每令親人覘衡所為。
entries.en: The emperor often ordered close associates to observe what Heng did.
entries.literal: The Emperor often ordered close associates to observe what Heng did.

entries.zh: 八年，帝 自遼東還都，衡妾言衡怨望，謗訕朝政，竟賜盡於家。
entries.en: In the eighth year the emperor returned from Liaodong to the capital. Heng's concubine reported that he harbored resentment and slandered court policy. He was ultimately granted death at home.
entries.literal: In the eighth year the Emperor returned from Liaodong to the capital; Heng's concubine said Heng harbored resentment and slandered court policy; he was ultimately granted death at home.

entries.zh: 臨死大言曰：「我為人作何物事，而望久活！」
entries.en: Facing death he cried out, "What sort of things have I done for others, yet hoped to live long!"
entries.literal: Facing death he spoke loudly: "What sort of things have I done for others, yet hoped to live long!"

entries.zh: 監刑者塞耳，促令殺之。
entries.en: The execution supervisor covered his ears and urged them to carry out the sentence at once.
entries.literal: The execution supervisor stopped his ears and hurried the killing.

entries.zh: 義寧中，以死非其罪，贈大將軍、南陽郡公，諡曰忠。
entries.en: In Yining, because his death was not for his crime, he was posthumously granted grand general and duke of Nanyang commandery, with posthumous title Loyal.
entries.literal: In Yining, because his death was not for his crime, he was posthumously granted Grand General and Duke of Nanyang Commandery, with posthumous title Loyal.

entries.zh: 有子希玄。
entries.en: His son was Xixuan.
entries.literal: He had a son named Xixuan.

entries.zh: 楊汪，字元度，本弘農華陰人也，曾祖順，徙居河東。
entries.en: Yang Wang, courtesy name Yuandu, was originally from Huayin in Hongnong. His great-grandfather Shun moved to settle in Hedong.
entries.literal: Yang Wang, styled Yuandu, was originally of Huayin in Hongnong; his great-grandfather Shun moved to settle in Hedong.

entries.zh: 父琛，儀同三司，及汪貴，追贈平鄉縣公。
entries.en: His father Chen held the rank Equal to the Three Excellencies. When Wang became honored, Chen was posthumously granted duke of Pingxiang county.
entries.literal: His father Chen was Equal to the Three Excellencies; when Wang became honored, he was posthumously granted Duke of Pingxiang County.

entries.zh: 汪少凶疏，好與人群鬥，拳所毆擊，無不顛踣。
entries.en: Wang from youth was fierce and unrestrained, fond of brawling in crowds. Those struck by his fists all toppled over.
entries.literal: Wang from youth was fierce and unrestrained, fond of fighting in crowds; those struck by his fists all toppled over.

entries.zh: 長更折節勤學，專精《左氏傳》，通《三禮》。
entries.en: When grown he reformed himself, studied diligently, specialized in the 《Zuo Tradition》, and mastered the 《Three Rites》.
entries.literal: When grown he reformed himself, studied diligently, and specialized in 《Zuo Tradition》 and mastered 《Three Rites》.

entries.zh: 解褐周冀王侍讀，王甚重之，每曰：「楊侍讀德業優深，孤之穆生也。」
entries.en: He began his career as reader to Prince of Ji of Zhou. The prince greatly valued him and often said, "Reader Yang's virtue and learning are deep and excellent—he is my Mu Sheng."
entries.literal: He began his career as Reader to Prince of Ji of Zhou; the Prince greatly valued him and often said: "Reader Yang's virtue and learning are deep and excellent—he is my Mu Sheng."

entries.zh: 其後問《禮》于沈重，受《漢書》于劉臻，二人推許之曰：「吾弗如也。」
entries.en: Later he studied the 《Rites》 under Shen Chong and received the 《Book of Han》 under Liu Zhen. The two men praised him, saying, "We are not his equal."
entries.literal: Later he studied 《Rites》 under Shen Chong and received 《Book of Han》 under Liu Zhen; the two men praised him, saying: "We are not his equal."

entries.zh: 由是知名，累遷夏官府都上士。
entries.en: Thereby he became renowned and rose to senior officer of the summer office.
entries.literal: Thereby he became renowned and was repeatedly transferred to Senior Officer of the Summer Office.

entries.zh: 及高祖居相，引知兵事，遷掌朝下大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu was Counsellor-in-chief, he was summoned to advise on military affairs and transferred to grand master for the court below.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu occupied the chancellorship, he was summoned to know military affairs and transferred to Grand Master for the Court Below.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，賜爵平鄉縣伯，邑二百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was granted the rank earl of Pingxiang county with a fief of two hundred households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was granted the rank Earl of Pingxiang County with a fief of 200 households.

entries.zh: 曆尚書司勳兵部二曹侍郎、秦州總管長史，名為明幹。
entries.en: He successively served as vice minister in the bureaus of merits and military affairs and as chief administrator to the governor-general of Qin prefecture, and was called clear and competent.
entries.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister in the Bureaus of Merits and Military Affairs and as Chief Administrator to the Governor-General of Qin Prefecture, and was called clear and capable.

entries.zh: 遷尚書左丞，坐事免。
entries.en: He was transferred to left vice director of the secretariat and was dismissed on account of an affair.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and was dismissed on account of an affair.

entries.zh: 後曆荊、洛二州長史，每聽政之暇，必延生徒講授，時人稱之。
entries.en: Later he successively served as chief administrator of Jing and Luo prefectures. Whenever he had leisure from hearing cases, he always invited students to lecture and teach, and people of the day praised him.
entries.literal: Later he successively served as Chief Administrator of the two prefectures of Jing and Luo; whenever he had leisure from hearing cases, he always invited students to lecture and teach, and people of the time praised him.

entries.zh: 數年，高祖謂諫議大夫王達曰：「卿為我覓一好左丞。」
entries.en: After several years Emperor Gaozu said to remonstrance officer Wang Da, "Find me a good left vice director."
entries.literal: After several years Emperor Gaozu said to Remonstrance Officer Wang Da: "Find me a good Left Vice Director."

entries.zh: 達遂私于汪曰：「我當薦君為左丞，若事果，當以良田相報也。」
entries.en: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as left vice director. If the matter succeeds, you should repay me with good fields."
entries.literal: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as Left Vice Director; if the matter succeeds, you should repay me with good fields."

entries.zh: 汪以達所言奏之，達竟以獲罪，卒拜汪為尚書左丞。
entries.en: Wang memorialized what Da said. Da was ultimately punished for his crime, and Wang was finally appointed left vice director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Wang memorialized what Da said; Da ultimately was punished by crime and Wang was finally appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 汪明習法令，果於剖斷，當時號為稱職。
entries.en: Wang was clearly versed in laws and statutes and decisive in judgment. At the time he was regarded as competent in office.
entries.literal: Wang was clearly versed in laws and statutes and decisive in judgment; at the time he was called competent in office.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，守大理卿。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he served as acting grand master for law.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he served as Acting Grand Master for Law.

entries.zh: 汪視事二日，帝將親省囚徒。
entries.en: Wang had been in office two days when the emperor was about to personally inspect the prisoners.
entries.literal: Wang had been in office two days when the Emperor was about to personally inspect the prisoners.

entries.zh: 其時系囚二百餘人，汪通宵究審，詰朝而奏，曲盡事情，一無遺誤，帝甚嘉之。
entries.en: At that time over two hundred prisoners were in custody. Wang examined them all night and by morning presented his report, fully covering the circumstances without a single omission or error. The emperor greatly commended him.
entries.literal: At that time bound prisoners numbered over 200; Wang examined them all night and by morning presented his report, fully covering the circumstances without a single omission or error; the Emperor greatly commended him.

entries.zh: 歲餘，拜國子祭酒。
entries.en: A year or so later he was appointed rector of the imperial university.
entries.literal: After a little over a year he was appointed Rector of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 帝令百僚就學，與汪講論，天下通儒碩學多萃焉，論難鋒起，皆不能屈。
entries.en: The emperor ordered the hundred officials to come study and debate with Wang. Eminent scholars throughout the realm gathered. Debate flared sharp, and none could bend him.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered the hundred officials to come study and debate with Wang; eminent scholars throughout the realm gathered; debate flared sharp and none could bend him.

entries.zh: 帝令御史書其問答奏之，省而大悅，賜良馬一匹。
entries.en: The emperor ordered the censorate to write down their questions and answers and present them. He read them and was greatly pleased, granting one fine horse.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered the censorate to write down their questions and answers and present them; he read and was greatly pleased and granted one fine horse.

entries.zh: 大業中，為銀青光祿大夫。
entries.en: In Daye he served as silver-gleaming grand master of the palace.
entries.literal: In Daye he served as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 及楊玄感反河南，贊治裴弘策出師禦之，戰不利，弘策出還，遇汪而屏人交語。
entries.en: When Yang Xuangan rebelled in Henan, assistant director Pei Hongce went out with troops to resist him. The battle went badly and Hongce returned. He met Wang and dismissed others to speak with him in private.
entries.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled in Henan, Assistant Director Pei Hongce went out with troops to resist him; the battle went badly and Hongce returned; he met Wang and dismissed others to speak with him in private.

entries.zh: 既而留守樊子蓋斬弘策，以狀奏汪，帝疑之，出為梁郡通守。
entries.en: Soon garrison commander Fan Zigai executed Hongce and memorialized Wang's situation. The emperor suspected him and sent him out as administrator of Liang commandery.
entries.literal: Soon Garrison Commander Fan Zigai executed Hongce and memorialized Wang's situation; the Emperor suspected him and sent him out as Administrator of Liang Commandery.

entries.zh: 後李密已逼東都，其徒頻寇梁郡，汪勒兵拒之，頻挫其銳。
entries.en: Later Li Mi had already pressed the eastern capital. His followers repeatedly raided Liang commandery. Wang led troops to resist them and repeatedly blunted their edge.
entries.literal: Later Li Mi had already pressed the Eastern Capital; his followers repeatedly raided Liang Commandery; Wang led troops to resist them and repeatedly blunted their edge.

entries.zh: 煬帝崩，王世充推越王侗為主，征拜吏部尚書，頗見親委。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed Prince Tong of Yue as ruler and summoned Wang as minister of personnel. He was greatly trusted and relied upon.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed Prince of Yue Tong as ruler and summoned Wang as Minister of Personnel; he was greatly trusted and relied upon.

entries.zh: 及世充僭號，汪複用事，世充平，以凶黨誅死。
entries.en: When Shichong usurped the throne, Wang again held power. When Shichong was pacified, Wang was executed as a villainous partisan.
entries.literal: When Shichong usurped the throne, Wang again held power; when Shichong was pacified, he was executed as a villainous partisan.

entries.zh: 隋書卷五十六列傳第二十一
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume 56, Biography 21
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 56, Biography 21

entries.zh: 煬帝三男：蕭皇后生元德太子昭、齊王暕，蕭嬪生趙王杲。
entries.en: Emperor Yang had three sons: Empress Xiao bore the Yuande Heir Apparent Zhao and Prince Zheng of Qi; Consort Xiao bore Prince Gao of Zhao.
entries.literal: Emperor Yang had three sons: Empress Xiao bore the Yuande Heir Apparent Zhao and Prince of Qi Zheng; Consort Xiao bore Prince of Zhao Gao.

entries.zh: 元德太子昭，煬帝長子也，生而高祖命養宮中。
entries.en: Yang Zhao, posthumously honored as the Yuande Heir Apparent, was Emperor Yang's eldest son. From birth Emperor Wen ordered that he be raised in the palace.
entries.literal: The Yuande Heir Apparent Zhao—the Yuande Heir Apparent—was Emperor Yang's eldest son; from birth the High Ancestor ordered that he be reared in the palace.

entries.zh: 三歲時，於玄武門弄石師子，高祖與文獻後至其所。
entries.en: At the age of three he was playing with a stone lion at the Xuanwu Gate when Emperor Wen and Empress Wenxian came to where he was.
entries.literal: When he was three, he was playing with a stone lion at the Xuanwu Gate; the High Ancestor and Empress Wenxian came to where he was.

entries.zh: 高祖適患腰痛，舉手憑後，昭因避去，如此者再三。
entries.en: Emperor Wen happened to be troubled by back pain and raised his hand to lean on the empress; each time Zhao drew aside out of propriety, and this happened three times.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor happened to be suffering from back pain and raised his hand to lean on the empress; Zhao thereupon withdrew—this happened three times.

entries.zh: 高祖歎曰：「天生長者，誰複教乎！」
entries.en: Emperor Wen sighed and said, "He is born a man of thorough propriety—who could teach him such conduct!"
entries.literal: The High Ancestor sighed and said: "Born a man of thorough propriety—who else could teach him!"

entries.zh: 由是大奇之。
entries.en: From this he came to regard the boy with wonder.
entries.literal: Because of this he greatly marveled at him.

entries.zh: 高祖嘗謂曰：「當為爾娶婦。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen once told him, "When the time comes I shall find you a wife."
entries.literal: The High Ancestor once said to him: "When the time comes I shall find you a wife."

entries.zh: 昭應聲而泣。
entries.en: Zhao burst into tears at once.
entries.literal: Zhao answered with a cry.

entries.zh: 高祖問其故，對曰：「漢王未婚時，恆在至尊所，一朝娶婦，便則出外。
entries.en: Emperor Wen asked why; he answered, "When the Prince of Han was still unmarried he was always at Your Majesty's side; the day he married he went out to his own residence at once.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor asked the reason; he replied: "When the Prince of Han was still unmarried, he was always at Your Majesty's side; once he took a wife, he went outside at once.

entries.zh: 懼將違離，是以啼耳。」
entries.en: I am afraid I shall be separated from you—that is why I weep."
entries.literal: I fear I shall be parted from you, and that is why I weep."

entries.zh: 上歎其有至性，特鍾愛焉。
entries.en: The emperor marveled at his deep filial nature and favored him with special affection.
entries.literal: The sovereign sighed at his utmost sincerity and lavished special affection on him.

entries.zh: 有子三人，韋妃生恭皇帝，大劉良娣生燕王倓，小劉良娣生越王侗。
entries.en: He had three sons: Consort Wei bore the future Emperor Gong; the elder Worthy Companion Lady Liu bore Prince Tan of Yan; the younger Worthy Companion Lady Liu bore Prince Tong of Yue.
entries.literal: He had three sons: the Consort Wei bore Emperor Gong; the elder Lady Liu, Worthy Companion, bore Prince of Yan Tan; the younger Lady Liu, Worthy Companion, bore Prince of Yue Tong.

entries.zh: 燕王倓字仁安。
entries.en: Prince Tan of Yan, whose style name was Ren'an,
entries.literal: Prince of Yan Tan, styled Ren'an,

entries.zh: 敏慧美姿儀，煬帝于諸孫中特所鍾愛，常置左右。
entries.en: was clever and handsome in bearing. Among all his grandsons Emperor Yang favored him above the rest and kept him constantly at his side.
entries.literal: was clever and handsome in bearing; among all his grandsons Emperor Yang especially cherished him and kept him constantly at his side.

entries.zh: 性好讀書，尤重儒素，非造次所及，有若成人。
entries.en: By nature he loved books and especially honored Confucian simplicity; his attainments were not hurried or shallow—he seemed already a grown man.
entries.literal: By nature he loved reading and especially valued Confucian plainness; what he achieved was not the work of a moment—he was like a grown man.

entries.zh: 良娣早終，每至忌日，末嘗不流涕嗚咽。
entries.en: His mother, a Worthy Companion, had died young; on every anniversary of her death he wept and sobbed without fail.
entries.literal: His Worthy Companion mother died early; on every anniversary of her death he never failed to shed tears and sob.

entries.zh: 帝由是益以奇之。
entries.en: Because of this the emperor came to regard him with still greater wonder.
entries.literal: Because of this the emperor regarded him with still greater wonder.

entries.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，倓覺變，欲入奏，恐露其事，因與梁公蕭钜、千牛宇文皛等穿芳林門側水竇而入。
entries.en: When Yuwen Huaji carried out his regicide, Tan sensed the uprising. He wished to go in and report to the emperor but feared betraying his purpose, so with Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Palace Attendant Yuwen Hao, and others he entered through the water sluice beside the Fanglin Gate.
entries.literal: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide Tan perceived the uprising; he wished to enter and report but feared exposing the matter, and so with Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Palace Attendant Yuwen Hao, and others he passed through the water conduit beside the Fanglin Gate to enter.

entries.zh: 至玄武門，詭奏曰：「臣卒中惡，命縣俄頃，請得面辭，死無所恨。」
entries.en: At the Xuanwu Gate he sent in a false report: "I have been stricken with sudden illness and my life hangs by a moment. I beg to take leave of Your Majesty in person—then I shall die without regret."
entries.literal: At the Xuanwu Gate he made a false report, saying: "Your servant has been stricken with sudden illness; my life hangs by a moment. I beg to take leave of you in person—then I shall die without regret."

entries.zh: 冀以見帝，為司宮者所遏，竟不得聞。
entries.en: He hoped in this way to reach the emperor, but the palace attendants stopped him, and in the end his message never reached the throne.
entries.literal: He hoped thereby to see the emperor, but was blocked by the palace attendants and in the end could not be heard.

entries.zh: 俄而難作，為賊所害，時年十六。
entries.en: Before long the uprising erupted and he was killed by the rebels. He was sixteen.
entries.literal: Before long the catastrophe broke out and he was killed by the rebels; he was sixteen years old.

entries.zh: 越王侗字仁謹，美姿儀，性寬厚。
entries.en: Prince Tong of Yue, whose style name was Renjin, was handsome in bearing and generous by nature.
entries.literal: Prince of Yue Tong, styled Renjin, was handsome in bearing and generous by nature.

entries.zh: 大業二年，立為越王。
entries.en: In the second year of Daye, he was invested as Prince of Yue.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daye, he was invested as Prince of Yue.

entries.zh: 帝每巡幸，侗常留守東都。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor traveled on tour, Tong was regularly left behind to guard the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Tong regularly remained to hold the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 楊玄感作亂之際，與民部尚書樊子蓋拒之。
entries.en: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he joined Minister of the Household Fan Zigai in resisting him.
entries.literal: When Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion, he joined with Minister of the Household Fan Zigai to resist him.

entries.zh: 及玄感平，朝于高陽，拜高陽太守。
entries.en: After Xuangan was defeated, he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Administrator of Gaoyang.
entries.literal: When Xuangan was pacified, he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Administrator of Gaoyang.

entries.zh: 俄以本官複留守東都。
entries.en: Before long he resumed his former role and was again left to guard the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Before long, in his former capacity, he again remained to hold the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 十三年，帝幸江都，複令侗與金紫光祿大夫段達、太府卿元文都、攝民部尚書韋津、右武衛將軍皇甫無逸等總留台事。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again entrusted Tong, together with Duan Da, Yuan Wendu, Wei Jin acting as Minister of the Household, Huangfu Wuyi as General of the Right Martial Guards, and others, with overall charge of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again charged Tong, together with Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Duan Da, Grand Steward Yuan Wendu, Acting Minister of the Household Wei Jin, General of the Right Martial Guards Huangfu Wuyi, and others, to oversee all affairs of the capital left behind.

entries.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，文都等議，以侗元德太子之子，屬最為近，於是乃共尊立，大赦，改元曰皇泰。
entries.en: When Yuwen Huaji carried out his regicide, Wendu and the others reasoned that Tong, as a son of the Yuande Heir Apparent, was closest in the imperial line. They jointly enthroned him, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.
entries.literal: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Wendu and the others deliberated; because Tong was a son of the Yuande Heir Apparent and the closest in the imperial line, they thereupon jointly raised him to the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.

entries.zh: 諡帝曰明，廟號世祖。
entries.en: They gave the murdered emperor the posthumous title Ming and the temple name Shizu.
entries.literal: They gave the deceased emperor the posthumous title Ming and the temple name Shizu.

entries.zh: 追尊元德太子為孝成皇帝，廟號世宗。
entries.en: They posthumously honored the Yuande Heir Apparent as Emperor Xiaocheng with the temple name Shizong.
entries.literal: They posthumously honored the Yuande Heir Apparent as Emperor Xiaocheng with the temple name Shizong.

entries.zh: 尊其母劉良娣為皇太后。
entries.en: They honored his mother, Worthy Companion Lady Liu, as Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: They honored his mother, the Worthy Companion Lady Liu, as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 以段達為納言、右翊衛大將軍、攝禮部尚書，王世充亦納言、左翊衛大將軍、攝吏部尚書，元文都內史令、左驍衛大將軍，盧楚亦內史令，皇甫無逸兵部尚書、右武衛大將軍，郭文懿內史侍郎，趙長文黃門侍郎，委以機務，為金書鐵券，藏之宮掖。
entries.en: Duan Da was made Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guards, and acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong likewise Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guards, and acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Palace Secretariat and General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Cavalry; Lu Chu also Director of the Palace Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards; Guo Wenyi Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; Zhao Changwen Vice Director of the Yellow Gate. They were entrusted with state affairs, granted iron tallies inscribed in gold, and the tallies were kept in the inner palace.
entries.literal: Duan Da was made Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guards, and Acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong likewise Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guards, and Acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Palace Secretariat and General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Cavalry; Lu Chu also Director of the Palace Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards; Guo Wenyi Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; Zhao Changwen Vice Director of the Yellow Gate—they were entrusted with state affairs, granted golden-script iron tallies, and the tallies were stored in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 于時洛陽稱段達等為「七貴」。
entries.en: At that time Luoyang called Duan Da and his colleagues the "Seven Nobles."
entries.literal: At that time Luoyang called Duan Da and the others the "Seven Nobles."

entries.zh: :我大隋之有天下，於茲三十八載。
entries.en: Our Great Sui has held the realm for thirty-eight years now.
entries.literal: Our Great Sui has possessed the realm for thirty-eight years to this day.

entries.zh: 高祖文皇帝聖略神功，載造區夏。
entries.en: Emperor Wen, the High Ancestor, by sacred strategy and divine power recreated the central realm.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor, Emperor Wen, by sacred strategy and divine achievement recreated the central realm.

entries.zh: 世祖明皇帝則天法地，混一華戎。
entries.en: Emperor Ming, the Shizu, took heaven and earth as his model and united Chinese and foreign peoples under one rule.
entries.literal: The Shizu, Emperor Ming, modeled himself on heaven and earth and united Chinese and barbarian.

entries.zh: 東暨蟠木，西通細柳，前逾丹徼，後越幽都。
entries.en: East to Panmu, west to Xiliu; south beyond the southern marches, north past Youdu.
entries.literal: East to Panmu, west to Xiliu; south beyond the red frontier, north past Youdu.

entries.zh: 日月之所臨，風雨之所至，圓首方足，稟氣食芼，莫不盡入提封，皆為臣妾。
entries.en: Wherever sun and moon shine, wherever wind and rain reach—all who draw breath and live upon the earth—none failed to enter the imperial domain; all became subjects.
entries.literal: Wherever sun and moon shine, wherever wind and rain reach—all round-headed, square-footed beings who receive breath and eat vegetation—none failed to enter the measured bounds; all became subjects.

entries.zh: 加以寶貺畢集，靈瑞咸臻，作樂制禮，移風易俗。
entries.en: Moreover precious tributes poured in; auspicious omens appeared on every side; music was composed and rites established; customs were transformed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Moreover precious tributes gathered in full; numinous omens all arrived; music was composed and rites established; customs were transformed.

entries.zh: 智周寰海，萬物鹹受其賜，道濟天下，百姓用而不知。
entries.en: His wisdom encompassed the seas; the myriad things all received his bounty; his Way sustained the world, and the people benefited without even knowing it.
entries.literal: Wisdom encompassed the seas; the myriad things all received his bounty; the Way aided the world, and the common people benefited without knowing it.

entries.zh: 世祖往因曆試，統臨南服，自居皇極，順茲望幸。
entries.en: The Shizu had formerly, through successive appointments, governed the southern regions; once he took the throne, he continued with tours of inspection as the people desired.
entries.literal: The Shizu formerly, through successive trials, governed the southern domains; once he ascended the imperial pinnacle, he followed this with tours of inspection.

entries.zh: 所以往歲省方，展禮肆覲，停鑾駐蹕，按駕清道，八屯如昔，七萃不移。
entries.en: Therefore in years past he toured the provinces, displayed the rites and received homage; the imperial carriage halted and the procession paused; escorts cleared the road; the palace guards stood as before and did not stir.
entries.literal: Therefore in years past he inspected the regions, displayed rites and received homage; the imperial carriage halted and the procession paused; escorts cleared the road; the eight encampments stood as before and the seven guards did not stir.

entries.zh: 豈意釁起非常，逮於軒陛，災生不意，延及冕旒。
entries.en: Who could have thought that rebellion would arise beyond all expectation, reaching the imperial hall, and disaster strike unlooked-for, touching the imperial crown itself?
entries.literal: Who could have thought that calamity would arise beyond the ordinary, reaching the imperial hall, and disaster strike unlooked-for, extending to the imperial crown?

entries.zh: 奉諱之日，五情崩隕，攀號荼毒，不能自勝。
entries.en: On the day I received the mournful tidings, my heart gave way; I cried out in anguish and could not master my grief.
entries.literal: On the day I received the mournful tidings, my five emotions collapsed; I cried out in anguish and could not master myself.

entries.zh: 年十二，立為河南王。
entries.en: When he was twelve he was made King of Henan.
entries.literal: At the age of twelve he was invested as King of Henan.

entries.zh: 仁壽初，徙為晉王，拜內史令，兼左衛大將軍。
entries.en: At the opening of the Renshou era he was moved to Prince of Jin, named Director of the Palace Secretariat, and concurrently made General-in-Chief of the Left Guards.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was transferred to Prince of Jin, appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat, and concurrently General-in-Chief of the Left Guards.

entries.zh: 後三年，轉雍州牧。
entries.en: Three years after that he was appointed Governor of Yong Province.
entries.literal: Three years later he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，便幸洛陽宮，昭留守京師，
entries.en: When Emperor Yang acceded, he went at once to the Luoyang palace while Zhao stayed behind to guard the capital.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he went at once to the Luoyang palace; Zhao remained to hold the capital.

entries.zh: 大業元年，帝遣使者立為皇太子。
entries.en: In the first year of Daye, the emperor then sent envoys to invest him as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daye, the emperor sent envoys to invest him as crown prince.

entries.zh: 昭有武力，能引強弩。
entries.en: Zhao was physically strong and could draw powerful crossbows.
entries.literal: Zhao had physical strength and could draw powerful crossbows.

entries.zh: 性謙沖，言色恂恂，未嘗忿怒。
entries.en: By nature he was modest and self-effacing; in speech and countenance he was gentle and deferential, and he was never seen angry.
entries.literal: By nature he was humble and restrained; his speech and bearing were mild and respectful, and he was never angry.

entries.zh: 有深嫌可責者，但雲「大不是」。
entries.en: Even when someone had given grave cause for blame, he would only say, "That is quite wrong."
entries.literal: When someone had done something seriously blameworthy, he would only say, "That is very wrong."

entries.zh: 所膳不許多品，帷席極於儉素。
entries.en: His table was not served many dishes, and his curtains and mats were kept severely plain.
entries.literal: His meals were not allowed many courses; curtains and mats were extremely plain.

entries.zh: 臣吏有老父母者，必親問其安否，歲時皆有惠賜。
entries.en: When any of his officials had elderly parents, he would personally ask after their health, and at the turn of each year he always gave them gifts.
entries.literal: If among his subordinates there were those with aged parents, he would personally inquire after their well-being, and at year's end always bestowed favors.

entries.zh: 其仁愛如此。
entries.en: Such was the kindness he showed.
entries.literal: Such was his benevolence.

entries.zh: 明年，朝於洛陽。
entries.en: The following year he came to court at Luoyang.
entries.literal: The next year he attended court at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 後數月，將還京師，願得少留，帝不許，拜請無數。
entries.en: Some months later, when he was about to return to the capital, he asked to stay a little longer; the emperor refused, and he bowed and pleaded again and again without success.
entries.literal: Some months later, as he was about to return to the capital, he begged to remain a little longer; the emperor would not allow it, and though he bowed and pleaded countless times—

entries.zh: 體素肥，因致勞疾。
entries.en: His body was naturally heavy, and from this he fell ill with exhaustion.
entries.literal: His constitution was naturally stout, and thereby he fell ill from exhaustion.

entries.zh: 帝令巫者視之，雲：「房陵王為祟。」
entries.en: The emperor had a shaman look into the matter; the man said, "Prince Yong of Fangling is haunting him."
entries.literal: The emperor had a shaman examine him; the man said: "The Prince of Fangling is afflicting him."

entries.zh: 未幾而薨。
entries.en: Before long he died.
entries.literal: Before long he died.

entries.zh: 詔內史侍郎虞世基為哀冊文曰：:維大業二年七月癸丑朔二十三日，皇太子薨于行宮。
entries.en: An edict directed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Yu Shiji to compose the lamentation text for the funerary book. It read: In the second year of Daye, on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, on the first day of the guichou cycle, the crown prince died at the traveling palace.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Yu Shiji to compose a lamentation for the funerary book, which read: In the second year of Daye, on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, whose first day was guichou, the crown prince died at the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 時制縣令無故不得出境，有伊闕令皇甫詡幸於暕，違禁將之汾陽宮。
entries.en: At that time magistrates might not leave their districts without cause; Huangfu Xu, magistrate of Yique, who enjoyed Zheng's favor, violated the prohibition and accompanied him to Fenyang Palace.
entries.literal: At that time the rule was that magistrates might not leave their districts without cause; the magistrate of Yique, Huangfu Xu, who enjoyed Zheng's favor, violated the prohibition and took him to Fenyang Palace.

entries.zh: 又京兆人達奚通有妾王氏善歌，貴遊宴聚，多或要致，於是輾轉亦出入王家。
entries.en: Moreover Daxi Tong of Jingzhao had a concubine, Lady Wang, skilled in song; at banquets of the noble and powerful many would request her, and so by turns she also came and went at Zheng's residence.
entries.literal: Moreover Daxi Tong of Jingzhao had a concubine, Lady Wang, skilled in song; at banquets of the noble and powerful many would request her presence, and so by turns she also came and went at the prince's residence.

entries.zh: 禦史韋德裕希旨劾暕，帝令甲士千餘大索暕第，因窮治其事。
entries.en: Censor Wei Deyu, following the emperor's intent, impeached Zheng; the emperor ordered more than a thousand armored soldiers to search his residence thoroughly and pursued the matter to its full extent.
entries.literal: Censor Wei Deyu, following the emperor's intent, impeached Zheng; the emperor ordered more than a thousand armored soldiers to search Zheng's residence thoroughly and pursued the matter to its full extent.

entries.zh: 暕妃韋氏者，民部尚書沖之女也，早卒，暕遂與妃姊元氏婦通，遂產一女，外人皆不得知。
entries.en: Zheng's consort was Lady Wei, daughter of Minister of the Household Chong; she died young, and Zheng then had relations with his consort's elder sister, wife of the Yuan clan, who bore a daughter—outsiders knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: Zheng's consort was of the Wei clan, daughter of Minister of the Household Chong; she died early, and Zheng then had relations with his consort's elder sister, wife of the Yuan clan, and she bore a daughter—outsiders knew nothing of it.

entries.zh: 陰引喬令則於第內酣宴，令則稱慶，脫暕帽以為歡樂。
entries.en: He secretly brought Qiao Lingze into the residence for a drunken feast; Lingze offered congratulations and removed Zheng's cap in celebration.
entries.literal: He secretly brought Qiao Lingze into the residence for a drunken feast; Lingze offered congratulations and removed Zheng's cap for merriment.

entries.zh: 召相工令遍視後庭，相工指妃姊曰：「此產子者當為皇后。
entries.en: He summoned a physiognomist to inspect the entire rear court; the physiognomist pointed to the consort's sister and said, "She who has borne a child shall become empress.
entries.literal: He summoned a physiognomist to inspect the entire rear court; the physiognomist pointed to the consort's sister and said: "She who has borne a child shall become empress.

entries.zh: 王貴不可言。」
entries.en: The prince's honor is beyond words."
entries.literal: The prince's honor is beyond words."

entries.zh: 時國無儲副，暕自謂次當得立。
entries.en: At that time the state had no heir apparent; Zheng considered himself next in line for the succession.
entries.literal: At that time the state had no heir apparent; Zheng considered himself next in line to be established.

entries.zh: 又以元德太子有三子，內常不安，陰挾左道，為厭勝之事。
entries.en: Moreover, because the Yuande Heir Apparent had three sons, he was inwardly uneasy and secretly employed heterodox arts to perform rites of magical suppression.
entries.literal: Moreover, because the Yuande Heir Apparent had three sons, he was inwardly never at ease and secretly employed heterodox arts to perform rites of magical suppression.

entries.zh: 至是，事皆發，帝大怒，斬令則等數人，妃姊賜死，暕府僚皆斥之邊遠。
entries.en: At this point all the matters came to light; the emperor was greatly angered, executed Lingze and several others, ordered the consort's sister to take her own life, and banished all of Zheng's staff to the distant frontier.
entries.literal: At this point all the matters came to light; the emperor was greatly angered, executed Lingze and several others, ordered the consort's sister to take her own life, and banished all of Zheng's staff to the distant frontier.

entries.zh: 時趙王杲猶在孩孺，帝謂侍臣曰：「朕唯有暕一子，不然者，當肆諸市朝，以明國憲也。」
entries.en: At that time Prince Gao of Zhao was still an infant; the emperor said to his attendants, "I have only Zheng as a grown son; otherwise I would execute him in the marketplace and make clear the laws of the state."
entries.literal: At that time Prince of Zhao Gao was still an infant; the emperor said to his attendants: "I have only Zheng as a son; otherwise I would expose him in the marketplace and make clear the laws of the state."

entries.zh: 暕自是恩寵日衰，雖為京尹，不復關預時政。
entries.en: From this time Zheng's favor daily declined; though he was Intendant of the Capital, he no longer had any part in government affairs.
entries.literal: From this time Zheng's favor daily declined; though he was Intendant of the Capital, he no longer had any part in current government.

entries.zh: 帝恆令武賁郎將一人監其府事，暕有微失，武賁輒奏之。
entries.en: The emperor constantly assigned one Captain of the Martial Guard to oversee his residence; if Zheng had the slightest fault, the guard would report it at once.
entries.literal: The emperor constantly assigned one Captain of the Martial Guard to oversee his residence affairs; if Zheng had the slightest fault, the guard would report it at once.

entries.zh: 帝亦常慮暕生變，所給左右，皆以老弱，備員而已。
entries.en: The emperor also constantly feared Zheng might stir up trouble; those assigned to attend him were all old and weak, filling posts in name only.
entries.literal: The emperor also constantly feared Zheng might stir up trouble; those assigned to attend him were all old and weak, filling posts in name only.

entries.zh: 暕每懷危懼，心不自安。
entries.en: Zheng constantly lived in fear; his heart was never at peace.
entries.literal: Zheng constantly harbored fear and danger; his heart was never at peace.

entries.zh: 又帝在江都宮，元會，暕具法服將朝，無故有血從裳中而下。
entries.en: Moreover when the emperor was at the Jiangdu palace for the New Year audience, Zheng dressed in ceremonial robes to attend court, and for no reason blood flowed down from within his garments.
entries.literal: Moreover when the emperor was at the Jiangdu palace for the New Year audience, Zheng dressed in ceremonial robes to attend court, and for no reason blood flowed down from within his garments.

entries.zh: 又坐齋中，見群鼠數十，至前而死，視皆無頭。
entries.en: Again while seated in his study he saw several dozen rats come before him and die; when he looked, all were headless.
entries.literal: Again while seated in his study he saw several dozen rats come before him and die; when he looked, all were headless.

entries.zh: 暕意甚惡之。
entries.en: Zheng was deeply troubled by this.
entries.literal: Zheng was deeply troubled by this.

entries.zh: 俄而化及作亂，兵將犯蹕，帝聞，顧謂蕭後曰：「得非阿孩邪？」
entries.en: Before long Huaji rose in rebellion and troops were about to assault the imperial escort; when the emperor heard, he turned to Empress Xiao and said, "Could it not be Ahai?"
entries.literal: Before long Huaji rose in rebellion and troops were about to assault the imperial escort; when the emperor heard, he turned to Empress Xiao and said: "Could it not be Ahai?"

entries.zh: 其見疏忌如此。
entries.en: Such was the estrangement and suspicion with which he was regarded.
entries.literal: Such was the estrangement and suspicion with which he was regarded.

entries.zh: 化及複令人捕暕，暕時尚臥未起，賊既進，暕驚曰：「是何人？」
entries.en: Huaji again sent men to seize Zheng; Zheng was still lying abed; when the rebels entered, he cried in alarm, "Who are you?"
entries.literal: Huaji again sent men to seize Zheng; Zheng was still lying abed and had not risen; when the rebels entered, Zheng cried in alarm: "Who are you?"

entries.zh: 莫有報者，暕猶謂帝令捕之，因曰：「詔使且緩。
entries.en: No one answered; Zheng still thought the emperor had ordered his arrest, and said, "Imperial envoy, wait a moment.
entries.literal: No one answered; Zheng still thought the emperor had ordered his arrest, and therefore said: "Imperial envoy, wait a moment.

entries.zh: 兒不負國家。」
entries.en: Your son has not betrayed the state."
entries.literal: Your son has not betrayed the state."

entries.zh: 賊於是曳至街而斬之，及其二子亦遇害。
entries.en: The rebels then dragged him into the street and beheaded him; his two sons were also killed.
entries.literal: The rebels then dragged him to the street and beheaded him; his two sons also met with harm.

entries.zh: 暕竟不知殺者為誰。
entries.en: Zheng never knew who his killers were.
entries.literal: Zheng to the end did not know who his killers were.

entries.zh: 時年三十四。
entries.en: He was thirty-four years old.
entries.literal: He was thirty-four years old.

entries.zh: 粵三年五月庚辰朔六日，將遷座于莊陵，禮也。
entries.en: On the sixth day of the fifth month in the third year of his reign, on the gengchen cycle, the coffin is to be transferred to Zhuang Mausoleum, as ritual requires.
entries.literal: On the sixth day of the fifth month in the third year, whose first day was gengchen, the coffin will be moved to Zhuang Mausoleum—such is the rite.

entries.zh: 蜃綍宵載，鶴關曉辟，肅文物以具陳，儼賓從其如昔。
entries.en: The imperial hearse moves by night; at dawn the palace gate opens; ritual regalia is set out in full solemn array, and the retinue stands in ranks as before.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage is borne by night; at dawn the Crane Gate opens; ritual objects are solemnly arrayed in full; the entourage stands in ordered ranks as of old.

entries.zh: 皇帝悼離方之雲晦，嗟震宮之虧象，顧守器以長懷，臨登餕而興想。
entries.en: The emperor mourns the darkened clouds over the land of the departed, laments the broken image of the eastern palace, broods long over the heir who held the vessel of state, and, as the funeral offerings are raised, is stirred to grief.
entries.literal: The emperor grieves that the clouds over the departing quarter have darkened, laments the diminished image of the Thunder Palace, looks long upon the heir who guarded the vessel, and, facing the ascending offerings, is moved to thought.

entries.zh: 先遠戒日，占謀允從，庭彝徹祖，階所收重，抗銘旌以啟路，動徐輪于振容。
entries.en: The day appointed for the departed is kept; augury and counsel agree; ancestral vessels are set out in the hall; the bier is received upon the steps; inscribed banners are raised to clear the road, and the wheels of the mourning carriage turn slowly onward.
entries.literal: The day forewarned by the departed is observed; divination and counsel are followed; ancestral vessels are displayed in the hall; the steps receive the honored bier; inscribed banners are raised to open the way; the slow wheels move upon the mourning carriage.

entries.zh: 揆行度名，累德彰諡，爰詔史冊，式遵典志，俾浚哲之徽猷，播長久乎天地。
entries.en: His deeds are weighed to fix his name, his accumulated virtue to proclaim his posthumous title; the annals are charged, following canonical precedent, that his luminous wisdom and merit may resound through heaven and earth for ages to come.
entries.literal: We measure conduct to fix the name, accumulate virtue to display the posthumous title; thus we charge the historical records, following the canonical statutes, that his far-reaching wisdom and fine conduct may be broadcast long upon heaven and earth.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The text reads:
entries.literal: The text reads:

entries.zh: 帝深追悼。
entries.en: The emperor mourned him with deep grief.
entries.literal: The emperor mourned him deeply.

entries.zh: :且聞之，自古代有屯剝，賊臣逆子，無世無之。
entries.en: Moreover it is said that from antiquity there have been times of hardship; treacherous ministers and rebellious sons have existed in every age.
entries.literal: Moreover I have heard that from antiquity there have been times of hardship; treacherous ministers and rebellious sons exist in no age without them.

entries.zh: 至如宇文化及，世傳庸品。
entries.en: As for Yuwen Huaji, the world has long regarded him as a man of mediocre talent.
entries.literal: As for Yuwen Huaji, the world has handed down the report that he is a mediocre sort.

entries.zh: 其父述，往屬時來，早沾厚遇，賜以婚媾，置之公輔，位尊九命，祿重萬鐘，禮極人臣，榮冠世表。
entries.en: His father Shu, when fortune favored him, received generous treatment early on: he was granted a marriage alliance with the imperial house, placed among the chief ministers, honored with the highest rank, paid a stipend of ten thousand piculs, accorded the utmost rites due a subject, and his glory crowned his generation.
entries.literal: His father Shu, when the times favored him, early received generous treatment: granted marriage alliance, placed among chief ministers, rank honored with the nine orders, stipend heavy with ten thousand piculs, rites reaching the utmost for a subject, glory crowning his generation.

entries.zh: 徒承海嶽之恩，未有涓塵之益。
entries.en: They merely received favor vast as seas and mountains, yet rendered no benefit even the size of a drop of water or grain of dust.
entries.literal: They merely received favor vast as seas and mountains, yet rendered no benefit even the size of a drop or mote of dust.

entries.zh: 化及以此下材，夙蒙顧盼，出入外內，奉望階墀。
entries.en: Huaji, for all his inferior talent, long enjoyed the emperor's favor, passing in and out of the inner and outer courts and attending upon the palace steps.
entries.literal: Huaji, with this inferior talent, long enjoyed the imperial gaze, passing in and out of the inner and outer courts and attending upon the palace steps.

entries.zh: 昔陪籓國，統領禁衛，及從升皇祚，陪列九卿。
entries.en: Formerly he served in the princely household and commanded the palace guards; when the emperor took the throne, he took rank among the Nine Ministers.
entries.literal: Formerly he attended the princely domain and commanded the palace guards; when the emperor ascended the throne, he took rank among the Nine Ministers.

entries.zh: 但本性兇狠，恣其貪穢，或交結惡黨，或侵掠貨財，事重刑篇，狀盈獄簡。
entries.en: But by nature he was fierce and cruel, indulging his greed and corruption—now consorting with evil factions, now plundering goods and wealth—offenses grave under the penal code, charges filling the prison records.
entries.literal: But by nature he was fierce and cruel, indulging his greed and corruption—now consorting with evil factions, now plundering goods and wealth—matters grave under the penal code, charges filling the prison records.

entries.zh: 在上不遺簪履，恩加草芥，應至死辜，每蒙恕免。
entries.en: The sovereign did not cast him off even for the smallest offense; his grace extended even to the lowliest—though deserving death, he was pardoned again and again.
entries.literal: The sovereign did not cast away even hairpin and shoes; his grace extended even to grass and husks—though deserving death, he was each time pardoned.

entries.zh: 三經除解，尋複本職，再徙邊裔，仍即追還。
entries.en: Three times he was dismissed from office, yet soon restored to his former post; twice banished to the frontier, yet immediately recalled.
entries.literal: Three times he was dismissed from office, yet soon restored to his former post; twice banished to the frontier, yet immediately recalled.

entries.zh: 生成之恩，昊天罔極，獎擢之義，人事罕聞。
entries.en: The grace of giving him life was boundless as heaven; such promotion and favor is rarely heard of among men.
entries.literal: The grace of giving him life was boundless as heaven; the principle of promoting and elevating him is rarely heard of among men.

entries.zh: 化及梟獍為心，禽獸不若，縱毒興禍，傾覆行宮。
entries.en: Huaji had the heart of an owl or a jackal—worse than any beast; he unleashed poison and raised calamity, overthrowing the traveling palace.
entries.literal: Huaji had the heart of an owl or a jackal—worse than beasts; he unleashed poison and raised calamity, overthrowing the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 諸王兄弟，一時殘酷，痛暴行路，世不忍言。
entries.en: The imperial princes were slaughtered in a single moment with cruel violence; the anguish on the roads was such that the age cannot bear to speak of it.
entries.literal: The princely brothers were slaughtered in a single moment with cruel violence; the anguish on the roads was such that the age cannot bear to speak of it.

entries.zh: 有窮之在夏時，犬戎之于周代，釁辱之極，亦未是過。
entries.en: The outrage of Youqiong in the Xia age, the Dog Rong in the Zhou era—even the utmost of insult and shame did not surpass this.
entries.literal: The outrage of Youqiong in the Xia age, the Dog Rong in the Zhou era—even the utmost of insult and shame did not surpass this.

entries.zh: 朕所以刻骨崩心，飲膽嘗血，瞻天視地，無處容身。
entries.en: Therefore I have carved this into my bones and shattered my heart, drunk gall and tasted blood, looked up to heaven and down to earth, and found nowhere to hide my shame.
entries.literal: Therefore I have carved this into my bones and shattered my heart, drunk gall and tasted blood, looked up to heaven and down to earth, and found nowhere to hide my person.

entries.zh: 密見使者，大悅，北面拜伏，臣禮甚恭。
entries.en: When Li Mi saw the envoys he was overjoyed, faced north, bowed prostrate, and performed the ceremonies of a subject with great reverence.
entries.literal: When Li Mi saw the envoys he was greatly pleased, faced north, bowed prostrate, and performed the ceremonies of a subject with great reverence.

entries.zh: 密遂東拒化及。
entries.en: Li Mi thereupon marched east to resist Huaji.
entries.literal: Li Mi thereupon marched east to resist Huaji.

entries.zh: 「七貴」頗不協，陰有相圖之計。
entries.en: The "Seven Nobles" were rather at odds and secretly plotted against one another.
entries.literal: The "Seven Nobles" were rather at odds and secretly plotted against one another.

entries.zh: 未幾，元文都、盧楚、郭文懿、趙長文等為世充所殺，皇甫無逸遁歸長安。
entries.en: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Shichong; Huangfu Wuyi fled back to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Shichong; Huangfu Wuyi fled and returned to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 世充詣侗所陳謝，辭情哀苦。
entries.en: Shichong went to Tong's residence to apologize; his words were piteous and anguished.
entries.literal: Shichong went to Tong's residence to offer apology; his words were piteous and anguished.

entries.zh: 侗以為至誠，命之上殿，被發為盟，誓無貳志。
entries.en: Tong took this as utmost sincerity, summoned him to the hall, and with hair unbound they made a covenant, swearing he had no second intent.
entries.literal: Tong took this as utmost sincerity, ordered him up to the hall, and with loose hair they made a covenant, swearing he had no second intent.

entries.zh: 自是侗無所關預。
entries.en: From this time Tong had no part in affairs.
entries.literal: From this time Tong had no part in affairs.

entries.zh: 侗心不能平，遂與記室陸士季謀圖世充，事不果而止。
entries.en: Tong's heart could not be at peace; he then joined with his recorder Lu Shiji in plotting against Shichong, but the affair did not succeed and was abandoned.
entries.literal: Tong's heart could not be at peace; he then joined with Recorder Lu Shiji in plotting against Shichong, but the affair did not succeed and was abandoned.

entries.zh: 及世充破李密，眾望益歸之，遂自為鄭王，總百揆，加九錫，備法物，侗不能禁也。
entries.en: When Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular expectation turned increasingly to him; he thereupon made himself Prince of Zheng, took charge of all government, received the Nine Bestowals, and prepared the ritual regalia—and Tong could not stop him.
entries.literal: When Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular expectation turned increasingly to him; he thereupon made himself Prince of Zheng, took charge of all government, received the Nine Bestowals, and prepared the ritual regalia—and Tong could not stop him.

entries.zh: 段達、雲定興等十人入見於侗曰：「天命不常，鄭王功德甚盛，願陛下揖讓告禪，遵唐、虞之跡。」
entries.en: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others came before Tong and said, "The Mandate of Heaven is not constant; the Prince of Zheng's merit and virtue are very great. We beg Your Majesty to yield the throne and announce abdication, following the example of Tang and Yu."
entries.literal: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others entered to see Tong and said: "The Mandate of Heaven is not constant; the Prince of Zheng's merit and virtue are very great. We beg Your Majesty to yield by bowing and announce abdication, following the traces of Tang and Yu."

entries.zh: 侗聞之怒曰：「天下者，高祖之天下，東都者，世祖之東都。
entries.en: When Tong heard this he said in anger, "The realm belongs to Emperor Wen; the Eastern Capital belongs to Emperor Yang.
entries.literal: When Tong heard this he said in anger: "The realm belongs to the High Ancestor; the Eastern Capital belongs to the Shizu.

entries.zh: 若隋德未衰，此言不可發；
entries.en: If Sui virtue has not yet declined, such words must not be spoken;
entries.literal: If Sui virtue has not yet declined, such words must not be spoken;

entries.zh: 必天命有改，亦何論於禪讓！
entries.en: even if the Mandate has changed, what talk is there of abdication!
entries.literal: even if the Mandate has changed, what talk is there of abdication!

entries.zh: 公等或先朝舊臣，績宣上代，或勤王立節，身服軒冕，忽有斯言，朕複當何所望！」
entries.en: You gentlemen are either old ministers of the former court who served the previous reign with merit, or men who upheld the throne with loyal resolve and wear court robes—suddenly to speak such words, what may I still hope for!"
entries.literal: You gentlemen are either old ministers of the former court who displayed merit in the previous reign, or men who upheld the throne with loyal resolve and wear court robes—suddenly to have such words, what may I still hope for!"

entries.zh: 神色懍然，侍衛者莫不流汗。
entries.en: His expression was stern; every attendant broke into a sweat.
entries.literal: His expression was stern; none of the attendants but broke into a sweat.

entries.zh: 既而退朝，對良娣而泣。
entries.en: Afterward he left court and wept before his mother, the Worthy Companion.
entries.literal: Afterward he left court and wept before the Worthy Companion.

entries.zh: 世充更使人謂侗曰：「今海內未定，須得長君。
entries.en: Shichong again sent someone to say to Tong, "The realm is not yet settled; a mature ruler is needed.
entries.literal: Shichong again sent someone to say to Tong: "Now the realm within the seas is not settled; a mature ruler is needed.

entries.zh: 待四方乂安，複子明辟，必若前盟，義不違負。」
entries.en: When the four quarters are at peace, I shall restore you to the throne; as in our former covenant, in righteousness I shall not break faith."
entries.literal: When the four quarters are at peace, I shall restore you to the bright throne; as in our former covenant, in righteousness I shall not break faith."

entries.zh: 侗不得已，遜位於世充，遂被幽於含涼殿。
entries.en: Tong had no choice; he yielded the throne to Shichong and was then confined in the Hanliang Hall.
entries.literal: Tong had no choice; he yielded the throne to Shichong and was then confined in the Hanliang Hall.

entries.zh: 世充僭偽號，封為潞國公，邑五千戶。
entries.en: Shichong usurped the imperial title and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu with a fief of five thousand households.
entries.literal: Shichong usurped the imperial title and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu with a fief of five thousand households.

entries.zh: 月餘，宇文儒童、裴仁基等謀誅世充，複尊立侗，事泄，並見害。
entries.en: After more than a month Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Shichong and restore Tong to the throne; the affair was exposed and they were all killed.
entries.literal: After more than a month Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Shichong and restore Tong to the throne; the affair was exposed and they were all killed.

entries.zh: 世充兄世惲因勸世充害侗，以絕民望。
entries.en: Shichong's elder brother Shiyun thereupon urged Shichong to kill Tong in order to cut off popular hope in the Sui line.
entries.literal: Shichong's elder brother Shiyun thereupon urged Shichong to kill Tong in order to cut off popular expectation.

entries.zh: 世充遣其侄行本齎鴆詣侗所曰：「願皇帝飲此酒。」
entries.en: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben bearing poison to Tong's residence, saying, "I beg the emperor to drink this wine."
entries.literal: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben bearing poison to Tong's residence, saying: "I beg the emperor to drink this wine."

entries.zh: 侗知不免，請與母相見，不許。
entries.en: Tong knew he could not escape; he begged to see his mother and was refused.
entries.literal: Tong knew he could not escape; he begged to see his mother and was not permitted.

entries.zh: 遂布席焚香禮佛，咒曰：「從今以去，願不生帝王尊貴之家。」
entries.en: He then spread a mat, burned incense, and worshiped the Buddha, praying, "From this time forward, may I never be born into an imperial or exalted house."
entries.literal: He then spread a mat, burned incense, and worshiped the Buddha, praying: "From this time forward, may I never be born into an imperial or exalted house."

entries.zh: 於是仰藥。
entries.en: He then drank the poison.
entries.literal: He then drank the poison.

entries.zh: 不能時絕，更以帛縊之。
entries.en: He did not die at once, and they strangled him with silk.
entries.literal: He did not die at once, and they further strangled him with silk.

entries.zh: 世充偽諡為恭皇帝。
entries.en: Shichong falsely gave him the posthumous title Emperor Gong.
entries.literal: Shichong falsely gave him the posthumous title Emperor Gong.

entries.zh: 齊王暕，字世朏，小字阿孩。
