entries.en: Prince Zheng of Qi, whose style name was Shifu and childhood name Ahai,
entries.literal: Prince of Qi Zheng, styled Shifu, childhood name Ahai,

entries.zh: 美容儀，疏眉目，少為高祖所愛。
entries.en: was handsome in bearing with well-spaced brows and eyes; from youth he was loved by Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: was handsome in bearing with well-spaced brows and eyes; from youth he was loved by the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 開皇中，立為豫章王，邑千戶。
entries.en: During the Kaihuang era he was made Prince of Yuzhang with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: During the Kaihuang era he was invested as Prince of Yuzhang with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 及長，頗涉經史，尤工騎射。
entries.en: When he grew up he studied the classics and histories widely and was especially skilled at mounted archery.
entries.literal: When he grew up he ranged widely through the classics and histories and was especially skilled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 初為內史令。
entries.en: At first he served as Director of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: At first he was Director of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，拜揚州總管沿淮以南諸軍事。
entries.en: During the Renshou era he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou with authority over military affairs south of the Huai.
entries.literal: During Renshou he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou and military affairs south of the Huai.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，進封齊王，增邑四千戶，
entries.en: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was advanced to Prince of Qi and his fief was increased by four thousand households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was advanced to Prince of Qi and his fief was increased by four thousand households.

entries.zh: 大業二年，帝初入東都，盛陳鹵簿，暕為軍導。
entries.en: In the second year of Daye, when the emperor first entered the Eastern Capital, the imperial guard of honor was displayed in full splendor, and Zheng served as military vanguard.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daye, when the emperor first entered the Eastern Capital, the imperial guard of honor was displayed in full splendor, and Zheng served as military vanguard.

entries.zh: 尋轉豫州牧。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Governor of Yu Province.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to Governor of Yu Province.

entries.zh: 俄而元德太子薨，朝野注望，鹹以暕當嗣。
entries.en: Before long the Yuande Heir Apparent died; court and countryside fixed their hopes on Zheng, believing he would be named heir.
entries.literal: Before long the Yuande Heir Apparent died; court and countryside fixed their hopes on Zheng, all holding that he should succeed.

entries.zh: 帝又敕吏部尚書牛弘妙選官屬，公卿由是多進子弟。
entries.en: The emperor also ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to select excellent staff for him; the chief ministers therefore mostly advanced their sons and younger relatives.
entries.literal: The emperor also ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to select excellent staff; the chief ministers therefore mostly advanced their sons and younger relatives.

entries.zh: 明年，轉雍州牧，尋徙河南尹、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: The next year he was appointed Governor of Yong Province, and soon became Intendant of Henan and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Three Honors.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province, and soon moved to Intendant of Henan and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Three Honors.

entries.zh: 元德太子左右二萬餘人悉隸於暕，寵遇益隆，自樂平公主及諸戚屬競來致禮，百官稱謁，填咽道路。
entries.en: More than twenty thousand attendants of the Yuande Heir Apparent all came under Zheng's command; his favor grew ever greater; from the Princess of Leping and all the imperial kin, gifts poured in; officials paid their respects until the roads were choked.
entries.literal: More than twenty thousand attendants of the Yuande Heir Apparent all came under Zheng's command; his favor grew ever greater; from the Princess of Leping and all the kin, gifts were offered in rivalry; officials paid their respects until the roads were choked.

entries.zh: 暕頗驕恣，昵近小人，所行多不法，遣喬令則、劉虔安、裴該、皇甫諶、庫狄仲錡、陳智偉等求聲色狗馬。
entries.en: Zheng was arrogant and willful, intimate with petty men; much of what he did was unlawful. He sent Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, Kudi Zhongqi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to seek music, women, dogs, and horses.
entries.literal: Zheng was rather arrogant and willful, intimate with petty men; much of what he did was unlawful. He sent Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, Kudi Zhongqi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to seek music, women, dogs, and horses.

entries.zh: 令則等因此放縱，訪人家有女者，輒矯暕命呼之，載入暕宅，因緣藏隱，恣行淫穢，而後遣之。
entries.en: Lingze and the others therefore ran wild; wherever they found a household with a daughter, they would forge Zheng's order to summon her, carry her into his residence, hide her by various pretexts, indulge in debauchery at will, and only then send her away.
entries.literal: Lingze and the others therefore ran wild; wherever they found a household with a daughter, they would forge Zheng's order to summon her, carry her into Zheng's residence, hide her by various pretexts, indulge in debauchery at will, and only then send her away.

entries.zh: 仲錡、智偉二人詣隴西，撾炙諸胡，責其名馬，得數匹以進於。
entries.en: Zhongqi and Zhiwei went to Longxi, abused the foreign traders there, demanded their famous horses, and obtained several steeds to present to Zheng.
entries.literal: Zhongqi and Zhiwei two men went to Longxi, beat and roasted various foreigners, demanded their famous horses, and obtained several steeds to present to him.

entries.zh: 暕令還主，仲錡等詐言王賜，將歸於家，暕不之知也。
entries.en: Zheng ordered the horses returned to their owners; Zhongqi and the others falsely claimed the prince had bestowed them and took them home—Zheng knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: Zheng ordered them returned to their owners; Zhongqi and the others falsely claimed the prince had bestowed the horses and took them home—Zheng did not know of this.

entries.zh: 又樂平公主嘗奏帝，言柳氏女美者，帝未有所答。
entries.en: Moreover the Princess of Leping once told the emperor that a daughter of the Liu clan was beautiful; the emperor made no reply.
entries.literal: Moreover the Princess of Leping once reported to the emperor that a daughter of the Liu clan was beautiful; the emperor made no reply.

entries.zh: 久之，主複以柳氏進於暕，暕習納之。
entries.en: After a long time the princess again presented the Liu girl to Zheng, and he readily took her in.
entries.literal: After a long time the princess again presented the Liu girl to Zheng, and Zheng readily took her in.

entries.zh: 其後帝問主柳氏女所在，主曰：「在齊王所。」
entries.en: Later the emperor asked the princess where the Liu girl was; the princess said, "She is at Prince Zheng of Qi's residence."
entries.literal: Later the emperor asked the princess where the Liu girl was; the princess said: "She is at the Prince of Qi's residence."

entries.zh: 帝不悅。
entries.en: The emperor was displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 暕于東都營第，大門無故而崩，聽事栿中折，識者以為不祥。
entries.en: When Zheng was building a residence in the Eastern Capital, the main gate collapsed for no reason and the central beam of the reception hall broke in two; those who understood such things took it as an ill omen.
entries.literal: When Zheng was building a residence in the Eastern Capital, the main gate collapsed for no reason and the central beam of the reception hall broke in two; those who understood such things took it as ill omen.

entries.zh: 其後從帝幸榆林，暕督後軍步騎五萬，恆與帝相去數十裡而舍。
entries.en: Afterward he followed the emperor to Yulin; Zheng commanded the rear army of fifty thousand foot and horse, always encamping several tens of li from the emperor.
entries.literal: Afterward he followed the emperor to Yulin; Zheng commanded the rear army of fifty thousand foot and horse, always encamping several tens of li from the emperor.

entries.zh: 會帝于汾陽宮大獵，詔暕以千騎入圍。
entries.en: When the emperor held a great hunt at Fenyang Palace, he ordered Zheng to enter the hunting enclosure with a thousand horsemen.
entries.literal: When the emperor held a great hunt at Fenyang Palace, he ordered Zheng to enter the hunting enclosure with a thousand horsemen.

entries.zh: 暕大獲麋鹿以獻，而帝未有得也，乃怒從官，皆言為暕左右所遏，獸不得前。
entries.en: Zheng took many elk and deer and presented them, but the emperor had caught nothing; he raged at his attendants, who all said Zheng's men had blocked the way and kept the game from reaching the emperor.
entries.literal: Zheng took many elk and deer and presented them, but the emperor had caught nothing; he thereupon raged at his attendants, who all said Zheng's men had blocked the way and the game could not advance.

entries.zh: 帝於是發怒，求暕罪失。
entries.en: The emperor thereupon grew angry and sought out Zheng's offenses.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry and sought out Zheng's offenses.

entries.zh: :宸基峻極，帝緒會昌。
entries.en: The imperial foundation towers to its height; the royal line enters its age of glory.
entries.literal: The imperial foundation rises to its utmost height; the imperial line meets its flourishing age.

entries.zh: 體元襲聖，儀耀重光。
entries.en: He embodied the primal virtue and inherited the sage's mantle; his presence shone with redoubled brilliance.
entries.literal: Embodying the Origin, inheriting the Sage; his bearing shines with renewed radiance.

entries.zh: 氣秀春陸，神華少陽。
entries.en: His vital spirit flourished like spring upon the earth; his brilliance shone in the quarter of youth.
entries.literal: His vital breath flourished like spring upon the land; his spirit blossomed in the eastern quarter of youth.

entries.zh: 居周軼誦，處漢韜莊。
entries.en: Among the sons of Zhou he surpassed the classic recitations; among the princes of Han he bore himself with hidden gravity.
entries.literal: In Zhou he surpassed the recitations; in Han he concealed his solemnity.

entries.zh: 有縱生知，誕膺惟睿。
entries.en: Knowledge came to him from birth; he was endowed alone with sagely wisdom.
entries.literal: He possessed innate knowledge from birth and received the sole charge of wisdom.

entries.zh: 性道觿日，幾深綺歲。
entries.en: His nature and the Way appeared from the day he was girded; subtle understanding came in the flower of youth.
entries.literal: His nature and the Way showed from the day of his girdling; subtle insight came in his brocade years.

entries.zh: 降跡大成，俯情多藝。
entries.en: He took his place in the great completion of learning and bent his heart to many accomplishments.
entries.literal: He descended to trace the Great Completion and bent his heart to many arts.

entries.zh: 樹親建國，命懿作籓。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed among the royal kin and founded his state, charged with virtue to rule as a prince.
entries.literal: He planted kin and founded states, appointing the virtuous to serve as feudatories.

entries.zh: 威蕤先路，舄奕渠門。
entries.en: His majesty went before on the road; his splendor filled the palace gates.
entries.literal: His majesty adorned the vanguard; his splendor filled the palace gates.

entries.zh: 庸服有紀，分器惟尊。
entries.en: His duties were ordered by rule; in the apportionment of regalia he held the highest place.
entries.literal: His service had its proper measure; in the division of vessels he held the highest rank.

entries.zh: 風高楚殿，雅盛梁園。
entries.en: His refinement rose like the halls of Chu; his literary grace flourished like the gardens of Liang.
entries.literal: His refinement towered like the Chu hall; his elegance flourished like the Liang garden.

entries.zh: 睿後膺儲，天人協順。
entries.en: The sagely heir received the succession; heaven and mankind were in harmony.
entries.literal: The wise heir received the succession; heaven and man were in accord.

entries.zh: 本茂條遠，基崇體峻。
entries.en: His root was deep and his branches far-reaching; his foundation was high and his stature imposing.
entries.literal: His root was luxuriant and his branches far-reaching; his foundation was lofty and his stature towering.

entries.zh: 改王參墟，奄有唐、晉。
entries.en: He was made prince at the ancient seat of Canxu and came to hold the domains of Tang and Jin.
entries.literal: He was transferred to prince at Canxu and came to hold Tang and Jin.

entries.zh: 在貴能謙，居沖益慎。
entries.en: Though exalted in rank he remained humble; dwelling in modesty he grew ever more careful.
entries.literal: Though noble he could be humble; dwelling in modesty he grew ever more cautious.

entries.zh: 封畿千里，閶闔九重。
entries.en: His domain stretched a thousand li; the palace gates towered in ninefold depth.
entries.literal: His fief stretched a thousand li; the palace gates rose ninefold.

entries.zh: 神州王化，禁旅軍容。
entries.en: He bore the royal civilizing charge of the central realm and the martial array of the palace guards.
entries.literal: He bore the kingly transformation of the divine land and the military bearing of the palace guard.

entries.zh: 瞻言偃草，高視折衝。
entries.en: His words could still contention like wind over grass; his lofty gaze could break the enemy's charge.
entries.literal: His words made the grass lie down; his lofty gaze broke the enemy's charge.

entries.zh: 帷扆清秘，親賢允屬。
entries.en: At the imperial screen he served in pure confidence; drawing near the worthy was truly his appointed role.
entries.literal: At the screen and armrest he was pure and secretive; to be near the worthy was truly his charge.

entries.zh: 泛景風瀾，飛華螭玉。
entries.en: He moved through scenes of light and wind-swept grandeur; flowering brilliance adorned dragon motifs and jade.
entries.literal: He floated upon luminous scenes and wind-swept waves; flowering brilliance flew upon dragon and jade.

entries.zh: 揮翰泉湧，敷言藻縟。
entries.en: When he took up the brush words poured forth like a spring; his discourse was woven with rich ornament.
entries.literal: When he wielded the brush words gushed like a spring; his spread discourse was brocaded and rich.

entries.zh: 式是便煩，思謀啟沃。
entries.en: Thus he took on the weight of affairs and offered counsel to nourish the throne.
entries.literal: Thus he took on pressing affairs and offered counsel to nourish the ruler.

entries.zh: 洪惟積德，豐衍繁祉。
entries.en: Greatly did he accumulate virtue; blessings multiplied and flourished.
entries.literal: Greatly did he accumulate virtue; blessings spread abroad in abundance.

entries.zh: 粵自天孫，光升元子。
entries.en: From the heaven-descended lineage his light rose to the eldest son.
entries.literal: From the Heaven-descended scion his radiance rose to the eldest son.

entries.zh: 綠車逮事，翠纓奉祀。
entries.en: In the green carriage he attended to his duties; with the azure cap-tassel he performed the sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the green carriage he attended to affairs; with the azure tassel he performed the sacrifices.

entries.zh: 肅穆滿容，儀形讓齒。
entries.en: Solemn dignity filled his bearing; in deportment he yielded by rank and age.
entries.literal: Solemn reverence filled his countenance; in bearing and form he yielded by precedence.

entries.zh: 禮樂交暢，愛敬兼資。
entries.en: Rites and music harmonized in him; love and reverence were joined in equal measure.
entries.literal: Rites and music flowed together; love and reverence were joined in him.

entries.zh: 優遊養德，恭己承儀。
entries.en: At leisure he cultivated virtue; with reverent bearing he upheld ritual propriety.
entries.literal: At ease he nourished virtue; with reverent self he upheld the rites.

entries.zh: 南山聘隱，東序尊師。
entries.en: Like the southern mountain he sought out the hidden worthy; in the eastern school he honored his teachers.
entries.literal: Like the southern mountain he sought the recluse; in the eastern school he honored his teachers.

entries.zh: 有粹神儀，深穆其度。
entries.en: He possessed a pure and spirited bearing; profound and solemn was his demeanor.
entries.literal: He possessed pure spiritual bearing; profound and solemn was his measure.

entries.zh: 顯顯觀德，溫溫審諭。
entries.en: Brightly he displayed his virtue for all to see; gently and warmly he taught and advised.
entries.literal: Brightly he displayed virtue for all to see; gently and warmly he instructed.

entries.zh: 炯戒齊箴，留連王賦。
entries.en: Bright was his admonition and even his restraint; lingering was his princely literary work.
entries.literal: Bright was his admonition and equal his caution; lingering was his princely composition.

entries.zh: 入監出撫，日就月將。
entries.en: Entering the palace to oversee affairs, going forth to comfort the people—day by day he advanced, month by month he matured.
entries.literal: Entering to oversee, going forth to comfort—day by day he advanced, month by month he grew.

entries.zh: 沖情玉裕，令問金相。
entries.en: His modest heart was rich as jade; his fine reputation shone like gold.
entries.literal: His modest heart was jade-abundant; his fine reputation had the luster of gold.

entries.zh: 宜綏景福，永作元良。
entries.en: He should have secured bright blessings and forever stood as the foremost heir.
entries.literal: He should have soothed bright blessings and forever served as the eldest worthy.

entries.zh: 神理冥漠，天道難究。
entries.en: The divine principle lies dark and remote; the way of heaven is beyond full understanding.
entries.literal: The divine principle is dark and remote; the way of heaven is hard to fathom.

entries.zh: 仁不必壽，善或愆祐。
entries.en: Benevolence does not assure long life; goodness may yet be denied its blessing.
entries.literal: Benevolence does not guarantee long life; goodness may miss its blessing.

entries.zh: 遽瑤山之頹壞，忽桂宮之毀構。
entries.en: Suddenly the jade mountain fell in ruin; in an instant the cassia palace's structure was destroyed.
entries.literal: Suddenly the jade mountain collapsed; abruptly the cassia palace's structure was destroyed.

entries.zh: 痛結幽明，悲纏宇宙。
entries.en: Grief bound the realms of the living and the dead; sorrow filled the universe.
entries.literal: Grief bound the hidden and the manifest; sorrow entwined the cosmos.

entries.zh: 慟皇情之深憫，摧具僚其如疚。
entries.en: The emperor's heart was stricken with deep grief; all his officials were crushed as though bearing guilt themselves.
entries.literal: The emperor's heart was stricken with deep compassion; all his officials were crushed as if guilty.

entries.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
entries.en: Alas, how mournful!
entries.literal: Alas, how mournful!

entries.zh: 回環氣朔，荏苒居諸。
entries.en: The seasons wheel through their cycles; time slips swiftly onward.
entries.literal: The seasons wheel through their cycles; time slips swiftly onward.

entries.zh: 沾零露於瑤圍，下申霜於玉除。
entries.en: Scattered dew falls upon the jade courtyard; descending frost settles on the jade-paved steps.
entries.literal: Scattered dew falls upon the jade enclosure; descending frost settles on the jade steps.

entries.zh: 夜漏盡兮空階曙，曉月懸兮帷殿虛。
entries.en: The night water-clock runs out and dawn light fills the empty steps; the morning moon hangs while the curtained hall stands empty.
entries.literal: The night water-clock runs out and dawn light fills the empty steps; the morning moon hangs and the curtained hall stands void.

entries.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
entries.en: Alas, how mournful!
entries.literal: Alas, how mournful!

entries.zh: 將寧甫竁，長違望苑。
entries.en: He is about to find rest in the new tomb and part forever from the Prospect Garden.
entries.literal: He is about to find rest in the new tomb and part forever from the Prospect Garden.

entries.zh: 渡渭涘於造舟，遵長平之修阪。
entries.en: They cross the Wei shore by the royal ferry and follow the long ascent of Changping.
entries.literal: They cross the Wei shore by the ferry of Zao; they follow the long slope of Changping.

entries.zh: 望鶴駕而不追，顧龍樓而日遠。
entries.en: They gaze upon the imperial hearse but cannot follow; they look back at the dragon tower growing more distant by the day.
entries.literal: They gaze upon the crane carriage but cannot pursue; they look back at the dragon tower growing daily more remote.

entries.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
entries.en: Alas, how mournful!
entries.literal: Alas, how mournful!

entries.zh: 永隔存沒，長分古今。
entries.en: Forever parted are the living and the dead; long divided are the present and what has passed.
entries.literal: Forever parted are the living and the dead; long divided are present and past.

entries.zh: 去榮華于人世，即潛之幽深。
entries.en: He leaves splendor in the world of the living and enters the hidden depths below.
entries.literal: He leaves splendor in the human world and enters the hidden depths.

entries.zh: 霏夕煙而稍起，慘落景而將沉。
entries.en: Evening mist rises thinly; the mournful setting sun is about to sink.
entries.literal: Evening mist rises thinly; the mournful setting sun is about to sink.

entries.zh: 聽哀挽之悽楚，雜灌木之悲吟。
entries.en: They hear the mournful dirge of the funeral procession, mingled with the sorrowful sighing of the thickets.
entries.literal: They hear the mournful lament of the funeral dirge, mingled with the sorrowful cry of the thickets.

entries.zh: 紛徒禦而流袂，欷纓弁以沾衿。
entries.en: The attendants stream forward with sleeves awash in tears; officials in caps sob and soak their collars.
entries.literal: The crowd of attendants streams with flowing sleeves; officials in caps sob and wet their collars.

entries.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
entries.en: Alas, how mournful!
entries.literal: Alas, how mournful!

entries.zh: 九地黃泉，千年白日。
entries.en: The ninefold earth and the yellow springs; a thousand years of daylight.
entries.literal: The ninefold earth and the yellow springs; a thousand years of white sun.

entries.zh: 雖金石之能久，終天壤乎長畢。
entries.en: Though metal and stone may endure, in the end heaven and earth themselves reach their close.
entries.literal: Though metal and stone may endure long, in the end heaven and earth reach their long close.

entries.zh: 敢圖芳於篆素，永飛聲而騰實。
entries.en: We dare inscribe his virtue upon the written record, that his fame may soar forever and his merit rise on high.
entries.literal: We dare inscribe his fragrance upon the red silk, that his fame may fly forever and his merit rise on high.

entries.zh: 有遺腹子政道，與蕭後同入突厥，處羅可汗號為隋王，中國人沒入北蕃者，悉配之以為部落，以定襄城處之。
entries.en: He had a posthumous son Zhengdao, who entered the Turks together with Empress Xiao; Quluo Khan styled him Prince of Sui; Chinese taken captive in the northern lands were all assigned to him as a tribe and settled at Dingxiang.
entries.literal: He had a posthumous son Zhengdao, who entered the Turks together with Empress Xiao; Quluo Khan styled him Prince of Sui; Chinese taken captive in the northern barbarian lands were all assigned to him as a tribe, and they were settled at Dingxiang city.

entries.zh: 及突厥滅，歸於大唐，授員外散騎侍郎。
entries.en: When the Turks were destroyed he returned to the Tang and was appointed Vice Director of the Attendant Cavalry.
entries.literal: When the Turks were destroyed he returned to Great Tang and was appointed Vice Director of the Attendant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 趙王杲，小字季子。
entries.en: Prince Gao of Zhao, whose childhood name was Jizi.
entries.literal: Prince Gao of Zhao, childhood name Jizi.

entries.zh: 年七歲，以大業九年封趙王。
entries.en: At the age of seven, in the ninth year of Daye he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: At the age of seven, in the ninth year of Daye he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 尋授光祿大夫，拜河南尹。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made Intendant of Henan.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made Intendant of Henan.

entries.zh: 從幸淮南，詔行江都太守事。
entries.en: He followed the emperor to Huainan and was ordered to act as Administrator of Jiangdu.
entries.literal: He followed the emperor to Huainan and was ordered to act as Administrator of Jiangdu.

entries.zh: 杲聰令，美容儀，帝有所制詞賦，杲多能誦之。
entries.en: Gao was clever and bright, handsome in bearing; whenever the emperor composed lyrics or rhapsodies, Gao could often recite them from memory.
entries.literal: Gao was clever and bright, handsome in bearing; whenever the emperor composed lyrics or rhapsodies, Gao could often recite them.

entries.zh: 性至孝，常見帝風動不進膳，杲亦終日不食。
entries.en: By nature he was utterly filial; whenever he saw the emperor afflicted by wind and refusing food, Gao also would not eat all day.
entries.literal: By nature he was utterly filial; whenever he saw the emperor troubled by wind and refusing food, Gao also would not eat all day.

entries.zh: 又蕭後當灸，杲先請試炷，後不許之，杲泣請曰：「後所服藥，皆蒙嘗之。
entries.en: Moreover when Empress Xiao was to undergo moxibustion, Gao first begged to test the cautery himself; the empress refused; Gao wept and pleaded, "All the medicines the empress takes, I have tasted for her.
entries.literal: Moreover when Empress Xiao was to undergo moxibustion, Gao first begged to test the cautery; the empress would not allow it; Gao wept and pleaded: "All the medicines the empress takes, I have tasted for her.

entries.zh: 今灸，願聽嘗炷。」
entries.en: Now for moxibustion, I beg to be allowed to test the cautery first."
entries.literal: Now for moxibustion, I beg to be allowed to test the cautery first."

entries.zh: 悲咽不已。
entries.en: He sobbed without cease.
entries.literal: He sobbed without cease.

entries.zh: 後竟為其停灸，由是尤愛之。
entries.en: The empress in the end suspended the moxibustion for his sake, and because of this loved him all the more.
entries.literal: The empress in the end suspended the moxibustion for his sake, and because of this loved him all the more.

entries.zh: 後遇化及反，杲在帝側，號慟不已。
entries.en: Later when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the emperor's side, crying and wailing without cease.
entries.literal: Later when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the emperor's side, crying and wailing without cease.

entries.zh: 裴虔通使賊斬之於帝前，血湔禦服。
entries.en: Pei Qiantong had the rebels behead him before the emperor; blood splashed the imperial robes.
entries.literal: Pei Qiantong had the rebels behead him before the emperor; blood splashed the imperial robes.

entries.zh: 時年十二。
entries.en: He was twelve years old.
entries.literal: He was twelve years old.

entries.zh: 【論】史臣曰：元德太子雅性謹重，有君人之量，降年不永，哀哉！
entries.en: [Commentary] The historiographer says: The Yuande Heir Apparent was refined and grave by nature, with the measure of a ruler; his years were cut short—how mournful!
entries.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: The Yuande Heir Apparent by nature was refined and grave, with the measure of a ruler; his years were cut short—how mournful!

entries.zh: 齊王敏慧可稱，志不及遠，頗懷驕僭，故煬帝疏而忌之。
entries.en: Prince Zheng of Qi was clever and admirable, but his aims did not reach far; he rather harbored arrogance and presumption, and so Emperor Yang kept him at a distance and was wary of him.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qi was clever and admirable, but his aims did not reach far; he rather harbored arrogance and presumption, and so Emperor Yang kept him at a distance and was wary of him.

entries.zh: 心無父子之親，貌展君臣之敬，身非積善，國有餘殃。
entries.en: In heart he had no bond of father and son; in appearance he displayed the respect of subject and ruler; his person had not accumulated goodness, and the state bore the calamity that followed.
entries.literal: In heart he had no bond of father and son; in appearance he displayed the respect of subject and ruler; his person had not accumulated goodness, and the state bore remaining calamity.

entries.zh: 至令趙及燕、越皆不得其死，悲夫！
entries.en: So that even the princes of Zhao, Yan, and Yue all failed to meet natural deaths—how lamentable!
entries.literal: So that even Zhao and Yan and Yue all failed to meet natural deaths—how lamentable!

entries.zh: 宇文述，字伯通，代郡武川人也。
entries.en: Yu Wenshu, whose courtesy name was Botong, came from Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.
entries.literal: Yu Wenshu—Yu Wenshu, courtesy name Botong, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.

entries.zh: 本姓破野頭，役屬鮮卑俟豆歸，後從其主為宇文氏。
entries.en: He had originally borne the surname Poyetou and served under the Xianbei leader Houdougou; he later took the Yuwen surname along with his master.
entries.literal: His original surname was Poyetou; he served as a dependent of the Xianbei chief Houdougou, and later followed his lord in adopting the surname Yuwen.

entries.zh: 父盛，周上柱國。
entries.en: His father Yu Sheng had held the rank of Superior Pillar of State under the Northern Zhou.
entries.literal: His father Sheng was a Superior Pillar of State under the Zhou.

entries.zh: 述少驍銳，便弓馬。
entries.en: As a youth, Shu was fierce and quick, and excelled at archery and horsemanship.
entries.literal: In youth Shu was fierce and keen, skilled with bow and horse.

entries.zh: 年十一時，有相者謂述曰：「公子善自愛，後當位極人臣。」
entries.en: When he was eleven, a physiognomist told him, "Take good care of yourself, young sir—you will one day rise to the highest ministerial rank."
entries.literal: At age eleven a physiognomist told Shu, "Young lord, take good care of yourself—you will later reach the highest rank among ministers."

entries.zh: 周武帝時，以父軍功，起家拜開府。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Zhou, he began his career thanks to his father's military service and was appointed a Colonel-Director-in-Chief.
entries.literal: During Emperor Wu of Zhou, by virtue of his father's military merit, he entered office and was appointed Colonel-Director-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 述性恭謹沈密，周大塚宰宇文護甚愛之，以本官領護親信。
entries.en: Shu was respectful, cautious, and reserved by nature. The Zhou regent Yuwen Hu took a great liking to him and left him in his original post while putting him in charge of the guard of personal confidants.
entries.literal: Shu was by nature respectful, cautious, and reserved; the Zhou Grand Minister Yuwen Hu greatly favored him and had him retain his existing office while leading the guard of close associates.

entries.zh: 及帝親總萬機，召為左宮伯，累遷英果中大夫，賜爵博陵郡公，尋改封濮陽郡公。
entries.en: When the emperor personally took the reins of government, Shu was summoned to serve as Left Palace Steward. He was successively promoted to Resolute Valor Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Duke of Boling, and shortly afterward given the title Duke of Puyang.
entries.literal: When the emperor personally assumed control of state affairs, he was summoned to serve as Left Palace Steward, was repeatedly promoted to Resolute Valor Grand Master of the Palace, was granted the title Duke of Boling Commandery, and soon thereafter was reenfeoffed as Duke of Puyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 凡述所薦達，皆至大官。
entries.en: All whom Shu recommended and advanced reached high office.
entries.literal: All whom Shu recommended and advanced reached high office.

entries.zh: 趙行樞乙太常樂戶，家財億計，述謂為兄，多受其賄。
entries.en: Zhao Xingshu, a musician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, had household wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions. Shu called him elder brother and received many bribes from him.
entries.literal: Zhao Xingshu, a musician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, had household wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions; Shu called him elder brother and received many bribes from him.

entries.zh: 稱其驍勇，起家為折衝郎將。
entries.en: Praising his valor, Shu had him enter office as a Resolute Assault Commandant.
entries.literal: Praising his valor, he entered office as a Resolute Assault Commandant.

entries.zh: 郭衍，字彥文，自雲太原介休人也。
entries.en: Guo Yan, whose courtesy name was Yanwen, claimed to be a native of Jiexiu in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Guo Yan—Guo Yan, courtesy name Yanwen, claimed to be a native of Jiexiu in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 父以舍人從魏武帝入關，其後官至侍中。
entries.en: His father, as a palace attendant, followed Emperor Wu of Wei through the passes and later rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: His father, as a palace attendant, followed Emperor Wu of Wei through the passes and later rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 衍少驍武，善騎射。
entries.en: As a youth, Yan was valiant in arms and skilled at riding and archery.
entries.literal: In youth Yan was valiant in arms and skilled at riding and archery.

entries.zh: 周陳王純引為左右，累遷大都督。
entries.en: Prince Chun of Chen of Zhou took him into his personal service and repeatedly promoted him to Grand Commander.
entries.literal: Prince Chun of Chen of Zhou took him into his personal service and repeatedly promoted him to Grand Commander.

entries.zh: 時齊氏未平，衍奉詔於天水募人，以鎮東境，得樂徙千餘家，屯於陝城。
entries.en: At that time the Qi had not yet been pacified. Yan received orders to recruit men at Tianshui to guard the eastern frontier, obtained more than a thousand households of music-office dependents, and encamped them at Shancheng.
entries.literal: At that time the Qi had not yet been pacified; Yan received orders to recruit men at Tianshui to guard the eastern frontier, obtained more than a thousand households of music-office dependents, and encamped them at Shancheng.

entries.zh: 拜使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Director with the Ceremonial Equipage of the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Director with the Ceremonial Equipage of the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 每有寇至，輒率所領禦之，一歲數告捷，頗為齊人所憚。
entries.en: Whenever raiders came, he led those under his command to repel them. Several times in a year he reported victory, and the Qi people came to fear him considerably.
entries.literal: Whenever raiders came, he would lead those under his command to repel them; several times in a year he reported victory, and the Qi people came to fear him considerably.

entries.zh: 王益親任之。
entries.en: The prince came to trust and employ him all the more.
entries.literal: The prince came to trust and employ him all the more.

entries.zh: 建德中，周武帝出幸雲陽，衍朝於行所，時議欲伐齊，衍請為前鋒。
entries.en: In the Jiande era Emperor Wu of Zhou went out to Yunyang. Yan attended him at the traveling residence, and when deliberations turned to attacking Qi, Yan requested to serve as vanguard.
entries.literal: In the Jiande era Emperor Wu of Zhou went out to Yunyang; Yan attended him at the traveling residence, and when deliberations turned to attacking Qi, Yan requested to serve as vanguard.

entries.zh: 攻河陰城，授儀同大將軍。
entries.en: He attacked Heyin and was appointed General-in-Chief with the Ceremonial Equipage.
entries.literal: He attacked Heyin city and was appointed General-in-Chief with the Ceremonial Equipage.

entries.zh: 武帝圍晉州，慮齊兵來援，令衍從陳王守千里徑。
entries.en: Emperor Wu besieged Jinzhou, fearing that Qi troops would come to its relief, and ordered Yan to follow Prince Chen in guarding the Thousand-Li Path.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu besieged Jinzhou, fearing that Qi troops would come to its relief, and ordered Yan to follow Prince Chen in guarding the Thousand-Li Path.

entries.zh: 又從武帝與齊主大戰于晉州，追齊師至高壁，敗之。
entries.en: He also followed Emperor Wu in the great battle with the Qi ruler at Jinzhou, pursued the Qi army to Gaobi, and defeated it.
entries.literal: He also followed Emperor Wu in the great battle with the Qi ruler at Jinzhou, pursued the Qi army to Gaobi, and defeated it.

entries.zh: 仍從平并州，以功加授開府，封武強縣公，邑一千二百戶，賜姓叱羅氏，
entries.en: He still followed in the pacification of Bingzhou. For his merit he was further granted the title of Director-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang with a fief of twelve hundred households, and given the surname Chiluo.
entries.literal: He still followed in the pacification of Bingzhou; for his merit he was further granted the title of Director-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang County with a fief of twelve hundred households, and given the surname Chiluo.

entries.zh: 宣政元年，為右中軍熊渠中大夫。
entries.en: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was appointed Right Central Army Bear-Channel Grand Master of the Palace.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was appointed Right Central Army Bear-Channel Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂相州，述以行軍總管率步騎三千，從韋孝寬擊之。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, Yuchi Jiong raised a rebellion at Xiangzhou. Shu, acting as campaign commander-in-chief, led three thousand foot and horse soldiers to join Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Yu Chi rebelled at Xiangzhou; Shu, as campaign commander-in-chief, led three thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him alongside Wei Xiaokuan.

entries.zh: 軍至河陽，迥遣將李俊攻懷州，述別擊俊軍，破之。
entries.en: When the army reached Heyang, Chi sent his general Li Jun to attack Huaizhou. Shu struck Jun's force separately and routed it.
entries.literal: When the army reached Heyang, Chi sent the general Li Jun to attack Huaizhou; Shu separately attacked Jun's army and defeated it.

entries.zh: 又與諸將擊尉惇於永橋，述先鋒陷陣，俘馘甚眾。
entries.en: He also joined the other generals in attacking Yuchi Dun at Yong Bridge. Shu led the vanguard through the enemy formation and took a great many prisoners and heads.
entries.literal: He also joined the other generals in attacking Yu Dun at Yong Bridge; Shu led the vanguard in breaking the enemy line and took many captives and heads.

entries.zh: 平尉迥，每戰有功，超拜上柱國，進爵褒國公，賜縑三千匹。
entries.en: In the campaign to put down Yuchi Jiong, he distinguished himself in every battle. He was promoted out of turn to Superior Pillar of State, raised to Duke of Bao, and granted three thousand bolts of silk.
entries.literal: In pacifying Yu Chi, he distinguished himself in every battle and was promoted above the usual order to Superior Pillar of State, advanced in rank to Duke of the State of Bao, and granted three thousand bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 開皇初，拜右衛大將軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 平陳之役，複以行軍總管率眾三萬，自六合而濟。
entries.en: During the campaign to conquer Chen, he again served as campaign commander-in-chief, leading thirty thousand men across the river from Liuhe.
entries.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, he again served as campaign commander-in-chief, leading thirty thousand troops across from Liuhe.

entries.zh: 時韓擒、賀若弼兩軍趣丹陽，述進據石頭，以為聲援。
entries.en: At that time the armies of Han Qin and He Ruobi were pressing toward Danyang. Shu advanced and seized Shitou to serve as a supporting position.
entries.literal: At that time the armies of Han Qin and He Ruobi were pressing toward Danyang; Shu advanced and seized Shitou as a supporting position.

entries.zh: 陳主既擒，而蕭瓛、蕭岩據東吳之地，擁兵拒守。
entries.en: After the Chen ruler had been captured, Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan still held eastern Wu, gathering troops to resist the invaders.
entries.literal: After the Chen ruler had been captured, Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan held the lands of eastern Wu, mustering troops to resist and defend.

entries.zh: 述領行軍總管元契、張默言等討之，水陸兼進。
entries.en: Shu led the campaign commanders Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others against them, advancing by both land and water.
entries.literal: Shu led the campaign commanders Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others to attack them, advancing by both land and water.

entries.zh: 落叢公燕榮以舟師自海至，亦受述節度。
entries.en: Yan Rong, Duke of Luocong, brought a fleet from the sea and likewise placed himself under Shu's command.
entries.literal: Duke of Luocong Yan Rong brought a fleet from the sea and also came under Shu's command.

entries.zh: 上下詔曰：「公鴻勳大業，名高望重，奉國之誠，久所知悉。
entries.en: The emperor issued an edict saying, "Your great achievements and lofty reputation are well known, as is the loyalty you have long shown to the state.
entries.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying, "Sir, your great merit and vast achievement, your lofty name and heavy prestige, and your long-known loyalty to the state are well understood.

entries.zh: 金陵之寇，既已清蕩，而吳會之地，東路為遙，蕭岩、蕭瓛，並在其處。
entries.en: The enemy at Jinling has already been swept away, but Wu and Kuai lie far to the east, and both Xiao Yan and Xiao Kan are there.
entries.literal: The enemy at Jinling has already been swept away, but the lands of Wu and Kuai lie far to the east, and Xiao Yan and Xiao Kan are both there.

entries.zh: 公率將戎旅，撫慰彼方，振揚國威，宣佈朝化。
entries.en: Lead your troops to pacify that region, display the power of the state, and proclaim the civilizing influence of the court.
entries.literal: Sir, lead your troops to pacify and comfort that region, display the state's might, and proclaim the court's civilizing influence.

entries.zh: 以公明略，乘勝而往，風行電掃，自當稽服。
entries.en: With your clear strategy, advance on the momentum of victory. Like wind and lightning you will sweep them away, and they will surely submit.
entries.literal: With your clear strategy, go forth on the momentum of victory; like wind and lightning you will sweep them away, and they will surely submit.

entries.zh: 若使干戈不用，黎庶獲安，方副朕懷，公之力也。」
entries.en: If arms need not be used and the people gain peace, that will truly fulfill my wish—and it will be through your efforts."
entries.literal: If arms need not be used and the common people gain peace, that will truly accord with my heart—and it will be through your effort."

entries.zh: 陳永新侯陳君范自晉陵奔瓛，並軍合勢。
entries.en: Chen Junfan, Marquis of Yongxin, fled from Jinling to join Kan, and their armies united their forces.
entries.literal: Chen Junfan, Marquis of Yongxin, fled from Jinling to join Kan, and their armies united their strength.

entries.zh: 見述軍且至，瓛懼，立柵于晉陵城東，又絕塘道，留兵拒述。
entries.en: Seeing that Shu's army was approaching, Kan grew afraid. He built palisades east of Jinling, cut off the canal road, and left troops to resist Shu.
entries.literal: Seeing that Shu's army was about to arrive, Kan was afraid; he built palisades east of Jinling city, cut off the canal road, and left troops to resist Shu.

entries.zh: 瓛自義興入太湖，圖掩述後。
entries.en: Kan himself entered Lake Tai from Yixing, intending to strike at Shu's rear.
entries.literal: Kan himself entered Lake Tai from Yixing, intending to strike at Shu's rear.

entries.zh: 述進破其柵，回兵擊瓛，大敗之，斬瓛司馬曹勒叉。
entries.en: Shu advanced, broke through the palisades, turned his army to strike Kan, and inflicted a crushing defeat, beheading Kan's marshal Cao Lecha.
entries.literal: Shu advanced, broke through the palisades, turned his army to strike Kan, and inflicted a great defeat, beheading Kan's marshal of the left Cao Lecha.

entries.zh: 前軍複陷吳州，瓛以餘眾保包山，燕榮擊破之。
entries.en: The vanguard again captured Wuzhou. Kan held Baoshan with his remaining troops, but Yan Rong attacked and defeated him.
entries.literal: The vanguard again captured Wuzhou; Kan held Baoshan with his remaining troops, and Yan Rong attacked and defeated him.

entries.zh: 述進至奉公埭，蕭岩、陳君範等以會稽請降。
entries.en: Shu advanced to Fenggong Dam, where Xiao Yan, Chen Junfan, and others offered to surrender Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Shu advanced to Fenggong Dam; Xiao Yan, Chen Junfan, and others offered to surrender Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 述許之，二人面縛路左，吳會悉平。
entries.en: Shu accepted. The two men bound themselves and stood by the roadside, and Wu and Kuai were entirely pacified.
entries.literal: Shu accepted; the two men bound themselves and stood by the roadside, and Wu and Kuai were entirely pacified.

entries.zh: 以功拜一子開府，賜物三千段，拜安州總管。
entries.en: For his merit one of his sons was appointed Colonel-Director-in-Chief, he was granted three thousand lengths of goods, and he was appointed Area Commander of Anzhou.
entries.literal: For his merit one son was appointed Colonel-Director-in-Chief, he was granted three thousand lengths of goods, and he was appointed Area Commander of Anzhou.

entries.zh: 尉迥之起逆，從韋孝寬戰于武陟，進戰於相州。
entries.en: When Yuchi Jiong raised a rebellion, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in battle at Wuzhi and advanced to fight at Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: When Yu Chi raised a rebellion, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in battle at Wuzhi and advanced to fight at Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 先是，迥遣弟子勤為青州總管，率青、齊之眾來助迥。
entries.en: Earlier Chi had sent his younger brother's son Qin as Area Commander of Qingzhou to lead the masses of Qing and Qi to aid Chi.
entries.literal: Earlier Chi had sent his younger brother's son Qin as Area Commander of Qingzhou to lead the masses of Qing and Qi to aid Chi.

entries.zh: 迥敗，勤與迥子惇、祐等欲東奔青州。
entries.en: When Chi was defeated, Qin, together with Chi's sons Dun and You and others, wished to flee east to Qingzhou.
entries.literal: When Chi was defeated, Qin, together with Chi's sons Dun and You and others, wished to flee east to Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 衍將精騎一千追破之，執祐於陣，勤遂遁走，而惇亦逃逸。
entries.en: Yan led a thousand elite cavalry in pursuit and defeated them. He seized You on the battlefield, Qin fled, and Dun also escaped.
entries.literal: Yan led a thousand elite cavalry in pursuit, defeated them, seized You on the battlefield, and Qin thereupon fled, while Dun also escaped.

entries.zh: 衍至濟州，入據其城，又擊其餘党於濟北，累戰破之，執送京師。
entries.en: Yan reached Jizhou, entered and seized its city, and again attacked the remaining factions in Jibei. After repeated battles he defeated them and sent the captives to the capital.
entries.literal: Yan reached Jizhou, entered and seized its city, and again attacked the remaining factions in Jibei; after repeated battles he defeated them and sent the captives to the capital.

entries.zh: 超授上柱國，封武山郡公。
entries.en: He was promoted out of turn to Superior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Wushan.
entries.literal: He was promoted above the usual order to Superior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Wushan Commandery.

entries.zh: 賞物七千段。
entries.en: He was rewarded with seven thousand lengths of goods.
entries.literal: He was rewarded with seven thousand lengths of goods.

entries.zh: 密勸高祖殺周室諸王，早行禪代。
entries.en: He secretly urged Emperor Gaozu to kill the princes of the Zhou house and carry out the transfer of the mandate early.
entries.literal: He secretly urged Emperor Gaozu to kill the princes of the Zhou house and carry out the transfer of the mandate early.

entries.zh: 由是大被親昵，
entries.en: Thereby he came to be greatly favored and intimate.
entries.literal: Thereby he came to be greatly favored and intimate.

entries.zh: 開皇元年，敕復舊姓為郭氏。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaihuang, an edict restored his former surname as Guo.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, an edict restored his former surname as Guo.

entries.zh: 突厥犯塞，以衍為行軍總管，領兵屯於平涼。
entries.en: When the Turks raided the frontier, Yan was appointed campaign commander-in-chief and led troops to encamp at Pingliang.
entries.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Yan was appointed campaign commander-in-chief and led troops to encamp at Pingliang.

entries.zh: 數歲，虜不入。
entries.en: For several years the barbarians did not enter.
entries.literal: For several years the barbarians did not enter.

entries.zh: 征為開漕渠大監。
entries.en: He was summoned to serve as Grand Supervisor of the Opening of the Transport Canal.
entries.literal: He was summoned to serve as Grand Supervisor of the Opening of the Transport Canal.

entries.zh: 部率水工，鑿渠引渭水，經大興城北，東至於潼關，漕運四百餘裡。
entries.en: He directed water workers, cut a canal to draw the Wei River past the north of Daxing east to Tong Pass, and transported grain by water for more than four hundred li.
entries.literal: He directed water workers, cut a canal to draw the Wei River past the north of Daxing city east to Tong Pass, and transported grain by water for more than four hundred li.

entries.zh: 關內賴之，名之曰富民渠。
entries.en: The Guanzhong region relied upon it, and it was named the Canal for Enriching the People.
entries.literal: The Guanzhong region relied upon it, and it was named the Canal for Enriching the People.

entries.zh: 五年，授瀛州刺史。
entries.en: In year five he was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: In year five he was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 遇秋霖大水，其屬縣多漂沒，民皆上高樹，依大家。
entries.en: He encountered autumn rains and great floods. Many subordinate counties were washed away, and the people climbed tall trees and relied on great households.
entries.literal: He encountered autumn rains and great floods; many subordinate counties were washed away, and the people all climbed tall trees and relied on great households.

entries.zh: 衍親備舩栰，並齎糧拯救之，民多獲濟。
entries.en: Yan personally prepared boats and rafts, brought grain as well, and rescued them. Many of the people were saved.
entries.literal: Yan personally prepared boats and rafts, brought grain as well, and rescued them; many of the people were saved.

entries.zh: 衍先開倉賑恤，後始聞奏。
entries.en: Yan first opened the granaries for relief before memorializing the matter.
entries.literal: Yan first opened the granaries for relief before memorializing the matter.

entries.zh: 上大善之，選授朔州總管。
entries.en: The emperor greatly approved and selected him for appointment as Area Commander of Shuozhou.
entries.literal: The emperor greatly approved and selected him for appointment as Area Commander of Shuozhou.

entries.zh: 所部有恆安鎮，北接蕃境，常勞轉運。
entries.en: Within his jurisdiction was Heng'an Fort, which bordered the barbarian frontier to the north and constantly burdened transport.
entries.literal: Within his jurisdiction was Heng'an Fort, which bordered the barbarian frontier to the north and constantly burdened transport.

entries.zh: 衍乃選沃饒地，置屯田，歲剩粟萬餘石，民免轉輸之勞。
entries.en: Yan then selected fertile land and established military colonies. Each year more than ten thousand piculs of grain remained, and the people were spared the labor of transport.
entries.literal: Yan then selected fertile land and established military colonies; each year more than ten thousand piculs of grain remained, and the people were spared the labor of transport.

entries.zh: 又築桑乾鎮，皆稱旨。
entries.en: He also built Sanggan Fort—all met with imperial approval.
entries.literal: He also built Sanggan Fort—all met with imperial approval.

entries.zh: 十年，從晉王廣出鎮揚州。
entries.en: In year ten he followed Prince Guang of Jin out to station at Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In year ten he followed Prince Guang of Jin out to station at Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 遇江表構逆，命衍為總管，領精銳萬人先屯京口。
entries.en: When rebellion arose south of the Yangzi, he was ordered to serve as commander-in-chief, leading ten thousand elite troops to encamp first at Jingkou.
entries.literal: When rebellion arose south of the Yangzi, he was ordered to serve as commander-in-chief, leading ten thousand elite troops to encamp first at Jingkou.

entries.zh: 于貴洲南與賊戰，敗之，生擒魁帥，大獲舟楫糧儲，以充軍實，乃討東陽、永嘉、宣城、黟、歙諸洞，盡平之。
entries.en: South of Guizhou he fought the rebels and defeated them, capturing the chieftain alive and gaining a great store of boats and grain supplies to fill the army's needs. He then campaigned against the cave settlements of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She and pacified them all.
entries.literal: South of Guizhou he fought the rebels, defeated them, captured the chieftain alive, and gained a great store of boats and grain supplies to fill the army's needs; he then campaigned against the cave settlements of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She and pacified them all.

entries.zh: 授蔣州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 時晉王廣鎮揚州，甚善於述，欲述近己，因奏為壽州刺史總管。
entries.en: At that time Prince Guang of Jin was stationed at Yangzhou and was on very good terms with Shu. Wishing to keep Shu near himself, he memorialized to have him appointed Area Commander and Inspector of Shouzhou.
entries.literal: At that time Prince of Jin Guang was stationed at Yangzhou and was on very good terms with Shu; wishing to keep Shu near himself, he memorialized to have him appointed Area Commander and Inspector of Shouzhou.

entries.zh: 王時陰有奪宗之志，請計於述，述曰：「皇太子失愛已久，令德不聞於天下。
entries.en: The prince at that time secretly harbored the ambition to seize the succession and sought Shu's counsel. Shu said, "The Crown Prince has long since lost favor, and his virtue is not known throughout the realm.
entries.literal: The prince at that time secretly harbored the ambition to seize the succession and sought Shu's counsel. Shu said, "The Crown Prince has long since lost favor, and his virtue is not heard of throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 大王仁孝著稱，才能蓋世，數經將領，深有大功。
entries.en: Your Highness is renowned for benevolence and filial piety, your talent surpasses the age, you have repeatedly led armies, and you have achieved great merit.
entries.literal: Your Highness is renowned for benevolence and filial piety, your talent surpasses the age, you have repeatedly led armies, and you have achieved great merit.

entries.zh: 主上之與內宮，鹹所鍾愛，四海之望，實歸於大王。
entries.en: Both the sovereign and the inner palace cherish you alike, and the hopes of the empire truly rest upon Your Highness.
entries.literal: Both the sovereign and the inner palace alike cherish you; the hopes of the four seas truly rest upon Your Highness.

entries.zh: 然廢立者，國家之大事，處人父子骨肉之間，誠非易謀也。
entries.en: Yet deposition and installation are great affairs of state, and to stand between father and son is truly no easy matter to plot.
entries.literal: Yet deposition and installation are great affairs of state; to stand between father and son in flesh and blood is truly no easy matter to plot.

entries.zh: 然能移主上者，唯楊素耳。
entries.en: Yet the one who can move the sovereign is Yang Su alone.
entries.literal: Yet the one who can move the sovereign is only Yang Su.

entries.zh: 素之謀者，唯其弟約。
entries.en: Of those who counsel Su, only his younger brother Yue matters.
entries.literal: Among those who counsel Su, only his younger brother Yue matters.

entries.zh: 述雅知約，請朝京師，與約相見，共圖廢立。」
entries.en: Shu was on familiar terms with Yue. He asked to go to the capital, meet with Yue, and together plot the change of succession."
entries.literal: Shu was on familiar terms with Yue; he asked to go to the capital, meet with Yue, and together plot deposition and installation."

entries.zh: 晉王大悅，多齎金寶，資述入關。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin was greatly pleased and loaded Shu with gold and jewels to fund his journey to the capital.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin was greatly pleased and loaded Shu with gold and jewels to fund his entry into the passes.

entries.zh: 述數請約，盛陳器玩，與之酣暢，因而共博，每佯不勝，所齎金寶盡輸之。
entries.en: Shu repeatedly invited Yue, lavishly displayed vessels and curios, and drank freely with him. They then gambled together, and each time Shu pretended to lose until all the gold and jewels he had brought had passed to Yue.
entries.literal: Shu repeatedly invited Yue, lavishly displayed vessels and curios, drank freely with him, and then gambled together; each time he pretended to lose, and all the gold and jewels he had brought were lost to Yue.

entries.zh: 約所得既多，稍以謝述。
entries.en: Once Yue had gained a great deal, he gradually began to thank Shu.
entries.literal: Once Yue had gained much, he gradually began to thank Shu.

entries.zh: 述因曰：「此晉王之賜，令述與公為歡樂耳。」
entries.en: Shu then said, "These were gifts from the Prince of Jin, meant only for us to enjoy together."
entries.literal: Shu then said, "These were gifts from the Prince of Jin, meant only for Shu and you to enjoy together."

entries.zh: 約大驚曰：「何為者？」
entries.en: Yue was greatly startled and said, "What is the meaning of this?"
entries.literal: Yue was greatly startled and said, "What is the meaning of this?"

entries.zh: 述因為王申意。
entries.en: Shu then conveyed the prince's intentions on his behalf.
entries.literal: Shu then conveyed the prince's intentions on his behalf.

entries.zh: 約然其說，退言於素，素亦從之。
entries.en: Yue approved of this plan, withdrew and spoke of it to Su, and Su assented as well.
entries.literal: Yue approved of this plan, withdrew and spoke of it to Su, and Su also assented.

entries.zh: 於是素每與述謀事。
entries.en: Thereafter Su regularly plotted affairs together with Shu.
entries.literal: Thereafter Su regularly plotted affairs together with Shu.

entries.zh: 晉王與述情好益密，命述子士及尚南陽公主，前後賞賜不可勝計。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin and Shu grew ever closer. He arranged for Shu's son Shiji to marry the Princess of Nanyang, and the rewards bestowed before and after were beyond counting.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin and Shu grew ever closer in affection; he ordered Shu's son Shiji to marry the Princess of Nanyang, and the rewards bestowed before and after were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 及晉王為皇太子，以述為左衛率。
entries.en: When the Prince of Jin became Crown Prince, Shu was appointed Colonel of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jin became Crown Prince, Shu was appointed Colonel of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 舊令，率官第四品，上以述素貴，遂進率品為第三，其見重如此。
entries.en: By the old regulations the colonel's office was fourth rank, but because the emperor considered Shu inherently noble, he advanced the colonel's rank to third—such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: By the old regulations the colonel's office was fourth rank, but because the emperor considered Shu inherently noble, he advanced the colonel's rank to third—such was the esteem in which he was held.

entries.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜左衛大將軍，改封許國公，
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Shu was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and reenfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Shu was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and reenfeoffed as Duke of the State of Xu.

entries.zh: 大業三年，加開府儀同三司，每冬正朝會，輒給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: In the third year of Daye, he was further granted the title of Director-in-Chief with the Ceremonial Equipage of the Three Excellencies, and at each winter court assembly he was given a set of martial music.
entries.literal: In the third year of Daye, he was further granted the title of Director-in-Chief with the Ceremonial Equipage of the Three Excellencies, and at each winter court assembly he was given a set of martial music.

entries.zh: 從幸榆林，時鐵勒契弊歌棱攻敗吐谷渾，其部攜散，遂遣使請降求救。
entries.en: He accompanied the emperor to Yulin. At that time the Tiele chief Qibili Geling attacked and defeated Tuyuhun, whose tribes scattered in flight, and they then sent envoys to request surrender and aid.
entries.literal: He accompanied the emperor to Yulin; at that time the Tiele chief Qibili Geling attacked and defeated Tuyuhun, whose tribes scattered in flight, and they then sent envoys to request surrender and aid.

entries.zh: 帝令述以兵屯西平之臨羌城，撫納降附。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Shu to station troops at Linqiang in Xiping to pacify and receive those who surrendered.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Shu to station troops at Linqiang city in Xiping to pacify and receive those who surrendered.

entries.zh: 吐谷渾見述擁強兵，懼不敢降，遂西遁。
entries.en: Tuyuhun, seeing that Shu commanded a strong army, was afraid to surrender and fled westward.
entries.literal: Tuyuhun, seeing that Shu commanded a strong army, was afraid and did not dare to surrender, and fled westward.

entries.zh: 述領鷹揚郎將梁元禮、張峻、崔師等追之，至曼頭城，攻拔之，斬三千餘級。
entries.en: Shu led the Eagle-Flying Commandants Liang Yuanli, Zhang Jun, Cui Shi, and others in pursuit. Reaching Mantou, they attacked and captured it, beheading more than three thousand.
entries.literal: Shu led the Eagle-Flying Commandants Liang Yuanli, Zhang Jun, Cui Shi, and others in pursuit; reaching Mantou city, they attacked and captured it, beheading more than three thousand.

entries.zh: 乘勝至赤水城，複拔之。
entries.en: Pressing the victory to Chishui, they captured that city as well.
entries.literal: Pressing the victory to Chishui city, they captured it as well.

entries.zh: 其餘黨走屯丘尼川，述進擊，大破之，獲其王公、尚書、將軍二百人，前後虜男女四千口而還。
entries.en: The remaining factions fled and encamped at Qiuni River. Shu advanced and inflicted a crushing defeat, capturing two hundred of their princes, ministers, and generals, and in all took four thousand men and women captive before returning.
entries.literal: The remaining factions fled and encamped at Qiuni River; Shu advanced and inflicted a great defeat, capturing two hundred of their princes, ministers, and generals, and before and after took four thousand men and women captive before returning.

entries.zh: 渾主南走雪山，其故地皆空。
entries.en: The Tuyuhun ruler fled south to Snow Mountain, and his former lands were left empty.
entries.literal: The Tuyuhun ruler fled south to Snow Mountain, and his former lands were all emptied.

entries.zh: 帝大悅。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 明年，從帝西幸，巡至金山，登燕支，述每為斥候。
entries.en: The following year he accompanied the emperor on a western tour to Mount Jin and the ascent of Mount Yanzhi, serving each time as scout.
entries.literal: The following year he accompanied the emperor on a western tour to Mount Jin, ascending Mount Yanzhi; Shu each time served as scout.

entries.zh: 時渾賊複寇張掖，進擊走之。
entries.en: At that time the Tuyuhun bandits again raided Zhangye. He advanced and drove them off.
entries.literal: At that time the Tuyuhun bandits again raided Zhangye; he advanced and drove them off.

entries.zh: 還至江都宮，敕述與蘇威常典選舉，參預朝政。
entries.en: Returning to the Jiangdu Palace, the emperor ordered Shu and Su Wei regularly to oversee selections and appointments and to participate in court governance.
entries.literal: Returning to the Jiangdu Palace, the emperor ordered Shu and Su Wei regularly to oversee selections and appointments and to participate in court governance.

entries.zh: 述時貴重，委任與蘇威等，其親愛則過之。
entries.en: Shu was at that time noble and powerful. His commissions of trust were equal to Su Wei and the others, but in personal favor he surpassed them.
entries.literal: Shu was at that time noble and powerful; his commissions of trust were equal to Su Wei and the others, but in personal favor he surpassed them.

entries.zh: 帝所得遠方貢獻及四時口味，輒見班賜，中使相望於道。
entries.en: Whatever the emperor received in tribute from distant lands and seasonal delicacies, he would at once bestow a share upon Shu, and palace envoys lined the roads in succession.
entries.literal: Whatever the emperor received in tribute from distant lands and seasonal delicacies, he would at once bestow a share upon Shu; palace envoys lined the roads in succession.

entries.zh: 述善於供奉，俯仰折旋，容止便辟，宿衛者鹹取則焉。
entries.en: Shu was skilled at attendance. In bowing and rising, turning and wheeling, his bearing and manner were nimble and pleasing, and the palace guards all took him as their model.
entries.literal: Shu was skilled at attendance; in bowing and rising, turning and wheeling, his bearing and manner were nimble and pleasing, and the palace guards all took him as their model.

entries.zh: 又有巧思，凡有所裝飾，皆出人意表。
entries.en: He also had ingenious ideas, and whatever he decorated was beyond people's expectations.
entries.literal: He also had ingenious ideas; whatever he decorated was beyond people's expectations.

entries.zh: 數以奇服異物進獻宮掖，由是帝彌悅焉。
entries.en: He repeatedly presented strange garments and exotic objects to the inner palace, and thereby the emperor grew ever more pleased with him.
entries.literal: He repeatedly presented strange garments and exotic objects to the inner palace, and thereby the emperor grew ever more pleased with him.

entries.zh: 時述貴幸，言無不從，勢傾朝廷。
entries.en: At that time Shu was noble and favored. None of his words went unheeded, and his power overshadowed the court.
entries.literal: At that time Shu was noble and favored; none of his words went unheeded, and his power overshadowed the court.

entries.zh: 左衛將軍張瑾與述連官，嘗有評議，偶不中意，述張目叱之，瑾惶懼而走，文武百僚莫敢違忤。
entries.en: Left Guard General Zhang Jin served in the same office as Shu. They once had a discussion in which Jin happened to displease him, and Shu glared and shouted at him. Jin fled in fear, and none of the civil and military officials dared to defy him.
entries.literal: Left Guard General Zhang Jin served in the same office as Shu; they once had a discussion in which Jin happened to displease him, and Shu glared and shouted at him. Jin fled in fear, and none of the civil and military officials dared to defy him.

entries.zh: 然性貪鄙，知人有珍異之物，必求取之。
entries.en: Yet by nature he was greedy and base. If he learned that someone possessed rare and precious things, he was sure to seek and take them.
entries.literal: Yet by nature he was greedy and base; if he learned that someone possessed rare and precious things, he was sure to seek and take them.

entries.zh: 富商大賈及隴右諸胡子弟，述皆接以恩意，呼之為兒。
entries.en: Great merchants and the sons of the various Hu families west of Long—Shu treated them all with gracious favor and called them his sons.
entries.literal: Great merchants and the sons of the various Hu families west of Long, Shu all treated with gracious favor and called them his sons.

entries.zh: 由是競加饋遺，金寶累積。
entries.en: Thereby they vied in presenting gifts, and gold and jewels piled up.
entries.literal: Thereby they vied in presenting gifts, and gold and jewels piled up.

entries.zh: 後庭曳羅綺者數百，家僮千餘人，皆控良馬，被服金玉。
entries.en: In the rear courtyard several hundred women trailed silk and brocade. More than a thousand household servants all rode fine horses and wore gold and jade.
entries.literal: In the rear courtyard several hundred women trailed silk and brocade; more than a thousand household servants all rode fine horses and wore gold and jade.

entries.zh: 述之寵遇，當時莫與為比。
entries.en: The favor shown to Shu at that time had no equal.
entries.literal: The favor shown to Shu at that time had no equal.

entries.zh: 衍臨下甚踞，事上奸諂。
entries.en: Yan was very overbearing toward those below and fawning and sycophantic toward those above.
entries.literal: Yan was very overbearing toward those below and fawning and sycophantic toward those above.

entries.zh: 晉王愛昵之，宴賜隆厚。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin loved and favored him, bestowing feasts and gifts with great generosity.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin loved and favored him, bestowing feasts and gifts with great generosity.

entries.zh: 遷洪州總管。
entries.en: He was transferred to Area Commander of Hongzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Area Commander of Hongzhou.

entries.zh: 王有奪宗之謀，托衍心腹，遣宇文述以情告之。
entries.en: The prince had a plot to seize the succession and entrusted Yan as a confidant, sending Yu Wenshu to inform him of the matter in full.
entries.literal: The prince had a plot to seize the succession and entrusted Yan as a confidant, sending Yu Wenshu to inform him of the matter in full.

entries.zh: 衍大喜曰：「若所謀事果，自可為皇太子。
entries.en: Yan was greatly pleased and said, "If the matter you plot succeeds, you may naturally become Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Yan was greatly pleased and said, "If the matter you plot succeeds, you may naturally become Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 如其不諧，亦須據淮海，複梁、陳之舊。
entries.en: If it does not succeed, you must still hold the Huai and sea region and restore the old domains of Liang and Chen.
entries.literal: If it does not succeed, you must still hold the Huai and sea region and restore the old domains of Liang and Chen.

entries.zh: 副君酒客，其如我何？」
entries.en: As for a deputy lord and wine companion—what can he do to me?"
entries.literal: As for a deputy lord and wine companion—what can he do to me?"

entries.zh: 王因召衍，陰共計議。
entries.en: The prince thereupon summoned Yan and secretly deliberated with him.
entries.literal: The prince thereupon summoned Yan and secretly deliberated with him.

entries.zh: 又恐人疑無故來往，托以衍妻患癭，王妃蕭氏有術能療之。
entries.en: He also feared that people would suspect their coming and going without cause, and used as a pretext that Yan's wife suffered from goiter and that the princess consort Xiao had a technique that could cure it.
entries.literal: He also feared that people would suspect their coming and going without cause, and used as a pretext that Yan's wife suffered from goiter and that the princess consort Xiao had a technique that could cure it.

entries.zh: 以狀奏高祖，高祖聽衍共妻向江都，往來無度。
entries.en: He memorialized the situation to Emperor Gaozu, and Gaozu permitted Yan to bring his wife to Jiangdu. Their comings and goings knew no limit.
entries.literal: He memorialized the situation to Emperor Gaozu, and Gaozu permitted Yan to bring his wife to Jiangdu; their comings and goings knew no limit.

entries.zh: 衍又詐稱桂州俚反，王乃奏衍行兵討之。
entries.en: Yan also falsely claimed that the Li of Guizhou had rebelled, and the prince then memorialized that Yan should lead troops to suppress them.
entries.literal: Yan also falsely claimed that the Li of Guizhou had rebelled, and the prince then memorialized that Yan should lead troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 由是大修甲仗，陰養士卒。
entries.en: Thereby he greatly repaired armor and weapons and secretly nurtured soldiers.
entries.literal: Thereby he greatly repaired armor and weapons and secretly nurtured soldiers.

entries.zh: 及王入為太子，征授左監門率，轉左宗衛率。
entries.en: When the prince entered the capital as Crown Prince, Yan was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Left Gate Guard, then transferred to Colonel of the Left Palace Guard.
entries.literal: When the prince entered the capital as Crown Prince, Yan was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Left Gate Guard, then transferred to Colonel of the Left Palace Guard.

entries.zh: 高祖于仁壽宮將大漸，太子與楊素矯詔，令衍、宇文述領東宮兵，帖上臺宿衛，門禁並由之。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu at Renshou Palace was about to reach his end, the Crown Prince and Yang Su forged an edict ordering Yan and Yu Wenshu to lead the Eastern Palace troops, post them for night guard at the upper terrace, and place gate control entirely in their hands.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu at Renshou Palace was about to reach his end, the Crown Prince and Yang Su forged an edict ordering Yan and Yu Wenshu to lead the Eastern Palace troops, post them for night guard at the upper terrace, and place gate control entirely in their hands.

entries.zh: 及上崩，漢王起逆，而京師空虛，使衍馳還，總兵居守，
entries.en: When the emperor died, Prince Han raised a rebellion while the capital was empty. Yan was sent to ride back in haste and take overall command to hold the defense.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, the Prince of Han raised a rebellion while the capital was empty; Yan was sent to ride back in haste and take overall command to hold the defense.

entries.zh: 大業元年，拜左武衛大將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Daye, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daye, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 帝幸江都，令衍統左軍，改授光祿大夫。
entries.en: When the emperor visited Jiangdu, he ordered Yan to command the left army and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: When the emperor visited Jiangdu, he ordered Yan to command the left army and transferred him to the post of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 又從討吐谷渾，出金山道，納絳二萬餘戶。
entries.en: He again followed in the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and receiving more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang people.
entries.literal: He again followed in the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and receiving more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang.

entries.zh: 衍能揣上意，阿諛順旨。
entries.en: Yan could gauge the sovereign's intent and fawned upon him, always complying with his wishes.
entries.literal: Yan could gauge the sovereign's intent and fawned upon him, complying with his wishes.

entries.zh: 帝每謂人曰：「唯有郭衍，心與朕同。」
entries.en: The emperor often told others, "Only Guo Yan has a heart in accord with mine."
entries.literal: The emperor often told others, "Only Guo Yan has a heart in accord with mine."

entries.zh: 又嘗勸帝取樂，五日一視事，無得效高祖空自劬勞。
entries.en: He also once urged the emperor to seek pleasure, attend to affairs once every five days, and not imitate Emperor Gaozu in toiling in vain.
entries.literal: He also once urged the emperor to seek pleasure, attend to affairs once every five days, and not imitate Emperor Gaozu in toiling in vain.

entries.zh: 帝從之，益稱其孝順。
entries.en: The emperor followed this advice and praised his filial obedience all the more.
entries.literal: The emperor followed this advice and praised his filial obedience all the more.

entries.zh: 初，新令行，衍封爵從例除。
entries.en: Initially, when the new regulations took effect, Yan's enfeoffment and title were removed according to precedent.
entries.literal: Initially, when the new regulations took effect, Yan's enfeoffment and title were removed according to precedent.

entries.zh: 六年，以恩幸封真定侯。
entries.en: In year six, by grace of favor he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending.
entries.literal: In year six, by grace of favor he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending.

entries.zh: 七年，從往江都，卒。
entries.en: In year seven he followed the emperor to Jiangdu and died there.
entries.literal: In year seven he followed the emperor to Jiangdu and died.

entries.zh: 贈左衛大將軍，賵賜甚厚，諡曰襄。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted the title of General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, given very generous funeral gifts, and granted the posthumous title Xiang.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, funeral gifts were very generous, and his posthumous title was Xiang.

entries.zh: 長子臻，武牙郎將。
entries.en: His eldest son Zhen served as a Martial Tusk Commandant.
entries.literal: His eldest son Zhen was a Martial Tusk Commandant.

entries.zh: 次子嗣本，孝昌縣令。
entries.en: His second son Siben served as Magistrate of Xiaochang County.
entries.literal: His second son Siben was Magistrate of Xiaochang County.

entries.zh: 【論】史臣曰：謇謇匪躬，為臣之高節，和而不同，事君之常道。
entries.en: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Earnest devotion without sparing oneself is the highest integrity of a minister; harmony without conformity is the constant way of serving a ruler.
entries.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Earnest devotion without sparing oneself is the highest integrity of a minister; harmony without conformity is the constant way of serving a ruler.

entries.zh: 宇文述、郭衍以水濟水，如脂如韋，便辟足恭，柔顏取悅。
entries.en: Yu Wenshu and Guo Yan were as water added to water, as pliant as tallow and leather—nimble in bearing and obsequious in deference, soft of countenance to win favor.
entries.literal: Yu Wenshu and Guo Yan added water to water, were like tallow and like leather, nimble in bearing and full in deference, soft of countenance to win favor.

entries.zh: 君所謂可，亦曰可焉，君所謂不，亦曰不焉。
entries.en: What the lord calls acceptable, they too say is acceptable; what the lord calls not, they too say is not.
entries.literal: What the lord calls acceptable, they too say is acceptable; what the lord calls not, they too say is not.

entries.zh: 無所是非，不能輕重，默默苟容，偷安高位，甘素餐之責，受彼己之譏。
entries.en: They had no judgment of right and wrong, could not weigh what mattered, silently tolerated all, stole ease in high position, willingly bore the blame of eating salary without work, and accepted the ridicule of others upon themselves.
entries.literal: They had no judgment of right and wrong, could not weigh what mattered, silently tolerated all, stole ease in high position, willingly bore the blame of eating salary without work, and accepted the ridicule of others upon themselves.

entries.zh: 此固君子所不為，亦丘明之深恥也。
entries.en: This is certainly what a gentleman would not do—and it is also what Zuo Qiuming would have regarded with deep shame.
entries.literal: This is certainly what a gentleman would not do, and it is also what Zuo Qiuming would have regarded with deep shame.

entries.zh: :《禮圖》曰：「建武三十年作明堂，明堂上圓下方，上圓法天，下方法地，十二堂法日辰，九室法九州。
entries.en: The Litu says: "In Jianwu 30, in building the Bright Hall, the Bright Hall is round above and square below — round above follows Heaven, square below follows Earth; twelve halls follow the day-stars, nine chambers follow the Nine Provinces.
entries.literal: The Litu says: "In Jianwu 30, in building the Bright Hall, the Bright Hall is round above and square below — round above follows Heaven, square below follows Earth; twelve halls follow the day-stars, nine chambers follow the Nine Provinces.

entries.zh: 室八牖，八九七十二，法一時之王。
entries.en: Each chamber has eight windows; eight times nine is seventy-two, following the king of one season.
entries.literal: Each chamber has eight windows; eight times nine is seventy-two, following the king of one season.

entries.zh: 室有二戶，二九十八戶，法土王十八日。
entries.en: Each chamber has two doors; two times nine is eighteen doors, following Earth's eighteen days of kingship.
entries.literal: Each chamber has two doors; two times nine is eighteen doors, following Earth's eighteen days of kingship.

entries.zh: 內堂正壇高三尺，土階三等。」
entries.en: The inner hall's central altar is three chi high, with three earthen steps."
entries.literal: The inner hall's central altar is three chi high, with three earthen steps."

entries.zh: 胡伯始注《漢官》雲：「古清廟蓋以茅，今蓋以瓦，瓦下藉茅，以存古制。」
entries.en: Hu Boshi's commentary on the Han guan says: "In antiquity the Pure Temple was thatched with reeds; now it is covered with tiles, with reeds placed beneath the tiles to preserve the ancient institution."
entries.literal: Hu Boshi's commentary on the Hangguan says: "In antiquity the Pure Temple was thatched with reeds; now it is covered with tiles, with reeds placed beneath the tiles to preserve the ancient institution."

entries.zh: 《東京賦》曰：「乃營三宮，布政頒常。
entries.en: The Dongjing Fu says: "Then the three palaces were built, government was dispensed and regular laws proclaimed.
entries.literal: The Dongjing Fu says: "Then the three palaces were built, government was dispensed and regular laws proclaimed.

entries.zh: 複廟重屋，八達九房。
entries.en: Double temples and layered roofs, eight thoroughfares and nine chambers.
entries.literal: Double temples and layered roofs, eight thoroughfares and nine chambers.

entries.zh: 造舟清池，惟水泱泱。」
entries.en: Boats were built on the clear pool, and the waters flowed wide."
entries.literal: Boats were built on the clear pool, and the waters flowed wide."

entries.zh: 薛綜注雲：「複重廇覆，謂屋平覆重棟也。」
entries.en: Xue Zong's commentary says: "Double layered covering means the roof flatly covers with double ridgepoles."
entries.literal: Xue Zong's commentary says: "Double layered covering means the roof flatly covers with double ridgepoles."

entries.zh: 《續漢書·祭祀志》雲：「明帝永平二年，祀五帝於明堂，五帝坐各處其方，黃帝在未，皆如南郊之位。
entries.en: The Xu Hanshu · Jisi Zhi says: "In Yongping 2, Emperor Ming sacrificed to the Five Emperors in the Bright Hall; the Five Emperors each sat in their direction, the Yellow Emperor at wei — all as at the southern suburb positions.
entries.literal: The Xu Hanshu · Jisi Zhi says: "In Yongping 2, Emperor Ming sacrificed to the Five Emperors in the Bright Hall; the Five Emperors each sat in their direction, the Yellow Emperor at wei — all as at the southern suburb positions.

entries.zh: 光武位在青帝之南，少退西面，各一犢，奏樂如南郊。」
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu's seat was south of the Green Emperor, slightly withdrawn to the west; each had one calf, and music was performed as at the southern suburb."
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu's seat was south of the Green Emperor, slightly withdrawn to the west; each had one calf, and music was performed as at the southern suburb."

entries.zh: 臣愷按《詩》雲，《我將》祀文王於明堂，「我將我享，維牛維羊」。
entries.en: Your subject Kai cites the Shi, which says in "Wo Jiang" that King Wen was sacrificed to in the Bright Hall: "I will offer, I will enjoy — only oxen and sheep."
entries.literal: Your subject Kai cites the Shi, which says in "Wo Jiang" that King Wen was sacrificed to in the Bright Hall: "I will offer, I will enjoy — only oxen and sheep."

entries.zh: 據此則備太牢之祭。
entries.en: According to this, the complete tai lao sacrifice was prepared.
entries.literal: According to this, the complete tai lao sacrifice was prepared.

entries.zh: 今雲一犢，恐與古殊。
entries.en: Now it says one calf — I fear this differs from antiquity.
entries.literal: Now it says one calf — I fear this differs from antiquity.

entries.zh: 自晉以前，未有鶉尾，其圓牆璧水，一依本圖。
entries.en: Before the Jin, there was no Chunwei; the round wall and jade-ring water all followed the original diagram.
entries.literal: Before the Jin, there was no Chunwei; the round wall and jade-ring water all followed the original diagram.

entries.zh: 《晉起居注》裴頠議曰：「尊祖配天，其義明著，廟宇之制，理據未分。
entries.en: The Jin Qiju Zhu: Pei Yi argued: "Honoring the ancestor as companion to Heaven — its meaning is clear and evident; but the institution of the temple's structure, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.
entries.literal: The Jin Qiju Zhu: Pei Yi argued: "Honoring the ancestor as companion to Heaven — its meaning is clear and evident; but the institution of the temple's structure, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.

entries.zh: 直可為一殿，以崇嚴祀，其餘雜碎，一皆除之。」
