entries.en: One may simply make one hall to elevate solemn sacrifice; all other miscellaneous elements should be entirely removed."
entries.literal: One may simply make one hall to elevate solemn sacrifice; all other miscellaneous elements should be entirely removed."

entries.zh: 臣愷案，天垂象，聖人則之。
entries.en: Your subject Kai observes that Heaven displays signs, and the sage follows them.
entries.literal: Your subject Kai observes that Heaven displays signs, and the sage follows them.

entries.zh: 辟雍之星，既有圖狀，晉堂方構，不合天文。
entries.en: The star of the Imperial Academy already had a diagram; the Jin hall was built square, not conforming to celestial patterns.
entries.literal: The star of the Imperial Academy already had a diagram; the Jin hall was built square, not conforming to celestial patterns.

entries.zh: 既闕重樓，又無璧水，空堂乖五室之義，直殿違九階之文。
entries.en: It lacked layered towers, and also had no jade-ring water; an empty hall violated the meaning of five chambers, and a straight hall violated the text of nine steps.
entries.literal: It lacked layered towers, and also had no jade-ring water; an empty hall violated the meaning of five chambers, and a straight hall violated the text of nine steps.

entries.zh: 非古欺天，一何過甚！
entries.en: Deviating from antiquity and deceiving Heaven — how excessive!
entries.literal: Deviating from antiquity and deceiving Heaven — how excessive!

entries.zh: 後魏于北台城南造圓牆，在璧水外，門在水內迥立，不與牆相連。
entries.en: Later Wei built a round wall south of Beitai city, outside the jade-ring water; the gates stood separately inside the water, not connected to the wall.
entries.literal: Later Wei built a round wall south of Beitai city, outside the jade-ring water; the gates stood separately inside the water, not connected to the wall.

entries.zh: 其堂上九室，三三相重，不依古制，室間通巷，違舛處多。
entries.en: Above the hall were nine chambers, three by three overlapping; it did not follow the ancient institution, and passages ran between chambers — there were many violations.
entries.literal: Above the hall were nine chambers, three by three overlapping; it did not follow the ancient institution, and passages ran between chambers — there were many violations.

entries.zh: 其室皆用墼累，極成褊陋。
entries.en: All its chambers were built up with bricks, becoming extremely cramped and crude.
entries.literal: All its chambers were built up with bricks, becoming extremely cramped and crude.

entries.zh: 後魏《樂志》曰：「孝昌二年立明堂，議者或言九室，或言五室，詔斷從五室。
entries.en: The Later Wei Yue Zhi says: "In Xiaochang 2, the Bright Hall was established; debaters said either nine chambers or five chambers; an edict decided on five chambers.
entries.literal: The Later Wei Yue Zhi says: "In Xiaochang 2, the Bright Hall was established; debaters said either nine chambers or five chambers; an edict decided on five chambers.

entries.zh: 後元叉執政，複改為九室，遭亂不成。」
entries.en: Later when Yuan Cha held power, it was changed back to nine chambers, but chaos prevented completion."
entries.literal: Later when Yuan Cha held power, it was changed back to nine chambers, but chaos prevented completion."

entries.zh: 《宋起居注》曰：「孝武帝大明五年立明堂，其牆宇規範，擬則太廟，唯十二間，以應期數。
entries.en: The Song Qiju Zhu says: "In Daming 5, Emperor Xiaowu established the Bright Hall; its walls and structure were modeled on the Grand Temple, with only twelve bays to correspond to the cycle of numbers.
entries.literal: The Song Qiju Zhu says: "In Daming 5, Emperor Xiaowu established the Bright Hall; its walls and structure were modeled on the Grand Temple, with only twelve bays to correspond to the cycle of numbers.

entries.zh: 依漢《汶上圖儀》，設五帝位。
entries.en: Following the Han Wenshang Tuyi, seats for the Five Emperors were set up.
entries.literal: Following the Han Wenshang Tuyi, seats for the Five Emperors were set up.

entries.zh: 太祖文皇帝對饗，鼎俎簠簋，一依廟禮。」
entries.en: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen was paired in the feast; tripods, stands, and grain vessels all followed temple ritual."
entries.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen was paired in the feast; tripods, stands, and grain vessels all followed temple ritual."

entries.zh: 梁武即位之後，移宋時太極殿以為明堂。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu of Liang succeeded to the throne, he moved the Song-era Hall of Supreme Ultimate to serve as the Bright Hall.
entries.literal: After Emperor Wu of Liang succeeded to the throne, he moved the Song-era Hall of Supreme Ultimate to serve as the Bright Hall.

entries.zh: 無室，十二間。
entries.en: It had no chambers, only twelve bays.
entries.literal: It had no chambers, only twelve bays.

entries.zh: 《禮疑議》雲：「祭用純漆俎瓦樽，文於郊，質於廟。
entries.en: The Li Yiyi says: "In sacrifice, pure lacquer stands and earthenware goblets were used — refined at the suburb, plain at the temple.
entries.literal: The Li Yiyi says: "In sacrifice, pure lacquer stands and earthenware goblets were used — refined at the suburb, plain at the temple.

entries.zh: 止一獻，用清酒。」
entries.en: Only one presentation, using clear wine."
entries.literal: Only one presentation, using clear wine."

entries.zh: 平陳之後，臣得目觀，遂量步數，記其尺丈。
entries.en: After the pacification of Chen, your subject was able to see it with his own eyes, and thereupon measured the paces and recorded its dimensions in chi and zhang.
entries.literal: After the pacification of Chen, your subject was able to see it with his own eyes, and thereupon measured the paces and recorded its dimensions in chi and zhang.

entries.zh: 猶見基內有焚燒殘柱，毀斫之餘，入地一丈，儼然如舊。
entries.en: One could still see within the foundation burned remnant pillars; of what remained after destruction and cutting, one zhang entered the ground, standing as if still intact.
entries.literal: One could still see within the foundation burned remnant pillars; of what remained after destruction and cutting, one zhang entered the ground, standing as if still intact.

entries.zh: 柱下以樟木為跗，長丈餘，闊四尺許，兩兩相並。
entries.en: Beneath the pillars camphor wood was used for bases, more than one zhang long and about four chi wide, placed two by two side by side.
entries.literal: Beneath the pillars camphor wood was used for bases, more than one zhang long and about four chi wide, placed two by two side by side.

entries.zh: 瓦安數重。
entries.en: Tiles were placed in several layers.
entries.literal: Tiles were placed in several layers.

entries.zh: 宮城處所，乃在郭內。
entries.en: The palace city's location was inside the outer wall.
entries.literal: The palace city's location was inside the outer wall.

entries.zh: 雖湫隘卑陋，未合規摹，祖宗之靈，得崇嚴祀。
entries.en: Although cramped, low, and crude, not conforming to the standard design, the spirits of the ancestors could still receive elevated and solemn sacrifice.
entries.literal: Although cramped, low, and crude, not conforming to the standard design, the spirits of the ancestors could still receive elevated and solemn sacrifice.

entries.zh: 周、齊二代，闕而不修，大饗之典，於焉靡托。
entries.en: Under the Zhou and Qi dynasties, it was left unrepaired; the great feast ritual had no place to rely upon.
entries.literal: Under the Zhou and Qi dynasties, it was left unrepaired; the great feast ritual had no place to rely upon.

entries.zh: 宇文愷，字安樂，杞國公忻之弟也。
entries.en: Yu Wenkai, whose courtesy name was Anle, was the younger brother of the Duke of Qi, Xin.
entries.literal: Yu Wenkai, courtesy name Anle, was the younger brother of Duke of Qi Xin.

entries.zh: 在周，以功臣子，年三歲，賜爵雙泉伯，七歲，進封安平郡公，邑二千戶。
entries.en: During the Northern Zhou, as the son of a meritorious minister, he received the title Baron of Shuangquan at age three and was promoted to Duke of Anping Commandery at age seven, with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: Under the Zhou, as the son of a meritorious minister, at age three he was granted the title Baron of Shuangquan; at age seven he was advanced to Duke of Anping Commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 愷少有器局。
entries.en: From an early age, Yu Wenkai showed great talent and breadth of vision.
entries.literal: Kai from youth had capacity and breadth of mind.

entries.zh: 家世武將，諸兄並以弓馬自達，愷獨好學，博覽書記，解屬文，多伎藝，號為名父公子。
entries.en: His family had long been a line of military men, and all his elder brothers made their way through archery and horsemanship. Yu Wenkai alone loved learning, read widely in books and records, was skilled at literary composition, and mastered many crafts. He was known as a son worthy of his distinguished father.
entries.literal: His family for generations were military generals; all his elder brothers achieved advancement through bow and horse, but Kai alone loved learning, broadly read books and records, understood literary composition, and had many skills and arts, and was called a son of a famous father.

entries.zh: 初為千牛，累遷禦正中大夫、儀同三司。
entries.en: He began as a Thousand-Ox guard and rose through successive appointments to Grand Master of the Center for Imperial Correction and Yitong Third Rank.
entries.literal: At first he served as Thousand-Ox [guard], and was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Director of the Imperial Clan and Yitong Third Rank.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，加上開府中大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen was still Chancellor, Yu Wenkai was additionally granted Grand Master of the Center with Superior Opening of the Office.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was Chancellor, he was additionally appointed Supervising Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 及踐阼，誅宇文氏，愷初亦在殺中，以其與周本別，兄忻有功于國，使人馳赦之，僅而得免。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he executed the Yuwen clan. Yu Wenkai was initially marked for death as well, but because his branch of the family was distinct from the Zhou royal house and his elder brother Xin had served the state with merit, the emperor sent a messenger posthaste to pardon him, and he barely escaped with his life.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne, the Yuwen clan was executed; Kai at first was also among those to be killed, but because his branch was separate from the Zhou royal house and his elder brother Xin had rendered service to the state, the emperor sent a messenger racing to pardon him, and he barely escaped.

entries.zh: 後拜營宗廟副監、太子左庶子。
entries.en: He was later appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Ancestral Temple and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Ancestral Temple and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 廟成，別封甑山縣公，邑千戶。
entries.en: When the temple was completed, he received a separate enfeoffment as Duke of Zengshan County, with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: When the temple was completed, he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Zengshan County, with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 及遷都，上以愷有巧思，詔領營新都副監。
entries.en: When the capital was relocated, the emperor, recognizing Yu Wenkai's ingenious mind, appointed him Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the New Capital.
entries.literal: When the capital was moved, the emperor, because Kai had ingenious ideas, ordered him to take charge as Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the New Capital.

entries.zh: 高熲雖總大綱，凡所規畫，皆出於愷。
entries.en: Although Gao Jiong held overall authority, every plan and design came from Yu Wenkai.
entries.literal: Although Gao Jiong held overall authority, all planning and design came from Kai.

entries.zh: 後決渭水達河，以通運漕，詔愷總督其事。
entries.en: Later, when the Wei River was cut through to the Yellow River to open a transport canal, the emperor put Yu Wenkai in overall charge of the project.
entries.literal: Later the Wei River was cut through to reach the Yellow River to open transport and grain shipment; the emperor ordered Kai to supervise the whole affair.

entries.zh: 後拜萊州刺史，甚有能名。
entries.en: He was later appointed Governor of Laizhou, where he earned a strong reputation for competence.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Laizhou and gained a great reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 兄忻被誅，除名於家，久不得調。
entries.en: After his elder brother Xin was executed, Yu Wenkai was struck from the family register and went for a long time without a new appointment.
entries.literal: When his elder brother Xin was executed, he was struck from the family register and for a long time could not be reassigned.

entries.zh: 會朝廷以魯班故道久絕不行，令愷修復之。
entries.en: At that time the court found that the old Lu Ban canal route had long been abandoned and impassable, and ordered Yu Wenkai to restore it.
entries.literal: It happened that the court, because the old Lu Ban route had long been abandoned and impassable, ordered Kai to restore it.

entries.zh: 既而上建仁壽宮，訪可任者，右僕射楊素言愷有巧思，上然之，於是檢校將作大匠。
entries.en: Soon afterward the emperor began building Renshou Palace and sought someone capable of overseeing it. Right Vice Director Yang Su recommended Yu Wenkai for his ingenious mind, and the emperor agreed, appointing him Acting Chief of Palace Construction.
entries.literal: Soon afterward the emperor built Renshou Palace and sought someone fit for the task; Right Vice Director Yang Su said Kai had ingenious ideas, and the emperor agreed; thereupon he was appointed Acting Chief of Palace Construction.

entries.zh: 歲餘，拜仁壽宮監，授儀同三司，尋為將作少監。
entries.en: After more than a year he was made Supervisor of Renshou Palace and granted Yitong Third Rank, and soon afterward became Deputy Chief of Palace Construction.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Supervisor of Renshou Palace, granted Yitong Third Rank, and soon became Deputy Chief of Palace Construction.

entries.zh: 文獻皇后崩，愷與楊素營山陵事，上善之，複爵安平郡公，邑千戶。
entries.en: When Empress Wenxian died, Yu Wenkai and Yang Su oversaw the construction of her tomb. The emperor was pleased and restored his title as Duke of Anping Commandery, with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Empress Wenxian died, Kai together with Yang Su undertook the construction of the imperial tomb; the emperor approved of this and restored his title as Duke of Anping Commandery, with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，遷都洛陽，以愷為營東都副監，尋遷將作大匠。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang took the throne and moved the capital to Luoyang, Yu Wenkai was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Eastern Capital and soon promoted to Chief of Palace Construction.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne and moved the capital to Luoyang, Kai was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Eastern Capital, and soon was promoted to Chief of Palace Construction.

entries.zh: 愷揣帝心在宏侈，於是東京制度窮極壯麗。
entries.en: Reading the emperor's taste for grandeur and extravagance, Yu Wenkai designed the Eastern Capital to the utmost in scale and splendor.
entries.literal: Kai surmised that the emperor's heart lay in grandeur and extravagance, and so the institutions of the Eastern Capital were pushed to the utmost in magnificence.

entries.zh: 帝大悅之，進位開府，拜工部尚書。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to Kaifu rank, and appointed him Minister of Works.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to the rank of Kaifu, and appointed him Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 及長城之役，詔愷規度之。
entries.en: When work on the Great Wall began, the emperor ordered Yu Wenkai to plan and survey it.
entries.literal: When the Great Wall project was undertaken, the emperor ordered Kai to plan and measure it.

entries.zh: 時帝北巡，欲誇戎狄，令愷為大帳，其下坐數千人。
entries.en: When the emperor toured the north and wished to impress the frontier peoples, he had Yu Wenkai build a great tent large enough to seat several thousand people beneath it.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor toured the north and wished to impress the barbarians; he ordered Kai to make a great tent under which several thousand people could sit.

entries.zh: 帝大悅，賜物千段。
entries.en: The emperor was delighted and rewarded him with one thousand bolts of goods.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed one thousand bolts of goods.

entries.zh: 又造觀風行殿，上容侍衛者數百人，離合為之，下施輪軸，推移倏忽，有若神功。
entries.en: He also built the Wind-Viewing Mobile Hall, whose upper level could hold several hundred attendants and guards. Assembled in detachable sections and mounted on wheels and axles below, it could be moved in an instant, as if by supernatural craft.
entries.literal: He also built the Wind-Viewing Mobile Hall, which could hold several hundred attendants and guards on its upper level; it was made in sections that could be joined and separated, with wheels and axles beneath, so that it could be moved in an instant, as if by divine power.

entries.zh: 戎狄見之，莫不驚駭。
entries.en: The frontier peoples who saw it were all struck with astonishment.
entries.literal: When the barbarians saw it, none failed to be astonished and awed.

entries.zh: 帝彌悅焉，前後賞賚，不可勝紀。
entries.en: The emperor was still more pleased, and the rewards he received before and after were beyond counting.
entries.literal: The emperor was all the more pleased; rewards before and after were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 陸彥師，字雲房，魏郡臨漳人。
entries.en: Lu Yanshi, styled Yunfang, was a native of Linzhang in Wei commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Yanshi, styled Yunfang, was a native of Linzhang in Wei commandery.

entries.zh: 祖希道，魏定州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Xidao had been governor of Dingzhou under Wei.
entries.literal: His grandfather Xidao was governor of Dingzhou under Wei.

entries.zh: 父子彰，中書監。
entries.en: His father Zizhang had served as Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His father Zizhang was Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 彥師少有行檢，為邦族所稱。
entries.en: From youth Yanshi conducted himself with propriety and was praised throughout his clan and neighborhood.
entries.literal: Yanshi from youth had proper conduct and was praised by his clan and neighbors.

entries.zh: 長而好學，解屬文。
entries.en: As he matured he took to learning and became adept at literary composition.
entries.literal: When grown he loved learning and was skilled in literary composition.

entries.zh: 魏襄城王元旭引為參軍事。
entries.en: Yuan Xu, Prince of Xiangcheng under Wei, took him on as a staff officer.
entries.literal: The Prince of Xiangcheng of Wei, Yuan Xu, brought him in as a staff officer.

entries.zh: 以父艱去職，哀毀殆不勝喪。
entries.en: When his father died he left office; his grief was so extreme that he nearly perished in mourning.
entries.literal: On his father's death he left office; his grief and emaciation nearly overwhelmed the mourning rites.

entries.zh: 與兄卬廬于墓次，負土成墳。
entries.en: He and his elder brother Ang lived in a mourning hut beside the tomb, carrying earth by hand to raise the burial mound.
entries.literal: With his elder brother Ang he dwelt in a hut by the grave and carried earth to build the mound.

entries.zh: 公卿重之，多就墓側存問，晦朔之際，車馬不絕。
entries.en: High officials held him in esteem; many came to the graveside to pay their respects, and on the first and fifteenth of each month the stream of carriages never stopped.
entries.literal: The high officials esteemed him; many came to the grave to inquire after him, and at the new and full moon carriages and horses never ceased.

entries.zh: 齊文宣聞而嘉歎，旌表其閭，號其所住為孝終裡。
entries.en: When Emperor Wenxuan of Qi heard of this he expressed his admiration, erected an honorific marker at his lane, and named his neighborhood Filial Mourning Lane.
entries.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi heard and praised him, marked out his lane with an honorific tablet, and named his dwelling-place Filial Mourning Lane.

entries.zh: 中書令河間邢邵表薦之，未報，彭城王浟為司州牧，召補主簿。
entries.en: Xing Shao of Hejian, Director of the Secretariat, recommended him by memorial, but before any response arrived Chou, Prince of Pengcheng and governor of Sizhou, summoned him to serve as chief clerk.
entries.literal: Xing Shao of Hejian, Director of the Secretariat, submitted a memorial recommending him, but before a reply came the Prince of Pengcheng, Chou, as governor of Sizhou, summoned him to fill the post of chief clerk.

entries.zh: 後曆中外府東閣祭酒。
entries.en: He later held the post of Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion in both the central and outer administrations.
entries.literal: Later he served in succession as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion in the central and outer offices.

entries.zh: 兄卬當襲父始平侯，以彥師昆弟中最幼，表讓封焉。
entries.en: His brother Ang was due to inherit their father's marquisate of Shiping; because Yanshi was the youngest brother, Ang petitioned to yield the fief to him.
entries.literal: His brother Ang was to inherit their father's marquisate of Shiping; because Yanshi was the youngest among the brothers, Ang submitted a memorial offering him the fief.

entries.zh: 彥師固辭而止。
entries.en: Yanshi firmly refused, and the matter was dropped.
entries.literal: Yanshi firmly declined and the matter stopped.

entries.zh: 時稱友悌孝義，總萃一門。
entries.en: The age praised their brotherly devotion and filial righteousness, virtues that seemed to concentrate in a single family.
entries.literal: At the time they were praised for brotherly affection and filial righteousness, all gathered in one household.

entries.zh: 遷中書舍人，尋轉通直散騎侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat and soon after transferred to Gentleman of the Palace in Regular Attendance.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat, and soon transferred to Gentleman of the Palace in Regular Attendance.

entries.zh: 每陳使至，必令高選主客，彥師所接對者，前後六輩。
entries.en: Whenever envoys from Chen arrived, the court always selected the most distinguished men to receive them — Yanshi handled such duties for six missions in succession.
entries.literal: Whenever Chen envoys arrived, the highest-ranking hosts were always chosen; those Yanshi received numbered six missions in all.

entries.zh: 曆中書黃門侍郎，以不阿宦者，遇讒，出為中山太守，有惠政。
entries.en: He served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate at the Secretariat; because he refused to curry favor with eunuchs he was slandered and sent out as governor of Zhongshan, where his rule was marked by kindness.
entries.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate at the Secretariat; because he would not flatter eunuchs he met with slander and was sent out as governor of Zhongshan, where he had benevolent administration.

entries.zh: 數年，徵為吏部郎中。
entries.en: Several years later he was recalled to serve as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: After several years he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 周武平齊，授載師下大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Carriage Masters.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Carriage Masters.

entries.zh: 宣帝時，轉少納言，賜爵臨水縣男，奉使幽、薊。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuan he became Junior Remonstrator, was enfeoffed as Baron of Linshui county, and was dispatched on a mission to You and Ji.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Xuan he was transferred to Junior Remonstrator, enfeoffed as Baron of Linshui county, and sent on mission to You and Ji.

entries.zh: 俄而高祖為丞相，彥師遇疾，請假還鄴。
entries.en: Before long Gaozu became Chancellor; Yanshi fell ill and requested leave to return to Ye.
entries.literal: Soon afterward Gaozu became Chancellor; Yanshi fell ill and asked leave to return to Ye.

entries.zh: 尉迥將為亂，彥師微知之，遂委妻子，潛歸長安。
entries.en: When Wei Jiong was preparing to rebel, Yanshi had some inkling of it; he abandoned wife and children and stole back to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Wei Jiong was about to rebel; Yanshi had a slight foreknowledge of it, so he left wife and children and secretly returned to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉之，授內史下大夫，拜上儀同。
entries.en: Gaozu praised him, appointed him Grand Master of the Palace in the Secretariat, and granted him the rank of Senior Yitong.
entries.literal: Gaozu commended him, appointed him Grand Master of the Palace in the Secretariat, and bestowed the rank of Senior Yitong.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，拜尚書左丞，進爵為子。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and raised in rank to Viscount.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and advanced in rank to Viscount.

entries.zh: 彥師素多病，未幾，以務劇疾動，乞解所職，有詔聽以本官就第。
entries.en: Yanshi had long been in poor health; before long the strain of office aggravated his illness, and he petitioned to resign; an edict allowed him to retain his title and retire home.
entries.literal: Yanshi had long been prone to illness; before long, because the duties were heavy his illness worsened, and he begged to be released from office; an edict permitted him to keep his title and retire to his residence.

entries.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部侍郎。
entries.en: A year later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 隋承周制，官無清濁，彥師在職，凡所任人，頗甄別於士庶，論者美之。
entries.en: The Sui followed Zhou institutions, in which offices carried no distinction of pure versus impure rank; in office Yanshi carefully distinguished gentry from commoners in every appointment he made, and commentators praised him for it.
entries.literal: Sui followed Zhou institutions, and offices had no distinction of pure and impure rank; while Yanshi held office, everyone he appointed was carefully distinguished between gentry and commoners, and commentators praised this.

entries.zh: 後復以病出為汾州刺史，卒官。
entries.en: Later, again on account of illness, he was sent out as governor of Fenzhou, where he died in office.
entries.literal: Later, again because of illness, he was sent out as governor of Fenzhou and died in office.

entries.zh: 紐回，字孝政，河東安邑人也。
entries.en: Niu Hui, whose courtesy name was Xiaozheng, came from Anyi in Hedong.
entries.literal: Niu Hui, courtesy name Xiaozheng, was a native of Anyi in Hedong.

entries.zh: 性至孝，周武成中，父母喪，廬於墓側，負土成墳。
entries.en: He was utterly filial. During the Wucheng era of Zhou, when his parents died, he lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.
entries.literal: He was utterly filial. During the Wucheng era of Zhou, when his parents died, he lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.

entries.zh: 廬前生麻一株，高丈許，圍之合拱，枝葉鬱茂，冬夏恆青。
entries.en: Before his hut a hemp plant grew to about one zhang in height, its trunk spanning a full arm's grasp, its foliage lush—it stayed green winter and summer.
entries.literal: Before his hut a hemp plant grew to about one zhang in height, its trunk spanning a full arm's grasp, its foliage lush—it stayed green winter and summer.

entries.zh: 有烏棲其上，回舉聲哭，烏即悲鳴，時人異之。
entries.en: A crow perched on it. When Hui cried aloud the crow at once answered with mournful cries, and people found it extraordinary.
entries.literal: A crow perched on it. When Hui cried aloud the crow at once answered with mournful cries, and people found it extraordinary.

entries.zh: 周武帝表其閭，擢授甘棠令。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou honored his neighborhood and promoted him to Magistrate of Gantang.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou honored his neighborhood and promoted him to Magistrate of Gantang.

entries.zh: 開皇初卒。
entries.en: He died early in the Kaihuang era.
entries.literal: He died early in the Kaihuang era.

entries.zh: 書成而絕，時年四十二。
entries.en: When the letter was finished he died; he was forty-two years old.
entries.literal: When the letter was finished he died; he was forty-two years old.

entries.zh: 有司以聞，高祖為之屑涕，降使齎冊書弔祭曰：「皇帝諮故考功侍郎薛濬：於戲！
entries.en: The authorities reported it; Gaozu wept for him and sent an envoy bearing a patent of condolence that read: "The Emperor addresses the late Vice Director of Evaluations Xue Jun: Alas!
entries.literal: The authorities reported it; Gaozu shed tears for him and sent an envoy bearing a patent of condolence and sacrifice, saying: "The Emperor addresses the late Vice Director of Evaluations Xue Jun: Alas!

entries.zh: 惟爾操履貞和，器業詳敏，允膺列宿，勤謇克彰。
entries.en: Your conduct was pure and harmonious, your talent and achievement refined and keen; you truly matched the stars in their courses; diligence and integrity shone forth in you.
entries.literal: You alone had conduct that was pure and harmonious, talent and achievement detailed and keen, truly matching the arrayed stars; diligence and integrity were fully displayed.

entries.zh: 及遘私艱，奄從毀滅。
entries.en: When you met with private bereavement, you were suddenly consumed by grief.
entries.literal: When you met private bereavement, suddenly you followed destruction.

entries.zh: 嘉爾誠孝，感於朕懷，奠酹有加，抑惟朝典。
entries.en: I praise your sincere filial devotion, which moves my heart; the offerings I send exceed the usual measure, yet this too accords with court precedent.
entries.literal: I praise your sincere filial piety, moved in my breast; libations and offerings are increased, yet this also accords with court precedent.

entries.zh: 故遣使人，指申往命，魂而有靈，歆茲榮渥。
entries.en: Therefore I send an envoy to convey this charge; if your soul has awareness, receive this honored grace.
entries.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to convey this former command; if your soul has awareness, receive this honored grace.

entries.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！」
entries.en: Alas, how mournful!"
entries.literal: Alas, how mournful!"

entries.zh: 濬性清儉，死之日，家無遺資。
entries.en: Jun was by nature pure and frugal; when he died his household had nothing left behind.
entries.literal: Jun's nature was pure and frugal; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth.

entries.zh: 濬初為童兒時，與宗中諸兒遊戲於澗濱。
entries.en: When Jun was a boy he played with the other children of the clan beside a stream.
entries.literal: When Jun was first a child, he played with the boys of the clan by a stream bank.

entries.zh: 見一黃蛇有角及足，召群兒共視，了無見者。
entries.en: He saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet and called the other boys to look, but none of them could see it.
entries.literal: He saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet, called the boys to look together, but none saw it at all.

entries.zh: 濬以為不祥，歸大憂悴。
entries.en: Jun took this as an ill omen and returned home deeply troubled and haggard.
entries.literal: Jun took it as ill omen and returned home in great grief and emaciation.

entries.zh: 母逼而問之，濬以實對。
entries.en: His mother pressed him until he told her; Jun answered truthfully.
entries.literal: His mother pressed him to ask; Jun answered with the truth.

entries.zh: 時有胡僧詣宅乞食，濬母怖而告之，僧曰：「此乃兒之吉應。
entries.en: A foreign monk came to the house to beg food; Jun's mother, frightened, told him what had happened; the monk said: "This is an auspicious sign for your son.
entries.literal: At that time a foreign monk came to the house to beg food; Jun's mother, in fear, told him; the monk said: "This is the boy's auspicious response.

entries.zh: 且是兒也，早有名位，然壽不過六七耳。」
entries.en: Moreover, this boy will win fame and office early in life, yet his years will not exceed six times seven (forty-two)."
entries.literal: Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed six times seven (forty-two)."

entries.zh: 言終而出，忽然不見，時咸異之。
entries.en: When he had finished speaking he departed and suddenly vanished; everyone at the time found it extraordinary.
entries.literal: When he finished speaking he went out and suddenly vanished; at the time all regarded it as strange.

entries.zh: 既而終於四十二，六七之言，於是驗矣。
entries.en: He later died at forty-two, and the monk's words about six times seven were thus fulfilled.
entries.literal: Later he died at forty-two; the words 'six times seven' were thus fulfilled.

entries.zh: 子乾福，武安郡司倉書佐。
entries.en: His son Qianfu served as a clerk in the granary office of Wu'an commandery.
entries.literal: His son Qianfu was a clerk in the granary office of Wu'an commandery.

entries.zh: 田德懋，觀國公仁恭之子也。
entries.en: Tian Demao was a son of Rengong, Duke of Guanguo.
entries.literal: Tian Demao was a son of Duke of Guanguo Rengong.

entries.zh: 少以孝友著名。
entries.en: From youth he was renowned for filial devotion and brotherly affection.
entries.literal: From youth he was famed for filial piety and brotherly affection.

entries.zh: 開皇初，以父軍功賜爵平原郡公，授太子千牛備身。
entries.en: At the start of the Kaihuang era, on account of his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan commandery and appointed Attendant of the Thousand Oxen for the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, on account of his father's military merit he was granted the title Duke of Pingyuan commandery and appointed Attendant of the Thousand Oxen for the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 丁父艱，哀毀骨立，廬於墓側，負土成墳。
entries.en: When his father died his grief wore him to skin and bone; he lived in a mourning hut beside the tomb and carried earth by hand to raise the burial mound.
entries.literal: On his father's death his grief and emaciation left him skin and bone; he dwelt in a hut beside the grave and carried earth to build the mound.

entries.zh: 上聞而嘉之，遣員外散騎侍郎元志就吊焉。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of this he expressed his approval and sent Yuan Zhi, Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry in Extraordinary Service, to offer condolences.
entries.literal: The emperor heard and commended him, sending Yuan Zhi, Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry in Extraordinary Service, to offer condolences.

entries.zh: 復降璽書曰：「皇帝謝田德懋。
entries.en: He also sent an imperial letter: "The Emperor addresses Tian Demao.
entries.literal: He also issued an imperial letter saying: "The Emperor thanks Tian Demao.

entries.zh: 知在窮疾，哀毀過禮，倚廬墓所，負土成墳。
entries.en: We know you are in deep affliction, that your grief exceeds the proper measure of mourning, that you dwell in a hut at the graveside and have built the mound with your own hands.
entries.literal: Knowing you are in extreme affliction, your grief and emaciation exceed the rites, you dwell in a hut at the grave and carry earth to build the mound.

entries.zh: 朕孝理天下，思弘名教，復與汝通家，情義素重，有聞孝感，嘉歎兼深。
entries.en: I govern the realm through filial principle and seek to spread moral teaching; our families are moreover joined by marriage and our bond has always been close — hearing of your filial devotion, my admiration and compassion are profound.
entries.literal: I govern the realm through filial principle and wish to spread the teaching of renown; moreover our families are joined by marriage and our affection has long been deep — hearing of your filial response, my praise and sighs are alike profound.

entries.zh: 春日暄和，氣力何似？
entries.en: The spring days are mild — how is your strength holding up?
entries.literal: The spring days are warm and mild — how is your strength?

entries.zh: 宜自抑割，以禮自存也。」
entries.en: You should restrain your grief and preserve yourself according to the rites."
entries.literal: You should restrain yourself and preserve yourself according to the rites."

entries.zh: 並賜縑二百匹，米百石。
entries.en: He also bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and a hundred piculs of grain.
entries.literal: He also bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and a hundred piculs of grain.

entries.zh: 復下詔表其門閭。
entries.en: An edict was also issued to honor his household with a public commendation.
entries.literal: He further issued an edict marking out his gate and lane.

entries.zh: 後曆太子舍人、義州司馬。
entries.en: He later served as Attendant of the Crown Prince and as Administrator of Yizhou.
entries.literal: Later he served in succession as Attendant of the Crown Prince and as Administrator of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 大業中，為給事郎、尚書駕部郎，卒官。
entries.en: During the Daye era he served as Gentleman of the Palace Gate and as Director of the Carriage Office in the Secretariat, and died in office.
entries.literal: During the Daye era he served as Gentleman of the Palace Gate and as Director of the Carriage Office in the Secretariat, and died in office.

entries.zh: 王頒，字景彥，太原祁人也。
entries.en: Wang Ban, whose courtesy name was Jingyan, came from Qi in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Wang Ban, courtesy name Jingyan, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 祖神念，梁左衛將軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Shennian served as Left Guard General of Liang.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shennian was Left Guard General of Liang.

entries.zh: 父僧辯，太尉。
entries.en: His father Sengbian held the rank of Grand Commander.
entries.literal: His father Sengbian was Grand Commander.

entries.zh: 頒少俶儻，有文武幹局。
entries.en: As a youth Ban was spirited and bold, possessing both literary and military talent.
entries.literal: Ban in youth was bold and unrestrained, with civil and military capacity.

entries.zh: 其父平侯景，留頒質於荊州，遇元帝為周師所陷，頒因入關。
entries.en: His father subdued Hou Jing and left Ban as a hostage in Jingzhou; when Emperor Yuan was overrun by Zhou armies, Ban crossed into the Guanzhong region.
entries.literal: When his father pacified Hou Jing, he left Ban as a hostage in Jingzhou; when Emperor Yuan was overrun by Zhou forces, Ban thereupon entered the passes.

entries.zh: 聞其父為陳武帝所殺，號慟而絕，食頃乃蘇，哭泣不絕聲，毀瘠骨立。
entries.en: When he heard his father had been killed by Emperor Wu of Chen, he cried out and collapsed; after the space of a meal he revived, wept without stopping, and wasted away until only bone remained.
entries.literal: Hearing his father was killed by Emperor Wu of Chen, he wailed and fainted; after the time of a meal he revived, weeping without cease, wasting away until only bone remained.

entries.zh: 至服闋，常布衣蔬食，藉槁而臥。
entries.en: When the mourning period ended, he habitually wore plain cloth and ate simple food, sleeping on straw.
entries.literal: When the mourning period ended, he constantly wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, sleeping on straw.

entries.zh: 周明帝嘉之，召授左侍上士，累遷漢中太守，尋拜儀同三司。
entries.en: Emperor Ming of Zhou praised him, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon appointed an official with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming of Zhou commended this, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon made Yitong Sansi.

entries.zh: 開皇初，以平蠻功，加開府，封蛇丘縣公。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era, for his merit in pacifying the barbarians he was granted the privilege of an open office and enfeoffed as Duke of Sheqiu county.
entries.literal: Early in the Kaihuang era, for merit in pacifying the barbarians he was granted an open office and enfeoffed as Duke of Sheqiu county.

entries.zh: 獻取陳之策，上覽而異之，召與相見，言畢而歔欷，上為之改容。
entries.en: He submitted a plan for conquering Chen; the emperor read it and was struck by it, summoned him for an audience, and when he had finished speaking both men sobbed—the emperor's expression changed entirely.
entries.literal: He presented a plan to take Chen; the emperor read it and regarded it as extraordinary, summoned him to meet; when speech was finished both sobbed, and the emperor's countenance changed for it.

entries.zh: 及大舉伐陳，頒自請行，率徒數百人，從韓擒先鋒夜濟。
entries.en: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Ban volunteered to take part, leading several hundred men to cross the Yangtze by night with Han Qin's vanguard.
entries.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Ban himself requested to go, leading several hundred followers to cross the river by night with Han Qin's vanguard.

entries.zh: 力戰被傷，恐不堪復鬥，悲感嗚咽。
entries.en: He fought fiercely and was wounded; fearing he could not fight again, he sobbed in grief.
entries.literal: He fought fiercely and was wounded, feared he could not fight again, and sobbed in grief.

entries.zh: 夜中因睡，夢有人授藥，比寤而創不痛，時人以為孝感。
entries.en: In the night he fell asleep and dreamed someone gave him medicine; when he woke his wound no longer hurt—people at the time attributed this to filial devotion moving Heaven.
entries.literal: In the night he fell asleep and dreamed someone gave him medicine; when he woke his wound no longer hurt—people at the time took it as filial piety moving Heaven.

entries.zh: 及陳滅，頒密召父時士卒，得千餘人，對之涕泣。
entries.en: When Chen fell, Ban secretly gathered more than a thousand of his father's former soldiers and wept before them.
entries.literal: When Chen fell, Ban secretly summoned more than a thousand of his father's former soldiers and wept before them.

entries.zh: 其間壯士或問頒曰：「郎君來破陳國，滅其社稷，讎恥已雪，而悲哀不止者，將為霸先早死，不得手刃之邪？
entries.en: Some of the stalwarts among them asked Ban: "Young master, you came to destroy Chen and extinguish its altars of state—your revenge is already fulfilled—yet your grief never ends. Is it because Baxian died too soon and you could not kill him with your own hand?
entries.literal: Among them a stalwart asked Ban, saying: "Young master, you came to break Chen and destroy its altars of state—your revenge and shame are already cleared—yet your grief never stops. Is it because Baxian died too soon and you could not kill him with your own hand?

entries.zh: 請發其丘壟，斷櫬焚骨，亦可申孝心矣。」
entries.en: Please open his tomb mound, break open the coffin, and burn his bones—that too would fulfill your filial devotion."
entries.literal: Please open his tomb mound, break open the coffin, and burn his bones—that too can express your filial heart."

entries.zh: 頒頓顙陳謝，額盡流血，答之曰：「其為帝王，墳塋甚大，恐一宵發掘，不及其屍，更至明朝，事乃彰露，若之何？」
entries.en: Ban kowtowed again and again in apology until his forehead bled, and answered: "He was an emperor; his tomb precinct is vast. I fear that digging for a single night would not reach the corpse, and if we wait until dawn the deed would be exposed—what then could we do?"
entries.literal: Ban repeatedly kowtowed in apology until his forehead bled, and answered: "He was an emperor; his tomb precinct is vast. I fear that digging for a single night would not reach the corpse, and if we wait until dawn the deed would be exposed—what then could we do?"

entries.zh: 諸人請具鍬鍤，一旦皆萃。
entries.en: The men offered to bring hoes and spades, and in one day all assembled.
entries.literal: The men offered to bring hoes and spades, and in one day all assembled.

entries.zh: 於是夜發其陵，剖棺，見陳武帝須並不落，其本皆出自骨中。
entries.en: That night they opened the mausoleum and split the coffin. Chen Emperor Wu's beard had not fallen away at all—its roots still grew from the bones.
entries.literal: Thereupon that night they opened the mausoleum and split the coffin. Chen Emperor Wu's beard had not fallen away at all—its roots still grew from the bones.

entries.zh: 頒遂焚骨取灰，投水而飲之。
entries.en: Ban then burned the bones, took the ashes, mixed them in water, and drank them.
entries.literal: Ban then burned the bones, took the ashes, mixed them in water, and drank them.

entries.zh: 既而自縛，歸罪於晉王。
entries.en: He then bound himself and surrendered to take blame before the Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: Thereupon he bound himself and surrendered to take blame before the Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 王表其狀，高祖曰：「朕以義平陳，王頒所為，亦孝義之道也，朕何忍罪之！」
entries.en: The prince reported what had happened. Emperor Gaozu said: "I conquered Chen in the name of righteousness. What Wang Ban did belongs to the way of filial devotion and righteousness as well—how could I bear to punish him!"
entries.literal: The prince reported the circumstances. Emperor Gaozu said: "I conquered Chen in the name of righteousness. What Wang Ban did belongs to the way of filial devotion and righteousness as well—how could I bear to punish him!"

entries.zh: 舍而不問。
entries.en: He pardoned him and took no further action.
entries.literal: He pardoned him and took no further action.

entries.zh: 有司錄其戰功，將加柱國，賜物五千段，頒固辭曰：「臣緣國威靈，得雪怨恥，本心徇私，非是為國，所加官賞，終不敢當。」
entries.en: The authorities recorded his battle achievements and proposed to make him a Pillar of State and grant him five thousand rolls of goods. Ban firmly declined: "Through the state's awesome authority I was able to settle my grievance; my heart was bent on private revenge, not on serving the state. The offices and rewards you would bestow I dare not accept."
entries.literal: The authorities recorded his battle achievements and proposed to make him a Pillar of State and grant him five thousand rolls of goods. Ban firmly declined, saying: "Through the state's awesome authority I was able to settle my grievance; my heart was bent on private revenge, not on serving the state. The offices and rewards you would bestow I ultimately dare not accept."

entries.zh: 高祖從之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The emperor assented.

entries.zh: 拜代州刺史，甚有惠政。
entries.en: He was appointed Governor of Daizhou and governed with notable benevolence.
entries.literal: He was appointed Governor of Daizhou and governed with notable benevolence.

entries.zh: 母憂去職。
entries.en: He left office upon his mother's death.
entries.literal: He left office upon his mother's death.

entries.zh: 後為齊州刺史，卒官，時年五十二。
entries.en: He later served as Governor of Qizhou and died in office at the age of fifty-two.
entries.literal: He later served as Governor of Qizhou and died in office at the age of fifty-two.

entries.zh: 弟頍，見《文學傳》。
entries.en: His younger brother Kui is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.
entries.literal: His younger brother Kui is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.

entries.zh: 楊慶，字伯悅，河間人也。
entries.en: Yang Qing, whose courtesy name was Boyue, came from Hejian.
entries.literal: Yang Qing, courtesy name Boyue, was a native of Hejian.

entries.zh: 祖玄，父剛，並以至孝知名。
entries.en: His grandfather Xuan and his father Gang were both renowned for utmost filial piety.
entries.literal: His grandfather Xuan and his father Gang were both renowned for utmost filial piety.

entries.zh: 慶美姿儀，性辯慧。
entries.en: Qing was handsome in bearing and clever by nature.
entries.literal: Qing had a fine appearance and a clever, eloquent nature.

entries.zh: 年十六，齊國子博士徐遵明見而異之。
entries.en: At sixteen the Qi erudite of the National University Xu Zunming saw him and was struck by his qualities.
entries.literal: At sixteen the Qi erudite of the National University Xu Zunming saw him and marveled.

entries.zh: 及長，頗涉書記。
entries.en: When he grew up he applied himself considerably to letters and record-keeping.
entries.literal: When he grew up he applied himself considerably to letters and record-keeping.

entries.zh: 年二十五，郡察孝廉，以侍養不行。
entries.en: At twenty-five the commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he declined to go because he was caring for his parents.
entries.literal: At twenty-five the commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he declined to go because he was caring for his parents.

entries.zh: 其母有疾，不解襟帶者七旬。
entries.en: When his mother fell ill he did not unfasten his collar or belt for seventy days.
entries.literal: When his mother fell ill he did not unfasten his collar or belt for seventy days.

entries.zh: 及居母憂，哀毀骨立，負土成墳。
entries.en: During mourning for his mother he grieved until only bone remained and carried earth to build the tomb mound himself.
entries.literal: During mourning for his mother he grieved until only bone remained and carried earth to build the tomb mound himself.

entries.zh: 齊文宣帝表其門閭，賜帛三十匹，綿十屯，粟五十石。
entries.en: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi honored his household gate, granting thirty bolts of silk, ten bales of cotton, and fifty piculs of grain.
entries.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi honored his household gate, granting thirty bolts of silk, ten bales of cotton, and fifty piculs of grain.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，屢加褒賞，擢授儀同三司，版授平陽太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to Yitong Sansi, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.

entries.zh: 年八十五，終於家。
entries.en: He died at home at the age of eighty-five.
entries.literal: He died at home at the age of eighty-five.

entries.zh: 子士雄，少質直孝友，喪父，復廬於墓側，負土成墳。
entries.en: His son Shixiong was by nature simple, upright, filial, and friendly. When his father died he again lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.
entries.literal: His son Shixiong was by nature simple, upright, filial, and friendly. When his father died he again lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.

entries.zh: 其庭前有一槐樹，先甚鬱茂，及士雄居喪，樹遂枯死。
entries.en: A locust tree before his courtyard had been very lush, but when Shixiong entered mourning it withered and died.
entries.literal: A locust tree before his courtyard had been very lush, but when Shixiong entered mourning it withered and died.

entries.zh: 服闋還宅，死樹復榮。
entries.en: When mourning ended and he returned home, the dead tree flourished again.
entries.literal: When mourning ended and he returned home, the dead tree flourished again.

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，歎其父子至孝，下詔褒揚，號其所居為累德里。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu heard this he sighed at the father and son's utmost filial piety, issued an edict of praise, and named their dwelling Accumulated Virtue Lane.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu heard this he sighed at the father and son's utmost filial piety, issued an edict of praise, and named their dwelling Accumulated Virtue Lane.

entries.zh: 劉士俊，彭城人也。
entries.en: Liu Shijun was from Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Liu Shijun was a native of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 性至孝，丁母喪，絕而復蘇者數矣。
entries.en: He was utterly filial. During mourning for his mother he fainted and revived several times.
entries.literal: He was utterly filial. During mourning for his mother he fainted and revived several times.

entries.zh: 勺飲不入口者七日，廬於墓側，負土成墳，列植松柏。
entries.en: For seven days he took neither spoon nor drink. He lived in a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to build the mound, and planted pines and cypresses in rows.
entries.literal: For seven days he took neither spoon nor drink. He lived in a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to build the mound, and planted pines and cypresses in rows.

entries.zh: 狐狼馴擾，為之取食。
entries.en: Foxes and wolves grew tame and familiar, and he brought them food.
entries.literal: Foxes and wolves grew tame and familiar, and he brought them food.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，表其門閭。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he honored Shijun's household gate.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he honored Shijun's household gate.

entries.zh: 薛濬，字道賾，刑部尚書、內陽公胄之從祖弟也。
entries.en: Xue Jun, styled Daoyin, was a younger cousin of Zhou, Duke of Neiyang, who had served as Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: Xue Jun, styled Daoyin, was a younger cousin of Zhou, Duke of Neiyang, Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 父琰，周渭南太守。
entries.en: His father Yan had been governor of Weinan under Zhou.
entries.literal: His father Yan was governor of Weinan under Zhou.

entries.zh: 濬少喪父，早孤，養母以孝聞。
entries.en: Jun lost his father in childhood and was orphaned young; he supported his mother and became renowned for filial devotion.
entries.literal: Jun lost his father in youth and was orphaned early; he supported his mother and was famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 幼好學，有志行，尋師于長安。
entries.en: From childhood he loved learning and showed strength of character; he went to Chang'an in search of a teacher.
entries.literal: From childhood he loved learning, had resolve and conduct, and sought a teacher in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 時初平江陵，何妥歸國，見而異之，授以經業。
entries.en: Jiangling had just been pacified; He Tuo had returned from captivity, saw him and was struck by his promise, and instructed him in the classics.
entries.literal: At that time Jiangling had just been pacified; He Tuo returned to the state, saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, and taught him the classics.

entries.zh: 周天和中，襲爵虞城侯，歷納言上士、新豐令。
entries.en: During the Tianhe era of Zhou he inherited the marquisate of Yucheng and served as Senior Clerk of the Remonstrance Bureau and as magistrate of Xinfeng.
entries.literal: In the Tianhe era of Zhou he inherited the marquisate of Yucheng and served in succession as Senior Clerk of the Remonstrance Bureau and as magistrate of Xinfeng.

entries.zh: 開皇初，擢拜尚書虞部侍郎，尋轉考功侍郎。
entries.en: At the start of Kaihuang he was promoted to Vice Director of the Parks Office in the Secretariat and soon transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was promoted to Vice Director of the Parks Office in the Secretariat, and soon transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

entries.zh: 帝聞濬事母至孝，以其母老，賜輿服機杖，四時珍味，當時榮之。
entries.en: When the emperor heard that Jun served his mother with utmost devotion, and because his mother was elderly, he bestowed a carriage, robes, a staff, and seasonal delicacies — an honor greatly envied at the time.
entries.literal: The emperor heard that Jun served his mother with utmost filial piety; because his mother was old, he bestowed a carriage, robes, a staff, and delicacies for all four seasons — at the time this was counted an honor.

entries.zh: 後其母疾，濬貌甚憂瘁，親故弗之識也。
entries.en: When his mother later fell ill, Jun grew so haggard with worry that relatives and friends scarcely recognized him.
entries.literal: Later when his mother fell ill, Jun's appearance was so haggard with worry that kin and friends did not recognize him.

entries.zh: 暨丁母艱，詔鴻臚監護喪事，歸葬夏陽。
entries.en: When his mother died, an edict ordered the Director of Guests to oversee the funeral, and he returned to bury her at Xiayang.
entries.literal: When his mother's death came, an edict ordered the Director of Guests to oversee the funeral; he returned to bury her at Xiayang.

entries.zh: 于時隆冬極寒，濬衰絰徒跣，冒犯霜雪，自京及鄉，五百餘里，足凍墜指，瘡血流離，朝野為之傷痛。
entries.en: It was the depths of winter and bitterly cold; Jun wore mourning garments and went barefoot through frost and snow from the capital to his home, more than five hundred li; his feet froze until his toes fell off, his wounds bled freely — court and countryside alike were stricken with grief for him.
entries.literal: At that time it was deep winter and extreme cold; Jun wore mourning garments and went barefoot, braving frost and snow from the capital to his home district, more than five hundred li; his feet froze and toes fell off, wounds bled and ran — court and countryside alike were pained for him.

entries.zh: 州裡賵助，一無所受。
entries.en: He accepted none of the condolence gifts offered by his district and neighbors.
entries.literal: Condolence gifts from the district and neighborhood — he accepted none.

entries.zh: 尋起令視事，濬屢陳誠款，請終喪制，優詔不許。
entries.en: He was soon recalled to resume office; Jun repeatedly petitioned in all sincerity to complete the full mourning period, but gracious edicts would not allow it.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled to resume office; Jun repeatedly stated his sincere wish to complete the full mourning term, but gracious edicts would not permit it.

entries.zh: 及至京，上見其毀瘠過甚，為之改容，顧謂群臣曰：「吾見薛濬哀毀，不覺悲感傷懷。」
entries.en: When he reached the capital, the emperor saw how grievously he had wasted away, and his expression changed; turning to the assembled ministers he said: "When I see Xue Jun's grief and emaciation, I cannot help but feel sorrow pierce my heart."
entries.literal: When he reached the capital, the emperor saw how excessively emaciated he was, changed countenance for him, and turning to the assembled ministers said: "When I see Xue Jun's grief and emaciation, I cannot help but feel sorrow and grief in my breast."

entries.zh: 嗟異久之。
entries.en: He sighed and marveled for a long while.
entries.literal: He sighed and marveled for a long while.

entries.zh: 濬竟不勝喪，病且卒。
entries.en: In the end Jun could not survive his grief; he fell ill and was near death.
entries.literal: Jun in the end could not bear the mourning; he fell ill and was about to die.

entries.zh: 其弟謨時為晉王府兵曹參軍事，在揚州，濬遺書與謨曰：
entries.en: His younger brother Mo was then a staff officer in the Military Affairs Section of the Prince of Jin's household in Yangzhou; Jun left a letter for Mo that read:
entries.literal: His younger brother Mo was at that time a staff officer in the Military Affairs Section of the Prince of Jin's household, in Yangzhou; Jun left a letter for Mo saying:

entries.zh: 郭俊，字弘乂，太原文水人也。
entries.en: Guo Jun, whose courtesy name was Hongyi, came from Wenshui in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Guo Jun, courtesy name Hongyi, was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 家門雍睦，七葉共居，犬豕同乳，烏鵲通巢，時人以為義感之應。
entries.en: His clan lived in harmony—seven generations under one roof. Dogs and pigs nursed from the same mother, crows and magpies shared nests, and people of the time took this as a sign stirred by their righteousness.
entries.literal: His clan lived in harmony—seven generations under one roof. Dogs and pigs nursed from the same mother, crows and magpies shared nests, and people of the time took this as a sign stirred by their righteousness.

entries.zh: 州縣上其事，上遣平昌公宇文弼詣其家勞問之。
entries.en: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and commend them and inquire after their welfare.
entries.literal: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and extend commendation and inquiries.

entries.zh: 治書御史柳彧巡省河北，表其門閭。
entries.en: The investigating censor Liu Yu, while touring Hebei, honored their household gate.
entries.literal: The investigating censor Liu Yu, while touring Hebei, honored their household gate.

entries.zh: 漢王諒為并州總管，聞而嘉歎，賜兄弟二十餘人衣各一襲。
entries.en: Prince of Han Yang Liang, as chief commander of Bingzhou, heard of this, sighed in admiration, and gave each of the more than twenty brothers a suit of clothing.
entries.literal: Prince of Han Yang Liang, as chief commander of Bingzhou, heard of this, sighed in admiration, and gave each of the more than twenty brothers a suit of clothing.

entries.zh: 華秋，汲郡臨河人也。
entries.en: Hua Qiu was from Linhe in Ji commandery.
entries.literal: Hua Qiu was a native of Linhe in Ji commandery.

entries.zh: 幼喪父，事母以孝聞。
entries.en: He lost his father in childhood and was famed for serving his mother with filial devotion.
entries.literal: He lost his father in childhood and was known for serving his mother with filial piety.

entries.zh: 家貧，傭賃為養。
entries.en: The family was poor, and he hired himself out as a laborer to support her.
entries.literal: The family was poor; he hired himself out as labor to support her.

entries.zh: 其母遇患，秋容貌毀悴，須鬢頓改，州裡咸嗟異之。
entries.en: When his mother fell ill, Qiu's face wasted away and his beard and whiskers turned grey overnight; people throughout the district marveled and sighed.
entries.literal: When his mother fell ill, Qiu's face wasted away and his beard and whiskers suddenly changed color, and throughout the district people all sighed in wonder.

entries.zh: 及母終之後，遂絕櫛沐，發盡禿落。
entries.en: After his mother died he ceased combing and bathing, and his hair fell out until he was completely bald.
entries.literal: After his mother died he ceased combing and washing himself, and his hair fell out completely bald.

entries.zh: 廬於墓側，負土成墳，有人欲助之者，秋輒拜而止之。
entries.en: He lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound himself; whenever anyone offered to help, Qiu would bow and refuse.
entries.literal: He lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound; whenever anyone wished to help, Qiu would bow and stop him.

entries.zh: 大業初，調狐皮，郡縣大獵。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Daye reign a levy for fox pelts was issued, and the commandery and county organized a great hunt.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Daye a levy for fox pelts was issued, and the commandery and county launched a great hunt.

entries.zh: 有一兔，人逐之，奔入秋廬中，匿秋膝下。
entries.en: A rabbit was being chased; it fled into Qiu's hut and hid beneath his knees.
entries.literal: There was one rabbit men pursued; it fled into Qiu's hut and hid beneath his knees.

entries.zh: 獵人至廬所，異而免之。
entries.en: When the hunters reached the hut they took it as a marvel and spared the rabbit.
entries.literal: When the hunters reached the hut they regarded it as strange and spared it.

entries.zh: 自爾此兔常宿廬中，馴其左右。
entries.en: From then on the rabbit often lodged in the hut, tame at his side.
entries.literal: From then on this rabbit often lodged in the hut, tame at his left and right.

entries.zh: 郡縣嘉其孝感，俱以狀聞。
entries.en: The commandery and county praised his moving filial piety and all reported the matter to the throne.
entries.literal: The commandery and county praised his filial response, and all reported the matter upward.

entries.zh: 煬帝降使勞問，表其門閭。
entries.en: Emperor Yang sent envoys to console him and honored his household with an imperial marker.
entries.literal: Emperor Yang sent envoys to console him and honored his household gate.

entries.zh: 後群盜起，常往來廬之左右，咸相誡曰：「勿犯孝子。」
entries.en: Later when bandits rose they often passed near the hut, and all warned one another: "Do not harm the filial son."
entries.literal: Later when bandits rose they often passed to and fro near the hut, and all warned one another, saying, "Do not harm the filial son."

entries.zh: 鄉人賴秋而全者甚眾。
entries.en: A great many in the village owed their safety to Qiu.
entries.literal: Many in the village owed their safety to Qiu.

entries.zh: 隋書卷七十二列傳第三十七
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume 72, Biographies 37
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 72, Biographies 37

entries.zh: 李士謙，字子約，趙郡平棘人也。
entries.en: Li Shiqian, styled Ziyue, was a native of Pingji in Zhao Commandery.
entries.literal: Li Shiqian, style Ziyue, was a native of Pingji in Zhao Commandery.

entries.zh: 髫齔喪父，事母以孝聞。
entries.en: He lost his father in childhood and became known for his filial devotion to his mother.
entries.literal: In infancy he lost his father and became known for filial service to his mother.

entries.zh: 母曾嘔吐，疑為中毒，因跪而嘗之。
entries.en: When his mother once vomited, fearing she had been poisoned, he knelt and tasted the vomit himself.
entries.literal: His mother once vomited; suspecting poison, he knelt and tasted it.

entries.zh: 伯父魏岐州刺史瑒，深所嗟尚，每稱曰：「此兒吾家之顏子也。」
entries.en: His uncle Yang, who served as Inspector of Qizhou in Wei, held him in deep admiration and would often say, "This boy is the Yan Hui of our house."
entries.literal: His uncle Yang, Inspector of Qizhou in Wei, deeply admired him and would often say, "This boy is the Yan Hui of our family."

entries.zh: 年十二，魏廣平王贊辟開府參軍事。
entries.en: At the age of twelve, Zan, Prince of Guangping of Wei, recruited him as Record Keeper of the Prince's Household Staff.
entries.literal: At age twelve, Zan, Prince of Guangping of Wei, recruited him as Record Keeper of the Prince's Household Staff.

entries.zh: 後丁母憂，居喪骨立。
entries.en: Later, when his mother died, he mourned until he was skin and bone.
entries.literal: Later, upon his mother's death, in mourning he was reduced to skin and bone.

entries.zh: 有姊適宋氏，不勝哀而死。
entries.en: An elder sister of his, married into the Song clan, died of grief she could not bear.
entries.literal: He had an elder sister married to the Song clan who, unable to bear the grief, died.

entries.zh: 士謙服闋，舍宅為伽藍，脫身而出。
entries.en: When Shiqian's mourning period ended, he gave his house over to become a Buddhist monastery and withdrew from worldly life.
entries.literal: When Shiqian's mourning period ended, he gave his house to become a monastery and withdrew from worldly life.

entries.zh: 詣學請業，研精不倦，遂博覽群籍，兼善天文術數。
entries.en: He went to study and pursued learning with tireless refinement, eventually reading widely in all the classics and also excelling in astronomy and numerology.
entries.literal: He went to school to seek learning, studying with tireless refinement, and came to read broadly in all books, also excelling in astronomy and numerology.

entries.zh: 齊吏部尚書辛術召署員外郎，趙郡王睿舉德行，皆稱疾不就。
entries.en: Xin Shu, Minister of the Civil Service in Qi, summoned him to serve as Supernumerary Gentleman, and Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery recommended him for moral conduct—each time he pleaded illness and declined.
entries.literal: Xin Shu, Minister of the Civil Service in Qi, summoned him to serve as Supernumerary Gentleman; Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery recommended him for moral conduct—on each occasion he pleaded illness and did not accept.

entries.zh: 和士開亦重其名，將諷朝廷，擢為國子祭酒。
entries.en: He Shikai also valued his reputation and intended to prompt the court to appoint him Director of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: He Shikai also valued his reputation and was about to prompt the court to promote him to Director of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 士謙知而固辭，得免。
entries.en: Shiqian learned of this and firmly declined, and so was spared the appointment.
entries.literal: Shiqian learned of it and firmly declined, and was spared.

entries.zh: 隋有天下，畢志不仕。
entries.en: When the Sui came to rule the empire, he held firm to his resolve and never took office.
entries.literal: When Sui possessed the empire, he fulfilled his resolve and did not take office.

entries.zh: 自以少孤，未嘗飲酒食肉，口無殺害之言。
entries.en: Because he had been orphaned young, he never drank wine or ate meat, and never spoke words of killing.
entries.literal: Because he had been orphaned young, he never drank wine or ate meat, and his mouth held no words of killing.

entries.zh: 至於親賓來萃，輒陳樽俎，對之危坐，終日不倦。
entries.en: When relatives and guests gathered, he would set out wine and meat for them, sit upright in their company, and keep at it all day without tiring.
entries.literal: When relatives and guests gathered, he would set out wine and meat, sit upright facing them, and remain tireless all day.

entries.zh: 李氏宗党豪盛，每至春秋二社，必高會極歡，無不沉醉喧亂。
entries.en: The Li clan was powerful and numerous; whenever the spring and autumn communal sacrifices arrived, they held grand gatherings of utmost revelry, and none failed to end up drunk and disorderly.
entries.literal: The Li clan's lineage and kin were powerful and flourishing; whenever the spring and autumn communal sacrifices came, they would hold grand gatherings of utmost revelry, none failing to become drunk and riotous.

entries.zh: 嘗集士謙所，盛饌盈前，而先為設黍，謂群從曰：「孔子稱黍為五穀之長，荀卿亦雲食先黍稷，古人所尚，容可違乎？」
entries.en: They once gathered at Shiqian's home with lavish fare spread before them, yet he first set out millet and said to the assembled kin, "Confucius called millet the chief of the five grains, and Xunzi also said that in eating one should put millet and glutinous millet first—what the ancients honored—how could one go against this?"
entries.literal: They once gathered at Shiqian's place with lavish fare spread before them, yet he first set out millet and said to the assembled kin, "Confucius called millet the chief of the five grains; Xun Qing also said that in eating one should put millet and glutinous millet first—what the ancients honored—how could one go against this?"

entries.zh: 少長肅然，不敢馳惰，退而相謂曰：「既見君子，方覺吾徒之不德也。」
entries.en: Young and old grew solemn and dared not be lax; afterward they said to one another, "Having seen a gentleman, we now realize how lacking in virtue we ourselves are."
entries.literal: Young and old became solemn, not daring to be lax or idle; afterward they said to one another, "Having seen a gentleman, we now realize how lacking in virtue we ourselves are."

entries.zh: 士謙聞而自責曰：「何乃為人所疏，頓至於此！」
entries.en: When Shiqian heard this, he blamed himself, saying, "How have I come to be held at a distance by others, to this sudden degree!"
entries.literal: Shiqian heard and blamed himself, saying, "How have I come to be held aloof by others, to this sudden degree!"

entries.zh: 家富於財，躬處節儉，每以振施為務。
entries.en: His household was wealthy, yet he personally practiced thrift and made relief and charity his constant concern.
entries.literal: His household was rich in wealth, yet he personally practiced thrift and made relief and giving his constant task.

entries.zh: 州裡有喪事不辦者，士謙輒奔走赴之，隨乏供濟。
entries.en: When someone in the district could not manage a funeral, Shiqian would hurry to assist and supply whatever was lacking.
entries.literal: When someone in the district could not manage a funeral, Shiqian would hurry to help and supply whatever was lacking.

entries.zh: 有兄弟分財不均，至相鬩訟，士謙聞而出財，補其少者，令與多者相埒。
entries.en: When brothers divided property unequally and came to quarrel and sue one another, Shiqian heard of it, contributed funds to supplement the one who had less, and made his share equal to his brother's.
entries.literal: When brothers divided property unequally and came to quarrel and sue, Shiqian heard of it, contributed funds, supplemented the one who had less, and made him equal to the one who had more.

entries.zh: 兄弟愧懼，更相推讓，卒為善士。
entries.en: The brothers, ashamed and afraid, yielded to one another in turn and in the end became good men.
entries.literal: The brothers, ashamed and afraid, yielded to one another in turn and in the end became good men.

entries.zh: 有牛犯其田者，士謙牽置涼處飼之，過於本主。
entries.en: When an ox trespassed on his fields, Shiqian led it to a cool place and fed it, treating it better than its own owner did.
entries.literal: When an ox trespassed on his fields, Shiqian led it to a cool place and fed it, treating it better than its own owner.

entries.zh: 望見盜刈其禾黍者，默而避之。
entries.en: When he saw thieves reaping his grain and millet, he kept silent and withdrew from them.
entries.literal: When he saw thieves reaping his grain and millet, he kept silent and withdrew from them.

entries.zh: 其家僮嘗執盜粟者，士謙慰諭之曰：「窮困所致，義無相責。」
entries.en: When a household slave once seized a thief of grain, Shiqian comforted him and said, "Poverty drove him to it—by right one should not blame him."
entries.literal: His household slave once seized a thief of grain; Shiqian comforted and instructed him, saying, "Poverty drove him to it—by right one should not blame him."

entries.zh: 遽令放之。
entries.en: He immediately ordered the man released.
entries.literal: He immediately ordered him released.

entries.zh: 其奴嘗與鄉人董震因醉角力，震扼其喉，斃於手下。
entries.en: His slave once wrestled while drunk with a fellow townsman named Dong Zhen; Zhen seized his throat and killed him on the spot.
entries.literal: His slave once wrestled with a fellow townsman named Dong Zhen while drunk; Zhen seized his throat and killed him on the spot.

entries.zh: 震惶懼請罪，士謙謂之曰：「卿本無殺心，何為相謝！
entries.en: Zhen, fearful and remorseful, begged forgiveness; Shiqian said to him, "You had no intent to kill—why apologize!
entries.literal: Zhen, fearful and afraid, begged forgiveness; Shiqian said to him, "You originally had no intent to kill—why apologize!

entries.zh: 然可遠去，無為吏之所拘。」
entries.en: Yet you should go far away, lest the officials seize you."
entries.literal: Yet you should go far away, lest the officials seize you."

entries.zh: 性寬厚，皆此類也。
entries.en: His nature was generous and mild—all his conduct was of this kind.
entries.literal: His nature was generous and mild—all were of this kind.

entries.zh: 其後出粟數千石，以貸鄉人，值年穀不登，債家無以償，皆來致謝。
entries.en: Later he distributed several thousand bushels of grain to lend to his fellow townspeople; when the year's harvest failed, the debtor households had no means to repay and all came to apologize.
entries.literal: Later he distributed several thousand bushels of grain to lend to his fellow townspeople; when the year's harvest failed, the debtor households had no means to repay and all came to apologize.

entries.zh: 士謙曰：「吾家餘粟，本圖振贍，豈求利哉！」
entries.en: Shiqian said, "The surplus grain in my household was meant for relief and support—how could I seek profit from it!"
entries.literal: Shiqian said, "The surplus grain in my household was originally intended for relief and support—how could I seek profit!"

entries.zh: 於是悉召債家，為設酒食，對之燔契，曰：「債了矣，幸勿為念也。」
entries.en: Thereupon he summoned all the debtor households, set out wine and food, and burned the contracts before them, saying, "The debt is settled—please do not brood on it."
entries.literal: Thereupon he summoned all the debtor households, set out wine and food for them, and burned the contracts before them, saying, "The debt is settled—please do not brood on it."

entries.zh: 各令罷去。
entries.en: He had each of them depart.
entries.literal: He had each of them depart.

entries.zh: 明年大熟，債家爭來償謙，謙拒之，一無所受。
entries.en: The next year the harvest was abundant; the debtor households vied to repay Shiqian, but he refused them and accepted nothing.
entries.literal: The next year the harvest was abundant; the debtor households vied to repay Shiqian, but he refused them and accepted nothing.

entries.zh: 他年又大饑，多有死者，士謙罄竭家資，為之糜粥，賴以全活者將萬計。
entries.en: Another year brought great famine and many deaths; Shiqian exhausted his household's resources to make gruel for the hungry, and those who survived by his aid numbered nearly ten thousand.
entries.literal: Another year there was again great famine and many died; Shiqian exhausted his household's resources to make gruel for them, and those who lived through it by his aid numbered nearly ten thousand.

entries.zh: 收埋骸骨，所見無遺。
entries.en: He gathered and buried the bones of the dead—none that he saw were left unattended.
entries.literal: He gathered and buried the bones of the dead—none he saw were left unattended.

entries.zh: 至春，又出糧種，分給貧乏。
entries.en: When spring came, he again distributed grain and seed to the poor.
entries.literal: When spring came, he again distributed grain and seed to the poor.

entries.zh: 趙郡農民德之，撫其子孫曰：「此乃李參軍遺惠也。」
entries.en: The farmers of Zhao Commandery were grateful to him and would tell their sons and grandsons, "This is the lingering kindness left by Registrar Li."
entries.literal: The farmers of Zhao Commandery were grateful to him and would stroke their sons and grandsons, saying, "This is the lingering kindness left by Registrar Li."

entries.zh: 或謂士謙曰：「子多陰德。」
entries.en: Someone said to Shiqian, "Sir, you have much hidden virtue."
entries.literal: Someone said to Shiqian, "Sir, you have much hidden virtue."

entries.zh: 士謙曰：「所謂陰德者何？
entries.en: Shiqian said, "What is meant by hidden virtue?
entries.literal: Shiqian said, "What is meant by hidden virtue?

entries.zh: 猶耳鳴，已獨聞之，人無知者。
entries.en: It is like ringing in the ears—one alone hears it, and others know nothing of it.
entries.literal: It is like ringing in the ears—one alone hears it, and others know nothing of it.

entries.zh: 今吾所作，吾子皆知，何陰德之有！」
entries.en: What I do now, my sons all know—how could there be hidden virtue!"
entries.literal: What I do now, my sons all know—how could there be hidden virtue!"

entries.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。
entries.en: Only yesterday I received your gracious letter; the favor shown me was beyond measure, and my heart was utterly overwhelmed.
entries.literal: The day before yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was extraordinary, and my spirit was lost within itself.

entries.zh: 若乃理高《象》、《系》，管輅思而不解，事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。
entries.en: Its reasoning rises above the Image and Judgment texts of the Changes—Guan Lu would have pondered in vain; its matter overflows the Classic of Mountains and Seas—even Guo Pu's commentary could not exhaust it.
entries.literal: As for its reasoning, it surpasses the Image and Link texts of the Changes—Guan Lu would ponder without understanding; its content is richer than the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated yet could not exhaust it.

entries.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。
entries.en: The five colors blend in harmony and the eight tones assemble in rich concord—phoenix song cannot describe it, and dragon pattern cannot match it.
entries.literal: As for the five colors harmonizing and the eight tones gathering richly—phoenix song is insufficient as analogy; dragon emblems cannot compare.

entries.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚，郢客之奏《陽春》，誰堪赴節！
entries.en: When Wu Zha discoursed on the Zhou Hymns, he could not fully praise them; when the guest of Ying played "Spring in the Capital," who could keep the beat?
entries.literal: Wu Zha discussing the Zhou Hymns—how could he fully extol it? The guest of Ying playing "Spring in the Capital"—who could match the measure!

entries.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道貴于東平，文藝高於北海。
entries.en: Your Highness the Illustrious Prince, nourished by the imperial lineage and shining with the sun's radiance, excels the Prince of Dongping in refined conduct and surpasses the Prince of Beihai in literary accomplishment.
entries.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Illustrious Prince, nourished by the Heavenly River, inheriting radiance from Mount Ri, ranks higher in refined learning than the Prince of Dongping and surpasses the Prince of Beihai in literary art.

entries.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華，雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。
entries.en: Han had Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; Jin had Pei Kai and Zhang Hua—your fame resounds like the rooster tree and spreads like the egret pool; looking toward my humble trail, the road between us is impossibly far.
entries.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wang; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua—the rooster tree resounds, the egret pool spreads fame; gazing toward my clear dust, the path is serenely cut off.

entries.zh: 祖浚燕南贅客，河朔惰游，本無意于希顏，豈有心于慕藺！
entries.en: Zujun is but an extra guest in the south and a lazy wanderer in the north; I never aspired to emulate Yan Hui—how could I dream of admiring Lin Xiangru!
entries.literal: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of the Yan, an idle wanderer north of the River; originally I had no thought of emulating Yan Hui—how could I have a heart set on admiring Lin Xiangru!

entries.zh: 未嘗聚螢映雪，懸頭刺股，讀《論》唯取一篇，披《莊》不過盈尺。
entries.en: I never studied by firefly or snowlight, never hung from a beam or pricked my thigh; I read only one chapter of the Analects and barely a foot of Zhuangzi.
entries.literal: I have never gathered fireflies to read by snow-light, hung my head or pricked my thigh; in reading the Analects I take only one chapter; in opening Zhuangzi I go no more than a full foot's length.

entries.zh: 複況桑榆漸暮，藜藿屢空，舉燭無成，穿楊盡棄。
entries.en: Moreover, sunset draws near like mulberry and elm at dusk; my larder is often bare; I have achieved nothing by lamplight and abandoned all hope of hitting the willow leaf.
entries.literal: Moreover, like the mulberry and elm at dusk, I am nearing old age; greens and coarse grains are repeatedly empty; raising the candle brings no achievement; shooting through the willow is all abandoned.

entries.zh: 但以燕求馬首，薛養雞鳴，謬齒鴻儀，虛班驥皁。
entries.en: Yet as Yan sought the horse's head and Xue kept the rooster crowing, I have wrongly taken my place among swans and falsely ranked among thoroughbreds.
entries.literal: Yet through Yan seeking the horse's head and Xue raising the rooster's crow, I wrongly count myself among the swan's ranks and vainly take place among the thoroughbred blacks.

entries.zh: 挾太山而超北海，比報德而非難，堙昆侖以為池，匹酬恩而反易。
entries.en: Carrying Mount Tai over the North Sea would be easier than repaying your virtue; damming Mount Kunlun to make a pool would be simpler than returning your kindness.
entries.literal: To grasp Mount Tai and leap over the North Sea—compared with repaying virtue that is not hard; to dam Mount Kunlun to make a pool—matching return of kindness is instead easy.

entries.zh: 忽屬周桐錫瑞，康水承家，門有將相，樹宜桃李。
entries.en: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia receives its omen and the house of Kang inherits the realm; generals and ministers stand at your gate, and your trees are fit to bear peach and plum.
entries.literal: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia bestows its auspice and the Kang waters inherit the house; at the gate are generals and ministers; the trees are fit for peach and plum.

entries.zh: 真龍將下，誰好有名，濫吹先逃，何須別聽！
entries.en: When the true dragon is about to descend, who still seeks renown? The incompetent musician has already fled—why should anyone else stay to listen!
entries.literal: When the true dragon is about to descend, who will crave fame? The one who blew poorly has already fled—why need anyone else listen!

entries.zh: 但慈旨抑揚，損上益下，江海所以稱王，丘陵為之不逮。
entries.en: Yet your gracious words humble yourself and exalt me; rivers and seas are called kings because they lie below, and hills and mounds cannot match them.
entries.literal: But your kindly words raise up the lowly and lower the lofty; it is for this that rivers and seas are called kings, and hills and mounds cannot compare.

entries.zh: 曹植儻預聞高論，則不隕令名，楊修若切在下風，亦詎虧淳德。
