entries.en: Had Cao Zhi heard your lofty discourse, his fine name would not have fallen; had Yang Xiu stood in your shadow, his pure virtue would not have suffered.
entries.literal: If Cao Zhi had chanced to hear your lofty discourse, he would not lose his fine name; if Yang Xiu were right beneath your wind, he too would not diminish pure virtue.

entries.zh: 無任荷戴之至，謹奉啟以聞。
entries.en: Overwhelmed with gratitude, I respectfully submit this reply for your notice.
entries.literal: I cannot bear the utmost of my burdened gratitude; I respectfully submit this letter to inform you.

entries.zh: 徐則，東海郯人也。
entries.en: Xu Ze was a native of Tan in Donghai Commandery.
entries.literal: Xu Ze was a native of Tan in Donghai.

entries.zh: 幼沈靜，寡嗜欲。
entries.en: From childhood he was calm and reserved, with little appetite for worldly things.
entries.literal: From youth he was quiet and still, with few desires.

entries.zh: 受業于周弘正，善三玄，精於議論，聲擅都邑，則歎曰：「名者實之賓，吾其為賓乎！」
entries.en: He studied under Zhou Hongzheng, mastered the Three Mysterious Learning, and excelled in debate until his reputation filled the capital; Ze sighed and said: "Fame is the guest of substance—am I to be the guest?"
entries.literal: He studied under Zhou Hongzheng, was skilled in the Three Mysterious Learning, excelled in disputation, and his fame dominated the capital; Ze sighed and said: "Fame is the guest of reality—am I to be the guest?"

entries.zh: 遂懷棲隱之操，杖策入縉雲山。
entries.en: With that he resolved to live in seclusion, took up his staff, and withdrew to Mount Jinyun.
entries.literal: Thereupon he harbored the resolve to live in seclusion, took staff in hand, and entered Mount Jinyun.

entries.zh: 後學數百人，苦請教授，則謝而遣之。
entries.en: Later several hundred students pleaded to become his disciples, but Ze refused and sent them away.
entries.literal: Later several hundred students earnestly begged to be taught; Ze declined and sent them away.

entries.zh: 不娶妻，常服巾褐。
entries.en: He never married and always wore a plain cap and hemp robe.
entries.literal: He did not marry and regularly wore cloth cap and hemp robe.

entries.zh: 陳太建時，應召來憩於至真觀。
entries.en: During the Taijian period of Chen he answered a summons and stayed for a time at the Zhizhen Abbey.
entries.literal: During the Taijian era of Chen, summoned, he came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.

entries.zh: 期月，又辭入天臺山，因絕穀養性，所資唯松水而已，雖隆冬洹寒，不服綿絮。
entries.en: After a month he declined further service and withdrew to Mount Tiantai, where he abstained from grain to nourish his nature and lived on pine and water alone; even in the bitter cold of midwinter he wore no padded clothes.
entries.literal: After a month he declined again and entered Mount Tiantai; there he ceased eating grain to nurture his nature, relying only on pine and water; even in the depths of winter's icy cold, he wore no cotton padding.

entries.zh: 太傅徐陵為之刊山立頌。
entries.en: Grand Tutor Xu Ling had an inscription carved on the mountain and a eulogy erected in his honor.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Xu Ling carved a mountain inscription and erected a eulogy for him.

entries.zh: 初在縉雲山，太極真人徐君降之曰：「汝年出八十，當為王者師，然後得道也。」
entries.en: While he was still on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected Man of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, appeared to him and said: "When you pass eighty, you will become a king's teacher, and only then will you attain the Way."
entries.literal: When he was first on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected Man of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, descended to him and said: "When your years pass eighty, you shall become teacher to a king—only then will you attain the Way."

entries.zh: 晉王廣鎮揚州，知其名，手書召之曰：「夫道得眾妙，法體自然，包涵二儀，混成萬物，人能弘道，道不虛行。
entries.en: When Prince Guang of Jin was stationed at Yangzhou, he learned Xu Ze's name and wrote him a personal summons: "The Way gathers all subtleties; the Law accords with nature; it embraces yin and yang and blends them into the ten thousand things. When a man can enlarge the Way, the Way does not pass in vain.
entries.literal: Prince of Jin Guang garrisoned Yangzhou, learned his name, and wrote him a personal summons, saying: "The Way attains the myriad subtleties; the Law embodies nature; it embraces the two principles and blends to form the ten thousand things; if a man can expand the Way, the Way will not act in vain.

entries.zh: 先生履德養空，宗玄齊物，深明義味，曉達法門。
entries.en: You, Master, practice virtue and cultivate emptiness, take the Mysterious as your guide and treat all things as equal; you deeply grasp the meaning of righteousness and clearly understand the gates of the Law.
entries.literal: You, Master, tread virtue and nurture emptiness, take the Mysterious as your standard and equalize things; you deeply understand the flavor of righteousness and clearly penetrate the gates of the Law.

entries.zh: 悅性沖玄，怡神虛白，餐松餌術，棲息煙霞。
entries.en: Your nature delights in purity and mystery; your spirit rests in tranquil emptiness; you feed on pine and live by alchemical arts, dwelling among mist and colored clouds.
entries.literal: Your nature delights in the subtle and mysterious; your spirit is serene in empty whiteness; you dine on pine and feed on arts; you dwell in mist and rosy clouds.

entries.zh: 望赤城而待風雲，遊玉堂而駕龍鳳，雖複藏名台嶽，猶且騰實江淮，藉甚嘉猷，有勞寤寐。
entries.en: You gaze toward Mount Chicheng awaiting wind and clouds, roam the Jade Hall borne by dragon and phoenix; though you hide your name on lofty peaks, your worth still shines across the Jiang-Huai, and your fine counsel has long occupied my thoughts day and night.
entries.literal: Gazing toward Chicheng while awaiting wind and clouds, roaming the Jade Hall while driving dragon and phoenix—though you hide your name on mountain peaks, your substance still soars in the Jiang-Huai; your excellent counsel is widely praised; I have toiled waking and sleeping.

entries.zh: 欽承素道，久積虛襟，側席幽人，夢想岩穴。
entries.en: I reverently honor the pure Way and have long kept an open heart; I sit with seat askew awaiting a recluse and dream of life in mountain caves.
entries.literal: I reverently inherit the pure Way and have long stored an empty breast; I sit askance awaiting the recluse and dream of mountain caves.

entries.zh: 霜風已冷，海氣將寒，偃息茂林，道體休悆。
entries.en: The frost wind has turned cold and the sea air is growing chill; rest in the deep forest and let your body of the Way find its ease.
entries.literal: Frost wind has already turned cold and sea air will soon be chill; rest in the lush forest—your Way-body is at ease.

entries.zh: 昔商山四皓，輕舉漢庭，淮南八公，來儀籓邸。
entries.en: Long ago the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang readily entered the Han court, and the Eight Lords of Huainan came to serve at a prince's residence.
entries.literal: Formerly the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang lightly rose to the Han court; the Eight Lords of Huainan came in ritual to a prince's residence.

entries.zh: 古今雖異，山谷不殊，市朝之隱，前賢已說，導凡述聖，非先生而誰！
entries.en: Times may change, but mountains and valleys remain the same; sages of old already spoke of hiding in plain sight within the city; to guide the ordinary and expound the sacred—if not you, Master, then who?
entries.literal: Past and present differ, yet valleys and hills are not different; reclusion in the marketplace—former sages have already spoken of it; to guide the common and declare the sage—if not you, Master, then who!

entries.zh: 故遣使人，往彼延請，想無勞束帶，賁然來思，不待蒲輪，去彼空穀。
entries.en: Therefore I send an envoy to invite you; I trust you need not trouble to dress formally—come at once in splendid readiness, without waiting for a carriage of rush wheels to draw you from your empty valley.
entries.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to go there and invite you; I think you need not trouble to gird your sash—come splendidly; wait not for the rush-wheeled carriage—leave that empty valley.

entries.zh: 希能屈己，佇望披雲。」
entries.en: I hope you will condescend to come; I stand waiting for the clouds to part."
entries.literal: I hope you can humble yourself; I stand awaiting the parting of clouds."

entries.zh: 則謂門人曰：「吾今年八十一，王來召我，徐君之旨，信而有徵。」
entries.en: Xu Ze told his disciples: "I am eighty-one this year, and the Prince has summoned me; Lord Xu's prophecy has proved true."
entries.literal: Ze told his disciples: "I am eighty-one this year; the Prince has come to summon me—the words of Lord Xu are trustworthy and have proof."

entries.zh: 於是遂詣揚州。
entries.en: With that he set out for Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 晉王將請受道法，則辭以時日不便。
entries.en: When the Prince of Jin was about to receive instruction in the Way, Ze declined, saying the time was not auspicious.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way and its methods, Ze declined on the grounds that the time was not suitable.

entries.zh: 其後夕中，命侍者取香火，如平常朝禮之儀。
entries.en: That evening he had his attendants bring incense and performed the rites he usually observed at dawn.
entries.literal: That evening he ordered his attendants to fetch incense and fire and performed the usual rites of morning audience.

entries.zh: 至於五更而死，支體柔弱如生，停留數旬，顏色無變。
entries.en: At the fifth watch he died; his body remained supple as in life, and for several weeks his complexion did not change.
entries.literal: At the fifth watch he died; his limbs were soft as in life; for several tens of days his complexion did not change.

entries.zh: 晉王下書曰：「天臺真隱東海徐先生，虛確居宗，沖玄成德，齊物處外，檢行安身。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin issued a proclamation: "The true recluse of Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai, took emptiness and certainty as his foundation, subtle mystery as his completed virtue, treated all things as equal while dwelling apart from the world, and disciplined his conduct to preserve his person.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin issued a document: "The true recluse of Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai—empty certainty as his standard, subtle mystery as his completed virtue, equalizing things while dwelling outside, restraining conduct to settle his person.

entries.zh: 草褐蒲衣，餐松餌術，棲隱靈岳，五十餘年。
entries.en: Clad in grass and rush, feeding on pine and living by alchemical arts, he dwelt hidden on sacred mountains for more than fifty years.
entries.literal: In grass cloak and rush garment, dining on pine and feeding on arts, dwelling hidden on spirit peaks—for more than fifty years.

entries.zh: 卓矣仙才，飄然勝氣，千尋萬頃，莫測其涯。
entries.en: His transcendent gifts were extraordinary, his spirit lofty and free; like a thousand fathoms of depth or ten thousand acres of breadth, none could fathom his limits.
entries.literal: Transcendent talent surpassing others, an ethereal victor's spirit—a thousand fathoms, ten thousand acres, none can measure its bounds.

entries.zh: 寡人欽承道風，久餐德素，頻遣使乎，遠此延屈，冀得虔受上法，式建良緣。
entries.en: I have long reverenced the wind of the Way and nourished myself on your pure virtue; again and again I sent envoys to invite you from afar, hoping devoutly to receive the supreme teaching and establish a worthy bond.
entries.literal: I have reverently inherited the wind of the Way and long fed on pure virtue; repeatedly I sent envoys to invite you from afar, hoping devoutly to receive the supreme Law and firmly establish a good bond.

entries.zh: 至此甫爾，未淹旬日，厭塵羽化，反真靈府。
entries.en: He had only just arrived, less than ten days ago, when he cast off the dusty world, ascended in transformation, and returned to the true realm of spirit.
entries.literal: He had only just arrived, not ten days full, when he wearied of the dust, transformed in feather, and returned to the true numinous realm.

entries.zh: 身體柔軟，顏色不變，經方所謂屍解地仙者哉！
entries.en: His body remained soft and his complexion unchanged—is this not what the medical classics call corpse liberation and earthly immortality!
entries.literal: His body soft and supple, his color unchanged—is this not what medical classics call corpse liberation into an earthly immortal!

entries.zh: 誠複師禮未申，而心許有在，雖忘怛化，猶愴於懷，喪事所資，隨須供給。
entries.en: Though the rites of discipleship were never completed, my heart had already pledged itself to him; though I should rejoice in his transformation, sorrow still fills my breast; provide whatever his funeral requires.
entries.literal: Truly teacher's rites were not yet fulfilled, yet a promise of the heart remains; though I forget sorrow at his transformation, grief still lodges in my breast; whatever the funeral requires, supply it as needed.

entries.zh: 霓裳羽蓋，既且騰雲，空槨餘衣，詎藉墳壟！
entries.en: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies—he has already ascended on clouds; an empty coffin and leftover garments—what need has he of mound and tomb!
entries.literal: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies—already he mounts the clouds; an empty coffin and leftover garments—how could he rely on mound and tomb!

entries.zh: 但杖為猶存，示同俗法，宜遣使人，送還天臺定葬。」
entries.en: Only his staff remains, to show conformity with ordinary custom; send envoys to return him to Mount Tiantai for proper burial."
entries.literal: Only his staff remains, to show conformity with common custom; you should send envoys to return him to Tiantai for proper burial."

entries.zh: 是時自江都至於天臺，在道多見則徒步，雲得放還。
entries.en: At that time, from Jiangdu to Mount Tiantai, travelers on the road often saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.
entries.literal: At that time from Jiangdu to Tiantai, on the road many saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.

entries.zh: 至其舊居，取經書道法，分遺弟子，仍令淨掃一房，曰：「若有客至，宜延之於此。」
entries.en: When he reached his old dwelling, he took his scriptures and Daoist texts and distributed them among his disciples; he had a room swept clean and said, "If guests come, receive them here."
entries.literal: When he reached his old dwelling, he took scriptures and Daoist methods and distributed them among his disciples; he also had a room swept clean and said, "If guests come, you should receive them here."

entries.zh: 然後跨石樑而去，不知所之。
entries.en: Then he crossed a stone bridge and departed—to where, no one knew.
entries.literal: Then he crossed a stone bridge and departed—none knew where he went.

entries.zh: 須臾，屍柩至，方知其靈化。
entries.en: Shortly afterward the coffin with his body arrived, and only then did they understand that he had undergone spiritual transformation.
entries.literal: In a moment the coffin with his corpse arrived, and only then did they know of his spiritual transformation.

entries.zh: 時年八十二。
entries.en: He was eighty-two years old at the time.
entries.literal: He was then eighty-two years old.

entries.zh: 晉王聞而益異之，賵物千段，遣畫工圖其狀貌，令柳抃為之贊曰：「可道非道，常道無名。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin heard this and was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand lengths of goods as funeral gifts, had painters depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bian to compose an encomium that began, "The Way that can be spoken is not the eternal Way; the eternal Way has no name.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin heard and was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand lengths of goods as funeral gifts, had painters depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bian to compose an encomium, saying, "The Way that can be spoken is not the eternal Way; the eternal Way has no name.

entries.zh: 上德不德，至德無盈。
entries.en: The highest virtue is not virtuous; the utmost virtue has no fullness.
entries.literal: The highest virtue is not virtuous; the utmost virtue has no fullness.

entries.zh: 玄風扇矣，而有先生。
entries.en: The mysterious wind had spread abroad, and there was the Master.
entries.literal: The mysterious wind has fanned forth, and there was the Master.

entries.zh: 夙煉金液，怡神玉清。
entries.en: Long he refined the golden elixir, delighting his spirit in jade purity.
entries.literal: Long he refined golden elixir, delighting his spirit in jade purity.

entries.zh: 石髓方軟，雲丹欲成。
entries.en: Stone marrow had just softened; cloud cinnabar was about to be perfected.
entries.literal: Stone marrow had just softened; cloud cinnabar was about to be perfected.

entries.zh: 言追葛稚，將侶茅嬴。
entries.en: He spoke of following Ge Hong and would take Mao Ying as his companion.
entries.literal: He spoke of following Ge Hong and would take as companion Mao Ying.

entries.zh: 我王遙屬，爰感靈誠。
entries.en: Our prince from afar was drawn to him and thus felt his numinous sincerity.
entries.literal: Our prince from afar was attached to him and thus felt his numinous sincerity.

entries.zh: 柱下暫啟，河上沉精。
entries.en: For a time he opened the pillar beneath; on the river he sank his essence.
entries.literal: For a time he opened the pillar beneath; on the river he sank his essence.

entries.zh: 留符告信，化杖飛聲。
entries.en: He left a talisman to announce his faith; transforming his staff, he flew away with a sound.
entries.literal: He left a talisman to announce faith; transforming his staff, he flew with a sound.

entries.zh: 永思靈跡，曷用攄情？
entries.en: Forever thinking on his numinous traces—how may one give full vent to feeling?
entries.literal: Forever thinking on his numinous traces—how may one give vent to feeling?

entries.zh: 時披素繪，如臨赤城。」
entries.en: At times one spreads the plain portrait, as if facing Red Wall."
entries.literal: At times one spreads the plain painting, as if facing Red Wall."

entries.zh: 賾字祖浚，七歲能屬文，容貌短小，有口才。
entries.en: Ze, styled Zujun, could compose essays at seven; he was short in stature but gifted with a ready tongue.
entries.literal: Ze, style Zujun, at seven years could compose literary pieces; his appearance was short in stature, and he had eloquence.

entries.zh: 開皇初，秦孝王薦之，射策高第，詔與諸儒定禮樂，授校書郎。
entries.en: Early in the Kaihuang reign, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him; he placed at the top of the policy examination and was ordered to join the Confucian scholars in fixing rites and music, receiving appointment as Collator.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince of Qin Xia recommended him; in the archery-and-policy examination he ranked at the top; an edict appointed him with various Confucians to fix rites and music, and he was made Collator.

entries.zh: 尋轉協律郎，太常卿蘇威雅重之。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Director of Harmonization, and Su Wei, the Minister of Ceremonies, greatly valued him.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of Harmonization; Su Wei, Minister of Ceremonies, held him in high esteem.

entries.zh: 母憂去職，性至孝，水漿不入口者五日。
entries.en: When his mother died he resigned his post; profoundly filial by nature, he went five days without food or drink.
entries.literal: On his mother's death he left office; by nature deeply filial, for five days he took no water or broth.

entries.zh: 征為河南、豫章二王侍讀，每更日來往二王之第。
entries.en: He was summoned to serve as Reader to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, spending alternate days at each prince's residence.
entries.literal: Summoned as Reader to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, he alternated days traveling between the two princes' residences.

entries.zh: 及河南為晉王，轉記室參軍，自此去豫章。
entries.en: When the Prince of Henan was made Prince of Jin, Ze became Staff Secretary and thereafter ceased attending Yuzhang.
entries.literal: When Henan became Prince of Jin, he was transferred to Staff Secretary; from then on he left Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 王重之不已，遺賾書曰：
entries.en: The Prince continued to esteem him and sent Ze a letter that read:
entries.literal: The Prince valued him ever more highly and sent Ze a letter, saying:

entries.zh: 時有建安宋玉泉、會稽孔道茂、丹陽王遠知等，亦行辟穀，以松水自給，皆為煬帝所重。
entries.en: At the time there were Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, and others who also practiced grain avoidance and sustained themselves on pine water—all were valued by Emperor Yang.
entries.literal: At the time there were Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, and others who also practiced grain avoidance, sustaining themselves on pine water—all were valued by Emperor Yang.

entries.zh: 豫章得書，賚米五十石，並衣服錢帛。
entries.en: The Prince of Yuzhang received the letter and sent fifty shi of rice along with clothing, money, and silk.
entries.literal: Yuzhang received the letter and bestowed fifty shi of rice, together with clothing, money, and silk.

entries.zh: 時晉邸文翰，多成其手。
entries.en: At that time most of the official writings of the Prince of Jin's household came from Ze's pen.
entries.literal: At that time the literary compositions of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his hand.

entries.zh: 王入東宮，除太子齋帥，俄遷舍人。
entries.en: When the Prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Fast and was soon promoted to Attendant.
entries.literal: When the Prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Fast; soon he was promoted to Attendant.

entries.zh: 及元德太子薨，以疾歸於家。
entries.en: After the Yuande Heir Apparent died, Ze went home, pleading illness.
entries.literal: When the Yuande Heir Apparent died, Ze returned home on account of illness.

entries.zh: 後征授起居舍人。
entries.en: He was later summoned and appointed Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
entries.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Attendant of the Diary of Rest and Movement.

entries.zh: 大業四年，從駕汾陽宮，次河陽鎮。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Fenyang Palace and stopped at Heyang garrison.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, he accompanied the emperor to Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang garrison.

entries.zh: 藍田令王曇于藍田山得一玉人，長三尺四寸，著大領衣，冠幘，奏之。
entries.en: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, found a jade figure on Mount Lantian three feet four inches tall, dressed in a broad-collared robe and wearing a headcloth, and presented it to the throne.
entries.literal: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, obtained a jade figure on Mount Lantian, three feet four inches tall, wearing a broad-collared robe and a headcloth; he reported it.

entries.zh: 詔問群臣，莫有識者，賾答曰：「謹按漢文已前，未有冠幘，即是文帝以來所製作也。
entries.en: The emperor asked his ministers, but none could identify it. Ze answered: "I respectfully observe that before Emperor Wen of Han there was no such headcloth; it must have been made since Emperor Wen's reign.
entries.literal: An edict asked the ministers; none recognized it. Ze replied: "I respectfully note that before Emperor Wen of Han there was no headcloth such as this; it is something made since Emperor Wen's time.

entries.zh: 臣見魏大司農盧元明撰《嵩高山廟記》雲，有神人，以玉為形，像長數寸，或出或隱，出則令世延長。
entries.en: I have read in Lu Yuanming's Record of the Songshan Shrine, written when he was Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, that a divine being took form in jade only a few inches long, appearing and disappearing; when it appeared, the age was lengthened.
entries.literal: I have seen in the Record of the Songshan Shrine by Lu Yuanming, Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, that there was a divine person in jade form, the image several inches long, appearing and vanishing; when it appeared, the age was prolonged.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下應天順民，定鼎嵩洛，嶽神自見，臣敢稱慶。」
entries.en: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty responds to Heaven and accords with the people, establishing the capital at Song and Luo; the mountain god has revealed himself— I dare offer congratulations."
entries.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty responds to Heaven and follows the people, establishing the tripod at Song and Luo—the mountain god has appeared of itself; I dare proclaim congratulations."

entries.zh: 因再拜，百官畢賀，天子大悅，賜縑二百匹。
entries.en: He bowed twice; all the officials congratulated him; the emperor was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: He then bowed twice; all officials congratulated; the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 從駕登太行山，詔問賾曰：「何處有羊腸阪？」
entries.en: While accompanying the emperor up Mount Taihang, he was asked by imperial edict: "Where is Yangchang Slope?"
entries.literal: Accompanying the imperial procession up Mount Taihang, an edict asked Ze: "Where is Yangchang Slope?"

entries.zh: 賾對曰：「臣按《漢書·地理志》，上党壺關縣有羊腸阪。」
entries.en: Ze answered: "According to the Geography Monograph in the Book of Han, Yangchang Slope is in Huchang County, Shangdang."
entries.literal: Ze replied: "According to the Geography Monograph of the Book of Han, Huchang County in Shangdang has Yangchang Slope."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「不是。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "That is not the one."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "That is not it."

entries.zh: 又答曰：「臣按皇甫士安撰《地書》雲，太原北九十裡有羊腸阪。」
entries.en: He answered again: "According to Huangfu Mi's Geographic Book, Yangchang Slope lies ninety li north of Taiyuan."
entries.literal: He answered again: "According to the Geographic Book by Huangfu Mi, ninety li north of Taiyuan there is Yangchang Slope."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「是也。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "That is the one."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "That is it."

entries.zh: 因謂牛弘曰：「崔祖浚所謂問一知二。」
entries.en: He then said to Niu Hong: "This is what Cui Zujun meant by 'ask one and know two.'"
entries.literal: He then said to Niu Hong: "That is what Cui Zujun means by 'ask one and know two.'"

entries.zh: 五年，受詔與諸儒撰《區宇圖志》二百五十卷，奏之。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was ordered to compile, with other scholars, the Geographic Records in 250 volumes, and submitted the work.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he received an edict to compile with various scholars the Geographic Records in 250 volumes, and submitted it.

entries.zh: 帝不善之，更令虞世基、許善心衍為六百卷。
entries.en: The emperor was dissatisfied with it and had Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin expand it to six hundred volumes.
entries.literal: The Emperor was displeased with it and had Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin expand it to six hundred volumes.

entries.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。
entries.en: When his father died he resigned, but was soon recalled and ordered back to duty.
entries.literal: On his father's death he left office; soon he was restored and ordered to resume his duties.

entries.zh: 遼東之役，授鷹揚長史，置遼東郡縣名，皆賾之議也。
entries.en: During the Liaodong campaign he was made Chief Secretary of the Eagle-Flying Guard; the names chosen for the new Liaodong commanderies and counties were all proposed by Ze.
entries.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Eagle-Flying Guard; the names of the Liaodong commanderies and counties established were all Ze's proposals.

entries.zh: 奉詔作《東征記》。
entries.en: By imperial command he composed the Record of the Eastern Expedition.
entries.literal: By imperial order he wrote the Record of the Eastern Expedition.

entries.zh: 九年，除越王長史。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Secretary to the Prince of Yue.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Secretary to the Prince of Yue.

entries.zh: 于時山東盜賊蜂起，帝令撫慰高陽、襄國，歸首者八百餘人。
entries.en: At that time bandits were rising throughout the east; the emperor sent him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and more than eight hundred men surrendered.
entries.literal: At that time bandits rose in swarms east of the mountains; the Emperor ordered him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo; more than eight hundred surrendered.

entries.zh: 十二年，從駕江都。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Jiangdu.

entries.zh: 宇文化及之弑帝也，引為著作郎，稱疾不起。
entries.en: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Ze was offered the post of Compiler but pleaded illness and refused to serve.
entries.literal: When Yuwen Huaji assassinated the Emperor, Ze was appointed Compiler but pleaded illness and did not take up the post.

entries.zh: 在路發疾，卒于彭城，時年六十九。
entries.en: He fell ill on the road and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.
entries.literal: On the road he fell ill and died at Pengcheng, aged sixty-nine.

entries.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺、東苑，慕義如林。
entries.en: In the days of the Han western capital and the Liang prince's founding of his realm, at Pingtai and the Eastern Park men who admired virtue gathered like trees in a forest.
entries.literal: In olden days the Han western capital and the Liang prince's founding of his state—with Pingtai and Dongyuan, those who admired righteousness were as thick as a forest.

entries.zh: 馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。
entries.en: Sima Xiangru left his post in the Palace Cavalry Guard, and Mei Sheng relinquished the governorship of Hongnong.
entries.literal: Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Cavalry Guard; Mei Sheng gave up the governorship of Hongnong.

entries.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗切怪之，何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？
entries.en: Whenever I read the historical records, I have always wondered why they would abandon official honor and settle in a prince's household.
entries.literal: Whenever I read the histories, I have deeply wondered: why cast off official glory and linger in a prince's residence?

entries.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。
entries.en: Looking from today back to antiquity, I finally grasp their noble purpose.
entries.literal: Viewing the past from the present, I now understand their lofty intent.

entries.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！
entries.en: Those two men surely did not act in vain!
entries.literal: Those two men—surely they were not without purpose!

entries.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似涉蒙山，對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。
entries.en: You are erudite and retentive, probing depths and reaching far; beside the Han minister's three satchels of books you seem to traverse Mount Meng, and before the Liang chancellor's five cartloads you seem to swallow Lake Yunmeng whole.
entries.literal: You are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing deep and reaching far; compared with the Han minister's three satchels, it is as if crossing Mount Meng; facing the Liang chancellor's five cartloads, it is as if swallowing the Yunmeng marsh.

entries.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。
entries.en: My elder brother honors the worthy and cherishes scholars with tireless devotion; he built a palace for Guo Wei and keeps sweet wine ready for Mu Sheng.
entries.literal: My elder brother reveres the worthy and esteems scholars, cherishing them without tiring; he first built the palace of Guo Wei and always keeps the wine of Mu Sheng on hand.

entries.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河，地方七百，牢籠曲阜，城兼七十，包舉臨淄，大啟南陽，方開東閤。
entries.en: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his pledge over land and river; his territory spans seven hundred li, embracing Qufu; his cities exceed seventy, taking in Linzi; he has thrown wide the gates of Nanyang and is now opening his eastern hall to guests.
entries.literal: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over the mountains and rivers; his territory extends seven hundred li, enclosing Qufu; his cities number seventy and more, embracing Linzi; he has greatly opened Nanyang and is now opening the eastern gate.

entries.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。
entries.en: I picture you riding beneath a flying canopy, trailing your long robe, seated on a tortoiseshell mat in pearl slippers, singing of mountain cassia and composing verses on the bamboo by the pool.
entries.literal: I imagine you joining under a flying canopy, trailing a long robe, resting on a tortoiseshell mat, treading in pearl slippers, singing of the towering mountain cassia and composing on the lush pool bamboo.

entries.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！
entries.en: Such is his lofty station, such his elegant bearing—what good fortune, what good fortune! What pleasure could equal it!
entries.literal: His lofty eminence is like that; his refinement is like this—great fortune, great fortune! What joy could compare!

entries.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖，才謝天人，多慚子建，書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。
entries.en: Gazing toward the capital, I think of Dezao; my talent falls far short of heaven and earth, and I feel deeply ashamed before Zijian; words cannot say all I mean, so why multiply them?
entries.literal: Looking down upon the upper capital, I miss Dezao; in talent I fall short of heaven and man; I am much ashamed before Zijian; the letter cannot exhaust my meaning—why await elaborate words?

entries.zh: 張文詡，河東人也。
entries.en: Zhang Wenxu was a native of Hedong.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenxu was a native of Hedong.

entries.zh: 父琚，開皇中為洹水令，以清正聞。
entries.en: His father Ju served as Magistrate of Huanshui during the Kaihuang era and was known for purity and uprightness.
entries.literal: His father Ju, in the Kaihuang era served as Magistrate of Huanshui and was known for purity and uprightness.

entries.zh: 有書數千卷，教訓子侄，皆以明經自達。
entries.en: He owned several thousand volumes of books and instructed his sons and nephews, all of whom attained office through mastery of the classics.
entries.literal: He had several thousand volumes of books and instructed his sons and nephews, all of whom attained office through mastery of the classics.

entries.zh: 文詡博覽文籍，特精《三禮》，其《周易》、《詩》、《書》及《春秋三傳》，並皆通習。
entries.en: Wenxu read broadly in literary works and was especially expert in the Three Rites; the Book of Changes, Book of Odes, Book of Documents, and the three commentaries to the Spring and Autumn Annals—all he mastered thoroughly.
entries.literal: Wenxu read broadly in literary works and was especially expert in the Three Rites; the Changes, Odes, Documents, and the three commentaries to the Spring and Autumn—all he mastered thoroughly.

entries.zh: 每好鄭玄注解，以為通博，其諸儒異說，亦皆詳究焉。
entries.en: He always favored Zheng Xuan's commentaries, considering them comprehensive and penetrating; the varying doctrines of other scholars he also investigated in detail.
entries.literal: He always favored Zheng Xuan's commentaries, considering them comprehensive and broad; the varying doctrines of other Ru scholars he also investigated in detail.

entries.zh: 高祖引致天下名儒碩學之士，其房暉遠、張仲讓、孔籠之徒，並延之于博士之位。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu drew in famous scholars and eminent learned men from across the empire; Fang Xianyuan, Zhang Zhongrang, Kong Long, and their kind were all invited to serve as Erudites.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu drew in famous Ru scholars and eminent learned men from all the empire; Fang Xianyuan, Zhang Zhongrang, Kong Long, and their kind were all extended invitations to the post of Erudite.

entries.zh: 文詡時遊太學，暉遠等莫不推伏之，學內翕然，咸共宗仰。
entries.en: When Wenxu visited the Imperial Academy, Xianyuan and the others all deferred to him; within the academy there was harmony, and all revered him together.
entries.literal: When Wenxu visited the Imperial Academy, Xianyuan and the others all deferred to him; within the academy there was harmony, and all together revered him.

entries.zh: 其門生多詣文詡，請質凝滯，文詡輒博引證據，辨說無窮，唯其所擇。
entries.en: His students often went to Wenxu to request clarification of points that troubled them; Wenxu would cite evidence broadly and argue without end, following only the course he chose.
entries.literal: His students often went to Wenxu to request clarification of points that troubled them; Wenxu would broadly cite evidence and argue without end, following only what he chose.

entries.zh: 治書侍御史皇甫誕一時朝彥，恆執弟子之禮。
entries.en: Huangfu Dan, Attending Secretary in the Imperial Library, was a leading figure of the court in his day and always observed the rites of a disciple toward him.
entries.literal: Huangfu Dan, Attending Secretary in the Imperial Library, was a leading figure of the court in his day and always observed the rites of a disciple toward him.

entries.zh: 適至南台，遽飾所乘馬，就學邀屈。
entries.en: When he happened to reach the Southern Terrace, he hastily adorned the horse he rode and went to the academy to invite Wenxu to accompany him.
entries.literal: When he happened to reach the Southern Terrace, he hastily adorned the horse he rode and went to the academy to invite and detain Wenxu.

entries.zh: 文詡每牽馬步進，意在不因人以自致也。
entries.en: Wenxu always led the horse and walked alongside, his intent being not to advance himself by relying on others.
entries.literal: Wenxu always led the horse and walked alongside, his intent being not to advance himself by relying on others.

entries.zh: 右僕射蘇威聞其名而召之，與語，大悅，勸令從官。
entries.en: Su Wei, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, heard his name and summoned him; after conversing with him he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office.
entries.literal: Su Wei, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, heard his name and summoned him; after conversing with him he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office.

entries.zh: 文詡意不在仕，固辭焉。
entries.en: Wenxu had no wish to serve in office and firmly declined.
entries.literal: Wenxu's intent was not in office; he firmly declined.

entries.zh: 仁壽末，學廢，文詡策杖而歸，灌園為業。
entries.en: At the end of the Renshou era the academy was abolished; Wenxu leaned on his staff and returned home, making irrigation and gardening his occupation.
entries.literal: At the end of the Renshou era the academy was abolished; Wenxu leaned on his staff and returned home, making irrigation and gardening his occupation.

entries.zh: 州郡頻舉，皆不應命。
entries.en: The province and commandery repeatedly recommended him, but he never responded to summons.
entries.literal: The province and commandery repeatedly recommended him, but he never responded to summons.

entries.zh: 事母以孝聞。
entries.en: He became known for his filial devotion to his mother.
entries.literal: He became known for filial service to his mother.

entries.zh: 每以德化人，鄉黨頗移風俗。
entries.en: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and district considerably shifted their customs.
entries.literal: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and district considerably shifted their customs.

entries.zh: 嘗有人夜中竊刈其麥者，見而避之，盜因感悟，棄麥而謝。
entries.en: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and withdrew, and the thief, moved by this, abandoned the wheat and apologized.
entries.literal: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and withdrew, and the thief, moved by this, abandoned the wheat and apologized.

entries.zh: 文詡慰諭之，自誓不言，固令持去。
entries.en: Wenxu comforted him, swore himself not to speak of it, and firmly had him take the wheat away.
entries.literal: Wenxu comforted and instructed him, swore himself not to speak of it, and firmly had him take the wheat away.

entries.zh: 經數年，盜者向鄉人說之，始為遠近所悉。
entries.en: After several years the thief told fellow townspeople of it, and only then was it known far and near.
entries.literal: After several years the thief told fellow townspeople of it, and only then was it known far and near.

entries.zh: 鄰家築牆，心有不直，文詡因毀舊堵以應之。
entries.en: A neighbor built a wall that was not quite straight; Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to match it.
entries.literal: A neighbor built a wall with a mind not quite straight; Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to match it.

entries.zh: 文詡嘗有腰疾，會醫者自言善禁，文詡令禁之，遂為刃所傷，至於頓伏床枕。
entries.en: Wenxu once had a pain in his lower back; a physician who claimed skill in spell-binding treated him and wounded him with a blade, so that he collapsed on his bed.
entries.literal: Wenxu once had a pain in his lower back; it happened that a physician claimed skill in spell-binding; Wenxu had him perform it and was wounded by a blade, to the point of collapsing on bed and pillow.

entries.zh: 醫者叩頭請罪，文詡遽遣之，因為其隱，謂妻子曰：「吾昨風眩，落坑所致。」
entries.en: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness; Wenxu immediately sent him away and covered the matter for him, telling his wife and children, "Yesterday I had a dizzy spell and fell into a pit—that is what caused it."
entries.literal: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness; Wenxu immediately sent him away and covered the matter for him, telling his wife and children, "Yesterday I had a dizzy spell from wind and fell into a pit—that is what caused it."

entries.zh: 其掩人之短，皆此類也。
entries.en: His way of covering others' faults was all of this kind.
entries.literal: His covering of others' faults was all of this kind.

entries.zh: 州縣以其貧素，將加振恤，輒辭不受。
entries.en: The province and county, because he was poor and plain, were about to offer relief and support, but he always declined and would not accept.
entries.literal: The province and county, because he was poor and plain, were about to add relief and support, but he always declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 每閒居無事，從容長歎曰：「老冉冉而將至，恐修名之不立！」
entries.en: Whenever at leisure with nothing to do, he would calmly sigh and say, "Old age comes on gradually—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!"
entries.literal: Whenever at leisure with nothing to do, he would calmly sigh long and say, "Old age comes on gradually—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!"

entries.zh: 以如意擊幾，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫原憲焉。
entries.en: He would strike the armrest with his ruyi scepter, each blow landing in its place; men of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
entries.literal: He would strike the armrest with his ruyi scepter, each blow landing in its place; men of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

entries.zh: 終於家，年四十。
entries.en: He died at home at the age of forty.
entries.literal: He died at home, aged forty.

entries.zh: 鄉人為立碑頌，號曰張先生。
entries.en: Fellow townspeople erected a stele in praise of him and called him Master Zhang.
entries.literal: Fellow townspeople erected a stele in praise of him and called him Master Zhang.

entries.zh: 隋書卷七十七列傳第四十二
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume 77, Biography 42
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 77, Biography 42

entries.zh: 曆觀前代外戚之家，乘母后之權以取高位厚秩者多矣，然而鮮有克終之美，必罹顛覆之患，何哉？
entries.en: Surveying the imperial affines of earlier dynasties, one finds countless families who rode an empress's power to high office and rich stipends, yet scarcely any who finished well; ruin was almost inevitable. Why?
entries.literal: Looking through successive ages at households of imperial affines, there were many who, relying on the empress's authority, seized high rank and generous emoluments; yet few ever achieved a fine end—they invariably met with the calamity of overturn. Why was this?

entries.zh: 皆由乎無德而尊，不知紀極，忽于滿盈之戒，罔念高危之咎，故鬼瞰其室，憂必及之。
entries.en: The reason lay in gaining rank without merit, in losing all sense of limit, in ignoring the lesson that plenty invites spillover and high position invites fall—the house watched by ghosts, and trouble never far behind.
entries.literal: All were because, honored without virtue, they did not know moderation; heedless of the warning against fullness to overflowing, unmindful of the fault of standing in extreme peril—therefore spirits peered into their chambers, and affliction was bound to reach them.

entries.zh: 夫其誠著艱難，功宣社稷，不以謙沖自牧，未免顛蹶之禍，而況道不足以濟時，仁不足以利物，自矜於己，以富貴驕人者乎？
entries.en: Even men whose loyalty had been proved in hardship and whose service had strengthened the realm, if they failed to keep themselves humble, still risked ruin—what then of those whose conduct could not steady the times, whose kindness could not help others, who merely preened on their own good fortune and lorded their riches over everyone else?
entries.literal: Even those whose sincerity shone through hardship and whose achievements proclaimed the altars of state, if they did not govern themselves with humility and restraint, could not escape the calamity of a fall—how much more those whose Way was insufficient to rescue the age, whose benevolence was insufficient to benefit things, who prided themselves and flaunted wealth and rank before others?

entries.zh: 此呂、霍、上官、閻、梁、竇、鄧所以繼踵而亡滅者也。
entries.en: This is why the Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng clans rose in turn only to be destroyed.
entries.literal: This is why the houses of Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng followed one another in succession yet perished.

entries.zh: 昔文皇潛躍之際，獻後便相推轂，煬帝大橫方兆，蕭妃密勿經綸，是以恩禮綢繆，始終不易。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen was still struggling toward power, Empress Xian already shared in steering the realm; when Emperor Yang's reign was taking shape, Lady Xiao joined him in the closest counsel. Favor and ceremony therefore ran deep and held steady to the end.
entries.literal: Formerly, when Emperor Wen was still rising in obscurity, Empress Xian already helped turn the wheel of state; when Emperor Yang's great mandate was just appearing, Consort Xiao took part in secret counsel on affairs of state—thus favor and ceremony were intimate and unchanging from first to last.

entries.zh: 然內外親戚，莫預朝權，昆弟在位，亦無殊寵。
entries.en: Yet none of their kin, whether by blood or marriage, was allowed into real power at court, and even brothers who held office received no special indulgence.
entries.literal: Yet among kinsmen within and without, none shared in court power; brothers who held office likewise received no extraordinary favor.

entries.zh: 至於居擅玉堂，家稱金穴，暉光戚裡，重灼四方，將三司以比儀，命五侯而同拜者，終始一代，寂無聞焉。
entries.en: As for the sort who seize the halls of state, whose homes are proverbial treasure vaults, whose glare dazzles the whole imperial clan and burns across the empire, who are treated like the Three Excellencies and have the Five Marquises bow beside them—for an entire reign there was not a trace of that.
entries.literal: As for those who monopolized the jade hall, whose households were called gold caves, whose brilliance lit the imperial affines and whose weight scorched the four quarters, who were paired in ceremony with the Three Excellencies and ordered the Five Marquises to bow with them—throughout a whole generation, not a whisper was heard of such things.

entries.zh: 考之前王，可謂矯其弊矣。
entries.en: Measured against earlier rulers, the Sui emperors may be said to have corrected that abuse.
entries.literal: Considering the former kings, one may say they corrected this abuse.

entries.zh: 故雖時經擾攘，無有陷於不義，市朝遷貿，而皆得以保全。
entries.en: So even when the times turned violent, none of these affines was driven into disgrace; though power shifted in the capital, they were still able to come through intact.
entries.literal: Therefore, although the age passed through turmoil, none fell into injustice; though markets and courts shifted and changed, all were able to preserve themselves.

entries.zh: 比夫憑藉寵私，階緣恩澤，乘其非據，旋就顛隕者，豈可同日而言哉！
entries.en: How can that be mentioned in the same breath as those who traded on private favor, climbed by imperial indulgence, seized what they had no right to hold, and were overturned almost at once?
entries.literal: Compared with those who relied on private favor, climbed by grace and bounty, seized what was not theirs to hold, and swiftly met with ruin—how can they be spoken of on the same day!

entries.zh: 此所謂愛之以禮，能改覆車。
entries.en: This is what it means to love one's kin with proper restraint and to keep the overturned cart from rolling again.
entries.literal: This is what is called loving them by means of ritual, and being able to overturn the overturned cart.

entries.zh: 輒敘其事，為《外戚傳》雲。
entries.en: I therefore relate these matters in the Biographies of Imperial Affines.
entries.literal: I therefore set forth these affairs and make them the "Biographies of Imperial Affines."

entries.zh: ○高祖外家呂氏
entries.en: ○ The Lü Clan, Maternal Kin of Gaozu
entries.literal: ○ The Lü Clan, Maternal Kin of Gaozu

entries.zh: 高祖外家呂氏，其族蓋微，平齊之後，求訪不知所在。
entries.en: Gaozu's mother's people, the Lü, were of humble origin; after the conquest of Qi, officials searched for them but could not find where they were.
entries.literal: Gaozu's maternal kin, the Lü clan, were in origin a humble family; after the pacification of Qi, searches were made but their whereabouts were unknown.

entries.zh: 至開皇初，濟南郡上言，有男子呂永吉，自稱有姑字苦桃，為楊忠妻。
entries.en: Early in the Kaihuang era, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed an aunt called Kutao had been the wife of Yang Zhong.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed to have an aunt styled Kutao who had been the wife of Yang Zhong.

entries.zh: 勘驗知是舅子，始追贈外祖雙周為上柱國、太尉、八州諸軍事、青州刺史，封齊郡公，諡曰敬，外祖母姚氏為齊敬公夫人。
entries.en: Investigation showed he was indeed a nephew on the mother's side. The court then posthumously honored the maternal grandfather Shuangzhou as Supreme Pillar of State, Grand Commandant, commander of military affairs in eight prefectures, and governor of Qing, enfeoffing him as Duke of Qi with the posthumous name Jing; the maternal grandmother, née Yao, was titled Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.
entries.literal: On investigation it was known that he was a nephew by the maternal line; only then were posthumous honors conferred on the maternal grandfather Shuangzhou as Supreme Pillar of State, Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Eight Prefectures, and Governor of Qing Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi commandery with the posthumous title Jing; the maternal grandmother, the Yao clan, was made Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.

entries.zh: 詔並改葬，于齊州立廟，置守塚十家。
entries.en: An edict ordered new burials, a temple built in Qi province, and ten households assigned to tend the graves.
entries.literal: An edict ordered them all reburied, a temple established in Qi province, and ten households appointed to guard the tombs.

entries.zh: 以永吉襲爵，留在京師。
entries.en: Yongji inherited the title and remained in the capital.
entries.literal: Yongji was made to inherit the title and was kept in the capital.

entries.zh: 大業中，授上党郡太守，性識庸劣，職務不理。
entries.en: In the Daye period he was made governor of Shangdang, but his mind was dull and he neglected his office.
entries.literal: During the Daye era he was appointed Governor of Shangdang commandery; his nature and understanding were coarse and inferior, and he did not attend to his duties.

entries.zh: 後去官，不知所終。
entries.en: He later left office, and nothing more is known of him.
entries.literal: Later he left office; no one knows how he ended.

entries.zh: 永吉從父道貴，性尤頑騃，言詞鄙陋。
entries.en: Yongji's cousin Daogui was even more obstinate and slow-witted, and his speech was coarse.
entries.literal: Yongji's father's younger cousin Daogui was by nature especially stubborn and dull, and his speech was vulgar and crude.

entries.zh: 初自鄉里征入長安，上見之悲泣。
entries.en: When he was first summoned from the countryside to Chang'an, the emperor wept at the sight of him.
entries.literal: When he was first summoned from the countryside into Chang'an, the emperor, on seeing him, wept in grief.

entries.zh: 道貴略無戚容，但連呼高祖名，雲：「種末定不可偷，大似苦桃姊。」
entries.en: Daogui showed no sign of family feeling at all. He only kept shouting Gaozu's personal name, saying, "The seed isn't set yet—you can't steal it. You're just like Big Sister Kutao."
entries.literal: Daogui showed scarcely any look of kinship feeling; he only kept calling Gaozu by his personal name, saying, "The seed is not yet fixed and must not be stolen—it is very like Elder Sister Kutao."

entries.zh: 是後數犯忌諱，動致違忤，上甚耽之。
entries.en: After that he broke taboo after taboo and constantly gave offense, until the emperor could hardly bear him.
entries.literal: Thereafter he repeatedly violated taboos and constantly gave offense; the emperor was deeply troubled by him.

entries.zh: 乃命高熲厚加供給，不許接對朝士。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Gao Jiong to provide for him generously but forbade him to associate with court officials.
entries.literal: The emperor then ordered Gao Jiong to supply him generously and forbade him to meet and converse with court officials.

entries.zh: 拜上儀同三司，出為濟南太守，令即之任，斷其入朝。
entries.en: He was made Senior Master of Uniformity of the Third Rank and sent out as governor of Jinan with orders to take up his post at once and never return to court.
entries.literal: He was appointed Senior Master of Uniformity of the Third Rank and sent out as Governor of Jinan, ordered to take up his post at once and cut off from attending court.

entries.zh: 道貴還至本郡，高自崇重，每與人言，自稱皇舅。
entries.en: Back in his home commandery, Daogui put on great airs and told everyone he was the emperor's uncle.
entries.literal: When Daogui returned to his home commandery, he held himself in high esteem; whenever he spoke with others he called himself the emperor's maternal uncle.

entries.zh: 數將儀衛出入閭裡，從故人游宴，官民鹹苦之。
entries.en: He often paraded through the streets with an escort, carousing with old friends, to the misery of officials and commoners alike.
entries.literal: He often led guards and attendants in and out of the lanes, followed old acquaintances to feasts and revels, and officials and commoners alike suffered from it.

entries.zh: 後郡廢，終於家，子孫無聞焉。
entries.en: When the commandery was later abolished, he died at home. Nothing more is known of his descendants.
entries.literal: Later the commandery was abolished; he died at home, and nothing was heard of his descendants.

entries.zh: 獨孤羅，字羅仁，雲中人也。
entries.en: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a native of Yunzhong.
entries.literal: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a native of Yunzhong.

entries.zh: 父信，初仕魏為荊州刺史。
entries.en: His father Xin first served Northern Wei as governor of Jing province.
entries.literal: His father Xin at first served Wei as Governor of Jing province.

entries.zh: 武帝之入關也，信棄父母妻子西歸長安，曆職顯貴，羅由是遂為高氏所囚。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Northern Wei entered the passes, Xin left his parents, wife, and children behind and went west to Chang'an, rising to high office; Luo was left behind and taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Northern Wei entered the passes, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices of eminent rank; because of this Luo was thereupon taken prisoner by the Gao clan.

entries.zh: 信後仕周為大司馬。
entries.en: Xin later served Zhou as Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Xin later served Zhou as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 及信為宇文護所誅，羅始見釋，寓居中山，孤貧無以自給。
entries.en: After Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was at last freed. He lived in Zhongshan, alone and destitute, with no way to support himself.
entries.literal: When Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was only then released; he lodged in Zhongshan, alone and poor, with no means to support himself.

entries.zh: 齊將獨孤永業以宗族之故，見而哀之，為買田宅，遺以資畜。
entries.en: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, a kinsman, took pity on him, bought him land and a house, and gave him livestock and supplies.
entries.literal: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, because of clan ties, saw him and pitied him, bought him fields and a house, and gave him livestock and goods.

entries.zh: 初，信入關之後，複娶二妻，郭氏生子六人，善、穆、藏、順、陀、整，崔氏生獻皇后。
entries.en: After Xin entered the passes he had taken two more wives. Lady Guo bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng—and Lady Cui bore Empress Xian.
entries.literal: Earlier, after Xin entered the passes, he took two wives again; the Guo clan bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng—and the Cui clan bore Empress Xian.

entries.zh: 及齊亡，高祖為定州總管，獻皇后遣人尋羅，得之，相見悲不自勝，侍御者皆泣。
entries.en: When Qi fell, Gaozu was governor-general of Dingzhou and Empress Xian sent men to find Luo. When they met, grief overwhelmed them and everyone present wept.
entries.literal: When Qi perished, Gaozu was Governor-General of Ding province; Empress Xian sent men to search for Luo, found him, and on meeting grieved beyond control—all who attended them wept.

entries.zh: 於是厚遺車馬財物。
entries.en: She then sent him a generous gift of carriages, horses, and valuables.
entries.literal: Thereupon she sent him a generous gift of carriages, horses, and valuables.

entries.zh: 未幾，周武帝以羅功臣子，久淪異域，征拜楚安郡太守。
entries.en: Soon afterward Emperor Wu of Zhou, seeing that Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long stranded in enemy territory, summoned him and made him governor of Chu'an commandery.
entries.literal: Before long, Emperor Wu of Zhou, because Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long lost in a foreign land, summoned and appointed him Governor of Chu'an commandery.

entries.zh: 以疾去官，歸於京師。
entries.en: Illness forced him to leave office, and he returned to the capital.
entries.literal: Because of illness he left office and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 諸弟見羅少長貧賤，每輕侮之，不以兄禮事也。
entries.en: His younger brothers, knowing he had grown up poor and far away, often slighted him and did not treat him as an elder brother.
entries.literal: His younger brothers, seeing that Luo had from youth grown up in poverty and low station, constantly treated him lightly and did not serve him with the rites due an elder brother.

entries.zh: 然性長者，亦不與諸弟校競長短，後由是重之。
entries.en: But Luo was by nature forbearing and never quarreled with them over precedence, and in time they came to respect him for it.
entries.literal: Yet by nature he was a man of forbearance and did not contend with his brothers over who was greater or lesser; afterward for this reason they came to respect him.

entries.zh: 及高祖為丞相，拜儀同，常置左右。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chancellor, Luo was made Master of Uniformity and kept constantly at his side.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Luo was appointed Master of Uniformity and constantly kept at his side.

entries.zh: 既受禪，下詔追贈羅父信官爵曰：「褒德累行，往代通規，追遠慎終，前王盛典。
entries.en: After Gaozu took the throne, he issued an edict posthumously honoring Luo's father Xin: "To reward accumulated virtue is the constant practice of antiquity; to honor the dead and finish well is the great rite of the ancient kings.
entries.literal: After he received the abdication, an edict was issued to posthumously confer offices and titles on Luo's father Xin, saying, "To honor virtue and accumulate conduct is the common rule of former ages; to pursue the distant and be careful at the end is the great ceremony of former kings.

entries.zh: 故柱國信，風宇高曠，獨秀生民，睿哲居宗，清猷映世。
entries.en: The late Pillar of State Xin bore himself with lofty breadth, outstanding among men; wise and far-seeing, he upheld the ancestral charge, and his pure designs illuminated the age.
entries.literal: The former Pillar of State Xin bore a lofty and spacious air, standing alone in excellence among the people; wise and perspicacious, he held the ancestral charge; his pure designs shone upon the age.

entries.zh: 宏謀長策，道著於弼諧，緯義經仁，事深於拯濟。
entries.en: His grand designs made the Way visible in counsel to the throne; in binding righteousness and ordering benevolence, his work went deep into the saving of the realm.
entries.literal: His great plans and long policies made the Way manifest in assisting harmony; weaving righteousness and threading benevolence, his affairs went deep into rescue and relief.

entries.zh: 方當宣風廊廟，亮采臺階，而運屬艱危，功高弗賞，眷言令範，事切於心。
entries.en: Just as he was to bring his influence to the court and lend his light to the throne, fate turned harsh; his merit went unrewarded, and the memory of his example still pierces the heart.
entries.literal: Just as he was about to spread virtue in the court hall and display his brilliance on the terrace steps, fate met with hardship and peril; his merit was high yet went unrewarded—recalling his fine example, the matter cuts to the heart.

entries.zh: 今景運初開，椒闈肅建，載懷塗山之義，無忘褒、紀之典。
entries.en: Now, as a new reign begins and the inner palace is duly established, mindful of the duty owed at Tushan, let us not forget the precedent set for the houses of Bao and Ji.
entries.literal: Now as the bright fortune first opens and the pepper chambers are solemnly established, bearing in mind the righteousness of Tushan, let us not forget the ceremonies of Bao and Ji.

entries.zh: 可贈太師、上柱國、冀定等十州刺史、趙國公，邑萬戶。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, governor of ten prefectures including Ji and Ding, and Duke of Zhao, with a fief of ten thousand households."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously conferred as Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, Governor of ten prefectures including Ji and Ding, and Duke of Zhao state, with a fief of ten thousand households."

entries.zh: 其諸弟以羅母沒齊，先無夫人之號，不當承襲。
entries.en: His younger brothers argued that because Luo's mother had died in Qi without ever receiving the title of Lady, he ought not to inherit the dukedom.
entries.literal: His younger brothers, because Luo's mother had died in Qi and had never borne the title of Lady, held that he ought not to inherit.

entries.zh: 上以問後，後曰：「羅誠嫡長，不可誣也。」
entries.en: The emperor asked the empress, who replied, "Luo is truly the eldest son of the primary line. That cannot be denied."
entries.literal: The emperor asked the empress; the empress said, "Luo is truly the eldest son of the primary wife—this cannot be denied."

entries.zh: 於是襲爵趙國公。
entries.en: Luo therefore inherited the title of Duke of Zhao.
entries.literal: Thereupon he inherited the title of Duke of Zhao.

entries.zh: 以其弟善為河內郡公，穆為金泉縣公，藏為武平縣公，陀為武喜縣公，整為千牛備身。
entries.en: His brother Shan was made Duke of Henei, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
entries.literal: His younger brother Shan was made Duke of Henei commandery, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

entries.zh: 擢拜羅為左領左右將軍，尋遷左衛將軍，前後賞賜不可勝計。
entries.en: Luo was promoted to general of the Left Retinue, then transferred to general of the Left Guard, and received rewards beyond counting.
entries.literal: Luo was promoted and appointed General of the Left Retinue of the Left and Right, and soon transferred to General of the Left Guard; rewards before and after were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 久而出為涼州總管，進位上柱國。
entries.en: After some time he was sent out as governor-general of Liangzhou and promoted to Supreme Pillar of State.
entries.literal: After a long while he went out as Governor-General of Liang province and advanced to Supreme Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，征拜左武衛大將軍。
entries.en: During the Renshou period he was recalled and made grand general of the Left Martial Guard.
entries.literal: During Renshou he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 煬帝嗣位，改封蜀國公。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo's title was changed to Duke of Shu.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo's fief was changed to Duke of Shu state.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒官，諡曰恭。
entries.en: He died in office not long afterward and was given the posthumous name Gong.
entries.literal: Before long he died in office; his posthumous title was Gong.

entries.zh: 獨孤陀，字黎邪。
entries.en: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.
entries.literal: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.

entries.zh: 仕周胥附上士，坐父徙蜀郡十餘年。
entries.en: He served Zhou as a gentleman-attendant of Xufu and, because of his father's case, was exiled to Shu commandery for more than ten years.
entries.literal: He served Zhou as a gentleman-attendant of Xufu; because of his father's case he was banished to Shu commandery for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 宇文護被誅，始歸長安。
entries.en: After Yuwen Hu was executed, he was at last allowed to return to Chang'an.
entries.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, he at last returned to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，拜上開府、右領左右將軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Tuo was made Senior Opener of the Mansion and general of the Right Retinue.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Tuo was appointed Senior Opener of the Mansion and General of the Right Retinue of the Left and Right.

entries.zh: 久之，出為郢州刺史，進位上大將軍，累轉延州刺史。
entries.en: After some time he was sent out as governor of E prefecture, promoted to grand general, and later transferred to governor of Yan prefecture.
entries.literal: After a long while he went out as Governor of E prefecture, advanced to Grand General, and was transferred in succession to Governor of Yan prefecture.

entries.zh: 好左道。
entries.en: He was devoted to heterodox cult practices.
entries.literal: He was fond of heterodox ways.

entries.zh: 其妻母先事貓鬼，因轉入其家。
entries.en: His wife's mother had first worshipped the cat-demon, and the practice passed into his household.
entries.literal: His wife's mother had first served the cat-demon, and the practice thereby passed into his household.

entries.zh: 上微聞而不之信也。
entries.en: The emperor heard rumors but did not believe them.
entries.literal: The emperor heard a little of it but did not believe it.

entries.zh: 會獻皇后及楊素妻鄭氏俱有疾，召醫者視之，皆曰：「此貓鬼疾也。」
entries.en: Then both Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife, Lady Zheng, fell ill. The physicians they summoned all said, "This is cat-demon sickness."
entries.literal: It happened that both Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife, the Zheng clan, fell ill; physicians were summoned to examine them, and all said, "This is cat-demon sickness."

entries.zh: 上以陀後之異母弟，陀妻楊素之異母妹，由是意陀所為，陰令其兄穆以情喻之。
entries.en: Because Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and his wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, the emperor suspected Tuo and secretly had his brother Mu reason with him.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and Tuo's wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, therefore suspected Tuo's doing and secretly ordered his elder brother Mu to explain the situation to him.

entries.zh: 上又避左右諷陀，陀言無有。
entries.en: The emperor also spoke to him privately, hinting at the matter, but Tuo denied everything.
entries.literal: The emperor also, avoiding attendants, admonished Tuo indirectly; Tuo said there was nothing of the kind.

entries.zh: 上不悅，左轉遷州刺史。
entries.en: Displeased, the emperor demoted him to governor of Qian prefecture.
entries.literal: The emperor was displeased and transferred him to the left as Governor of Qian prefecture.

entries.zh: 出怨言。
entries.en: He began to complain openly.
entries.literal: He uttered words of resentment.

entries.zh: 上令左僕射高熲、納言蘇威、大理正皇甫孝緒、大理丞楊遠等雜治之。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Palace Counselor Su Wei, Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Huangfu Xiaoxu, Assistant of the Court of Judicial Review Yang Yuan, and others to investigate jointly.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered the Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, the Palace Counselor Su Wei, the Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Huangfu Xiaoxu, the Assistant of the Court of Judicial Review Yang Yuan, and others jointly to try the case.

entries.zh: 陀婢徐阿尼言，本從陀母家來，常事貓鬼。
entries.en: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had come from his mother's household and had long served the cat-demon.
entries.literal: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had originally come from Tuo's mother's household and had constantly served the cat-demon.

entries.zh: 每以子日夜祀之。
entries.en: Every night at the hour of zi she made offerings to it.
entries.literal: Every night at the hour of zi she sacrificed to it.

entries.zh: 言子者鼠也。
entries.en: By "zi" she meant the rat—the hour of the rat.
entries.literal: "Zi" means the rat.

entries.zh: 其貓鬼每殺人者，所死家財物潛移於畜貓鬼家。
entries.en: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the victim's wealth was secretly transferred to the household that kept the demon.
entries.literal: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the property of the dead household was secretly transferred to the household that kept the cat-demon.

entries.zh: 陀嘗從家中素酒，其妻曰：「無錢可酤。」
entries.en: Tuo once asked for wine at home. His wife said, "We have no money to buy any."
entries.literal: Tuo once asked for wine at home; his wife said, "There is no money to buy any."

entries.zh: 陀因謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向越公家，使我足錢也。」
entries.en: Tuo then told Ani, "Send the cat-demon to Duke Yue's house and get me enough money."
entries.literal: Tuo thereupon said to Ani, "You can have the cat-demon go to Duke Yue's household and get me enough money."

entries.zh: 阿尼便咒之歸。
entries.en: Ani chanted the spell to send it off.
entries.literal: Ani then chanted to send it back.

entries.zh: 數日，貓鬼向素家。
entries.en: Within a few days the cat-demon was sent to Yang Su's house.
entries.literal: Within several days the cat-demon went toward Yang Su's household.

entries.zh: 十一年，上初從并州還，陀於園中謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向皇后所，使多賜吾物。」
entries.en: In the eleventh year, soon after the emperor returned from Bingzhou, Tuo told Ani in the garden, "Send the cat-demon to the empress and make her give me more gifts."
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, when the emperor had just returned from Bing province, Tuo said to Ani in the garden, "You can have the cat-demon go to the empress's quarters and make her bestow many things on me."

entries.zh: 阿尼複咒之，遂入宮中。
entries.en: Ani chanted again, and the demon entered the palace.
entries.literal: Ani again chanted, and it thereupon entered the palace.

entries.zh: 楊遠乃于門下外省遣阿尼呼貓鬼。
entries.en: Yang Yuan then had Ani summon the cat-demon at the Outer Office of the Gate Department.
entries.literal: Yang Yuan then, at the Outer Office of the Gate Department, sent Ani to summon the cat-demon.

entries.zh: 阿尼於是夜中置香粥一盆，以匙扣而呼之曰：「貓女可來，無住宮中。」
entries.en: That night Ani set out a bowl of fragrant porridge, tapped it with a spoon, and called, "Cat-girl, come—but do not stay in the palace."
entries.literal: Ani then, in the middle of the night, set out a basin of fragrant porridge, knocked it with a spoon, and called, "Cat-girl, you may come—do not stay in the palace."

entries.zh: 久之，阿尼色正青，若被牽曳者，雲貓鬼已至。
entries.en: After a long while her face turned blue, as if she were being pulled, and she said the cat-demon had come.
entries.literal: After a long while Ani's face turned pure blue, as if she were being dragged, and she said the cat-demon had arrived.

entries.zh: 上以其事下公卿，奇章公牛弘曰：「妖由人興，殺其人可以絕矣。」
entries.en: The emperor referred the case to the high officials. Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang, said, "Such evil rises through men. Kill the man and it will end."
entries.literal: The emperor submitted the matter to the dukes and ministers; Niuzhang Duke Niu Hong said, "Omens arise through men—kill the man and it can be ended."

entries.zh: 上令以犢車載陀夫妻，將賜死於其家。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Tuo and his wife taken in a cart to their home to be put to death.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Tuo and his wife loaded into a calf cart and sent to be granted death at their home.

entries.zh: 陀弟司勳侍中整詣闕求哀，於是免陀死，除名為民，以其妻楊氏為尼。
entries.en: Tuo's brother Zheng, Director of the Department of Merit and attendant-in-ordinary, pleaded at court for mercy. Tuo was spared death, reduced to commoner status, and his wife, Lady Yang, was made a nun.
entries.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng, Director of the Department of Merit and Attendant-in-Ordinary, went to the palace gate to plead for mercy; thereupon Tuo was spared death, struck from the registers and made a commoner, and his wife, the Yang clan, was made a nun.

entries.zh: 先是，有人訟其母為人貓鬼所殺者，上以為妖妄，怒而遣之。
entries.en: Earlier, a man had sued, claiming his mother had been killed by another person's cat-demon. The emperor dismissed it as superstitious nonsense and sent him away in anger.
entries.literal: Earlier, someone had sued, claiming his mother had been killed by another's cat-demon; the emperor regarded it as demonic delusion, grew angry, and sent him away.

entries.zh: 及此，詔誅被訟行貓鬼家。
entries.en: Now an edict ordered the household accused in that earlier suit to be executed.
entries.literal: At this point an edict ordered the execution of the household accused of practicing the cat-demon.

entries.zh: 經未幾而卒。
entries.en: He died not long afterward.
entries.literal: Before long he died.

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，追念舅氏，聽以禮葬，乃下詔曰：「外氏衰禍，獨孤陀不幸早世，遷卜有期。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang took the throne, mindful of his mother's kin, he allowed Tuo a proper burial and issued an edict: "My mother's clan has fallen on hard times. Dugu Tuo died young, and the time has come to move his tomb and set his burial.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, recalling his maternal kin, he permitted burial according to ritual and issued an edict saying, "My mother's clan has suffered decline and calamity; Dugu Tuo, unhappily, died young, and the time for moving the tomb and setting the burial date has come.

entries.zh: 言念渭陽之情，追懷傷切，宜加禮命，允備哀榮。
entries.en: Mindful of the bond between maternal kin, and deeply grieved in remembrance, let ritual honors be added and full mourning glory granted.
entries.literal: Speaking of the feeling of Weiyang, the pursuit of remembrance is grievously cutting; ritual honors should be increased, and mourning glory fully granted.

entries.zh: 可贈正議大夫。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously honored as Grand Master of Correct Discussion."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously conferred as Grand Master of Correct Discussion."

entries.zh: 帝意猶不已，複下詔曰：「舅氏之尊，戚屬斯重，而降年弗永，凋落相繼。
entries.en: The emperor was still not satisfied and issued another edict: "Maternal uncles are men of great honor, and affinal kin carry heavy weight—yet their years are short, and they fall away one after another.
entries.literal: The emperor's mind was still not satisfied, and he again issued an edict saying, "The honor due maternal uncles, the weight of affinal kin—yet their allotted years are not long, and they fall away one after another.

entries.zh: 緬惟先往，宜崇徽秩。
entries.en: Thinking of those who have gone before, their ranks should be raised in honor.
entries.literal: Looking back on those who went before, their eminent ranks should be exalted.

entries.zh: 複贈銀青光祿大夫。」
entries.en: He was again posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Silver-Green Light."
entries.literal: He was again posthumously conferred as Grand Master of the Silver-Green Light."

entries.zh: 有二子：延福、延壽。
entries.en: He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.
entries.literal: He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.

entries.zh: 蕭巋，字仁遠，梁昭明太子統之孫也。
entries.en: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming, Xiao Tong.
entries.literal: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming, Tong.

entries.zh: 父詧，初封岳陽王，鎮襄陽。
entries.en: His father Cha was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yueyang and posted at Xiangyang.
entries.literal: His father Cha was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Yueyang and garrisoned Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，其兄河東王譽與其叔父湘東王繹不協，為繹所害。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his elder brother Prince Yu of Hedong fell out with their uncle Prince Yi of Xiangdong and was killed by him.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his elder brother Prince of Hedong, Yu, was at odds with their uncle Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, and was killed by Yi.

entries.zh: 及繹嗣位，詧稱籓於西魏，乞師請討繹。
entries.en: When Yi took the throne, Cha submitted to Western Wei as a vassal, asked for troops, and requested a campaign against Yi.
entries.literal: When Yi succeeded to the throne, Cha declared himself a vassal of Western Wei, begged troops, and requested a campaign against Yi.

entries.zh: 周太祖以詧為梁主，遣柱國於謹等率騎五萬襲繹，滅之。
entries.en: Taizu of Zhou installed Cha as ruler of Liang and sent the Pillar of State Yu Jin with fifty thousand horsemen to strike Yi and destroy him.
entries.literal: Taizu of Zhou made Cha ruler of Liang and sent the Pillar of State Yu Jin and others at the head of fifty thousand horsemen to strike Yi and destroy him.

entries.zh: 詧遂都江陵，有荊郡、其西平州延袤三百里之地，稱皇帝于其國，車服節文一同王者。
entries.en: Cha then moved his capital to Jiangling, holding Jing commandery and Xiping prefecture to the west—a domain three hundred li across—and proclaimed himself emperor; his carriage regalia, dress, and ritual forms matched those of a true sovereign.
entries.literal: Cha then moved the capital to Jiangling, held Jing commandery and Xiping prefecture to the west—a territory three hundred li in extent—and styled himself emperor in his state; carriage regalia, dress, and ritual regulations were all the same as a king's.

entries.zh: 仍置江陵總管，以兵戍之。
entries.en: Zhou still stationed a governor-general at Jiangling with troops to hold the city.
entries.literal: A Jiangling Governor-General was still established to garrison it with troops.

entries.zh: 詧薨，巋嗣位，年號天保。
entries.en: When Cha died, Kui succeeded him under the era name Tianbao.
entries.literal: When Cha died, Kui succeeded him, with the era name Tianbao.

entries.zh: 巋俊辯有才學，兼好內典。
entries.en: Kui was handsome, eloquent, and learned, and also devoted to Buddhist scriptures.
entries.literal: Kui was handsome, eloquent, and learned, and was also fond of Buddhist scriptures.

entries.zh: 周武帝平齊之後，巋來賀，帝享之甚歡。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations and was entertained with great delight.
entries.literal: After Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations; the emperor entertained him with great delight.

entries.zh: 親彈琵琶，令巋起舞，巋曰：「陛下親禦五糸玄，臣敢不同百獸！」
entries.en: The emperor played the pipa himself and ordered Kui to dance. Kui replied, "Your Majesty plays the five-stringed lute—how dare I not join the hundred beasts in response!"
entries.literal: The emperor personally played the pipa and ordered Kui to dance; Kui said, "Your Majesty personally handles the five-stringed dark lute—how dare your servant not join the hundred beasts!"

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，恩禮彌厚，遣使賜金五百兩，銀千兩，布帛萬匹，馬五百匹。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, favor and ceremony grew still richer. Envoys were sent with five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, favor and ceremony grew still richer; envoys were sent to bestow five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.

entries.zh: 巋來朝，上甚敬焉，詔巋位在王公之上。
entries.en: When Kui came to court, the emperor treated him with great respect and ordered that his rank stand above the kings and dukes.
entries.literal: Kui came to court; the emperor greatly respected him and ordered that Kui's rank stand above the kings and dukes.

entries.zh: 巋被服端麗，進退閒雅，天子矚目，百僚傾慕。
entries.en: Kui dressed with dignified elegance and moved with easy grace. The emperor watched him closely, and the whole court looked on with admiration.
entries.literal: Kui's dress and adornment were dignified and beautiful; in advancing and withdrawing he was easy and elegant—the Son of Heaven fixed his gaze on him, and the hundred officials looked on him with admiration.

entries.zh: 賞賜以億計。
entries.en: Rewards and gifts ran into the hundreds of millions.
entries.literal: Rewards and gifts were reckoned in the hundreds of millions.

entries.zh: 月餘歸籓，帝親餞于滻水之上。
entries.en: After more than a month he returned to his domain, and the emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.
entries.literal: After more than a month he returned to his fief; the emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.

entries.zh: 後備禮納其女為晉王妃，又欲以其子瑒尚蘭陵公主。
entries.en: Later his daughter was married with full ceremony to the Prince of Jin, and the emperor also wished to marry Kui's son Yang to Princess Lanling.
entries.literal: Later, with full ceremony, his daughter was taken in marriage as consort to the Prince of Jin, and the emperor also wished to marry his son Yang to Princess Lanling.

entries.zh: 由是漸見親待。
entries.en: From then on he was increasingly treated as family.
entries.literal: From this he gradually came to be treated with intimacy.

entries.zh: 獻皇后言于上曰：「梁主通家，腹心所寄，何勞猜防也。」
entries.en: Empress Xian told the emperor, "The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, a man you trust with your heart—why trouble yourself with suspicion?"
entries.literal: Empress Xian said to the emperor, "The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, one in whom your heart is entrusted—why trouble yourself with suspicion and guard?"

entries.zh: 上然之，於是罷江陵總管，巋專制其國。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, abolished the Jiangling governor-general, and let Kui rule his state on his own.
entries.literal: The emperor agreed; thereupon the Jiangling Governor-General was abolished, and Kui held sole rule over his state.

entries.zh: 歲餘，巋又來朝，賜縑萬匹，珍玩稱是。
entries.en: A year later Kui came to court again and received ten thousand bolts of fine silk and treasures in like measure.
entries.literal: After more than a year Kui came to court again and was given ten thousand bolts of fine silk and treasures and curios in like measure.

entries.zh: 及還，上親執手曰：「梁主久滯荊楚，未復舊都，故鄉之念，良軫懷抱。
entries.en: When he departed, the emperor took his hand and said, "You have long been held in Jing-Chu and have not yet recovered your old capital. Thoughts of home must weigh heavily on your heart.
entries.literal: When he returned, the emperor personally took his hand and said, "The Lord of Liang has long been detained in Jing-Chu and has not yet recovered his old capital; thoughts of home must weigh heavily on your heart.

entries.zh: 朕當振旅長江，相送旋反耳。」
