entries.en: I shall raise an army on the Yangzi and send you home in triumph."
entries.literal: I shall raise an army on the Yangzi and send you back in triumph."

entries.zh: 巋拜謝而去。
entries.en: Kui bowed in thanks and departed.
entries.literal: Kui bowed in thanks and departed.

entries.zh: 其年五月，寢疾，臨終上表曰：「臣以庸暗，曲荷天慈，寵冠外籓，恩逾連山，爰及子女，尚主婚王。
entries.en: That fifth month he fell ill. On his deathbed he submitted a memorial: "Your servant, dull and unworthy, has undeservedly received Heaven's kindness. Favor has crowned me above the outer fiefs, grace has surpassed the mountains themselves; even my sons and daughters have married into the imperial house.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of that year he fell ill in bed; on his deathbed he submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant, dim and mediocre, has undeservedly received Heaven's kindness; favor has crowned me above the outer fiefs, grace has surpassed linked mountains; even my sons and daughters have married princesses and princes.

entries.zh: 每願躬擐甲胄，身先士卒，掃蕩逋寇，上報明時。
entries.en: I have always wished to don armor myself, lead the soldiers in person, sweep away the rebels, and repay this enlightened age.
entries.literal: I have always wished to don armor myself, take the lead before the soldiers, sweep away the fleeing bandits, and repay the enlightened age above.

entries.zh: 而攝生乖舛，遽罹屙疾，屬纊在辰，顧陰待謝。
entries.en: Yet I failed in caring for my health and have suddenly fallen gravely ill. Death is near, and I await the end.
entries.literal: Yet in nurturing life I went astray and suddenly met with wasting sickness; the silk of death is at hand, and I await the shade in farewell.

entries.zh: 長違聖世，感戀嗚咽，遺嗣孤藐，特乞降慈。
entries.en: I must leave this sage age, and grief overwhelms me. My orphaned heirs are young and helpless—I beg your mercy for them.
entries.literal: Long parted from the sage age, I grieve and sob in longing; my orphaned heirs are young and small—I specially beg your lowered kindness.

entries.zh: 伏願聖躬與山嶽同固，皇基等天日俱永，臣雖九泉，實無遣恨。」
entries.en: I pray that your sacred person may stand firm as the mountains, that the imperial foundation may last as long as heaven and sun—even in the grave I shall have no regret."
entries.literal: I bow and wish that your sacred person may be as firm as mountains and hills, that the imperial foundation may last as long as heaven and sun together—even in the nine springs, your servant would truly have no regret left behind."

entries.zh: 並獻所服金裝劍，上覽而嗟悼焉。
entries.en: He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn. The emperor read the memorial and sighed in grief.
entries.literal: He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn; the emperor read it and sighed in mourning.

entries.zh: 巋在位二十三年，年四十四薨，梁之臣子諡曰孝明皇帝，廟號世宗。
entries.en: Kui reigned twenty-three years and died at forty-four. Liang's ministers gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming and the temple name Shizong.
entries.literal: Kui reigned twenty-three years and died at age forty-four; Liang's ministers and subjects gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming and the temple name Shizong.

entries.zh: 子琮嗣。
entries.en: His son Cong succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Cong succeeded him.

entries.zh: 巋著《孝經》、《周易義記》及《大小乘幽微》十四卷，行於世。
entries.en: Kui wrote the Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Book of Changes, and Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles in fourteen scrolls, all of which circulated in his day.
entries.literal: Kui authored the Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Book of Changes, and Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles in fourteen scrolls, which circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 琮字溫文，性寬仁，有大度，倜儻不羈，博學有文義。
entries.en: Cong, styled Wenwen, was generous and humane, broad-minded, free-spirited and unrestrained, widely learned and accomplished in letters.
entries.literal: Cong, styled Wenwen, was by nature generous and humane, possessed of great breadth, free and unrestrained, broadly learned and skilled in literary meaning.

entries.zh: 兼善弓馬，遣人伏地著帖，琮馳馬射之，十發十中，持帖者亦不懼。
entries.en: He was also skilled with bow and horse. He had a man lie prone with a target on his back, then galloped and shot at it—ten shots, ten hits—and the man holding the target did not flinch.
entries.literal: He was also skilled in bow and horse; he had a man lie prone on the ground with a target affixed, and Cong galloped and shot at it—ten shots, ten hits—and the man holding the target was not afraid.

entries.zh: 初封東陽王，尋立為梁太子。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang and soon made crown prince of Liang.
entries.literal: He was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang and soon established as Liang's crown prince.

entries.zh: 及嗣位，上賜璽書曰：「負荷堂構，其事甚重，雖窮憂勞，常須自力。
entries.en: When he succeeded to the throne, the emperor sent a sealed letter: "To bear the weight of the realm is a grave matter. Though worn with worry and toil, you must constantly rely on your own strength.
entries.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, the emperor bestowed a sealed letter saying, "To bear the hall and framework is a weighty matter; though exhausted with worry and toil, you must constantly rely on your own strength.

entries.zh: 輯諧內外，親任才良，聿遵世業，是所望也。
entries.en: Harmonize within and without, personally employ the talented and worthy, and faithfully carry on your father's enterprise—that is my hope.
entries.literal: Harmonize within and without, personally employ the talented and good, and faithfully follow the enterprise of the age—this is what is hoped for.

entries.zh: 彼之疆守，咫尺陳人，水潦之時，特宜警備。
entries.en: Chen lies just beyond your border. In the rainy season you must be especially vigilant.
entries.literal: Their frontier garrisons are but a foot away from Chen; in times of flood and rain, special vigilance is fitting.

entries.zh: 陳氏比日雖複朝聘相尋，疆埸之間猶未清肅，唯當恃我必不可幹，勿得輕人而不設備。
entries.en: Though Chen has lately resumed diplomatic visits, the border is still unsettled. Trust that they cannot possibly defy me—but do not treat them lightly or neglect your defenses.
entries.literal: Though Chen of late has again sent envoys back and forth, the borderlands are still not clear and settled; you should rely on the fact that they cannot possibly resist me, yet must not treat others lightly and fail to make preparations.

entries.zh: 朕與梁國，積世相知，重以親姻，情義彌厚。
entries.en: Liang and I have known each other across generations, and marriage ties have made our bond still deeper.
entries.literal: I and the state of Liang have known each other through accumulated generations; redoubled by marriage ties, affection and righteousness grow still deeper.

entries.zh: 江陵之地，朝寄非輕，為國為民，深宜抑割，恆加饘粥，以禮自存。」
entries.en: Jiangling is no light charge from the court. For the sake of state and people you should restrain yourself, live simply on plain food, and preserve yourself through proper conduct."
entries.literal: The land of Jiangling is no light charge from the court; for state and for people you should deeply restrain yourself, constantly take thin gruel, and preserve yourself through ritual."

entries.zh: 又賜梁之大臣璽書，誠勉之。
entries.en: He also sent sealed letters to Liang's great ministers, sincerely exhorting them.
entries.literal: He also bestowed sealed letters on Liang's great ministers, sincerely exhorting them.

entries.zh: 時琮年號廣運，有識者曰：「運之為字，軍走也，吾君將奔走乎？」
entries.en: Cong's era name was Guangyun. Men of insight said, "The character yun combines 'army' and 'flee'—will our lord take to flight?"
entries.literal: At that time Cong's era name was Guangyun; men of insight said, "The character yun means 'army' and 'flee'—will our lord take to flight?"

entries.zh: 其年，琮遣大將軍戚昕以舟師襲陳公安，不克而還。
entries.en: That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's Gong'an but failed and returned.
entries.literal: That year Cong sent the Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen Gong'an but failed and returned.

entries.zh: 征琮叔父岑入朝，拜為大將軍，封懷義公，因留不遣。
entries.en: Cong's uncle Cen was summoned to court, made grand general, enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyi, and detained there.
entries.literal: Cong's uncle Cen was summoned to court, appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyi, and thereupon detained and not sent back.

entries.zh: 複置江陵總管以監之。
entries.en: The Jiangling governor-general was reinstated to keep watch over him.
entries.literal: The Jiangling Governor-General was again established to oversee him.

entries.zh: 琮所署大將軍許世武密以城召陳將宜黃侯陳紀，謀泄，琮誅之。
entries.en: Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly offered the city to Chen general Marquis Chen Ji of Yihuang. When the plot leaked, Cong executed him.
entries.literal: The Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly offered the city to summon the Chen general Marquis of Yihuang, Chen Ji; the plot leaked out, and Cong executed him.

entries.zh: 後二歲，上征琮入朝，率其臣下二百余人朝于京師，江陵父老莫不隕涕相謂曰：「吾君其不反矣！」
entries.en: Two years later the emperor summoned Cong to court. He led more than two hundred ministers to the capital, and the elders of Jiangling wept and said to one another, "Our lord will not return!"
entries.literal: Two years later the emperor summoned Cong to court; he led more than two hundred ministers and subordinates to attend court in the capital, and the elders of Jiangling all shed tears and said to one another, "Our lord will not return!"

entries.zh: 上以琮來朝，遣武鄉公崔弘度將兵戍之。
entries.en: Because Cong had come to court, the emperor sent Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu with troops to garrison Jiangling.
entries.literal: Because Cong had come to court, the emperor sent Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu to lead troops to garrison the place.

entries.zh: 軍至鄀州，琮叔父岩及弟瓛等懼弘度掩襲之，遂引陳人至城下，虜居民而叛，於是廢梁國。
entries.en: When the army reached E prefecture, Cong's uncle Yan and his brother Huan, fearing a surprise attack, brought Chen troops to the walls, seized the inhabitants, and rebelled. The state of Liang was abolished.
entries.literal: When the army reached E prefecture, Cong's uncle Yan and younger brother Huan and others, fearing that Hongdu would launch a surprise attack, thereupon brought Chen men to the foot of the walls, seized the inhabitants, and rebelled—whereupon the state of Liang was abolished.

entries.zh: 上遣左僕射高熲安集之，曲赦江陵死罪，給民複十年。
entries.en: The emperor sent Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify the region, granted a special pardon for capital crimes in Jiangling, and gave the people ten years of tax relief.
entries.literal: The emperor sent the Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify and settle the region, granted a special pardon for capital crimes in Jiangling, and gave the people tax relief for ten years.

entries.zh: 梁二主各給守墓十戶。
entries.en: Ten households were assigned to guard each of the two Liang rulers' tombs.
entries.literal: To each of the two Liang rulers ten households were assigned to guard the tombs.

entries.zh: 拜琮為柱國，賜爵莒國公。
entries.en: Cong was made Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.
entries.literal: Cong was appointed Pillar of State and granted the title Duke of Ju state.

entries.zh: 煬帝嗣位，以皇后之故，甚見親重。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Cong was greatly favored because of the empress.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, because of the empress he was greatly favored and esteemed.

entries.zh: 拜內史令，改封梁公。
entries.en: He was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and his title was changed to Duke of Liang.
entries.literal: He was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and his fief was changed to Duke of Liang.

entries.zh: 琮之宗族，緦麻以上，並隨才擢用，於是諸蕭昆弟布列朝廷。
entries.en: Cong's clansmen, even those in the remotest degree of kinship, were promoted according to talent, and Xiao brothers filled the court.
entries.literal: Cong's clansmen, from those in the finest mourning grade upward, were all promoted according to talent; thus the various Xiao brothers were arrayed throughout the court.

entries.zh: 琮性淡雅，不以職務自嬰，退朝縱酒而已。
entries.en: Cong was refined and detached by nature and did not burden himself with office; after court he merely drank.
entries.literal: Cong was by nature refined and detached; he did not burden himself with official duties—after court he merely drank freely.

entries.zh: 內史令楊約與琮同列，帝令約宣旨誡勵，約複以私情喻之。
entries.en: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Yue, Cong's equal in rank, was ordered to admonish him, and Yue spoke to him privately as well.
entries.literal: The Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Yue was of the same rank as Cong; the emperor ordered Yue to proclaim the imperial will and admonish him, and Yue again explained it in private terms.

entries.zh: 琮答曰：「琮若複事事，則何異於公哉！」
entries.en: Cong replied, "If I attended to every matter again, how would I differ from you!"
entries.literal: Cong replied, "If Cong again attended to every matter, how would he differ from you!"

entries.zh: 約笑而退。
entries.en: Yue laughed and withdrew.
entries.literal: Yue laughed and withdrew.

entries.zh: 約兄素，時為尚書令，見琮嫁從父妹于鉗耳氏，因謂琮曰：「公，帝王之族，望高戚美，何乃適妹鉗耳氏乎？」
entries.en: Yue's brother Su, then Director of the Department of State Affairs, saw that Cong had married a cousin to the Qian'er clan and said, "You are of imperial stock, with high standing and noble connections—why marry your sister to the Qian'er?"
entries.literal: Yue's elder brother Su, who was then Director of the Department of State Affairs, saw that Cong had married a younger cousin by the father's line to the Qian'er clan and therefore said to Cong, "Sir, you are of an imperial clan—your standing is high and your affinal beauty great—why marry your sister to the Qian'er clan?"

entries.zh: 琮曰：「前已嫁妹于侯莫陳氏，此複何疑！」
entries.en: Cong said, "I already married one sister to the Houmochen—what is there to question in this!"
entries.literal: Cong said, "I have already married a sister to the Houmochen clan before—what doubt is there in this!"

entries.zh: 素曰：「鉗耳，羌也，侯莫陳，虜也，何得相比！」
entries.en: Su said, "The Qian'er are Qiang; the Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
entries.literal: Su said, "Qian'er are Qiang; Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"

entries.zh: 素意以虜優羌劣。
entries.en: Su meant that barbarians ranked above the Qiang.
entries.literal: Su's meaning was that barbarians were superior and Qiang inferior.

entries.zh: 琮曰：「以羌異虜，未之前聞。」
entries.en: Cong said, "That the Qiang differ from barbarians is something I have never heard before."
entries.literal: Cong said, "That Qiang differ from barbarians is something never heard of before."

entries.zh: 素慚而止。
entries.en: Su, ashamed, said no more.
entries.literal: Su, ashamed, stopped.

entries.zh: 琮雖羈旅，見北間豪貴，無所降下。
entries.en: Though Cong lived as an exile in the north, he bowed to none of its great nobles.
entries.literal: Though Cong was a guest in exile, when he met the great and noble of the north he bowed to none.

entries.zh: 嘗與賀若弼深相友善，弼既被誅，複有童謠曰：「蕭蕭亦複起。」
entries.en: He had been close friends with He Ruobi. After Ruobi was executed, a children's song ran, "Xiao, xiao—they rise again."
entries.literal: He had once been deeply friendly with He Ruo Bi; after Bi was executed, there was again a children's song saying, "Xiao, xiao—again they rise."

entries.zh: 帝由是忌之，遂廢於家，未幾而卒。
entries.en: The emperor grew suspicious and confined him at home. He died not long afterward.
entries.literal: The emperor therefore grew suspicious of him, had him confined at home, and before long he died.

entries.zh: 贈左光祿大夫。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Left Light.
entries.literal: He was posthumously conferred as Grand Master of the Left Light.

entries.zh: 子鉉，襄城通守。
entries.en: His son Xian was defender of Xiangcheng.
entries.literal: His son Xian was Defender of Xiangcheng.

entries.zh: 複以琮弟子钜為梁公。
entries.en: Cong's nephew Ju was then made Duke of Liang.
entries.literal: Cong's nephew Ju was again made Duke of Liang.

entries.zh: 钜小名藏，煬帝甚昵之，以為千牛，與宇文皛出入宮掖，伺察內外。
entries.en: Ju, childhood name Zang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang. He was made an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard and, with Yuwen Xiao, went in and out of the inner palace, watching affairs within and without.
entries.literal: Ju, whose childhood name was Zang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang; he was made an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard and, together with Yuwen Xiao, went in and out of the palace women's quarters, observing within and without.

entries.zh: 帝每有遊宴，钜未嘗不從焉，遂于宮中多行淫穢。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor held excursions and banquets, Ju was always present, and he committed many lewd acts within the palace.
entries.literal: Whenever the emperor held excursions and banquets, Ju never failed to follow; he thereupon committed many lewd and filthy acts within the palace.

entries.zh: 江都之變，為宇文化及所殺。
entries.en: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
entries.literal: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.

entries.zh: 蕭巋子琮琮弟瓛
entries.en: Xiao Kui; His Son Cong; Cong's Brother Huan
entries.literal: Xiao Kui; his son Cong; Cong's younger brother Huan

entries.zh: 瓛字欽文，少聰敏，解屬文。
entries.en: Huan, styled Qinwen, was clever from youth and skilled in literary composition.
entries.literal: Huan, styled Qinwen, was from youth clever and keen and skilled in literary composition.

entries.zh: 在梁為荊州刺史，頗有能名。
entries.en: In Liang he was governor of Jing province and had a considerable reputation for ability.
entries.literal: In Liang he was Governor of Jing province and had a considerable reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 崔弘度以兵至鄀州，瓛懼，與其叔父岩奔于陳。
entries.en: When Cui Hongdu brought troops to Ruo prefecture, Huan fled to Chen with his uncle Yan.
entries.literal: When Cui Hongdu came with troops to Ruo prefecture, Huan was afraid; together with his uncle Yan he fled to Chen.

entries.zh: 陳主以為侍中、安東將軍、吳州刺史，甚得物情，三吳父老皆曰：「瓛吾君子也。」
entries.en: The Chen ruler made him attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and governor of Wu prefecture. He won great favor, and the elders of the Three Wu said, "Huan is our true gentleman."
entries.literal: The Lord of Chen made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Wu prefecture; he won the hearts of men greatly, and the elders of the Three Wu all said, "Huan is our gentleman."

entries.zh: 及陳亡，吳人推瓛為主。
entries.en: When Chen fell, the people of Wu urged Huan to lead them.
entries.literal: When Chen perished, the people of Wu urged Huan as their leader.

entries.zh: 吳人見梁武、簡文及詧、巋等兄弟並第三而踐尊位，瓛自以巋之第三子也，深自矜負。
entries.en: The people of Wu noted that Emperor Wu of Liang, Emperor Jianwen, and the brothers Cha and Kui had all been third sons yet reached the throne. Huan, as Kui's third son, took great pride in this.
entries.literal: The people of Wu saw that Emperor Wu of Liang, Emperor Jianwen, and the brothers Cha and Kui had all been third sons and yet ascended the honored throne; Huan, considering himself Kui's third son, deeply prided himself on this.

entries.zh: 有謝異者，頗知廢興，梁、陳之際，言無不驗，江南人甚敬信之。
entries.en: A man named Xie Yi was skilled at reading the rise and fall of states. In the transition between Liang and Chen, nothing he said failed to come true, and the people of Jiangnan greatly revered him.
entries.literal: There was one Xie Yi who was well versed in rise and fall; in the transition between Liang and Chen, nothing he said failed to come true, and the people of Jiangnan greatly revered and trusted him.

entries.zh: 及陳主被擒，異奔於瓛，由是益為眾所歸。
entries.en: When the Chen ruler was captured, Yi fled to Huan, and Huan gained still more support.
entries.literal: When the Lord of Chen was captured, Yi fled to Huan; thereby Huan came to be still more followed by the multitude.

entries.zh: 褒國公宇文述以兵討之，瓛遣王哀守吳州，自將拒述。
entries.en: Duke of Baoguo Yuwen Shu came with troops to suppress him. Huan sent Wang Ai to hold Wu prefecture and personally led the army against Shu.
entries.literal: Duke of Baoguo Yuwen Shu came with troops to suppress him; Huan sent Wang Ai to hold Wu prefecture and personally led the army to resist Shu.

entries.zh: 述遣兵別道襲吳州，哀懼，衣道士服，棄城而遁。
entries.en: Shu sent troops by another route to strike Wu prefecture. Ai, terrified, dressed as a Daoist priest, abandoned the city, and fled.
entries.literal: Shu sent troops by a separate route to strike Wu prefecture; Ai was afraid, put on a Daoist priest's robe, abandoned the city, and fled.

entries.zh: 瓛眾聞之，悉無鬥志，與述一戰而敗。
entries.en: When Huan's troops heard of this, they lost all fighting spirit. After one battle with Shu they were defeated.
entries.literal: When Huan's host heard of it, they all lost fighting spirit; after one battle with Shu they were defeated.

entries.zh: 瓛將左右數人逃於太湖，匿於民家，為人所執，送於述所，斬之長安，時年二十一。
entries.en: Huan fled to Lake Tai with a few attendants and hid in a commoner's house. He was seized, sent to Shu, and beheaded in Chang'an at the age of twenty-one.
entries.literal: Huan took a few attendants and fled to Lake Tai, hiding in a commoner's house; he was seized by someone, sent to Shu's camp, and beheaded in Chang'an at the age of twenty-one.

entries.zh: 弟璟，為朝請大夫、尚衣奉禦。
entries.en: His younger brother Jing was a grand master for imperial audience and attendant for imperial vestments.
entries.literal: His younger brother Jing was a Grand Master for Imperial Audience and Attendant for Imperial Vestments.

entries.zh: 瑒，曆衛尉卿、秘書監、陶丘侯。
entries.en: Yang served as commandant of the guards for the palace, director of the palace library, and Marquis of Taoqiu.
entries.literal: Yang successively held the offices of Commandant of the Guards for the Palace, Director of the Palace Library, and Marquis of Taoqiu.

entries.zh: 瑀，曆內史侍郎、河池太守。
entries.en: Yu served as vice director of the palace secretariat and governor of Hechi.
entries.literal: Yu successively held the offices of Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Governor of Hechi.

entries.zh: 隋書卷七十九列傳第四十四
entries.en: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44
entries.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44

entries.zh: 高祖既平陳，乃遣使獻方物，其後朝貢遂絕。
entries.en: After Emperor Gaozu conquered Chen, Linyi sent envoys bearing native products, but tributary missions soon ceased entirely.
entries.literal: After Gaozu pacified Chen, Linyi then sent envoys to present local products; thereafter tribute missions ceased.

entries.zh: 時天下無事，羣臣言林邑多奇寶者。
entries.en: With the empire at peace, court officials declared that Linyi held countless exotic treasures.
entries.literal: When the realm was at peace, officials said Linyi possessed many rare treasures.

entries.zh: 仁壽末，上遣大將軍劉方為驩州道行軍總管，率欽州刺史甯長真、驩州刺史李暈、開府秦雄步騎萬餘及犯罪者數千人擊之。
entries.en: Near the close of the Renshou era the emperor appointed Grand General Liu Fang commander of the Huanzhou expeditionary force. Liu Fang marched with Prefect of Qinzhou Ning Changzhen, Prefect of Huanzhou Li Yun, colonel Qin Xiong, over ten thousand foot and horse soldiers, and several thousand penal conscripts to strike Linyi.
entries.literal: At the end of Renshou, the emperor dispatched Grand General Liu Fang as commander-in-chief of the Huanzhou route army, leading Prefect of Qin Zhou Ning Changzhen, Prefect of Huan Zhou Li Yun, Colonel Qin Xiong with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry plus several thousand convicted men to attack.

entries.zh: 其王梵志率其徒乘巨象而戰，方軍不利。
entries.en: King Fan Zhi arrayed his warriors atop great elephants, and Liu Fang's forces suffered at first.
entries.literal: King Fan Zhi led his troops mounted on huge elephants to battle; Fang's army fared poorly.

entries.zh: 方於是多掘小坑，草覆其上，因以兵挑之。
entries.en: Liu Fang ordered countless shallow pits dug, masked with turf, and baited the enemy with skirmishers.
entries.literal: Fang then had many small pits dug, covered with grass, and provoked the enemy with troops.

entries.zh: 梵志悉眾而陣，方與戰，偽北，梵志逐之，至坑所，其眾多陷，轉相驚駭，軍遂亂。
entries.en: Fan Zhi drew up his full army; Liu Fang fought, then feigned defeat. Fan Zhi gave chase; when his men reached the pits masses stumbled in, terror rippled through the ranks, and the host collapsed into chaos.
entries.literal: Fan Zhi marshaled his entire host in formation; Fang engaged and feigned retreat; Fan Zhi pursued to the pits, many men fell in, panic spread, and the army fell into disorder.

entries.zh: 方縱兵擊之，大破之。
entries.en: Liu Fang unleashed his troops and routed them completely.
entries.literal: Fang let his troops strike and utterly defeated them.

entries.zh: 頻戰輒敗，遂棄城而走。
entries.en: Battle after battle ended in defeat until they abandoned their capital and fled.
entries.literal: Repeated battles they lost; finally they abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 方入其都，獲其廟主十八枚，皆鑄金為之，蓋其有國十八葉矣。
entries.en: Liu Fang entered the capital and took eighteen ancestral spirit tablets, all cast in gold—proof that the dynasty had ruled for eighteen generations.
entries.literal: Fang entered their capital and seized eighteen spirit tablets of their temple, all cast in gold—for their kingdom had endured eighteen generations.

entries.zh: 方班師，梵志復其故地，遣使謝罪，於是朝貢不絕。
entries.en: When Liu Fang withdrew, Fan Zhi regained his old lands and dispatched envoys to sue for pardon; from then on tribute flowed without interruption.
entries.literal: As Fang withdrew, Fan Zhi recovered his former territory and sent envoys to apologize; thereafter tribute never ceased.

entries.zh: 赤土國，扶南之別種也。
entries.en: Chitu (Red Earth)—This realm was an offshoot of Funan.
entries.literal: Chitu—The state of Red Earth was a separate branch of Funan.

entries.zh: 在南海中，水行百餘日而達所都。
entries.en: It stood amid the southern oceans; reaching its capital required more than a hundred days at sea.
entries.literal: It lay in the southern sea; a voyage of more than a hundred days reached its capital.

entries.zh: 土色多赤，因以為號。
entries.en: The earth was predominantly red, which gave the country its name.
entries.literal: Much of the soil was red, hence the name.

entries.zh: 東波羅剌國，西婆羅娑國，南訶羅旦國，北拒大海，地方數千里。
entries.en: To the east lay Boluola, to the west Parasa, to the south Haradanta, and to the north the open ocean; the domain stretched several thousand li.
entries.literal: East lay Boluola state, west Parasa state, south Haradanta state, north the great sea; the territory measured several thousand li.

entries.zh: 其王姓瞿曇氏，名利富多塞，不知有國近遠。
entries.en: The king belonged to the Gautama clan and was named Lifuduosai; he had no notion of other countries' proximity or distance.
entries.literal: The king's surname was Gautama; his name Lifuduosai; he knew neither how near nor how far other realms might be.

entries.zh: 稱其父釋王位出家為道，傳位於利富多塞，在位十六年矣。
entries.en: He explained that his father had abdicated to pursue the Buddhist path and passed the throne to Lifuduosai, who had already ruled sixteen years.
entries.literal: He said his father had relinquished the kingship to follow the Way and transmitted the throne to Lifuduosai, who had reigned sixteen years.

entries.zh: 有三妻，並鄰國王之女也。
entries.en: He kept three wives, each a princess from a neighboring realm.
entries.literal: He had three consorts, all daughters of neighboring kings.

entries.zh: 居僧祗城，有門三重，相去各百許步。
entries.en: His residence was the Sangha Capital, ringed by three gates spaced roughly a hundred paces apart.
entries.literal: He dwelt in the monk's quarter city; the gates were triple, each gate about a hundred paces apart.

entries.zh: 每門圖畫飛仙、仙人、菩薩之像，縣金花鈴毦，婦女數十人，或奏樂，或捧金花。
entries.en: Every gate was painted with flying immortals, perfected beings, and bodhisattvas; golden floral bells and pennants hung overhead while dozens of women played music or carried golden blossoms.
entries.literal: At each gate were painted flying immortals, transcendent beings, and bodhisattvas; golden-flower bells and tassels hung; dozens of women either played music or bore golden flowers.

entries.zh: 又飾四婦人，容飾如佛塔邊金剛力士之狀，夾門而立。
entries.en: Four attendants were costumed like the diamond guardians at a pagoda's base and stood on either side of the gate.
entries.literal: Four women were adorned in the manner of the vajra guardians beside a stupa, standing flanking the gate.

entries.zh: 門外者持兵仗，門內者執白佛。
entries.en: Outside the gate stood armed guards; inside, attendants bearing white Buddhist standards.
entries.literal: Those outside the gate bore weapons; those inside bore white Buddhist banners.

entries.zh: 夾道垂素網，綴花。
entries.en: The avenue was draped with white silk nets adorned with blossoms.
entries.literal: Along the roadway hung white silk nets strung with flowers.

entries.zh: 王宮諸屋悉是重閣，北戶，北面而坐。
entries.en: Every structure in the royal quarter was multi-storied, its doors opening to the north, and the king sat facing northward.
entries.literal: All palace buildings were storied structures with north-facing doors; he sat facing north.

entries.zh: 坐三重之榻。
entries.en: He occupied a couch stacked three tiers high.
entries.literal: He sat on a triple-layered couch.

entries.zh: 衣朝霞布，冠金花冠，垂雜寶瓔珞。
entries.en: Dawn-glow silk clothed him; a golden floral crown crowned him; strings of assorted gems hung from his neck.
entries.literal: He wore dawn-glow silk robes, a golden floral crown, and pendants of assorted gems.

entries.zh: 四女子立侍，左右兵衞百餘人。
entries.en: Four women waited at his side while more than a hundred armed attendants guarded him.
entries.literal: Four women stood in attendance; over a hundred armed guards flanked him left and right.

entries.zh: 王榻後作一木龕，以金銀五香木雜鈿之。
entries.en: Behind the royal couch rose a wooden shrine inlaid with gold, silver, and fragrant hardwoods.
entries.literal: Behind the royal couch stood a wooden shrine inlaid with gold, silver, and assorted fragrant woods.

entries.zh: 龕後懸一金光焰，夾榻又樹二金鏡，鏡前並陳金甕，甕前各有金香爐。
entries.en: A golden flame-banner hung behind the shrine; a pair of golden mirrors flanked the couch; golden vessels stood before the mirrors, each paired with a golden censer.
entries.literal: Behind the shrine hung a golden flame-banner; flanking the couch stood two golden mirrors; before the mirrors golden jars, and before each jar a golden incense burner.

entries.zh: 當前置一金伏牛，牛前樹壹寶蓋，蓋左右皆有寶扇。
entries.en: Before him stood a golden recumbent ox; before the ox rose one jeweled canopy flanked by jeweled fans.
entries.literal: In front was placed a golden recumbent ox; before the ox stood a single jeweled canopy, with jeweled fans on either side.

entries.zh: 婆羅門等數百人，東西重行，相向而坐。
entries.en: Several hundred Brahmins sat in facing ranks, east and west.
entries.literal: Several hundred brahmins sat in double rows east and west, facing one another.

entries.zh: 其官有薩陀迦羅一人，陀拏達义二人，迦利蜜迦三人，共掌政事；
entries.en: His chief ministers were one Saduogaluo, two Tanaodayi, and three Kalimijia, who jointly governed civil affairs;
entries.literal: Officials: one Saduogaluo, two Tanaodayi, three Kalimijia—together they managed government affairs;

entries.zh: 俱羅末帝一人，掌刑法。
entries.en: one Juluomodi who oversaw criminal law.
entries.literal: one Juluomodi in charge of penal law.

entries.zh: 每城置那邪迦一人，鉢帝十人。
entries.en: Each city had one Nayage and ten Bodai officers.
entries.literal: In each city one Nayage and ten Bodai were installed.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：禮云：「南方曰蠻，有不火食者矣。」
entries.en: The historiographer remarks: The Book of Rites says, "The south is called the land of the Man, where some peoples do not cook their food with fire."
entries.literal: The historiographer says: The Rites state: "The south is called Man; there are those who do not eat by fire."

entries.zh: 書稱：「蠻夷猾夏。」
entries.en: The Book of Documents declares, "The barbarians of the four quarters harass the central lands."
entries.literal: The Documents state: "The Man and Yi are unruly toward Xia."

entries.zh: 詩曰：「蠢爾蠻荊。」
entries.en: The Book of Odes says, "You foolish barbarians of Jing."
entries.literal: The Odes say: "You foolish Man of Jing."

entries.zh: 種類實繁，代為紛梗。
entries.en: Their tribes are indeed numerous, and age after age they have stirred disorder.
entries.literal: Their kinds are truly numerous; generation after generation they have been a source of turmoil.

entries.zh: 自秦并二楚，漢平百越，地窮丹徼，景極日南，水陸可居，咸為郡縣。
entries.en: From the Qin conquest of Chu and the Han pacification of the Hundred Yue, the frontier ran to the Vermilion March and the horizon to Rinan; every habitable coast and river valley was organized into commanderies and counties.
entries.literal: From Qin annexing the two Chu, Han pacifying the Hundred Yue, the land reaching the cinnabar frontier, the view extending to Rinan—all places habitable by water or land were made commanderies and counties.

entries.zh: 暨乎境分吳、蜀，時經晉、宋，道有污隆，服叛不一。
entries.en: When the land was split between Wu and Shu and through the Jin and Song eras, fortunes rose and fell and allegiance shifted without end.
entries.literal: Down to when the realm was divided between Wu and Shu, through the Jin and Song periods, the Way had its rises and falls, submission and rebellion never uniform.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，克平九宇，煬帝纂業，威加八荒。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu received Heaven's mandate and pacified the nine realms; Emperor Yang succeeded him and extended imperial might to the eight directions.
entries.literal: Gaozu received the Mandate and conquered the nine realms; Emperor Yang succeeded to the enterprise and extended awe to the eight wilds.

entries.zh: 甘心遠夷，志求珍異，故師出於流求，兵加於林邑，威振殊俗，過於秦、漢遠矣。
entries.en: He bent his will toward distant peoples and coveted exotic treasures, dispatching armies to Liuqiu and troops against Linyi until foreign realms trembled at Sui might—a reach that far exceeded Qin and Han.
entries.literal: He set his heart on distant barbarians and sought rare and strange things; thus armies went forth to Liuqiu, troops were applied to Linyi, awe shook alien customs—far surpassing Qin and Han.

entries.zh: 雖有荒外之功，無救域中之敗。
entries.en: For all their triumphs beyond the frontier, they could not stave off catastrophe at the heart of the empire.
entries.literal: Although there were achievements in the wild beyond, they could not rescue defeat within the realm.

entries.zh: 傳曰：「非聖人，外寧必內憂。」
entries.en: The Commentary says, "When the ruler is no sage, peace abroad is sure to breed trouble within."
entries.literal: The Commentary says: "If one is not a sage, external peace necessarily brings internal worry."

entries.zh: 誠哉斯言也！
entries.en: How true indeed that saying proves!
entries.literal: How true indeed are these words!

entries.zh: 煬帝即位，募能通絕域者。
entries.en: After Emperor Yang took the throne he sought out men capable of crossing to the remotest lands.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne he recruited men able to reach the farthest realms.

entries.zh: 大業三年，屯田主事常駿、虞部主事王君政等請使赤土。
entries.en: In Daye year 3, agricultural intendant Chang Jun and supplies officer Wang Junzheng petitioned to go to Chitu.
entries.literal: In the third year of Daye, agricultural officer Chang Jun and palace supplies officer Wang Junzheng and others requested mission to Chitu.

entries.zh: 帝大悅，賜駿等帛各百匹，時服一襲而遣。
entries.en: The emperor was delighted, granted each of them a hundred bolts of silk and a suit of court robes, and dispatched them.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed on Jun and the others one hundred bolts of silk each plus one set of court dress and sent them off.

entries.zh: 齎物五千段，以賜赤土王。
entries.en: They bore five thousand bolts of goods as gifts for the king of Red Earth.
entries.literal: They carried five thousand lengths of goods to bestow on the king of Chitu.

entries.zh: 其年十月，駿等自南海郡乘舟，晝夜二旬，每值便風。
entries.en: In the tenth month of that year they set sail from Nanhai Commandery and, with fair winds whenever they arose, made the passage in twenty days and nights.
entries.literal: That year in the tenth month Jun and the others embarked from Nanhai commandery; day and night for twenty days, whenever favoring winds blew.

entries.zh: 至焦石山而過，東南泊陵伽鉢拔多洲，西與林邑相對，上有神祠焉。
entries.en: They passed Jiaoshi Mountain and anchored southeast at Lingjiaboduo Island, west of which lay Linyi and on which stood a spirit shrine.
entries.literal: They passed Jiaoshi Mountain, then moored southeast at Lingjiaboduo Isle, which lay opposite Linyi to the west and held a spirit shrine.

entries.zh: 又南行，至師子石，自是島嶼連接。
entries.en: Continuing south they came to Lion Rock, beyond which islands stretched in an unbroken chain.
entries.literal: Sailing south again they reached Shizi Rock; from there islands linked one to the next.

entries.zh: 又行二三日，西望見狼牙須國之山，於是南達雞籠島，至於赤土之界。
entries.en: Two or three days farther on they sighted westward the mountains of Langyaxu, then sailed south to Jilong Island and entered Red Earth's territory.
entries.literal: After two or three more days they saw to the west the mountains of Langyaxu state; then south to Jilong Island, reaching the borders of Chitu.

entries.zh: 其王遣婆羅門鳩摩羅以舶三十艘來迎，吹蠡擊鼓，以樂隋使，進金鎖以纜駿船。
entries.en: The king sent the Brahmin Jumoluo with thirty ships to meet them. Conches blared and drums thundered in salute to the Sui mission, and golden chains were offered to berth Chang Jun's ship.
entries.literal: The king sent the brahmin Jumoluo with thirty ships to welcome them; conches and drums sounded; music honored the Sui envoys; golden chains were presented to moor Jun's vessel.

entries.zh: 月餘，至其都，王遣其子那邪迦請與駿等禮見。
entries.en: After more than a month they arrived at the capital, where the king sent his son Nayage to invite Chang Jun and his party to an audience.
entries.literal: After more than a month they reached the capital; the king sent his son Nayage to request an audience with Jun and the others.

entries.zh: 先遣人送金盤，貯香花并鏡鑷，金合二枚，貯香油，金瓶八枚，貯香水，白疊布四條，以擬供使者盥洗。
entries.en: Envoys went ahead with a golden tray of fragrant blossoms, mirror and tweezers, two golden boxes of scented oil, eight golden flasks of perfumed water, and four bolts of white gauze for the diplomats' ceremonial washing.
entries.literal: First they sent men bringing a golden platter holding fragrant flowers together with mirror tweezers, two golden boxes holding fragrant oil, eight golden bottles holding scented water, and four bolts of white layered cloth for the envoys' ablutions.

entries.zh: 其日未時，那邪迦又將象二頭，持孔雀蓋以迎使人，并致金花、金盤以藉詔函。
entries.en: That afternoon Nayage returned with two elephants and a peacock-feather canopy to greet the envoys, and sent golden blossoms and a golden tray to bear the imperial letter case.
entries.literal: That day at the wei hour Nayage again led two elephants, holding a peacock canopy to welcome the envoys, and also presented golden flowers and a golden platter to cushion the imperial letter case.

entries.zh: 男女百人奏蠡鼓，婆羅門二人導路，至王宮。
entries.en: A hundred men and women beat conch drums while two Brahmins led the procession to the palace.
entries.literal: A hundred men and women played conch drums; two brahmins guided the way to the royal palace.

entries.zh: 駿等奉詔書上閣，王以下皆坐。
entries.en: Chang Jun and his party presented the edict in the upper hall; the king and his court were seated.
entries.literal: Jun and the others presented the imperial letter on the upper hall; the king and all below sat.

entries.zh: 宣詔訖，引駿等坐，奏天竺樂。
entries.en: After the edict was read they seated Chang Jun and his companions and performed music from India.
entries.literal: When the edict had been proclaimed, they led Jun and the others to seats and performed Indian music.

entries.zh: 事畢，駿等還館，又遣婆羅門就館送食，以草葉為盤，其大方丈。
entries.en: When the ceremony ended the envoys returned to their quarters, where Brahmins brought food on leaf platters each about ten feet square.
entries.literal: When the affair was finished Jun and the others returned to the lodge; brahmins were again sent to the lodge with food, using grass leaves as platters about a zhang square.

entries.zh: 因謂駿曰：「今是大國中人，非復赤土國矣。
entries.en: They told Chang Jun, "You are guests of a great empire now, no longer mere visitors from Red Earth.
entries.literal: They then said to Jun: "You are now men of a great state, no longer of the state of Red Earth.

entries.zh: 飲食疎薄，願為大國意而食之。」
entries.en: Our fare is humble; please accept it in the spirit of your great realm."
entries.literal: The food is coarse and thin; we wish you to eat with the great state's intent in mind."

entries.zh: 後數日，請駿等入宴，儀衞導從如初見之禮。
entries.en: A few days later they invited the envoys to a banquet with the same guard and ceremonial escort as at the first audience.
entries.literal: Several days later they invited Jun and the others to a banquet; guards and attendants escorted them with the same ceremony as at the first audience.

entries.zh: 王前設兩牀，牀上并設草葉盤，方一丈五尺，上有黃白紫赤四色之餅，牛、羊、魚、鼈、猪、蝳蝐之肉百餘品。
entries.en: Before the king stood two couches, each bearing leaf platters fifteen feet square piled with yellow, white, purple, and red cakes and more than a hundred dishes of beef, mutton, fish, turtle, pork, and shellfish.
entries.literal: Before the king two couches were set; on each couch grass-leaf platters fifteen chi square, bearing yellow, white, purple, and red cakes, and more than a hundred kinds of beef, mutton, fish, turtle, pork, and oyster meat.

entries.zh: 延駿升牀，從者坐於地席，各以金鍾置酒，女樂迭奏，禮遺甚厚。
entries.en: Chang Jun was invited onto the couch while his attendants sat on mats below, each with a golden cup of wine; female musicians played in succession, and the hospitality was lavish.
entries.literal: They invited Jun up onto the couch; attendants sat on ground mats, each with a golden goblet set with wine; female musicians played in turn; gifts and courtesy were very generous.

entries.zh: 尋遣那邪迦隨駿貢方物，并獻金芙蓉冠、龍腦香。
entries.en: Soon Nayage was sent to accompany Chang Jun home with tribute goods, including a golden lotus crown and dragon-brain camphor.
entries.literal: Soon they sent Nayage to accompany Jun in presenting local products, and also offered a golden lotus crown and dragon-brain incense.

entries.zh: 以鑄金為多羅葉，隱起成文以為表，金函封之，令婆羅門以香花奏蠡鼓而送之。
entries.en: They cast gold into bodhi-leaf plaques inscribed with raised text as a formal tribute document, sealed it in a golden casket, and sent Brahmins with flowers and conch drums to see the mission off.
entries.literal: They cast gold into bodhi-leaf form with raised inscriptions as a memorial, sealed it in a golden case, and had brahmins with fragrant flowers playing conch drums to send them off.

entries.zh: 既入海，見綠魚羣飛水上。
entries.en: Once at sea they saw shoals of green fish skimming the surface.
entries.literal: Once they entered the sea they saw green fish flying in groups above the water.

entries.zh: 浮海十餘日，至林邑東南，並山而行。
entries.en: After more than ten days at sea they reached the southeast of Linyi and coasted along the mountains.
entries.literal: They floated on the sea more than ten days, reaching southeast of Linyi, sailing along the mountains.

entries.zh: 其海水闊千餘步，色黃氣腥，舟行一日不絕，云是大魚糞也。
entries.en: The water stretched more than a thousand paces across, yellow and foul; a ship could sail a full day without leaving it, which they said was the droppings of enormous fish.
entries.literal: The seawater there was more than a thousand paces wide, yellow in color and foul-smelling; a boat could sail a full day without passing through it—they said it was the excrement of great fish.

entries.zh: 循海北岸，達于交阯。
entries.en: They followed the northern coast until they reached Jiaozhi.
entries.literal: Following the northern shore of the sea, they reached Jiaozhi.

entries.zh: 駿以六年春與那邪迦於弘農謁，帝大悅，賜駿等物二百段，俱授秉義尉，那邪迦等官賞各有差。
entries.en: In the spring of Daye year 6 Chang Jun and Nayage were received at Hongnong. The emperor was delighted, granted two hundred lengths of goods to the envoys, appointed them all Bearer of Righteousness Commandants, and rewarded Nayage and his party with offices of varying rank.
entries.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Jun and Nayage had audience at Hongnong; the emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed on Jun and the others two hundred lengths of goods, all appointed Bearer of Righteousness Commandant, and Nayage and the others received official rewards in varying degrees.

entries.zh: 真臘國，在林邑西南，本扶南之屬國也。
entries.en: Zhenla—This kingdom lay southwest of Linyi and had originally been a dependency of Funan.
entries.literal: Zhenla—The state of Zhenla lay southwest of Linyi; it was originally a subject state of Funan.

entries.zh: 去日南郡舟行六十日，而南接車渠國，西有朱江國。
entries.en: It lay sixty days' sail from Rinan Commandery; Chequ bordered it to the south and Zhujiang to the west.
entries.literal: From Rinan commandery sixty days by boat; south it bordered Chequ state, west lay Zhujiang state.

entries.zh: 其王姓剎利氏，名質多斯那。
entries.en: The king belonged to the Kshatriya clan and was named Zhiduosina.
entries.literal: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Zhiduosina.

entries.zh: 自其祖漸已強盛，至質多斯那，遂兼扶南而有之。
entries.en: His line had grown steadily stronger since his forebears' day; under Zhiduosina they annexed Funan outright.
entries.literal: From his ancestors they had gradually grown strong; by Zhiduosina's time they had annexed Funan and possessed it.

entries.zh: 死，子伊奢那先代立。
entries.en: At his death his son Yishena ascended the throne.
entries.literal: When he died, his son Yishena succeeded in his place.

entries.zh: 居伊奢那城，郭下二萬餘家。
entries.en: He ruled from Yishena City, which held more than twenty thousand households within its outer walls.
entries.literal: He dwelt in Yishena city; outside the walls were more than twenty thousand households.

entries.zh: 城中有一大堂，是王聽政之所。
entries.en: A great hall in the city served as the seat of royal government.
entries.literal: Within the city was one great hall, the place where the king heard government affairs.

entries.zh: 總大城三十，城有數千家，各有部帥，官名與林邑同。
entries.en: The realm comprised thirty major cities of several thousand households each, each with its own commander; official titles matched those of Linyi.
entries.literal: In all thirty great cities, each with several thousand households, each with its own commander; official titles were the same as Linyi's.

entries.zh: 其王三日一聽朝，坐五香七寶牀，上施寶帳。
entries.en: The king held audience every third day, seated on a couch of five aromatics and seven treasures beneath a jeweled canopy.
entries.literal: The king held court every three days, seated on a five-fragrance seven-treasure couch with a jeweled canopy above.

entries.zh: 其帳以文木為竿，象牙、金鈿為壁，狀如小屋，懸金光焰，有同於赤土。
entries.en: The canopy's poles were carved hardwood, its walls ivory and gold inlay shaped like a small pavilion, with a golden flame-banner hanging above—much as in Red Earth.
entries.literal: The canopy used patterned wood for poles, ivory and gold inlay for walls, shaped like a small house, with a golden flame-banner suspended—much like Red Earth.

entries.zh: 前有金香鑪，二人侍側。
entries.en: A golden censer stood before him with two attendants at his side.
entries.literal: Before it stood a golden incense burner; two attendants waited at the side.

entries.zh: 王着朝霞古貝，瞞絡腰腹，下垂至脛，頭戴金寶花冠，被真珠瓔珞，足履革屣，耳懸金璫。
entries.en: The king wore dawn-glow cotton, a wrap about waist and hips falling to the shins, a golden floral crown studded with gems, strings of pearls, leather sandals, and golden earrings.
entries.literal: The king wore dawn-glow ancient shell cloth, a wrap around waist and belly hanging to the shins, a golden jeweled floral crown on his head, true-pearl pendants on his body, leather sandals on his feet, golden earrings suspended from his ears.

entries.zh: 常服白疊，以象牙為屩。
entries.en: For everyday dress he wore white gauze and ivory sandals.
entries.literal: For ordinary dress he wore white layered cloth and ivory for shoes.

entries.zh: 若露髮，則不加瓔珞。
entries.en: When his hair was uncovered he wore no pearl necklaces.
entries.literal: If his hair was uncovered, he did not add the pearl pendants.

entries.zh: 臣人服製，大抵相類。
entries.en: His subjects' dress followed much the same pattern.
entries.literal: Subjects' dress and regulations were generally similar.

entries.zh: 有五大臣，一曰孤落支，二曰高相憑，三曰婆何多陵，四曰舍摩陵，五曰髯多婁，及諸小臣。
entries.en: Five great ministers—Guluo Zhi, Gaoxiang Ping, Poheduo Ling, Shemo Ling, and Randuo Lou—headed a host of lesser officials.
entries.literal: There were five great ministers: first Guluo zhi, second Gaoxiang ping, third Poheduo ling, fourth Shemo ling, fifth Randuo lou, and various lesser ministers.

entries.zh: 朝於王者，輒以階下三稽首。
entries.en: Ministers approaching the throne always kowtowed three times at the foot of the steps.
entries.literal: Those attending audience with the king always performed three prostrations below the steps.

entries.zh: 王喚上階，則跪，以兩手抱膊，遶王環坐。
entries.en: When summoned up the steps they knelt, clasped their arms, and sat in a ring around the king.
entries.literal: When the king summoned them up the steps they knelt, embraced their arms with both hands, and sat in a circle around the king.

entries.zh: 議政事訖，跪伏而去。
entries.en: When business was finished they prostrated themselves and withdrew.
entries.literal: When government affairs had been discussed they knelt prostrate and departed.

entries.zh: 階庭門閣，侍衞有千餘人，被甲持仗。
entries.en: More than a thousand armored guards with weapons stood on the steps, in the courtyard, and at the gates.
entries.literal: On the steps, courtyard, gates, and pavilions, guards numbered more than a thousand, armored and bearing weapons.

entries.zh: 其國與參半、朱江二國和親，數與林邑、陀桓二國戰爭。
entries.en: Zhenla was allied by marriage with Canban and Zhujiang but fought repeatedly with Linyi and Tuohuan.
entries.literal: The state was allied by marriage with Canban and Zhujiang; it frequently warred with Linyi and Tuohuan.

entries.zh: 其人行止皆持甲仗，若有征伐，因而用之。
entries.en: Its people went about always armed; when war arose they were ready at once.
entries.literal: Its people in going about always carried armor and weapons; if there was campaigning, they used them accordingly.

entries.zh: 其俗非王正妻子，不得為嗣。
entries.en: By custom only a son of the king's principal wife could inherit the throne.
entries.literal: By their custom only the king's principal wife's son could succeed.

entries.zh: 王初立之日，所有兄弟並刑殘之，或去一指，或劓其鼻，別處供給，不得仕進。
entries.en: On the day a new king was enthroned every brother was mutilated—one finger cut off or the nose severed—then settled elsewhere on an allowance and barred from office forever.
entries.literal: On the day the king first took the throne, all his brothers were mutilated by punishment—some lost a finger, some had their noses cut off—settled elsewhere with provisions, and could not enter office.

entries.zh: 大業十二年，遣使貢獻，帝禮之甚厚，其後亦絕。
entries.en: In Daye year 12 they sent tribute envoys whom the emperor received with great honor; afterward contact ceased as well.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye they sent envoys with tribute; the emperor treated them very generously; thereafter tribute also ceased.

entries.zh: 婆利婆利國，自交阯浮海，南過赤土、丹丹，乃至其國。
entries.en: Bali—From Jiaozhi one sailed south past Red Earth and Dandan to reach this kingdom.
entries.literal: Bali—The state of Bali: from Jiaozhi by sea, south past Red Earth and Dandan, then reaching its state.

entries.zh: 國界東西四月行，南北四十五日行。
entries.en: The realm measured four months' travel east to west and forty-five days north to south.
entries.literal: The state's borders were four months' travel east-west, forty-five days north-south.

entries.zh: 王姓剎利邪伽，名護濫那婆。
entries.en: The king belonged to the Kshatriya clan and was named Hulannapo.
entries.literal: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Hulannapo.

entries.zh: 官曰獨訶邪挐，次曰獨訶氏挐。
entries.en: Chief ministers were titled Duheyanie, with Duheshanie beneath them.
entries.literal: Officials were titled Duheyanie, next Duheshanie.

entries.zh: 國人善投輪刀，其大如鏡，中有竅，外鋒如鋸，遠以投人，無不中。
entries.en: Its people excelled at hurling disc-knives as large as mirrors, pierced at the center with saw-toothed rims that never missed their mark at a distance.
entries.literal: The people were skilled at throwing wheel-knives, as large as mirrors, with a hole in the center, outer edge sharp like a saw; thrown from afar at people, none missed.

entries.zh: 其餘兵器與中國略同。
entries.en: Their other weapons were much the same as China's.
entries.literal: Their remaining weapons were roughly the same as China's.

entries.zh: 俗類真臘，物產同於林邑。
entries.en: Customs resembled Zhenla's and products matched Linyi's.
entries.literal: Customs resembled Zhenla's; products were the same as Linyi's.

entries.zh: 其殺人及盜，截其手，姦者鎖其足，朞年而止。
entries.en: Murderers and thieves had their hands cut off; adulterers were shackled by the feet for a year.
entries.literal: For murder and theft they cut off the hand; for adultery they shackled the feet, ending after one year.

entries.zh: 祭祀必以月晦，盤貯酒肴，浮之流水。
entries.en: Sacrifices were always held on the last day of the month, with platters of food and wine set adrift on the current.
entries.literal: Sacrifices were always on the last day of the month; platters held wine and food, floated on flowing water.

entries.zh: 每十一月，必設大祭。
entries.en: Every eleventh month they held a major festival.
entries.literal: Every eleventh month they invariably held a great sacrifice.

entries.zh: 海出珊瑚。
entries.en: Coral came from their seas.
entries.literal: The sea produced coral.

entries.zh: 有鳥名舍利，解人語。
entries.en: A bird called Sheli could understand human speech.
entries.literal: There was a bird named Sheli that understood human speech.

entries.zh: 大業十二年，遣使朝貢，後遂絕。
entries.en: In Daye year 12 they sent tribute envoys; contact ceased thereafter.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye they sent envoys to court with tribute; afterward it ceased.

entries.zh: 于時南荒有丹丹、盤盤二國，亦來貢方物，其風俗物產，大抵相類云。
entries.en: At that time the southern realms of Dandan and Panpan also sent native goods; their customs and products were said to be much the same.
entries.literal: At that time in the southern wilds the two states Dandan and Panpan also came to offer local products; their customs and products were generally similar, it is said.

entries.zh: 【序】南蠻雜類，與華人錯居，曰蜒，曰獽，曰俚，曰獠，曰㐌，俱無君長，隨山洞而居，古先所謂百越是也。
entries.en: [Preface] The miscellaneous peoples of the southern frontier live intermingled with the Chinese. They include the Yan, Xian, Li, Liao, and Yi. None of them have kings or chiefs; they take their dwellings in mountain caves. These are the peoples the ancients knew as the Hundred Yue.
entries.literal: [Preface] The various sorts of southern barbarians, interspersed with Chinese, are called Yan, Xian, Li, Liao, and Yi; all lack rulers and chiefs, dwelling wherever mountain caves offer shelter—they are what the ancients called the Hundred Yue.

entries.zh: 其俗斷髮文身，好相攻討，浸以微弱，稍屬於中國，皆列為郡縣，同之齊人，不復詳載。
entries.en: They cut their hair short and tattoo their bodies, and they relish raiding one another. As they grew weaker, they were gradually absorbed into the Chinese sphere; all were organized as commanderies and counties and governed like ordinary subjects of the central lands. They are no longer described in detail below.
entries.literal: Their custom is to cut the hair and tattoo the body; they are fond of attacking one another. Gradually weakening, they gradually came under China; all were enrolled as commanderies and counties and treated like the people of Qi—no further detailed record is given here.

entries.zh: 大業中，南荒朝貢者十餘國，其事迹多湮滅而無聞。
entries.en: During the Daye reign period more than a dozen southern realms sent tribute missions, but most of their histories have perished and their names are forgotten.
entries.literal: In the Daye era, more than a dozen states of the southern wilds came to court with tribute; most of their deeds have been lost and are unheard of.

entries.zh: 今所存錄，四國而已。
entries.en: Only four countries survive in the records that follow.
entries.literal: Of what is preserved in record today, there are only four states.

entries.zh: 林邑林邑之先，因漢末交阯女子徵側之亂，內縣功曹子區連殺縣令，自號為王。
entries.en: Linyi—The kingdom's origins lie in the turmoil at the end of the Han, when the Jiaozhi rebel Zheng Ce rose up. A clerk of the inner district named Qu Lian assassinated the magistrate and proclaimed himself king.
entries.literal: Linyi—The lineage of Linyi: because of the rebellion of the Jiaozhi woman Zheng Ce at the end of Han, the inner commandery clerk Qu Lian killed the magistrate and declared himself king.

entries.zh: 無子，其甥范熊代立，死，子逸立。
entries.en: Qu Lian left no son. His nephew Fan Xiong took the throne, and after Fan Xiong's death his son Yi became king.
entries.literal: He had no son; his sister's son Fan Xiong succeeded him. When he died, his son Yi succeeded.

entries.zh: 日南人范文因亂為逸僕隸，遂教之築宮室，造器械。
entries.en: During the upheaval a Rinan native named Fan Wen entered Yi's service as a bondservant and taught him palace-building and the forging of arms.
entries.literal: A man of Rinan named Fan Wen became Yi's slave during the disorder, and went on to teach him how to build palaces and manufacture weapons.

entries.zh: 逸甚信任，使文將兵，極得眾心。
entries.en: Yi relied on him completely, gave him command of the army, and Fan Wen won the wholehearted loyalty of the populace.
entries.literal: Yi trusted him deeply and put Fan Wen in command of troops; Fan Wen won the utmost devotion of the people.

entries.zh: 文因間其子弟，或奔或徙。
entries.en: Fan Wen meanwhile uprooted Yi's sons and younger relatives, sending some into exile and displacing others.
entries.literal: Fan Wen took the opportunity to drive away or disperse Yi's sons and younger kinsmen—some fled, some were relocated.

entries.zh: 及逸死，國無嗣，文自立為王。
entries.en: When Yi died leaving no successor, Fan Wen seized the throne for himself.
entries.literal: When Yi died without an heir, Fan Wen declared himself king.

entries.zh: 其後范佛為晉揚威將軍戴桓所破。
entries.en: Later his descendant Fan Fo was broken by Dai Huan, Jin's general of manifest authority.
entries.literal: Later Fan Fo was defeated by Dai Huan, general of manifest authority under Jin.

entries.zh: 宋交州刺史檀和之將兵擊之，深入其境。
entries.en: Under the Song, Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi marched against them and drove deep into their lands.
entries.literal: Song's Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi led troops to attack them and penetrated deep into their territory.

entries.zh: 至梁、陳，亦通使往來。
entries.en: Under the Liang and Chen dynasties too they continued to send missions back and forth.
entries.literal: Through the Liang and Chen periods as well, envoys were exchanged.

entries.zh: 五十六年，帝復如晉；
entries.en: In the fifty-sixth year the prince again went to Jin;
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, the emperor again went to Jin;

entries.zh: 其年冬，還國。
entries.en: and that winter came home to the realm.
entries.literal: that winter he returned to the state.

entries.zh: 晉遺帝錦、罽、繒、綵、綿、絹、諸物，咸出豐厚，車牛百乘。
entries.en: Jin sent him brocade, felt, silk, dyed cloth, cotton, gauze—gifts in lavish profusion, and a hundred ox-carts besides.
entries.literal: Jin presented the emperor brocade, felt, silk, colored silks, cotton, gauze—all manner of goods, lavishly generous, a hundred cartloads of cattle and oxen.

entries.zh: 行達并州，晉征北將軍衞瓘，以帝為人雄異，恐為後患，乃密啟晉帝，請留不遣。
entries.en: At Bingzhou, Jin's northern commander Wei Guan saw in the prince a man of singular power and feared trouble later on. He secretly memorialized the Jin throne to hold him and not let him go.
entries.literal: When the journey reached Bingzhou, Jin's General Who Conquers the North Wei Guan, because the emperor was a man of heroic singularity, feared he would be a later trouble—thereupon secretly memorialized the Jin emperor requesting to detain him and not send him on.

entries.zh: 晉帝難於失信，不許。
entries.en: The Jin emperor would not break his word and refused.
entries.literal: The Jin emperor found it hard to break faith and did not consent.

entries.zh: 瓘復請以金錦賂國之大人，令致間隙，使相危害。
entries.en: Wei Guan asked again to buy off the realm's chiefs with gold and brocade, sowing discord so they would turn on one another.
entries.literal: Wei Guan again requested to use gold and brocade to bribe the state's great chiefs, causing them to sow discord so that they would harm one another.

entries.zh: 晉帝從之，遂留帝。
entries.en: The Jin emperor agreed, and so the prince was kept.
entries.literal: The Jin emperor assented and thus detained the emperor.

entries.zh: 於是國之執事及外部大人，皆受瓘貨。
entries.en: Then the court officers and the outer chiefs all took Wei Guan's gifts.
entries.literal: Thereupon the state's executives and the outer great chiefs all received Wei Guan's bribes.

entries.zh: 其年，始祖不豫。
entries.en: That year, the Founding Ancestor fell ill.
entries.literal: That year, the Founding Ancestor was unwell.

entries.zh: 烏丸王庫賢，親近任勢，先受衞瓘之貨，故欲沮動諸部，因在庭中礪鉞斧，諸大人問欲何為，答曰：「上恨汝曹讒殺太子，今欲盡收諸大人長子殺之。」
entries.en: Kuxian, King of the Wuwan, was close to the ruler and used his influence. Having already accepted Wei Guan's bribes, he wanted to alarm the tribes, so he sharpened an axe in the courtyard. When the chiefs asked what he was doing, he said, "The sovereign hates you for slandering and killing the crown prince. Now he intends to seize every chief's eldest son and kill them."
entries.literal: Kuxian, King of the Wuwan, was intimate with him and relied on his influence. He had earlier accepted Wei Guan's bribes, and so wished to unsettle the tribes. He therefore sharpened an axe in the courtyard. When the chiefs asked what he intended to do, he replied: "The sovereign resents you all for slandering and killing the crown prince; now he wishes to seize the eldest sons of all the chiefs and kill them."

entries.zh: 大人皆信，各各散走。
entries.en: The chiefs all believed him and scattered in flight.
entries.literal: The chiefs all believed him and scattered in flight one by one.

entries.zh: 始祖尋崩。
entries.en: The Founding Ancestor soon died.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor soon died.

entries.zh: 凡饗國五十八年，年一百四歲。
entries.en: In all, he reigned fifty-eight years and lived to one hundred and four.
entries.literal: In all, he enjoyed the state for fifty-eight years and was one hundred and four years old.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，尊為始祖。
entries.en: When Taizu ascended the throne, he honored him as the Founding Ancestor.
entries.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, he honored him as the Founding Ancestor.

entries.zh: 五十八年，方遣帝。
entries.en: In the fifty-eighth year they at last let the prince go.
entries.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, they finally sent the emperor off.

entries.zh: 始祖聞帝歸，大悅，使諸部大人詣陰館迎之。
entries.en: When the Founding Ancestor learned the prince was coming home he rejoiced and sent chiefs of every tribe to Yin Lodge to welcome him.
entries.literal: When the Founding Ancestor heard the emperor was returning he was greatly pleased and sent great chiefs of various tribes to Yin Lodge to welcome him.

entries.zh: 酒酣，帝仰視飛鳥，謂諸大人曰：「我為汝曹取之。」
entries.en: As the wine deepened, the prince looked up at birds on the wing and told the chiefs: "I will fetch those down for you."
entries.literal: When the wine had gone deep, the emperor looked up at birds in flight and said to the great chiefs: "I will take them for you all."

entries.zh: 援彈飛丸，應弦而落。
entries.en: He took up a pellet bow and shot; at the snap of the string the birds dropped.
entries.literal: He took up his pellet-bow and flying pellets; at the twang of the string they fell.

entries.zh: 時國俗無彈，眾咸大驚，乃相謂曰：「太子風彩被服，同於南夏，兼奇術絕世，若繼國統，變易舊俗，吾等必不得志，不若在國諸子，習本淳樸。」
entries.en: The realm had never known the pellet bow; all were astonished and whispered: "The crown prince dresses and carries himself like the southern Chinese, and his uncanny skill has no match. If he inherits the throne and changes our ways, we shall lose our standing. Better a son raised here, steeped in our old simplicity."
entries.literal: At that time the state custom had no pellet-bows; the multitude was greatly startled and said among themselves: "The crown prince's manner and dress are like those of Southern Xia, and his strange arts surpass the world—if he inherits the state succession and alters the old customs, we shall certainly not get our way; better the sons within the state, who are versed in our native simplicity."

entries.zh: 咸以為然。
entries.en: They were agreed.
entries.literal: All thought this right.

entries.zh: 且離間素行，乃謀危害，並先馳還。
entries.en: The seeds of division Wei Guan had planted were already ripe; they plotted against the prince and raced home ahead of him.
entries.literal: Moreover the discord sown for many years—thereupon they plotted harm, and all galloped ahead to return first.

entries.zh: 始祖問曰：「我子既歷他國，進德何如？」
entries.en: The Founding Ancestor asked: "My son has lived in a foreign land—how has his character grown?"
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor asked: "My son, having passed through another state—how has his virtue advanced?"

entries.zh: 皆對曰：「太子才藝非常，引空弓而落飛鳥，是似得晉人異法怪術，亂國害民之兆，惟願察之。」
entries.en: They answered: "The crown prince's gifts are beyond the common run. He drew an empty bow and felled a bird in flight—as if he had learned Jin sorcery. It is an omen of chaos and harm to the people. We beg Your Majesty to look into this."
entries.literal: All replied: "The crown prince's talent is extraordinary; drawing an empty bow he brought down a flying bird—that is as if he had obtained Jin men's strange methods and occult arts, a portent of disordering the state and harming the people. We wish Your Majesty would examine this."

entries.zh: 自帝在晉之後，諸子愛寵日進，始祖年踰期頤，頗有所惑，聞諸大人之語，意乃有疑。
entries.en: Since the prince had gone to Jin, the other sons had won favor day by day. The Founding Ancestor was past a hundred and his mind was clouded; hearing the chiefs, he began to doubt.
entries.literal: From the time the prince had been in Jin, the love and favor toward the other sons daily grew; the Founding Ancestor, more than a hundred years old, was somewhat confused; hearing the great chiefs' words, his mind came to harbor doubt.

entries.zh: 因曰：「不可容者，便當除之。」
entries.en: He said: "If he cannot be borne, then do away with him."
entries.literal: He said: "Whoever cannot be tolerated—just remove him."

entries.zh: 於是諸大人乃馳詣塞南，矯害帝。
entries.en: The chiefs galloped south of the frontier passes and, by forged order, killed the prince.
entries.literal: Thereupon the great chiefs galloped to the south of the passes and, by forged command, killed the emperor.

entries.zh: 既而，始祖甚悔之。
entries.en: Soon after, the Founding Ancestor was filled with remorse.
entries.literal: Before long the Founding Ancestor deeply regretted it.

entries.zh: 帝身長八尺，英姿瓌偉，在晉之日，朝士英俊多與親善，雅為人物歸仰。
entries.en: The prince stood eight feet tall, splendid in bearing. In Jin many of the court's finest men befriended him; men of the age looked up to him.
entries.literal: The emperor stood eight feet in height, heroic and magnificent in bearing; during his days in Jin many of the court's gifted men were fond of him—he was esteemed among men of the age.

entries.zh: 後乃追諡焉。
entries.en: Later he was given a posthumous title.
entries.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed with a title.

entries.zh: 二年，葬文帝及皇后封氏。
entries.en: In the second year they interred Emperor Wen and Empress Feng.
entries.literal: In the second year they buried Emperor Wen and Empress Lady Feng.

entries.zh: 初，思帝欲改葬，未果而崩。
entries.en: Earlier Emperor Si had planned a reburial, but died before it could be done.
entries.literal: Earlier Emperor Si had wished to rebury them, but before accomplishing it he died.

entries.zh: 至是，述成前意焉。
entries.en: At last they carried out what he had intended.
entries.literal: Now they fulfilled his earlier intention.

entries.zh: 晉成都王司馬穎遣從事中郎田思，河間王司馬顒遣司馬靳利，并州刺史司馬騰遣主簿梁天，並來會葬。
entries.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, sent Tian Si as attendant-in-ordinary; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, sent Commandant Jin Li; Sima Teng, inspector of Bingzhou, sent registrar Liang Tian—all to attend the burial.
entries.literal: Sima Ying the Prince of Chengdu sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Tian Si; Sima Yong the Prince of Hejian sent Commandant Jin Li; Sima Teng the Inspector of Bingzhou sent Registrar Liang Tian—all came for the funeral.

entries.zh: 遠近赴者二十萬人。
entries.en: Nearly two hundred thousand mourners came from near and far.
entries.literal: From near and far two hundred thousand came to attend.

entries.zh: 十年，晉惠帝為成都王穎逼留在鄴。
entries.en: In the tenth year Emperor Hui of Jin was held at Ye by Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu.
entries.literal: In the tenth year Emperor Hui of Jin was compelled by Sima Ying the Prince of Chengdu to remain at Ye.

entries.zh: 匈奴別種劉淵反於離石，自號漢王。
entries.en: Liu Yuan, of a Xiongnu splinter line, rose at Lishi and proclaimed himself King of Han.
entries.literal: Liu Yuan, a separate branch of the Xiongnu, rebelled at Lishi and styled himself King of Han.

entries.zh: 并州刺史司馬騰來乞師，桓帝率十餘萬騎，帝亦同時大舉以助之，大破淵眾於西河、上黨。
entries.en: Sima Teng, inspector of Bingzhou, begged for aid. Emperor Huan led more than a hundred thousand cavalry, and Emperor Zhao mobilized on the same scale; together they shattered Liu Yuan's forces at Xihe and Shangdang.
entries.literal: Sima Teng, Inspector of Bingzhou, came to beg troops; Emperor Huan led more than a hundred thousand horse, and the emperor also launched a great campaign at the same time to assist, thoroughly defeating Liu Yuan's host at Xihe and Shangdang.

entries.zh: 會惠帝還洛，騰乃辭師。
entries.en: When Emperor Hui was restored to Luoyang, Teng released the allied troops.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, Teng then dismissed the army.

entries.zh: 桓帝與騰盟於汾東而還。
entries.en: Emperor Huan swore alliance with Teng east of the Fen River and marched home.
entries.literal: Emperor Huan made alliance with Teng east of the Fen and returned.

entries.zh: 乃使輔相衞雄、段繁，於參合陂西累石為亭，樹碑以記行焉。
entries.en: He had his ministers Wei Xiong and Duan Fan raise a stone pavilion west of Canhe Marsh and erect a stele to commemorate the campaign.
entries.literal: He sent his aides Wei Xiong and Duan Fan west of Canhepo to pile stones into a pavilion and set up a stele to record the journey.

entries.zh: 十年，遣使詣鄴觀釁。
entries.en: In the tenth year he sent envoys to Ye to spy out the situation.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he sent envoys to Ye to observe signs of trouble.

entries.zh: 是年，司馬聃擒李勢。
entries.en: That year Sima Dan captured Li Shi.
entries.literal: That year Sima Dan captured Li Shi.

entries.zh: 張重華遣使朝貢。
entries.en: Zhang Chonghua sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: Zhang Chonghua sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 七年春二月，遣大人長孫秩迎后慕容氏元真之女於境。
entries.en: In the second month of spring in the seventh year he sent the great lady Changsun Zhi to the border to welcome the empress—Murong Yuanzhen's daughter.
entries.literal: In the second month of spring of the seventh year he sent the great lady Changsun Zhi to welcome the empress, daughter of Murong Yuanzhen of the Murong clan, at the border.

entries.zh: 夏六月，皇后至自和龍。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer the empress arrived from Helong.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of summer the empress arrived from Helong.

entries.zh: 秋七月，慕容元真遣使奉聘，求交婚，帝許之，九月，以烈帝女妻之。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with betrothal gifts, seeking a marriage alliance. The emperor agreed, and in the ninth month gave Emperor Lie's daughter to him in marriage.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with betrothal gifts, seeking a marriage alliance; the emperor consented; in the ninth month he gave Emperor Lie's daughter to him in marriage.

entries.zh: 其年，司馬岳死，子聃僭立。
entries.en: That year Sima Yue died, and his son Dan usurped the throne.
entries.literal: That year Sima Yue died; his son Dan usurped the throne.

entries.zh: 二十四年春，衞辰遣使朝聘。
entries.en: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year Weichen sent envoys on a court visit.
entries.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year Weichen sent envoys on a court visit.

entries.zh: 是年，司馬聃死，衍子千齡僭立。
entries.en: That year Sima Dan died, and Yan's son Qianling usurped the throne.
entries.literal: That year Sima Dan died; Yan's son Qianling usurped the throne.

entries.zh: 三十四年春，長孫斤謀反，伏誅。
entries.en: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.
entries.literal: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.

entries.zh: 斤之反也，拔刃向御座，太子獻明皇帝諱寔格之，傷脅。
entries.en: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the throne; the crown prince—the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi—blocked him and was wounded in the flank.
entries.literal: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the imperial seat; the crown prince, the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi, blocked him and was wounded in the flank.

entries.zh: 夏五月，薨，後追諡焉。
entries.en: In the fifth month of summer he died; a posthumous title was conferred later.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of summer he died; posthumous title was conferred afterward.

entries.zh: 秋七月，皇孫珪生，大赦。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 是年，司馬弈臣桓溫，廢弈為海西公，立叡子昱。
entries.en: That year Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and enthroned Rui's son Yu.
entries.literal: That year the minister Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and installed Rui's son Yu.

entries.zh: 二十八年春正月，衞辰謀反，東渡河。
entries.en: In the first month of spring of the twenty-eighth year Weichen plotted rebellion and crossed the river to the east.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-eighth year Weichen plotted rebellion and crossed the river eastward.

entries.zh: 帝討之，衞辰懼而遁走。
entries.en: The emperor attacked him, and Weichen fled in fear.
entries.literal: The emperor attacked him; Weichen, in fear, fled.

entries.zh: 冬十二月，苻堅遣使朝貢。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter Fu Jian sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Fu Jian sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 是歲，司馬千齡死，弟弈僭立。
entries.en: That year Sima Qianling died, and his younger brother Yi usurped the throne.
entries.literal: That year Sima Qianling died; his younger brother Yi usurped the throne.

entries.zh: 三十五年，司馬昱死，子昌明僭立。
entries.en: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died, and his son Changming usurped the throne.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died; his son Changming usurped the throne.

entries.zh: 昔黃帝有子二十五人，或內列諸華，或外分荒服，昌意少子，受封北土，國有大鮮卑山，因以為號。
entries.en: Long ago the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons: some served within the Chinese heartland, others were sent to govern the outer marches. Changyi, his youngest, was enfeoffed in the north, where the great Xianbei Mountain stood—and from that mountain the people took their name.
entries.literal: In olden times the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; some were enrolled within the Chinese domains, some were apportioned to distant borderlands. Changyi was his youngest son; he received a fief in the northern lands. The state had the great Xianbei Mountain, and from it took its name.

entries.zh: 其後，世為君長，統幽都之北，廣漠之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木紀契而已，世事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。
entries.en: Afterward they ruled generation upon generation north of Youdu, across the wide steppe. They lived by herding, moving with the seasons, and by the hunt; their ways were plain, their customs unadorned. They had no script—only notches cut in wood to seal bargains. What happened near and far was handed down mouth to mouth, much as if scribes had kept annals.
entries.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they were chieftains, ruling north of Youdu in the vast deserts. Pastoral migration and hunting were their livelihood; simplicity their custom, plainness their transformation. They did not use writing, but only carved wood to record agreements. Affairs near and far were passed from person to person, like the records of historians.

entries.zh: 黃帝以土德王，北俗謂土為托，謂后為跋，故以為氏。
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor reigned under the virtue of Earth; northerners called earth tuo and called a queen ba—so the clan took the name Tuoba.
entries.literal: The Yellow Emperor ruled by the virtue of Earth; in northern custom earth was called tuo and a queen was called ba, hence they took it as their clan name.

entries.zh: 其裔始均，入仕堯世，逐女魃於弱水之北，民賴其勤，帝舜嘉之，命為田祖。
entries.en: A descendant, Shijun, served in the reign of Yao, driving the drought demon Nüba beyond the Weak Water. The people owed their relief to his labor; Shun commended him and named him Lord of the Fields.
entries.literal: His descendant Shijun entered service in the age of Yao, drove Nüba north of the Weak Water; the people relied on his diligence, Emperor Shun praised him, and appointed him Lord of the Fields.

entries.zh: 爰歷三代，以及秦漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代殘暴，作害中州，而始均之裔，不交南夏，是以載籍無聞焉。
entries.en: Through the Three Dynasties and on into Qin and Han, the Xiongnu and their kindred peoples—Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong—ravaged the Central Plains generation after generation. Yet Shijun's line never dealt with the southern realms, and so the written histories say nothing of them.
entries.literal: Thus through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu and their kind were generation after generation violent, harming the Central States—but the descendants of Shijun did not mingle with Southern Xia, and therefore they go unmentioned in written records.

entries.zh: 皇興元年春正月癸巳，尉元大破張永、沈攸之於呂梁東，斬首數萬級，凍死者甚眾。
entries.en: In the first month of spring of the first year of Huangxing, on the guisi day, Wei Yuan greatly defeated Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi east of Lüliang; heads taken numbered in the tens of thousands, and very many died of cold.
entries.literal: First year of Huangxing, spring, first month, day guisi: Wei Yuan greatly defeated Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi east of Lüliang; heads taken numbered in the tens of thousands; those who died of cold were very many.

entries.zh: 獲劉彧秦州刺史垣恭祖、羽林監沈承伯。
entries.en: Yuan Gongzu, Liu Yu's inspector of Qinzhou, and Shen Chengbo, Feathered Forest supervisor, were captured.
entries.literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Qinzhou Yuan Gongzu and Feathered Forest Supervisor Shen Chengbo were captured.

entries.zh: 永、攸之單騎走免。
entries.en: Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi fled alone on horseback and escaped.
entries.literal: Yong and Youzhi alone on horseback fled and escaped.

entries.zh: 獲軍資器械不可勝數。
entries.en: Military stores and weapons captured were beyond counting.
entries.literal: Military stores and weapons captured were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 劉彧遣使朝貢。
entries.en: Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 庚子，東平王道符謀反於長安，殺副將、駙馬都尉萬古真，鉅鹿公李恢，雍州刺史魚玄明。
entries.en: On the gengzi day Prince of Dongping Daofu plotted rebellion at Chang'an, killing the deputy commander Wangu Zhen, Commandant of the Majestic Steeds, Li Hui, Duke of Julu, and Yu Xuanming, inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Day gengzi: Prince of Dongping Daofu plotted rebellion at Chang'an, killed the deputy commander, Commandant of the Majestic Steeds Wangu Zhen, Duke of Julu Li Hui, and Inspector of Yongzhou Yu Xuanming.

entries.zh: 丙午，詔司空、平昌公和其奴，東陽公元丕等討道符。
entries.en: On the bingwu day an edict ordered He Qinu, Minister of Works and Duke of Pingchang, Yuan Pi, Prince of Dongyang, and others to campaign against Daofu.
entries.literal: Day bingwu: an edict that Minister of Works, Duke of Pingchang He Qinu, Prince of Dongyang Yuan Pi, and others were to campaign against Daofu.

entries.zh: 丁未，道符司馬段太陽攻道符，斬之，傳首京師。
entries.en: On the dingwei day Daofu's major Duan Taiyang attacked him, beheaded him, and sent the head to the capital.
entries.literal: Day dingwei: Daofu's Major Duan Taiyang attacked Daofu, beheaded him, and sent the head to the capital.

entries.zh: 道符兄弟皆伏誅。
entries.en: Daofu's brothers were all executed.
entries.literal: Daofu's brothers were all executed.

entries.zh: 閏月，以頓丘王李峻為太宰。
entries.en: In the intercalary month Li Jun, Prince of Dunqiu, was made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Intercalary month: Prince of Dunqiu Li Jun was made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 劉彧青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固並遣使請舉州內屬，詔平東將軍長孫陵，平南將軍、廣陵公侯窮奇赴援之。
