entries.en: Shen Wenxiu, Liu Yu's inspector of Qingzhou, and Cui Daogu, inspector of Jizhou, each sent envoys asking to submit their provinces inward; an edict ordered Changsun Ling, General Who Pacifies the East, and Hou Qiongqi, General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Guangling, to go to their aid.
entries.literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Qingzhou Shen Wenxiu and Inspector of Jizhou Cui Daogu each sent envoys asking to submit their provinces inward; an edict that General Who Pacifies the East Changsun Ling and General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Guangling Hou Qiongqi, were to go to their aid.

entries.zh: 二月，詔使持節、都督諸軍事、征南大將軍慕容白曜督騎五萬次於碻磝，為東道後援。
entries.en: In the second month an edict ordered Murong Baiyao, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs, and General Who Campaigns South, with fifty thousand cavalry, to encamp at Que'ao as reserve for the eastern route.
entries.literal: Second month: an edict that Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, General Who Campaigns South Murong Baiyao, with fifty thousand cavalry, was to encamp at Que'ao as eastern-route reserve.

entries.zh: 濟陰王小新成薨。
entries.en: Prince of Jiyin Xiaoxincheng died.
entries.literal: Prince of Jiyin Xiaoxincheng died.

entries.zh: 高麗、庫莫奚、具伏弗、郁羽陵、日連、匹黎尒、于闐諸國各遣使朝貢。
entries.en: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Khotan, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Khotan, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 劉彧東平太守申纂戍無鹽，遏絕王使，詔征南大將軍慕容白曜督諸軍以討之。
entries.en: Shen Zuan, Liu Yu's administrator of Dongping, garrisoned Wuyan, blocked the king's envoys, and cut off communications; an edict ordered Murong Baiyao, General Who Campaigns South, to command the armies against him.
entries.literal: Liu Yu's Administrator of Dongping Shen Zuan garrisoned Wuyan, blocked and cut off the king's envoys; an edict that General Who Campaigns South Murong Baiyao was to command the armies to attack him.

entries.zh: 三月甲寅，克之。
entries.en: In the third month, on the jiayin day, it was taken.
entries.literal: Third month, day jiayin: it was taken.

entries.zh: 沈文秀、崔道固復叛歸劉彧，白曜回師討之，拔彧肥城、垣苗、麋溝三戍。
entries.en: Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu again rebelled and returned to Liu Yu; Baiyao turned his army against them and took three of Liu Yu's garrisons—Feicheng, Yuanmiao, and Migou.
entries.literal: Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu again rebelled and returned to Liu Yu; Baiyao turned his army to campaign against them and took three of Liu Yu's garrisons—Feicheng, Yuanmiao, and Migou.

entries.zh: 夏四月辛丑，以南郡公李惠為征南大將軍、儀同三司、都督關右諸軍事、雍州刺史，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the xinchou day, Li Hui, Duke of Nanjun, was made General Who Campaigns South with equipage equal to the Three Directors, commander-in-chief of the military affairs of the passes west and inspector of Yongzhou, and advanced in rank to prince.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinchou: Duke of Nanjun Li Hui was made General Who Campaigns South, with Equipage Equal to the Three Directors, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the Passes West, and Inspector of Yongzhou; he was advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 高麗、庫莫奚、契丹，具伏弗、郁羽陵、日連、匹黎尒、叱六手、悉萬丹、阿大何、羽真侯、于闐、波斯國各遣使朝獻。
entries.en: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Chiliushou, Ximandan, A'dahe, Yuzhenhou, Khotan, Persia, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Chiliushou, Ximandan, A'dahe, Yuzhenhou, Khotan, Persia, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: [2]五月乙卯，田于崞山，遂幸繁畤。
entries.en: [2] In the fifth month, on the yimao day, a hunt was held on Mount Guo; then the court visited Fanchi.
entries.literal: [2] Fifth month, day yimao: a hunt was held on Mount Guo; then the court visited Fanchi.

entries.zh: 辛酉，還宮。
entries.en: On the xinyou day the court returned to the palace.
entries.literal: Day xinyou: returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 六月庚辰，以河南闢地，曲赦京師殊死以下。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on the gengchen day, because Henan had opened new lands, a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital for offenses below capital punishment.
entries.literal: Sixth month, day gengchen: because Henan had opened new lands, a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital for offenses below capital punishment.

entries.zh: 以昌黎王馮熙為太傅。
entries.en: Feng Xi, Prince of Changli, was made Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Prince of Changli Feng Xi was made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 顯祖獻文皇帝，諱弘，高宗文成皇帝之長子也，母曰李貴人。
entries.en: Xianzu, Emperor Xianwen, bore the taboo name Hong. He was the eldest son of Gaozong, Emperor Wencheng; his mother was Lady Li, Honored Person.
entries.literal: Xianzu, Emperor Xianwen, bore the taboo name Hong; he was Gaozong, Emperor Wencheng's eldest son; his mother was Lady Li, Honored Person.

entries.zh: 興光元年秋七月，生於陰山之北。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn of the first year of Xingguang he was born north of Yinshan.
entries.literal: First year of Xingguang, autumn, seventh month: he was born north of Yinshan.

entries.zh: 太安二年二月，立為皇太子。
entries.en: In the second month of the second year of Tai'an he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: Second year of Tai'an, second month: he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 聰叡機悟，幼而有濟民神武之規，仁孝純至，禮敬師友。
entries.en: Clever, perceptive, and quick of wit, even as a boy he showed a mind to succor the people with divine martial prowess. Pure in benevolence and filial piety, he honored teachers and friends with ritual courtesy.
entries.literal: Clever, perceptive, and quick of wit, in youth he already had a design to succor the people with divine martial prowess; pure in benevolence and filial piety, he honored teachers and friends with ritual courtesy.

entries.zh: 和平六年夏五月甲辰，即皇帝位，大赦天下。
entries.en: In the fifth month of summer of the sixth year of Heping, on the jiachen day, he took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Sixth year of Heping, summer, fifth month, day jiachen: he assumed the imperial throne; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 尊皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: The empress was honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: The empress was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 車騎大將軍乙渾矯詔殺尚書楊保年、平陽公賈愛仁、南陽公張天度于禁中。
entries.en: Yi Hun, General of Chariots and Cavalry, forged an edict and killed Yang Baonian, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Jia Airen, Duke of Pingyang, and Zhang Tiandu, Duke of Nanyang, within the inner palace.
entries.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yi Hun forged an edict and killed Minister of the Masters of Writing Yang Baonian, Duke of Pingyang Jia Airen, and Duke of Nanyang Zhang Tiandu within the inner palace.

entries.zh: 戊申，侍中、司徒、平原王陸麗自湯泉入朝，渾又殺之。
entries.en: On the wushen day Lu Li, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Masses, and Prince of Pingyuan, came to court from Tangquan; Yi Hun killed him as well.
entries.literal: Day wushen: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Masses, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li entered court from Tangquan; Hun killed him as well.

entries.zh: 己酉，以侍中、車騎大將軍乙渾為太尉、錄尚書事，東安王劉尼為司徒，尚書左僕射和其奴為司空。
entries.en: On the jiyou day Yi Hun, Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry, was made Grand Commandant and Recorder of Secretariat Affairs; Liu Ni, Prince of Dong'an, was made Minister of the Masses; and He Qinu, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Day jiyou: Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry Yi Hun was made Grand Commandant and Recorder of Secretariat Affairs; Prince of Dong'an Liu Ni was made Minister of the Masses; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Qinu was made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 壬子，以淮南王他為鎮西大將軍、儀同三司，鎮涼州。
entries.en: On the renzi day Prince of Huainan Ta was made Grand General Who Guards the West with equipage equal to the Three Directors and posted to garrison Liangzhou.
entries.literal: Day renzi: Prince of Huainan Ta was made Grand General Who Guards the West, with Equipage Equal to the Three Directors, and garrisoned Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 六月，封繁陽侯李嶷為丹陽王，征東大將軍馮熙為昌黎王。
entries.en: In the sixth month Li Ni, Marquis of Fanyang, was enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang, and Feng Xi, General Who Conquers the East, as Prince of Changli.
entries.literal: Sixth month: Marquis of Fanyang Li Ni was enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang; General Who Conquers the East Feng Xi was enfeoffed as Prince of Changli.

entries.zh: 乙丑，詔曰：「夫賦斂煩則民財匱，課調輕則用不足，是以十一而稅，頌聲作矣。
entries.en: On the yichou day an edict stated, "When levies and collections are burdensome the people's wealth is exhausted; when assessments are too light the treasury falls short—hence the one-tenth tax, and songs of praise arose.
entries.literal: Day yichou: an edict stated: "When levies and collections are burdensome the people's wealth is exhausted; when assessments and imposts are light expenditures are insufficient—hence the one-tenth tax, and songs of praise arose.

entries.zh: 先朝榷其輕重，以惠百姓。
entries.en: The former court weighed their burden to benefit the common people.
entries.literal: The former court weighed their lightness and heaviness to benefit the hundred surnames.

entries.zh: 朕承洪業，上惟祖宗之休命，夙興待旦，惟民之恤，欲令天下同於逸豫。
entries.en: We inherit the great enterprise and look up to the ancestors' mandate of blessing. Rising early and awaiting dawn, we think only of the people's hardship, wishing to make all under Heaven share in ease and delight.
entries.literal: We inherit the great enterprise, looking up to the ancestors' mandate of blessing; rising early and awaiting dawn, we think only of the people's hardship, wishing to make all under Heaven share in ease and delight.

entries.zh: 而徭賦不息，將何以塞煩去苛，拯濟黎元者哉！
entries.en: Yet corvée and levies do not cease—how shall we block excess, remove harshness, and rescue the common people!
entries.literal: Yet corvée and levies do not cease—how shall we block excess, remove harshness, and rescue the black-haired masses!

entries.zh: 今兵革不起，畜積有餘，諸有雜調，一以與民。」
entries.en: Now arms are not raised and stores are abundant; all miscellaneous levies are hereby remitted to the people."
entries.literal: Now arms are not raised and stores are abundant; all miscellaneous levies are hereby remitted to the people."

entries.zh: 二年春正月丁亥，詔曰：「朕以沖眇，纂承寶位，夙夜惟寅，若涉淵海。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the second year, on the dinghai day, an edict said, "We, young and slight, have succeeded to the precious throne; morning and evening we are reverent, as if crossing a deep sea.
entries.literal: First month of spring in the second year, day dinghai: an edict said, "We, young and slight, have succeeded to the precious throne; morning and evening we are reverent, as if crossing a deep sea.

entries.zh: 賴皇太后慈仁，被以夙訓。
entries.en: We rely on the empress dowager's compassionate benevolence, covered with early instruction.
entries.literal: We rely on the empress dowager's compassionate benevolence, covered with early instruction.

entries.zh: 自臨朝踐極，歲將半紀，天平地成，四海寧乂。
entries.en: Since holding court and treading the pinnacle, nearly half a reign has passed; heaven is level and earth at peace; within the four seas there is quiet.
entries.literal: Since holding court and treading the pinnacle, nearly half a reign has passed; heaven is level and earth at peace; within the four seas there is quiet.

entries.zh: 天道高遠，巍巍難名，猶以撝挹自居，稱號弗備，非所以崇奉坤元，允協億兆者也。
entries.en: The Way of Heaven is high and far, lofty and hard to name; yet we still restrain ourselves and hold back, our title not complete—not what is meant by honoring and serving Earth's origin and harmonizing with the hundred millions.
entries.literal: The Way of Heaven is high and far, lofty and hard to name; yet we still restrain ourselves and hold back, our title not complete—not what is meant by honoring and serving Earth's origin and harmonizing with the hundred millions.

entries.zh: 宜遵舊典，稱詔宇內，以副黎蒸元元之望。」
entries.en: We should follow the old canon and proclaim our title throughout the realm, to answer the hope of the black-haired masses."
entries.literal: We should follow the old canon and proclaim our title throughout the realm, to answer the hope of the black-haired masses."

entries.zh: 是月，改葬文昭皇太后高氏。
entries.en: That month Empress Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.
entries.literal: That month Empress Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.

entries.zh: 二月乙丑，齊郡王祐薨。
entries.en: In the second month, on the yichou day, You, Prince of Qi commandery, died.
entries.literal: Second month, day yichou: Prince of Qi Commandery You died.

entries.zh: 庚午，羽林千餘人焚征西將軍張彝第，毆傷彝，燒殺其子始均。
entries.en: On the gengwu day more than a thousand guardsmen burned the residence of Zhang Yi, general who campaigns west, beat Yi, and burned and killed his son Shi Jun.
entries.literal: Day gengwu: more than a thousand guardsmen burned the residence of General Who Campaigns West Zhang Yi, beat Yi, and burned and killed his son Shi Jun.

entries.zh: 吐谷渾、宕昌國並遣使朝貢。
entries.en: Tuyuhun and Dangchang both sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: Tuyuhun and Dangchang both sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 乙亥，大赦天下。
entries.en: On the yihai day a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Day yihai: a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 丁丑，詔求直言，諸有上書者聽密封通奏。
entries.en: On the dingchou day an edict sought forthright speech; those who submitted memorials were permitted to seal them and have them forwarded.
entries.literal: Day dingchou: an edict sought forthright speech; those who submitted memorials were permitted to seal them and have them forwarded.

entries.zh: 壬寅，詔曰：「農要之月，時澤弗應，嘉穀未納，三麥枯悴。
entries.en: On the renyin day an edict said, "In the crucial month of farming the seasonal rains have not responded; the good grain is not yet gathered; the three wheats wither.
entries.literal: Day renyin: an edict said, "In the crucial month of farming the seasonal rains have not responded; the good grain is not yet gathered; the three wheats wither.

entries.zh: 德之無感，歎懼兼懷。
entries.en: That virtue has no effect fills us with sighs and fear together.
entries.literal: That virtue has no effect fills us with sighs and fear together.

entries.zh: 可敕內外，依舊雩祈，率從祀典。
entries.en: Let inner and outer offices follow the old rain-prayer and lead the sacrificial canon.
entries.literal: Let inner and outer offices follow the old rain-prayer and lead the sacrificial canon.

entries.zh: 察獄理冤，掩胔埋骼。
entries.en: Examine prisons and right wrongs; cover exposed corpses and bury bones.
entries.literal: Examine prisons and right wrongs; cover exposed corpses and bury bones.

entries.zh: 冀瀛之境，往經寇暴，死者既多，白骨橫道，可遣專令收葬。
entries.en: In the Ji and Ying regions, which formerly suffered raids, the dead were many and white bones lay across the roads—special commissioners may be sent to gather and bury them.
entries.literal: In the Ji and Ying regions, which formerly suffered raids, the dead were many and white bones lay across the roads—special commissioners may be sent to gather and bury them.

entries.zh: 賑窮恤寡，救疾存老，準訪前式，務令周備。」
entries.en: Relieve the poor and comfort the widowed; heal the sick and preserve the aged; consult former models and see that all is thoroughly done."
entries.literal: Relieve the poor and comfort the widowed; heal the sick and preserve the aged; consult former models and see that all is thoroughly done."

entries.zh: 三月甲辰，澍雨大洽。
entries.en: In the third month, on the jiachen day, soaking rain fell abundantly.
entries.literal: Third month, day jiachen: soaking rain fell abundantly.

entries.zh: 肅宗孝明皇帝，諱詡，世宗宣武皇帝之第二子，母曰胡充華。
entries.en: Suzong, Emperor Xiaoming, bore the taboo name Xu. He was Shizong, Emperor Xuanwu's second son; his mother was Hu Chuhua.
entries.literal: Suzong, Emperor Xiaoming, bore the taboo name Xu; he was Shizong, Emperor Xuanwu's second son; his mother was Hu Chuhua.

entries.zh: 永平三年三月丙戌，帝生于宣光殿之東北，有光照于庭中。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongping, in the third month, on the bingxu day, the emperor was born northeast of the Xuanguang Hall; light shone in the courtyard.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongping, third month, day bingxu, the Emperor was born northeast of the Xuanguang Hall; light shone in the courtyard.

entries.zh: 延昌元年十月乙亥，立為皇太子。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the first year of Yanchang, on the yihai day, he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yanchang, day yihai, he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 從容雅服不得以矛釤從事 北史卷五「矛釤」作「務衫」。
entries.en: Easy and elegant dress may not be used for spear and halberd affairs Northern History volume 5 reads "spear and halberd" as "service shirt."
entries.literal: Easy and elegant dress may not be used to engage in spear and halberd affairs Northern History, volume 5, reads "spear and halberd" as "service shirt."

entries.zh: 張森楷云：「一作『絳衫』。」
entries.en: Zhang Senkai says: "Another reading is crimson shirt."
entries.literal: Zhang Senkai says: "Another reading is crimson shirt."

entries.zh: 按「釤」是刀名，作「矛釤」也可通。
entries.en: Comment: "halberd" is a blade name; "spear and halberd" can also make sense.
entries.literal: Comment: "halberd" is a blade name; "spear and halberd" can also make sense.

entries.zh: 「務衫」不可考。
entries.en: "Service shirt" cannot be verified.
entries.literal: "Service shirt" cannot be verified.

entries.zh: 絳衫是戎服，南齊書卷四七王融傳說他「戎服絳衫」，同書卷七一崔慧景附崔恭祖傳有「禿馬絳衫，手刺倒賊」之文。
entries.en: Crimson shirt is military dress; Southern Qi Shu volume 47, Wang Rong's biography, says he "wore military dress, crimson shirt," and volume 71, Cui Huizong with Cui Gongzu attached, has "bare horse, crimson shirt, hand stabbed the fallen bandit."
entries.literal: Crimson shirt is military dress; the Southern Qi Shu, volume 47, biography of Wang Rong, says he "wore military dress, crimson shirt," and the same book, volume 71, biography of Cui Huizong with attached biography of Cui Gongzu, has "bare horse, crimson shirt, hand stabbed the fallen bandit."

entries.zh: 上云「從容雅服」，下自當說不得戎服，作「絳衫」似較長。
entries.en: Above it says "easy and elegant dress"; below it should forbid military dress—"crimson shirt" seems preferable.
entries.literal: Above it says "easy and elegant dress"; below it should speak of not being allowed military dress—"crimson shirt" seems preferable.

entries.zh: 但不知張所云「一作」是哪一個本子，今仍之。
entries.en: But it is unknown which edition Zhang's "another reading" refers to; the received text is retained.
entries.literal: But it is unknown which edition Zhang's "another reading" refers to; the received text is retained.

entries.zh: 孝靜皇帝，諱善見，清河文宣王亶之世子也，母曰胡妃。
entries.en: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian. He was heir to Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Lady Hu.
entries.literal: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian; he was the heir of Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Consort Hu.

entries.zh: 永熙三年，拜通直散騎侍郎，八月，為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongxi he became direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry with an opening office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander.

entries.zh: 出帝既入關，齊獻武王奉迎不克，乃與百僚會議，推帝以奉肅宗之後，時年十一。
entries.en: After the western-departing emperor entered the passes, Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi tried to welcome him back and failed. He then convened the ministers and enthroned the boy to carry on the line of Emperor Suzong—eleven years old.
entries.literal: When the emperor who had gone west had entered the passes, Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi went to welcome him but could not succeed; he then met with the hundred officials in council and set up the emperor to continue the line after Emperor Suzong—he was eleven years old.

entries.zh: 明元皇帝七男。
entries.en: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons.

entries.zh: 杜密皇后生世祖太武皇帝。
entries.en: Empress Mi of the Du clan bore Shizu Emperor Taiwu.
entries.literal: Empress Mi of the Du clan gave birth to Shizu Emperor Taiwu.

entries.zh: 大慕容夫人生樂平戾王丕。
entries.en: Lady Da Murong bore Prince Pi of Leping, who received the posthumous title Ill-Fated King.
entries.literal: Lady Da Murong gave birth to Prince Pi of Leping, posthumously styled the Ill-Fated King.

entries.zh: 安定殤王彌闕母氏。
entries.en: Prince Mi of Anding, posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King, is of unknown maternity.
entries.literal: Prince Mi of Anding, posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King — his mother's name is not recorded.

entries.zh: 慕容夫人生樂安宣王範。
entries.en: Lady Murong bore Prince Fan of Le'an, who received the posthumous title Proclaiming King.
entries.literal: Lady Murong gave birth to Prince Fan of Le'an, posthumously styled the Proclaiming King.

entries.zh: 尹夫人生永昌莊王健。
entries.en: Lady Yin bore Prince Jian of Yongchang, who received the posthumous title Magnificent King.
entries.literal: Lady Yin gave birth to Prince Jian of Yongchang, posthumously styled the Magnificent King.

entries.zh: 建寧王崇、新興王俊二王，並闕母氏。
entries.en: The Princes Chong of Jianning and Jun of Xinxing both have unrecorded mothers.
entries.literal: The two princes, Chong of Jianning and Jun of Xinxing, both lack recorded mothers.

entries.zh: 樂平王丕，少有才幹，為世所稱。
entries.en: Pi, Prince of Leping, had talent and ability from youth and was praised by his generation.
entries.literal: Pi, Prince of Leping, had talent and ability from youth and was praised by his generation.

entries.zh: 太宗以丕長，愛其器度，特優異之。
entries.en: Because Pi was the eldest, Taizong admired his bearing and treated him with special favor.
entries.literal: Because Pi was the eldest, Taizong admired his bearing and treated him with special favor.

entries.zh: 泰常七年封，拜車騎大將軍。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Taichang he was enfeoffed and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang he was enfeoffed and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 後督河西、高平諸軍討南秦王楊難當，軍至略陽，禁令齊肅，所過無私，百姓爭致牛酒。
entries.en: Later he commanded the armies of Hexi and Gaoping against Yang Nandang, Prince of Southern Qin. When the army reached Lueyang, discipline was strict and orderly; wherever it passed there was no private plunder, and the people competed to bring cattle and wine.
entries.literal: Later he commanded the armies of Hexi and Gaoping against Yang Nandang, Prince of Southern Qin. When the army reached Lueyang, discipline was strict and orderly; wherever it passed there was no private plunder, and the people competed to bring cattle and wine.

entries.zh: 難當懼，還仇池。
entries.en: Nandang was afraid and returned to Chouchi.
entries.literal: Nandang was afraid and returned to Chouchi.

entries.zh: 而諸將議曰，若不誅豪帥，軍還之後，必聚而為寇。
entries.en: The generals argued, "If we do not execute the powerful leaders, then after the army returns they will surely gather and become bandits."
entries.literal: The generals argued, "If we do not execute the powerful leaders, then after the army returns they will surely gather and become bandits."

entries.zh: 又以大眾遠出，不有所掠，則無以充軍實，賞將士。
entries.en: They also reasoned that since the great army had come far, if nothing were seized there would be no way to fill the army stores and reward the soldiers.
entries.literal: They also reasoned that since the great army had come far, if nothing were seized there would be no way to fill the army stores and reward the soldiers.

entries.zh: 將從之。
entries.en: Pi was about to follow this advice.
entries.literal: Pi was about to follow this advice.

entries.zh: 時中書侍郎高允參丕軍事，諫曰：「今若誅之，是傷其向化之心，恐大軍一還，為亂必速。」
entries.en: At the time Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun was participating in Pi's military affairs. He remonstrated, "If we execute them now, this will wound their will to submit to transformation. I fear that once the great army returns, rebellion will come quickly."
entries.literal: At the time Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun was participating in Pi's military affairs. He remonstrated, "If we execute them now, this will wound their will to submit to transformation. I fear that once the great army returns, rebellion will come quickly."

entries.zh: 丕以為然，於是綏懷初附，秋毫無犯。
entries.en: Pi considered this right, and so he soothed and embraced those newly attached, without violating so much as an autumn hair.
entries.literal: Pi considered this right, and so he soothed and embraced those newly attached, without violating so much as an autumn hair.

entries.zh: 初，馮弘之奔高麗，世祖詔遣送之，高麗不遣，世祖怒，將討之。
entries.en: Earlier, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, Shizu ordered that he be sent back. Goguryeo did not send him, and Shizu was angry and intended to attack.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, Shizu ordered that he be sent back. Goguryeo did not send him, and Shizu was angry and intended to attack.

entries.zh: 丕上疏，以為和龍新定，宜優復之，使廣修農殖，以饒軍實，然後進圖，可一舉而滅。
entries.en: Pi submitted a memorial arguing that Helong had only recently been pacified and should be generously relieved so that farming and planting could be widely restored and military supplies made abundant; only afterward should plans advance, when Goguryeo could be destroyed in one stroke.
entries.literal: Pi submitted a memorial arguing that Helong had only recently been pacified and should be generously relieved so that farming and planting could be widely restored and military supplies made abundant; only afterward should plans advance, when Goguryeo could be destroyed in one stroke.

entries.zh: 帝納之，乃止。
entries.en: The emperor accepted this and stopped.
entries.literal: The emperor accepted this and stopped.

entries.zh: 後坐劉潔事，以憂薨。
entries.en: Later, implicated in Liu Jie's affair, Pi died of anxiety.
entries.literal: Later, implicated in Liu Jie's affair, Pi died of anxiety.

entries.zh: 事在
entries.en: The affair is recorded
entries.literal: The affair is recorded

entries.zh: 〈潔傳〉。
entries.en: in Jie's biography.
entries.literal: in Jie's biography.

entries.zh: 諡曰戾王。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Prince Li.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Prince Li.

entries.zh: 樂安王範，泰常七年封。
entries.en: Fan, Prince of Le'an, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.
entries.literal: Fan, Prince of Le'an, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

entries.zh: 雅性沉厚，寬和仁恕。
entries.en: His natural character was deep and generous, broad, mild, humane, and forgiving.
entries.literal: His natural character was deep and generous, broad, mild, humane, and forgiving.

entries.zh: 世祖以長安形勝之地，非範莫可任者，乃拜範都督五州諸軍事、衞大將軍、開府儀同三司、長安鎮都大將，高選才能，以為僚佐。
entries.en: Shizu considered Chang'an a strategically commanding place and believed no one but Fan could be entrusted with it. He therefore appointed Fan commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General of the Guards, with an opened office and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and grand general of Chang'an Garrison, selecting able men of high quality to serve as his staff.
entries.literal: Shizu considered Chang'an a strategically commanding place and believed no one but Fan could be entrusted with it. He therefore appointed Fan commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General of the Guards, with an opened office and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and grand general of Chang'an Garrison, selecting able men of high quality to serve as his staff.

entries.zh: 範謙恭惠下，推心撫納，百姓稱之。
entries.en: Fan was modest and respectful, kind to those below him, and received and soothed people with open sincerity; the common people praised him.
entries.literal: Fan was modest and respectful, kind to those below him, and received and soothed people with open sincerity; the common people praised him.

entries.zh: 時秦土新罹寇賊，流亡者相繼，範請崇易簡之治，帝納之。
entries.en: At the time the Qin lands had newly suffered bandits and rebels, and refugees followed one after another. Fan requested that rule there honor ease and simplicity, and the emperor accepted it.
entries.literal: At the time the Qin lands had newly suffered bandits and rebels, and refugees followed one after another. Fan requested that rule there honor ease and simplicity, and the emperor accepted it.

entries.zh: 於是遂寬徭，與人休息。
entries.en: Thereupon corvée was relaxed, and the people were allowed to rest.
entries.literal: Thereupon corvée was relaxed, and the people were allowed to rest.

entries.zh: 後劉潔之謀，範聞而不告。
entries.en: Later, when Liu Jie plotted, Fan heard of it but did not report it.
entries.literal: Later, when Liu Jie plotted, Fan heard of it but did not report it.

entries.zh: 事發，因疾暴薨。
entries.en: When the affair came to light, he suddenly died from illness.
entries.literal: When the affair came to light, he suddenly died from illness.

entries.zh: 長子良。
entries.en: His eldest son was Liang.
entries.literal: His eldest son was Liang.

entries.zh: 世祖未有子，嘗曰：「兄弟之子猶子也。」
entries.en: Shizu had not yet fathered a son and once said, "A brother's son is as good as one's own."
entries.literal: Shizu had no son yet and once said: "A brother's son is like one's own son."

entries.zh: 親撫養之。
entries.en: He raised Liang himself with fatherly care.
entries.literal: He personally reared and nurtured him.

entries.zh: 長而壯勇多知，常參軍國大計。
entries.en: When he came of age he was strong, courageous, and well informed, and he regularly joined in deliberations on matters of state and war.
entries.literal: When grown, he was bold, brave, and deeply informed, and he regularly took part in great plans of state and army.

entries.zh: 高宗時，襲王。
entries.en: Under Emperor Gaozong he inherited the princedom.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, he inherited the princedom.

entries.zh: 拜長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史，為內都大官。
entries.en: He was appointed Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison, Inspector of Yong Province, and Director of the Inner Capital.
entries.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Capital Garrison of Chang'an and Inspector of Yong Province, and served as Director of the Inner Capital.

entries.zh: 薨，諡曰簡王。
entries.en: He died and was given the posthumous title Simple King.
entries.literal: He died and was posthumously styled the Simple King.

entries.zh: 永昌王健，泰常七年封。
entries.en: Jian, Prince of Yongchang, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.
entries.literal: Jian, Prince of Yongchang, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

entries.zh: 健姿貌魁壯，善弓馬，達兵法，所在征戰，常有大功。
entries.en: Jian was imposing and robust in appearance, skilled with bow and horse, and expert in military methods; wherever he campaigned, he regularly won great merit.
entries.literal: Jian was imposing and robust in appearance, skilled with bow and horse, and expert in military methods; wherever he campaigned, he regularly won great merit.

entries.zh: 才藝比陳留桓王，而智略過之。
entries.en: In talent and skill he was comparable to Prince Huan of Chenliu, while in wisdom and strategy he surpassed him.
entries.literal: In talent and skill he was comparable to Prince Huan of Chenliu, while in wisdom and strategy he surpassed him.

entries.zh: 從世祖破赫連昌，遂西略至木根山。
entries.en: He followed Shizu in defeating Helian Chang and then campaigned west as far as Mugen Mountain.
entries.literal: He followed Shizu in defeating Helian Chang and then campaigned west as far as Mugen Mountain.

entries.zh: 討和龍，健別攻拔建德。
entries.en: During the campaign against Helong, Jian separately attacked and took Jiande.
entries.literal: During the campaign against Helong, Jian separately attacked and took Jiande.

entries.zh: 後平叛胡白龍餘黨于西河。
entries.en: Later he pacified the remaining followers of the rebel Hu Bailong in Xihe.
entries.literal: Later he pacified the remaining followers of the rebel Hu Bailong in Xihe.

entries.zh: 世祖襲蠕蠕，越涿邪山。
entries.en: When Shizu made a surprise attack on the Rouran, he crossed Zhuoxie Mountain.
entries.literal: When Shizu made a surprise attack on the Rouran, he crossed Zhuoxie Mountain.

entries.zh: 車駕還，詔健殿後，蠕蠕萬騎追之，健與數十騎擊之，矢不虛發，所中皆應弦而斃，遂退。
entries.en: As the imperial carriage returned, an edict ordered Jian to guard the rear. Ten thousand Rouran cavalry pursued, and Jian struck them with several dozen riders. Not one arrow was loosed in vain; whoever he hit fell dead at the string, and the pursuers withdrew.
entries.literal: As the imperial carriage returned, an edict ordered Jian to guard the rear. Ten thousand Rouran cavalry pursued, and Jian struck them with several dozen riders. Not one arrow was loosed in vain; whoever he hit fell dead at the string, and the pursuers withdrew.

entries.zh: 威震漠北。
entries.en: His awe shook the north of the desert.
entries.literal: His awe shook the north of the desert.

entries.zh: 尋從平涼州，健功居多。
entries.en: Soon afterward he followed in pacifying Liangzhou, and Jian's merit was the greatest.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he followed in pacifying Liangzhou, and Jian's merit was the greatest.

entries.zh: 又討破禿髮保周，自殺，傳首京師；
entries.en: He also attacked and defeated Tufa Baozhou, who killed himself, and Jian sent his head to the capital;
entries.literal: He also attacked and defeated Tufa Baozhou, who killed himself, and Jian sent his head to the capital;

entries.zh: 復降沮渠無諱。
entries.en: he then brought Juqu Wuhui to surrender.
entries.literal: he then brought Juqu Wuhui to surrender.

entries.zh: 無疾薨，諡曰莊王。
entries.en: He died without illness and received the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.
entries.literal: He died without illness and received the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.

entries.zh: 子仁，襲。
entries.en: His son Ren inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Ren succeeded.

entries.zh: 仁亦驍勇，有父風，世祖奇之。
entries.en: Ren was likewise fierce and brave, with his father's bearing, and Shizu took special notice of him.
entries.literal: Ren was also fierce and valiant, having his father's manner; Shizu regarded him with wonder.

entries.zh: 後與濮陽王閭若文謀為不軌，發覺，賜死，國除。
entries.en: Later he conspired in treason with Lü Ruowen, Prince of Puyang; when the plot was uncovered he was ordered to take his own life, and the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Later he plotted treason with Prince Ruowen of Puyang, Lü Ruowen; when discovered, he was ordered to commit suicide, and the fief was extinguished.

entries.zh: 論曰：樂平、樂安俱以將領自效，竟以憂迫而逝，驗克終之為鮮。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Leping and Le'an both proved themselves as commanders, yet in the end died under anxiety and pressure, showing how rare it is to come to a good end.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Leping and Le'an both proved themselves as commanders, yet in the end died under anxiety and pressure, showing how rare it is to come to a good end.

entries.zh: 莊王才力智謀，一時之傑，與夫建寧、新興，不同日也。
entries.en: Prince Zhuang, in talent, strength, wisdom, and strategy, was an outstanding man of his age; he cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Jianning and Xinxing.
entries.literal: Prince Zhuang, in talent, strength, wisdom, and strategy, was an outstanding man of his age; he cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Jianning and Xinxing.

entries.zh: 任城王雲，年五歲，恭宗崩，號哭不絕聲。
entries.en: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was only five when Gongzong died, yet he wailed without stopping.
entries.literal: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was five years old when Gongzong died, and he wailed without cease.

entries.zh: 世祖聞之而呼，抱之泣曰：「汝何知而有成人之意也！」
entries.en: Shizu heard and called for him, took him in his arms, and wept. "How is it that you already have a grown man's heart?"
entries.literal: Shizu heard of this, summoned him, embraced him, and wept, saying, "What do you know, to have the mind of a grown man?"

entries.zh: 和平五年封，拜使持節、侍中、征東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將。
entries.en: In Heping year 5 he received his fief and was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and commander of Helong Garrison.
entries.literal: In Heping year 5 he was enfeoffed and appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and grand commander of Helong Garrison.

entries.zh: 顯祖時，拜都督中外諸軍事、中都坐大官，聽理民訟，甚收時譽。
entries.en: Under Xianzu he commanded the armies inside and outside the court, served as seated high minister of the central capital, heard civil suits, and won wide renown.
entries.literal: Under Xianzu he was appointed commander of all military affairs within and beyond the court and seated high minister of the central capital; he heard civil lawsuits and won great praise in his time.

entries.zh: 延興中，顯祖集羣僚，欲禪位於京兆王子推。
entries.en: During the Yanxing era, Xianzu gathered his ministers, intending to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.
entries.literal: During Yanxing, Xianzu assembled the officials and wished to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 王公卿士，莫敢先言。
entries.en: Among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers, no one dared speak first.
entries.literal: None among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers dared speak first.

entries.zh: 雲進曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。
entries.en: Yun stepped forward. "Your Majesty is raising an age of peace and shelters all within the four seas. How could you turn away from the ancestral temples above and cast off the people below?
entries.literal: Yun stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty is now exalting great peace and overseeing all within the four seas; how could you above violate the ancestral temples and below abandon the myriad people?

entries.zh: 父子相傳，其來久矣，皇魏之興，未之有革。
entries.en: Father-to-son succession has long been the rule; since imperial Wei arose, it has never been altered.
entries.literal: The succession from father to son has come down for a long time; since the rise of imperial Wei, it has not been changed.

entries.zh: 皇儲正統，聖德夙章。
entries.en: The crown prince is the rightful heir, and his virtue has shone since early youth.
entries.literal: The crown prince is the orthodox heir, and his sagely virtue was manifest early.

entries.zh: 陛下必欲割捐塵務，頤神清曠者，冢副之寄，宜紹寶曆，若欲捨儲，輕移宸極，恐非先聖之意，駭動人情。
entries.en: If Your Majesty truly wishes to lay aside worldly affairs and nourish your spirit in quiet freedom, the throne should pass to the heir. If you set the heir aside and lightly move the imperial pivot, I fear this defies the former sages and will shock the hearts of men.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to cut away worldly affairs and nourish the spirit in clear freedom, the charge of the heir should continue the precious calendar; if you mean to set aside the heir and lightly shift the imperial pivot, I fear it is not the intention of the former sages and will alarm human feeling.

entries.zh: 又，天下是祖宗之天下，而陛下輒改神器，上乖七廟七靈，下長姦亂之道，此是禍福所由，願深思慎之。」
entries.en: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors. If Your Majesty suddenly changes the sacred vessel, you will offend the ancestral spirits above and open the way to treachery and disorder below. Fortune and disaster begin here; please think deeply and proceed with care."
entries.literal: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors, yet Your Majesty would suddenly change the sacred vessel, above going against the seven temples and seven spirits and below lengthening the road of treachery and disorder. This is where fortune and disaster begin; I beg you to think deeply and act carefully."

entries.zh: 太尉源賀又進曰：「陛下今欲外選諸王而禪位于皇叔者，臣恐春秋蒸嘗，昭穆有亂，脫萬世之後，必有逆饗之譏，深願思任城之言。」
entries.en: Grand Marshal Yuan He also spoke. "If Your Majesty chooses from among the princes and abdicates to an imperial uncle, I fear the order of the ancestral rites will be thrown into confusion, and later ages will condemn the offerings as improper. I beg you to weigh Rencheng's words."
entries.literal: Grand Marshal Yuan He also stepped forward and said, "If Your Majesty now wishes to choose externally among the princes and abdicate to an imperial uncle, I fear that in spring and autumn sacrifices the order of Zhao and Mu will be confused, and after ten thousand generations there will surely be criticism of improper offerings. I earnestly hope you will consider Rencheng's words."

entries.zh: 東陽公元丕等進曰：「皇太子雖聖德夙彰，然實沖幼。
entries.en: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others added, "Although the crown prince's virtue is already clear, he is still very young.
entries.literal: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others advanced and said, "Though the crown prince's sagely virtue has long been evident, he is in truth still young.

entries.zh: 陛下富於春秋，始覽機政，普天景仰，率土傒心，欲隆獨善，不以萬物為意，其若宗廟何，其若億兆何！」
entries.en: Your Majesty is young and has only begun to govern; all under heaven look to you, and every land waits on your heart. If you prize private purity and give no thought to the world, what becomes of the ancestral temples? What becomes of the people?"
entries.literal: Your Majesty is rich in years and has only begun to oversee the mechanisms of government; all under heaven look up to you, and the whole land waits with longing. If you wish to exalt solitary goodness and give no thought to the myriad things, what of the ancestral temples? What of the millions of people?"

entries.zh: 顯祖曰：「儲宮正統，受終文祖，羣公相之，有何不可。」
entries.en: Xianzu replied, "The crown prince is the rightful line, receiving the succession from Wenzu. With all of you to assist him, what could be wrong?"
entries.literal: Xianzu said, "The heir's palace is the orthodox line; he received the completion from Wenzu. If all you gentlemen assist him, what is unacceptable?"

entries.zh: 於是傳位於高祖。
entries.en: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.
entries.literal: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 後蠕蠕犯塞，雲為中軍大都督，從顯祖討之，遇於大磧。
entries.en: Later, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Yun served as grand commander of the central army and followed Xianzu against them, meeting them in the great desert.
entries.literal: Later, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Yun became grand commander of the central army, followed Xianzu in campaigning against them, and met them in the great desert.

entries.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。
entries.en: The affair is recorded in the Rouran biography.
entries.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the Rouran biography.

entries.zh: 後仇池氐反，以雲為征西大將軍討平之。
entries.en: Later, when the Qiuchi Di rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and put them down.
entries.literal: Later, when the Di of Qiuchi rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and suppressed them.

entries.zh: 除都督徐兗二州緣淮諸軍事、征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province.
entries.literal: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, with an opened office, and Inspector of Xu Province.

entries.zh: 雲以太妃蓋氏薨，表求解任，顯祖不許，雲悲號動疾，乃許之。
entries.en: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he asked to resign. Xianzu refused, but Yun grieved and wailed until he fell ill, and only then was he allowed to step down.
entries.literal: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he memorialized requesting release from office. Xianzu refused; Yun's grief and wailing brought on illness, and only then was he permitted.

entries.zh: 性善撫綏，得徐方之心，為百姓所追戀。
entries.en: He was naturally good at soothing and governing people, won the hearts of Xu, and was remembered fondly by its people.
entries.literal: By nature he was good at comforting and pacifying people, won the hearts of the Xu region, and was long remembered by the commoners.

entries.zh: 送遺錢貨，一無所受。
entries.en: He refused every gift of money or goods sent to him.
entries.literal: Of the money and goods sent to him as gifts, he accepted not a single thing.

entries.zh: 顯祖聞而嘉之。
entries.en: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.
entries.literal: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.

entries.zh: 復拜侍中、中都大官，賜帛千匹、羊千口。
entries.en: He was again made Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and received a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and was granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.

entries.zh: 出為冀州刺史，仍本將軍。
entries.en: He was sent out as inspector of Ji Province, retaining his former general's rank.
entries.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province, retaining his original generalship.

entries.zh: 雲留心政事，甚得下情，於是合州請戶輸絹五尺、粟五升以報雲恩。
entries.en: Yun governed attentively and understood those under him so well that the whole province asked to give five chi of silk and five sheng of grain per household in gratitude for his kindness.
entries.literal: Yun gave close attention to government and greatly won the feelings of those below; thereupon the whole province requested that each household contribute five chi of silk and five sheng of grain to repay Yun's kindness.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉之，遷使持節、都督陝西諸軍事、征南大將軍、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。
entries.en: Gaozu praised him and transferred him to serve as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, commander of Chang'an Garrison, and inspector of Yong Province.
entries.literal: Gaozu praised him and transferred him as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, grand commander of Chang'an Garrison, and Inspector of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 雲廉謹自修，留心庶獄，挫抑豪強，羣盜息止，州民頌之者千有餘人。
entries.en: Yun was upright and careful, gave close attention to common lawsuits, checked the powerful, and brought banditry to an end; more than a thousand people in the province praised him in verse.
entries.literal: Yun cultivated himself in integrity and caution, attended carefully to ordinary lawsuits, suppressed the powerful and arrogant, and bandits ceased; more than a thousand people of the province sang his praises.

entries.zh: 文明太后嘉之，賜帛千匹。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and gave him a thousand bolts of silk.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and granted him a thousand bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 太和五年，薨於州。
entries.en: In Taihe year 5 he died in office in the province.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he died in the province.

entries.zh: 遺令薄葬，勿受賵禭。
entries.en: In his last instructions he ordered a simple burial and forbade the acceptance of funerary gifts.
entries.literal: His final instructions ordered a modest burial and forbade acceptance of funerary gifts.

entries.zh: 諸子奉遵其旨。
entries.en: His sons carried out his wishes.
entries.literal: His sons respectfully followed his wishes.

entries.zh: 喪至京師，車駕親臨，哭之哀慟，贈以本官，諡曰康。
entries.en: When his coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person and wept bitterly over him; Yun was posthumously restored to his offices and titled Kang.
entries.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person, wept over him with deep grief, posthumously granted him his former offices, and gave him the title Kang.

entries.zh: 陪葬雲中之金陵。
entries.en: He was buried alongside the Jinling mausoleum at Yunzhong.
entries.literal: He was buried beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.

entries.zh: 雲長子澄，字道鎮，少而好學。
entries.en: Yun's eldest son Cheng, styled Daozhen, loved learning from an early age.
entries.literal: Yun's eldest son Cheng, courtesy name Daozhen, loved learning from youth.

entries.zh: 及康王薨，澄居喪以孝聞。
entries.en: After Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial devotion in mourning.
entries.literal: When Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial conduct during mourning.

entries.zh: 襲封，加征北大將軍。
entries.en: He inherited the fief and was given the added rank Grand General Who Conquers the North.
entries.literal: He inherited the fief and was additionally made Grand General Who Conquers the North.

entries.zh: 高祖時，蠕蠕犯塞，加澄使持節、都督北討諸軍事以討之。
entries.en: Under Gaozu, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Cheng was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the northern expedition against them.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's time, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Cheng was added as Bearer of the Staff and commander of the armies for the northern campaign to attack them.

entries.zh: 蠕蠕遁走，又以氐羌反叛，除都督梁益荊三州諸軍事、征南大將軍、梁州刺史。
entries.en: The Rouran fled. Later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and inspector of Liang Province.
entries.literal: The Rouran fled; later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and Inspector of Liang Province.

entries.zh: 文明太后引見澄，誡厲之，顧謂中書令李沖曰：「此兒風神吐發，德音閑婉，當為宗室領袖。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Wenming received Cheng, admonished him, then turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong. "This young man's bearing is splendid and his speech is gentle; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned Cheng, admonished him, and turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong, saying, "This child's bearing and expression are outstanding, and his words are gentle and refined; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 是行使之必稱我意。
entries.en: On this mission he will surely satisfy me.
entries.literal: On this mission he will certainly satisfy my intent.

entries.zh: 卿但記之，我不妄談人物也。」
entries.en: Remember this: I do not misjudge men."
entries.literal: You need only remember this; I do not speak of men falsely."

entries.zh: 梁州氐帥楊仲顯、婆羅、楊卜兄弟及符叱盤等，自以居邊地險，世為山狡。
entries.en: The Di leaders in Liang Province, including Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, and Fu Chipan, trusted in the rugged frontier and had long lived as mountain raiders.
entries.literal: The Di leaders of Liang Province, Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, Fu Chipan, and others relied on living in dangerous borderlands and had for generations acted as mountain brigands.

entries.zh: 澄至州，量彼風俗，誘導懷附。
entries.en: When Cheng arrived, he studied their customs and coaxed them into allegiance.
entries.literal: When Cheng reached the province, he assessed their customs and guided them into submission.

entries.zh: 表送婆羅，授仲顯循城鎮副將，楊卜廣業太守，叱盤固道鎮副將，自餘首帥，各隨才而用之，款附者賞，違命加誅，於是仇池帖然，西南款順。
entries.en: He sent Poluo to court, made Zhongxian deputy commander at Xuncheng, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander at Gudao, and used the other chiefs according to their abilities. Those who submitted were rewarded, those who resisted were punished; Qiuchi was pacified and the southwest came over.
entries.literal: He memorialized to send Poluo to court, appointed Zhongxian deputy commander of Xuncheng Garrison, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander of Gudao Garrison; the remaining chiefs were each employed according to their talents. Those who sincerely submitted were rewarded, and those who disobeyed were punished. Thus Qiuchi became settled, and the southwest submitted.

entries.zh: 加侍中，賜衣一襲、乘馬一匹，以旌其能。
entries.en: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and given a set of robes and a riding horse in recognition of his skill.
entries.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and was granted one set of robes and one riding horse to commend his ability.

entries.zh: 後轉征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史，甚有聲績。
entries.en: Later he became Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province, earning a strong record of achievement.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred as Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as Inspector of Xu Province, where he had a very strong reputation for achievement.

entries.zh: 朝於京師，引見於皇信堂。
entries.en: He came to the capital for court audience and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.
entries.literal: He came to court at the capital and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.

entries.zh: 高祖詔澄曰：「昔鄭子產鑄刑書，而晉叔向非之。
entries.en: Gaozu asked Cheng, "When Zheng Zichan cast the penal code, Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.
entries.literal: Gaozu issued an edict to Cheng: "In former times Zheng Zichan cast the written laws, and Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.

entries.zh: 此二人皆是賢士，得失竟誰？」
entries.en: Both were worthy men; in the end, who was right?"
entries.literal: Both men were worthies; in the end, who was right and who was wrong?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「鄭國寡弱，攝於強鄰，民情去就，非刑莫制，故鑄刑書以示威。
entries.en: Cheng replied, "Zheng was weak and hemmed in by powerful neighbors. The people could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the laws to show authority.
entries.literal: Cheng replied, "The state of Zheng was weak and constrained by powerful neighbors; the people's movements could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the written laws to display authority.

entries.zh: 雖乖古式，合今權道，隨時濟世，子產為得。
entries.en: Though it violated ancient form, it fit the needs of the moment. Zichan adapted to his age and helped the world, so he was right.
entries.literal: Though this departed from ancient norms, it suited the expedient way of that time; he adapted to the age and aided the world, so Zichan was right.

entries.zh: 而叔向譏議，示不忘古，可與論道，未可語權。」
entries.en: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he had not forgotten antiquity; one could discuss principle with him, but not expedience."
entries.literal: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he did not forget antiquity; one may discuss the Way with him, but not expediency."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「任城當欲為魏之子產也。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be Wei's Zichan."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be the Wei state's Zichan."

entries.zh: 澄曰：「子產道合當時，聲流竹素。
entries.en: Cheng replied, "Zichan's way suited his time, and his name passed into the histories.
entries.literal: Cheng said, "Zichan's way matched his time, and his name was handed down in the bamboo and silk records.

entries.zh: 臣既庸近，何敢庶幾。
entries.en: I am mediocre and shallow. How could I dare compare myself to him?
entries.literal: Your servant is mediocre and shallow; how would I dare hope to approach him?

entries.zh: 今陛下以四海為家，宣文德以懷天下，但江外尚阻，車書未一，季世之民，易以威伏，難以禮治。
entries.en: Your Majesty now makes the four seas your household and uses civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river resistance remains, and script and carriage tracks are not yet one. People in a late age are easy to subdue by force and hard to govern by ritual.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty has made the four seas your household and proclaims civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river there is still obstruction, and carriage tracks and writing have not yet been unified. People of a declining age are easy to subdue with authority and hard to govern by ritual.

entries.zh: 愚謂子產之法，猶應暫用，大同之後，便以道化之。」
entries.en: In my foolish view, Zichan's methods should still be used for a time; once unity is complete, then the Way can transform them."
entries.literal: In my foolish view, Zichan's laws should still be used for a time; after great unity is achieved, then they may be transformed by the Way."

entries.zh: 高祖心方革變，深善其對，笑曰：「非任城無以識變化之體。
entries.en: Gaozu was then intent on reform, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer. Smiling, he said, "Without Rencheng, no one would understand the essence of transformation.
entries.literal: Gaozu's mind was then set on reform and change, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer, smiling as he said, "Without Rencheng, no one could understand the substance of transformation.

entries.zh: 朕方創改朝制，當與任城共萬世之功耳。」
entries.en: I am just beginning to remake the court's institutions; Rencheng and I shall share in a work for ten thousand generations."
entries.literal: I am now beginning to alter the institutions of the court and shall share with Rencheng a work for ten thousand generations."

entries.zh: 後徵為中書令，改授尚書令。
entries.en: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and then made Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then reassigned as Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 蕭賾使庾蓽來朝，蓽見澄音韻遒雅，風儀秀逸，謂主客郎張彝曰：「往魏任城以武著稱，今魏任城乃以文見美也。」
entries.en: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi found Cheng's speech forceful and elegant and his bearing refined. He told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "The former Rencheng of Wei was known for arms; this Rencheng of Wei is admired for culture."
entries.literal: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi saw that Cheng's speech was strong and elegant and his bearing fine and graceful, and he told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "In the past Wei's Rencheng was known for martial prowess; now Wei's Rencheng is admired for culture."

entries.zh: 時詔延四廟之子，下逮玄孫之冑，申宗宴於皇信堂，不以爵秩為列，悉序昭穆為次，用家人之禮。
entries.en: At that time the court invited the imperial kin, from sons of the four temples down to great-great-grandsons, to a clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were seated not by rank but by ancestral order, using the rites of one family.
entries.literal: At the time an edict extended invitation from sons of the four temples down to descendants in the dark-garment generation, holding an imperial-clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were not arranged by noble rank, but all were ordered by Zhao and Mu seniority and treated with family rites.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「行禮已畢，欲令宗室各言其志，可率賦詩。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "The rites are finished. I want each kinsman to state his aspirations; let each compose a poem."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "The rites are complete; I wish each member of the imperial clan to speak his aspirations. You may all compose poems."

entries.zh: 特令澄為七言連韻，與高祖往復賭賽，遂至極歡，際夜乃罷。
entries.en: He specially ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes. Cheng and Gaozu traded verses in playful contest until they were thoroughly delighted, stopping only late at night.
entries.literal: He specifically ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes, and he and Gaozu exchanged verses in contest until their joy became extreme; only when night had fallen did they stop.

entries.zh: 後高祖外示南討，意在謀遷，齋於明堂左个，詔太常卿王諶，親令龜卜，易筮南伐之事，其兆遇革。
entries.en: Later Gaozu publicly presented plans for a southern campaign, while actually planning the capital move. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he had Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen personally divine by turtle and milfoil about the campaign; the omen was Revolution.
entries.literal: Later Gaozu outwardly displayed plans for a southern campaign, but his intention was to plan the move of the capital. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he ordered Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen to divine personally by turtle shell and milfoil about the southern campaign; the sign received was Revolution.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「此是湯武革命，順天應人之卦也。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and answering the people."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, following Heaven and responding to men."

entries.zh: 羣臣莫敢言。
entries.en: None of the ministers dared speak.
entries.literal: None of the ministers dared speak.

entries.zh: 澄進曰：「易言革者更也。
entries.en: Cheng stepped forward. "In the Changes, Revolution means change.
entries.literal: Cheng stepped forward and said, "In the Changes, ge means change.

entries.zh: 將欲應天順人，革君臣之命，湯武得之為吉。
entries.en: When Tang and Wu obeyed Heaven, answered the people, and changed the mandate between ruler and minister, this hexagram was auspicious.
entries.literal: When one is about to accord with Heaven and respond to men and change the mandate between ruler and minister, Tang and Wu obtained it as auspicious.

entries.zh: 階下帝有天下，重光累葉。
entries.en: Your Majesty already possesses the realm, with shining succession through many generations.
entries.literal: Your Majesty possesses the realm, and bright succession has continued through many generations.

entries.zh: 今曰卜征，乃可伐叛，不得云革命。
entries.en: Today the divination is for a campaign; it may mean attacking rebels, but it cannot mean changing the mandate.
entries.literal: Today you call this a divination for campaign; it can mean suppressing rebels, but it cannot be called changing the mandate.

entries.zh: 此非君人之卦，未可全為吉也。」
entries.en: This is not the hexagram for a reigning lord, and it cannot be taken as wholly auspicious."
entries.literal: This is not a hexagram for one who rules men, and it cannot be taken wholly as auspicious."

entries.zh: 高祖厲聲曰：「象云『大人虎變』，何言不吉也！」
entries.en: Gaozu said sternly, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said in a stern voice, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「陛下龍興既久，豈可方同虎變！」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long been established; how can it be compared to a tiger's change?"
entries.literal: Cheng said, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long endured; how can it be compared to the tiger's change?"

entries.zh: 高祖勃然作色曰：「社稷我社稷，任城而欲沮眾也！」
entries.en: Gaozu's face darkened. "The state is my state. Does Rencheng mean to obstruct everyone?"
entries.literal: Gaozu suddenly changed color and said, "The altars of state are my altars of state; does Rencheng wish to obstruct the assembly?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「社稷誠知陛下之社稷，然臣是社稷之臣子，豫參顧問，敢盡愚衷。」
entries.en: Cheng said, "I know well that the state is Your Majesty's, but I am its servant and son. Since I have been admitted to counsel, I dare give all my foolish sincerity."
entries.literal: Cheng said, "I truly know the altars of state are Your Majesty's altars, yet I am a servant and son of the state. Since I have been allowed to join in consultation, I dare exhaust my foolish sincerity."

entries.zh: 高祖既銳意必行，惡澄此對，久之乃解，曰：「各言其志，亦復何傷。」
entries.en: Gaozu was determined to proceed and disliked Cheng's answer, but after a long while he relented. "Each has stated his mind; what harm is there?"
entries.literal: Gaozu was already determined to proceed and disliked Cheng's reply, but after a long while he relented and said, "Each has spoken his will; what harm is there?"

entries.zh: 車駕還宮，便召澄，未及昇階，遙謂曰：「向者之革卦，今更欲論之。
entries.en: After returning to the palace, Gaozu immediately summoned Cheng. Before Cheng had mounted the steps, Gaozu called to him from afar, "About that Revolution hexagram: I want to discuss it further.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he at once summoned Cheng. Before Cheng had climbed the steps, Gaozu said to him from a distance, "That hexagram Revolution just now: I wish to discuss it further.

entries.zh: 明堂之忿，懼眾人競言，阻我大計，故厲色怖文武耳，想解朕意也。」
entries.en: In the Mingtang, I was angry because I feared everyone would start speaking at once and block my great plan, so I put on a stern face to frighten the civil and military officials. I trust you understood my intent."
entries.literal: In the anger in the Mingtang, I feared that everyone would compete to speak and obstruct my great plan, and therefore I showed a stern face to frighten the civil and military officials. I suppose you understood my meaning."

entries.zh: 乃獨謂澄曰：「今日之行，誠知不易。
entries.en: Then he said to Cheng privately, "I know very well that today's undertaking is not easy.
entries.literal: Then he said to Cheng alone, "Today's undertaking, I truly know, is not easy.

entries.zh: 但國家興自北土，徙居平城，雖富有四海，文軌未一，此間用武之地，非可文治，移風易俗，信為甚難。
entries.en: Our state rose in the north and later settled at Pingcheng. Though we possess the empire, its script and roads are not yet unified; this is a place for military power, not civil administration. Changing customs and habits here is truly difficult.
entries.literal: Yet the state rose from the northern lands and moved to reside at Pingcheng. Though it possesses all within the four seas, writing and carriage tracks are not yet one; this place is ground for using arms, not one that can be governed by civil rule. To move customs and change habits is indeed very difficult.

entries.zh: 崤函帝宅，河洛王里，因茲大舉，光宅中原，任城意以為何如？」
entries.en: The Xiao and Han passes are an imperial seat, and the He and Luo region is a royal home. If we use this great move to establish ourselves splendidly in the Central Plain, what does Rencheng think?"
entries.literal: Xiao and Han are the imperial dwelling, and the He and Luo are the royal precinct. If by this great act we brightly dwell in the Central Plain, what does Rencheng think?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「伊洛中區，均天下所據，陛下制御華夏，輯平九服，蒼生聞此，應當大慶。」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "The Yi and Luo region lies at the center, the seat shared by all under Heaven. If Your Majesty governs China from there and brings peace to the nine regions, the people will surely rejoice when they hear it."
entries.literal: Cheng said, "The Yi and Luo region is the central district, equally the place occupied by all under Heaven. If Your Majesty controls China and pacifies the nine regions, the common people, on hearing this, should greatly rejoice."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「北人戀本，忽聞將移，不能不驚擾也。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "The northerners cling to their homeland. If they suddenly hear that the capital is to be moved, they are bound to be alarmed and unsettled."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "The northerners are attached to their roots. If they suddenly hear that a move is planned, they cannot avoid alarm and disturbance."

entries.zh: 澄曰：「此既非常之事，當非常人所知，唯須決之聖懷，此輩亦何能為也。」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "This is an extraordinary matter, beyond the understanding of ordinary men. It only needs Your Majesty's decision; what can this crowd do about it?"
entries.literal: Cheng said, "Since this is an extraordinary matter, it is not what ordinary people should know. It need only be decided in the sacred mind; what can this crowd do?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「任城便是我之子房。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Rencheng is truly my Zifang."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng is indeed my Zifang."

entries.zh: 加撫軍大將軍、太子少保，又兼尚書左僕射。
entries.en: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while concurrently serving as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and also concurrently served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 及駕幸洛陽，定遷都之策，高祖詔曰：「遷移之旨，必須訪眾。
entries.en: When the emperor went to Luoyang and settled on moving the capital, Gaozu issued an edict: "The decision to relocate must be discussed with the officials.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Luoyang and the plan to move the capital was settled, Gaozu issued an edict saying, "The purpose of relocation must be put to consultation with the multitude.

entries.zh: 當遣任城馳驛向代，問彼百司，論擇可否。
entries.en: Rencheng should be sent by courier to Dai to ask the officials there and discuss whether the move is acceptable.
entries.literal: We should send Rencheng by relay horse toward Dai to ask the hundred offices there and deliberate on whether it should be chosen or not.

entries.zh: 近日論革，今真所謂革也，王其勉之。」
entries.en: Recently we discussed transformation; now this is transformation in the true sense. Let the prince exert himself."
entries.literal: Recently we discussed change; now this is truly what is called change. Prince, exert yourself in this."

entries.zh: 既至代都，眾聞遷詔，莫不驚駭。
entries.en: When he arrived at the old capital of Dai, all who heard the relocation edict were shocked and alarmed.
entries.literal: When he reached the capital at Dai, everyone who heard the edict to move the capital was shocked and frightened.

entries.zh: 澄援引今古，徐以曉之，眾乃開伏。
entries.en: Cheng cited examples from antiquity and recent times, explaining the matter patiently, and only then did everyone understand and accept it.
entries.literal: Cheng cited past and present and gradually explained it to them, and only then did all understand and submit.

entries.zh: 澄遂南馳還報，會車駕於滑臺。
entries.en: Cheng then hurried south to report back, meeting the emperor at Huatai.
entries.literal: Cheng then hastened south to report back and met the imperial carriage at Huatai.

entries.zh: 高祖大悅曰：「若非任城，朕事業不得就也。」
entries.en: Gaozu was delighted. "Without Rencheng, my undertaking could not have succeeded."
entries.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "If not for Rencheng, my undertaking could not have been accomplished."

entries.zh: 從幸鄴宮，除吏部尚書。
entries.en: He accompanied the emperor to Ye Palace and was appointed Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: He followed the emperor to Ye Palace and was appointed Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 及幸代，車駕北巡，留澄銓簡舊臣。
entries.en: When the emperor went to Dai and toured the north, Cheng was left to review and rank the old officials.
entries.literal: When the emperor went to Dai and the imperial carriage made a northern tour, Cheng was left behind to select and rank the former officials.

entries.zh: 初，魏自公侯以下，迄于選臣，動有萬數，冗散無事。
entries.en: At that time in Wei, from dukes and marquises down to appointed officials, there were often tens of thousands of supernumerary men, idle and without duties.
entries.literal: At first, in Wei, from dukes and marquises down to selected officials, there were often tens of thousands, redundant and scattered, with no duties.

entries.zh: 澄品為三等，量其優劣，盡其能否之用，咸無怨者。
entries.en: Cheng classified them into three grades, weighed their strengths and weaknesses, and used each according to his ability; no one complained.
entries.literal: Cheng graded them into three ranks, measured their merits and defects, and fully used what they could and could not do, and none resented it.

entries.zh: 駕還洛京，復兼右僕射。
entries.en: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, Cheng again served concurrently as Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the Luoyang capital, he again concurrently served as Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 高祖至北邙，遂幸洪池，命澄侍昇龍舟，因賦詩以序懷。
entries.en: When Gaozu reached Beimang, he went on to Hongchi, ordered Cheng to attend him aboard the imperial boat, and composed poems there to express his thoughts.
entries.literal: When Gaozu reached Beimang, he then went to Hongchi, ordered Cheng to attend him and board the dragon boat, and there composed poems to set forth his thoughts.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「朕昨夜夢一老公，頭鬢皓白，正理冠服，拜立路左。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Last night I dreamed of an old man with white hair and temples. His cap and robes were properly arranged, and he bowed as he stood on the left side of the road.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Last night I dreamed of an old man, with head and temples white, properly arranging his cap and garments, bowing and standing on the left side of the road.

entries.zh: 朕怪而問之，自云晉侍中嵇紹，故此奉迎。
entries.en: I was surprised and asked who he was. He said he was Xi Shao, Palace Attendant of Jin, and had come to welcome me.
entries.literal: I wondered at this and asked him, and he said he was Xi Shao, Palace Attendant of Jin, and therefore had come to receive me.

entries.zh: 神爽卑懼，似有求焉。」
entries.en: His spirit seemed humble and apprehensive, as though he had something to ask."
entries.literal: His spirit was humble and fearful, as if he had some request."

entries.zh: 澄對曰：「晉世之亂，嵇紹以身衞主，殞命御側，亦是晉之忠臣；
entries.en: Cheng replied, "During the disorders of Jin, Xi Shao shielded his lord with his own body and died at the emperor's side; he was a loyal minister of Jin.
entries.literal: Cheng replied, "In the disorder of the Jin age, Xi Shao used his own body to defend his lord and died beside the imperial carriage; he too was a loyal minister of Jin.

entries.zh: 比干遭紂兇虐，忠諫剖心，可謂殷之良士。
entries.en: Bigan suffered King Zhou's cruelty and had his heart cut out for his loyal remonstrance; he may be called a worthy man of Yin.
entries.literal: Bigan met the savagery of Zhou, and because of loyal remonstrance had his heart cut open; he may be called a worthy man of Yin.

entries.zh: 二人俱死於王事，墳塋並在於道周。
entries.en: Both men died in service to their rulers, and both of their tombs lie beside the road.
entries.literal: Both men died in royal service, and their tombs are both beside the road.

entries.zh: 然陛下徙御經殷墟而弔比干，至洛陽而遺嵇紹，當是希恩而感夢。」
entries.en: Yet as Your Majesty traveled, you passed the ruins of Yin and mourned Bigan, but when you reached Luoyang you passed over Xi Shao. He must have sought your favor and moved you through a dream."
entries.literal: Yet when Your Majesty moved the imperial carriage, you passed through the ruins of Yin and mourned Bigan, but reached Luoyang and omitted Xi Shao. It must be that he sought grace and moved you in a dream."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「朕何德，能幽感達士也。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "What virtue do I possess, that I could move a worthy man in the unseen world?
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "What virtue do I have that I can make a hidden response reach a worthy man?

entries.zh: 然實思追禮先賢，標揚忠懿，比干、嵇紹皆是古之誠烈，而朕務濃於比干，禮略於嵇紹，情有愧然。
entries.en: Still, I have truly wished to honor former worthies and make loyalty and righteousness shine. Bigan and Xi Shao were both faithful heroes of antiquity, but I gave Bigan rich attention and Xi Shao only slight rites. I am ashamed of this.
entries.literal: Yet I truly thought to pursue rites for former worthies and make loyalty and righteousness manifest. Bigan and Xi Shao were both sincere and fierce men of antiquity, but my attention was abundant toward Bigan and my rites slight toward Xi Shao, and in feeling I am ashamed.

entries.zh: 既有此夢，或如任城所言。」
entries.en: Since this dream has occurred, perhaps it is just as Rencheng says."
entries.literal: Since there has been this dream, perhaps it is as Rencheng has said."

entries.zh: 於是求其兆域，遣使弔祭焉。
entries.en: He then searched for the site of Xi Shao's tomb and sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice there.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sought the boundaries of Xi Shao's grave site and sent envoys to offer mourning and sacrifice there.

entries.zh: 蕭鸞既殺蕭昭業而自立，昭業雍州刺史曹虎請以襄陽內附。
entries.en: After Xiao Luan killed Xiao Zhaoye and took power, Cao Hu, Zhaoye's Inspector of Yongzhou, asked to surrender Xiangyang.
entries.literal: After Xiao Luan killed Xiao Zhaoye and set himself up, Cao Hu, Zhaoye's Inspector of Yongzhou, requested to bring Xiangyang in allegiance.

entries.zh: 分遣諸將，車駕將自赴之。
entries.en: Gaozu sent out several generals and was preparing to go there in person.
entries.literal: Gaozu separately dispatched the various generals, and the imperial carriage was about to go there in person.

entries.zh: 豫州又表，虎奉誠之使不復重來。
entries.en: Yuzhou then reported that no further envoy had come from Hu to confirm his sincerity.
entries.literal: Yuzhou further memorialized that Hu's envoy offering sincerity had not come again.

entries.zh: 高祖引澄及咸陽王禧、彭城王勰、司徒馮誕、司空穆亮、鎮南李沖等議之。
entries.en: Gaozu summoned Cheng, Yuan Xi the Prince of Xianyang, Yuan Xie the Prince of Pengcheng, Situ Feng Dan, Sikong Mu Liang, General Who Guards the South Li Chong, and others to discuss the matter.
entries.literal: Gaozu brought in Cheng, Xianyang Prince Xi, Pengcheng Prince Xie, Minister over the Masses Feng Dan, Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Guards the South Li Chong, and others to discuss it.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「比得邊州表云，襄陽慕化，朕將鳴鑾江沔，為彼聲勢。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Recently I received a report from the border province saying that Xiangyang longed for our transforming rule, and I was about to take the imperial carriage to the Jiang and Mian to support them.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Recently I received a memorial from the border province saying that Xiangyang admires our transformation, and I was about to sound the imperial bells by the Jiang and Mian to give them support.

entries.zh: 今復表稱，更無後信，於行留之計，竟欲如何？」
entries.en: Now another report says there has been no later message. So, on the question of going or staying, what do you finally advise?"
entries.literal: Now another memorial says that there has been no later message. As for the plan to go or remain, what, in the end, do you intend?"

entries.zh: 禧等或云宜行，或言宜止。
entries.en: Xi and the others were divided, some saying they should go and others saying they should stop.
entries.literal: Xi and the others sometimes said it was fitting to go, and sometimes said it was fitting to stop.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「眾人紛紜，意見不等，朕莫知所從。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Everyone is arguing at once and their opinions differ; I do not know whose advice to follow.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "The many men are in confusion, and their opinions are not the same; I do not know which to follow.

entries.zh: 必欲盡行留之勢，使言理俱暢者，宜有客主，共相起發。
entries.en: If we are to examine fully the case for going and the case for staying, so that both argument and principle are clear, we should set up opposing sides to draw each other out.
entries.literal: If we must exhaust the strengths of going and staying, and have words and principle both fully expressed, there should be guest and host, mutually drawing each other out.

entries.zh: 任城與鎮南為應留之議，朕當為宜行之論，諸公俱坐聽得失，長者從之。」
entries.en: Rencheng and the General Who Guards the South may argue for staying, and I will argue for going. Let the lords sit and hear the merits of each side, and then follow the better case."
entries.literal: Rencheng and General Who Guards the South will make the argument for staying; I shall make the argument for going. Let all the lords sit and listen to the gains and losses, and follow the superior argument."

entries.zh: 於是高祖曰：「二賢試言留計也。」
entries.en: Gaozu then said, "Let the two worthies state the plan for staying."
entries.literal: Thereupon Gaozu said, "Let the two worthies try to speak on the plan for staying."

entries.zh: 沖對曰：「臣等正以徒御草創，人斯樂安，內而應者未審，不宜輕爾動發。」
entries.en: Li Chong replied, "We only think that the retinue has just been organized, the people are content with peace, and the supposed supporters inside have not been confirmed. We should not set out lightly."
entries.literal: Chong replied, "We simply think that the servants and escorts have only just been established, the people are now happy in peace, and those within who would respond have not been verified; it is not fitting to set out lightly."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「襄陽款問，似當是虛。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Xiangyang's offer of submission may well be false.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "The message of submission from Xiangyang seems likely to be false.

entries.zh: 亦知初遷之民，無宜勞役。
entries.en: I also know that the people newly moved to the capital should not be burdened with service.
entries.literal: I also know that the people who have just been moved should not be burdened with labor.

entries.zh: 脫歸誠有實，即當乘其悅附，遠則有會稽之會，近則略平江北。
entries.en: But if their surrender is genuine, we should take advantage of their willingness to attach themselves to us. At best, we might hold an assembly at Kuaiji; at least, we could bring the land north of the Yangzi roughly under control.
entries.literal: But if the return to sincerity is real, then we should take advantage of their pleased attachment; at the farthest there may be an assembly at Kuaiji, and at the nearest we may roughly pacify the north of the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 如其送款是虛，且可遊巡淮楚，問民之瘼，使彼土蒼生，知君德之所在，復何所損而惜此一舉？
entries.en: If the offer is false, we can still tour Huai and Chu, inquire into the people's hardships, and let the people there see where the ruler's virtue lies. What harm would that do, that we should shrink from this single move?
entries.literal: If their sending of submission is false, we can simply make an inspection tour of Huai and Chu, ask after the people's sufferings, and let the common people of that land know where the ruler's virtue lies. What loss would there be, that we should begrudge this one move?

entries.zh: 脫降問是實，而停不撫接，不亦稽阻款誠，毀朕大略也。」
entries.en: If the surrender is real and we halt without receiving and reassuring them, would that not block their sincere submission and ruin my larger plan?"
