entries.literal: If the surrender message is real, and we stop without comforting and receiving them, would this not delay and obstruct their sincerity of submission and ruin my grand strategy?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「降問若審，應有表質。
entries.en: Cheng said, "If the surrender report were reliable, there should be a formal memorial and pledge.
entries.literal: Cheng said, "If the surrender message were verified, there should be a memorial and pledge.

entries.zh: 而使人一返，靜無音問，其詐也可見。
entries.en: But since the envoy returned, there has been only silence and no further message. Its falseness is obvious.
entries.literal: But after the envoy returned once, there has been silence and no further word; its falseness can be seen.

entries.zh: 今代遷之眾，人懷戀本，細累相攜，始就洛邑，居無一椽之室，家闕儋石之糧，而使怨苦即戎，泣當白刃，恐非歌舞之師也。
entries.en: The people moved from Dai still long for their old home. They have only just reached Luoyang with their families and dependents; they have not even a single-raftered house to live in, and their households lack a bare measure of grain. If we drive them bitterly to war, weeping before drawn blades, this will hardly be an army marching in joy.
entries.literal: Now the multitude moved from Dai all cherish attachment to their roots; bringing wives, children, and small dependents, they have only just reached Luoyi, have no house of even a single rafter to live in, and their households lack even a dan or shi of grain. To make them resentfully and bitterly take up arms, weeping before naked blades, I fear this is not an army of song and dance.

entries.zh: 今茲區宇初構，又東作方興，正是子來百堵之日，農夫肆力之秋，宜寬彼逋誅，惠此民庶。
entries.en: This region is only newly founded, and the spring labors are just beginning. It is the time for the people to build the city walls and for farmers to spend their strength in the fields. We should defer punishment over there and show kindness to the common people here.
entries.literal: Now this region has only just been built, and spring plowing is just beginning. This is precisely the day when the people come to build the hundred walls, the season when farmers exert their strength. It is fitting to be lenient toward those there who have escaped punishment and to show favor to these common people.

entries.zh: 且三軍已援，無稽赴接。
entries.en: Besides, the armies have already been sent in support; there is no need to rush in person to receive an unverified surrender.
entries.literal: Moreover, the three armies have already been sent as support; there is no need for an unverified hastening to receive them.

entries.zh: 苟其款實，力足納撫，待克平襄沔，然後動駕。
entries.en: If the offer is genuine, our forces are sufficient to receive and pacify them. Once Xiangyang and the Mian region have been secured, the emperor can move then.
entries.literal: If their submission is genuine, our forces are enough to take them in and pacify them; wait until Xiangyang and the Mian region have been pacified, and only then move the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 今無故勞涉，空為往返，恐挫損天威，更成賊膽，願上覽盤庚始遷之艱難，下矜詩人由庚之至詠，輯寧新邑，惠康億兆。」
entries.en: To make this hard journey without cause, only to go and return in vain, would damage imperial majesty and embolden the rebels. I ask Your Majesty to remember the hardships Pan Geng faced when he first moved the capital, and to heed the poet's deepest praise in "You Geng": settle the new city and bring comfort to the people."
entries.literal: Now to labor and travel without cause, merely going and returning in vain, I fear will damage the heavenly majesty and instead embolden the rebels. I beg Your Majesty above to consider the hardships when Pan Geng first moved the capital, and below to pity the utmost chant of the poet in "You Geng," to bring peace to the new city and grant ease to the multitudes."

entries.zh: 而司空亮以為宜行，公卿皆同之。
entries.en: But Sikong Mu Liang thought they should go, and the high ministers all agreed with him.
entries.literal: But Minister of Works Liang considered it fitting to go, and the dukes and ministers all agreed with him.

entries.zh: 澄謂亮曰：「公在外見旌鉞既張，而有憂色，每聞談論，不願此行，何得對聖顏更如斯之語也。
entries.en: Cheng said to Liang, "Outside, when you saw the banners and axes already set out, you looked worried; whenever you discussed it, you did not want this expedition. How can you now say such things before His Majesty?
entries.literal: Cheng said to Liang, "When you were outside and saw the banners and axes already arrayed, you had a worried look; whenever I heard you discuss it, you did not wish for this journey. How can you now, before the sacred countenance, speak like this?

entries.zh: 面背不同，事涉欺佞，非所謂論道之德，更失國士之體，或有傾側，當由公輩佞臣。」
entries.en: To say one thing to a man's face and another behind his back borders on deceitful flattery. That is not the virtue of one who debates principle, and it falls short of the bearing of a statesman. If the state is thrown off balance, it will be because of flatterers like you."
entries.literal: If face and back are not the same, the matter borders on deceit and flattery. This is not the virtue called discussing the Way, and further loses the bearing of a man of state. If there is any leaning and overturning, it will be because of flatterers like you."

entries.zh: 李沖曰：「任城王可謂忠於社稷，願陛下深察其言。
entries.en: Li Chong said, "The Prince of Rencheng can truly be called loyal to the state. I hope Your Majesty will weigh his words carefully.
entries.literal: Li Chong said, "The Prince of Rencheng may be called loyal to the altars of state. I hope Your Majesty will examine his words deeply.

entries.zh: 臣等在外，皆憚征行，唯貴與賤，不謀同辭，仰願聖心裁其可否。」
entries.en: Outside court, all of us fear the campaign. High and low have not conferred, yet we say the same thing. I beg Your Majesty to decide what is right."
entries.literal: When we are outside, all of us dread a campaign. Noble and base alike do not consult one another yet speak the same words. I look up and hope the sacred mind will decide whether it can be done or not."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「任城適以公等從朕，有如此論。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Rencheng made that argument just because you gentlemen sided with me.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng just now used the fact that you gentlemen follow me to make such an argument.

entries.zh: 不從朕者，何必皆忠而通識安危也。
entries.en: Are all who disagree with me necessarily loyal men with a penetrating grasp of danger and security?
entries.literal: Must those who do not follow me all be loyal and penetratingly understand safety and danger?

entries.zh: 小忠是大忠之賊，無乃似諸？」
entries.en: Small loyalty is the enemy of great loyalty. Is this not something like that?"
entries.literal: Small loyalty is the thief of great loyalty. Is this not rather like that?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「臣既愚闇，不識大理，所可言者，雖涉小忠，要是竭盡微款，不知大忠者竟何據？」
entries.en: Cheng said, "I am foolish and dim and do not understand great principles. What I say may be only small loyalty, but it is the full measure of my poor sincerity. I do not know: what, in the end, is great loyalty based on?"
entries.literal: Cheng said, "I am foolish and benighted and do not know the great principle. What I can say may border on small loyalty, but in the end it exhausts my slight sincerity. I do not know, on what does great loyalty finally rest?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「任城脫居台鼎之任，欲令大忠在己也。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "If Rencheng held the office of an Excellency, he would want great loyalty to belong to himself."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "If Rencheng were to occupy the responsibility of the Excellencies, he would want great loyalty to reside in himself."

entries.zh: 澄曰：「臣誠才非台弼，智闕和鼎，脫得濫居公鉉，庶當官而行，不負愚志。」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "My talent is not fit to support the highest offices, and my wisdom is not enough to season the cauldron of state. But if I undeservedly held an Excellency's place, I hope I would act according to the office and not betray my poor intentions."
entries.literal: Cheng said, "My talent is indeed not that of a support to the Excellencies, and my wisdom lacks what is needed to harmonize the cauldron. If I should undeservedly occupy the handles of an Excellency, I hope I would act according to my office and not betray my foolish intent."

entries.zh: 高祖大笑。
entries.en: Gaozu burst out laughing.
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed loudly.

entries.zh: 澄又謂亮曰：「昔汲黯於漢武前面折公孫食脫粟飯，臥布被，云其詐也。
entries.en: Cheng then said to Liang, "Long ago, in front of Emperor Wu of Han, Ji An accused Gongsun Hong to his face of eating coarse grain and sleeping under a plain cloth quilt as a fraud.
entries.literal: Cheng again said to Liang, "In the past, before Emperor Wu of Han, Ji An confronted Gongsun Hong to his face for eating coarse grain and sleeping under a cloth quilt, saying that it was fraudulent.

entries.zh: 于時公孫謙讓下之。
entries.en: At the time, Gongsun humbly yielded and put himself below him.
entries.literal: At that time Gongsun modestly yielded and placed himself below him.

entries.zh: 武帝歎汲黯至忠，公孫長者，二人稱賢。
entries.en: Emperor Wu admired Ji An for utmost loyalty and Gongsun for elder virtue, and both men were praised as worthy.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu sighed that Ji An was utterly loyal and Gongsun was an elder of virtue, and the two men were both called worthy.

entries.zh: 公既道均昔士，願思長者之言。」
entries.en: Since your conduct can equal that of men of old, I hope you will remember the elder's example."
entries.literal: Since your way is equal to that of the old scholars, I hope you will think on the words of the elder."

entries.zh: 高祖笑曰：「任城欲自比汲黯也。
entries.en: Gaozu laughed. "Rencheng wants to compare himself to Ji An.
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed and said, "Rencheng wishes to compare himself to Ji An.

entries.zh: 且所言是公，未知得失所在，何便謝司空也。」
entries.en: Besides, your words concerned the Duke, and we do not yet know who is right or wrong. Why rush to apologize to the Minister of Works?"
entries.literal: Besides, what was said concerns the Duke, and it is not yet known where gain and loss lie. Why apologize to the Minister of Works so readily?"

entries.zh: 駕遂南伐。
entries.en: The emperor then went south on campaign.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage then went south on campaign.

entries.zh: 五等開建，食邑一千戶。
entries.en: When the five ranks of nobility were instituted, his fief was set at one thousand households.
entries.literal: When the five ranks were established, his fief was one thousand households.

entries.zh: 後從征至懸瓠，以篤疾還京。
entries.en: Later he accompanied the campaign to Xuanhu, but returned to the capital because of serious illness.
entries.literal: Later he followed the campaign as far as Xuanhu, but because of severe illness returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 駕餞之汝濆，賦詩而別。
entries.en: The emperor saw him off on the bank of the Ru River, composing poems as they parted.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage gave him a farewell banquet on the bank of the Ru and composed poems on parting.

entries.zh: 車駕還洛，引見王公侍臣於清徽堂。
entries.en: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, he received the princes, dukes, and attendant ministers in Qinghui Hall.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, he received the princes, dukes, and attendant ministers in Qinghui Hall.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「此堂成來，未與王公行宴樂之禮。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Since this hall was completed, I have not yet held a proper feast here with the princes and dukes.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Since this hall was completed, I have not yet performed the rites of feasting and music with the princes and dukes.

entries.zh: 後東閤廡堂粗復始就，故今與諸賢欲無高而不昇，無小而不入。」
entries.en: Now that the eastern pavilion and side halls have roughly been completed, I want to go through them today with you worthies, ascending every height and entering every small place."
entries.literal: Afterward the eastern pavilion and side hall were roughly finished, and therefore today, together with the worthies, I wish there to be no high place we do not ascend and no small place we do not enter."

entries.zh: 因之流化渠。
entries.en: They then went to the Liuhua Canal.
entries.literal: They then went to the Liuhua Canal.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「此曲水者亦有其義，取乾道曲成，萬物無滯。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "This winding water has meaning too. It draws on the Way of Qian, which completes things by bending and leaves all things unobstructed."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "This winding water also has its meaning: it takes from the Way of Qian, which bends to complete things and lets the ten thousand things have no obstruction."

entries.zh: 次之洗煩池。
entries.en: Next they went to the Xifan Pond.
entries.literal: Next they went to the Xifan Pond.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「此池中亦有嘉魚。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "There are fine fish in this pond as well."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "There are fine fish in this pond too."

entries.zh: 澄曰：「此所謂『魚在在藻，有頒其首』。」
entries.en: Cheng said, "This is what the poem means: "The fish are there among the weeds; large are their heads.""
entries.literal: Cheng said, "This is what is meant by, "The fish are there among the weeds; large are their heads.""

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「且取『王在靈沼，於牣魚躍』。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Let us instead take the line, "The king is at the Spirit Pond; it is full, and the fish leap.""
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Let us rather take, "The king is in the Spirit Pond; how full it is, and the fish leap.""

entries.zh: 次之觀德殿。
entries.en: Next they went to the Hall for Observing Virtue.
entries.literal: Next they went to the Hall for Observing Virtue.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「射以觀德，故遂命之。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Archery is used to observe virtue, so I gave it this name."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Through archery one observes virtue, and therefore I named it so."

entries.zh: 次之凝閑堂。
entries.en: Next they went to the Ningxian Hall.
entries.literal: Next they went to the Ningxian Hall.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「名目要有其義，此蓋取夫子閑居之義。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "A name must have meaning. This one draws on the idea of the Master at leisure.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Names and labels must have meaning; this probably takes the meaning of the Master dwelling at leisure.

entries.zh: 不可縱奢以忘儉，自安以忘危，故此堂後作茅茨堂。」
entries.en: One must not indulge in luxury and forget thrift, or rest in safety and forget danger. That is why I built the Thatched Hall behind it."
entries.literal: One must not indulge extravagance and forget frugality, nor settle in safety and forget danger; therefore behind this hall I built the Thatched Hall."

entries.zh: 謂李沖曰：「此東曰步元廡，西曰遊凱廡。
entries.en: He said to Li Chong, "The eastern gallery is called Buyuan, and the western one Youkai.
entries.literal: He said to Li Chong, "This one to the east is called the Buyuan Gallery, and the one to the west is called the Youkai Gallery.

entries.zh: 此堂雖無唐堯之君，卿等當無愧於元、凱。」
entries.en: Although this hall has no ruler equal to Tang Yao, you gentlemen should not be ashamed before Yuan and Kai."
entries.literal: Though this hall has no ruler like Tang Yao, you gentlemen should have no shame before Yuan and Kai."

entries.zh: 沖對曰：「臣既遭唐堯之君，不敢辭元、凱之譽。」
entries.en: Chong replied, "Since I have encountered a ruler like Tang Yao, I dare not refuse the praise of being Yuan or Kai."
entries.literal: Chong replied, "Since I have met a ruler like Tang Yao, I dare not decline the praise of Yuan and Kai."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「光景垂落，朕同宗則有載考之義，卿等將出無遠，何得默爾，不示德音。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "The daylight is fading. For my clansmen there is the duty of continuing the feast into the night, and you gentlemen are about to withdraw though the hour is not far advanced. How can you stay silent and not give us worthy words?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "The light and shadows are about to fall. For my men of the same clan, there is the meaning of continuing the night gathering; you gentlemen are about to go out and are not far off, so how can you be silent and not show virtuous sounds?"

entries.zh: 即命黃門侍郎崔光、郭祚，通直郎邢巒、崔休等賦詩言志。
entries.en: He then ordered Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, Palace Attendants of the Yellow Gates, and Xing Luan, Cui Xiu, and others, Gentlemen for Unrestricted Attendance, to compose poems expressing their thoughts.
entries.literal: He at once ordered Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gates Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, and Gentleman for Unrestricted Attendance Xing Luan, Cui Xiu, and others to compose poems expressing their intentions.

entries.zh: 燭至，公卿辭退。
entries.en: When the candles were brought in, the dukes and ministers took their leave.
entries.literal: When the candles arrived, the dukes and ministers took leave and withdrew.

entries.zh: 李沖再拜上千萬歲壽。
entries.en: Li Chong bowed twice and offered a long-life toast of countless years.
entries.literal: Li Chong bowed twice and offered a toast for ten thousand times ten thousand years.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「卿向以燭至致辭，復獻千萬之壽，朕報卿以南山之詩。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "You used the arrival of the candles as a reason to withdraw, and then offered a toast of countless years. I will answer you with the poem of the Southern Mountain."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "You just now offered words of departure when the candles arrived, and then presented a toast of ten thousand times ten thousand years. I answer you with the poem of the Southern Mountain."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「燭至辭退，庶姓之禮；
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Taking leave when the candles arrive is the rite for those of other surnames;
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Withdrawing when the candles arrive is the rite for those of other surnames;

entries.zh: 在夜載考，宗族之義。
entries.en: continuing the gathering into the night is the duty of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: continuing the night gathering is the duty of the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 卿等且還，朕與諸王宗室，欲成此夜飲。」
entries.en: You gentlemen may go home for now. I and the princes of the imperial clan wish to finish tonight's drinking."
entries.literal: You gentlemen may return for now; I and the princes and imperial clansmen wish to complete this night's drinking."

entries.zh: 又從幸鄴。
entries.en: He again accompanied the emperor to Ye.
entries.literal: He again followed the emperor to Ye.

entries.zh: 還洛，以出納之勞，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: After returning to Luoyang, his fief was increased by five hundred households for his work handling communications and affairs.
entries.literal: On returning to Luoyang, because of his labor in receiving and dispatching affairs, his fief was increased by five hundred households.

entries.zh: 坐公事免官。
entries.en: He was dismissed from office over an official matter.
entries.literal: Because of an official matter, he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 尋兼吏部尚書。
entries.en: Soon he was made acting Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 恒州刺史穆泰在州謀反，推朔州刺史陽平王頤為主。
entries.en: Mu Tai, Inspector of Hengzhou, plotted rebellion in his province and proposed Yuan Yi, Prince of Yangping and Inspector of Shuozhou, as their leader.
entries.literal: Mu Tai, Inspector of Hengzhou, plotted rebellion in his province and put forward Yi, Prince of Yangping and Inspector of Shuozhou, as leader.

entries.zh: 頤表其狀。
entries.en: Yi reported the situation in a memorial.
entries.literal: Yi memorialized the circumstances.

entries.zh: 高祖召澄入見凝閑堂，曰：「適得陽平表曰，穆泰謀為不軌，招誘宗室。
entries.en: Gaozu summoned Cheng to Ningxian Hall and said, "I have just received Yangping's memorial. It says that Mu Tai is plotting rebellion and trying to draw in members of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Gaozu summoned Cheng in to be seen at Ningxian Hall and said, "I have just received Yangping's memorial, saying that Mu Tai is plotting lawlessness and enticing the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 脫或必然，遷京甫爾，北人戀舊，南北紛擾，朕洛陽不立也。
entries.en: If this is true, the capital has only just been moved, the northerners still cling to the old places, north and south will fall into turmoil, and my Luoyang will not stand.
entries.literal: If this should prove certainly true, the move of the capital has only just happened, the northerners are attached to the old place, north and south will be in disorder, and my Luoyang will not stand.

entries.zh: 此事非任城不辦，可為我力疾向北。
entries.en: No one but Rencheng can handle this. For my sake, struggle through your illness and go north.
entries.literal: This matter cannot be handled by anyone but Rencheng; for me, exert yourself despite illness and go north.

entries.zh: 如其弱也，直往擒翦；
entries.en: If he is weak, go directly and capture or destroy him;
entries.literal: If he is weak, go straight there and seize and cut him down;

entries.zh: 若其勢強，可承制發并肆兵以殄之。
entries.en: if his forces are strong, you may act under imperial authority and mobilize the troops of Bing and Si to wipe him out.
entries.literal: if his power is strong, you may receive authority from the throne and call out the troops of Bing and Si to annihilate him.

entries.zh: 雖知王患，既是國家大事，不容辭也。」
entries.en: I know you are ill, but this is a great matter of state and cannot be declined."
entries.literal: Although I know the Prince is ill, this is a great affair of state and does not permit refusal."

entries.zh: 澄曰：「泰等愚惑，正戀本為此，非有遠圖。
entries.en: Cheng said, "Mu Tai and the others are foolish and confused. They do this only from attachment to their old home; they have no long-term plan.
entries.literal: Cheng said, "Mu Tai and the others are foolish and deluded; they are doing this only because they are attached to their old home, and they have no far-reaching plan.

entries.zh: 臣誠怯弱，不憚是輩，雖復患惙，豈敢有辭。
entries.en: I am timid and weak, but I do not fear men like these. Though I am ill and worn down, how could I dare refuse?
entries.literal: I am indeed timid and weak, but I do not fear this sort. Though I am again ill and exhausted, how would I dare make any refusal?

entries.zh: 謹當罄盡心力，繼之以死，願陛下勿憂。」
entries.en: I will devote all my heart and strength, even unto death. I ask Your Majesty not to worry."
entries.literal: I shall reverently exhaust all my heart and strength and follow it with death; I hope Your Majesty will not worry."

entries.zh: 高祖笑曰：「得任城此行，朕復何憂也。」
entries.en: Gaozu laughed. "With Rencheng making this trip, what do I have left to worry about?"
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed and said, "Having Rencheng make this journey, what further worry do I have?"

entries.zh: 遂授節，銅虎、竹使符，御仗，左右，仍行恒州事。
entries.en: He then granted Cheng the staff, bronze tiger tally and bamboo envoy tally, imperial weapons and attendants, and had him administer Hengzhou affairs.
entries.literal: Thereupon he granted him the staff of authority, bronze tiger and bamboo envoy tallies, imperial weapons, and attendants on left and right, and had him continue to act in the affairs of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 行達雁門，太守夜告泰已握眾西就陽平，城下聚結，唯見弓仗。
entries.en: When Cheng reached Yanmen, the governor reported by night that Mu Tai had gathered his followers and gone west to join Yangping. Men were assembling below the city, and bows and weapons were everywhere.
entries.literal: When his journey reached Yanmen, the commandery governor reported at night that Tai had already taken control of the crowd and gone west to join Yangping; below the city they were gathering, and only bows and weapons could be seen.

entries.zh: 澄聞便速進。
entries.en: On hearing this, Cheng advanced at once.
entries.literal: When Cheng heard this, he immediately advanced rapidly.

entries.zh: 時右丞孟斌曰：「事不可量，須依敕召并肆兵，然後徐動。」
entries.en: Right Aide Meng Bin said, "The situation is uncertain. We should obey the edict, summon the troops of Bing and Si, and only then proceed carefully."
entries.literal: At the time, Right Aide Meng Bin said, "The situation cannot be measured; we must follow the edict and summon the troops of Bing and Si, and only afterward move slowly."

entries.zh: 澄曰：「泰既構逆，應據堅城，而更迎陽平，度其所為，似當勢弱。
entries.en: Cheng said, "If Tai has truly mounted a rebellion, he should be holding a strong city; instead he has gone to meet Yangping. From his conduct, his position seems weak.
entries.literal: Cheng said, "Since Tai has formed a rebellion, he should occupy a strong city, yet instead he has gone to meet Yangping. Judging what he is doing, his position seems likely to be weak.

entries.zh: 泰既不相拒，無故發兵，非宜也。
entries.en: Since Tai is not opposing us directly, it would be wrong to call up troops without cause.
entries.literal: Since Tai is not resisting us, to raise troops without cause is not fitting.

entries.zh: 但速往鎮之，民心自定。」
entries.en: If we simply get there quickly and hold things down, the people will settle by themselves."
entries.literal: If we only go there quickly and suppress it, the hearts of the people will settle of themselves."

entries.zh: 遂倍道兼行，出其不意。
entries.en: He then doubled his stages, pressed forward, and caught them by surprise.
entries.literal: He then traveled double stages and pressed the journey, coming out where they did not expect him.

entries.zh: 又遣治書侍御史李煥先赴，至即擒泰，民情怡然。
entries.en: He also sent Li Huan, Investigating Censor for the Bureau of Evaluation, ahead. When Li Huan arrived he immediately captured Tai, and the people were reassured.
entries.literal: He also sent Li Huan, Investigating Censor for the Bureau of Evaluation, ahead; when Huan arrived, he immediately seized Tai, and the people's feelings were calm and pleased.

entries.zh: 窮其黨與，罪人皆得，鉅鹿公陸叡、安樂侯元隆等百餘人皆獄禁。
entries.en: They tracked down his associates and captured all the offenders. Lu Rui, Duke of Julu, Yuan Long, Marquis of Anle, and more than a hundred others were imprisoned.
entries.literal: They pursued his associates to the end, and all the criminals were obtained; Lu Rui, Duke of Julu, Yuan Long, Marquis of Anle, and more than a hundred others were all imprisoned.

entries.zh: 具狀表聞，高祖覽表大悅，召集公卿以下以表示之，曰：「我任城可謂社稷臣也，尋其罪案，正復臯陶斷獄，豈能過之。」
entries.en: Cheng reported the full case in a memorial. Gaozu read it with great delight, summoned the high ministers and officials, showed them the memorial, and said, "My Rencheng may truly be called a minister of state. In investigating this case, even Gaoyao himself could not have surpassed him."
entries.literal: He reported the full circumstances in a memorial. Gaozu read the memorial and was greatly pleased; he summoned and gathered the dukes and ministers and those below them, showed them the memorial, and said, "My Rencheng may be called a minister of the altars of state. If one examines his criminal case, even Gaoyao deciding lawsuits, how could he surpass it?"

entries.zh: 顧謂咸陽王等曰：「汝等脫當其處，不能辦此。」
entries.en: He turned to the Prince of Xianyang and the others. "Had you been in his place, you could not have managed this."
entries.literal: He looked back and said to the Prince of Xianyang and the others, "If you had been in that position, you could not have handled this."

entries.zh: 車駕尋幸平城，勞澄曰：「任城此行，深副遠寄。」
entries.en: Soon afterward the emperor went to Pingcheng and commended Cheng: "Rencheng's mission has fully answered the trust placed in him from afar."
entries.literal: The imperial carriage soon went to Pingcheng, and he comforted Cheng, saying, "Rencheng's journey has deeply fulfilled the distant charge."

entries.zh: 對曰：「陛下威靈遠被，罪人無所逃刑，臣何勞之有。」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's awe reaches far; the guilty had nowhere to escape punishment. What effort of mine was there?"
entries.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty's awe-inspiring spirit reaches far; the criminals had nowhere to escape punishment. What labor of mine was there?"

entries.zh: 引見逆徒，無一人稱枉，時人莫不歎之。
entries.en: When the rebels were presented, not one claimed to have been wronged, and everyone at the time marveled.
entries.literal: When the rebel followers were brought in and seen, not one person claimed injustice, and people of the time all sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 高祖顧謂左右曰：「昔仲尼云：『聽訟吾猶人也，必也使無訟乎。』
entries.en: Gaozu turned to his attendants and said, "Long ago Confucius said, 'In hearing lawsuits I am no different from others; what matters is making it so there are no lawsuits.'
entries.literal: Gaozu looked back and said to his attendants, "In the past Zhongni said, 'In hearing lawsuits I am like other men; what is necessary is to make there be no lawsuits.'

entries.zh: 然聖人之聽訟，殆非常人所匹，必也無訟，今日見之矣。」
entries.en: But a sage's handling of cases is hardly something ordinary men can match. Today I have seen what it means to leave no one with a grievance."
entries.literal: Yet a sage's hearing of lawsuits is probably not something ordinary men can match; as for there necessarily being no lawsuits, today I have seen it."

entries.zh: 以澄正尚書。
entries.en: He made Cheng a full Minister of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He made Cheng a regular Minister of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 車駕南伐，留澄居守，復兼右僕射。
entries.en: When the emperor campaigned south, Cheng was left in charge of the capital and again concurrently served as Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Cheng was left to guard the capital and again concurrently served as Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 澄表請以國秩一歲租布帛助供軍資，詔受其半。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized asking to contribute one year of his fief income in cloth and silk to military supplies; by edict the court accepted half.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized requesting that one year's rent in cloth and silk from his state rank be used to help provide military supplies; the edict accepted half of it.

entries.zh: 高祖幸鄴，值高車樹者反叛，車駕將親討之。
entries.en: When Gaozu went to Ye, the Shuzhe branch of the Gaoche rebelled, and the emperor was about to campaign against them personally.
entries.literal: When Gaozu went to Ye, he encountered the rebellion of the Shuzhe of the Gaoche, and the imperial carriage was about to campaign against them in person.

entries.zh: 澄表諫不宜親行。
entries.en: Cheng sent a memorial remonstrating that the emperor should not go in person.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized in remonstrance that it was not fitting for him to go in person.

entries.zh: 會江陽王繼平之，乃止。
entries.en: Then Yuan Ji, Prince of Jiangyang, pacified them, and the expedition was called off.
entries.literal: It happened that Jiangyang Prince Ji pacified them, and so it stopped.

entries.zh: 高祖還洛，引見公卿。
entries.en: When Gaozu returned to Luoyang, he received the high ministers.
entries.literal: When Gaozu returned to Luoyang, he received the dukes and ministers.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「營國之本，禮教為先。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Ritual instruction comes first in ordering the state.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "In the foundation of ordering the state, ritual teaching comes first.

entries.zh: 朕離京邑以來，禮教為日新以不？」
entries.en: Since I left the capital, has ritual instruction been renewed day by day, or not?"
entries.literal: Since I left the capital city, has ritual teaching become daily renewed or not?"

entries.zh: 澄對曰：「臣謂日新。」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "I believe it has been renewed day by day."
entries.literal: Cheng replied, "I think it is daily renewed."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「朕昨入城，見車上婦人冠帽而著小襦襖者，若為如此，尚書何為不察？」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Yesterday as I entered the city, I saw women on carts wearing caps and little short jackets. If this is going on, why has the Ministry failed to investigate?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Yesterday, when I entered the city, I saw women on carts wearing caps and dressed in small short jackets. If things are like this, why does the Ministry not inspect it?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「著猶少於不著者。」
entries.en: Cheng said, "Those wearing them are still fewer than those who are not."
entries.literal: Cheng said, "Those wearing them are still fewer than those not wearing them."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「深可怪也！
entries.en: Gaozu said, "That is astonishing!
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "This is deeply astonishing!

entries.zh: 任城意欲令全著乎？
entries.en: Does Rencheng mean he wants all of them to wear such things?
entries.literal: Does Rencheng mean to have them all wear them?

entries.zh: 一言可以喪邦者，斯之謂歟？
entries.en: Is this what is meant by a single word being able to ruin a state?
entries.literal: A single word may lose a state: is this what is meant?

entries.zh: 可命史官書之。」
entries.en: Have the historian record it."
entries.literal: Order the historian to write this down."

entries.zh: 又曰：「王者不降佐於蒼昊，皆拔才而用之。
entries.en: He also said, "Rulers do not receive assistants dropped down from Heaven; they select talented men and employ them.
entries.literal: He also said, "Kings do not receive assistants sent down by blue Heaven; they all select talent and use it.

entries.zh: 朕失於舉人，任許一羣婦人輩奇事，當更銓簡耳。
entries.en: I made a mistake in appointing men, allowing this strange business with a group of women. The officials must be reviewed and selected again.
entries.literal: I erred in choosing men, allowing the strange affair of a group of women. We should select and rank officials anew.

entries.zh: 任城在省，為舉天下綱維，為當署事而已？」
entries.en: Is Rencheng in the department to uphold the governing order of the realm, or merely to sign papers?"
entries.literal: Is Rencheng in the department in order to raise up the guiding ropes of all under Heaven, or merely to sign documents?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「臣實署事而已。」
entries.en: Cheng said, "In truth, I am only signing papers."
entries.literal: Cheng said, "I am indeed only signing documents."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「如此便一令史足矣，何待任城。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "If that is so, one clerk would be enough. Why would we need Rencheng?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "If it is like this, then one clerk is enough. Why wait for Rencheng?"

entries.zh: 又曰：「我遣舍人宣詔，何為使小人聞之？」
entries.en: He also said, "I sent a palace attendant to proclaim the edict. Why did you let petty men hear it?"
entries.literal: He also said, "I sent a palace attendant to proclaim the edict; why did you let petty men hear it?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「時雖有幹吏，去榜亦遠。」
entries.en: Cheng said, "At the time there were capable officials, but they too were far from the posted proclamation."
entries.literal: Cheng said, "At the time, although there were capable officials, they were also far from the proclamation board."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「遠則不聞，聞則不遠。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "If they were far away, they could not have heard it; if they heard it, they were not far away.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "If they were far away, they would not have heard; if they heard, they were not far away.

entries.zh: 既得聞詔，理故可知。」
entries.en: Since they heard the edict, they should have understood the principle."
entries.literal: Since they were able to hear the edict, the principle could certainly be known."

entries.zh: 於是留守羣臣遂免冠謝罪。
entries.en: The ministers left in charge of the capital then removed their caps and apologized for their fault.
entries.literal: Thereupon the ministers left to guard the capital all removed their caps and apologized for their offense.

entries.zh: 尋除尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 蕭寶卷遣其太尉陳顯達入寇漢陽。
entries.en: Xiao Baojuan sent his Grand Commandant Chen Xianda to invade Hanyang.
entries.literal: Xiao Baojuan sent his Grand Commandant Chen Xianda to invade Hanyang.

entries.zh: 是時高祖不豫，引澄入見清徽堂。
entries.en: At the time Gaozu was ill, and he summoned Cheng to Qinghui Hall.
entries.literal: At this time Gaozu was unwell and brought Cheng in for audience at Qinghui Hall.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「顯達侵亂，沔陽不安，朕不親行，莫攘此賊。
entries.en: The edict said, "Xianda has invaded and thrown Mianyang into disorder. Unless I go in person, no one will repel this rebel.
entries.literal: The edict said, "Xianda is invading and causing disorder, and Mianyang is not at peace. If I do not go in person, no one will drive off this rebel.

entries.zh: 朕疾患淹年，氣力惙弊，如有非常，委任城大事。
entries.en: My illness has dragged on for years, and my strength is spent. If anything unexpected happens, I entrust the great affairs to Rencheng.
entries.literal: My illness has lingered for years, and my strength and breath are exhausted. If anything extraordinary happens, I entrust great affairs to Rencheng.

entries.zh: 是段任城必須從朕。」
entries.en: For this campaign, Rencheng must accompany me."
entries.literal: On this occasion Rencheng must follow me."

entries.zh: 澄涕泣對曰：「臣謹當竭股肱之力，以命上報。」
entries.en: Cheng replied through tears, "I will devote all the strength of my limbs and repay Your Majesty with my life."
entries.literal: Cheng replied in tears, "I shall respectfully exhaust the strength of my limbs and repay Your Majesty with my life."

entries.zh: 遂從駕南伐。
entries.en: He then accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign.
entries.literal: He then followed the imperial carriage on the southern campaign.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，澄受顧命。
entries.en: When Gaozu died, Cheng received his final charge.
entries.literal: When Gaozu died, Cheng received the testamentary charge.

entries.zh: 世宗初，有降人嚴叔懋告尚書令王肅遣孔思達潛通寶卷，圖為叛逆，寶卷遣俞公喜送敕於肅，公喜還南，肅與裴叔業馬為信。
entries.en: At the start of Shizong's reign, a defector named Yan Shumao accused Wang Su, Director of the Department of State Affairs, of sending Kong Sida to communicate secretly with Baojuan and plot rebellion. Baojuan, he said, had sent Yu Gongxi with an edict for Su; after Gongxi returned south, Su and Pei Shuye exchanged horses as tokens.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign, a surrendered man, Yan Shumao, accused Wang Su, Director of the Department of State Affairs, of sending Kong Sida to communicate secretly with Baojuan and plot rebellion; Baojuan had sent Yu Gongxi to deliver an edict to Su, Gongxi had returned south, and Su and Pei Shuye had used horses as tokens.

entries.zh: 澄信之，乃表肅將叛，輒下禁止。
entries.en: Cheng believed the accusation, memorialized that Su was about to rebel, and immediately detained him.
entries.literal: Cheng believed this, and therefore memorialized that Su was about to rebel, then immediately placed him under detention.

entries.zh: 咸陽、北海二王奏澄擅禁宰輔，免官歸第。
entries.en: The princes of Xianyang and Beihai memorialized that Cheng had detained a chief minister on his own authority, and Cheng was dismissed and sent home.
entries.literal: The two princes of Xianyang and Beihai memorialized that Cheng had arbitrarily detained a chief minister; he was dismissed from office and returned to his residence.

entries.zh: 尋出為平西將軍、梁州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Liangzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 辭以母老。
entries.en: He declined because his mother was elderly.
entries.literal: He declined on the grounds that his mother was old.

entries.zh: 除安東將軍、相州刺史，復固辭。
entries.en: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xiangzhou, but again firmly refused.
entries.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xiangzhou, but again firmly declined.

entries.zh: 改授安西將軍、雍州刺史。
entries.en: His appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: The appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 尋徵赴季秋講武。
entries.en: Soon he was summoned to attend the late-autumn martial review.
entries.literal: Soon he was summoned to attend the late-autumn martial review.

entries.zh: 除都督淮南諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、開府、揚州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed Commander of all military affairs in Huainan, Grand General Who Guards the South with an open office, and Inspector of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He was appointed Commander of all military affairs in Huainan, Grand General Who Guards the South, with an open office, and Inspector of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 下車封孫叔敖之墓，毀蔣子文之廟。
entries.en: On taking office, he marked and protected Sunshu Ao's tomb and destroyed the temple of Jiang Ziwen.
entries.literal: When he arrived in office, he sealed the tomb of Sunshu Ao and destroyed the temple of Jiang Ziwen.

entries.zh: 頻表南伐，世宗不許。
entries.en: He repeatedly memorialized urging a southern campaign, but Shizong would not allow it.
entries.literal: He repeatedly memorialized in favor of a southern campaign, but Shizong did not permit it.

entries.zh: 又辭母老，乞解州任，寢而不報。
entries.en: Again citing his mother's age, he asked to be relieved of the province, but the request was shelved without response.
entries.literal: He again declined because his mother was old and begged to be relieved of his provincial office, but the request was put aside without reply.

entries.zh: 加散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: He was additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 澄表曰：「臣參訓先朝，藉規有日，前言舊軌，頗亦聞之。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized, "I took part in the instruction of the former court and have long lived under its rules; I have heard something of its words and precedents.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I took part in instruction under the former court and have long relied upon its norms; I have also heard something of former sayings and old regulations.

entries.zh: 又昔在恒代，親習皇宗，熟祕序疑庭無闕日。
entries.en: In earlier days at Heng and Dai, I was personally familiar with the imperial clan, and there was no lack of instruction, inquiry, and court discussion.
entries.literal: Moreover, in former times at Heng and Dai, I personally became familiar with the imperial clan; the schools, secret repositories, ordered inquiries, and court discussions had no days of absence.

entries.zh: 臣每於侍坐，先帝未嘗不以書典在懷，禮經為事，周旋之則，不輟於時。
entries.en: Whenever I sat in attendance, the former emperor always kept the texts and classics in mind and made the ritual classics his concern; the rules of conduct were never neglected.
entries.literal: Whenever I attended in seated audience, the former emperor never failed to keep the books and classics in mind and to make the ritual classics his business; the rules of movement and conduct were never interrupted at any time.

entries.zh: 自鳳舉中京，方隆禮教，宗室之範，每蒙委及，四門之選，負荷銓量。
entries.en: After the move to the central capital, ritual instruction flourished. Matters concerning the imperial clan's standards were often entrusted to me, and I bore responsibility for evaluating candidates for the Four Gates school.
entries.literal: Since the phoenix rose to the central capital, ritual teaching was then flourishing. The standards of the imperial clan were often entrusted to me, and in the selection for the Four Gates I bore the burden of weighing and ranking.

entries.zh: 自先皇升遐，未遑修述，學宮虛荷四門之名，宗人有闕四時之業，青衿之緒，於茲將廢。
entries.en: Since the former emperor passed away, there has been no time to restore these institutions. The school palace bears the Four Gates name in vain, the clansmen lack their seasonal studies, and the line of students is on the verge of disappearing.
entries.literal: Since the former emperor ascended afar, there has been no leisure to repair and set forth these things; the school palace emptily bears the name of the Four Gates, the clansmen lack the work of the four seasons, and the line of blue-collared students is about to be abandoned here.

entries.zh: 臣每惟其事，竊所傷懷。
entries.en: Whenever I think of this, I am privately grieved.
entries.literal: Whenever I think on this matter, it secretly grieves my heart.

entries.zh: 伏惟聖略宏遠，四方罕務，宴安之辰，於是乎在。
entries.en: I humbly think that Your Majesty's strategy is broad and far-reaching, and with few urgent affairs on the frontiers, this is the moment for secure repose.
entries.literal: I bow and consider that Your Sacred Strategy is vast and far-reaching, and there are few pressing affairs on the four sides; the time of repose and security is now.

entries.zh: 何為太平之世，而令子衿之歎興焉；
entries.en: Why, in an age of great peace, should the lament for neglected students arise?
entries.literal: Why, in an age of great peace, should the lament over the students arise?

entries.zh: 聖明之日，而使宗人之訓闕焉。
entries.en: Why, in days of sage enlightenment, should the instruction of the imperial clan be lacking?
entries.literal: In days of sage brightness, why allow the instruction of the clansmen to be lacking?

entries.zh: 愚謂可敕有司，修復皇宗之學，開闢四門之教，使將落之族，日就月將。」
entries.en: In my foolish view, the offices should be ordered to restore the imperial clan school and reopen the Four Gates instruction, so that a clan now close to decline may improve day by day and month by month."
entries.literal: In my foolish opinion, an order may be given to the proper offices to restore the school of the imperial clan and open the teaching of the Four Gates, so that the clan now about to decline may advance by day and improve by month."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「冑子崇業，自古盛典，國均之訓，無應久廢，尚書更可量宜修立。」
entries.en: The edict said, "The education of noble sons has been a great institution since antiquity, and instruction in the state schools should not long be abandoned. The Department may consider what is suitable and restore it."
entries.literal: The edict said, "For sons of nobles to honor their studies has been a grand institution since antiquity, and the instruction of the state schools should not long remain abandoned. The Department of State Affairs may again assess what is suitable and restore it."

entries.zh: 澄又表母疾解州任，不聽。
entries.en: Cheng again memorialized that his mother was ill and asked to be relieved of his province, but this was not allowed.
entries.literal: Cheng again memorialized that his mother was ill and asked to be relieved of his provincial office, but it was not permitted.

entries.zh: 蕭衍將張囂之寇陷夷陵戍，澄遣輔國將軍成興步騎赴討，大破之，復夷陵，囂之遁走。
entries.en: When Xiao Yan's general Zhang Xiaozhi captured the Yiling Garrison, Cheng sent Cheng Xing, General Who Assists the State, with infantry and cavalry to attack. Cheng Xing defeated him badly, recovered Yiling, and Xiaozhi fled.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan's general Zhang Xiaozhi attacked and captured the Yiling Garrison; Cheng sent General Who Assists the State Cheng Xing with infantry and cavalry to go and attack him, greatly defeated him, recovered Yiling, and Xiaozhi fled.

entries.zh: 又遣長風戍主奇道顯攻蕭衍陰山戍，破之，斬其戍主龍驤將軍、都亭侯梅興祖。
entries.en: He also sent Qi Daoxian, commander of Changfeng Garrison, to attack Xiao Yan's Yinshan Garrison. Qi defeated it and beheaded its commander Mei Xingzu, General Who Rouses Dragons and Marquis of Duting.
entries.literal: He also sent Qi Daoxian, commander of the Changfeng Garrison, to attack Xiao Yan's Yinshan Garrison; he defeated it and beheaded its garrison commander, Mei Xingzu, General Who Rouses Dragons and Marquis of Duting.

entries.zh: 仍引攻白槀戍，又破之，斬其寧朔將軍、關內侯吳道爽。
entries.en: He then pressed on to attack Baigao Garrison, defeated it as well, and beheaded Wu Daoshuang, General Who Pacifies the North and Marquis within the Passes.
entries.literal: He then led the attack on Baigao Garrison, again defeated it, and beheaded its General Who Pacifies the North and Marquis within the Passes, Wu Daoshuang.

entries.zh: 澄表曰：「蕭衍頻斷東關，欲令巢湖汎溢。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized, "Xiao Yan has repeatedly breached Dongguan, intending to make Chaohu overflow.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized, "Xiao Yan has repeatedly cut through Dongguan, wishing to make Chaohu overflow.

entries.zh: 湖周回四百餘里，東關合江之際，廣不過數十步，若賊計得成，大湖傾注者，則淮南諸戍必同晉陽之事矣。
entries.en: The lake is over four hundred li in circuit, and where Dongguan meets the river it is only a few dozen paces wide. If the rebels succeed and the great lake pours out, all our Huainan garrisons will suffer the fate of Jinyang.
entries.literal: The lake is more than four hundred li around. Where Dongguan joins the river, its width is no more than several tens of paces. If the rebel plan succeeds and the great lake pours out, then all the Huainan garrisons will surely share the fate of Jinyang.

entries.zh: 又吳楚便水，且灌且掠，淮南之地，將非國有。
entries.en: Moreover, Wu and Chu are skilled in water warfare. If they flood while raiding, Huainan will no longer be ours.
entries.literal: Moreover, Wu and Chu are adept at water; flooding as they plunder, the lands of Huainan will no longer belong to the state.

entries.zh: 壽陽去江五百餘里，眾庶惶惶，並懼水害。
entries.en: Shouyang lies more than five hundred li from the river, and the people are terrified, all fearing flood damage.
entries.literal: Shouyang is more than five hundred li from the river, and the masses are anxious and afraid, all fearing the harm of water.

entries.zh: 脫乘民之願，攻敵之虛，豫勒諸州，纂集士馬，首秋大集，則南瀆可為飲馬之津，霍嶺必成徙倚之觀，事貴應機，經略須早。
entries.en: If we use the people's wishes, strike the enemy's weak point, prearrange the provinces, gather troops and horses, and assemble them in early autumn, then the southern channel can become a ford for watering our horses, and Huo Ridge a height from which we look out at ease. Opportunity must be answered, and planning must begin early.
entries.literal: If we take advantage of the people's wishes and attack the enemy's emptiness, prearrange the provinces, gather soldiers and horses, and assemble them at the beginning of autumn, then the southern channel may become a ford where we water horses, and Huo Ridge will surely become a lookout where we linger. Affairs value response to opportunity, and planning must be early.

entries.zh: 縱混一不可必果，江西自是無虞。
entries.en: Even if complete unification cannot be guaranteed, the lands west of the Yangzi will at least be secure.
entries.literal: Even if complete unification cannot be certainly achieved, the west of the Yangzi will naturally be without worry.

entries.zh: 若猶豫緩圖，不加除討，關塞既成，襄陵方及，平原民戍定為魚矣。」
entries.en: If we hesitate and delay instead of eliminating the threat, then once the barriers are finished and the waters rise to the hills, the people and garrisons of the plains will become fish."
entries.literal: If we still hesitate and slowly make plans, without adding removal and punishment, once the passes and barriers are completed and the waters reach the hills, the people and garrisons of the plains will certainly become fish."

entries.zh: 詔發冀、定、瀛、相、并、濟六州二萬人，馬一千五百匹，令仲秋之中畢會淮南，并壽陽先兵三萬，委澄經略。
entries.en: An edict mobilized twenty thousand men and fifteen hundred horses from Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Ji provinces, ordering them to assemble in Huainan by mid-autumn. Together with Shouyang's existing thirty thousand troops, they were placed under Cheng's command.
entries.literal: An edict mobilized twenty thousand men and one thousand five hundred horses from the six provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Ji, ordering them all to assemble in Huainan by mid-autumn; together with Shouyang's previous thirty thousand troops, they were entrusted to Cheng for planning.

entries.zh: 先是朝議有南伐之意，以蕭寶夤為東揚州刺史據東城，陳伯之為江州刺史戍陽石，以澄總督二鎮，授之節度。
entries.en: Earlier, the court had planned a southern campaign, placing Xiao Baoyin at Dongcheng as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou and Chen Bozhi at Yangshi as Inspector of Jiangzhou. Cheng was put in overall command of the two positions.
entries.literal: Before this, the court deliberations had intended a southern campaign, appointing Xiao Baoyin Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou to occupy Dongcheng and Chen Bozhi Inspector of Jiangzhou to garrison Yangshi; Cheng was made commander-in-chief of the two garrisons and given authority over their commands.

entries.zh: 至是勒兵進討。
entries.en: At this point he ordered the troops forward.
entries.literal: At this point he ordered the troops forward to attack.

entries.zh: 以東關水衝，大峴險要，東關縱水，陽石、合肥有急懸之切，不圖大峴，則歷陽有乘險之援，淮陵陸道，九山水路，並宜經略。
entries.en: Dongguan controlled the water flow, and Daxian was a crucial pass. If Dongguan released the water, Yangshi and Hefei would be in immediate danger; if Daxian was ignored, Liyang could use the pass as support. The Huailing land route and the Jiushan water route both had to be included in the plan.
entries.literal: Because Dongguan was the water choke point and Daxian was a strategic pass, if Dongguan released water, Yangshi and Hefei would face an urgent suspended danger; if Daxian was not planned for, then Liyang would have support by using the pass. The land route through Huailing and the water route through Jiushan both had to be planned for.

entries.zh: 於是遣統軍傅豎眼、王神念等進次大峴、東關、九山、淮陵，皆分部諸將，倍道據之，總勒大眾，絡繹相接。
entries.en: He therefore sent Fu Shuyan, Wang Shennian, and other commanders to advance to Daxian, Dongguan, Jiushan, and Huailing. The generals divided the sectors, hurried to occupy them, and linked the main forces in a continuous line.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent Commanders Fu Shuyan, Wang Shennian, and others to advance and camp at Daxian, Dongguan, Jiushan, and Huailing. All divided the generals by sections, marched by double stages to occupy them, and brought the great host under command, one unit after another in continuous connection.

entries.zh: 而神念克其關要、潁川二城，斬衍軍主費尼。
entries.en: Wang Shennian captured Guanyao and Yingchuan and beheaded Fei Ni, one of Xiao Yan's commanders.
entries.literal: Shennian captured the two cities of Guanyao and Yingchuan and beheaded Xiao Yan's army commander Fei Ni.

entries.zh: 而寧朔將軍韋惠、龍驤將軍李伯由仍固大峴。
entries.en: Ning Shuo General Wei Hui and Longxiang General Li Boyou were still holding Daxian.
entries.literal: Ning Shuo General Wei Hui and Longxiang General Li Boyou still firmly held Daxian.

entries.zh: 澄遣統軍党法宗、傅豎眼等進軍克之，遂圍白塔、牽城，數日之間，便即逃潰。
entries.en: Cheng sent Dang Fazong, Fu Shuyan, and other commanders forward to take it. They then besieged Baita and Qiancheng, which fled and collapsed within a few days.
entries.literal: Cheng sent Commanders Dang Fazong, Fu Shuyan, and others to advance their armies and take it. They then surrounded Baita and Qiancheng, and within several days these immediately fled and collapsed.

entries.zh: 衍清溪戍望風散走。
entries.en: Xiao Yan's Qingxi Garrison scattered at the news.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan's Qingxi Garrison scattered and fled at the sight of their momentum.

entries.zh: 衍徐州刺史司馬明素率眾三千，欲援九山；
entries.en: Sima Mingsu, Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou, led three thousand men to reinforce Jiushan;
entries.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou Sima Mingsu led three thousand men, wishing to reinforce Jiushan;

entries.zh: 徐州長史潘伯隣規固淮陵；
entries.en: Pan Bolin, Chief Clerk of Xuzhou, planned to hold Huailing;
entries.literal: Pan Bolin, Chief Clerk of Xuzhou, planned to hold Huailing;

entries.zh: 寧朔將軍王燮負險焦城。
entries.en: and Ning Shuo General Wang Xie relied on the strong position at Jiaocheng.
entries.literal: Ning Shuo General Wang Xie relied on the defenses of Jiaocheng.

entries.zh: 法宗進克焦城，破淮陵，擒明素，斬伯隣。
entries.en: Dang Fazong advanced, captured Jiaocheng, broke Huailing, captured Mingsu, and beheaded Bolin.
entries.literal: Fazong advanced, captured Jiaocheng, broke Huailing, captured Mingsu, and beheaded Bolin.

entries.zh: 其濟陰太守王厚強、廬江太守裴邃即亦奔退。
entries.en: Wang Houqiang, their Governor of Jiyin, and Pei Sui, Governor of Lujiang, also fled.
entries.literal: Their Governor of Jiyin Wang Houqiang and Governor of Lujiang Pei Sui then also fled in retreat.

entries.zh: 詔澄曰：「將軍文德內昭，武功外暢，奮揚大略，將蕩江吳。
entries.en: The edict to Cheng said, "General, your civil virtue shines within and your military achievements resound abroad. You have displayed a grand strategy and are about to sweep away Jiang and Wu.
entries.literal: The edict to Cheng said, "General, your civil virtue shines within and your military achievement spreads without; you raise and display grand strategy and are about to sweep away Jiang and Wu.

entries.zh: 長旌始舒，賊徒懾氣，銳旅方馳，東關席卷。
entries.en: As soon as the long banners were unfurled, the rebels lost heart; as the elite troops began to advance, Dongguan was rolled up like a mat.
entries.literal: When the long banners first unfurled, the rebel followers lost heart; as the sharp troops were only beginning to race forward, Dongguan was swept up like a mat.

entries.zh: 想江湖弭波，在旦夕耳。
entries.en: I expect the rivers and lakes to be pacified very soon.
entries.literal: I expect the rivers and lakes will calm their waves in the space of morning and evening.

entries.zh: 所送首虜，並已聞之。」
entries.en: The heads and captives you sent have all been reported."
entries.literal: The heads and captives you sent have all been reported."

entries.zh: 初，澄出討之後，衍將姜慶真襲據壽春外郭，齊王蕭寶夤擊走之。
entries.en: Earlier, after Cheng had marched out, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen attacked and occupied the outer wall of Shouchun, but Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi, attacked and drove him away.
entries.literal: At first, after Cheng went out to attack, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen attacked and occupied the outer wall of Shouchun, and Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi, attacked and drove him off.

entries.zh: 長史韋纘坐免官，澄以在外無坐。
entries.en: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was dismissed for this, while Cheng was not held responsible because he was away.
entries.literal: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was dismissed from office for the offense, while Cheng, because he was away, was not implicated.

entries.zh: 遂攻鍾離。
entries.en: Cheng then attacked Zhongli.
entries.literal: He then attacked Zhongli.

entries.zh: 又詔：「鍾離若食盡，三月已前，固有可克，如至四月，淮水泛長，舟行無礙，宜善量之。
entries.en: Another edict said, "If Zhongli runs out of food, it can surely be taken before the third month; but if matters reach the fourth month, the Huai will rise and boats will pass freely. Weigh this carefully.
entries.literal: Another edict said, "If Zhongli exhausts its food, before the third month it can certainly be taken; if it reaches the fourth month, the Huai waters will rise and swell, and boats will move without obstruction. You should measure this well.

entries.zh: 前事捷也，此實將軍經略，勳有常焉。
entries.en: The earlier victory was truly due to your planning, General, and that merit stands secure.
entries.literal: The previous success was truly the result of your planning, General, and the merit has its constant place.

entries.zh: 如或以水盛難圖，亦可為萬全之計，不宜昧利無成，以貽後悔也。」
entries.en: If high water makes the objective difficult, you may choose a safer plan. Do not be blinded by advantage, fail to achieve the goal, and leave regret for later."
entries.literal: If perhaps the high water makes it difficult to plan, you may also make a plan of complete safety. It is not fitting to be blinded by advantage, achieve nothing, and leave later regret."

entries.zh: 蕭衍冠軍將軍張惠紹，游擊將軍殷暹、驍騎將軍趙景悅、龍驤將軍張景仁等率眾五千，送糧鍾離。
entries.en: Xiao Yan's generals Zhang Huishao, Yin Xian, Zhao Jingyue, Zhang Jingren, and others led five thousand men escorting grain to Zhongli.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan's General Who Conquers Champions Zhang Huishao, General of Mobile Assault Yin Xian, General of Valiant Cavalry Zhao Jingyue, Longxiang General Zhang Jingren, and others led five thousand men to send grain to Zhongli.

entries.zh: 澄遣統軍王足、劉思祖等邀擊惠紹等，大破之。
entries.en: Cheng sent Wang Zu, Liu Sizu, and other commanders to intercept Huishao and his men, defeating them badly.
entries.literal: Cheng sent Commanders Wang Zu, Liu Sizu, and others to intercept and strike Huishao and the others, greatly defeating them.

entries.zh: 獲惠紹、殷暹、景仁及其屯騎校尉史文淵等軍主以上二十七人。
entries.en: They captured Huishao, Yin Xian, Jingren, Shi Wenyuan, their Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, and twenty-seven officers of army commander rank or higher.
entries.literal: They captured Huishao, Yin Xian, Jingren, and Shi Wenyuan, their Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, along with twenty-seven men of army commander rank and above.

entries.zh: 既而遇雨，淮水暴長，引歸壽春。
entries.en: Soon afterward rain came, the Huai rose sharply, and Cheng withdrew to Shouchun.
entries.literal: Afterward, they met with rain, the Huai waters suddenly rose, and he withdrew back to Shouchun.

entries.zh: 還既狼狽，失兵四千餘人。
entries.en: The retreat became disordered, and he lost more than four thousand men.
entries.literal: Once the return had become disorderly, he lost more than four thousand soldiers.

entries.zh: 頻表解州，世宗不許。
entries.en: He repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved of his province, but Shizong refused.
entries.literal: He repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved of his province, but Shizong did not permit it.

entries.zh: 有司奏軍還失路，奪其開府，又降三階。
entries.en: The officials memorialized that the returning army had lost its route; Cheng was stripped of his open office and demoted three ranks.
entries.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that the army had lost the road on its return; his open office was taken away, and he was further lowered three ranks.

entries.zh: 時蕭衍有移，求換張惠紹。
entries.en: At the time Xiao Yan sent a letter requesting an exchange for Zhang Huishao.
entries.literal: At the time Xiao Yan had sent an official letter requesting an exchange for Zhang Huishao.

entries.zh: 澄表請不許，詔付八座會議。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized that the request should not be allowed, and the edict referred it to the Eight Seats for conference.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized requesting that this not be permitted, and an edict referred it to the Eight Seats for joint discussion.

entries.zh: 尚書令、廣陽王嘉等奏宜還之，詔乃聽還。
entries.en: Jia, Prince of Guangyang and Director of the Department of State Affairs, and others memorialized that Zhang Huishao should be returned, and the edict allowed it.
entries.literal: Director of the Department of State Affairs Jia, Prince of Guangyang, and others memorialized that he should be returned, and the edict then permitted the return.

entries.zh: 後果復寇邊。
entries.en: Later, as expected, he raided the border again.
entries.literal: Later, as expected, he again raided the border.

entries.zh: 轉澄鎮北大將軍、定州刺史。
entries.en: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
entries.literal: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 初，民中每有橫調，百姓煩苦，前後牧守，未能蠲除，澄多所省減，民以忻賴。
entries.en: The people had long suffered from arbitrary levies, which previous governors and administrators had failed to abolish. Cheng reduced many of them, and the people rejoiced and relied on him.
entries.literal: At first, whenever there were arbitrary levies among the people, the common people were troubled and suffering. The governors and administrators before and after him had not been able to remove them, but Cheng reduced many of them, and the people joyfully relied on him.

entries.zh: 又明黜陟賞罰之法，表減公園之地，以給無業貧口，禁造布絹不任衣者。
entries.en: He also clarified rules for promotion, demotion, reward, and punishment; memorialized to reduce public parkland and give it to poor households without livelihoods; and banned the production of cloth and silk unfit for clothing.
entries.literal: He also clarified the laws of demotion and promotion, reward and punishment, memorialized to reduce the land of public parks in order to give it to poor households without occupations, and prohibited the making of cloth and silk not fit for clothing.

entries.zh: 母孟太妃薨，居喪毀瘠，當世稱之。
entries.en: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, he wasted away in mourning, and his contemporaries praised him for it.
entries.literal: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, his mourning left him wasted and thin, and the age praised him.

entries.zh: 服闋，除太子太保。
entries.en: After the mourning period ended, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When the mourning period was complete, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 於時高肇當朝，猜忌賢戚。
entries.en: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious of worthy imperial relatives.
entries.literal: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious and jealous of worthy imperial relatives.

entries.zh: 澄為肇間構，常恐不全，乃終日昏飲，以示荒敗。
entries.en: Cheng was slandered and isolated by Gao Zhao and constantly feared for his life, so he drank heavily all day to appear ruined and useless.
entries.literal: Cheng was estranged and framed by Zhao, and constantly feared he would not be preserved; he therefore drank muddily all day to show ruin and failure.

entries.zh: 所作詭越，時謂為狂。
entries.en: His strange, excessive behavior was taken at the time for madness.
entries.literal: The strange and excessive things he did were called madness at the time.

entries.zh: 世宗夜崩，時事倉卒，高肇擁兵於外，肅宗沖幼，朝野不安。
entries.en: When Shizong died at night, events were sudden and confused. Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was still a child, and both court and countryside were uneasy.
entries.literal: Shizong died at night, events were urgent and confused, Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was young, and court and countryside were unsettled.

entries.zh: 澄疏斥不預機要，而朝望所屬，領軍于忠、侍中崔光等奏澄為尚書令，於是眾心忻服。
entries.en: Cheng had been kept at a distance and excluded from confidential affairs, but the court's hopes rested on him. Yu Zhong, Commander of the Guards, Cui Guang, Palace Attendant, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and everyone gladly accepted this.
entries.literal: Cheng had been distantly rejected and did not take part in the essentials of policy, yet the hopes of the court rested on him. Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong, Palace Attendant Cui Guang, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and at this the hearts of the multitude joyfully submitted.

entries.zh: 又加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍，尋遷司空，加侍中，俄詔領尚書令。
entries.en: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was promoted to Minister of Works with the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward was ordered to concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was transferred to Minister of Works and given the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward an edict had him concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 初，正始之末，詔百司普昇一級，而執事者不達旨意，刺史、守、令限而不及。
entries.en: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict raised all offices by one grade, but the officials implementing it misunderstood the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were excluded.
entries.literal: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict had raised all the offices by one grade, but those handling the matter did not understand the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were limited and did not receive it.

entries.zh: 澄奏曰：「竊惟雲構鬱起，澤及百司，企春望榮，內外同慶。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized, "I humbly think that when imperial favor rose like gathering clouds and reached the hundred offices, officials inside and outside the court looked toward renewed honor and rejoiced together.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I privately consider that the cloud-built grace rose richly and its favor reached the hundred offices; looking toward spring and hoping for glory, inner and outer officials celebrated together.

entries.zh: 至於賞陟，不及守宰，爾來十年，冤訟不絕。
entries.en: Yet the promotion did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years grievances and appeals have continued without end.
entries.literal: But when it came to rewarding advancement, it did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years since then grievances and lawsuits have not ceased.

entries.zh: 封回自鎮遠、安州入為太尉長史，元匡自征虜、恒州入作宗卿，二人遷授，並在先詔。
entries.en: Feng Hui came in from Zhenyuan General and Anzhou to serve as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, while Yuan Kuang came in from Zhenglu General and Hengzhou to serve as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. Both appointments occurred before the earlier edict.
entries.literal: Feng Hui entered from General Who Guards Afar and Anzhou to become Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant; Yuan Kuang entered from General Who Conquers Caitiffs and Hengzhou to become Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. The promotions and appointments of these two men were both before the earlier edict.

entries.zh: 應蒙之理，備在於斯。
entries.en: These cases fully show the principle by which they should receive the benefit.
entries.literal: The principle that they should receive the benefit is fully present in these cases.

entries.zh: 兼州佐停私之徒，陪臣郡丞之例，尚蒙天澤下降，榮及當時。
entries.en: Moreover, provincial assistants, private retainers who had ceased service, subordinate officers, and commandery deputies all received the court's favor and shared in the honor at the time.
entries.literal: In addition, provincial assistants, those who had suspended private service, subordinate ministers, and commandery deputies still received the descent of heavenly favor, and the honor reached them at the time.

entries.zh: 然參佐之來，皆因府主，今府主不霑，佐官獨預，棄本賞末，愚謂未允。
entries.en: But assistants come forward through their chiefs. For the chiefs to receive nothing while their subordinates alone benefit abandons the root and rewards the branch; in my foolish view this is not just.
entries.literal: Yet assistants come in all because of their office heads. Now the office heads do not receive the favor, while assistant officials alone participate; abandoning the root and rewarding the branch, in my foolish opinion, is not fair.

entries.zh: 今計刺史、守、宰之官，請準回匡，悉同汎限，上允初旨百司之章，下覆訟者元元之心。」
entries.en: I therefore ask that inspectors, governors, and magistrates be treated according to the precedents of Feng Hui and Yuan Kuang and included within the general scope, above fulfilling the original edict's words about the hundred offices, and below satisfying the hearts of the people who have appealed."
entries.literal: Now, calculating the offices of inspectors, governors, and magistrates, I request that they be modeled on Hui and Kuang and all be included within the general limit, above fulfilling the original edict's phrase "the hundred offices," and below answering the hearts of the common people who have appealed."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「自今已後，內外之事，嘗經先朝者，不得重聞。」
entries.en: The edict said, "From now on, internal and external matters already handled under the former reign may not be reported again."
entries.literal: The edict said, "From now on, matters inside and outside the court that once passed through the former reign may not be reported again."

entries.zh: 澄奏曰：「臣聞堯懸諫諍之鼓，舜置誹謗之木，皆所以廣耳目於芻蕘，達四聰於天下。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung up the remonstrance drum and Shun set up the criticism post, both to widen their hearing and sight among even the humblest people and let the ruler's fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung the drum for remonstrance and Shun set up the wood for criticism; both were means to broaden ears and eyes among woodcutters and herdsmen and make the fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 伏惟太祖開基，化隆自遠，累聖相承，於今九帝。
entries.en: Taizu founded the dynasty and his transforming rule spread far. Sage rulers have succeeded one another, down to the ninth emperor today.
entries.literal: I bow and consider that Taizu opened the foundation and his transformation flourished from afar; successive sages have inherited one another, now reaching nine emperors.

entries.zh: 重光疊照，汚隆必同，與奪隨時，道無恒體。
entries.en: Their radiance has shone one after another; whether in decline or flourishing, the principle is the same. Granting and withholding follow the times, and the Way has no fixed form.
entries.literal: Repeated radiance and layered illumination, decline and flourishing must all be the same; granting and taking follow the time, and the Way has no constant form.

entries.zh: 思過如渴，言重千金，故稱無諱之朝，邁蹤三、五。
entries.en: They thirsted for reflection on their faults and valued speech at a thousand pieces of gold; thus ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.
entries.literal: They thirsted to think on faults and valued words at a thousand in gold; therefore ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the tracks of the Three and Five.

entries.zh: 高祖沖年纂曆，文明協統，變官易律，未為違典。
entries.en: Gaozu inherited the throne while young, and Empress Wenming assisted the government. They changed offices and laws, yet did not violate classical norms.
entries.literal: Gaozu succeeded to the calendar at a tender age, and Wenming cooperated in rule; they changed offices and altered laws, but this did not violate the classics.

entries.zh: 及慈聖臨朝，母儀宇縣，爰發慈令，垂心滯獄，深枉者仰日月於九泉，微屈者希曲照於盆下。
entries.en: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal example covered the realm. She issued merciful orders and attended to stalled cases, so the deeply wronged looked up to sun and moon even from the Nine Springs, and the slightly aggrieved hoped for a slant of light beneath the overturned basin.
entries.literal: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal model covered the realm; she then issued compassionate orders and set her heart on delayed lawsuits, so those deeply wronged looked up to the sun and moon from the Nine Springs, and those slightly aggrieved hoped for a bent light beneath the overturned basin.

entries.zh: 今乃格以先朝，限以一例，斯誠奉遵之本心，實乖元元之至望。
entries.en: Now to block such cases as belonging to the former reign and limit them by one rule may be meant as obedience, but it truly violates the people's deepest hopes.
entries.literal: Now to bar them by saying "the former reign" and limit them by a single rule truly follows the root intention of obedience, but in fact goes against the utmost hopes of the common people.

entries.zh: 在于謙挹，有乖舊典。
entries.en: As a matter of humble receptiveness, it also departs from the old institutions.
entries.literal: In humility and yielding, it departs from the old institutions.

entries.zh: 謹尋抱枉求直，或經累朝。
entries.en: I have examined those who carry grievances and seek justice; some cases have lasted through several reigns.
entries.literal: I have carefully examined those who hold grievances and seek straightening; some have passed through several reigns.

entries.zh: 毫釐之差，正之宜速；
entries.en: A difference of a hair's breadth should be corrected quickly;
entries.literal: A difference of a hair or a li should be corrected quickly;

entries.zh: 謬若千里，駟馬弗追。
entries.en: if an error becomes a thousand li, even a four-horse team cannot catch it.
entries.literal: if the error is like a thousand li, even a team of four horses cannot catch it.

entries.zh: 故禮有損益，事有可否，父有諍子，君有諫臣，琴瑟不調，理宜改作。
entries.en: Thus ritual can be reduced or augmented, affairs can be approved or rejected, fathers have sons who argue with them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate. If zithers and lutes are out of tune, they should be adjusted.
entries.literal: Therefore ritual has diminutions and additions, affairs have what may and may not be done, fathers have sons who contest them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate with them. If zithers and lutes are not in tune, principle says they should be adjusted.

entries.zh: 是以防川之論，小決則通；
entries.en: Thus, in the argument over blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;
entries.literal: Thus in the argument about blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;

entries.zh: 鄉校之言，擁則敗國。
entries.en: and as for speech in the village schools, blocking it ruins the state.
entries.literal: as for speech in the village schools, if it is blocked, it ruins the state.

entries.zh: 矧伊陳屈，而可抑以先朝。
entries.en: How much more when people are presenting grievances: how can they be suppressed merely because they concern a former reign?
entries.literal: How much more when they are setting forth grievances: how can they be suppressed by saying "the former reign"?

entries.zh: 且先朝屈者，非故屈之，或有司愛憎，或執事濁僻，空文致法，以誤視聽。
entries.en: Those wronged under the former reign were not wronged deliberately by the throne. Sometimes officials were moved by favoritism or hatred, sometimes clerks were corrupt and biased, and empty paperwork produced legal judgments that misled the court.
entries.literal: Moreover, those wronged under the former reign were not intentionally wronged. Sometimes there was love or hatred by the offices, sometimes murky partiality among those handling matters, and empty documents brought about law, thereby misleading hearing and sight.

entries.zh: 如此冤塞，彌在可哀。
entries.en: Such obstructed grievances are all the more pitiful.
entries.literal: Such blocked grievances are all the more worthy of pity.

entries.zh: 僭之與濫，寧失不經，乞收今旨，還依前詔。」
entries.en: If there is risk of excess, I would rather err on the side of irregular openness. I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to the previous edict."
entries.literal: As for overstepping and excess, I would rather err on the side of irregularity; I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to following the previous edict."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「省奏，深體毗贊之情，三皇異軌，五代殊風，一時之制，何必詮改。
entries.en: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand your wish to assist the throne. The Three Sovereigns followed different paths and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one period all be revised?
entries.literal: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand the feeling of assisting and supporting. The Three Sovereigns had different tracks and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one time all be weighed and changed?

entries.zh: 必謂虛文設旨，理在可申者，何容不同來執。
entries.en: If one says that formal texts merely express an intention and that the principle may be extended, then how could similar cases not all come forward to be taken up?
entries.literal: If it is necessarily said that empty texts set forth intentions and that the principle lies in what can be extended, how could we allow them not all to come and be taken up alike?

entries.zh: 可依往制。」
entries.en: Let the former system be followed."
entries.literal: It may follow the former system."

entries.zh: 澄表上皇誥宗制并訓詁各一卷，意欲皇太后覽之，思勸戒之益。
entries.en: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, hoping the Empress Dowager would read them and consider their value for admonition.
entries.literal: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, intending that the Empress Dowager read them and consider their benefit for exhortation and warning.

entries.zh: 又奏利國濟民所宜振舉者十條。
entries.en: He also submitted ten recommendations for measures that should be revived to benefit the state and aid the people.
entries.literal: He also memorialized ten articles on what should be revived and promoted to benefit the state and aid the people.

entries.zh: 一曰律度量衡，公私不同，所宜一之。
entries.en: First: statutes, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use and should be unified.
entries.literal: The first said: laws, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use; they should be unified.

entries.zh: 二曰宜興學校，以明黜陟之法。
entries.en: Second: schools should be promoted to clarify the rules for demotion and promotion.
entries.literal: The second said: schools should be promoted in order to clarify the law of demotion and promotion.

entries.zh: 三曰宜興滅繼絕，各舉所知。
entries.en: Third: fallen lines should be revived and extinct lines continued, with each official recommending those he knows.
entries.literal: The third said: what has perished should be revived and extinct lines continued, and each should recommend those he knows.

entries.zh: 四曰五調之外，一不煩民，任民之力，不過三日。
entries.en: Fourth: beyond the five regular levies, the people should not be burdened, and labor service should not exceed three days.
entries.literal: The fourth said: beyond the five levies, the people should not be troubled at all, and use of the people's labor should not exceed three days.

entries.zh: 五曰臨民之官，皆須黜陟，以旌賞罰。
entries.en: Fifth: officials who govern the people must be subject to promotion and demotion, so that reward and punishment are clear.
entries.literal: The fifth said: officials who govern the people must all be demoted or promoted in order to make rewards and punishments clear.

entries.zh: 六曰逃亡代輸，去來年久者，若非伎作，任聽即住。
entries.en: Sixth: fugitives whose obligations are being paid by substitutes, and whose absence or return has lasted for years, should be allowed to settle where they are, unless they are registered artisans.
entries.literal: The sixth said: for fugitives whose dues are paid by substitutes, and whose coming and going has lasted many years, if they are not artisans, they should be freely allowed to settle where they are.

entries.zh: 七曰邊兵逃走，或實陷沒，皆須精檢；
entries.en: Seventh: cases of border soldiers who flee, or who have truly been captured or killed, must be carefully investigated;
entries.literal: The seventh said: border soldiers who flee, or who in fact have fallen or been lost, must all be carefully examined;

entries.zh: 三長及近親，若實隱之，徵其代輸，不隱勿論。
