entries.en: if the three chiefs or close relatives truly concealed the facts, collect the substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal them, do not prosecute.
entries.literal: if the three chiefs and close kin have truly concealed it, collect substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal it, do not prosecute them.

entries.zh: 八曰工商世業之戶，復徵租調，無以堪濟，今請免之，使專其業。
entries.en: Eighth: hereditary artisan and merchant households are again being charged rents and levies beyond what they can bear. I request that they be exempted so they can concentrate on their work.
entries.literal: The eighth said: households whose hereditary occupations are crafts and commerce are again being charged rents and levies and have no means to endure and meet them. I now request that they be exempted, so that they may specialize in their occupations.

entries.zh: 九曰三長禁姦，不得隔越相領，戶不滿者，隨近并合。
entries.en: Ninth: the three chiefs, in suppressing crime, should not command across boundaries; where there are too few households, they should be merged with nearby units.
entries.literal: The ninth said: the three chiefs, in preventing wrongdoing, may not cross boundaries to command one another; where households are insufficient, they should be merged with nearby units.

entries.zh: 十曰羽林虎賁，邊方有事，暫可赴戰，常戍宜遣蕃兵代之。
entries.en: Tenth: the Yulin and Huben guards may be sent temporarily to fight when there is trouble on the frontier, but regular garrison duty should be assigned to tribal troops in their place.
entries.literal: The tenth said: the Yulin and Huben guards may temporarily go to war when there are affairs on the frontier, but for regular garrison duty tribal troops should be sent to replace them.

entries.zh: 靈太后下其奏，百僚議之，事有同否。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Ling sent his memorial down for discussion by the officials, who agreed on some points and disagreed on others.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent down his memorial for the hundred officials to discuss, and in the matters there were agreements and disagreements.

entries.zh: 時四中郎將兵數寡弱，不足以襟帶京師，澄奏宜以東中帶滎陽郡，南中帶魯陽郡，西中帶恒農郡，北中帶河內郡，選二品、三品親賢兼稱者居之，省非急之作，配以強兵，如此則深根固本、強幹弱枝之義也。
entries.en: At the time the four Central Gentleman-General commands had too few weak troops to protect the capital. Cheng proposed that the Eastern Center be linked with Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center with Luyang, the Western Center with Hengnong, and the Northern Center with Henei; that qualified close and worthy men of the second and third ranks be chosen to hold them; that nonurgent works be reduced; and that strong troops be assigned. This, he said, would deepen the roots, strengthen the base, strengthen the trunk, and weaken the branches.
entries.literal: At the time the troops of the four Gentlemen Generals of the Center were few and weak, insufficient to belt and protect the capital. Cheng memorialized that the Eastern Center should take in Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center Luyang Commandery, the Western Center Hengnong Commandery, and the Northern Center Henei Commandery; that men of the second and third ranks who were close, worthy, and qualified should be selected to occupy them; that nonurgent works should be eliminated; and that strong troops should be assigned. In this way, he said, lay the meaning of deepening the roots and strengthening the foundation, strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.

entries.zh: 靈太后初將從之，後議者不同，乃止。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Ling initially intended to follow the proposal, but later the discussants disagreed, so it was dropped.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Ling at first was about to follow this, but later the discussants disagreed, and so it was stopped.

entries.zh: 澄又重奏曰：「固本宜強，防微在豫，故雖有文事，不忘武功。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized again, "To secure the root, it must be strengthened; to guard against small dangers, one must prepare in advance. Thus even in civil affairs, military power is not forgotten.
entries.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "To secure the root it should be strengthened, and prevention of the slight lies in preparation; therefore, even when there are civil affairs, military achievement is not forgotten.

entries.zh: 況今南蠻仍獷，北妖頻結，來事難圖，勢同往變。
entries.en: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and northern enemies repeatedly combine. Future events are hard to foresee, and the situation resembles past upheavals.
entries.literal: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and the northern demons repeatedly form alliances; future events are difficult to plan for, and the situation is the same as past disturbances.

entries.zh: 脫暴勃忽起，振動關畿，四府羸卒，何以防擬。
entries.en: If a sudden uprising breaks out and shakes the passes and capital region, how can the weak troops of the four offices defend against it?
entries.literal: If sudden violence abruptly arises and shakes the passes and capital region, with the weak soldiers of the four offices, how will we defend and prepare?

entries.zh: 平康之世，可以寄安，遺之久長，恐非善策。
entries.en: In peaceful times one may rely on security, but to leave matters this way for long is not good policy.
entries.literal: In an age of peace and health, we may entrust ourselves to security, but to leave it so for a long time, I fear, is not a good plan.

entries.zh: 如臣愚見，郎將領兵，兼總民職，省官實祿，於是乎在。
entries.en: In my foolish view, the Gentleman Generals should command troops while also overseeing civil duties; this is where offices can be reduced while real salaries are preserved.
entries.literal: In my foolish view, that the Gentleman Generals command troops while also overseeing civil duties, and that offices be reduced while real salaries remain, lies precisely here.

entries.zh: 求還依前增兵益號，將位既重，則念報亦深，軍郡相依，則表裏俱濟，朝廷無四顧之憂，姦宄絕窺覦之望矣。」
entries.en: I ask that we return to the earlier plan of increasing troops and strengthening the titles. If the generals' posts are weighty, their sense of obligation will deepen; if army and commandery depend on one another, inner and outer defenses will both be supplied. The court will have no worries on any side, and criminals will lose hope of taking advantage."
entries.literal: I ask that we return to the former system of increasing troops and augmenting titles. Once the generals' positions are weighty, their thought of repaying the state will also be deep; when army and commandery rely on each other, inside and outside will both be aided, the court will have no worries on four sides, and criminals will lose any hope of peering in."

entries.zh: 卒不納。
entries.en: In the end the proposal was not accepted.
entries.literal: In the end it was not accepted.

entries.zh: 又以流人初至遠鎮，衣食無資，多有死者，奏并其妻子給糧一歲，從之。
entries.en: He also noted that exiles newly sent to distant garrisons lacked clothing and food and often died, so he memorialized that they and their families be given a year's grain. This was approved.
entries.literal: He also, because exiles newly arrived at distant garrisons had no resources for clothing and food and many died, memorialized that they, together with their wives and children, be given grain for one year, and this was followed.

entries.zh: 尋以疾患，求解任，不許。
entries.en: Soon afterward he asked to be relieved because of illness, but this was not allowed.
entries.literal: Soon, because of illness, he requested to be relieved of office, but it was not permitted.

entries.zh: 蕭衍於浮山斷淮為堰，以灌壽春，乃除使持節、大將軍、大都督、南討諸軍事，勒眾十萬，將出彭宋，尋淮堰自壞，不行。
entries.en: When Xiao Yan dammed the Huai at Fushan to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, and Grand Commander of the southern campaign armies, with orders to lead one hundred thousand men out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam collapsed on its own, and the campaign did not proceed.
entries.literal: When Xiao Yan, at Fushan, cut off the Huai to make a dam in order to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Grand Commander of all armies for the southern campaign, and ordered to command one hundred thousand men and prepare to go out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam broke by itself, and he did not proceed.

entries.zh: 澄以北邊鎮將選舉彌輕，恐賊虜闚邊，山陵危迫，奏求重鎮將之選，修警備之嚴，詔不從。
entries.en: Cheng believed that commanders for the northern frontier garrisons were being chosen too lightly. Fearing that raiders would threaten the border and endanger the imperial tombs, he memorialized asking that garrison commanders be selected more carefully and defenses tightened, but the edict did not accept this.
entries.literal: Because Cheng considered the selection of commanders for the northern frontier garrisons increasingly slight, and feared that rebel captives would peer at the border and the imperial tombs would be endangered, he memorialized requesting that selection of garrison commanders be made weightier and the strictness of warning and defense be repaired, but the edict did not follow it.

entries.zh: 賊虜入寇，至於舊都，鎮將多非其人，所在叛亂，犯逼山陵，如澄所慮。
entries.en: When the raiders entered and reached the old capital, many garrison commanders proved unfit, rebellions broke out in many places, and the imperial tombs were threatened, exactly as Cheng had feared.
entries.literal: When rebel captives entered and raided, reaching the old capital, many garrison commanders were not the right men, rebellions broke out everywhere, and they violated and pressed upon the imperial tombs, just as Cheng had feared.

entries.zh: 澄奏都城府寺猶未周悉，今軍旅初寧，無宜發眾，請取諸職人及司州郡縣犯十杖已上百鞭已下收贖之物，絹一匹，輸磚二百，以漸修造。
entries.en: Cheng memorialized that the capital's offices and temples were still incomplete, but since the armies had only just settled, the people should not be mobilized. He asked instead to use office laborers and the redemption payments for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes to one hundred lashes: each bolt of silk would be commuted to two hundred bricks, so construction could proceed gradually.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized that the offices and temples of the capital city were still not complete; now that military affairs had just become quiet, it was not fitting to mobilize the masses. He requested that they take from various office workers and from the ransom goods paid for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes or more and one hundred lashes or less: for one bolt of silk, two hundred bricks should be delivered, gradually to carry out construction.

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The edict approved this.
entries.literal: The edict followed this.

entries.zh: 太傅、清河王懌表奏其事，遂寢不行。
entries.en: The Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, submitted a memorial about the matter, and it was shelved without being carried out.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Yi, Prince of Qinghe, memorialized on the matter, and it was then set aside and not carried out.

entries.zh: 澄又奏曰：「臣聞賞必以道，用防淫人之姦；
entries.en: Cheng also memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must follow the Way, to guard against the schemes of corrupt men;
entries.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must accord with the Way, to guard against the wickedness of excessive men;

entries.zh: 罰不濫及，以戒良士之困。
entries.en: punishments must not be indiscriminate, lest good men be driven into distress.
entries.literal: punishments must not reach indiscriminately, in order to warn against the distress of good men.

entries.zh: 刑者，侀也。
entries.en: Punishment is a matter of setting a model.
entries.literal: Punishment means modeling.

entries.zh: 每垂三宥，秉律執請，不得已而用之。
entries.en: One should always extend the three pardons, and only when the law is upheld and the request cannot be granted should punishment be used.
entries.literal: One always extends the three pardons, and only when holding the law and presenting the request leaves no alternative is it used.

entries.zh: 是故小大之獄，察之以情，一人呼嗟，或虧王道。
entries.en: Thus in cases great and small, one examines the circumstances; even one person crying out in grievance can diminish the kingly Way.
entries.literal: Therefore, in prisons small and great, cases are examined according to feeling; if one person cries out in sorrow, it may diminish the kingly Way.

entries.zh: 刑罰得失，乃興廢之所由也。
entries.en: The success or failure of punishments is the source of a state's rise or decline.
entries.literal: The success and failure of punishments are the route by which states rise or fall.

entries.zh: 竊聞司州牧、高陽王臣雍栲殺奉朝請韓元昭、前門下錄事姚敬賢，雖因公事，理實未盡。
entries.en: I have heard privately that Yuan Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, the facts were not fully investigated.
entries.literal: I have privately heard that Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, in principle the facts were not exhausted.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why do I say this?
entries.literal: Why is this?

entries.zh: 太平之世，草不橫伐，行葦之感，事驗隆周。
entries.en: In an age of great peace, even grasses are not wantonly cut; the compassion shown in "Walking among the Reeds" was proven in the flourishing Zhou.
entries.literal: In an age of great peace, even grass is not cut sideways; the feeling of "walking among the reeds" was verified in the flourishing Zhou.

entries.zh: 若昭等狀彰，死罪以定，應刑於都市，與眾棄之；
entries.en: If the crimes of Yuanzhao and the others were clear and death sentences certain, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast out before the crowd;
entries.literal: If the circumstances of Zhao and the others were manifest and the capital crime fixed, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast away with the crowd;

entries.zh: 如其疑似不分，情理未究，不宜以三清九流之官杖下便死，輕絕民命，傷理敗法。
entries.en: if the suspicions had not been distinguished and the facts had not been fully examined, officials of their rank should not have died under the cudgel, their lives lightly cut off in a way that injured principle and ruined law.
entries.literal: if suspicion and likeness were not distinguished and the facts and principle not fully examined, it was not fitting for officials of pure rank and regular service to die beneath the staff, lightly cutting off the people's lives and injuring principle and ruining law.

entries.zh: 往年州於大市鞭殺五人，及檢贓狀，全無寸尺。
entries.en: In a previous year the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the alleged stolen goods were investigated there was not the slightest evidence.
entries.literal: In a previous year, the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the circumstances of stolen goods were inspected, there was not even an inch or foot of evidence.

entries.zh: 今復酷害，一至於此。
entries.en: Now its cruelty has once again gone this far.
entries.literal: Now again cruel harm has once reached this point.

entries.zh: 朝野云云，咸懷驚愕。
entries.en: Court and countryside are talking, and everyone is shocked.
entries.literal: Court and countryside are full of talk, and all harbor shock and alarm.

entries.zh: 若殺生在下，虐專於臣，人君之權，安所復用。
entries.en: If life and death lie in the hands of subordinates and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, what use remains for the ruler's authority?
entries.literal: If killing and giving life are in those below, and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, where can the ruler's authority be used again?

entries.zh: 自開古以來，明明之世，未聞斯比也。
entries.en: Since antiquity began, in bright and enlightened ages, I have never heard of such a thing.
entries.literal: From the opening of antiquity onward, in clear and enlightened ages, I have never heard of anything like this.

entries.zh: 武王曰：『吾不以一人之命而易天下。』
entries.en: King Wu said, "I would not trade one man's life for all under Heaven."
entries.literal: King Wu said, "I would not exchange all under Heaven for the life of one man."

entries.zh: 蓋重民命也。
entries.en: This was because he valued human life.
entries.literal: This was because he valued the people's lives.

entries.zh: 請以見事付廷尉推究，驗其為劫之狀，察其栲殺之理，使是非分明，幽魂獲雪。」
entries.en: I request that the case be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement to investigate, verify the alleged robbery, and examine the grounds for the torture-killings, so that right and wrong become clear and the dead may be vindicated."
entries.literal: I request that the present matter be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement for investigation, to verify the circumstances of their robbery and examine the principle of the torture-killings, so that right and wrong may be made clear and the hidden souls may obtain exoneration."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The edict approved this.
entries.literal: The edict followed this.

entries.zh: 澄當官而行，無所回避。
entries.en: Cheng acted according to his office and avoided nothing.
entries.literal: Cheng acted according to his office and had nothing from which he turned aside or avoided.

entries.zh: 又奏墾田授受之制八條，甚有綱貫，大便於時。
entries.en: He also memorialized eight provisions on the system for allotting reclaimed fields. They were orderly and coherent, and greatly suited the needs of the time.
entries.literal: He also memorialized eight articles on the system for granting and receiving cultivated fields; they had much order and coherence and were greatly convenient at the time.

entries.zh: 前來尚書文簿，諸曹須，則出借。
entries.en: Previously, when the various bureaus needed documents and registers from the Department of State Affairs, the records were lent out.
entries.literal: Previously, when documents and registers of the Department of State Affairs were needed by the various bureaus, they were lent out.

entries.zh: 時公車署以理冤事重。
entries.en: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages regarded the handling of grievance cases as important.
entries.literal: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages considered the handling of grievance cases important.

entries.zh: 奏請真案。
entries.en: It memorialized requesting the original case files.
entries.literal: It memorialized requesting the original case files.

entries.zh: 澄執奏以尚書政本，特宜遠慎，故凡所奏事，閣道通之，蓋以祕要之切，防其宣露，寧有古制所重，今反輕之，內猶設禁，外更寬也。
entries.en: Cheng insisted in a memorial that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and had to be handled with special caution. All memorialized matters were transmitted through the palace galleries precisely because secrecy was urgent and disclosure had to be prevented. How could something the ancient system treated as weighty now be treated lightly, keeping restrictions inside while loosening them outside?
entries.literal: Cheng firmly memorialized that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and especially should be treated with far-reaching caution; therefore, all memorialized affairs were transmitted through the gallery passage, precisely because of the urgent importance of secrecy and to guard against their being disclosed. How could something valued by the ancient system now instead be treated lightly, with prohibitions still set inside while outside they were made even looser?

entries.zh: 宜繕寫事意，以付公車。
entries.en: The substance of the case should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.
entries.literal: The meaning of the matter should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。
entries.en: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.
entries.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.

entries.zh: 彝兄順，字子和。
entries.en: Yi's elder brother Shun was styled Zihe.
entries.literal: Yi's elder brother Shun was styled Zihe.

entries.zh: 九歲師事樂安陳豐，初書王羲之小學篇數千言，晝夜誦之，旬有五日，一皆通徹。
entries.en: At nine, he studied with Chen Feng of Le'an. He first copied several thousand words of Wang Xizhi's Elementary Primer, reciting it day and night, and in fifteen days he had mastered it all.
entries.literal: At nine, he studied under Chen Feng of Le'an. At first he copied several thousand words of Wang Xizhi's Elementary Primer and recited it day and night; in fifteen days he had understood it all.

entries.zh: 豐奇之，白澄曰：「豐十五從師，迄于白首，耳目所經，未見此比，江夏黃童，不得無雙也。」
entries.en: Feng marveled and told Cheng, "I have studied with teachers from the age of fifteen to white-haired old age, and never in all I have seen or heard have I met his equal. The yellow-haired prodigy of Jiangxia cannot be peerless after all."
entries.literal: Feng marveled at him and told Cheng, "I followed teachers from fifteen until white hair, and in all that my ears and eyes have passed through, I have never seen his like. The yellow-haired boy of Jiangxia cannot be without a match."

entries.zh: 澄笑曰：「藍田生玉，何容不爾。」
entries.en: Cheng smiled. "Lantian produces jade; how could it be otherwise?"
entries.literal: Cheng smiled and said, "Lantian produces jade; how could it not be so?"

entries.zh: 十六，通杜氏春秋，恒集門生，討論同異。
entries.en: At sixteen he mastered Master Du's Spring and Autumn and often gathered students to debate points of agreement and difference.
entries.literal: At sixteen he understood Master Du's Spring and Autumn, and he constantly gathered students to discuss agreements and differences.

entries.zh: 于時四方無事，國富民康，豪貴子弟，率以朋遊為樂，而順下帷讀書，篤志愛古。
entries.en: At the time the frontiers were quiet, the state was rich, and the people were at peace. The sons of the powerful generally amused themselves with companions, but Shun shut himself behind the curtain to read, devoted to antiquity.
entries.literal: At the time there were no affairs on the four sides, the state was wealthy and the people at ease, and the sons of the powerful and noble generally took pleasure in companionable excursions; but Shun lowered the curtain and read, firmly intent on loving antiquity.

entries.zh: 性謇諤，淡於榮利，好飲酒，解鼓琴，能長吟永歎，吒詠虛室。
entries.en: He was naturally blunt, indifferent to honor and profit, fond of wine, and skilled at the zither; he could chant at length, sigh deeply, and sing out in an empty room.
entries.literal: By nature he was blunt in remonstrance, indifferent to glory and profit, fond of drinking wine, understood playing the zither, and could chant long and sigh deeply, crying out and singing in an empty room.

entries.zh: 世宗時，上魏頌，文多不載。
entries.en: During Shizong's reign he submitted a Eulogy of Wei, though much of the text is not preserved.
entries.literal: In Shizong's time, he submitted a Eulogy of Wei; much of the text is not recorded.

entries.zh: 起家為給事中。
entries.en: He began his career as Supervising Attendant.
entries.literal: He began his career as Supervising Attendant.

entries.zh: 時尚書令高肇，帝舅權重，天下人士，望塵拜伏。
entries.en: At the time Gao Zhao, Director of the Department and the emperor's maternal uncle, held immense power; men throughout the realm bowed before even the dust of his carriage.
entries.literal: At the time Gao Zhao, Director of the Department of State Affairs, was the emperor's maternal uncle, and his power was weighty; men of the realm bowed and prostrated themselves at the sight of his dust.

entries.zh: 順曾懷刺詣肇門，門者以其年少，答云「在坐大有貴客」，不肯為通。
entries.en: Shun once brought a calling card to Zhao's gate. Seeing his youth, the gatekeeper answered, "There are many great guests seated inside," and refused to announce him.
entries.literal: Shun once carried a calling card to Zhao's gate, but the gatekeeper, because he was young, replied, "Inside there are many honored guests seated," and refused to announce him.

entries.zh: 順叱之曰：「任城王兒，可是賤也！」
entries.en: Shun scolded him: "Can the son of the Prince of Rencheng be someone base?"
entries.literal: Shun rebuked him, saying, "Can the son of the Prince of Rencheng be base?"

entries.zh: 及見，直往登牀，捧手抗禮，王公先達，莫不怪慴，而順辭吐傲然，若無所覩。
entries.en: When admitted, he went straight to the couch, mounted it, clasped his hands, and greeted Zhao as an equal. Princes, dukes, and elder worthies were all startled and awed, while Shun spoke proudly as if no one else were there.
entries.literal: When he was received, he went straight forward and climbed onto the couch, held up his hands, and performed equal courtesy; the princes, dukes, and senior worthies all marveled and were awed, yet Shun's words and expression were proud, as though he saw no one.

entries.zh: 肇謂眾賓曰：「此兒豪氣尚爾，況其父乎！」
entries.en: Zhao told his guests, "If the boy's spirit is already like this, how much more his father!"
entries.literal: Zhao told the assembled guests, "This boy's heroic spirit is already like this; how much more his father!"

entries.zh: 及出，肇加敬送之。
entries.en: When Shun left, Zhao treated him with added respect and saw him off.
entries.literal: When he went out, Zhao showed added respect and saw him off.

entries.zh: 澄聞之，大怒，杖之數十。
entries.en: When Cheng heard of this, he was furious and had him caned several dozen strokes.
entries.literal: When Cheng heard of it, he was furious and beat him several dozen strokes with a staff.

entries.zh: 後超轉中書侍郎，俄遷太常少卿。
entries.en: Later he was promoted out of turn to Secretariat Attendant, and soon advanced to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
entries.literal: Later he was exceptionally transferred to Secretariat Attendant, and shortly afterward promoted to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

entries.zh: 以父憂去職，哭泣嘔血，身自負土。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his father, wept until he vomited blood, and carried earth for the grave himself.
entries.literal: Because of mourning for his father he left office; he wept until he vomited blood and personally carried earth.

entries.zh: 時年二十五，便有白髮，免喪抽去，不復更生，世人以為孝思所致。
entries.en: He was twenty-five at the time, yet already had white hair. After mourning ended he plucked it out, and it never grew back; people believed this came from filial grief.
entries.literal: At that time he was twenty-five, yet already had white hair; when mourning was complete, he plucked it out, and it did not grow again. People of the age thought this was caused by filial grief.

entries.zh: 尋除給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 時領軍元叉威勢尤盛，凡有遷授，莫不造門謝謁。
entries.en: At the time Yuan Cha, Commander of the Guards, was extremely powerful. Whenever anyone received a transfer or appointment, he went to Yuan Cha's gate to give thanks.
entries.literal: At the time Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha's authority was especially great; whenever anyone received a transfer or appointment, none failed to visit his gate and offer thanks.

entries.zh: 順拜表而已，曾不詣叉。
entries.en: Shun merely submitted a memorial of thanks and never called on Yuan Cha.
entries.literal: Shun merely submitted a memorial of thanks and never went to Cha.

entries.zh: 叉謂順曰：「卿何謂聊不見我？」
entries.en: Yuan Cha said to Shun, "Why have you not come to see me at all?"
entries.literal: Cha said to Shun, "What do you mean by not once coming to see me?"

entries.zh: 順正色曰：「天子富於春秋，委政宗輔，叔父宜以至公為心，舉士報國，如何賣恩，責人私謝，豈所望也！」
entries.en: Shun answered sternly, "The Son of Heaven is young and has entrusted government to clan ministers. Uncle should act with perfect fairness, raise worthy men, and serve the state. How can you sell favors and demand private thanks? This is not what one expects."
entries.literal: Shun said with a stern expression, "The Son of Heaven is young, and government is entrusted to clan assistants. Uncle should take utmost fairness as his heart, promote scholars, and repay the state. How can you sell favors and demand private thanks from people? This is not what one would hope."

entries.zh: 至於朝論得失，順常鯁言正議，曾不阿旨，由此見憚。
entries.en: In court debates over right and wrong, Shun always spoke bluntly and argued uprightly, never bending to anyone's wishes; for this he was feared.
entries.literal: As for gains and losses in court discussion, Shun always spoke chokingly direct words and upright arguments, never once flattering the intent; because of this he was feared.

entries.zh: 出除平北將軍、恒州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
entries.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 順謂叉曰：「北鎮紛紜，方為國梗，桑乾舊都，根本所繫，請假都督，為國捍屏。」
entries.en: Shun told Yuan Cha, "The northern garrisons are in turmoil and threaten the state. Sanggan and the old capital are bound to our foundation. Give me temporary command, and I will serve as the state's shield."
entries.literal: Shun said to Cha, "The northern garrisons are in turmoil and are just now a blockage to the state. Sanggan and the old capital are tied to the root and base. I request temporary authority as commander-in-chief, to serve as shield and screen for the state."

entries.zh: 叉心疑難，不欲授以兵官，謂順曰：「此朝廷之事，非我所裁。」
entries.en: Yuan Cha was suspicious and reluctant to give him a military post, so he said, "This is a court matter, not mine to decide."
entries.literal: Cha suspected and found this difficult; not wishing to grant him a military office, he said to Shun, "This is the court's affair, not something I decide."

entries.zh: 順曰：「叔父既握國柄，殺生由己，自言天之歷數應在我躬，何得復有朝廷也！」
entries.en: Shun said, "Uncle holds state power, and life and death come from you. You yourself say Heaven's mandate should rest in your own person; how can there still be a court?"
entries.literal: Shun said, "Since Uncle holds the handle of the state, killing and giving life come from yourself. You yourself say the heavenly calendar should be in your person; how can there again be a court?"

entries.zh: 叉彌忿憚之。
entries.en: Yuan Cha grew even angrier and more afraid of him.
entries.literal: Cha grew still more angry and afraid of him.

entries.zh: 轉為安東將軍、齊州刺史。
entries.en: Shun was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qizhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qizhou.

entries.zh: 順自負有才，不得居內，每懷鬱怏，形於言色，遂縱酒歡娛，不親政事。
entries.en: Confident in his talent and unable to remain at court, Shun nursed resentment that showed in his face and speech. He then gave himself over to wine and amusement and neglected government.
entries.literal: Shun relied on his own talent, and because he could not remain inside the court, he always harbored resentment, which showed in his words and expression; he then indulged in wine and pleasure and did not attend personally to government affairs.

entries.zh: 叉解領軍，徵為給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: When Yuan Cha was relieved of command of the Guards, Shun was summoned as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: When Cha was relieved of the Guards command, Shun was summoned as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 親友郊迎，賀其得入。
entries.en: Relatives and friends met him in the suburbs and congratulated him on returning to court.
entries.literal: Relatives and friends met him in the suburbs and congratulated him on being able to enter.

entries.zh: 順曰：「不患不入，正恐入而復出耳。」
entries.en: Shun said, "I am not worried about failing to enter; I only fear entering and then being sent out again."
entries.literal: Shun said, "I do not worry about not entering; I only fear entering and then going out again."

entries.zh: 俄兼殿中尚書，轉侍中。
entries.en: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of the Palace and was then transferred to Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of the Palace and was transferred to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 初，中山王熙起兵討元叉，不果而誅，及靈太后反政，方得改葬。
entries.en: Earlier, Xi, Prince of Zhongshan, had raised troops against Yuan Cha, failed, and been executed. Only after Empress Dowager Ling resumed power was he allowed reburial.
entries.literal: Earlier, Xi, Prince of Zhongshan, had raised troops to attack Yuan Cha; he failed and was executed. When Empress Dowager Ling returned to government, only then was he able to be reburied.

entries.zh: 順侍坐西遊園，因奏太后曰：「臣昨往看中山家葬，非唯宗親哀其冤酷，行路士女，見其一家七喪，皆為澘然，莫不酸泣。」
entries.en: While sitting in attendance in the Western Tour Garden, Shun said to the Empress Dowager, "Yesterday I went to see the burial of the Zhongshan household. Not only did the imperial kin mourn their cruel wrong; travelers, men and women alike, saw seven dead from one family and all wept bitterly."
entries.literal: Shun was sitting in attendance in the Western Tour Garden and thereupon memorialized to the Empress Dowager, "Yesterday I went to see the burial of Zhongshan's household. Not only did the imperial kin mourn their cruel wrong; men and women on the road, seeing seven funerals from one family, were all moved to tears and sobbed bitterly."

entries.zh: 叉妻時在太后側，順指之曰：「陛下奈何以一妹之故，不伏元叉之罪，使天下懷冤！」
entries.en: Yuan Cha's wife was beside the Empress Dowager at the time. Shun pointed to her and said, "How can Your Majesty, for the sake of one sister, fail to punish Yuan Cha's crime and leave the whole realm nursing injustice?"
entries.literal: Cha's wife was then at the Empress Dowager's side. Shun pointed to her and said, "How can Your Majesty, because of one younger sister, not punish Yuan Cha's crime, making all under Heaven harbor injustice?"

entries.zh: 太后默然不語。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was silent.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager was silent and did not speak.

entries.zh: 就德興反於營州，使尚書盧同往討之，大敗而返。
entries.en: When Jiu Dexing rebelled in Yingzhou, Lu Tong of the Department was sent against him but returned after a major defeat.
entries.literal: Jiu Dexing rebelled in Yingzhou, and the Department official Lu Tong was sent to attack him, but returned in great defeat.

entries.zh: 屬侍中穆紹與順侍坐，因論同之罪。
entries.en: Palace Attendant Mu Shao happened to be sitting in attendance with Shun, and they discussed Lu Tong's offense.
entries.literal: It happened that Palace Attendant Mu Shao was sitting in attendance with Shun, and they discussed Tong's crime.

entries.zh: 同先有近宅借紹，紹頗欲為言。
entries.en: Lu Tong had earlier lent Shao a nearby residence, and Shao wanted to speak for him.
entries.literal: Tong previously had a nearby residence that he lent to Shao, and Shao rather wished to speak on his behalf.

entries.zh: 順勃然曰：「盧同終將無罪！」
entries.en: Shun suddenly said, "Lu Tong will end up without guilt!"
entries.literal: Shun suddenly said, "Lu Tong in the end will have no crime!"

entries.zh: 太后曰：「何得如侍中之言？」
entries.en: The Empress Dowager said, "How can it be as the Palace Attendant says?"
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "How can it be as the Palace Attendant says?"

entries.zh: 順曰：「同有好宅與要勢侍中，豈慮罪也。」
entries.en: Shun replied, "Tong has a fine house to give a powerful Palace Attendant. Why should he worry about guilt?"
entries.literal: Shun said, "Tong has a fine residence to give to an important and powerful Palace Attendant; why would he worry about guilt?"

entries.zh: 紹慚，不敢復言。
entries.en: Shao was ashamed and did not dare speak again.
entries.literal: Shao was ashamed and did not dare speak again.

entries.zh: 靈太后頗事妝飾，數出遊幸。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Ling was much occupied with adornment and often went out on excursions.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Ling rather occupied herself with adornment and often went out on pleasure tours.

entries.zh: 順面諍曰：「禮，婦人夫喪，自稱未亡人，首去珠玉，衣不被綵。
entries.en: Shun remonstrated with her directly: "According to ritual, when a woman loses her husband she calls herself the one not yet dead, removes pearls and jade from her hair, and does not wear colored clothing.
entries.literal: Shun remonstrated to her face, saying, "According to ritual, when a woman's husband has died, she calls herself the one not yet dead, removes pearls and jade from her head, and does not wear colored garments.

entries.zh: 陛下母臨天下，年垂不惑，過甚修飾，何以示後世？」
entries.en: Your Majesty rules the realm as mother and is nearly forty, yet you adorn yourself excessively. What example does this show later generations?"
entries.literal: Your Majesty mothers all under Heaven and is nearly forty, yet you excessively cultivate adornment. How will you show yourself to later generations?"

entries.zh: 靈太后慚而不出。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Ling was ashamed and stopped going out.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was ashamed and did not go out.

entries.zh: 還入宮，責順曰：「千里相徵，豈欲眾中見辱也！」
entries.en: When she returned to the palace, she rebuked Shun: "I summoned you from a thousand li away; did you intend to shame me in public?"
entries.literal: After returning to the palace, she reproached Shun, saying, "I summoned you from a thousand li away; did I mean to be humiliated before the crowd?"

entries.zh: 順曰：「陛下盛服炫容，不畏天下所笑，何耻臣之一言乎？」
entries.en: Shun replied, "Your Majesty dresses splendidly and displays your beauty without fearing the laughter of the realm. Why be ashamed of one word from me?"
entries.literal: Shun said, "Your Majesty wears splendid robes and dazzles with your appearance, yet does not fear the laughter of all under Heaven. Why be ashamed of one word from me?"

entries.zh: 初，城陽王徽慕順才名，偏相結納。
entries.en: Earlier, Hui, Prince of Chengyang, admired Shun's talent and reputation and made special efforts to befriend him.
entries.literal: Earlier, Hui, Prince of Chengyang, admired Shun's talent and reputation and especially befriended and received him.

entries.zh: 而廣陽王淵姦徽妻于氏，大為嫌隙。
entries.en: But Yuan, Prince of Guangyang, had an affair with Hui's wife Lady Yu, creating a deep rift.
entries.literal: But Yuan, Prince of Guangyang, committed adultery with Hui's wife, Lady Yu, creating a great rift.

entries.zh: 及淵自定州被徵，入為吏部尚書，兼中領軍。
entries.en: When Yuan was summoned from Dingzhou to serve as Minister of Personnel and concurrently Central Commander of the Guards,
entries.literal: When Yuan was summoned from Dingzhou and entered as Minister of Personnel, concurrently Central Commander of the Guards,

entries.zh: 順為詔書，辭頗優美。
entries.en: Shun drafted the edict for him in notably elegant language.
entries.literal: Shun drafted the edict for him, and its wording was quite excellent.

entries.zh: 徽疑順為淵左右，由是與徐紇間順於靈太后，出順為護軍將軍、太常卿。
entries.en: Hui suspected Shun of favoring Yuan, so he and Xu He slandered Shun to Empress Dowager Ling. Shun was sent out as General Who Protects the Army and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
entries.literal: Hui suspected Shun of siding with Yuan, and because of this, together with Xu He, he alienated Shun from Empress Dowager Ling; Shun was sent out as General Who Protects the Army and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

entries.zh: 順奉辭於西遊園，徽紇侍側，順指之謂靈太后曰：「此人魏之宰嚭，魏國不滅，終不死亡。」
entries.en: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden while Hui and Xu He stood at the side. Pointing at Xu He, he said to Empress Dowager Ling, "This man is Wei's Zai Pi. Unless Wei is destroyed, he will never die."
entries.literal: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden, with Hui and He standing in attendance at the side. Shun pointed to them and said to Empress Dowager Ling, "This man is Wei's Zai Pi; if the state of Wei is not destroyed, he will never die."

entries.zh: 紇脅肩而出。
entries.en: Xu He went out with his shoulders hunched.
entries.literal: He went out with his shoulders hunched.

entries.zh: 順遂抗聲叱之曰：「爾刀筆小人，正堪為几案之吏，寧應忝茲執戟，虧我彝倫！」
entries.en: Shun then shouted after him, "You petty clerk with knife and brush are fit only for desk work. How can you presume to hold a halberd here and disgrace our proper order!"
entries.literal: Shun then raised his voice and rebuked him, saying, "You petty knife-and-brush man are fit only to be a desk clerk. How could you shamefully hold this halberd and damage our proper human relations!"

entries.zh: 遂振衣而起。
entries.en: He shook out his robe and rose.
entries.literal: He then shook out his robe and rose.

entries.zh: 靈太后默而不言。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Ling said nothing.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was silent and did not speak.

entries.zh: 時追論順父顧託之功，增任城王彝邑二千戶，又析彝邑五百戶以封順，為東阿縣開國公。
entries.en: At the time the court was reviewing the merit of Shun's father in the imperial entrustment. Yi, Prince of Rencheng, received two thousand additional households, and five hundred households were carved from Yi's fief to enfeoff Shun as Founding Duke of Dong'e County.
entries.literal: At the time the court was retrospectively discussing the merit of Shun's father in receiving the testamentary charge. It increased the fief of Yi, Prince of Rencheng, by two thousand households, and also divided five hundred households from Yi's fief to enfeoff Shun as Founding Duke of Dong'e County.

entries.zh: 順疾徽等間之，遂為蠅賦曰：「余以仲秋休沐，端坐衡門，寄想琴書，託情紙翰，而蒼蠅小蟲，往來牀几，疾其變白，聊為賦云：遐哉大道，廓矣洪氛。
entries.en: Shun hated Hui and the others for slandering him, and so he wrote a Rhapsody on Flies: "In mid-autumn, resting from office, I sat quietly at my humble gate, my thoughts on zither and books and my feelings entrusted to paper and brush. But tiny bluebottle flies came and went over bed and table. Hating how they transform white, I have made this rhapsody: Vast is the great Way, broad the primal vapor.
entries.literal: Shun hated that Hui and the others had alienated him, and so he composed a Rhapsody on Flies, saying, "In mid-autumn, while resting from office, I sat upright by my humble gate, setting my thoughts on zither and books and entrusting my feelings to paper and brush; but the small insects, the bluebottle flies, came and went over bed and table. Hating how they change white, I have briefly made a rhapsody, saying: Vast is the great Way, broad the primal vapor.

entries.zh: 肇立秋夏，爰啟冬春。
entries.en: It first set autumn and summer in place, then opened winter and spring.
entries.literal: It first established autumn and summer, and then opened winter and spring.

entries.zh: 既含育於萬性，又芻狗而不仁。
entries.en: It contains and nurtures all natures, yet like straw dogs it is not benevolent.
entries.literal: It both contains and nurtures the ten thousand natures, and yet, like straw dogs, is not benevolent.

entries.zh: 隨因緣以授體，齊美惡而無分。
entries.en: Following conditions, it grants bodies, making no distinction between fair and foul.
entries.literal: Following causes and conditions, it grants bodies, equalizing beautiful and ugly without distinction.

entries.zh: 生茲穢類，靡益於人。
entries.en: Thus this filthy kind is born, bringing no benefit to people.
entries.literal: It gives birth to this filthy kind, with no benefit to human beings.

entries.zh: 名備羣品，聲損眾倫。
entries.en: Its name is counted among living things, but its buzzing harms the order of all beings.
entries.literal: Its name is included among the many creatures, but its sound damages all relations.

entries.zh: 欹脛纖翼，紫首蒼身。
entries.en: Crooked legs, slender wings, purple heads, blue bodies.
entries.literal: Crooked shins and slender wings, purple heads and blue bodies.

entries.zh: 飛不能迥，聲若遠聞。
entries.en: It cannot fly far, yet its noise seems to carry into the distance.
entries.literal: It cannot fly far, but its sound seems heard from afar.

entries.zh: 點緇成素，變白為黑。
entries.en: It spots black onto white and turns white into black.
entries.literal: It dots black and makes white; it changes white into black.

entries.zh: 寡愛蘭芳，偏貪穢食。
entries.en: It cares little for orchid fragrance and craves filthy food.
entries.literal: It has little love for orchid fragrance and is especially greedy for filthy food.

entries.zh: 集桓公之屍，居平叔之側。
entries.en: It gathered on Duke Huan's corpse and lingered at Pingshu's side.
entries.literal: It gathered on Duke Huan's corpse and dwelt by Pingshu's side.

entries.zh: 亂鷄鳴之響，毀皇宮之飾。
entries.en: It confused the sound of the cockcrow and defiled the ornaments of the imperial palace.
entries.literal: It disordered the sound of the cockcrow and ruined the ornaments of the imperial palace.

entries.zh: 習習戶庭，營營榛棘。
entries.en: Fluttering through doors and courtyards, buzzing among thorns and brambles.
entries.literal: Fluttering through doors and courtyards, buzzing among thorns and brambles.

entries.zh: 反覆往還，譬彼讒賊。
entries.en: Back and forth it comes and goes, like slanderous traitors.
entries.literal: Back and forth it goes and returns, like those slanderous rebels.

entries.zh: 膚受既通，譖潤罔極。
entries.en: Once slander penetrates the skin, its soaking accusations know no limit.
entries.literal: Once skin-deep slander gets through, soaking accusations have no limit.

entries.zh: 緝緝幡幡，交亂四國。
entries.en: Whispering and fluttering, they throw the four quarters into disorder.
entries.literal: Whispering and fluttering, they cross and disorder the four states.

entries.zh: 於是妖姬進，邪士來，聖賢擁，忠孝摧。
entries.en: Then seductive women advance, wicked men arrive, sages and worthies are blocked, and the loyal and filial are crushed.
entries.literal: Thereupon seductive women advance, wicked men come, sages and worthies are blocked, and the loyal and filial are crushed.

entries.zh: 周昌拘於牖里，天乙囚於夏臺。
entries.en: Zhou Chang was confined at Youli, and Tianyi imprisoned at Xiatai.
entries.literal: Zhou Chang was confined at Youli, and Tianyi was imprisoned at Xiatai.

entries.zh: 伯奇為之痛結，申生為之蒙災。
entries.en: Boqi was bound in grief because of them, and Shensheng was overtaken by disaster because of them.
entries.literal: Boqi was knotted in pain by them, and Shensheng was covered with disaster by them.

entries.zh: 鴟鴞悲其室，採葛懼其懷。
entries.en: The Owl lamented its ruined house, and Gathering Kudzu feared what lay in the heart.
entries.literal: The Owl grieved for its house, and Gathering Kudzu feared what was in the heart.

entries.zh: 小弁隕其涕，靈均表其哀。
entries.en: Xiaobian shed tears, and Lingjun made his sorrow known.
entries.literal: Xiaobian shed its tears, and Lingjun displayed his sorrow.

entries.zh: 自古明哲猶如此，何況中庸與凡才。
entries.en: Even the enlightened and wise of antiquity suffered so; how much more men of middling or ordinary talent?
entries.literal: From antiquity, the enlightened and wise were still like this; how much more the middling and ordinary talents?

entries.zh: 若夫天生地養，各有所親。
entries.en: As for the beings Heaven gives birth to and Earth nourishes, each has its proper affinities.
entries.literal: As for what Heaven gives birth to and Earth nourishes, each has what it is close to.

entries.zh: 獸必依地，鳥亦憑雲。
entries.en: Beasts rely on the earth, and birds depend on the clouds.
entries.literal: Beasts must rely on the earth, and birds also depend on the clouds.

entries.zh: 或來儀以呈祉，或自擾而見文。
entries.en: Some come in stately display to present blessings; some are domesticated and display patterned beauty.
entries.literal: Some come in ritual display to present blessings; some are tamed and show patterned beauty.

entries.zh: 或負圖而歸德，或銜書以告真。
entries.en: Some bear diagrams and return to virtue; some carry writings in their mouths to reveal the true.
entries.literal: Some bear diagrams and return to virtue; some hold writings in their mouths and announce the true.

entries.zh: 或夭胎而奉味，或殘軀以獻珍。
entries.en: Some are taken before birth to provide flavor; some, with damaged bodies, offer delicacies.
entries.literal: Some are cut short in the womb to offer flavor; some offer preciousness with damaged bodies.

entries.zh: 或主皮而興禮，或牢豢以供神。
entries.en: Some, as hides, give rise to ritual; some, as sacrificial animals, serve the spirits.
entries.literal: Some, as hides, promote ritual; some, as stall-fed animals, supply the spirits.

entries.zh: 雖死生之異質，俱有益於國人。
entries.en: Though they differ as living and dead, all benefit the people of the state.
entries.literal: Although dead and living are different in substance, all are of benefit to the people of the state.

entries.zh: 非如蒼蠅之無用，唯構亂於蒸民。」
entries.en: They are not like the bluebottle fly, useless and only sowing disorder among the people."
entries.literal: They are not like the bluebottle fly, which is useless and only constructs disorder among the multitudes."

entries.zh: 遂屬疾在家，杜絕慶弔。
entries.en: He then fell ill at home and refused all visits of congratulation or condolence.
entries.literal: He then became ill at home and cut off congratulations and condolences.

entries.zh: 後除吏部尚書，兼右僕射。
entries.en: Later he was appointed Minister of Personnel and concurrently Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of Personnel and concurrently Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 及上省，登階向榻，見榻甚故，問都令史徐仵起。
entries.en: When he went up to the Department and approached the couch, he saw that it was very old and asked Chief Clerk Xu Wuqi about it.
entries.literal: When he went up to the Department, climbed the steps toward the couch, and saw that the couch was very old, he asked the Chief Clerk Xu Wuqi about it.

entries.zh: 仵起曰：「此榻曾經先王坐。」
entries.en: Wuqi said, "The former prince once sat on this couch."
entries.literal: Wuqi said, "This couch was once sat on by the former king."

entries.zh: 順即哽塞，涕泗交流，久而不能言，遂令換之。
entries.en: Shun immediately choked up, tears streaming down; for a long while he could not speak, and then ordered the couch replaced.
entries.literal: Shun immediately choked up, tears and mucus flowing together; for a long while he could not speak, and he then ordered it changed.

entries.zh: 時三公曹令史朱暉，素事錄尚書、高陽王雍，雍欲以為廷尉評，頻請託順，順不為用。
entries.en: At the time Zhu Hui, a clerk in the Bureau of the Three Excellencies, had long served Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang and Recording Director of the Department. Yong wanted to make him an Evaluator in the Court of Justice and repeatedly pressed Shun, but Shun refused to use him.
entries.literal: At the time Zhu Hui, a clerk in the Bureau of the Three Excellencies, had long served Yong, Recording Director of the Department and Prince of Gaoyang. Yong wished to make him an Evaluator in the Court of Justice and repeatedly asked and entrusted Shun, but Shun would not employ him.

entries.zh: 雍遂下命用之，順投之於地。
entries.en: Yuan Yong then issued an order appointing him, and Shun threw it on the ground.
entries.literal: Yong then issued an order to use him, and Shun threw it on the ground.

entries.zh: 雍聞之，大怒，昧爽坐都廳，召尚書及丞郎畢集，欲待順至，於眾挫之。
entries.en: When Yong heard, he was furious. At dawn he sat in the metropolitan hall and summoned all the Ministers, Aides, and Gentlemen, intending to humiliate Shun publicly when he arrived.
entries.literal: When Yong heard of this, he was furious. At dawn he sat in the metropolitan hall and summoned the Ministers, Aides, and Gentlemen to assemble completely, intending to wait for Shun to arrive and humiliate him before the crowd.

entries.zh: 順日高方至，雍攘袂撫几而言曰：「身，天子之子，天子之弟，天子之叔，天子之相，四海之內，親尊莫二，元順何人，以身成命，投棄於地！」
entries.en: Shun arrived only when the sun was high. Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the table, and said, "I am the Son of Heaven's son, brother, uncle, and chief minister. Within the four seas no one is closer or more honored. Who is Yuan Shun, to take my completed order and throw it on the ground!"
entries.literal: Only when the sun was high did Shun arrive. Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the armrest, and said, "I am son of the Son of Heaven, brother of the Son of Heaven, uncle of the Son of Heaven, and minister of the Son of Heaven. Within the four seas none is closer or more honored. What sort of man is Yuan Shun, to take an order completed by me and throw it away on the ground!"

entries.zh: 順鬚鬢俱張，仰面看屋，憤氣奔涌，長歔而不言。
entries.en: Shun's beard and temples bristled. He looked up at the rafters, anger surging, and gave a long sigh without speaking.
entries.literal: Shun's beard and temples both bristled; he raised his face and looked at the roof, angry breath surging, and sighed long without speaking.

entries.zh: 久之，搖一白羽扇，徐而謂雍曰：「高祖遷宅中土，創定九流，官方清濁，軌儀萬古。
entries.en: After a long while, he waved a white feather fan and slowly said to Yong, "Gaozu moved the capital to the central lands and established the nine ranks; he distinguished pure and impure offices, setting a model for all ages.
entries.literal: After a long while, he waved a white feather fan and slowly said to Yong, "Gaozu moved his residence to the central lands and first fixed the nine ranks; offices were divided into pure and impure, a model for ten thousand ages.

entries.zh: 而朱暉小子，身為省吏，何合為廷尉清官！
entries.en: Zhu Hui is a petty man, a mere Department clerk. How is he fit for a pure office in the Court of Justice?
entries.literal: Yet Zhu Hui is a petty man, himself a department clerk. How is he fit for a pure office in the Court of Justice?

entries.zh: 殿下既先皇同氣，宜遵成旨，自有短垣而復踰之也。」
entries.en: Your Highness shares the late emperor's blood and should follow the established decree. Even a low wall is still a boundary; why overstep it again?"
entries.literal: Since Your Highness is of the same breath as the former emperor, you should follow the completed decree. There is already a low wall, and yet you overstep it again."

entries.zh: 雍曰：「身為丞相、錄尚書，如何不得用一人為官？」
entries.en: Yong said, "I am Chancellor and Recording Director of the Department. How can I not appoint one man to office?"
entries.literal: Yong said, "I am Chancellor and Recording Director of the Department of State Affairs; how can I not be allowed to use one man as an official?"

entries.zh: 順曰：「庖人雖不治庖，尸祝不得越樽俎而代之。
entries.en: Shun replied, "Even if the cook does not manage the kitchen, the invocator may not step beyond the vessels and stands to take his place.
entries.literal: Shun said, "Though the cook does not manage the kitchen, the invocator may not step past the wine vessels and stands to replace him.

entries.zh: 未聞有別旨，令殿下參選事。」
entries.en: I have heard of no separate edict ordering Your Highness to take part in personnel selection."
entries.literal: I have not heard of a separate decree ordering Your Highness to take part in selection affairs."

entries.zh: 順又厲聲曰：「殿下必如是，順當依事奏聞！」
entries.en: Shun then said sharply, "If Your Highness insists, I will memorialize the matter according to the facts!"
entries.literal: Shun again said in a stern voice, "If Your Highness insists on being like this, I shall memorialize the matter according to the facts!"

entries.zh: 雍遂笑而言曰：「豈可以朱暉小人，便相忿恨。」
entries.en: Yong then laughed. "How could we become angry with one another over a petty man like Zhu Hui?"
entries.literal: Yong then laughed and said, "How could we become angry with each other over a petty man like Zhu Hui?"

entries.zh: 遂起，呼順入室，與之極飲。
entries.en: He rose, called Shun inside, and drank with him to the fullest.
entries.literal: He then rose, called Shun into the inner room, and drank with him to the utmost.

entries.zh: 順之亢毅不撓，皆此類也。
entries.en: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this sort.
entries.literal: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this kind.

entries.zh: 後除征南將軍、右光祿大夫，轉兼左僕射。
entries.en: Later he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Right Guanglu Grandee, then transferred to concurrently serve as Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Right Guanglu Grandee, and was transferred to concurrently serve as Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 爾朱榮之奉莊帝，召百官悉至河陰，素聞順數諫諍，惜其亮直，謂朱瑞曰：「可語元僕射，但在省，不須來。」
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuang, he summoned all officials to Heyin. Having long heard that Shun often remonstrated and valuing his clear integrity, he told Zhu Rui, "Tell Vice Director Yuan to stay in the Department; he need not come."
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuang, he summoned all the officials to Heyin. He had long heard that Shun had repeatedly remonstrated and argued, and he cherished his bright uprightness, so he said to Zhu Rui, "You may tell Vice Director Yuan only to remain in the Department; he need not come."

entries.zh: 順不達其旨，聞害衣冠，遂便出走，為陵戶鮮于康奴所害。
entries.en: Shun did not understand the warning. Hearing that the officials were being slaughtered, he fled and was killed by Xianyu Kangnu, a tomb-household man.
entries.literal: Shun did not understand his intent. Hearing that the officials were being harmed, he immediately fled and was killed by Xianyu Kangnu, a tomb household man.

entries.zh: 家徒四壁，無物斂屍，止有書數千卷而已。
entries.en: His house was bare, with nothing to shroud his body; it contained only several thousand scrolls of books.
entries.literal: His house had only four bare walls, and there was nothing with which to enshroud the corpse; there were only several thousand scrolls of books.

entries.zh: 門下通事令史王才達裂裳覆之。
entries.en: Wang Caida, Clerk for Communications under the Gate, tore his robe to cover the body.
entries.literal: Wang Caida, Clerk for Communications under the Gate, tore his garment to cover him.

entries.zh: 莊帝還宮，遣黃門侍郎山偉巡喻京邑。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour the capital and reassure it.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour and reassure the capital.

entries.zh: 偉臨順喪，悲慟無已。
entries.en: Shan Wei visited Shun's mourning place and wept without stopping.
entries.literal: Wei came to Shun's funeral and grieved without cease.

entries.zh: 既還，莊帝怪而問曰：「黃門何為聲散？」
entries.en: When he returned, Emperor Zhuang was surprised and asked, "Why is the Yellow Gate attendant's voice hoarse?"
entries.literal: After he returned, Emperor Zhuang was surprised and asked, "Why is the Yellow Gate's voice broken?"

entries.zh: 偉以狀對。
entries.en: Shan Wei told him what had happened.
entries.literal: Wei answered with the circumstances.

entries.zh: 莊帝敕侍中元祉曰：「宗室喪亡非一，不可周贍。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuang instructed Palace Attendant Yuan Zhi, "Many members of the imperial clan have died, and we cannot provide fully for all of them.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuang ordered Palace Attendant Yuan Zhi, "There is more than one death in the imperial clan, and they cannot all be fully provided for.

entries.zh: 元僕射清苦之節，死乃益彰，特贈絹百匹，餘不得例。」
entries.en: Vice Director Yuan's austere integrity shines even more in death. Grant him one hundred bolts of silk as a special gift; let this not become precedent for the others."
entries.literal: The austere integrity of Vice Director Yuan is only more manifest in death. Specially grant him one hundred bolts of silk; the rest may not follow this as precedent."

entries.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、定州刺史，諡曰文烈。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Dingzhou, and was given the posthumous title Wenlie.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenlie.

entries.zh: 順撰帝錄二十卷，詩賦表頌數十篇，今多亡失。
entries.en: Shun compiled Imperial Records in twenty fascicles and wrote several dozen poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies, most of which are now lost.
entries.literal: Shun compiled Imperial Records in twenty fascicles, as well as several tens of poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies; most are now lost.

entries.zh: 長子朗，時年十七。
entries.en: His eldest son Lang was seventeen at the time.
entries.literal: His eldest son Lang was seventeen at the time.

entries.zh: 枕戈潛伏積年，乃手刃康奴，以首祭於順墓，然後詣闕請罪。
entries.en: For years he slept on his spear and hid in secret. Then he killed Kangnu with his own hand, offered the head at Shun's tomb, and afterward went to the palace gate to confess.
entries.literal: He slept on his spear and hid in secret for years, then personally killed Kangnu, sacrificed the head at Shun's tomb, and only afterward went to the palace gate to confess his crime.

entries.zh: 朝廷嘉而不問。
entries.en: The court praised him and did not punish him.
entries.literal: The court praised him and did not prosecute.

entries.zh: 朗涉歷書記，為司徒屬。
entries.en: Lang was experienced in documents and records and served as an attendant to the Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: Lang had experience in documents and records and served as an attendant to the Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 天平中，為奴所害。
entries.en: In the Tianping era, he was killed by a slave.
entries.literal: In the Tianping era, he was killed by a slave.

entries.zh: 贈都督瀛冀二州諸軍事、□□將軍、尚書右僕射、冀州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted Commander of all military affairs in Ying and Ji provinces, an unspecified generalship, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Commander of all military affairs in Ying and Ji provinces, General with title missing, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.

entries.zh: 順弟淑，淑弟悲，並早卒。
entries.en: Shun's younger brother Shu and Shu's younger brother Bei both died young.
entries.literal: Shun's younger brother Shu and Shu's younger brother Bei both died young.

entries.zh: 悲弟紀，字子綱。
entries.en: Bei's younger brother Ji was styled Zigang.
entries.literal: Bei's younger brother Ji was styled Zigang.

entries.zh: 永熙中，給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: In the Yongxi era he served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: In the Yongxi era, he was Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 隨出帝，沒於關中。
entries.en: He followed the Emperor Who Went Out and died in Guanzhong.
entries.literal: He followed the Emperor Who Went Out and died in Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 澄弟嵩，字道岳。
entries.en: Cheng's younger brother Song was styled Daoyue.
entries.literal: Cheng's younger brother Song was styled Daoyue.

entries.zh: 高祖時，自中大夫遷員外常侍，轉步兵校尉。
entries.en: In Gaozu's time he moved from Palace Grandee to Regular Attendant Outside the Ranks, then became Infantry Commandant.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's time, he was transferred from Palace Grandee to Regular Attendant Outside the Ranks, then transferred to Infantry Commandant.

entries.zh: 大司馬、安定王休薨，未及卒哭，嵩便遊田。
entries.en: When Xiu, Grand Marshal and Prince of Anding, died, Song went hunting before the mourning rites had even ended.
entries.literal: When Xiu, Grand Marshal and Prince of Anding, died, before the final wailing had been completed, Song immediately went hunting.

entries.zh: 高祖聞而大怒，詔曰：「嵩不能克己復禮，企心典憲，大司馬薨殂甫爾，便以鷹鷂自娛。
entries.en: When Gaozu heard, he was furious and issued an edict: "Song cannot master himself and return to ritual or set his mind on law and precedent. The Grand Marshal has only just died, and already he amuses himself with hawks and falcons.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard of this, he was furious and issued an edict: "Song cannot overcome himself and return to ritual or set his mind on standards and laws. The Grand Marshal has only just died, and he immediately amuses himself with hawks and sparrowhawks.

entries.zh: 有如父之痛，無猶子之情，捐心棄禮，何其太速！
entries.en: He should feel pain as for a father, yet he lacks even a nephew's feeling; he casts aside feeling and abandons ritual. How terribly hasty!
entries.literal: He has pain as though for a father, but lacks the feeling of a nephew; he casts aside feeling and abandons ritual. How far too quick this is!

entries.zh: 便可免官。」
entries.en: He may be dismissed from office."
entries.literal: He may be dismissed from office."

entries.zh: 後從平沔北，累有戰功，除左中郎將，兼武衞將軍。
entries.en: Later he took part in pacifying the north of the Mian, repeatedly earned battle merit, and was appointed Left Gentleman General of the Center, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.
entries.literal: Later he followed in pacifying north of the Mian, repeatedly had battle merits, and was appointed Left Gentleman General of the Center, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 高祖南伐，蕭寶卷將陳顯達率眾拒戰。
entries.en: When Gaozu campaigned south, Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda led troops to resist him.
entries.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda led troops to resist in battle.

entries.zh: 嵩身備三仗，免冑直前，將士從之，顯達奔潰，斬獲萬計。
entries.en: Song armed himself with three weapons, removed his helmet, and advanced straight ahead. The officers and soldiers followed; Xianda's forces fled in collapse, and the dead and captured numbered in the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Song himself was equipped with three weapons, removed his helmet, and advanced straight ahead. The officers and soldiers followed him, Xianda fled in collapse, and beheadings and captures were counted by the ten thousand.

entries.zh: 嵩於爾日勇冠三軍。
entries.en: That day, Song's courage surpassed the whole army.
entries.literal: On that day Song's courage topped the three armies.

entries.zh: 高祖大悅而言曰：「任城康王大有褔德，文武頓出其門。」
entries.en: Gaozu was delighted. "Prince Kang of Rencheng had great fortune and virtue; civil and martial talent have both burst from his household."
entries.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "Prince Kang of Rencheng has great fortune and virtue; civil and martial talent have suddenly emerged from his gate."

entries.zh: 以功賜爵高平縣侯，賚帛二千五百匹。
entries.en: For his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoping County and awarded twenty-five hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: For his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoping County and given two thousand five hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 初，高祖之發洛也，馮皇后以罪幽於宮內。
entries.en: Earlier, when Gaozu left Luoyang, Empress Feng had been confined inside the palace for an offense.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu departed Luoyang, Empress Feng had been confined inside the palace for an offense.

entries.zh: 既平顯達，回次穀唐原，高祖疾甚，將賜后死，曰：「使人不易可得。」
entries.en: After Xianda was defeated, Gaozu stopped on the return at Gutangyuan. Gravely ill, he was about to order the empress to die and said, "A suitable envoy is not easy to find."
entries.literal: After Xianda had been pacified, on the return they stopped at Gutangyuan. Gaozu was gravely ill and was about to grant the empress death, saying, "A suitable envoy is not easy to obtain."

entries.zh: 顧謂任城王澄曰：「任城必不負我，嵩亦當不負任城，可使嵩也。」
entries.en: He turned to Cheng, Prince of Rencheng: "Rencheng will not fail me, and Song will not fail Rencheng. Send Song."
entries.literal: He looked back and said to Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, "Rencheng will surely not fail me, and Song will also not fail Rencheng. Song may be sent."

entries.zh: 於是引嵩入內，親詔遣之。
entries.en: Song was then brought inside, and Gaozu personally ordered him dispatched.
entries.literal: Thereupon Song was brought inside, and Gaozu personally issued an edict dispatching him.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，以武衞將軍兼侍中，出為平南將軍、荊州刺史。
entries.en: When Shizong ascended the throne, Song served as General of the Martial Guard and concurrently Palace Attendant, then was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jingzhou.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Song served as General of the Martial Guard concurrently Palace Attendant, and was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 嵩表曰：「蕭寶卷骨肉相殘，忠良先戮，臣下囂然，莫不離背，君臣攜貳，干戈日尋。
entries.en: Song memorialized, "Xiao Baojuan slaughters his own kin and kills loyal men first. His ministers are in uproar and all are turning from him. Ruler and ministers are divided, and war grows daily.
entries.literal: Song memorialized, "Xiao Baojuan's own flesh and blood harm one another, loyal and good men are first killed, his ministers are in uproar, and none fails to leave and turn away. Ruler and ministers are divided, and weapons are sought daily.

entries.zh: 流聞寶卷雍州刺史蕭衍兄懿於建業阻兵，與寶卷相持，荊郢二州刺史並是寶卷之弟，必有圖衍之志。
entries.en: I have heard that Xiao Yi, elder brother of Xiao Yan, Baojuan's Inspector of Yongzhou, is holding troops at Jianye against Baojuan; the Inspectors of Jingzhou and Yingzhou are both Baojuan's younger brothers and surely plan to move against Yan.
entries.literal: I have heard it said that Xiao Yi, elder brother of Baojuan's Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Yan, is holding troops at Jianye and opposing Baojuan, while the Inspectors of Jingzhou and Yingzhou are both Baojuan's younger brothers and surely intend to scheme against Yan.

entries.zh: 臣若遣書相聞，迎其本謀，冀獲同心，并力除衍。
entries.en: If I send letters and meet them in their own plans, we may act with one mind and combine forces to eliminate Yan.
entries.literal: If I send letters to communicate with them and meet their original plan, I hope to obtain common purpose and combine strength to eliminate Yan.

entries.zh: 平衍之後，彼必旋師赴救丹陽，當不能復經營疆陲，全固襄沔。
entries.en: Once Yan is pacified, they will have to turn back to rescue Danyang and will no longer be able to manage the frontier or secure Xiang and Mian.
entries.literal: After Yan is pacified, they will surely turn their armies back to rescue Danyang, and then will no longer be able to manage the frontier and fully secure Xiang and Mian.

entries.zh: 臣之軍威已得臨據，則沔南之地可一舉而收。
entries.en: If our army has already established a commanding position, the land south of the Mian can be taken in a single move.
entries.literal: If my army's power has already reached and occupied a commanding position, then the land south of the Mian can be taken in one move.

entries.zh: 緣漢曜兵，示以威德，思歸有道者則引而納之，受疑告危者則援而接之。
entries.en: If we display troops along the Han and show both power and virtue, those who wish to return to the Way can be welcomed, and those in danger under suspicion can be rescued and received.
entries.literal: By displaying troops along the Han and showing them awe and virtue, those who think of returning to the Way can be drawn in and received, and those who are under suspicion and report danger can be aided and accepted.

entries.zh: 總兵竚銳，觀釁伺隙，若其零落之形已彰，怠懈之勢已著，便可順流摧鋒，長驅席卷。」
entries.en: With troops gathered and ready, we can watch for cracks and openings. Once their collapse is clear and their slackness plain, we can move with the current, break their front, drive deep, and sweep them up like a mat."
entries.literal: With the army gathered and its edge held ready, we can observe rifts and wait for openings. If their form of collapse is already clear and their slackened condition already manifest, then we can follow the current, crush their front, drive deep, and roll them up like a mat."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「所陳嘉謀，深是良計。
entries.en: The edict said, "The fine plan you present is truly sound strategy.
entries.literal: The edict said, "The excellent plan you set forth is deeply a good strategy.

entries.zh: 如當機形可進，任將軍裁之。」
entries.en: If the moment and situation permit an advance, the General may decide."
entries.literal: If the opportunity and situation allow advance, it is entrusted to the General to decide."

entries.zh: 既而蕭衍尋克建業，乃止。
entries.en: Soon afterward Xiao Yan captured Jianye, and the plan was dropped.
entries.literal: Soon afterward Xiao Yan captured Jianye, and so the matter stopped.

entries.zh: 除平北將軍、恒州刺史。
entries.en: Song was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
entries.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 轉平東將軍、徐州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 又轉安南將軍、揚州刺史。
entries.en: He was later transferred again as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 蕭衍湘州刺史楊公則率眾二萬，屯軍洛口，姜慶真領卒五千，據於首陂，又遣其左軍將軍騫小眼，軍主何天祚、張俊興等率眾七千，攻圍陸城，嵩乃遣統軍封邁、王會等步騎八千討之。
entries.en: Yang Gongze, Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xiangzhou, led twenty thousand men to Luokou; Jiang Qingzhen led five thousand to Shoubei; and Yan sent Left Army General Qian Xiaoyan, with army commanders He Tianzuo, Zhang Junxing, and others, leading seven thousand men to besiege Lucheng. Song sent Feng Mai, Wang Hui, and other commanders with eight thousand infantry and cavalry against them.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xiangzhou Yang Gongze led twenty thousand men and stationed his army at Luokou; Jiang Qingzhen led five thousand soldiers and occupied Shoubei; and Yan also sent his Left Army General Qian Xiaoyan, army commanders He Tianzuo, Zhang Junxing, and others with seven thousand men to attack and surround Lucheng. Song then sent Commanders Feng Mai, Wang Hui, and others with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to attack them.

entries.zh: 邁達陸城，賊皆夜遁，追擊破之，斬獲數千，公則、慶真退還馬頭。
entries.en: When Feng Mai reached Lucheng, the rebels fled by night. He pursued and defeated them, killing or capturing several thousand, while Gongze and Qingzhen retreated to Matou.
entries.literal: When Mai reached Lucheng, the rebels all fled by night; he pursued and defeated them, beheading and capturing several thousand, and Gongze and Qingzhen retreated back to Matou.

entries.zh: 衍徐州刺史昌義之屯據高皇，遣三軍潛寇陰陵，以淮水淺竭，不通船艦，屯於馬頭。
entries.en: Chang Yizhi, Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou, held Gaohuang and sent three armies in a secret raid on Yinling. Since the Huai was too shallow for boats to pass, he stationed at Matou.
entries.literal: Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou Chang Yizhi garrisoned and occupied Gaohuang, and sent three armies secretly to raid Yinling. Because the Huai water was shallow and exhausted and boats could not pass, he stationed at Matou.

entries.zh: 衍將田道龍、何景先等領卒三千已至衡山，規寇陸城。
entries.en: Yan's generals Tian Daolong, He Jingxian, and others led three thousand soldiers to Hengshan, planning to raid Lucheng.
entries.literal: Yan's generals Tian Daolong, He Jingxian, and others led three thousand soldiers and had already reached Hengshan, planning to raid Lucheng.

entries.zh: 寇並充逼。
entries.en: The raiders pressed in from all sides.
entries.literal: The raiders were all pressing in densely.

entries.zh: 嵩遣兼統軍李叔仁等援合肥、小峴、楊石，頻戰破之。
entries.en: Song sent acting Commander Li Shuren and others to reinforce Hefei, Xiaoxian, and Yangshi, repeatedly defeating the enemy in battle.
entries.literal: Song sent acting Commander Li Shuren and others to reinforce Hefei, Xiaoxian, and Yangshi, and in repeated battles they defeated them.

entries.zh: 衍征虜將軍趙草屯於黃口，嵩遣軍司趙熾等往討之，先遣統軍安伯醜潛師夜渡，伏兵下蔡。
entries.en: Zhao Cao, Yan's General Who Conquers Caitiffs, was stationed at Huangkou. Song sent Army Marshal Zhao Chi and others to attack, first dispatching Commander An Bochou to cross secretly by night and set an ambush at Xiacai.
entries.literal: Yan's General Who Conquers Caitiffs Zhao Cao was stationed at Huangkou. Song sent Army Marshal Zhao Chi and others to attack him, first sending Commander An Bochou to lead a hidden force across by night and place ambush troops at Xiacai.

entries.zh: 草率卒四千，逆來拒戰，伯醜與下蔡戍主王虎等前後夾擊，大敗之，俘斬溺死四千餘人。
entries.en: Zhao Cao led four thousand men to meet them. An Bochou and Wang Hu, commander of Xiacai Garrison, struck from front and rear, badly defeated him, and captured, killed, or drowned more than four thousand men.
entries.literal: Cao led four thousand soldiers to come against them and resist in battle; Bochou and Wang Hu, commander of the Xiacai Garrison, attacked from front and rear and greatly defeated him, capturing, beheading, and drowning more than four thousand men.

entries.zh: 統軍李叔仁等夜襲硤石之賊，又破之。
entries.en: Commander Li Shuren and others made a night attack on the rebels at Xiashi and defeated them as well.
entries.literal: Commander Li Shuren and others made a night attack on the rebels at Xiashi and again defeated them.

entries.zh: 衍將姜慶真專據肥汭，冠軍將軍曹天寶屯於鷄口，軍主尹明世屯東硤石。
entries.en: Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen held Feirui, Champion General Cao Tianbao was stationed at Jikou, and army commander Yin Mingshi at Eastern Xiashi.
entries.literal: Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen alone occupied Feirui, Champion General Cao Tianbao was stationed at Jikou, and army commander Yin Mingshi was stationed at Eastern Xiashi.

entries.zh: 嵩遣別將羊引次于淮西，去賊營十里，司馬趙熾率兵一萬為表裏聲勢。
entries.en: Song sent the separate general Yang Yin to camp at Huaixi, ten li from the rebel camp, while Marshal Zhao Chi led ten thousand troops to create pressure from inside and outside.
entries.literal: Song sent separate general Yang Yin to halt at Huaixi, ten li from the rebel camp, while Marshal Zhao Chi led ten thousand soldiers to form an inner and outer show of force.

entries.zh: 眾軍既會，分擊賊之四壘。
entries.en: When the armies had assembled, they split up and attacked the rebels' four forts.
entries.literal: Once the various armies had assembled, they divided and attacked the rebels' four fortifications.

entries.zh: 四壘之賊，戰敗奔走，斬獲數千，溺死萬數。
entries.en: The rebels in the four forts were defeated and fled; several thousand were killed or captured, and tens of thousands drowned.
entries.literal: The rebels in the four fortifications were defeated in battle and fled; several thousand were beheaded or captured, and those who drowned were counted by the ten thousand.

entries.zh: 統軍牛敬賓攻硤石，明世宵遁。
entries.en: Commander Niu Jingbin attacked Xiashi, and Yin Mingshi fled by night.
entries.literal: Commander Niu Jingbin attacked Xiashi, and Mingshi fled by night.

entries.zh: 慶真合餘燼浮淮下，下蔡戍主王略截流擊之，俘斬太半。
entries.en: Jiang Qingzhen gathered the remnants and moved down the Huai; Wang Lue, commander of Xiacai Garrison, intercepted him on the river and captured or killed more than half.
entries.literal: Qingzhen gathered the remaining embers and floated down the Huai; Wang Lue, commander of the Xiacai Garrison, cut off the current and attacked him, capturing and beheading more than half.

entries.zh: 於是威名大振。
entries.en: Thereafter Song's reputation for military power greatly flourished.
entries.literal: Thereupon Song's awe-inspiring reputation greatly flourished.

entries.zh: 後為蒼頭李太伯等同謀害嵩，并妻穆氏及子世賢。
entries.en: Later Li Taibo and other cangtou retainers conspired to murder Song, together with his wife Lady Mu and his son Shixian.
entries.literal: Later the cangtou Li Taibo and others conspired together and murdered Song, along with his wife Lady Mu and his son Shixian.

entries.zh: 世宗為嵩舉哀於東堂，賻絹一千匹，贈車騎將軍、領軍，諡曰剛侯。
entries.en: Shizong held mourning for Song in the Eastern Hall, granted one thousand bolts of silk for the funeral, posthumously awarded him General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander of the Guards, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Gang.
entries.literal: Shizong raised mourning for Song in the Eastern Hall, gave one thousand bolts of silk for funeral expenses, posthumously granted him General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander of the Guards, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Gang.

entries.zh: 第二子世儁，頗有幹用，而無行業。
entries.en: His second son Shijun had some practical ability but no moral conduct.
entries.literal: His second son Shijun had considerable practical ability, but no moral conduct.

entries.zh: 襲爵，除給事中、東宮舍人。
entries.en: He inherited the title and was appointed Supervising Attendant and Household Gentleman of the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: He inherited the title and was appointed Supervising Attendant and Household Gentleman of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 伯父澄表求轉階授之，於是除員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: His uncle Cheng memorialized asking that a rank be transferred to him, and Shijun was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Outside the Ranks.
entries.literal: His uncle Cheng memorialized requesting that his rank be transferred and awarded to him, and thereupon he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Outside the Ranks.

entries.zh: 肅宗時，追論嵩勳，封世儁衞縣開國男，食邑二百戶。
entries.en: In Suzong's reign, Song's merits were reviewed, and Shijun was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Wei County with two hundred households.
entries.literal: In Suzong's time, Song's merit was retrospectively discussed, and Shijun was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Wei County, with a fief of two hundred households.

entries.zh: 遷冠軍將軍、宗正少卿，又為散騎常侍、安南將軍、武衞將軍、河南尹。
entries.en: He rose to Champion General and Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, then served as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Martial Guard, and Governor of Henan.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Champion General and Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, and later became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Martial Guard, and Governor of Henan.

entries.zh: 尋除鎮東將軍、青州刺史，轉征東將軍，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qingzhou, then transferred to General Who Conquers the East with the added title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
