entries.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qingzhou, transferred to General Who Conquers the East, and additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 邢杲之亂，圍逼州城，世儁憑城拒守，遂得保全。
entries.en: During Xing Gao's rebellion, the provincial city was surrounded and pressed hard. Shijun held the walls and defended it, preserving the city intact.
entries.literal: During Xing Gao's rebellion, Gao surrounded and pressed the provincial city, and Shijun relied on the walls to resist and defend, so that it was preserved intact.

entries.zh: 孝莊時，除衞將軍、吏部尚書。
entries.en: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was appointed General of the Guard and Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time, he was appointed General of the Guard and Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 爾朱兆寇京師，詔世儁以本官為都督，防守河橋。
entries.en: When Erzhu Zhao raided the capital, an edict kept Shijun in his current office and made him Commander-in-Chief for the defense of Heqiao.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Zhao raided the capital, an edict appointed Shijun, in his original office, as Commander-in-Chief to defend Heqiao.

entries.zh: 及兆至河，世儁初無拒守意，便隔岸遙拜，時論疾之。
entries.en: When Zhao reached the river, Shijun had no intention of resisting. He immediately bowed from across the bank, and public opinion despised him.
entries.literal: When Zhao reached the river, Shijun from the start had no intention of resisting and defending, and at once bowed from across the bank; opinion at the time detested him.

entries.zh: 前廢帝世，為驃騎將軍，仍加尚書，尤為爾朱世隆所昵。
entries.en: Under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was General of Agile Cavalry with the added title Minister of State Affairs, and he was especially close to Erzhu Shilong.
entries.literal: In the reign of the Former Deposed Emperor, he was General of Agile Cavalry and was additionally made Minister of State Affairs; he was especially intimate with Erzhu Shilong.

entries.zh: 出帝初，加儀同三司，改封武陽縣開國子，食邑五百戶。
entries.en: At the start of the Emperor Who Went Out's reign, he was given Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and re-enfeoffed as Founding Viscount of Wuyang County with five hundred households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the reign of the Emperor Who Went Out, he was given Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, his enfeoffment was changed to Founding Viscount of Wuyang County, with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 世儁居選曹，不能厲心，多所受納，為中尉彈糾，坐免官。
entries.en: While Shijun served in the selections bureau, he failed to discipline himself and accepted many gifts. The Censor-in-Chief impeached him, and he was dismissed.
entries.literal: When Shijun occupied the selections bureau, he could not discipline his mind and accepted many gifts; he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief and dismissed from office for the offense.

entries.zh: 尋復本職。
entries.en: Soon he was restored to his former office.
entries.literal: Soon he was restored to his original office.

entries.zh: 孝靜初，加侍中、尚書右僕射，遷尚書令。
entries.en: At the start of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was made Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then promoted to Director of the Department.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was given the added title Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was promoted to Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 世儁輕薄，好去就，詔送晉陽。
entries.en: Shijun was frivolous and fond of shifting allegiance, so an edict sent him to Jinyang.
entries.literal: Shijun was frivolous and liked to shift his allegiances, so an edict sent him to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 興和中，薨。
entries.en: He died in the Xinghe era.
entries.literal: In the Xinghe era, he died.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、都督冀定瀛殷四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、太傅、定州刺史，尚書令、開國公如故，諡曰躁戾。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Inspector of Dingzhou, while retaining Director of the Department of State Affairs and Founding Duke as before. His posthumous title was Zaoli.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Inspector of Dingzhou; Director of the Department of State Affairs and Founding Duke remained as before; his posthumous title was Zaoli.

entries.zh: 子景遠襲，散騎侍郎。
entries.en: His son Jingyuan succeeded and served as Cavalier Attendant.
entries.literal: His son Jingyuan succeeded; he was Cavalier Attendant.

entries.zh: 世賢弟世哲，武定中，吏部郎。
entries.en: Shixian's younger brother Shizhe served in the Wuding era as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: Shixian's younger brother Shizhe, in the Wuding era, was Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 嵩弟贍，字道周。
entries.en: Song's younger brother Zhan was styled Daozhou.
entries.literal: Song's younger brother Zhan was styled Daozhou.

entries.zh: 高祖時，自□大夫稍遷宗正少卿、龍驤將軍、光州刺史、散騎常侍、左將軍，遷平東將軍、兗州刺史。
entries.en: In Gaozu's time, from a Grandee title with one missing character, he gradually rose to Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, Longxiang General, Inspector of Guangzhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Left, then was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's time, from a Grandee title with one character missing he gradually rose to Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, Longxiang General, Inspector of Guangzhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Left, and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 頗愛書史，而貪暴好殺。
entries.en: He had some love for books and histories, but was greedy, violent, and fond of killing.
entries.literal: He rather loved books and histories, but was greedy, violent, and fond of killing.

entries.zh: 澄深恥忿之，絕其往來。
entries.en: Cheng was deeply ashamed and angered by him and broke off all contact.
entries.literal: Cheng was deeply ashamed and angered by him and cut off dealings with him.

entries.zh: 有四子。
entries.en: He had four sons.
entries.literal: He had four sons.

entries.zh: 長子遠，尚書郎。
entries.en: The eldest son, Yuan, was a Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: The eldest son, Yuan, was a Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：顯祖之將禪讓，可謂國之大節。
entries.en: The historian says: When Xianzu was about to abdicate, it was a great test of the state.
entries.literal: The historian says: When Xianzu was about to abdicate, it may be called a great joint of the state.

entries.zh: 康王毅然庭諍，德音孔昭，一言興邦，其斯之謂歟？
entries.en: Prince Kang remonstrated firmly in court, his virtuous words shining clearly; one word raised the state. Is this not the phrase made real?
entries.literal: Prince Kang firmly remonstrated in court, and his virtuous words were very bright; one word raised the state. Is this not what is meant?

entries.zh: 文宣貞固俊遠，鬱為宗傑，身因累朝，寧濟夷險，既社稷是任，其梁棟之望也。
entries.en: Wenxuan was upright, firm, outstanding, and far-seeing, a flourishing hero of the imperial clan. Serving through successive reigns, calm in ease and danger, he bore responsibility for the state and was the hope of its beams and pillars.
entries.literal: Wenxuan was upright, firm, outstanding, and far-reaching, richly becoming a hero of the imperial clan; in person he followed successive reigns, calmly crossing ease and danger, and since the altars of state were entrusted to him, he was the hope of beams and pillars.

entries.zh: 順謇諤俶儻，有汲黯之風，不用於時，橫招非命，惜矣。
entries.en: Shun was blunt and free-spirited, with the air of Ji An. Unused by his time, he wrongly met an untimely death. A pity!
entries.literal: Shun was blunt in remonstrance and free in spirit, with the manner of Ji An. Not used by his age, he unjustly met untimely death. A pity!

entries.zh: 嵩有行陳之氣，儁則裂冠之徒歟？
entries.en: Song had the spirit of the battle line; Jun was surely a cap-tearing sort of man, was he not?
entries.literal: Song had the spirit of the battle line, while Jun was the sort of man who tears the cap, was he not?

entries.zh: 熙既蕃王之貴，加有文學，好奇愛異，交結偉俊，風氣甚高，名美當世，先達後進，多造其門。
entries.en: A frontier prince and a man of letters, he sought out brilliant company; the age praised him, and many came to his door.
entries.literal: Xi, being noble among the frontier princes, moreover had literature; he loved the strange and cherished the different, formed ties with great and handsome men, his air very lofty, his name beautiful in the age—elders before and juniors after, many came to his gate.

entries.zh: 始熙之鎮鄴也，知友才學之士袁翻、李琰、李神儁、王誦兄弟、裴敬憲等咸餞於河梁，賦詩告別。
entries.en: When he left for Ye, Yuan Fan, Li Shenjun, the Wang brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others saw him off at River Bridge with poems.
entries.literal: When Xi first went to govern Ye, talented literary men Yuan Fan, Li Yan, Li Shenjun, the Wang Song brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others all saw him off at River Bridge, composing poems in farewell.

entries.zh: 及熙將死，復與知故書曰：「吾與弟並蒙皇太后知遇，兄據大州，弟則入侍，殷勤言色，恩同慈母。
entries.en: Before death he wrote to friends: "My brother and I were cherished by the Empress Dowager—he in a great province, I at court—treated like sons.
entries.literal: When Xi was about to die he again wrote to old friends: "I and my younger brother both received the Empress Dowager's knowing encounter; elder brother held a great province, younger brother then entered attendance—earnest words and color, grace like a loving mother.

entries.zh: 今皇太后見廢北宮，太傅清河王橫受屠酷，主上幼年，獨在前殿。
entries.en: Now she is confined in the North Palace, Prince Yi was butchered, and the boy emperor sits alone.
entries.literal: Now the Empress Dowager is deposed in the North Palace; the Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe was slaughtered across; the lord is young, alone in the front hall.

entries.zh: 君親如此，無以自安，故率兵民建大義於天下。
entries.en: I could not rest; I raised arms in the name of righteousness.
entries.literal: Lord and kin thus—I cannot be at peace; therefore I lead soldiers and people to raise great righteousness under Heaven.

entries.zh: 但智力淺短，旋見囚執，上慚朝廷，下愧相知。
entries.en: My wits were short; I was seized at once—shame to the court, shame to you.
entries.literal: But my strength and wit shallow and short—soon I was seized; above I shame the court, below I fail my friends.

entries.zh: 本以名義干心，不得不爾，流腸碎首，復何言哉！
entries.en: Duty drove me; guts spill—what more can I say?
entries.literal: Originally it was fame and duty that moved my heart—I could not do otherwise; guts streaming, head smashed—what more is there to say!

entries.zh: 昔李斯憶上蔡黃犬，陸機想華亭鶴唳，豈不以恍惚無際，一去不還者乎？
entries.en: Li Si remembered Shangcai's yellow dog; Lu Ji the crane at Huating—gone, never back.
entries.literal: In old times Li Si remembered the yellow dog of Shangcai; Lu Ji thought of the crane's cry at Huating—was it not because illusion has no bound, once gone never to return?

entries.zh: 今欲對秋月，臨春風，藉芳草，蔭花樹，廣召名勝，賦詩洛濱，其可得乎？
entries.en: I will not face the moon, the wind, the grass, the trees, or poems on the Luo again.
entries.literal: Now I wish to face the autumn moon, meet the spring wind, lean on fragrant grass, shade flowering trees, broadly summon famous guests, compose poems on the Luo shore—can it be obtained?

entries.zh: 凡百君子，各敬爾宜，為國為身，善勗名節，立功立事，為身而已，吾何言哉！」
entries.en: Live for the state and for yourselves; make merit; I have no more words."
entries.literal: All you gentlemen, each respect your proper conduct; for the state and for the body, well urge fame and integrity, establish merit and affairs—for the body alone—what have I to say!

entries.zh: 時人憐之。
entries.en: Men pitied him.
entries.literal: People of the time pitied him.

entries.zh: 南安王楨，皇興二年封，加征南大將軍、中都大官，尋遷內都大官。
entries.en: Zhen, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed in Huangxing year 2, made Grand General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, and soon moved to the inner directorate.
entries.literal: Zhen, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing, appointed Grand General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, and soon transferred to Director of the Inner Palace within the capital.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，除涼州鎮都大將。
entries.en: At Gaozu's accession he was made commander of Liangzhou Garrison.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Grand General of Liangzhou Garrison.

entries.zh: 尋以綏撫有能，加都督西戎諸軍事、征西大將軍、領護西域校尉、儀同三司、涼州刺史。
entries.en: Soon, for skill in pacification, he was added commander of Western Rong armies, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Protector-General of the Western Regions, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Liangzhou.
entries.literal: Soon, for able pacification, he was added commander of all military affairs of the Western Rong, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Protector-General of the Western Regions, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 徵為內都大官，出為使持節、侍中、本將軍、開府、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。
entries.en: He was recalled to the inner directorate, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff and Palace Attendant with his former rank, an open office, command of Chang'an Garrison, and the Yongzhou inspectorate.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Inner Palace within the capital, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, his former rank, with an open office, Grand General of Chang'an Garrison, and Inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 楨性忠謹，事母以孝聞，賜帛千匹以褒之。
entries.en: Zhen was loyal and careful, famed for filial service to his mother; the court gave him a thousand bolts of silk in praise.
entries.literal: Zhen was by nature loyal and careful; he served his mother with a fame for filial piety and was rewarded with a thousand bolts of silk in praise.

entries.zh: 文成皇帝七男：孝元皇后生獻文皇帝。
entries.en: Emperor Wencheng had seven sons: Empress Xiaoyuan bore Emperor Xianwen.
entries.literal: Emperor Wencheng had seven sons: Empress Xiaoyuan bore Emperor Xianwen.

entries.zh: 李夫人生安樂厲王長樂。
entries.en: Lady Li bore Changle, Prince Li of Anle.
entries.literal: Lady Li bore Changle, Prince Li of Anle.

entries.zh: 曹夫人生廣川莊王略。
entries.en: Lady Cao bore Lue, Prince Zhuang of Guangchuan.
entries.literal: Lady Cao bore Lue, Prince Zhuang of Guangchuan.

entries.zh: 沮渠夫人生齊郡順王簡。
entries.en: Lady Juqu bore Jian, Prince Shun of Qi Commandery.
entries.literal: Lady Juqu bore Jian, Prince Shun of Qi Commandery.

entries.zh: 乙夫人生河間孝王若。
entries.en: Lady Yi bore Ruo, Prince Xiao of Hejian.
entries.literal: Lady Yi bore Ruo, Prince Xiao of Hejian.

entries.zh: 悅夫人生安豐匡王猛。
entries.en: Lady Yue bore Meng, Prince Kuang of Anfeng.
entries.literal: Lady Yue bore Meng, Prince Kuang of Anfeng.

entries.zh: 玄夫人生韓哀王安平，王早薨，無傳。
entries.en: Lady Xuan bore Anping, Prince Ai of Han; the prince died young and has no biography.
entries.literal: Lady Xuan bore Anping, Prince Ai of Han; the prince died young and has no biography.

entries.zh: 子靈道，襲。
entries.en: His son Lingdao succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Lingdao inherited.

entries.zh: 卒，諡悼王。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Dao.
entries.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Dao.

entries.zh: 齊郡王簡，字叔亮。
entries.en: Jian, Prince of Qi Commandery, was styled Shuliang.
entries.literal: Jian, Prince of Qi Commandery, was styled Shuliang.

entries.zh: 太和五年封，位中都大官。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed in Taihe year 5 and served as Chief Official of the Central Capital.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed in Taihe year 5 and held office as Chief Official of the Central Capital.

entries.zh: 簡母，沮渠牧犍女也。
entries.en: Jian's mother was a daughter of Juqu Mujian.
entries.literal: Jian's mother was a daughter of Juqu Mujian.

entries.zh: 簡性貌特類外祖。
entries.en: In temperament and looks, Jian closely resembled his maternal grandfather.
entries.literal: In nature and appearance, Jian especially resembled his maternal grandfather.

entries.zh: 後為內都大官。
entries.en: Later he became Chief Official of the Inner Capital.
entries.literal: Later he became Chief Official of the Inner Capital.

entries.zh: 高祖嘗與簡俱朝文明太后於皇信堂，簡居帝之右，行家人禮。
entries.en: Gaozu once paid court to Empress Dowager Wenming with Jian at Huangxin Hall. Jian sat to the emperor's right, and they observed family rites.
entries.literal: Gaozu once attended on Empress Dowager Wenming with Jian at Huangxin Hall; Jian occupied the emperor's right side, and they observed the rites of family members.

entries.zh: 遷太保。
entries.en: He was promoted to Grand Protector.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Grand Protector.

entries.zh: 高祖仁孝，以諸父零落，存者唯簡。
entries.en: Gaozu was benevolent and filial; his uncles had died off, and only Jian remained.
entries.literal: Gaozu was benevolent and filial; his uncles had fallen away, and only Jian remained alive.

entries.zh: 每見，立以待之，俟坐，致敬問起居，停簡拜伏。
entries.en: Whenever he saw Jian, he stood to wait for him; once Jian was seated, Gaozu respectfully asked after his health and prevented him from bowing prostrate.
entries.literal: Whenever he saw Jian, he stood waiting for him; after Jian was seated, he showed respect, asked after his health, and stopped Jian from bowing prostrate.

entries.zh: 簡性好酒，不能理公私之事。
entries.en: Jian loved wine by nature and could not manage public or private affairs.
entries.literal: Jian loved wine by nature and could not manage public or private affairs.

entries.zh: 妻常氏，燕郡公常喜女也，文明太后以賜簡。
entries.en: His wife, Lady Chang, was a daughter of Chang Xi, Duke of Yan Commandery, and Empress Dowager Wenming gave her to Jian.
entries.literal: His wife, Lady Chang, was a daughter of Chang Xi, Duke of Yan Commandery, and Empress Dowager Wenming bestowed her on Jian.

entries.zh: 性幹綜家事，頗節斷簡酒，乃至盜竊，求乞婢侍，卒不能禁。
entries.en: She was naturally capable in managing household affairs and tried hard to limit Jian's drinking; he even stole and begged wine from maidservants and attendants, and in the end she could not stop him.
entries.literal: By nature she was capable at managing household affairs and rather sharply restricted Jian's wine; he went so far as to steal it and beg maidservants and attendants for it, but in the end she could not stop him.

entries.zh: 二十三年薨。
entries.en: He died in the twenty-third year.
entries.literal: He died in the twenty-third year.

entries.zh: 時高祖不豫，詔曰：「叔父薨背，痛慕摧絕，不自勝任，但虛頓床枕，未堪奉赴，當力疾發哀。」
entries.en: Gaozu was ill at the time and issued an edict: "My uncle has passed away; grief and longing crush me beyond endurance. I am weak and confined to bed, and cannot yet attend in person, but I will force myself through illness to express my mourning."
entries.literal: At the time Gaozu was unwell. He issued an edict: "My uncle has died and departed; grief and longing crush me beyond what I can bear. But I am weak and prostrate on bed and pillow and cannot yet go to attend in person. I shall force myself through illness to send forth mourning."

entries.zh: 諡曰靈王。
entries.en: He was posthumously named Prince Ling.
entries.literal: He was posthumously named Prince Ling.

entries.zh: 世宗時，改諡曰順。
entries.en: In Shizong's time, the posthumous name was changed to Shun.
entries.literal: In Shizong's time, the posthumous name was changed to Shun.

entries.zh: 子祐，字伯授，襲。
entries.en: His son You, styled Boshou, succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son You, styled Boshou, succeeded him.

entries.zh: 母常氏，高祖以納不以禮，不許其為妃。
entries.en: Because his mother, Lady Chang, had not been taken as consort according to proper ritual, Gaozu did not permit her to be made princess.
entries.literal: His mother, Lady Chang, had been taken by Gaozu in a manner that did not conform to ritual, so he did not permit her to become the princess.

entries.zh: 世宗以母從子貴，詔特拜為齊國太妃。
entries.en: Shizong held that a mother follows the rank of her son and issued an edict specially appointing her Grand Princess Dowager of Qi.
entries.literal: Shizong, on the grounds that a mother follows the rank of her son, issued an edict specially appointing her Grand Princess Dowager of Qi.

entries.zh: 祐位涇州刺史。
entries.en: You served as Inspector of Jingzhou.
entries.literal: You held office as Inspector of Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 薨，諡曰敬。
entries.en: When he died, he was posthumously named Jing.
entries.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Jing.

entries.zh: 河間王若，字叔儒。
entries.en: Ruo, Prince of Hejian, was styled Shuru.
entries.literal: Ruo, Prince of Hejian, was styled Shuru.

entries.zh: 年十六，未封而薨，追封河間，諡曰孝。
entries.en: He died at sixteen before receiving a fief; he was posthumously made Prince of Hejian and given the posthumous name Xiao.
entries.literal: At age sixteen he died before being enfeoffed; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Hejian and given the posthumous name Xiao.

entries.zh: 詔京兆康王子太安為後。
entries.en: An edict appointed Taian, son of Prince Kang of Jingzhao, as his heir.
entries.literal: An edict made Taian, son of Prince Kang of Jingzhao, his heir.

entries.zh: 太安於若為從弟，非相後之義，廢之，以齊郡王子琛繼。
entries.en: Taian was Ruo's younger cousin, which did not accord with the principles of succession, so he was removed and Chen, son of the Prince of Qi Commandery, succeeded instead.
entries.literal: Taian was Ruo's younger cousin, which was not the principle for making one heir to another, so he was removed and Chen, son of the Prince of Qi Commandery, was made successor.

entries.zh: 安樂王長樂，皇興四年封建昌王，後改封安樂王。
entries.en: Changle, Prince of Anle, was made Prince of Jianchang in Huangxing year 4 and later transferred to Anle.
entries.literal: Prince of Anle Changle, in the fourth year of Huangxing was enfeoffed Prince of Changchang, later changed to Prince of Anle.

entries.zh: 長樂性凝重，顯祖器愛之。
entries.en: Changle was sober and steady in temperament; Xianzu prized and favored him.
entries.literal: Changle was by nature grave and steady; Xianzu valued and loved him.

entries.zh: 承明元年拜太尉，出為定州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Chenming he became Grand Commandant and went out as Dingzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In the first year of Chenming he was appointed Grand Commandant and sent out as Inspector of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 鞭撻豪右，頓辱衣冠，多不奉法，為人所患。
entries.en: He lashed powerful clans and shamed the gentry; many broke the law under him, and he was widely hated.
entries.literal: He flogged powerful families and humiliated the gentry; many did not keep the law and were resented.

entries.zh: 百姓詣闕訟其過。
entries.en: Commoners went to the capital to accuse him of misconduct.
entries.literal: The common people went to the capital to sue him for his faults.

entries.zh: 高祖罰杖三十。
entries.en: Gaozu had him beaten thirty strokes with the staff.
entries.literal: Gaozu punished him with thirty strokes of the staff.

entries.zh: 貪暴彌甚，以罪徵詣京師。
entries.en: His greed and brutality only deepened, until crimes brought him summoned to the capital.
entries.literal: His greed and violence grew worse; for crime he was summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 後與內行長乙肆虎謀為不軌，事發，賜死於家。
entries.en: Later he plotted treason with Inner-Steward Chief Yi Sihu; when it was exposed he was ordered to take his own life at home.
entries.literal: Later he and Inner-Steward Chief Yi Sihu plotted rebellion; when the affair broke out he was ordered to die at home.

entries.zh: 葬以王禮，諡曰厲。
entries.en: He was buried with princely honors and given the posthumous name Li, meaning Fierce.
entries.literal: He was buried with princely rites; posthumous title Li.

entries.zh: 子諧，字仲和，襲。
entries.en: His son Xie, styled Zhonghe, succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Xie, style Zhonghe, inherited.

entries.zh: 十九年薨。
entries.en: He died in Taihe year 19.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕宗室多故，從弟諧喪逝，悲痛摧割，不能已已。
entries.en: An edict read: "The imperial house has suffered too many losses; my cousin Xie is gone, and grief cuts so deep I cannot master it.
entries.literal: An edict said: "My imperial clan has known many losses; my younger cousin Xie has passed away, and grief cuts me so I cannot stop.

entries.zh: 古者，大臣之喪，有三臨之禮，此蓋三公已上。
entries.en: In antiquity great ministers were mourned with three personal visits—a rite reserved for the Three Excellencies and above.
entries.literal: In antiquity, for the mourning of great ministers there was the rite of three personal visits—this applied to those of the rank of the Three Excellencies and above.

entries.zh: 至於卿司已下，故應。
entries.en: Ministers and offices below them were expected to attend in due measure.
entries.literal: As for ministers and offices below that, they should attend accordingly.

entries.zh: 闕自漢已降，多無此禮。
entries.en: Since Han times the rite has largely fallen away.
entries.literal: Since Han and downward the rite has largely been absent.

entries.zh: 朕欲遵古典，哀感從情，雖以尊降伏，私痛寧爽。
entries.en: I mean to follow the ancient canon and let compassion follow feeling; though rank demands restraint, private pain will not ease.
entries.literal: I wish to follow the ancient canon and let compassion follow feeling; though I lower myself by rank, private pain will not be eased.

entries.zh: 欲令諸王有期親者為之三臨，大功之親者為之再臨，小功緦麻為之一臨。
entries.en: I would have princes in the closest mourning circle pay three visits, those in the great-achievement circle two, and those in lesser or finest mourning one.
entries.literal: I wish princes with kin in the period of mourning to make three visits, those of great-achievement kin to make two visits, and those of lesser-achievement and finest-mourning kin to make one visit.

entries.zh: 廣川王於朕大功，必欲再臨。
entries.en: Prince Guangchuan stands to me in the great-achievement circle; I shall certainly mourn him twice.
entries.literal: The Prince of Guangchuan bears to me a great-achievement bond; I must certainly pay two visits.

entries.zh: 再臨者，欲於大殮之日，親臨盡哀，成服之後，緦衰而弔。
entries.en: By two visits I mean: on the day of the great encoffment to come in person and exhaust grief, and after the mourning garments are complete to return in finest hemp and offer condolence.
entries.literal: The two visits mean: on the day of the great encoffment, to come in person and exhaust grief; after the mourning garments are complete, to go in finest hemp and offer condolence.

entries.zh: 既殯之緦麻，理在無疑，大殮之臨，當否如何？
entries.en: Condolence in finest hemp after encoffment is plainly required; but is a visit at the great encoffment itself fitting?
entries.literal: For finest-mourning kin after the encoffment there is no doubt in principle; as for the visit at the great encoffment—is it fitting or not?

entries.zh: 為須撫柩於始喪，為應盡哀於闔棺？
entries.en: Should one comfort the bier at the first mourning, or exhaust grief only when the coffin is closed?
entries.literal: Must one comfort the bier at the first mourning, or should one exhaust grief at the closing of the coffin?

entries.zh: 早晚之宜，擇其厥中。」
entries.en: Whether early or late is better—choose the mean."
entries.literal: As to whether early or late is proper, choose the mean between them."

entries.zh: 黃門侍郎崔光、宋弁，通直常侍劉芳，典命下大夫李元凱，中書侍郎高聰等議曰：[4]「三臨之事，乃自古禮，爰及漢魏，行之者稀。
entries.en: Cui Guang and Song Bian of the Yellow Gate, Liu Fang, regular attendant of direct transmission, Li Yuankai, master of ceremonies lower grandee, Gao Cong, secretariat attendant, and others replied:[4] "Three visits are an ancient rite, yet from Han through Wei few have practiced it.
entries.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Guang, Song Bian, Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission Liu Fang, Master of Ceremonies Lower Grandee Li Yuankai, Secretariat Attendant Gao Cong, and others deliberated:[4] "The matter of three visits is indeed an ancient rite; even through Han and Wei it has rarely been practiced.

entries.zh: 陛下至聖慈仁，方遵前軌，志必哀喪，慮同寧戚。
entries.en: Your Majesty is supremely sagely and benevolent and means to follow the former track; your will is true mourning, your heart the same as one dwelling in the mourning hut.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is supremely sagely and benevolent and is about to follow the former track; your will must mourn the dead and your thought is the same as dwelling in the mourning hut.

entries.zh: 臣等以為若期親三臨，大功宜再。
entries.en: We hold that if the closest kin pay three visits, great-achievement kin should pay two.
entries.literal: We your subjects consider that if period kin make three visits, great-achievement kin should make two.

entries.zh: 始喪之初，哀之至極，既以情降，宜從始喪。
entries.en: At the beginning of mourning grief is at its height; since feeling has already bent rank, the first visit should fall at the beginning of mourning.
entries.literal: At the beginning of first mourning grief is at its utmost; since feeling has already lowered rank, one should follow the beginning of mourning.

entries.zh: 大殮之臨，伏如聖旨。」
entries.en: As for the visit at the great encoffment, we bow to Your Majesty's intent."
entries.literal: As for the visit at the great encoffment, we bow to the sagely edict.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「魏晉已來，親臨多闕，至於戚臣，必於東堂哭之。
entries.en: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, emperors have rarely mourned in person; for ministerial kin they wept in the Eastern Hall instead.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, personal visits have largely been wanting; for kin among ministers one necessarily wept in the Eastern Hall.

entries.zh: 頃大司馬、安定王薨，朕既臨之後，復更受慰於東堂，今日之事，應更哭否？」
entries.en: When the Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, died I visited him in person and still received condolences in the Eastern Hall; for today's rite, should I weep there again?"
entries.literal: Recently when Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, died, after I had already visited him I again received condolences in the Eastern Hall; for today's affair, should I weep again?

entries.zh: 光等議曰：「東堂之哭，蓋以不臨之故。
entries.en: Guang and the others replied: "The Eastern Hall weeping existed because the emperor did not visit in person.
entries.literal: Guang and the others deliberated: "Weeping in the Eastern Hall was because one did not visit in person.

entries.zh: 今陛下躬親撫視，羣臣從駕，臣等參議，以為不宜復哭。」
entries.en: Now Your Majesty will comfort the bier in person and the ministers will follow your carriage—we hold there should be no second weeping."
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty in person comforts and views; the ministers follow the imperial carriage—we your subjects jointly consider that one should not weep again.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「若大司馬戚尊位重，必哭於東堂，而廣川既是諸王之子，又年位尚幼，卿等議之，朕無異焉。」
entries.en: An edict said: "For the Grand Marshal, kin of the highest rank, the Eastern Hall is required; but Guangchuan is a prince's son and still young in years and station—deliberate as you see fit; I raise no objection."
entries.literal: An edict said: "If the Grand Marshal is kin of weighty rank and position, one must weep in the Eastern Hall; yet Guangchuan is both a prince's son and still young in years and rank—you may deliberate as you will; I have no objection.

entries.zh: 諧將大殮，高祖素服深衣哭之，入室，哀慟，撫尸而出。
entries.en: On the eve of Xie's great encoffment Gaozu came in plain white and deep mourning, wept, entered the chamber, was overcome, comforted the corpse, and withdrew.
entries.literal: When Xie was about to undergo the great encoffment, Gaozu in plain white garments and deep mourning robes wept for him, entered the chamber, was stricken with grief, comforted the corpse, and went out.

entries.zh: 有司奏，廣川王妃薨於代京，未審以新尊從於卑舊，為宜卑舊來就新尊。
entries.en: The relevant office reported: the Princess of Guangchuan died in the Dai capital; it was unclear whether the newly honored dead should follow the humbler old, or the humbler old should be brought to the newly honored.
entries.literal: The relevant office memorialized: the Princess of Guangchuan died in the capital of Dai; it is unclear whether the newly honored should follow the humbler old, or the humbler old should come to the newly honored.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「遷洛之人，自茲厥後，悉可歸骸邙嶺，皆不得就塋恒代。
entries.en: An edict said: "For families who moved to Luoyang, from now on all may rest their bones on Mount Mang; none may bury in the old Dai tombs.
entries.literal: An edict said: "For those who moved to Luoyang, from this time onward all may return their bones to Mount Mang; none may bury at the old tombs in Dai.

entries.zh: 其有夫先葬在北，婦今喪在南，婦人從夫，宜還代葬；
entries.en: If the husband was buried first in the north and the wife dies in the south, the wife follows the husband and should return to Dai for burial;
entries.literal: Where the husband was first buried in the north and the wife now dies in the south, the woman follows the husband and should be returned for burial in Dai;

entries.zh: 若欲移父就母，亦得任之。
entries.en: if one wishes to move the father's grave to the mother's side, that may also be done.
entries.literal: if one wishes to move the father's grave to join the mother, that too may be done at will.

entries.zh: 其有妻墳於恒代，夫死於洛，不得以尊就卑；
entries.en: If the wife's tomb lies in Dai and the husband dies in Luoyang, rank may not draw the lofty down to the humble;
entries.literal: Where the wife's tomb is in Dai and the husband dies in Luo, one may not let rank draw the lofty to the humble;

entries.zh: 欲移母就父，宜亦從之；
entries.en: if one wishes to move the mother to the father, that should be allowed;
entries.literal: if one wishes to move the mother to join the father, that should also be followed;

entries.zh: 若異葬亦從之。
entries.en: separate burial may also be chosen.
entries.literal: if separate burial is desired, that too may be followed.

entries.zh: 若不在葬限，身在代喪，葬之彼此，皆得任之。
entries.en: If the case falls outside these limits and the mourner is in Dai, burial on either side is at choice.
entries.literal: If outside the burial limits, while the body lies in mourning in Dai, burial on either side may be done at will.

entries.zh: 其戶屬恒燕，身官京洛，去留之宜，亦從所擇。
entries.en: Where registers remain in Heng and Yan but office and person are in Jing and Luo, staying or leaving is likewise at choice.
entries.literal: Where household registers belong to Heng and Yan but office and person are in Jing and Luo, as to staying or leaving, that too follows choice.

entries.zh: 其屬諸州者，各得任意。」
entries.en: Those attached to other provinces may each decide for themselves."
entries.literal: Those attached to other provinces may each do as they wish.

entries.zh: 詔贈諧武衞將軍，諡曰剛。
entries.en: An edict posthumously made Xie General of Martial Guard and gave him the posthumous name Gang.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made Xie General of Martial Guard; posthumous title Gang.

entries.zh: 及葬，高祖親臨送之。
entries.en: At the burial Gaozu attended in person to see him off.
entries.literal: At the burial Gaozu in person attended and saw him off.

entries.zh: 琛字曇寶，幼而敏慧，高祖愛之。
entries.en: Chen, styled Tanbao, was clever even as a child; Gaozu doted on him.
entries.literal: Chen, style Tanbao, was clever and quick as a child; Gaozu loved him.

entries.zh: 世宗時，拜定州刺史。
entries.en: Under Shizong he became Dingzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In Shizong's time he was appointed Inspector of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 琛妃，世宗舅女，高皇后妹。
entries.en: Chen's consort was Shizong's niece by marriage, the younger sister of Empress Gao.
entries.literal: Chen's consort was Shizong's maternal niece, younger sister of Empress Gao.

entries.zh: 琛憑恃內外，多所受納，貪惏之極。
entries.en: Chen leaned on court and family ties and took endless bribes; his greed had no bottom.
entries.literal: Chen relied on inside and outside connections and received many bribes; his greed knew no limit.

entries.zh: 及還朝，靈太后詔曰：「琛在定州，惟不將中山宮來，自餘無所不致，何可更復敍用。」
entries.en: On his return Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "In Dingzhou Chen took everything but the Zhongshan Palace itself—how can he be used again?"
entries.literal: When he returned to court, Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "At Dingzhou Chen failed only to carry off the Zhongshan Palace; otherwise there was nothing he would not seize—how can he be employed again?"

entries.zh: 由是遂廢于家。
entries.en: He was thereupon dismissed and kept at home.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was dismissed and kept at home.

entries.zh: 琛以肅宗始學，獻金字孝經。
entries.en: When Suzong first took up his studies, Chen presented a gilt-letter Classic of Filial Piety.
entries.literal: When Suzong first began his studies, Chen presented a gilt-letter Classic of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 又無方自達，乃與劉騰為養息，賂騰金寶巨萬計。
entries.en: With no other path forward he became Liu Teng's adopted son and paid him bribes in gold and jewels beyond counting.
entries.literal: Having no other way to advance, he became Liu Teng's adopted son and bribed Teng with gold and jewels numbering in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 騰屢為之言，乃得兼都官尚書，出為秦州刺史。
entries.en: Teng spoke for him again and again until he won the directorship of the Court for the Imperial Clan and went out as Qinzhou inspector.
entries.literal: Teng repeatedly spoke for him; he then obtained concurrent office as Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan and was sent out as Inspector of Qin Province.

entries.zh: 在州聚斂，百姓吁嗟。
entries.en: In his province he amassed wealth while the people groaned.
entries.literal: In the province he amassed wealth; the common people groaned.

entries.zh: 屬東益、南秦二州氐反，詔琛為行臺，仍充都督，還攝州事。
entries.en: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict named him to a mobile office and kept him as commissioner while he resumed the provincial post.
entries.literal: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict made Chen Mobile Office and still charged him as Commissioner, returning him to oversee the province.

entries.zh: 琛性貪暴，既總軍省，求欲無厭，百姓患害，有甚狼虎。
entries.en: Greedy and brutal by nature, he now held army and province together and took without end; the people suffered worse than from wolves.
entries.literal: Chen was by nature greedy and violent; holding both army and province he sought without end; the people suffered harm worse than from wolves and tigers.

entries.zh: 進討氐羌，大被摧破，士卒死者千數，率眾走還。
entries.en: He marched against the Di and Qiang and was shattered; a thousand soldiers died and he fled with the remnant.
entries.literal: Advancing to attack the Di and Qiang, he suffered great defeat; a thousand soldiers died; he led the host in flight back.

entries.zh: 內恃劉騰，無所畏憚，為中尉糾彈，會赦，除名為民。
entries.en: Backed by Liu Teng within, he feared nothing until the chief commandant impeached him; an amnesty spared his life but he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
entries.literal: Relying within on Liu Teng, he feared nothing; the chief commandant impeached him; an amnesty came and he was stripped of name and made a commoner.

entries.zh: 尋復王爵，後討鮮于脩禮，敗，免官爵。
entries.en: His princely title was soon restored; later, campaigning against Xianyu Xiuli, he was defeated and lost office and title.
entries.literal: Soon his princely title was restored; later in campaigning against Xianyu Xiuli he was defeated and stripped of office and title.

entries.zh: 後討汾晉胡、蜀，卒於軍，追復王爵。
entries.en: Later, campaigning against the Hu of Fen and Jin and the Shu, he died on campaign; his princely title was posthumously restored.
entries.literal: Later in campaigning against the Hu of Fen and Jin and the Shu, he died in the army; his princely title was posthumously restored.

entries.zh: 子詮，字搜賢，襲。
entries.en: His son Quan, styled Souxian, succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Quan, style Souxian, inherited.

entries.zh: 世宗初，為涼州刺史。
entries.en: Early in Shizong's reign he became Liangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made Inspector of Liang Province.

entries.zh: 在州貪穢，政以賄成。
entries.en: In his province he was corrupt; office went to the highest bidder.
entries.literal: In the province he was greedy and corrupt; government was accomplished by bribes.

entries.zh: 後除定州刺史。
entries.en: He was later transferred to the Dingzhou inspectorate.
entries.literal: Later he was removed and made Inspector of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 及京兆王愉之反，詐言國變。
entries.en: When Prince Yu of Jingzhao rose in rebellion, Yu spread false word of a dynastic crisis.
entries.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Yu falsely reported that the realm was in turmoil.

entries.zh: 在北州鎮，咸疑朝廷有釁，遣使觀詮動靜。
entries.en: Northern border provinces suspected trouble at court and sent agents to watch Quan.
entries.literal: The northern garrison provinces all suspected trouble at court and sent envoys to observe Quan's movements.

entries.zh: 詮具以狀告，州鎮帖然。
entries.en: Quan reported the facts in full, and the provinces and garrisons calmed.
entries.literal: Quan reported the full situation; the provinces and garrisons were settled.

entries.zh: 愉奔信都，詮與李平、高殖等四面攻燒，[3]愉突門而出。
entries.en: Yu fled to Xindu; Quan, Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others besieged him from four sides and set fires;[3] Yu broke through the gate and escaped.
entries.literal: Yu fled to Xindu; Quan with Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked from four sides and set fires;[3] Yu burst through the gate and fled.

entries.zh: 尋除侍中，兼以首告之功，除尚書左僕射。
entries.en: Soon he was palace attendant; for being first to report the rebellion he was also made left vice director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant; for merit in being first to report, he was also made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 薨，諡曰武康。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously titled Wukang.
entries.literal: He died; posthumous title Wukang.

entries.zh: 子延明，襲。
entries.en: His son Yanming succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Yanming inherited.

entries.zh: 世宗時，授太中大夫。
entries.en: Under Shizong he was made grand master of the palace.
entries.literal: In Shizong's time he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 延昌初，歲大飢，延明乃減家財，以拯賓客數十人，并贍其家。
entries.en: Early in Yanchang, in a year of great famine, Yanming spent his household wealth to save several dozen guests and support their families as well.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yanzhang, when the year brought great famine, Yanming then reduced his household wealth to save several dozen guests and also support their families.

entries.zh: 至肅宗初，為豫州刺史，甚有政績，累遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: At Suzong's accession he became Yuzhou inspector with a strong record of governance and rose to attendant of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: By the beginning of Suzong's reign he was made Inspector of Yu Province and had great administrative achievements; he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 子鑒，字長文，襲。
entries.en: His son Jian, styled Changwen, succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Jian, style Changwen, inherited.

entries.zh: 後除相州刺史、北討大都督，討葛榮。
entries.en: He was later made Xiangzhou inspector and grand commander of the northern campaign against Ge Rong.
entries.literal: Later he was made Inspector of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign to attack Ge Rong.

entries.zh: 仍兼尚書右僕射、北道行臺、尚書令，與都督裴衍共救信都。
entries.en: He still held the right vice directorship, the northern route mobile office, and the directorship of the Masters of Writing, and with Commissioner Pei Yan relieved Xindu.
entries.literal: He still held concurrent office as Right Vice Director, Northern Route Mobile Office, and Director of the Masters of Writing; with Commissioner Pei Yan he jointly relieved Xindu.

entries.zh: 鑒既庸才，諸弟粗暴，見天下多事，遂謀反，降附葛榮。
entries.en: Jian was a mediocrity and his brothers violent; when the realm fell into chaos they plotted rebellion and went over to Ge Rong.
entries.literal: Jian was a mediocrity; his younger brothers were violent and rough; seeing the realm in turmoil they plotted rebellion and surrendered to Ge Rong.

entries.zh: 都督源子邕與裴衍合圍鑒，斬首傳洛，詔改其元氏。
entries.en: Commissioner Yuan Ziyin and Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian; his head was sent to Luoyang, and an edict stripped the clan of the surname Yuan.
entries.literal: Commissioner Yuan Ziyin with Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian; his head was sent to Luoyang; an edict changed their Yuan surname.

entries.zh: 莊帝初，許復本族，又特復鑒王爵，贈司空。
entries.en: At Emperor Zhuang's accession the clan was allowed to resume its original name; Jian's princely title was specially restored and he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign restoration of the original clan was permitted; Jian's princely title was specially restored and he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 鑒弟斌之，字子爽。
entries.en: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, styled Zishuang.
entries.literal: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, style Zishuang.

entries.zh: 性險無行，及與鑒反，敗，遂奔葛榮。
entries.en: Treacherous and without principle, he joined Jian's rebellion; when it failed he fled to Ge Rong.
entries.literal: His nature was treacherous and without conduct; when he joined Jian in rebellion and was defeated, he fled to Ge Rong.

entries.zh: 榮滅，得還。
entries.en: After Ge Rong's fall he was able to return.
entries.literal: When Ge Rong was destroyed he was able to return.

entries.zh: 出帝時，封潁川郡王，委以腹心之任。
entries.en: Under Emperor Chu he was made Prince of Yingchuan commandery and given the emperor's innermost trust.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan commandery and entrusted with duties at the emperor's bosom.

entries.zh: 帝入關，斌之奔蕭衍，後還長安。
entries.en: When the emperor entered the Pass, Binzhi fled to Xiao Yan; he later returned to Chang'an.
entries.literal: When the emperor entered the Pass, Binzhi fled to Xiao Yan; later he returned to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 及元法僧反，詔為東道行臺、徐州大都督，節度諸軍事，與都督臨淮王彧、尚書李憲等討法僧。
entries.en: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, he was named eastern-route mobile secretariat and grand commander of Xuzhou, with command of all armies, and marched with Prince of Linhuai Yu, Minister Li Xian, and others against Faseng.
entries.literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, an edict made him Eastern-Route Mobile Secretariat, Grand Commander of Xuzhou, and controller of all military affairs, to campaign against Faseng together with Commander-in-Chief the Prince of Linhuai Yu, Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Xian, and others.

entries.zh: 蕭衍遣其豫章王綜鎮徐州。
entries.en: Xiao Yan posted his Prince of Yuzhang, Zong, to hold Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Zong to garrison Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 延明先牧徐方，甚得民譽，招懷舊土，遠近歸之。
entries.en: Having once governed Xu with a strong popular name, he called back the old land and won submission from far and near.
entries.literal: Yanming had earlier governed the Xu region and won great praise among the people; he now rallied the old domain, and near and far submitted to him.

entries.zh: 綜既降，延明因以軍乘之，復東南之境，至宿豫而還。
entries.en: When Zong surrendered, Yanming pressed the pursuit, recovered the southeast as far as Suyu, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Once Zong had surrendered, Yanming thereupon drove the army in pursuit, recovered the southeastern territory, and returned on reaching Suyu.

entries.zh: 遷都督、徐州刺史。
entries.en: He was made commander-in-chief and inspector of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 頻經師旅，人物凋弊，延明招攜新故，人悉安業，百姓咸附。
entries.en: War had repeatedly ravaged the region; he gathered old and new inhabitants until every household had its livelihood and the people clung to him.
entries.literal: The region had repeatedly suffered armies; people and goods were wasted and ruined; Yanming rallied new settlers and old residents alike, so that all settled into their trades and the common folk all attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 莊帝時，兼尚書令、大司馬。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhuang he served concurrently as director of the Masters of Writing and grand marshal.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Zhuang he concurrently held Minister of the Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 及元顥入洛，延明受顥委寄，率眾守河橋。
entries.en: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Yanming was entrusted with his cause and held Heqiao with an army.
entries.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yanming received Hao's trust, led troops, and held Heqiao Bridge.

entries.zh: 顥敗，遂將妻子奔蕭衍，死於江南。
entries.en: Hao's fall sent him south to Xiao Yan with his family; he died in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: When Hao was defeated, he took wife and children and fled to Xiao Yan, and died in the lands south of the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 莊帝末，喪還。
entries.en: Late in Zhuangdi's reign his coffin came home.
entries.literal: At the end of Emperor Zhuang's reign his remains were returned.

entries.zh: 出帝初，贈太保，王如故，諡曰文宣。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was posthumously titled grand mentor, his princedom left as before, with the posthumous name Prince Wenzuan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously given Grand Mentor, his princedom unchanged, posthumous title Wenzuan.

entries.zh: 所著詩賦讚頌銘誄三百餘篇，又撰五經宗略、詩禮別義，注帝王世紀及列仙傳。
entries.en: He left more than three hundred poems, fu, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges, compiled Summaries of the Five Classics and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites, and annotated the Chronological Record of Emperors and Kings and the Biographies of Transcendents.
entries.literal: Works he authored—poems, fu, encomia, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges—numbered more than three hundred pieces; he also compiled Summaries of the Five Classics' Main Points and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites, and annotated Huangfu Mi's Chronological Record of Emperors and Kings and the Biographies of Transcendents.

entries.zh: 又以河間人信都芳工算術，引之在館。
entries.en: He also summoned Xin Du Fang of Hejian, a master of mathematics, to his library.
entries.literal: Moreover, because Xin Du Fang of Hejian was skilled in calculation and astronomy, he brought him into his household academy.

entries.zh: 其撰古今樂事九章十二圖，又集器準九篇，芳別為之注，皆行於世。
entries.en: His nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music through the ages, and nine chapters on instrument measures with Fang's separate commentary, all circulated.
entries.literal: He compiled nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music old and new, and also gathered nine chapters on instrument standards; Fang separately annotated them, and all circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 論曰：文成五王，安豐特標令望。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Among Wencheng's five princes, Anfeng especially stood out with an excellent reputation.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Among Wencheng's five princes, Anfeng especially stood out with an excellent reputation.

entries.zh: 延明學業該贍，加以雅談之美；
entries.en: Yanming's learning was broad and ample, and he added the refinement of elegant conversation;
entries.literal: Yanming's learning was broad and ample, and he added to it the refinement of elegant conversation;

entries.zh: 及于永安，運跡冠戎。
entries.en: when the Yong'an era came, events placed him at the head of the army.
entries.literal: when the Yong'an era came, the course of events placed him at the head of the army.

entries.zh: 卒致奔亡，亦其命也。
entries.en: That he finally came to flight and exile was also his fate.
entries.literal: That he finally came to flight and exile was also his fate.

entries.zh: 孝文皇帝七男：林皇后生廢太子恂。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen had seven sons: Empress Lin bore Xun, the Deposed Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen had seven sons: Empress Lin bore Xun, the Deposed Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 廢太子庶人恂，字元道。
entries.en: The Deposed Crown Prince Xun, reduced to commoner rank, styled Yuandao.
entries.literal: The Deposed Crown Prince, the commoner Xun, styled Yuandao.

entries.zh: 生而母死，文明太后撫視之，常置左右。
entries.en: His mother died when he was born; Empress Dowager Wenming reared him and kept him constantly at her side.
entries.literal: At birth his mother died; Empress Dowager Wenming raised and watched over him, always keeping him at her side.

entries.zh: 年四歲，太皇太后親為立名恂，字元道，於是大赦。
entries.en: When he was four the Grand Empress Dowager herself named him Xun, styled Yuandao, and a general amnesty was declared.
entries.literal: At age four the Grand Empress Dowager personally established his name Xun, styled Yuandao, and thereupon a general amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: [3]太和十七年七月癸丑，立恂為皇太子。
entries.en: [3] In the seventh month of Taihe year 17, on the day guichou, Xun was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: [3] In the seventh month of Taihe year seventeen, on day guichou, Xun was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 及冠恂於廟，高祖臨光極東堂，引恂入見，誡以冠義曰：「夫冠禮表之百代，所以正容體，齊顏色，順辭令。
entries.en: When Xun was capped in the ancestral temple, Gaozu received him in the east hall of the Guangji Palace and taught him the meaning of the ceremony: "The capping rite stands for a hundred generations. It sets the body upright, aligns the face, and orders the tongue.
entries.literal: At his capping in the ancestral temple Gaozu sat in the east hall of the Guangji Palace, drew Xun in to see him, and admonished him on the meaning of the cap, saying: "The capping rite manifests itself to a hundred generations; by it one sets the body right, aligns the complexion, and orders one's speech.

entries.zh: 容體正，顏色齊，辭令順；
entries.en: When bearing is upright, the face composed, and words measured,
entries.literal: When the body is right, the complexion aligned, and speech in order;

entries.zh: 故能正君臣，親父子，和長幼。
entries.en: then ruler and minister are set right, father and son brought near, and elder and younger brought into harmony.
entries.literal: then lord and minister can be set right, father and son drawn close, elder and younger harmonized.

entries.zh: 然母見必拜，兄弟必敬，責以成人之禮。
entries.en: Yet he must bow when he sees his mother and show respect to his brothers, for he is now bound by the rites of adulthood.
entries.literal: Yet when he sees his mother he must bow, to his brothers he must show respect—charged with the rites of a grown man.

entries.zh: 字汝元道，所寄不輕。
entries.en: Your style is Ru Yuandao—what is laid upon you is no small thing.
entries.literal: Your style is Ru Yuandao; what is entrusted to you is not light.

entries.zh: 汝當尋名求義，以順吾旨。」
entries.en: Seek the meaning in your name and walk in accord with my intent."
entries.literal: You should seek the meaning in your name and follow my intent."

entries.zh: 二十年，改字宣道。
entries.en: In year 20 his style was changed to Xuandao.
entries.literal: In year twenty his style was changed to Xuandao.

entries.zh: 遷洛，詔恂詣代都。
entries.en: When the court moved to Luoyang, Xun was ordered to go to the Dai capital.
entries.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an edict ordered Xun to proceed to the Dai capital.

entries.zh: 其進止儀禮，高祖皆為定。
entries.en: Gaozu prescribed every detail of his movements and ceremonial bearing.
entries.literal: His comings and goings and ritual deportment Gaozu fixed for him in every detail.

entries.zh: 及恂入辭，高祖曰：「今汝不應向代，但太師薨於恒壤，朕既居皇極之重，不容輕赴舅氏之喪，欲使汝展哀舅氏，拜汝母墓，一寫為子之情。
entries.en: When Xun came to take leave Gaozu said, "You are not to turn toward Dai. The Grand Preceptor has died at Hengrang. I bear the weight of the throne and cannot lightly attend my uncle's mourning. Go and mourn for him in my stead, bow at your mother's tomb, and pour out there everything a son owes.
entries.literal: When Xun entered to take leave Gaozu said: "Now you should not go toward Dai; but the Grand Preceptor has died at Hengrang. I, having taken up the weight of the imperial pole, cannot lightly go to my maternal uncle's mourning. I wish you to extend mourning for your maternal uncle and bow at your mother's tomb, writing out in full a son's feeling.

entries.zh: 汝至彼，太師事畢後日，宜一拜山陵。
entries.en: When you arrive, wait one day after the Grand Preceptor's rites are done, then bow once at the imperial tombs.
entries.literal: When you arrive there, one day after the Grand Preceptor's rites are finished you should once bow at the mountain tomb.

entries.zh: 拜訖，汝族祖南安可一就問訊。
entries.en: After that you may call once on your clan-grandfather, the Prince of Nan'an.
entries.literal: When the bowing is finished your clan-grandfather the Prince of Nan'an may once be approached for inquiry.

entries.zh: 在途，當溫讀經籍。
entries.en: On the road, read the classics with steady care.
entries.literal: On the road you should diligently read the classics.

entries.zh: 今日親見吾也。」
entries.en: Today you see me face to face."
entries.literal: Today you see me in person."

entries.zh: [4]後高祖每歲征幸，恂常留守，主執廟祀。
entries.en: [4] Thereafter, whenever Gaozu marched out each year, Xun stayed behind to guard the capital and preside over the ancestral rites.
entries.literal: [4] Afterward, whenever Gaozu went on campaign each year, Xun always remained to guard the capital and preside over temple sacrifices.

entries.zh: 恂不好書學，體貌肥大，深忌河洛暑熱，意每追樂北方。
entries.en: Xun cared little for books. He was heavy of build and loathed the heat of the He-Luo basin; his heart always turned northward.
entries.literal: Xun did not love literary study; his body was large and fat; he deeply dreaded the heat of the He-Luo region; his mind always yearned for the pleasures of the north.

entries.zh: 中庶子高道悅數苦言致諫，恂甚銜之。
entries.en: His household steward Gao Daoyue admonished him again and again until Xun came to hate him.
entries.literal: The household steward Gao Daoyue repeatedly spoke bitter admonition; Xun greatly harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 高祖幸崧岳，恂留守金墉，於西掖門內與左右謀，欲召牧馬輕騎奔代，手刃道悅於禁中。
entries.en: While Gaozu was at Mount Song, Xun held Jinyong. Inside the west side gate he plotted with his attendants to call up the horse-keepers' light cavalry and flee to Dai, and with his own hand killed Daoyue in the inner palace.
entries.literal: When Gaozu visited Mount Song, Xun guarded Jinyong; within the west side gate he plotted with his attendants to summon the horse-tenders' light cavalry and flee to Dai, and with his own hand cut down Daoyue in the forbidden precinct.

entries.zh: 領軍元儼勒門防遏，夜得寧靜。
entries.en: The commandant of guards Yuan Yan barred the gates and held the night quiet.
entries.literal: The commandant of guards Yuan Yan restrained the gates; by night all was quiet.

entries.zh: 厥明，尚書陸琇馳啟高祖於南，高祖聞之駭惋，外寢其事，仍至汴口而還。
entries.en: At dawn Director of Documents Lu Xiu sent an urgent report south. Gaozu was shaken and grieved, but outwardly he hid the affair and still rode as far as Bian mouth before turning back.
entries.literal: At dawn Director of Documents Lu Diu hurried a memorial to Gaozu in the south; Gaozu, hearing it, was alarmed and grieved; outwardly he concealed the matter and still went as far as Bian mouth before returning.

entries.zh: 引恂數罪，與咸陽王禧等親杖恂，又令禧等更代，百餘下，扶曳出外，不起者月餘。
entries.en: He recited Xun's crimes one by one. With the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally beat him, then had them take turns until more than a hundred strokes were laid on. Xun was dragged out and could not rise for over a month.
entries.literal: He drew out Xun's many crimes; with the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally caned Xun, and ordered Xi and the others to take turns—more than a hundred blows—and had him dragged out; for more than a month he could not rise.

entries.zh: 拘於城西別館。
entries.en: He was confined in a lodge apart, west of the city.
entries.literal: He was confined in a separate lodge west of the city.

entries.zh: 引見羣臣於清徽堂，議廢之。
entries.en: Gaozu summoned the ministers to the Clear Emblem Hall to discuss deposing him.
entries.literal: Gaozu summoned the ministers at the Clear Emblem Hall and discussed deposing him.

entries.zh: 司空、太子太傅穆亮，尚書僕射、少保李沖，並免冠稽首而謝。
entries.en: Director of Works and crown prince grand tutor Mu Liang, and vice director and junior tutor Li Chong, both removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.
entries.literal: Director of Works and Crown Prince Grand Tutor Mu Liang, and Vice Director and Junior Tutor Li Chong, both removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「卿所謝者私也，我所議者國也。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "What you apologize for is a private matter. What I discuss is the state.
entries.literal: Gaozu said: "What you apologize for is private; what I discuss is the state.

entries.zh: 古人有言，大義滅親。
entries.en: The ancients said that great righteousness may destroy one's own kin.
entries.literal: The ancients had a saying: great righteousness extinguishes kin.

entries.zh: 今恂欲違父背尊，跨據恒朔。
entries.en: Xun now means to defy his father, abandon his rank, and seize the north at Heng and Shuo.
entries.literal: Now Xun wishes to oppose his father, turn from his superior, seize and hold Heng and Shuo.

entries.zh: 天下未有無父國，何其包藏，心與身俱。
entries.en: There is no realm without a father. How deep is his treachery—heart and deed as one.
entries.literal: Under Heaven there has never been a state without a father; how deep is his concealment—heart and body together.

entries.zh: 此小兒今日不滅，乃是國家之大禍，脫待我無後，恐有永嘉之亂。」
entries.en: If I do not destroy this boy today, he will be the state's great ruin. If I wait until I have no heir left, I fear another Yongjia upheaval."
entries.literal: If this boy today is not destroyed he is the great calamity of the state; if we wait until I have no successor, I fear there will be chaos like that of Yongjia."

entries.zh: 乃廢為庶人，置之河陽，以兵守之，服食所供，粗免飢寒而已。
entries.en: He was deposed to commoner rank and sent to Heyang under guard. Food and clothing were given only enough to keep hunger and cold at bay.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was deposed to commoner rank, placed at Heyang, guarded by soldiers; food and clothing supplied barely kept off hunger and cold.

entries.zh: 恂在困躓，頗知咎悔，恒讀佛經，禮拜歸心於善。
entries.en: In his fall Xun came partly to repent. He read Buddhist sutras, bowed, and turned his heart toward what was good.
entries.literal: Xun in his straits came somewhat to know fault and repentance; he constantly read Buddhist sutras, bowed, and turned his heart toward good.

entries.zh: 高祖幸代，遂如長安。
entries.en: When Gaozu went to Dai he continued on to Chang'an.
entries.literal: When Gaozu visited Dai he then proceeded to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 中尉李彪承間密表，告恂復與左右謀逆。
entries.en: Commandant of palace guards Li Biao sent a secret memorial reporting that Xun was again plotting rebellion with his attendants.
entries.literal: The commandant of palace guards Li Biao seized an interval with a secret memorial reporting that Xun again plotted rebellion with his attendants.

entries.zh: 高祖在長安，使中書侍郎邢巒與咸陽王禧，奉詔齎椒酒詣河陽，賜恂死，時年十五。
entries.en: At Chang'an Gaozu sent palace secretariat attendant Xing Luan with the Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict and peppered wine to Heyang, and had Xun put to death. He was fifteen.
entries.literal: Gaozu at Chang'an sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Xing Luan with the Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict and carrying peppered wine to Heyang, and bestowed death on Xun; he was then fifteen.

entries.zh: 殮以粗棺常服，瘞於河陽城。
entries.en: He was laid in a plain coffin in ordinary dress and buried in Heyang.
entries.literal: He was enfolded in a coarse coffin in common dress and buried in Heyang city.

entries.zh: 二十二年冬，御史臺令史龍文觀坐法當死，告廷尉，稱恂前被攝左右之日，有手書自理不知狀，而中尉李彪、侍御史賈尚寢不為聞。
entries.en: In the winter of year 22 the reviewing censor's clerk Long Wenguan, condemned to death for a legal offense, told the Court Commander that when Xun was seized his attendants had found a handwritten plea that he did not know what was afoot, yet Commandant Li Biao and attendant censor Jia Shang had buried the matter and never reported it.
entries.literal: In the winter of year twenty-two the reviewing censor's clerk Long Wenguan, sentenced to death for violating the law, reported to the Court Commander that when Xun before was seized by his attendants he had written by hand a plea that he did not know the circumstances, yet Li Biao the commandant and attendant censor Jia Shang suppressed it and did not report upward.

entries.zh: 賈坐繫廷尉。
entries.en: Jia was sentenced and held at the Court Commander's office.
entries.literal: Jia was sentenced and imprisoned at the Court Commander.

entries.zh: 時彪免歸，高祖在鄴，尚書表收彪赴洛，會赦，遂不窮其本末。
entries.en: By then Biao had been dismissed and gone home. Gaozu was at Ye. The secretariat memorialized to arrest Biao and send him to Luoyang, but an amnesty intervened and the case was never pursued to its roots.
entries.literal: At that time Biao had been dismissed and returned home; Gaozu was at Ye; the Director of Documents memorialized to seize Biao and send him to Luoyang; they met an amnesty, and therefore the matter was not pursued to the end.

entries.zh: 賈尚出繫，暴病數日死。
entries.en: Jia Shang was released from prison, fell suddenly ill, and died within days.
entries.literal: Jia Shang was released from prison; sudden illness; within several days he died.

entries.zh: 初，高祖將為恂娶司徒馮誕長女，以女幼，待年長。
entries.en: At first Gaozu meant to marry Xun to the eldest daughter of Minister of Works Feng Dan, but because the girl was young he waited until she grew.
entries.literal: Initially Gaozu was to marry Xun to Minister of Works Feng Dan's eldest daughter; because the girl was young he waited until she came of age.

entries.zh: 先為娉彭城劉長文、滎陽鄭懿女為左右孺子，時恂年十三四。
entries.en: He first betrothed to him the daughters of Liu Changwen of Pengcheng and Zheng Yi of Xingyang as left and right concubines when Xun was thirteen or fourteen.
entries.literal: First he betrothed for him the daughters of Pengcheng Liu Changwen and Xingyang Zheng Yi as left and right Ruzi; at the time Xun was thirteen or fourteen.

entries.zh: 高祖泛舟天淵池，謂郭祚、崔光、宋弁曰：「人生須自放，不可終朝讀書。
entries.en: Gaozu drifted a boat on the Tianyuan Pool and said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian, "A man must sometimes loosen the rein. He cannot read from dawn to dusk.
entries.literal: Gaozu floated a boat on the Tianyuan Pool and said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian: "In life one must let oneself go; one cannot read books from morning to night.

entries.zh: 我欲使恂旦出省經傳，食後還內，晡時復出，日夕而罷。
entries.en: I mean to have Xun go out each morning to study the classics, return at midday, go out again in the afternoon, and be done by evening.
entries.literal: I wish to have Xun go out in the morning to review the classics, return within after eating, go out again at the hour of shen, and stop at dusk.

entries.zh: 卿等以為何如？」
entries.en: What do you think?"
entries.literal: You all take it how?"

entries.zh: 光曰：「孔子稱：『血氣未定，戒之在色』，傳曰：『晝以訪事，夜以安身』。
entries.en: Cui Guang said, "Confucius warned, 'When blood and breath are unsettled, beware of desire.' The tradition says, 'By day attend to affairs; by night rest the body.'
entries.literal: Guang said: "Confucius said: 'When the blood and breath are not yet settled, beware of color'; the tradition says: 'By day inquire into affairs, by night rest the body.'

entries.zh: 太子以幼年涉學之日，不宜於正晝之時，捨書御內，又非所以安柔弱之體，固永年之命。」
entries.en: The crown prince is still in his first years of study. He should not in broad daylight leave his books for the inner quarters—that is no way to guard a tender frame or secure a long life."
entries.literal: The crown prince, in the years when he first touches learning, should not in the bright hours of day set aside his books and enter the inner quarters; this also is not how to settle a tender body and secure years of life."

entries.zh: 高祖以光言為然，乃不令恂晝入內。
entries.en: Gaozu accepted Guang's counsel and would not let Xun enter the inner palace by day.
entries.literal: Gaozu took Guang's words as right and therefore did not let Xun enter within by day.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He left no sons.
entries.literal: He had no sons.

entries.zh: 清河王懌，字宣仁。
entries.en: Qinghe Wang Yi, styled Xuanren.
entries.literal: Prince Qinghe Yi, courtesy name Xuanren.

entries.zh: 幼而敏惠，美姿貌，高祖愛之。
entries.en: As a boy he was clever and handsome, and Gaozu doted on him.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and quick-witted, of fine appearance; Emperor Gaozu loved him.

entries.zh: 彭城王勰甚器異之，並曰：「此兒風神外偉，黃中內潤，若天假之年，比二南矣。」
entries.en: Prince Pengcheng Xie prized him highly and said with others, "This child's bearing is outwardly grand and inwardly rich; given a full span of years he would rival the Two Souths."
entries.literal: Prince Pengcheng Xie greatly prized and singled him out, and together they said: "This boy's spirit and bearing are outwardly grand, his yellow core inwardly lustrous; if Heaven grants him years, he will rival the Two Souths."

entries.zh: 博涉經史，兼綜羣言，有文才，善談理，寬仁容裕，喜怒不形於色。
entries.en: He mastered classics and histories, absorbed many traditions, wrote well, argued ably, and was magnanimous—joy and anger never showed on his face.
entries.literal: He ranged broadly through the classics and histories, took in many schools of thought, had literary talent, was skilled at discourse on principle, generous and tolerant in bearing, and did not let joy or anger show on his face.

entries.zh: 太和二十一年封。
entries.en: He received his fief in Taihe year 21.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taihe he was enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 世宗初，拜侍中，轉尚書僕射。
entries.en: When Shizong acceded he became palace attendant, then vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was appointed Palace Attendant, then transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 及齊獻武王既誅榮，以悅高祖子，宜承大業，乃令人示意。
entries.en: After Duke Xianwu of Qi killed Rong, deeming Yue Gaozu's son fit for the throne, he sent word of his intent.
entries.literal: When Duke Xianwu of Qi had already killed Rong, because Yue was Emperor Gaozu's son and ought to inherit the great enterprise, he therefore had someone convey his intent.

entries.zh: 悅既至，清狂如故，動為罪失，不可扶持，乃止。
entries.en: Yue arrived as reckless as ever; his acts were crimes—he could not be enthroned, and they desisted.
entries.literal: Yue, having arrived, was wild and unbridled as before; his actions were crimes and failures—he could not be supported, and they stopped.

entries.zh: 出帝初，除大司馬。
entries.en: At the Deposed Emperor's accession he was made grand marshal.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was appointed Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 論曰：庶人險暴之性，自幼而長，終以廢黜，不得其終。
entries.en: The appraisal says: The commoner's dangerous and violent nature grew from childhood; in the end he was deposed and did not come to a proper end.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: The commoner's dangerous and violent nature grew from childhood; in the end he was deposed and did not attain a proper end.

entries.zh: 斯乃硃、均之性，堯、舜不能訓也。
entries.en: Such was the nature of Zhu and Jun; Yao and Shun could not instruct it.
entries.literal: This was the nature of Zhu and Jun; Yao and Shun could not instruct it.

entries.zh: 京兆早有令問，晚致顛覆，習於所染，可不慎乎！
entries.en: Jingzhao early won fair renown, but late came to ruin; once habituated to what stains one, can one fail to be cautious!
entries.literal: Jingzhao early had fair renown, but late came to ruin; habituation to what stains one--can one fail to be cautious!

entries.zh: 清河器識才譽，以懿親作輔，時鐘屯詖，始遘牆茨之逼。
entries.en: Qinghe had capacity, insight, talent, and reputation, and as an excellent kinsman served as assistant, but the age fell into hardship and crookedness, and he first met the pressure of the wall-thorns.
entries.literal: Qinghe had capacity, insight, talent, and reputation, and as an excellent kinsman served as assistant, but the time fell on hardship and crookedness, and he first met the pressure of the wall-thorns.

entries.zh: 運屬道消，晚扼凶權之手。
entries.en: His fortunes met a time when the Way declined, and late he was throttled by violent power.
entries.literal: His fortunes belonged to a time when the Way declined, and late he was gripped in the hands of violent power.

entries.zh: 悲哉！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 廣平早歲驕盈，汝南性致狂逸，揆其終始，俱不足論。
entries.en: Guangping was arrogant and full in his early years, and Runan by nature ran to wild excess; judged from beginning to end, neither is worth discussing.
entries.literal: Guangping was arrogant and full in his early years, and Runan by nature reached wild excess; weighing their ends from their beginnings, both are not worth discussing.

entries.zh: 而悅以天人所棄，卒嬰猜懼之毒，蓋地逼之尤也。
entries.en: Yet Yue, abandoned by Heaven and men, finally suffered the poison of suspicion and fear; this was likely the extreme result of a prince pressed too near the throne.
entries.literal: Yet Yue, abandoned by Heaven and men, finally suffered the poison of suspicion and fear; this was likely the extreme result of being pressed too close by position.

entries.en: The text is deficient.
entries.literal: The text is deficient.

entries.zh: 文昭皇后生宣武皇帝、廣平文穆王懷。
entries.en: Empress Wenzhao bore Emperor Xuanwu and Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping.
entries.literal: Empress Wenzhao bore Emperor Xuanwu and Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping.

entries.zh: 袁貴人生京兆王愉。
entries.en: Noble Lady Yuan bore Yu, Prince of Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Noble Lady Yuan bore Yu, Prince of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 羅夫人生清河文獻王懌、汝南文宣王悅。
entries.en: Lady Luo bore Yi, Prince of Qinghe (posthumous Wenxian), and Yue, Prince of Runan (posthumous Wenzuan).
entries.literal: Lady Luo gave birth to Prince of Qinghe, posthumous Wenxian Yi, and Prince of Runan, posthumous Wenzuan Yue.

entries.zh: 鄭充華生皇子恌，未封，早夭。
entries.en: Zheng Chonghua bore the prince Ti, who was never enfeoffed and died in infancy.
entries.literal: Zheng Chonghua bore the prince Ti; he was not enfeoffed and died young.

entries.zh: 京兆王愉，字宣德。
entries.en: Yu, Prince of Jingzhao, styled Xuande.
entries.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, styled Xuande.

entries.zh: 太和二十一年封。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed in Taihe year 21.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed in Taihe year twenty-one.

entries.zh: 拜都督、徐州刺史，以彭城王中軍府長史盧陽烏兼長史，州事巨細，委之陽烏。
entries.en: He was made commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou. Lu Yangwu, chief clerk of the Prince of Pengcheng's center-army office, served as acting chief clerk, and every detail of the province was left to him.
entries.literal: He was appointed commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou; Pengcheng Wang's center-army office chief clerk Lu Yangwu was made acting chief clerk, and great and small matters of the province were entrusted to Yangwu.

entries.zh: 世宗初，為護軍將軍。
entries.en: At the start of Shizong's reign he was made guardian general of the army.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made guardian general of the army.

entries.zh: 世宗留愛諸弟，愉等常出入宮掖，晨昏寢處，若家人焉。
entries.en: Shizong doted on his younger brothers. Yu and the others moved freely through the palace quarters, sleeping and waking with him morning and evening like members of one household.
entries.literal: Shizong cherished his younger brothers; Yu and the others constantly went in and out of the palace women's quarters, morning and evening sleeping and dwelling as if a family household.

entries.zh: 世宗每日華林戲射，衣衫騎從，往來無間。
entries.en: Every day Shizong shot for sport in the Hualin Garden, and Yu rode with him in light dress, back and forth without pause.
entries.literal: Each day Shizong shot for sport in the Hualin Garden; in light dress and mounted retinue they came and went without interval.

entries.zh: 遷中書監。
entries.en: He was transferred to director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 世宗為納順皇后妹為妃，而不見禮答。
entries.en: Shizong gave him the younger sister of Empress Shun as consort, but Yu never showed her proper courtesy.
entries.literal: Shizong married for him the younger sister of Empress Shun as consort, but Yu did not treat her with ritual courtesy.

entries.zh: 愉在徐州，納妾李氏，本姓楊，東郡人，夜聞其歌，悅之，遂被寵嬖。
entries.en: While Yu held Xuzhou he took a concubine, Lady Li—born Yang, from Dong commandery. He heard her sing one night, was delighted, and thereafter she held his favor.
entries.literal: While Yu was in Xuzhou he took a concubine, Lady Li, originally surnamed Yang, a woman of Dong commandery; hearing her sing at night he was pleased and thereafter she received his favor.

entries.zh: 罷州還京，欲進貴之，託右中郎將趙郡李恃顯為之養父，就之禮逆，產子寶月。
entries.en: When he left office for the capital he wished to raise her standing. He had Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery stand as her adoptive father, married her by that rite, and she bore Baoyue.
entries.literal: When he left the province and returned to the capital he wished to advance her rank; he entrusted Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery to act as her adoptive father, and by that rite married her; she bore the son Baoyue.

entries.zh: 順皇后召李入宮，毀擊之，強令為尼於內，以子付妃養之。
entries.en: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace, struck and abused her, forced her to take the tonsure inside, and gave the child to the consort to raise.
entries.literal: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace, beat and reviled her, forced her to become a nun within, and gave the child to the consort to rear.

entries.zh: 歲餘，后父于勁，以后久無所誕，乃上表勸廣嬪侍。
entries.en: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, seeing that she still bore no child, memorialized urging that secondary consorts attend the bed.
entries.literal: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, because the empress long had borne no child, submitted a memorial urging that secondary consorts attend the bed.

entries.zh: 因令后歸李於愉，舊愛更甚。
entries.en: The empress was made to return Li to Yu, and his old love burned hotter than before.
entries.literal: Thereupon he had the empress return Li to Yu; the old love grew still stronger.

entries.zh: 愉好文章，頗著詩賦。
entries.en: Yu loved letters and wrote poetry and fu with some distinction.
entries.literal: Yu loved literary composition and notably composed poetry and fu.

entries.zh: 時引才人宋世景、李神儁、祖瑩、邢晏、王遵業、張始均等共申宴喜，招四方儒學賓客嚴懷真等數十人，館而禮之。
entries.en: He often gathered men of talent—Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others—for feasts and delight, and hosted several dozen Confucian guests from across the realm, including Yan Huaizhen, treating them with full ceremony.
entries.literal: At the time he constantly drew in talented men Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others to share feasts and joy; he recruited several tens of Confucian guests from the four directions such as Yan Huaizhen, housed them, and honored them with ritual.

entries.zh: 所得穀帛，率多散施。
entries.en: Most of the grain and silk that came to him he gave away.
entries.literal: The grain and silk he received he mostly dispersed in gifts.

entries.zh: 又崇信佛道，用度常至不接。
entries.en: He also devoted himself to Buddhism, and his expenses often outran his income.
entries.literal: He also revered the Buddhist way; his expenses often fell short.

entries.zh: 與弟廣平王懷頗相夸尚，競慕奢麗，貪縱不法。
entries.en: With his younger brother Huai, Prince of Guangping, he vied in display, each chasing extravagance, greedy and heedless of law.
entries.literal: With his younger brother the Prince of Guangping Huai he rather vied in display, emulating extravagant splendor, greedy and lawless.

entries.zh: 於是世宗攝愉禁中推案，杖愉五十，出為冀州刺史。
entries.en: Shizong then had Yu seized in the inner palace, investigated him, gave him fifty strokes, and sent him out as governor of Ji.
entries.literal: Thereupon Shizong took Yu into the forbidden precinct to investigate, caned him fifty times, and sent him out as governor of Ji.

entries.zh: 始愉自以職求侍要，[5]既勢劣二弟，潛懷愧恨，頗見言色。
entries.en: At first Yu had believed his rank would win him a place near power; [5] finding himself weaker than his two younger brothers, he nursed secret shame and let it show in word and face.
entries.literal: At first Yu himself thought that by his office he might obtain attendance on important affairs; [5] now that his power was inferior to his two younger brothers he secretly harbored shame and resentment and rather showed it in speech and countenance.

entries.zh: 又以幸妾屢被頓辱，內外離抑。
entries.en: His favored concubine had been shamed again and again, and at court and at home he was isolated and pressed down.
entries.literal: Also because his favored concubine was repeatedly humiliated, within and without he was estranged and suppressed.

entries.zh: 及在州謀逆，愉遂殺長史羊靈引及司馬李遵，稱得清河王密疏，云高肇謀殺害主上。
entries.en: While he was in the province he rose in rebellion. Yu killed chief clerk Yang Lingyin and marshal Li Zun, claiming a secret letter from the Prince of Qinghe that Gao Zhao meant to murder the emperor.
