entries.literal: When in the province he plotted rebellion, Yu then killed chief clerk Yang Lingyin and marshal Li Zun, claiming to have received a secret letter from the Prince of Qinghe saying Gao Zhao plotted to murder the sovereign.

entries.zh: 於是遂為壇於信都之南，柴燎告天，即皇帝位。
entries.en: He built an altar south of Xindu, burned offerings and declared himself to Heaven, and took the imperial title on the spot.
entries.literal: Thereupon he made an altar south of Xindu, burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and at once took the imperial title.

entries.zh: 赦天下，號建平元年，立李氏為皇后。
entries.en: He proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era name Jianping year 1, and made Lady Li empress.
entries.literal: He proclaimed amnesty for all under Heaven, era name Jianping year one, and installed Lady Li as empress.

entries.zh: 世宗詔尚書李平討愉。
entries.en: Shizong ordered Director of Documents Li Ping to suppress Yu.
entries.literal: Shizong ordered Director of Documents Li Ping to campaign against Yu.

entries.zh: 愉出拒王師，頻敗，遂嬰城自守。
entries.en: Yu marched out against the imperial host, was beaten again and again, and finally shut himself in the city.
entries.literal: Yu went out to resist the imperial army, was repeatedly defeated, and then closed the city and held it.

entries.zh: 愉知事窮，攜李及四子數十騎出門，諸軍追之，見執以送。
entries.en: Seeing all was lost, Yu took Li and four sons and rode out with a few dozen horsemen. The armies overtook him, seized him, and sent him in.
entries.literal: Yu knew the affair was exhausted; he took Li and four sons with several tens of horsemen and went out the gate; the armies pursued and seized him and sent him in.

entries.zh: 詔徵赴京師，申以家人之訓。
entries.en: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him as kin.
entries.literal: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him with the teaching of a family.

entries.zh: 愉每止宿亭傳，必攜李手，盡其私情。
entries.en: At every post station Yu held Li by the hand and gave their private bond its full expression.
entries.literal: Whenever Yu halted at a post station he always took Li by the hand and indulged their private feeling to the full.

entries.zh: 雖鎖縶之中，飲食自若，略無愧懼之色。
entries.en: Even in chains he ate and drank as before, showing hardly a trace of shame or fear.
entries.literal: Though in fetters, in eating and drinking he was as before, with scarcely a shade of shame or fear.

entries.zh: 至野王，愉語人曰：「雖主上慈深，不忍殺我，吾亦何面目見於至尊！」
entries.en: At Yewang Yu told those about him, "The emperor's mercy runs deep and he may spare my life—but what face have I left to show the throne?"
entries.literal: When he reached Yewang Yu said to others: "Though the sovereign's kindness is deep and he will not bear to kill me, what face have I to see the August One!"

entries.zh: 於是歔欷流涕，絕氣而死，年二十一。
entries.en: He wept until his breath failed and he died. He was twenty-one.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sobbed, tears flowing; his breath broke and he died; he was then twenty-one.

entries.zh: 或云高肇令人殺之。
entries.en: Some said Gao Zhao had him killed.
entries.literal: Some say Gao Zhao had men kill him.

entries.zh: 斂以小棺，瘞之。
entries.en: He was laid in a small coffin and buried.
entries.literal: He was enfolded in a small coffin and buried.

entries.zh: 諸子至洛，皆赦之。
entries.en: When his sons reached Luoyang they were all pardoned.
entries.literal: When the sons reached Luoyang they were all pardoned.

entries.zh: 後靈太后令愉之四子皆附屬籍，追封愉臨洮王。
entries.en: Later Empress Dowager Ling had Yu's four sons entered on the clan register and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.
entries.literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling ordered that Yu's four sons all be entered on the register of kin, and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.

entries.zh: 子寶月襲。
entries.en: His son Baoyue inherited the title.
entries.literal: The son Baoyue inherited.

entries.zh: 乃改葬父母，追服三年。
entries.en: He reburied his parents and observed three years of mourning.
entries.literal: He then reburied his parents and observed mourning for three years.

entries.zh: 懌才長從政，明於斷決，割判眾務，甚有聲名。
entries.en: Yi excelled in administration, decided cases with clarity, cut through piled business, and won wide renown.
entries.literal: Yi was talented and long in government; clear in judgment and decision, he sliced through the multitude of affairs and won a great reputation.

entries.zh: 司空高肇以帝舅寵任，既擅威權，謀去良宗，屢譖懌及愉等。
entries.en: Gao Zhao, the emperor's uncle by marriage, already held unchecked power and sought to purge the princes, repeatedly denouncing Yi, Yu, and others.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Gao Zhao, favored as the emperor's maternal uncle, already monopolized awesome power and plotted to remove worthy clansmen, repeatedly slandering Yi and Yu and the rest.

entries.zh: 愉不勝其忿怒，遂舉逆冀州。
entries.en: Yu, unable to endure the pressure, rebelled in Jizhou.
entries.literal: Yu could not bear his fury and thereupon raised rebellion in Jizhou.

entries.zh: 因愉之逆，又構殺勰。
entries.en: He used Yu's revolt as pretext to frame and kill Xie as well.
entries.literal: Using Yu's rebellion as pretext, he also framed and killed Xie.

entries.zh: 懌恐不免。
entries.en: Yi feared he would not escape.
entries.literal: Yi feared he could not escape.

entries.zh: 肇又錄囚徒，以立私惠。
entries.en: Zhao again reviewed prisoners to curry private favor.
entries.literal: Zhao again reviewed prisoners to build private goodwill.

entries.zh: 懌因侍宴酒酣，乃謂肇曰：「天子兄弟，詎有幾人，而炎炎不息。
entries.en: When wine had deepened at a feast Yi told Zhao, "The emperor's brothers are few—why does your flame never die down?
entries.literal: At a banquet where Yi attended him, wine deep, Yi said to Zhao: "The Son of Heaven's brothers—how many are there?—yet you blaze on without cease.

entries.zh: 昔王莽頭禿，亦藉渭陽之資，遂篡漢室，今君曲形見矣，恐復終成亂階。」
entries.en: Wang Mang was bald yet rode empress-kin ties to seize the Han throne; your crooked shape is plain already—I fear you will be disorder's stair again."
entries.literal: In old times Wang Mang's head was bald, yet he still relied on kin through the empress's family and usurped the Han house; now your bent form is already plain to see—I fear you will again become the stairway of disorder."

entries.zh: 又言於世宗曰：「臣聞唯器與名，不可以假人。
entries.en: He also told Shizong, "I have heard that ritual vessels and titles must not be lent away.
entries.literal: He also said to Emperor Shizong: "Your servant has heard that vessels and names may not be lent to others.

entries.zh: 是故季氏旅泰，宣尼以為深譏；
entries.en: When the Ji clan overreached at Mount Tai, Confucius censured it deeply;
entries.literal: Therefore when the Ji clan overstepped at Mount Tai, Confucius deeply censured it;

entries.zh: 仲叔軒懸，丘明以為至誡。
entries.en: when Zhongsun's house displayed lordly drums, Qiu Ming called it the gravest warning.
entries.literal: when Zhongsun hung his drums as for a lord, Qiu Ming took it as the utmost warning.

entries.zh: 諒以天尊地卑，君臣道別，宜杜漸防萌，無相僭越。
entries.en: Heaven is high and earth low; ruler and minister are separate—one must nip usurpation in the bud.
entries.literal: Truly heaven is honored and earth is lowly—the way of ruler and minister is distinct; one should stop the first sprout and guard against encroachment.

entries.zh: 至於減膳錄囚，人君之事，今乃司徒行之，詎是人臣之義？
entries.en: Reducing meals and reviewing prisoners belong to the ruler; for the minister of works to do them—what subject's duty is that?
entries.literal: As for reducing meals and reviewing prisoners—these are a ruler's affairs; now the Minister of Works performs them—how is that the meaning of a subject?

entries.zh: 且陛下修政教，解獄訟，則時雨可降，玉燭知和，何使明君失之於上，姦臣竊之於下。
entries.en: If Your Majesty reforms rule and clears suits, timely rain and harmony follow—why let the wise ruler lose these above while traitors seize them below?
entries.literal: Moreover Your Majesty reforms government and teaching and releases prisoners from litigation—then timely rain may descend and the jade candle know harmony; why let an enlightened ruler lose them above while treacherous ministers steal them below?

entries.zh: 長亂之基，於此在矣。」
entries.en: The root of lasting disorder is here."
entries.literal: The root of long disorder lies here."

entries.zh: 世宗笑而不應。
entries.en: Shizong smiled and made no reply.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong smiled and did not answer.

entries.zh: 廣平王懷。
entries.en: Guangping Wang Huai.
entries.literal: Prince Guangping Huai.

entries.en: 〈The text is deficient.〉
entries.literal: 〈The text is deficient.〉

entries.zh: 有魏諸王。
entries.en: Among the princes of Wei,
entries.literal: There were princes of Wei.

entries.zh: 召入華林別館，禁其出入，令四門博士董徵，授以經傳。
entries.en: they were summoned to the Hualin Park lodge, confined from going abroad, and Four-Gate academician Dong Zheng taught them the classics.
entries.literal: They were summoned into the separate lodge of the Hualin Park, their going out and coming in forbidden, and Four-Gate Academician Dong Zheng was ordered to teach them the classics and transmissions.

entries.zh: 世宗崩，乃得歸。
entries.en: When Shizong died they were allowed home.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong died they were then able to return.

entries.zh: 及尒朱榮舉兵向洛。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang,
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang.

entries.zh: 既憶入間。
entries.en: The text is corrupt; he may already have hoped to enter Luoyang.
entries.literal: Already he recalled entering among men.

entries.en: 〈Doubtful text; the transmitted line is corrupt.〉
entries.literal: 〈The reading here is doubtful.〉

entries.zh: 俄而聞榮肆毒於河陰，遂南奔蕭衍。
entries.en: Soon he heard Rong's massacre at Heyin and fled south to Xiao Yan.
entries.literal: Before long he heard that Rong had wantonly slaughtered at Heyin and thereupon fled south to Xiao Yan.

entries.zh: 衍立為魏主，號年更興。
entries.en: Xiao Yan set him up as Wei ruler under the reign title Gengxing.
entries.literal: Yan installed him as Wei sovereign and changed the reign title to Gengxing.

entries.zh: 衍遣其將軍王辯送置於境上，以覬侵逼。
entries.en: Xiao Yan sent Wang Bian to place him on the border [10] as a lever for invasion.
entries.literal: Yan sent his general Wang Bian to escort and place him on the border; [10] thereby to covet invasion and pressure.

entries.zh: 衞操，字德元，代人也。
entries.en: Wei Cao, whose style was Deyuan, came from Dai.
entries.literal: Wei Cao, styled Deyuan, was a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 少通俠，有才略。
entries.en: As a young man he lived by the code of the knight-errant and showed both talent and strategic mind.
entries.literal: In youth he mastered chivalry and possessed talent and stratagem.

entries.zh: 晉征北將軍衞瓘以操為牙門將，數使於國，頗自結附。
entries.en: Jin's General Who Pacifies the North, Wei Guan, appointed Cao gate officer and often sent him on missions to the Dai state, where Cao gradually built ties of his own.
entries.literal: Jin General Who Pacifies the North Wei Guan made Cao a gate officer; he was repeatedly sent to the state and rather attached himself on his own.

entries.zh: 始祖崩後，與從子雄及其宗室鄉親姬澹等十數人，同來歸國，說桓穆二帝招納晉人，於是晉人附者稍眾。
entries.en: When the founding ancestor passed away, Cao came home with his nephew Xiong and a dozen-odd kinsmen and neighbors, among them Ji Dan, and urged the Huan and Mu emperors to welcome Jin subjects. From then on Jin adherents grew steadily in number.
entries.literal: After the founding ancestor died, together with his nephew Xiong and more than ten clansmen and fellow-townsmen such as Ji Dan, he came in a body to return to the state, urging the Huan and Mu emperors to recruit Jin people; thereafter those of Jin who attached themselves grew somewhat numerous.

entries.zh: 桓帝嘉之，以為輔相，任以國事。
entries.en: Emperor Huan approved and named him chief minister, charging him with the affairs of the realm.
entries.literal: Emperor Huan commended this and made him chief minister, entrusting him with state affairs.

entries.zh: 及劉淵、石勒之亂，勸桓帝匡助晉氏。
entries.en: When Liu Yuan and Shi Le threw the north into rebellion, he pressed Emperor Huan to stand with the house of Jin.
entries.literal: When the disorders of Liu Yuan and Shi Le arose, he urged Emperor Huan to support and aid the Jin house.

entries.zh: 東瀛公司馬騰聞而善之，表加將號。
entries.en: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing this, praised the policy and memorialized the throne to grant Cao further military rank.
entries.literal: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing of it, approved and memorialized to add military titles.

entries.zh: 稍遷至右將軍，封定襄侯。
entries.en: He rose in stages to Right General and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Right General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.

entries.zh: 顯子題，亦有策謀。
entries.en: Xian's son Ti was likewise a man of counsel.
entries.literal: Xian's son Ti also had stratagems.

entries.zh: 太祖使題與將軍王建等三軍，討慕容寶廣寧太守劉亢埿，斬之。
entries.en: Taizu sent Ti with General Wang Jian and a three-wing army against Murong Bao's Guangning prefect Liu Kangqi and took his head.
entries.literal: Taizu sent Ti with the general Wang Jian and the three armies to campaign against Murong Bao's Guangning prefect Liu Kangqi and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 徙亢埿部落于平城。
entries.en: Kangqi's tribes were resettled at Pingcheng.
entries.literal: Kangqi's tribes were moved to Pingcheng.

entries.zh: 寶上谷太守驎，捐郡逃走，太祖追討，題為大將，別出東道。
entries.en: Bao's Shanggu prefect Lin deserted his commandery and fled; Taizu pursued him; Ti was made grand general and took a separate eastern road.
entries.literal: Bao's Shanggu prefect Lin abandoned the commandery and fled; Taizu pursued in punishment; Ti was made grand general and marched out by the eastern route.

entries.zh: 以功賜爵東宛侯。
entries.en: For his merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongwan.
entries.literal: For merit he was given the enfeoffment Marquis of Dongwan.

entries.zh: 及還京師，常與李栗侍宴。
entries.en: Back at the capital he often shared the emperor's table with Li Li.
entries.literal: When he returned to the capital he constantly attended banquets with Li Li.

entries.zh: 栗坐不敬獲罪，題亦被黜為濟陽太守。
entries.en: Li was punished for disrespect at court; Ti was demoted as well, to administrator of Jiyang.
entries.literal: Li was punished for irreverence in seating; Ti was also demoted to Administrator of Jiyang.

entries.zh: 後太祖欲廣宮室，規度平城四方數十里，將模鄴、洛、長安之制，運材數百萬根。
entries.en: Later Taizu planned to expand the palace quarter, surveyed dozens of li around Pingcheng, and meant to imitate Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an; millions of timbers were hauled in.
entries.literal: Later Taizu wished to enlarge the palaces and measured several tens of li around Pingcheng, intending to model Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an; timber in the millions of logs was transported.

entries.zh: 以題機巧，徵令監之。
entries.en: Ti's mechanical ingenuity won him summons to oversee the work.
entries.literal: Because Ti was ingenious in mechanism he was summoned and ordered to supervise.

entries.zh: 召入，與論興造之宜。
entries.en: He was called in to debate the right scale and design of the build.
entries.literal: He was called in and discussed the fitness of the construction.

entries.zh: 題久侍頗怠，賜死。
entries.en: After long attendance Ti grew careless in his duties and was put to death.
entries.literal: Ti after long attendance grew somewhat slack; he was granted death.

entries.zh: 題弟雲，好學善射。
entries.en: Ti's younger brother Yun loved books and excelled at the bow.
entries.literal: Ti's younger brother Yun loved learning and was skilled at archery.

entries.zh: 太祖時，常典選曹，轉給事中。
entries.en: Under Taizu he ran the Selection Bureau and later became palace attendant.
entries.literal: In Taizu's time he constantly managed the Selection Bureau and was transferred to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 以功賜爵安德侯。
entries.en: For merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Ande.
entries.literal: For merit he was given the enfeoffment Marquis of Ande.

entries.zh: 遷執金吾，常參軍國謀議。
entries.en: He rose to Commandant of Cavalry and sat in on every major counsel of war and state.
entries.literal: He was promoted Commandant of Cavalry and constantly took part in deliberations on army and state.

entries.zh: 世祖之克赫連昌，詔雲與常山王素留鎮統萬。
entries.en: When Shizu took Helian Chang, he ordered Yun and Prince Su of Changshan to hold Tongwan.
entries.literal: When Shizu captured Helian Chang, he issued an edict Yun and the Prince of Changshan Su to remain and garrison Tongwan.

entries.zh: 進爵安定公，加平西將軍，後遷鎮西大將軍。
entries.en: He was raised to Duke of Anding and General Who Pacifies the West, then to Grand General Who Guards the West.
entries.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Anding, with added General Who Pacifies the West; later he was transferred Grand General Who Guards the West.

entries.zh: 時初并河西，人心未一，雲撫慰新舊，皆得其所。
entries.en: The Hexi had only just been absorbed and loyalties were still divided; Yun soothed old subjects and new until each settled where he belonged.
entries.literal: At that time the Hexi region had just been annexed and hearts were not yet one; Yun comforted old and new alike and all found their place.

entries.zh: 神䴥中卒，諡曰敬公。
entries.en: He died in the Shenju era and was posthumously titled Duke Reverent.
entries.literal: He died in the Shenju era; posthumous title: Duke Reverent.

entries.zh: 族人奴真領部來附。
entries.en: Nuzhen, a kinsman of the line, brought his following in to submit.
entries.literal: A clansman, Nuzhen, led his division in submission.

entries.zh: 奴真兄犍，先居賀蘭部。
entries.en: His elder brother Jian had long lived among the Helan.
entries.literal: Nuzhen's elder brother Jian had earlier dwelt with the Helan tribe.

entries.zh: 至是，奴真請召犍而讓部焉。
entries.en: Now Nuzhen asked to call Jian in and turn the tribe over to him.
entries.literal: At this time Nuzhen asked to summon Jian and yield the division to him.

entries.zh: 太祖義而許之。
entries.en: Taizu, approving the act, allowed it.
entries.literal: Taizu, moved by the righteousness of it, granted his request.

entries.zh: 犍既領部，自以久託賀訥，德之，乃使弟去斤遺之金馬。
entries.en: When Jian took command, he felt himself long beholden to He Ne and sent his brother Qujin with a gift of a golden horse.
entries.literal: Once Jian held the division, deeming himself long indebted to He Ne for shelter, he sent his younger brother Qujin to present him with a golden horse.

entries.zh: 訥弟染干因謂之曰：「我待汝兄弟厚，汝今領部，宜來從我。」
entries.en: He Ne's brother Ran'gan told him, "I have been generous to you two; now that you lead a division, you should come over to my side."
entries.literal: He Ne's younger brother Ran'gan then said to him: "I have treated you brothers generously; now that you lead a division, you ought to come follow me."

entries.zh: 去斤請之奴真。
entries.en: Qujin put the matter to Nuzhen.
entries.literal: Qujin asked Nuzhen about it.

entries.zh: 奴真曰：「父為國家附臣，世効忠貞。
entries.en: Nuzhen replied, "Our father was the state's man; our house has served with loyalty for generations.
entries.literal: Nuzhen said: "Our father was a subject attached to the state; for generations we have served with loyal fidelity.

entries.zh: 我志全名節，是故推讓。
entries.en: I meant to keep our name whole, and that is why I yielded the tribe.
entries.literal: I sought to preserve our name and honor intact, and for that reason I yielded the division.

entries.zh: 今汝等無狀，乃欲叛主懷貳。」
entries.en: Now you act shamefully and would turn traitor with a double heart."
entries.literal: Now you behave disgracefully and would betray your lord with divided hearts."

entries.zh: 於是殺犍及去斤。
entries.en: He killed Jian and Qujin on the spot.
entries.literal: He then killed Jian and Qujin.

entries.zh: 染干聞其殺兄，率騎討之，奴真懼，徙部來奔太祖。
entries.en: Ran'gan, hearing his brother had been killed, led cavalry against him; Nuzhen in alarm moved his people to seek refuge with Taizu.
entries.literal: When Ran'gan heard that he had killed his elder brother, he led horsemen to attack him; Nuzhen in fear moved his division to flee to Taizu.

entries.zh: 太祖自迎之，遣使責止染干。
entries.en: Taizu rode out to meet him and sent envoys to rebuke Ran'gan and make him stop.
entries.literal: Taizu went out in person to welcome him and sent envoys to reprimand Ran'gan and halt him.

entries.zh: 奴真感恩，請奉妹充後宮，太祖納之。
entries.en: Nuzhen, moved by the grace shown him, offered his younger sister to the inner palace, and Taizu took her.
entries.literal: Grateful, Nuzhen offered his younger sister for the inner palace; Taizu took her.

entries.zh: 衛操 莫含 劉庫仁
entries.en: Biographies of Wei Cao, Mo Han, and Liu Kuren
entries.literal: Wei Cao; Mo Han; Liu Kuren

entries.zh: 張袞，字洪龍，上谷沮陽人也。
entries.en: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, came from Juyang in Shanggu.
entries.literal: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was a man of Juyang in Shanggu.

entries.zh: 祖翼，遼東太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Yi had been administrator of Liaodong.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yi was Administrator of Liaodong.

entries.zh: 父卓，昌黎太守。
entries.en: His father Zhuo was administrator of Changli.
entries.literal: His father Zhuo was Administrator of Changli.

entries.zh: 袞初為郡五官掾，純厚篤實，好學，有文才。
entries.en: Gun began as the commandery registrar of five offices — honest, steady, studious, and gifted in letters.
entries.literal: Gun at first was the commandery Registrar of Five Offices — pure, thick, and sincere, loving learning, with literary talent.

entries.zh: 太祖為代王，選為左長史。
entries.en: When Taizu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen as left chief of staff.
entries.literal: When Taizu was Prince of Dai he was chosen as Left Chief of Staff.

entries.zh: 玄伯自非朝廷文誥，四方書檄，初不染翰，故世無遺文。
entries.en: Unless for court edicts or letters to the four quarters, Xuanbo never took up the brush — and so no writings of his survive.
entries.literal: Unless for court documents of the throne or letters to the four directions, Xuanbo never touched the brush — hence no writings survive in the world.

entries.zh: 尤善草隸行押之書，為世摹楷。
entries.en: He excelled above all in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script, and the age copied him as its model.
entries.literal: He was especially skilled in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script — models for the age.

entries.zh: 玄伯祖悅與范陽盧諶，並以博藝著名。
entries.en: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang's Lu Chen were both famed for wide learning in the arts.
entries.literal: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang Lu Chen were both famed for broad arts.

entries.zh: 諶法鍾繇，悅法衞瓘，而俱習索靖之草，皆盡其妙。
entries.en: Chen took Zhong You as his model, Yue took Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive until each reached its utmost subtlety.
entries.literal: Chen learned from Zhong You, Yue from Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive — each attaining the utmost subtlety.

entries.zh: 諶傳子偃，偃傳子邈；
entries.en: Chen passed the art to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;
entries.literal: Chen passed it to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;

entries.zh: 悅傳子潛，潛傳玄伯。
entries.en: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo — so the record runs.
entries.literal: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo.

entries.zh: 世不替業。
entries.en: The craft never failed from father to son.
entries.literal: The craft was never broken through the generations.

entries.zh: 故魏初重崔盧之書。
entries.en: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were held in highest esteem.
entries.literal: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were prized.

entries.zh: 又玄伯之行押，特盡精巧，而不見遺迹。
entries.en: Xuanbo's running-draft hand too was wrought to rare refinement, yet no trace of it remains.
entries.literal: Xuanbo's running-draft script too was especially refined and ingenious, yet no traces survive.

entries.zh: 子浩，襲爵，別有傳。
entries.en: His son Hao inherited the title and has a separate biography.
entries.literal: His son Hao inherited the title; he is treated in a separate biography.

entries.zh: 計彼主篡殺之迹，人鬼同知，疑親猜貴，早暴遐邇。
entries.en: Weigh that lord's usurpation and murder — known to men and spirits alike; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble were long ago plain far and near.
entries.literal: Consider the traces of that lord's usurpation and murder — known alike to men and spirits; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble long ago exposed far and near.

entries.zh: 兄投心逆節，千載何名！
entries.en: Elder brother, to set your heart on rebellion — what name will stand for a thousand years?
entries.literal: Elder brother, to cast your heart into rebellion — what name for a thousand years!

entries.zh: 物患無施，器非時用，生不振世，沒無令聲，先師以為鄙，君子以為耻。
entries.en: When things have no place to be used and vessels are unfit for the age, to live without stirring the world and die without a fair name — the ancients called that base, gentlemen called it shame.
entries.literal: When things have no scope for use and vessels are unfit for the time, one who lives without stirring the age and dies without a fair reputation — the former masters held this base, gentlemen held it shameful.

entries.zh: 此則事困伎殫，自勉無益，故其宜矣。
entries.en: Here affairs are tight and arts spent; urging oneself on brings no gain — hence the proper course.
entries.literal: Here events are straitened and skills exhausted; self-exhortation brings no gain — hence the fit course.

entries.zh: 以兄之才，夙超鄉土，如弟之徒，誰不瞻仰，每尋昔念，未敢忘懷。
entries.en: With your talent, elder brother, you have long outshone our homeland — who like me does not look up to you? I never dare forget our old bond.
entries.literal: With elder brother's talent, from old surpassing your homeland — who among men like me does not look up to you? Whenever I recall former thoughts, I dare not forget.

entries.zh: 雖復途遙二千，心想若對，敬遵軌範，以資一生。
entries.en: Though two thousand li lie between us, in thought we meet as face to face; reverently I follow your example for my whole life.
entries.literal: Though the road spans two thousand li, in thought we meet face to face; reverently I follow the norm and draw on it for a lifetime.

entries.zh: 今名可揚矣而不能顯親，事可變矣而不能離辱，故世之所未解也。
entries.en: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot honor your kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot shake off disgrace — that is what the age cannot understand.
entries.literal: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot glorify kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot leave disgrace — hence what the age has not understood.

entries.zh: 且君子在家也不過孝於其親，入朝也不過忠於其君。
entries.en: A gentleman at home is filial to his kin; in court he is loyal to his lord — no more.
entries.literal: And the gentleman at home does no more than show filial piety to his kin; in court does no more than show loyalty to his lord.

entries.zh: 主上之於兄，恩則不可酬，義則不可背。
entries.en: The sovereign's treatment of you, elder brother — grace that cannot be repaid, righteousness that cannot be betrayed.
entries.literal: The sovereign's treatment of elder brother — in grace it cannot be repaid, in righteousness it cannot be betrayed.

entries.zh: 身可殺也，故非其酬；
entries.en: One's person may be given up — that is not repayment;
entries.literal: The person may be killed — hence this is not the repayment;

entries.zh: 功不逮也，故非其報。
entries.en: merit does not stretch so far — that is not return.
entries.literal: Merit does not reach so far — hence this is not the return.

entries.zh: 今可以效矣而又弗為，非孝也。
entries.en: Now you could act loyally and again you will not — that is unfilial.
entries.literal: Now you could effect loyalty yet again do not — this is unfilial.

entries.zh: 即實而言，兄之不變，得為忠乎？
entries.en: Judged by fact, elder brother, can your refusal to change count as loyalty?
entries.literal: Judged by fact, elder brother's not changing — can this count as loyalty?

entries.zh: 至於講武爭強，不敵者久矣；
entries.en: As for drilling in arms and contending for mastery, you have long been unmatched;
entries.literal: As for training in arms and contending for supremacy, the unmatched have long been so;

entries.zh: 論安與危，不同者驗矣；
entries.en: weigh safety against peril and the unlike cases have been proved;
entries.literal: Discussing security and danger, those not alike have been proved;

entries.zh: 羣情背去，獨留者謬矣。
entries.en: the crowd's heart has turned away — to stand alone is error.
entries.literal: Mass sentiment turns away in desertion; to remain alone is error.

entries.zh: 願深察之。
entries.en: I beg you to weigh this deeply.
entries.literal: I beg deep scrutiny of this.

entries.zh: 王晏道絕外交，器非雄朗，專華保望，便就屠割。
entries.en: Wang Yan cut off every outside tie; his talent was not bold and bright; clinging to glory and nursing hope, he was at once put to the sword.
entries.literal: Wang Yan utterly cut off external ties; his capacity was not heroic and bright; clinging to splendor and guarding hope, he was at once sent to slaughter.

entries.zh: 方之於兄，其全百倍。
entries.en: Compared with you, elder brother, he was not one part in a hundred.
entries.literal: Compared with elder brother, you are whole a hundredfold.

entries.zh: 且淮蕃海捍，本出北豪，壽春之任，兄何由免？
entries.en: Moreover the Huai frontier and the coastal garrisons bred northern champions — could you, elder brother, escape the Shouchun command?
entries.literal: Moreover the Huai lands and the coastal marches originally produced northern champions — could elder brother escape the charge at Shouchun?

entries.zh: 以是而言，猜嫌已決。
entries.en: On that ground suspicion is already fixed.
entries.literal: On this ground, suspicion and mistrust are already settled.

entries.zh: 又宗門未幾，南北莫寄，先構之重，非兄何託，受社之榮，鄙心之相望矣。
entries.en: Moreover the house is still young; north and south have nowhere else to lodge — to whom but you, elder brother, can the weight of the founding be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — my humble heart has long looked for it.
entries.literal: Moreover the ancestral house is not many generations old; north and south have no other lodging — to whom but elder brother can the weight of the prior structure be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — this humble heart has longed for it.

entries.zh: 今執志不寤，忠孝兩忘，王晏之辜，安能自保，見機而作，其在茲乎。
entries.en: Now you cling to your resolve without waking, forgetting both filial piety and loyalty — Wang Yan's guilt, how could he save himself? To act when the moment shows itself — is it not now?
entries.literal: Now clinging to resolve without waking, both filial piety and loyalty forgotten — Wang Yan's crime, how can he protect himself? To act when the moment appears — is it not here?

entries.zh: 燕鳳 許謙 張袞 崔玄伯 鄧淵
entries.en: Biographies of Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Zhang Gun, Cui Xuanbo, and Deng Yuan
entries.literal: Yan Feng; Xu Qian; Zhang Gun; Cui Xuanbo; Deng Yuan

entries.zh: 長孫嵩 長孫道生
entries.en: Biographies of Changsun Song and Changsun Daosheng
entries.literal: Changsun Song; Changsun Daosheng

entries.zh: 子悅，襲爵。
entries.en: His son Yue inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Yue inherited the rank.

entries.zh: 建義初，復本王爵，尋降為公。
entries.en: At the start of Jianyi his royal title was restored; before long he was reduced again to duke.
entries.literal: At the opening of the Jianyi era his original kingly rank was restored; soon he was again demoted to duke.

entries.zh: 位光祿少卿。
entries.en: He served as Vice Director of the Palace Enfeoffments.
entries.literal: He held the post of Vice Director of the Palace Enfeoffments.

entries.zh: 卒，贈司空。
entries.en: At his death he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 長孫道生，嵩從子也。
entries.en: Changsun Daosheng was Song's nephew.
entries.literal: Changsun Daosheng was Song's cousin's son.

entries.zh: 忠厚廉謹，太祖愛其慎重，使掌幾密，與賀毗等四人內侍左右，出入詔命。
entries.en: Steadfast, loyal, and careful, he won Taizu's trust for his gravity; Taizu set him over secret matters, and with He Pi and three others he waited on the throne, carrying orders in and out.
entries.literal: Steadfast, loyal, and scrupulous, Taizu loved his careful manner and put him in charge of confidential affairs; with He Pi and three others he attended within at the left and right, bearing edicts in and out.

entries.zh: 太宗即位，除南統將軍、冀州刺史。
entries.en: At Taizong's accession he was named General of the Southern Command and inspector of Jizhou.
entries.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was made General of the Southern Command and inspector of Jizhou.

entries.zh: 後取人美女以獻太宗，切責之，以舊臣不加罪黜。
entries.en: Later he took a beautiful woman and offered her to Taizong; Taizong rebuked him sharply yet, as a veteran of the founding, withheld punishment or dismissal.
entries.literal: Later he took a beautiful woman and presented her to Taizong; Taizong sternly rebuked him but, as an old servant, did not punish or dismiss him.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，進爵汝陰公，[8]遷廷尉卿。
entries.en: At Shizu's accession he was raised to Duke of Ruyin; [8] he was moved to Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Ruyin; [8] he was transferred to Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 從征蠕蠕，與尉眷等率眾出白黑兩漠間，大捷而還。
entries.en: He marched against the Rouran; with Wei Juan and others he led troops through the country between the White and Black Deserts and came back in triumph.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against the Rouran; with Wei Juan and others he led forces out between the White and Black Deserts and returned in great victory.

entries.zh: 世祖征赫連昌，道生與司徒長孫翰、宗正娥青為前驅，遂平其國。
entries.en: On Shizu's campaign against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Changsun Han, Minister over the Masses, and E Qing, Director of the Imperial Clan, led the van and brought the realm down.
entries.literal: When Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Minister over the Masses Changsun Han and Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing served as vanguard and thereupon pacified the state.

entries.zh: 昌弟定走保平涼，劉義隆遣將到彥之、王仲德寇河南以救定。
entries.en: Chang's brother Ding withdrew to Pingliang; Liu Yilong sent Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde to strike Henan and relieve Ding.
entries.literal: Chang's younger brother Ding fled to hold Pingliang; Liu Yilong sent the generals Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde to raid Henan and rescue Ding.

entries.zh: 詔道生與丹陽王太之屯河上以禦之。
entries.en: The court ordered Daosheng and Taizhi, Prince of Danyang, to hold the river line against them.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Daosheng with Prince of Danyang Taizhi to encamp on the river and resist them.

entries.zh: 遂誘義隆將檀道濟，邀其前後，追至歷城而還。
entries.en: They baited Tan Daoji of Liu Yilong's host, caught him fore and aft, chased him to Licheng, and withdrew.
entries.literal: They thereupon lured Liu Yilong's general Tan Daoji, caught him between front and rear, pursued him to Licheng, and returned.

entries.zh: 除司空，加侍中，進封上黨王。
entries.en: He was named Minister of Works and attendant-in-ordinary and raised to Prince of Shangdang.
entries.literal: He was made Minister of Works, added attendant-in-ordinary, and advanced to Prince of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 薨，年八十二。
entries.en: He passed away at eighty-two.
entries.literal: He died at eighty-two.

entries.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰靖。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous name Jing.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant; posthumous name Jing.

entries.zh: 抗子觀，少以壯勇知名，後襲祖爵上黨王。
entries.en: Kang's son Guan won early fame for fierce courage and later inherited his grandfather's title as Prince of Shangdang.
entries.literal: Kang's son Guan, in youth famed for bold courage, later inherited his grandfather's rank as Prince of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 時異姓諸王，襲爵多降為公，帝以其祖道生佐命先朝，故特不降。
entries.en: By then most non-imperial clansmen who inherited were cut to duke; because Daosheng had served the founding, the Emperor left Guan's princely rank untouched.
entries.literal: At that time most kings of other surnames who inherited were demoted to duke; because his grandfather Daosheng had aided the founding court, the Emperor specially did not lower his rank.

entries.zh: 以征西大將軍、假司空、督河西七鎮諸軍，討吐谷渾。
entries.en: He was named General Who Campaigns West, acting Minister of Works, and overseer of the seven Hexi garrisons to strike Tuyuhun.
entries.literal: He was made General Who Campaigns West, acting Minister of Works, and overseer of the seven garrisons of the Hexi circuit, to campaign against Tuyuhun.

entries.zh: 部帥拾寅遁藏，焚其所居城邑而還。
entries.en: The Tuyuhun chief Shiyin vanished into concealment; Guan burned his settlements and withdrew.
entries.literal: The tribal chief Shiyin fled into hiding; Guan burned his towns and strongholds and returned.

entries.zh: 高祖初，拜殿中尚書、侍中。
entries.en: Early in Gaozu's reign he was made Director in the Palace Department and attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign he was made Director in the Palace Department and attendant-in-ordinary.

entries.zh: 吐谷渾又侵逼，復假觀司空討降之。
entries.en: When Tuyuhun raided again, Guan was again lent the acting seal of Minister of Works to bring them to heel.
entries.literal: When Tuyuhun again pressed the border, Guan was again lent the acting rank of Minister of Works to subdue them.

entries.zh: 後為征南大將軍。
entries.en: He was later named General Who Campaigns South.
entries.literal: Later he was made General Who Campaigns South.

entries.zh: 薨，諡曰定。
entries.en: He died and was given the posthumous name Ding.
entries.literal: He died; posthumous name Ding.

entries.zh: 葬禮依其祖靖王故事，陪葬雲中金陵。
entries.en: His burial followed his grandfather King Jing's rites, and he was laid to rest beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.
entries.literal: His funeral followed the precedent of his grandfather King Jing and he was buried beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.

entries.zh: 道生廉約，身為三司，而衣不華飾，食不兼味。
entries.en: Daosheng lived sparely: though a pillar of state, he wore no finery and ate but one course.
entries.literal: Daosheng was frugal; though he held one of the Three Excellencies, his clothes bore no rich ornament and his meals no second dish.

entries.zh: 一熊皮鄣泥，數十年不易，時人比之晏嬰。
entries.en: One bear-hide riding apron he kept for decades without replacing; his contemporaries likened him to Yan Ying.
entries.literal: A single bear-pelt mud-guard he did not change for decades; men of the time compared him to Yan Ying.

entries.zh: 第宅卑陋，出鎮後，其子弟頗更修繕，起堂廡。
entries.en: His dwelling was humble; once he had left on frontier command his sons and nephews refurbished it and built halls.
entries.literal: His house was low and mean; after he went out on garrison duty his sons and nephews somewhat repaired it and raised halls and galleries.

entries.zh: 道生還，歎曰：「昔霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為，今強寇尚遊魂漠北，吾豈可安坐華美也！」
entries.en: On his return Daosheng sighed: "Huo Qubing once said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed a man had no business with a home — and mighty enemies still haunt the northern sands; how should I dwell in comfort and show?"
entries.literal: When Daosheng returned he sighed and said: "In old times Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed he would not concern himself with a household — and now strong foes still wander the soul of the northern desert; how can I sit at ease amid splendor!"

entries.zh: 乃切責子弟，令毀宅。
entries.en: He rebuked his sons and nephews harshly and made them tear the house down.
entries.literal: He thereupon sternly rebuked his sons and nephews and ordered the house destroyed.

entries.zh: 其恭慎如此。
entries.en: In such ways he kept his reverent care.
entries.literal: Such was his respectful caution.

entries.zh: 世祖世，所在著績，每建大議，多合時機。
entries.en: Under Shizu he left his mark in every post; on great questions his counsel usually hit the hour.
entries.literal: In Shizu's age he won distinction wherever he served; whenever he framed a great proposal it mostly matched the moment.

entries.zh: 為將有權略，善待士眾。
entries.en: In command he was resourceful and kind to his troops.
entries.literal: As a general he had stratagem and treated officers and men well.

entries.zh: 帝命歌工歷頌羣臣，曰：「智如崔浩，廉如道生。」
entries.en: The Emperor had singers pass among the ministers in praise, saying: "Wise as Cui Hao, spare as Daosheng."
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered singing masters to go through the ministers in praise, saying: "Wise as Cui Hao, frugal as Daosheng."

entries.zh: 及年老，頗惑其妻孟氏，以此見譏。
entries.en: In age he fell under his wife Lady Meng's sway and was laughed at for it.
entries.literal: In his old age he was much swayed by his wife Lady Meng, for which he was mocked.

entries.zh: 與從父嵩俱為三公，當世以為榮。
entries.en: He and his uncle Song both reached the Three Excellencies — a glory of their day.
entries.literal: He and his uncle Song both held one of the Three Excellencies — an honor for their generation.

entries.zh: 魏書卷二十五 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」。
entries.en: Every edition's table of contents marks Wei shu juan 25 "lacunose."
entries.literal: In the tables of contents of all editions of Wei shu juan 25 this scroll is marked "lacunose."

entries.zh: 百衲本、南本、汲本卷末殘存宋人校語：「魏收書列傳第十三。」
entries.en: Patchwork, Southern, and Jishui editions keep Song notes at the scroll's end: "Wei Shou's book, Biographies 13."
entries.literal: The Patchwork, Southern, and Jishui editions at the end of the scroll preserve Song-dynasty collation notes: "Wei Shou's book, Biographies section 13."

entries.zh: 局本下補「亡」字。
entries.en: The Bureau edition adds "lost" below.
entries.literal: The Bureau edition supplies below the character "lost."

entries.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書闕，後人所補。」
entries.en: Palace Edition textual notes: "Wei Shou's text is missing; later hands supplied this."
entries.literal: The Palace Edition textual verification states: "Wei Shou's book is lacunose; later men supplemented it."

entries.zh: 按此卷以北史卷二二長孫嵩、長孫道生傳補，附長孫稚傳有溢出語，當出於高氏小史。
entries.en: The received scroll was patched from Beishi juan 22 (Changsuns Song and Daosheng); the attached Zhi life has overflow wording likely from the Gao clan Minor History.
entries.literal: On examination this scroll was supplemented from Beishi juan 22, the biographies of Changsun Song and Changsun Daosheng; the attached Changsun Zhi biography has overflowing wording that should come from the Gao clan Minor History.

entries.zh: 進爵汝陰公 張森楷云：「以前初無封爵之文，而云『進爵』，疑誤。」
entries.en: He was advanced to duke of Ruyin. Zhang Senkai: "No prior enfeoffment is recorded, yet it says 'advanced'—likely error."
entries.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Ruyin. Zhang Senkai states: "Earlier there was no text of an initial enfeoffment, yet it says 'advanced in rank'—suspected error."

entries.zh: 按此傳以北史卷二二長孫道生傳補，當是李延壽刪節之失。
entries.en: This life was patched from Beishi juan 22, Daosheng; the fault is Li Yanshou's abridgment.
entries.literal: Commentary: This biography was supplemented from Beishi juan 22, Changsun Daosheng biography; it should be Li Yanshou's faulty abridgment.

entries.zh: 這種刪節失當，下文還有，如「帝以其祖道生佐命先朝」，不知為何帝；
entries.en: Such cuts recur below—"the emperor, because his grandfather Daosheng aided the founding court," without naming which emperor;
entries.literal: Such faulty abridgment appears again below—for example, "the emperor, because his grandfather Daosheng aided the founding court," without stating which emperor;

entries.zh: 「以本使達鄴城」，不知為何使。
entries.en: "as envoy reached Ye," without naming the mission.
entries.literal: "in his capacity as envoy reached Ye," without stating what envoy.

entries.zh: 今不悉出校記。
entries.en: Further collation is not set out in full.
entries.literal: Not all collation notes are given here.
